_source.definition_text: used before a noun to refer to a single thing or person but not a particular thing or person or not one that you have referred to before
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's got a boyfriend.; Someone left an umbrella here yesterday.; Is he a friend of yours?; You can make a quick snack, for example a sandwich.

_source.definition_text: used to mean any or every thing or person of the type you are referring to
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you ride a bike?; A child needs love.; A cheetah can run faster than a lion.; I don't need it because I'm too old to have a doll.

_source.definition_text: one
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hundred dollars; a dozen eggs; Dear Ally, All my friends [from] school were here, more than a hundred people.

_source.definition_text: used to state what type of thing or person something or someone is
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sally's an engineer.; It's a rabbit.; She's a teacher.

_source.definition_text: used before some phrases saying how much of something there is
_source.learnerexamples_text: a few days; a bit of wool; Please come next Monday with old clothes and a bit of green paint.

_source.definition_text: used before some action nouns when referring to one example of the action
_source.learnerexamples_text: Take a look at this, Jez.; I'm just going to have a wash.; I took a shower and ate my breakfast.

_source.definition_text: used before the first but not the second of two nouns that are often used together
_source.learnerexamples_text: a cup and saucer; a knife and fork; I like a clean fork and knife.

_source.definition_text: used when referring to a unit of something, especially something you eat or drink
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd love a coffee.; All I had for lunch was a yogurt.; We both had a coke and a hot dog.

_source.definition_text: used between a fraction and a unit of measurement
_source.learnerexamples_text: half a mile; a quarter of a kilo; three-quarters of an hour; The lesson is half an hour but you have to be ther[e] 10 minutes before.

_source.definition_text: used when referring to a certain period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Take one tablet three times a day.; She earns $100 000 a year.; I can write to him or her twice a week.

_source.definition_text: to leave someone or something somewhere, sometimes not returning to get them
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were forced to abandon the car.; As a baby, he'd been abandoned by his mother.; We were sinking fast, and the captain gave the order to abandon ship.; I lived with my mother and brother but my father was never there. I knew that he had abandoned us for another woman.

_source.definition_text: to stop doing something before it is finished, or to stop following a plan, idea, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The match was abandoned because of rain.; How would you feel if you establish[ed] a long-time plan for your career and then you ha[d] to abandon it?

_source.definition_text: having been left somewhere, intentionally
_source.learnerexamples_text: An abandoned baby was found in a box on the hospital steps.; Please, just have a look [at] your wife Margaret and her eyes will tell you that she is this abandoned princess of your childhood fairy-tale.

_source.definition_text: left empty or not working
_source.learnerexamples_text: an abandoned factory/village; Arriving [at] an altitude of 2000m, people can visit the abandoned salt-mines.

_source.definition_text: the physical or mental skill or qualities that you need to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had the ability to explain things clearly.; athletic/academic ability; The protagonist had been bitten by a strange spider and some days later, he noticed [he had] some strange powers, such as the ability to create spider[s'] webs.

_source.definition_text: to have the ability to do something or the possibility of doing something
_source.searchterms_text: able;abler;ablest;be able to do sth;be able to do sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He'll be able to help you.; Will she be able to do the work?; I'm sorry that I wasn't able to phone you yesterday.; It's so wonderful being able to see the sea from my window.; I will be able to go to your house next Friday.

_source.definition_text: clever or good at doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's a very able student.; They contend that this will lead to better grades, better results in key stage test[s], and a more able work force.

_source.definition_text: different from what is normal or usual, in a way which is strange or dangerous
_source.learnerexamples_text: abnormal behaviour/weather ;  They found abnormal levels of lead in the water. ; The cost of it for the Chinese population is an abnormal level of pollution, that causes many deaths every year.

_source.definition_text: on or onto a plane, ship, bus, or train
_source.learnerexamples_text: Welcome aboard flight BA109 to Paris. ; Competition entry "Welcome aboard on the flight to ancient Rome..." Please fasten your seatbelts...

_source.definition_text: to officially end something, especially a law or system
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think bullfighting should be abolished.; National Service was abolished in Britain in 1962.; Therefore, I suggest you should not change or abolish any event for any reason.

_source.definition_text: a medical operation to end a pregnancy when the baby is still too small to live
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had an abortion. ; Some of these problems are serious and should be eliminated, such as abortion and domestic violence.

_source.definition_text: relating to a particular subject or person
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's she talking about?; I've got a book about Jung.; I like my IT course becaus[e] I want to learn about computers.

_source.definition_text: used to ask for someone's opinion on a particular subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: What about Ava - is she nice? ; So the town was nice - how about the food?; I also enjoy shopping for shoes, what about you?

_source.definition_text: used when suggesting or offering something to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: How about a trip to the zoo this afternoon?; "Coffee, Sarah?" "No, thanks." "What about you, Kate?"; How about cycling there?; What about going on Saturday?

_source.definition_text: a little more or less than the stated number or amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: It happened about two months ago.; "What time are you leaving work today?" "About five."; It's not far [from] my home, about 20 minut[es'] walk, [or] 5 minut[es] by bus.

_source.definition_text: to or in different parts of a place, often without purpose or order
_source.learnerexamples_text: They heard someone moving/walking about outside.

_source.definition_text: to be going to do something very soon
_source.searchterms_text: about;be (just) about to do sth;be (just) about to do sth ;be just about to do sth;be just about to do sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was about to leave when Mark arrived.; When I was just about to cross the road, I realised that I was going to faint [at] any moment.

_source.definition_text: in or to a higher position than something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's a mirror above the washbasin.; Her name comes above mine on the list.; I think I have [put] it above the bookshelf.

_source.definition_text: more than an amount or level
_source.learnerexamples_text: It says on the box it's for children aged three and above.; Rates of pay are above average.; The weather is too hot in Beijing. Every day [it] is above 30 degrees.

_source.definition_text: most importantly
_source.learnerexamples_text: Above all, I'd like to thank my family.; He is known above all for his film roles.; She is a very nice person and above all, she is really cheerful.

_source.definition_text: too good or important for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: No one is above suspicion in this matter.

_source.definition_text: higher on the page
_source.learnerexamples_text: the above diagram; Match these words with the pictures above.; Please send the articles to the address given/shown above.; I can be contacted at the above address and I would be free to attend an interview at any time from Monday to Saturday.

_source.definition_text: in or to a foreign country
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's currently abroad on business.; We always go abroad in the summer.; I have never been abroad.

_source.definition_text: sudden and not expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our conversation came to an abrupt end. ; Their income came from the revenues obtained by selling milk, fruit, jelly and other perishable goods, but they had to pay John, or their happy lifestyle would come to an abrupt end.

_source.definition_text: dealing with people in a quick way that is unfriendly or rude
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has a rather abrupt manner. ; I was poorly received and the general tone of the person assisting me was rude and abrupt.

_source.definition_text: when someone is not where they are usually expected to be
_source.learnerexamples_text: A new manager was appointed during/in her absence.; She has had repeated absences from work this year.; Thank you very much for letting me stay in your flat during your absence on holiday.

_source.definition_text: suddenly and quickly
_source.learnerexamples_text: They abruptly left the party.; His speech ended abruptly and he left the stage.; When she became an adolescent, her perspective changed abruptly.

_source.definition_text: when something does not exist
_source.learnerexamples_text: He drew attention to the absence of concrete evidence against the defendant.; The biggest difference the absence of TV made in my life was that I actually started living.

_source.definition_text: not in the place where you are expected to be, especially at school or work
_source.learnerexamples_text: John has been absent from school/work for three days now.; I would like to apologise, because I'm missing tomorrow's class. I'm going to be absent because my grandmother is ill and I have to take care of her.

_source.definition_text: complete and definite
_source.learnerexamples_text: absolute control; He's an absolute idiot!; That's absolute rubbish!; I have no experience [of] surfing - I am an absolute beginner with high motivation.

_source.definition_text: completely
_source.learnerexamples_text: The food was absolutely delicious.; It's absolutely ridiculous.; I have absolutely no idea what she's talking about.; We've achieved absolutely nothing today.; I absolutely hate it.

_source.definition_text: used to strongly agree with someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Do you think it helped his career?" "Absolutely."; "It was an excellent film, though." "Absolutely!"; So have the Swedish grandparents got funkier? Absolutely!

_source.definition_text: used to strongly disagree with someone or to agree with something negative
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Are you suggesting that we should just ignore the problem?" "No, absolutely not."; Does it mean the parents will allow them to eat anything they please? Absolutely not. You have to give the children some options, instead of imposing things on them.

_source.definition_text: to give all your attention to something that you are doing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Simon was so absorbed in his computer game that he didn't notice me come in.; We hadn't noticed them at first because we were absorbed in [listening to the] birds singing.

_source.definition_text: to take something in, especially gradually
_source.learnerexamples_text: Plants absorb carbon dioxide.; The drug is quickly absorbed into the bloodstream.; Everything is getting intermingled and absorbed into the system, making life terribly efficient, quick and easy.

_source.definition_text: relating to ideas and not real things
_source.learnerexamples_text: abstract ideas; Truth and beauty are abstract concepts.; Reading improve[s] your ability to imagine and your abstract thinking skills.

_source.definition_text: to understand and remember facts that you read or hear
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's hard to absorb so much information.; You will have only three school [subjects] and that'[ll] make it easier to absorb the new knowledge.

_source.definition_text: very silly
_source.learnerexamples_text: What an absurd explanation!; Don't be so absurd! Of course I want you to come.; It's an absurd situation - neither of them will talk to the other.; [In your article,] some performers are called 'second-rate', which, in my view, is absurd when talking about such famous groups as 'Snakes' and 'KGB'.

_source.definition_text: Abstract art involves shapes and colours and not images of real things or people.
_source.learnerexamples_text: abstract paintings/sculpture; What kind of material will you use for this painting? Will it be a realistic picture or an abstract one?

_source.definition_text: bad or cruel treatment of people or animals
_source.learnerexamples_text: sexual/psychological/mental abuse; The rescued dogs had been victims of physical abuse.; The one side opposes this treatment as an abuse of living creatures while the other side denies any suffering and points at the values of zoos for people.

_source.definition_text: the use of a substance in an unsuitable and harmful way or for the wrong purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: Drug and alcohol abuse contributed to his early death.; This program tries to address problems that lead to substance abuse.; Get information about the [effect]s of drug abuse and make your generation a better one.

_source.definition_text: an action or activity that is morally wrong or not allowed
_source.learnerexamples_text: The politician's behaviour was an abuse of power.; It is a vast resource of information, but the abuse of it may have detrimental consequences.

_source.definition_text: rude and offensive words said to another person
_source.learnerexamples_text: Rival fans shouted abuse at each other.; I went all the way back cycling on the wrong side of the road, and anyone who said something about it could expect a stream of abuse.

_source.definition_text: saying rude and offensive words to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: an abusive phone call ; This is partly true, because even [a] slightly abusive expression might result in discord or [rupture] between seemingly close friends.

_source.definition_text: relating to schools, colleges and universities, or to subjects which involve thinking and studying and not technical or practical skills
_source.learnerexamples_text: academic subjects/qualifications/books; academic standards; As a member of our academic community, I'm very glad to hear that our college will have a surplus in its annual budget.

_source.definition_text: clever and good at studying
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's not very academic.

_source.definition_text: to start to happen more quickly, or to make something start to happen more quickly
_source.learnerexamples_text: Inflation is likely to accelerate this year. ; Fashion has always been changing but I think this process accelerated after the Second World War.

_source.definition_text: to move or cause yourself or a vehicle to move faster
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car in front accelerated and left us behind.; When I ride my bike and start accelerating, I feel that I move with the speed of the wind.

_source.definition_text: a mark written or printed over a letter to show you how to pronounce it
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's an acute accent on the 'e' of 'café'.

_source.definition_text: the way in which people in a particular area, country or social group pronounce words
_source.learnerexamples_text: an American accent; He speaks with a broad/heavy/strong Yorkshire accent.; Our teacher is a middle-aged lady with a kind smile and [a] British accent.

_source.definition_text: to agree to take something that is offered to you
_source.learnerexamples_text: to accept an apology/invitation/offer; I've been invited to their wedding, but I haven't decided whether to accept.; She won't accept advice from anyone.; I hope that you accept my apology.

_source.definition_text: to admit that something is true, often something unpleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: He refuses to accept that he's made a mistake.; I can't accept that there's nothing we can do.; David told her that the reason [for] his failure was her, because she used to press him a lot and she couldn't accept that he wanted to be an actor.

_source.definition_text: to allow someone to join an organization or become part of a group
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's been accepted by two universities.; He was accepted as a full member of the society.; His fellow workers refused to accept him.; When I returned home I check[ed] my mail and I ha[d] a new message from my uncle, saying that the university have accepted me.

_source.definition_text: to admit that you caused something bad that happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: I accept full responsibility for the failure of the plan.

_source.definition_text: good enough
_source.learnerexamples_text: work of an acceptable standard; Clearly we need to come to an arrangement that is acceptable to both parties.; This kind of attitude is simply not acceptable.; So what is an acceptable level of radiation?; I am sure that finally I will succeed in [us]ing English in an acceptable way!

_source.definition_text: allowed or approved of
_source.learnerexamples_text: Smoking is less and less socially acceptable.; They should teach them what is right [and] wrong, and what is morally and socially acceptable.

_source.definition_text: when you accept something
_source.learnerexamples_text: His acceptance of the award was controversial.;  There is a growing public acceptance of alternative medicine. ; The main reason for the "fast-food" groceries winning acceptance in Swedish culture is lack of time.

_source.definition_text: agreed or approved by most people
_source.learnerexamples_text: an accepted spelling; Competition can also be an accepted form of expression of one's aggression.

_source.definition_text: the right or opportunity to use or look at something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Internet access; The system has been designed to give the user quick and easy access to the required information.; I would suggest free Internet access as an extra facility in our library.

_source.definition_text: the way in which you can enter a place or get to a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: disabled access; The only access to the village is by boat.; I think it would be better if you stayed in a small village which has easy access to the city centre.

_source.definition_text: to find or see information, especially using a computer
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can access the files over the Internet.; We have more time to stay together at home, because we can access [the] internet at home.

_source.definition_text: able to be reached or easily got
_source.learnerexamples_text: The resort is easily accessible by road, rail and air.; It is very accessible because it is situated in the centre.

_source.definition_text: easy to understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are attempting to make opera accessible to a wider audience.;  Jacques Prevert, the French poet, changed our way [of seeing] the world by making poetry accessible to everyone.

_source.definition_text: something bad which happens that is not expected or intended, and which causes injury or damage
_source.learnerexamples_text: Josh had an accident and spilled water all over his work.; She was injured in a car/road accident.; I had an accident two weeks ago and now I can't do sport.

_source.definition_text: something extra which is not necessary but is attractive or useful
_source.learnerexamples_text: bathroom accessories;  computer accessories; They find pleasure in looking at different clothes, shoes, accessories, gadgets and home furnishings.

_source.definition_text: without being intended
_source.learnerexamples_text: I deleted the file by accident.; I was dancing and someone [kicked me] by accident and my glasses fell [off].

_source.definition_text: happening by chance
_source.learnerexamples_text: accidental damage; The archeological site was located after the accidental discovery of bones in a field.

_source.definition_text: by chance or by mistake
_source.learnerexamples_text: She accidentally knocked over a glass of water.; I accidentally broke one of your vases - the most beautiful one.

_source.definition_text: praised by a lot of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: the acclaimed singer and songwriter; In order to avoid s[uch an] embarrassing inconsistency in the next meeting, I suggest inviting Colin Briggs, the acclaimed footballer, to talk to his fans.

_source.definition_text: a place where you live or stay
_source.learnerexamples_text: rented accommodation; The price includes flights, all meals and accommodation.; There's a shortage of cheap accommodation.; You can find cheap accommodation in a student room because they are usually free in July an[d] August.

_source.definition_text: to go somewhere with someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: We accompanied her back to her hotel.; Children under 10 must be accompanied by an adult.; I asked my cousin to accompany me because she knew the way to the temple.

_source.definition_text: to happen or exist at the same time as something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: The course books are accompanied by four CDs.; The salmon was accompanied by a fresh green salad.; The weather was very hot and a shining sun accompanied us during our trip.

_source.definition_text: to play music to support someone else who is playing or singing
_source.learnerexamples_text: He accompanied me on the piano.; Last year, for instance, the concert became a recital: two singers performed Lieder by Schubert accompanied by the piano and by the sweet sound of Arimany's golden flute.

_source.definition_text: to succeed in doing something good
_source.learnerexamples_text: I feel as if I've accomplished nothing all day. ; To accomplish this, schools should try to respect the individuality of each child, give them chances to think more freely.

_source.definition_text: If you do something of your own accord, you choose to do it and no one else forces you.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She left of her own accord.; She would go alone, but it was something that was chosen of her own accord.

_source.definition_text: in the way described by a rule, law, or wish
_source.learnerexamples_text: Both companies have insisted that they were acting in accordance with the law.; Although they do not earn much money in this profession, they try to do their best and judge in accordance with the law which they also have to interpret.

_source.definition_text: as said by someone or shown by something
_source.learnerexamples_text: According to Sarah, they're not getting on very well at the moment.; According to our records, you owe us £45.; According to the guide, it was a famous culture in ancient times.

_source.definition_text: in a way that agrees with
_source.learnerexamples_text: Students are all put in different groups according to their ability.; The job included organizing suitable activities according to their age, capability and wishes.

_source.definition_text: an arrangement with a bank to keep your money there and to allow you to take it out when you need to
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've opened an account with another bank.; I paid the money into my account this morning.; The man, whose name I can't remember, wrote a serious looking message in which he [talked about] a money transfer to a Swiss bank account.

_source.definition_text: a written or spoken description of something that has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: She gave a thrilling account  of her life in the jungle.; The documents provide a detailed account of the town's early history.; I would be very interested [in participating] and [writing] the accounts of our journeys.

_source.definition_text: to consider something when judging a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: A good architect takes account of the building's surroundings.; I hope you will take account of our request.

_source.definition_text: to consider something when judging a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think you have to take into account the fact that he's a good deal younger than the rest of us.; Taking into account all these arguments, I also think, like many people, that keeping animals in zoos is cruel and unnecessary.

_source.definition_text: because of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He doesn't eat any dairy products on account of the diet he is following.; On account of its location, it is always busy.

_source.definition_text: as said by a lot of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: The party was, by all accounts, a great success.; I have known Michael Van Cleef for over two decades now, and he is, by all accounts, an exemplary worker.

_source.base_text: on no account; not on any account
_source.definition_text: not for any reason or in any situation
_source.searchterms_text: account;accounts;on no account not on any account;on no account; not on any account
_source.learnerexamples_text: On no account must these records be changed.; Mary did not want Martin to leave on any account, let alone move to a foreign country.

_source.definition_text: to be the reason for something, or to explain the reason for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you account for your absence last Friday?; He'd had an argument with Caroline, which accounts for his bad mood this morning.; She was asked to account for the missing money.; I was at a loss for words when I tried to account for her behaviour, but I never ceased to consider her a very valuable friend.

_source.definition_text: responsible for what you do and having to be able to explain your actions
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hospitals must be held accountable for their mistakes.; Politicians should be accountable to the public that elects them.; Finally, there should be a person who should be held accountable and [is] accessible to our complaints.

_source.definition_text: someone whose job is to keep or examine the financial records of a person or organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: a firm of accountants; I am working as an accountant at Deloitte & Touche.

_source.definition_text: to increase in amount over a period of time, or to make something increase over a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: The chemicals accumulate in your body.; Rain water then accumulates in the reservoir.

_source.definition_text: an amount of something that has been collected
_source.learnerexamples_text: Despite this accumulation of evidence, the government did nothing.; What is success? For some it is the accumulation of pos[s]es[s]ions, for others it's fame, health, love.

_source.definition_text: how correct or exact something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: We can predict changes with a surprising degree of accuracy.; I was very disappointed to observe your lack of accuracy in the description of this wonderful event.

_source.definition_text: correct, exact and without any mistakes
_source.learnerexamples_text: accurate information/measurements; She was able to give the police a fairly accurate description of the man.; Her novel is an accurate reflection of life in post-war Spain.; We hope to become more accurate in predicting earthquakes.; Some information in the Guidebook was not very accurate.

_source.definition_text: in an accurate way
_source.learnerexamples_text: The plans should be drawn as accurately as possible, showing all the measurements.; It's necessary to consider a lot of aspects to answer this question accurately, but in general I would prefer to go to work by bicycle.

_source.definition_text: when you say that someone has done something bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: He made a number of accusations against his former colleagues.; I have enclosed the Distribution Chart in order to prevent you from [making] further accusations.

_source.definition_text: to say that someone has done something bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's been accused of robbery/murder.; Are you accusing me of lying?; They were accused of vandalism.

_source.definition_text: If you are accustomed to something, you have experienced it often enough for it to seem normal to you.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've worked nights for years now so I've grown accustomed to it.; She isn't accustomed to dealing with so much media attention.; I am quite accustomed to being with many kinds of people of different ages.

_source.definition_text: a feeling of pain over an area of your body which continues for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: As you get older, you have all sorts of aches and pains.; I've got an ache in my lower back.; Since then, I have [had] a[n] ache in my left leg.

_source.definition_text: to have a continuous pain that is unpleasant but not strong
_source.learnerexamples_text: My head/tooth/back aches.; I ache/I'm aching all over.; After a[n] hour of horseback riding your muscles can really ache.

_source.definition_text: to succeed in doing something good, usually by working hard
_source.learnerexamples_text: She finally achieved her ambition to visit South America.; The government's training policy, he claimed, was achieving its objectives.; My father is a person who has achieved a lot of great things in his life.

_source.definition_text: something very good and difficult that you have succeeded in doing
_source.learnerexamples_text: An Olympic silver medal is a remarkable achievement for such a young athlete.; It gives you a sense of achievement if you actually make it to the end of a very long book.; I think this is an achievement because he is now a lawyer.

_source.definition_text: to accept that something is true or exists
_source.learnerexamples_text: He acknowledged that there was a problem.; They fully acknowledge the need to keep fit as a part of being a healthy and well-educated person.

_source.definition_text: a liquid substance which can react chemically with and sometimes dissolve other materials
_source.learnerexamples_text: hydrochloric/fatty acid; Vinegar is an acid.; We saw a little black dragon with scales like iron charging [at] us and spitting acid.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone, usually in writing, that you have received something they sent you
_source.learnerexamples_text: He sent a letter acknowledging receipt of her application.; Re: Follow-up job as interpreter, I acknowledge receipt of your recent correspondence.

_source.definition_text: someone who you know but do not know well
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's just a business acquaintance.; Should you not give us a printed apology, I would seriously consider recommending all my friends and acquaintances not to trust your future articles.

_source.definition_text: to get something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He acquired the firm in 1978.; I seem to have acquired two copies of this book.; I would like to join the club because I will be able to acquire more stamps for my collection.

_source.definition_text: to learn something
_source.learnerexamples_text: to acquire knowledge/skills; I have already acquired experience in the Tourism Field, working as a guard in a summer camp in Florida in 1997.

_source.definition_text: a unit for measuring area, equal to 4047 square metres
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's got 400 acres of land in Wales.; We have to admit that, not only because of the financial weakness but also because of the badly organized plans, we failed to achieve the planting of 10,000 trees per acre.

_source.definition_text: from one side of something to the other
_source.learnerexamples_text: She walked across the field/road.; They're building a new bridge across the river.; When I reached the river, I simply swam across.; My new phone is great. It is black with white lines going across it.

_source.definition_text: happening or having an effect on people at every level and in every area
_source.learnerexamples_text: The improvement has been across the board, with all divisions reporting increased profits.; Children in separate schools get on with things regardless of it being work for boys or girls, which can be quite positive especially in today's lifestyles where chores are done across the board.

_source.definition_text: on the opposite side of

_source.definition_text: doing a lot of things, or moving around a lot

_source.definition_text: the work of a group or organization to achieve an aim

_source.definition_text: to intentionally not do something

_source.definition_text: not sleeping

_source.definition_text: to be completely awake

_source.definition_text: to give money or a prize following an official decision
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was awarded the Nobel Prize for physics.; The university has awarded her a $500 travel grant.; As you will see, I was awarded a grade A.

_source.definition_text: a prize given to someone for something they have achieved
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Academy Award for Best Director; Both films have received/won several awards.; He became world-famous when he won the Oscar award for best song last year.

_source.definition_text: knowing that something exists, or having knowledge or experience of a particular thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Were you aware of the risks at the time?; I wasn't even aware that he was ill.; She was well aware that he was married.; I suddenly became aware of him looking at me.; First of all, we aren't aware of the necessity of learning such things as biology or maths.

_source.definition_text: when you know about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Environmental awareness is increasing all the time.; Thirdly, I have a strong awareness of issues which are important to my local community.

_source.definition_text: at a particular distance from a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: The nearest town was ten miles away.; The office is a half-hour drive away.; We live 5 km away from the coast.; I like it because its remote control could control distances [of] 1 or 2 meters away.

_source.definition_text: in a different place, position or situation

_source.definition_text: in or into the usual or a suitable place, especially one that can be closed

_source.definition_text: used after a verb to mean 'continuously or repeatedly'

_source.definition_text: gradually disappearing until mostly or completely gone
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the snow had melted away.; The music faded away as the procession moved slowly up the street.; I always feel so fatigued at the end of the day but after a mile, the aches of the day seem to fade away.

_source.definition_text: at a particular time in the future

_source.definition_text: If a sports team is playing away, the game is at the place where the other team usually plays.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were playing away.

_source.definition_text: a feeling of great respect and sometimes fear
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was filled with awe at the sheer size of the building.; As a child growing up, the presence of my grandmother filled me with awe.

_source.definition_text: to feel great respect for and sometimes fear of someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: As children we were rather in awe of our grandfather.; As I was the eldest of [the] siblings, they used to respect all my orders and [even] now, they are a bit in awe of me.

_source.definition_text: extremely good
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your new haircut is awesome.; My birthday party was awesome!

_source.definition_text: great or special and causing deep feelings of admiration, respect, or sometimes fear
_source.learnerexamples_text: an awesome achievement; The scenery was truly awesome.; Italy is crowded by groups sheepishly following their guide[s] in an awesome silence and respect.

_source.definition_text: a very large amount

_source.definition_text: difficult or causing problems or embarrassment

_source.definition_text: not relaxed or confident

_source.definition_text: a very young child
_source.learnerexamples_text: a baby boy/girl ; baby clothes ; Sandra had a baby on May 29th.; Every day Elisa go[es] to work, make[s] dinner for her little baby and watch[es] the T.V. with her husban[d].

_source.definition_text: a very young animal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a baby elephant/monkey; They would take us to see some baby sharks, dolphins, and w[h]ales.

_source.definition_text: to look after someone's child in their home while they are not there

_source.definition_text: where someone or something was before

_source.definition_text: as a reply or reaction to something

_source.definition_text: in a direction behind you

_source.definition_text: to the state something or someone was in before

_source.definition_text: in one direction, then the opposite way, then in the original direction again many times

_source.definition_text: the part of something that is furthest from the front or in the opposite direction to the front
_source.learnerexamples_text: He wrote her email address down on the back of an envelope.; Our seats were right at the back of the theatre.; My cousins love mermaids, so each sweater has one on the back.

_source.definition_text: the part of your body from your shoulders to your bottom
_source.learnerexamples_text: back injuries/pain ; I've got a bad back.; He lay on his back, staring at the ceiling.; The look on his face stopped me cold, as if someone had just poured freezing water down my back.

_source.definition_text: with the back part of something where the front should be
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've got your trousers on back to front.; Therefore, the government needs to cut expenditure and as a result of this, health faciliti[es] will only be accessible for rich people. Then we are back to front.

_source.learnerexamples_text: Have they been saying things about me behind my back?; The food must be perfect, too, or else her mother-in-law and my father's sisters will think that she's not a proper wife, and will probably say insulting things about her behind her back.

_source.definition_text: to decide to stop having contact with someone or something, or to refuse to help someone

_source.base_text: be (like) water off a duck's back

_source.definition_text: a very small road or street that goes behind or between buildings

_source.definition_text: at or near the back of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a back door/garden ; the back page/seat; I put it in the back pocket of my jeans.; There are two movies, but one is for adults so we will see "The back garden".

_source.definition_text: to move backwards or drive backwards

_source.definition_text: to give support or help to a person, plan, or idea

_source.base_text: back up sb or back sb up

_source.base_text: back up sth or back sth up

_source.definition_text: pain in your back

It was my boyfriend apologizing for his bad behaviour at the party we had had the night before.

_source.definition_text: very serious or severe

_source.definition_text: not lucky, or not happening how you would like

_source.definition_text: the ground at the bottom of the sea, a river, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: the sea bed; They landed upside down on a river bed and almost everyone was killed during the fall.

_source.definition_text: a piece of ground that is used for growing plants, especially flowers
_source.learnerexamples_text: a flower bed; Having lived in a small town in a cosy detached house with [a] flower bed in front and [an] enormous garden at the back, I was [as] happy as [I'd] ever [been].

_source.definition_text: a room used for sleeping in
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our home has three bedrooms.; I think my T-shirt is in your bedroom.

_source.definition_text: a yellow and black flying insect which makes honey and can sting you
_source.learnerexamples_text: A swarm of bees flew into the garden.; I was stung by a bee.; Did you know that bees are endangered?

_source.definition_text: the meat of a cow
_source.learnerexamples_text: roast beef; They like eating beef, lamb and salad.

_source.definition_text: an alcoholic drink made from grain
_source.learnerexamples_text: a pint of beer; Would you like another beer?; This beer is brewed in Mexico.; She likes drink[ing] beer and sometimes goes to the nightclub.

_source.definition_text: earlier than something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: two days before the summer holidays; She arrived before me.; You should always wash your hands before meals.; Think hard before accepting the offer.; We will come before 7 o'clock and help you with dinner.

_source.definition_text: at a place that you arrive at first when travelling towards another place
_source.learnerexamples_text: The hospital is just before the bridge.; Drivers've got often a problem with finding some space and there is another problem - the car park is open just until 8 pm, so the better thin[g] to do is leave a car in car park before the city centre.

_source.definition_text: in a position in front of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've never performed this before an audience.

_source.definition_text: in front of someone or something in an order or a list
_source.learnerexamples_text: The letter K comes before L in the English alphabet.

_source.definition_text: treated as more important than someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They always put the children's needs before their own.; She puts people with their needs before her own comfort, that is why she is successful.

_source.definition_text: earlier than the time when something happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was a teacher before he became famous.; Before he could reach the door, she quickly closed it.; Before we make a decision, does anyone want to say anything else?; I think the notebook is in your bedroom. I was studying there before I left your home.

_source.definition_text: in order to avoid something bad happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: Put that stick down before you hurt someone!

_source.definition_text: very soon
_source.learnerexamples_text: We'll be there before you know it.; It is a bit dark inside and especially in winter, it is dark before you know it.

_source.definition_text: until (the event mentioned)
_source.learnerexamples_text: It took a few moments before I realized that he was joking.

_source.definition_text: a long period of time before something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was a vegetarian long before I met Sally.; The cups belonged to my family long before I was born and the fact they are [a] part of my family tradition makes them valuable in my eyes.

_source.definition_text: at an earlier time, or on a previous occasion
_source.learnerexamples_text: He said he had never seen her before.; I feel as though I've been here before.; My father never b[ought me] any birthday presents before.

_source.definition_text: to ask someone for food or money, because you do not have any
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are more and more homeless people begging on the streets these days.; She had to beg for money and food for her children.; He had [a] shabby coat, old shoes and he was begging for money.

_source.definition_text: to make a very strong and urgent request
_source.learnerexamples_text: They begged for mercy.; "Please, please forgive me!" she begged (him).; He begged her to stay.; But before she left I begged her not to tell anybody.

_source.definition_text: to start to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The children began to cry.; Have they begun building the new bridge yet?; We began to talk about music.

_source.definition_text: to start to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: What time does the concert begin?; The film they want to watch begins at seven.; I think the class began yesterday.

_source.definition_text: to have something at the start
_source.learnerexamples_text: The word 'cat' begins with the letter 'c'.

_source.definition_text: at the start of a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: To begin with, the two girls got on well.; It wasn't stunningly beautiful, but a bed and a bathroom is really all we need[ed] to begin with!

_source.definition_text: used to give the first important reason for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: To begin with, we can't afford to move.; To begin with, it doesn't pollute and I think it's time we started thinking about [the] environment.

_source.definition_text: someone who is starting to do or learn something for the first time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm a complete beginner at yoga.; This judo class is for beginners only.; The book must have the vo[cabulary] for [a] beginner.

_source.definition_text: the first part of something or the start of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We met at the beginning of 1998.; She sat down and read the book straight through from beginning to end.; I enjoyed my job at/in the beginning, but I'm bored with it now.; At the beginning of the party, we danced and sang.

_source.base_text: on behalf of sb or on sb's behalf
_source.definition_text: If you do something on behalf of someone, you do it for them or instead of them.
_source.searchterms_text: behalf;behalfs;on behalf of sb or on sb's behalf
_source.learnerexamples_text: On behalf of the entire company, I would like to thank you for all your work.; Unfortunately, George cannot be with us today so I am pleased to accept this award on his behalf.; I am writing on behalf of our college English club members to welcome you [to] our city.

_source.definition_text: to do or say things in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She always behaves badly at bedtime.; He's been behaving very strangely recently.; You behaved like an idiot!; As always, I'll behave like a gentleman.

_source.definition_text: to be polite and not make a situation difficult
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did the children behave (themselves)?; Team sports can also help children to behave themselves.

_source.definition_text: the way that you behave
_source.learnerexamples_text: bad/good behaviour; Her behaviour was appalling.; Did you notice anything strange about his behaviour?; I was on the beach when my mobile phone rang. It was my boyfriend apologizing for his bad behaviour at the party we had had the night before.

_source.definition_text: slower or less successful than someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The project is already behind schedule.; Arsenal are six points behind Manchester United with three matches still to play.; Secondly, the show did not start until 20:15 pm. That was almost one hour behind schedule.

_source.definition_text: at or to the back of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Close the door behind you.; Their office is behind the main building.; I think [we should meet] in front of the restaurant, behind the library.

_source.definition_text: giving your help or support to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: The group is 100 percent behind her.; He is very nice because if you have problems he is always behind you to help you.

_source.definition_text: in prison
_source.learnerexamples_text: He will spend the rest of his life behind bars.; In the darkness, Lew Kuan Yee had sworn revenge against Michael, the detective who had sent him behind bars.

_source.definition_text: If a bad experience or your own bad behaviour is behind you, it does not exist or affect your life now.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's put his criminal past behind him.; We have got to put the past behind us.

_source.definition_text: causing something, or responsible for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: What was the reason behind her decision to leave?; Another reason behind this kind of thinking is that some boys feel a[w]kward when they see girls and they think they are being ignored in the class.

_source.definition_text: If you do something behind someone's back, you do it without them knowing, often in an unfair way.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have they been saying things about me behind my back?; The food must be perfect, too, or else her mother-in-law and my father's sisters will think that she's not a proper wife, and will probably say insulting things about her behind her back.

_source.definition_text: If something happens behind the scenes, it happens secretly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: A lot of hard work has been going on behind the scenes.; Ms. Bolam knew a lot of things going on behind the scenes, [which were] not [known to] the patients.

_source.definition_text: privately and not in public
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most of the deals were done behind closed doors.; Decisions which affect the whole world are made behind closed doors and are top secret.

_source.definition_text: in the place where someone or something was before
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was annoyed to discover that I'd left my bag behind.; After the party a few people stayed behind to help clear up.; The bus driver told him that a suitcase was left behind because nobody claimed it.

_source.definition_text: at or to the back of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Somebody grabbed me from behind.; An old man appeared from behind wearing the same clothes [as] the owner of the phone and asked [her] for it.

_source.definition_text: not fashionable or modern
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dad's a bit behind the times.; We [should] improve our equipment. Otherwise we will be behind the times.

_source.definition_text: slower or later than someone else, or than you should be
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's behind with the rent.; Those children who do not get this at home are the ones who are behind in their schoolwork.

_source.definition_text: to start to exist
_source.learnerexamples_text: The new law comes into being next month. ; Only with knowledge of the written word were villages able to organise themselves in larger forms of government, leading from local to regional to national levels, [and] finally leading to transnational structures as they came into being mostly during the last 100 years.

_source.definition_text: when you believe that something is true or real
_source.learnerexamples_text: a common/popular/widely-held belief; He called at her house in the belief that she would lend him the money.; It is my firm/strong belief that the public have a right to know. ; She took this medicine in the mistaken belief that it would cure her.; At this time, tango was considered an immoral type of music; but Carlos Gardel changed this belief, [and] people from all over the world loved him.

_source.definition_text: the feeling that someone or something is effective or right
_source.learnerexamples_text: a belief in social justice; I'll try to give my children a feeling of security within themselves and a belief in themselves, so that they will be able to stand up [to] danger in society.

_source.definition_text: an idea that you are certain is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: All non-violent religious and political beliefs should be respected equally.; We get to know the beliefs, superstitions or the principles of other religious denominations.

_source.definition_text: too bad, good, difficult, etc. to be real
_source.learnerexamples_text: The evil of this man is beyond belief.; I completely agree with the idea that homelessness in the third world is increasing to rates beyond belief.

_source.definition_text: to think that something is true, or that what someone says is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: They believe that their health has suffered because of the chemicals.; I can't believe that she wants to go out with me.; I told you she was there but you wouldn't believe me.; I believe him.

_source.definition_text: to think something, without being completely sure
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Is she coming alone?" "I believe so."; All the crew are missing, believed dead.; I believe it is in your bedroom.

_source.definition_text: to be very surprised when you see someone or something, or when you hear what someone says
_source.learnerexamples_text: I couldn't believe my ears when Dan said they were getting married.; Well, this church was extremely simple [o]n the outside, but when I got inside it, I couldn't believe my eyes.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something is true although it seems surprising
_source.learnerexamples_text: He even remembered my birthday, believe it or not.; First I visited the "Roman Bath'' which is more than 2000 years old and, believe it or not, it still works!

_source.definition_text: to be certain that something exists
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you believe in ghosts?; Claire I want to tell you that we have to believe in miracles!

_source.definition_text: to be confident that something is effective and right
_source.searchterms_text: believe;believe in sth/doing sth;believe in sth/doing sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He believes in saying what he thinks.; Nowadays I don't believe in changing your decision.

_source.definition_text: a hollow, metal object, shaped like a cup, that makes a ringing sound when you hit it
_source.learnerexamples_text: the sound of church bells ringing ; At the begin[n]ing I was very excited, living in an old house, not too far from the city (you could still hear the church bells chiming) but far enough [away] to live your own life without nosy neighbours.

_source.definition_text: an electrical object that makes a ringing sound when you press a button
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please ring the bell for attention.; I was relaxing at home when suddenly the bell rang.

_source.definition_text: If a word, especially a name, rings a bell, you think you have heard it before.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Shane Watson? That name rings a bell.; Its name is Laser - I suppose it rings a bell?

_source.definition_text: If something belongs somewhere, that is the place it should be in.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This table belongs in the sitting room.; These papers belong with the others.; I can understand people wh[o] say that animals belong in nature.

_source.definition_text: to feel happy or comfortable in a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: I spent two years in Oxford but I never felt that I belonged there.

_source.definition_text: If something belongs to you, you own it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This book belongs to Sarah.; You shouldn't take what doesn't belong to you.; I need it back because it belongs to my cousin.

_source.definition_text: to be a member of a group or organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: We belong to the same tennis club.; Also, I belonged to [a] golf club when I went to university in Japan.

_source.definition_text: in a lower position than someone or something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: From the top of the skyscraper the cars below us looked like insects.; Send your answers to the address below.; I think it's a nice place, because you have a great view of the other mountains and the country below you.

_source.definition_text: the things that a person owns, especially those which can be carried
_source.learnerexamples_text: I put a few personal belongings in a bag and left the house for the last time.; Five different kings have lived there with their families and it is possible to see several of their personal belongings.

_source.definition_text: less than a particular amount or level
_source.learnerexamples_text: His marks in English have been below average for some time now.; The temperature has fallen below zero/freezing recently.; We have to learn that [it] is not natural for a lion [to be] living in a country where, in winter, [the] temperature can fall below zero.

_source.definition_text: lower in rank
_source.learnerexamples_text: Monica is a grade below me.; [With] him being only 37 years old and [having] been promoted to the second level below the board of directors of a well-known international company, he seems like a good example [of] a successful person, at least in this area of success.

_source.definition_text: a long, thin piece of leather, cloth, or plastic that you wear around your waist
_source.learnerexamples_text: She fastened her belt tightly around her waist.; He had eaten so much that he had to undo his belt.; Juliana gave me a pink belt.

_source.definition_text: to try to spend less money
_source.learnerexamples_text: Since I lost my job we've all had to tighten our belts.; All this costs money and where do we get this extra money from but from the tax payers, who once again have to tighten their belts.

_source.definition_text: to move your body or part of your body so that it is not straight
_source.learnerexamples_text: Bend your knees when lifting heavy objects.; She bent down to pick up the pen.; Now, bend forwards/over and touch your toes!; My friend was bending over the table laughing hysterically.

_source.definition_text: a long seat for two or more people, usually made of wood or metal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a park bench; At 1 p.m. Paul was sitting on a bench and waiting for Julia.

_source.definition_text: to (cause to) curve
_source.learnerexamples_text: The road bends to the left after the first set of traffic lights.; The trees were bending in the wind.; I saw fir trees bending in half and 500-year-old oaks shedding their leaves.

_source.definition_text: a curved part of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's a bend in the pipe so you can't see from one end to the other.; There's a sharp bend in the road.; The other car disappeared around a sharp bend and when we came round it, we saw that the car had stopped in the middle of the road.

_source.definition_text: to make someone very angry, especially by continuing to do something annoying
_source.learnerexamples_text: This computer is driving me round the bend.; I could not work with a beginner as it would drive me round the bend if I was interrupted every few minutes and asked to elucidate to him/her something as easy as pie.

_source.definition_text: under something, or in a lower position than something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Jeremy hid the letter beneath a pile of papers.; After weeks at sea, it was wonderful to feel firm ground beneath our feet once more.; She could feel the train coming because the ground beneath her feet was moving.

_source.definition_text: If someone or something is beneath you, you think you are too important or from too high a social class to spend time on them.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He thinks housework is beneath him.; He hadn't realised how much he would miss the high-life until he was forced to watch all the rich and famous people come into the restaurant and look down [on] everything and everyone who was beneath them.

_source.definition_text: If it is beneath your dignity to do something, you think you are too important or from too high a class to do it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She felt that it was beneath her dignity to wear a name badge.; He thought it was beneath his dignity to talk about his master's decisions and ideas.

_source.definition_text: helpful, useful or good
_source.learnerexamples_text: The improvement in sales figures had a beneficial effect on the company as a whole.; Exercise is beneficial to almost everyone.; To sum up, team sports are beneficial to children so if the schools they attend do not have any, they should take up [something].

_source.definition_text: something that helps you or gives you an advantage
_source.learnerexamples_text: The discovery of oil brought many benefits to the town.; One of the many benefits of foreign travel is learning how to cope with the unexpected.; He's had the benefit of an expensive education and yet he continues to work as a waiter.; Taking everything [into] account, the drawbacks far outweigh its benefits.

_source.definition_text: in order to help someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: We bought the piano for the children's benefit.; Needless to say, I hope you take [all this] into consideration not only for Gustavo's benefit, but also for the benefit of the astronaut training programme and the world.

_source.base_text: give sb the benefit of the doubt
_source.definition_text: to choose to believe what someone tells you even though it may be wrong or a lie
_source.searchterms_text: benefit;benefits;give sb the benefit of the doubt
_source.learnerexamples_text: She says her train was late, so I suppose we'd better give her the benefit of the doubt.; Every time our parents tell us ".. have you thought about it, are you sure you are not making a mistake?" we just answer "sure I have, no problem." Next time they do, let's give them the benefit of the doubt and let's think twice about the subject.

_source.definition_text: to be helped by something or to help someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: I feel that I have benefited greatly from her experience.; How can we benefit those who most need our help?; I am sure that the café would benefit a great deal from a non-smoking-area.

_source.definition_text: a small round fruit on particular plants and trees
_source.learnerexamples_text: I usually scatter a few berries on my muesli.; Every day we were swimming, fishing, picking mushro[om]s and berries, hunting and making fires to prepare food.

_source.definition_text: next to someone or something, or very near them
_source.learnerexamples_text: Come and sit here beside me.; Our school was built right beside a river.; We shall go shopping after the film because the shopping complex is beside the cinema.

_source.definition_text: to experience a powerful emotion
_source.searchterms_text: be beside yourself (with sth);be beside yourself with sth;beside
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was beside himself with rage.; Spending one's spare time being beside oneself with anger scarcely ever makes holidays [enjoy]able.

_source.definition_text: not important or not connected with what you are talking about
_source.learnerexamples_text: The fact that he doesn't want to come is beside the point - he should have been invited.

_source.definition_text: used to give another reason for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She won't mind your being late - besides, it's hardly your fault.; I think that I'm going to buy "Troy" because it looks to me [to be] a great movie - besides, it reminds me of your vacations in Mexico.

_source.definition_text: in addition to something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you play any other sports besides football and basketball?; It's a Chinese food buffet but besides Chinese food they also have Italian food like pizza.

_source.definition_text: in addition to
_source.learnerexamples_text: Besides looking after the children, she runs a successful business.; But besides playing, you can also sit [i]n the "club lounge", where you can drink something with your friends or just play cards.

_source.definition_text: (superlative of good) better than any other
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was my best friend.; This is the best meal I've ever had.; He's one of our best students.; Are you sure this is the best way of doing it?; Your parents only want what is best for you.

_source.definition_text: something that you write at the end of a letter
_source.learnerexamples_text: With best wishes, Anna; With best wishes,

_source.definition_text: the thing that is best, if you cannot have or do the thing you really want
_source.searchterms_text: best;next best thing;the next best thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Coaching football is the next best thing to playing.; For many working people, there is hardly time to cook and prepare your dinner, so the next best thing is to rush into a Macdonalds' or Burger King.

_source.definition_text: Someone’s best bet is the action most likely to be successful.
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you want to get to the theater on time, your best bet is to get a cab.; The international cuisine chef can whip up some delicious creations from time to time; but your best bet is to go for one of the delicious steaks served.

_source.definition_text: (superlative ofwell) in the most suitable or satisfactory way
_source.learnerexamples_text: I sleep best with the window open.; The Grand Canyon is best seen at sunset when it seems to change colour.; It would be best if you c[a]me on Wednesday 27th.

_source.definition_text: (superlative ofwell) most, or more than any other
_source.learnerexamples_text: Which of the songs did you like best?; They were the best-dressed couple at the party.; I like Australia best.

_source.definition_text: to be the most suitable person to have responsibility and make important decisions
_source.learnerexamples_text: When it comes to dealing with my own son, I think I know best.; How true is that expression "Father knows best". If my father [was alive] today he would probably be laughing his head off.

_source.definition_text: someone or something that is better than any other
_source.learnerexamples_text: I like all of Hitchcock's films, but I think 'Notorious' is the best.; Chris and I are the best of friends.; The trip was the best I have ever been [on] in my life.

_source.definition_text: used to say that you hope someone will be happy, healthy, successful, etc., often when saying goodbye
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the best, then - it was nice to meet you!; Please wish him all the best for his new job.; I want to wish you all the best!

_source.definition_text: at the highest level of achievement or quality
_source.searchterms_text: at his/its etc best;at his/its, etc. best;best
_source.learnerexamples_text: The article is an example of journalism at its best.; I enjoyed this trip because we got to stay in the countryside and [see] nature at its very best.

_source.definition_text: to make the greatest effort possible
_source.learnerexamples_text: I did my best to persuade him.; And the police said that they will try their best.

_source.definition_text: to try to be positive about a situation you do not like but cannot change
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our hotel room is rather small, but we'll just have to make the best of it.; Unfortunately I don't have very much spare time so we will have to arrange it carefully in order to make the best of your time in London.

_source.definition_text: to have the advantages of two different situations
_source.searchterms_text: (have) the best of both worlds;best;have the best of both worlds
_source.learnerexamples_text: Living in the country and working in the city you have the best of both worlds.; Only those that can afford to live in the suburban areas can combine the best of both worlds and they tend to be rather affluent.

_source.definition_text: used to show that the most positive way of considering something is still not good
_source.learnerexamples_text: At best, only 50 per cent of babies born at 24 weeks will survive.;  Then, due to the social standards, the old find themselves being abandoned and helpless. At best, such people are hospitalized.

_source.definition_text: If something is for the best, it seems unpleasant now, but will improve a situation in the future.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Divorce is always painful, but it really was for the best.; It's a kind of sad thing to think about but maybe it's for the best.

_source.base_text: bring out the best in sb
_source.definition_text: to cause someone's best qualities to show
_source.searchterms_text: best;bring out the best in sb
_source.learnerexamples_text: This chance to work with young people has really brought out the best in him.; TV can be a baby-sitter, but such a relationship is not going to bring out the best in a child.

_source.definition_text: used to show that something is not good when it is the best it can be
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's not exactly patient at the best of times.; They knew that even at the best of times he looked unpleasant but now he was of [a] completely different [appearance].

_source.definition_text: something that you say to show that you believe that something is true or will happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: I bet you she's missed the bus.; I bet that he won't come.; The movie is amazing. I bet you'll see it soon.

_source.definition_text: a very popular book that many people have bought
_source.learnerexamples_text: His latest book is likely to be another bestseller.; Maybe your parents could bring me one of the newest bestsellers, which haven't been translated [in]to Polish yet.

_source.definition_text: when you risk money on the result of a game, competition, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She won her bet.; He put a bet on Manchester United winning on Saturday.; A couple of betting shops attract many people, mostly men, who often come in a hurry to place a bet, some of them in their working uniform with a large apron.

_source.definition_text: to risk money on the result of a game, competition, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He lost all his money betting on horses.; I bet him a dollar that I was right.; The game lost its innocence long before 1985 when players were betting on the result of their own game.

_source.definition_text: the best decision or choice
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your best bet in terms of value would be the Regent Hotel.; The international cuisine chef can whip up some delicious creations from time to time; but your best bet is to go for one of the delicious steaks served [there].

_source.definition_text: something that you are certain will happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: Wheeler is a safe bet for a place on the team.; Automatically, we think that black is a safe bet for any occasion.

_source.definition_text: to behave in a dishonest or cruel way to someone who trusts you
_source.learnerexamples_text: She felt betrayed by her mother's lack of support.; He promised never to betray her.; He couldn't believe that his best friend had betrayed him.

_source.definition_text: (comparative of good) of a higher quality, more effective, or more enjoyable than something or someone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's found a better job.; The film was better than I expected.; She is much better at tennis than I am.; If you cook it this way it's far better.; Relations between the two countries have never been better.

_source.definition_text: healthy, or less ill than before
