_source.learnerexamples_text: Sarah bounced into the room with a big smile on her face.; Would you like to wear balloon clothes and bounce around the world?

_source.definition_text: to (cause to) move up or away after hitting a surface
_source.learnerexamples_text: The ball bounced off the post and into the net.; She bounced the ball quickly.

_source.definition_text: to start to be successful again after a difficult period
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stock prices bounced back after a steep plunge earlier this week.; After a terrible start the team bounced back and won the game.; The figures reflecting the number of tonnes carried by the rail network had initially fallen in the nineteen eighties and nineteen nineties by about 40 per cent but then bounced back by the begin[n]ing of the new century.

_source.definition_text: If an email bounces back, it is returned to you because the address is not correct or there is a computer problem.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tried to send you an email, but it bounced back.

_source.definition_text: travelling towards a particular place
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was on a train bound for Berlin.; The only risk you run is [gett]ing on a bus bound for Boras, so take care you avoid this one.

_source.definition_text: certain to do something, or certain to happen
_source.searchterms_text: bound to do sth;bound;bound to do sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: You're bound to feel nervous before your driving test.; If you're stressed for a long period, it's bound to affect your health.; I'm bound to feel nervous.

_source.definition_text: closely connected with something
_source.learnerexamples_text: A country's culture is bound up with its language and history.; It's just the way of the world, I will have to say, and convince myself that I am not as inextricably bound up with that particular diary.

_source.definition_text: a limit
_source.learnerexamples_text: Such violence is beyond the boundaries of civilized conduct. ; This is a movie that reminds us that a man's soul cannot be measured with a measuring tape, that passion knows no boundaries, and that love accepts no defeat.

_source.definition_text: a line that divides two areas or forms an edge around an area
_source.learnerexamples_text: The mountains mark the boundary between the two countries. ; This gives youngsters the opportunity to exchange opinions with people all over the world, and so the boundaries of the countries or the continents have less meaning.

_source.definition_text: a piece of curved wood with string fixed to both ends, used for shooting arrows
_source.learnerexamples_text: a bow and arrows; The bow was very beautiful and there were some letters on [it]: Artemis. He could not believe it, he had the bow of Artemis.

_source.definition_text: a knot with two curved parts and two loose ends, that is used to tie shoes or as decoration
_source.learnerexamples_text: The present was wrapped in gold paper and tied with a big red bow.; He saw a big black bow [o]n the handle of the door.

_source.definition_text: a round, deep dish used for holding soup and other food
_source.learnerexamples_text: a bowl of soup; a soup/cereal/salad/sugar bowl; Sift the flour and baking powder into a mixing bowl.; We also used to complain [about] the fact that we had to have a bowl of soup every single day.

_source.definition_text: a long, thin piece of wood with hair stretched between the ends, used to play some musical instruments
_source.learnerexamples_text: a violin bow; The feeling was, moreover, enhanced by his unique style, as for instance [with] the guitar solo on "Dazed and confused", played with a violin bow.

_source.definition_text: a square or rectangular container
_source.learnerexamples_text: a cardboard box; a box of chocolates; I got clothes and a box of chocolates.

_source.definition_text: a sport in which two competitors fight by hitting each other with their hands
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many doctors believe that boxing is too dangerous and should be banned.; He's a former world heavyweight boxing champion.; You can do gym, boxing, squash, [and] tennis.

_source.definition_text: a small square on a page that gives you information or where you write information
_source.learnerexamples_text: Choose an adjective from the box to complete each sentence.; If you would like more information, tick this box.

_source.definition_text: a male child or young man
_source.learnerexamples_text: a teenage boy; You've been a very naughty boy!; All right, boys and girls, quiet now!; I hope it's a boy.

_source.definition_text: a man or boy who someone is having a romantic relationship with
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's not my boyfriend - we're just good friends!; Cathy's ex-boyfriend was a really nice guy.; Maria and her boyfriend gave me a wonderful mirror.

_source.definition_text: a piece of women's underwear that supports the breasts
_source.learnerexamples_text: She knew that I had bought my first bra without having asked her for advice.

_source.definition_text: a piece of jewellery that you wear around your wrist
_source.learnerexamples_text: a gold/silver/diamond bracelet; Actually I was very sad as the bracelet was particularly valuable to me.

_source.definition_text: either of two symbols put around a word, phrase or sentence in a piece of writing to show that what is between them should be considered as separate from the main part
_source.learnerexamples_text: square/round brackets; Biographical information is included in brackets.

_source.definition_text: a group of people whose ages, taxes, etc are between two limits
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most heart attack victims are in the 45-65 age bracket.; The 35-49 age bracket remained constant in terms of cinema attendance and [the] same also with the 50+ age bracket.

_source.definition_text: the organ inside your head that controls thought, memory, feelings and activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: Doctors can measure activity in her brain.; The accident left him with permanent brain damage.; His wife died from a brain tumour.; He said the Martians opened his head and [did] experi[ments] with his brain.

_source.definition_text: the part of a vehicle that makes it stop or move more slowly
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had no brakes on her bicycle.; It has 24 active gears and multilink kevlor brakes.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to intelligence
_source.learnerexamples_text: That can't possibly be the right way to do it - use your brain!; He's got brains but he's too lazy to use them.; The whole [of] Western society already seems to be founded on computers and relying on chips, which to a certain extent has taken away our own abilities of using our brains.

_source.definition_text: to make a vehicle stop or move more slowly
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tried to brake but it was too late. ; The motorcyclist cut in dangerously, so we had to brake.

_source.definition_text: one of the many parts of a tree that grows out from its trunk
_source.learnerexamples_text: Birds often make nests in the top branches of the tree. ; She slowly climbed the tree and sat on one of the biggest branches.

_source.definition_text: one of several shops, offices, etc. that are part of a company or organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: I used to work in the local branch of a large bank.; She's a branch manager.; He has come from our branch office in New York, where he worked as [an] assistant.

_source.definition_text: a part of a subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: Immunology is a branch of biological science.; As a matter of fact, in[n]ovations have taken place quite frequently in every branch of science.

_source.definition_text: completely new
_source.learnerexamples_text: The washing machine is brand new.; Well, I've decided to buy a new TV set and a brand new sofa!

_source.definition_text: a type of product made by a particular company
_source.learnerexamples_text: a best-selling/popular brand of toothpaste; This isn't my usual brand of deodorant.; My computer brand is Acer.

_source.definition_text: the group of musical instruments made from brass
_source.learnerexamples_text: a brass band ; I liked it so much that I decided to become a brass band musician myself.

_source.definition_text: a shiny yellow metal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a door with a brass handle ; The dark marble is easy to keep clean and the solid brass handles look luxur[ious].

_source.definition_text: in a brave way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She faced the consequences bravely.

_source.definition_text: showing no fear of dangerous or difficult situations
_source.learnerexamples_text: a brave soldier; It was a brave decision to leave her job and start her own business.; She was very brave to learn to ski at fifty.; Of the three organizations criticized, only one was brave enough to face the press.; Richards has made a brave attempt to answer his critics.

_source.definition_text: a basic food made by mixing flour, water and sometimes yeast
_source.learnerexamples_text: a slice of bread; a loaf of bread;  white/brown bread;  sliced bread;  fresh/stale bread

_source.definition_text: when someone is brave
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was awarded a medal for his bravery in battle.; Of course my bravery disappeared and I felt my heart beating faster and faster.

_source.definition_text: the great number of different things that someone has done, knows, is interested in, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: breadth;breadths;sb's breadth of experience/knowledge/interest etc;sb's breadth of experience/knowledge/interest, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her novels show her huge breadth of knowledge.; In my opinion, it is irresponsible to base our knowledge only on our experience and to overlook the example of all those who, with their breadth of learning, made amazing innovations and helped society.

_source.base_text: the length and breadth of sth
_source.definition_text: in every part of a place
_source.searchterms_text: breadth;breadths;length and breadth of sth;the length and breadth of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: They travelled the length and breadth of Scotland together.; It is the reason that we can easily see the foreigners wandering [the] length and breadth [of] the museum being unaware of the origin of items they look at.

_source.definition_text: to separate into two or more pieces or to make something do this
_source.learnerexamples_text: The dish fell to the floor and broke.; They had to break a window to get in.; I dropped the vase and it broke into pieces.; I broke a beautiful glass.

_source.definition_text: If you break a machine, object, etc., or if it breaks, it stops working because it is damaged.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think I've broken your camera.; I'd like [a new mobile phone] because the other one ha[s] broken.

_source.definition_text: to damage a bone in your arm/leg, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: break;break your arm/leg etc;break your arm/leg, etc.;breaking;breaks;broke;broken
_source.learnerexamples_text: Barbara slipped on the ice and broke her arm.; I['m] sell[ing] my bicycle because I broke my leg.

_source.definition_text: to come to an end or make something come to an end
_source.learnerexamples_text: Eventually someone spoke, breaking the silence.; The factory brought in outside workers in an attempt to break the strike.; George was looking outside when something broke the silence.

_source.definition_text: to stop doing something for a short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's break for lunch.; If you sit at a desk all day, try to break your routine with a walk or a swim.; I think the most important aim of a holiday is to break your daily routine.

_source.definition_text: to not do what you should do
_source.searchterms_text: break;break an agreement/promise etc;break an agreement/promise, etc.;breaking;breaks;broke;broken
_source.learnerexamples_text: She agreed not to tell anyone but she has broken her promise.; I am very surprised that such a reputable theatre [as] yours has been able to break all [the] promises that appeared in the advertisement.

_source.definition_text: to do something better, faster, etc. than anyone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: Usain Bolt broke the world record for the 200 metres.; I personally think that nobody will ever break his record of being champion seven times.

_source.definition_text: to do something illegal
_source.learnerexamples_text: He didn't know he was breaking the law by smoking inside the building.; Jem, the youngest brother, is a horse-thief, so he breaks the law as well, but his crime is a minor one.

_source.definition_text: to make people feel more relaxed in a social situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: I told everyone a joke, which helped to break the ice.; And, of course, don't forget that a warm smile is one of the best ways to break the ice.

_source.definition_text: to make someone feel extremely sad
_source.learnerexamples_text: She really broke his heart when she left.; It breaks my heart when I hear the terrible things that have been said about him.; I thought that the hamster would live forever but I was wrong and that mistake broke my heart.

_source.definition_text: to not make money but also not lose money
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company only managed to break even this year.; Company C does not seem to be doing well. In the year 2000, it just seems to be breaking even.

_source.definition_text: If news or a story breaks, or if someone breaks it, it becomes known by the public for the first time.
_source.learnerexamples_text: News of the scandal broke just before the election.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone about something unpleasant that has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: Who's going to break the news to his wife?; She broke the news to his wife Helen.

_source.definition_text: to suddenly escape or become separate from something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The prisoner broke free while the guards weren't looking.

_source.definition_text: to escape from someone or something that is controlling you
_source.learnerexamples_text: She tried to break free from the social conditioning of her upbringing.; I would like to revisit there one day as it's firmly connected to my ad[o]lescence, when I struggled to break free from my peers, [and] tried to establish my own identity.

_source.definition_text: If a storm breaks, it starts suddenly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The storm broke just as we reached home.; Suddenly the moon disappeared behind the clouds and, in a few moments, a violent storm broke.

_source.definition_text: If the weather breaks, it changes suddenly, and usually becomes worse.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The weather is due to break at the weekend.

_source.definition_text: If a machine or vehicle breaks down, it stops working.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our car broke down and we had to push it off the road.; I'm just writing to tell you why I [need to] borrow your bicycle, because I am going to go [to] my farm next week and my car has broken down.

_source.definition_text: to do something that is different to anything that has been done before
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their research is really breaking new ground.; Paul decided to break new ground in music no matter how long it took.

_source.base_text: break in or break into sth
_source.definition_text: to get into a building or car using force, usually to steal something
_source.searchterms_text: break;break in or break into sth;break in or break into sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: The burglars broke in through the kitchen window.; My car's been broken into twice this month.; I even thought a burglar might have broken into my house and was going to kill me.

_source.definition_text: to end (something) suddenly
_source.searchterms_text: break;break off (sth) or break (sth) off;break off sth or break sth off
_source.learnerexamples_text: She broke off in the middle of a sentence.; She broke off the engagement just two weeks before the wedding.; As you remember, my car didn't work as well as it should and I had to break off my [trip].

_source.definition_text: If something dangerous or unpleasant breaks out, it suddenly starts.
_source.learnerexamples_text: War broke out in 1914.; The fire broke out in the early morning.; Fighting has broken out all over the city.; Unfortunately everything was stopped because [the] Second World War broke out.

_source.definition_text: to force your way through something that is holding you back
_source.learnerexamples_text: Protesters broke through the barriers.; It broke through the ceiling and when she looked she saw [it was] a UFO.

_source.definition_text: When schools or colleges break up, the classes end and the holidays begin.
_source.learnerexamples_text: What date do we break up this year?; Summer is my favourite season, because schools break up for [the] holidays.

_source.definition_text: If two people break up, they stop having a relationship.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Jenny and George have broken up.; She's just broken up with her boyfriend.; The problem is that a few months ago, when he had broken up with me, I wanted him to feel jealous, so I started meeting with Fredo, a friend.

_source.definition_text: a holiday or period of time away from work, school, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a weekend break to Paris; He had a break for the weekend, and he called me: "I am in London, so, if you want to see me, it's the time!"

_source.definition_text: when you stop an activity for a short time, usually to rest or to eat
_source.learnerexamples_text: a coffee/lunch break; We'll take another break at 3.30.; They worked through the night without a break.; You must bring an old shirt, pencils, water and some food for the break.

_source.definition_text: a lucky opportunity
_source.learnerexamples_text: His big break came when he was offered a part in a TV series.; Meeting Tom was my lucky break.

_source.definition_text: where something has separated in an accident
_source.learnerexamples_text: a break in the bone

_source.definition_text: easy to break
_source.learnerexamples_text: That vase is breakable so be careful.

_source.definition_text: a short period of mental illness when people are too ill to continue with their normal lives
_source.learnerexamples_text: Later that year she had a breakdown.; a nervous breakdown; Instead of that I almost end[ed] up in hospital suffering [a] nervous breakdown.

_source.definition_text: when a vehicle or machine stops working for a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had a breakdown in the middle of the road.; On Friday we went to Scotland but unfortunately we had a breakdown. By chance a very nice farmer fixed our car and [as] it was late he suggested we should spend the night on his farm.

_source.definition_text: when something such as communication or a relationship fails or ends
_source.learnerexamples_text: a breakdown in the peace talks; Eventually, society may be affected by the breakdown of these relationships.

_source.definition_text: a short explanation of the details of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I need a breakdown of the costs involved.; The pie charts showing the breakdown of annual spending of the school take into account money spent on insurance, teachers' salaries, furniture and equipment, resources (such as books), and other workers' salaries.

_source.definition_text: the food you eat in the morning after you wake up
_source.learnerexamples_text: What do you want for breakfast?; Have you had breakfast?; Breakfast is served in the dining room between 8.30 and 10.; You can have breakfast in my house.

_source.definition_text: an important discovery or event that helps to improve a situation or provide an answer to a problem
_source.learnerexamples_text: Scientists are hoping for a breakthrough in the search for a cure for cancer.; A major breakthrough in negotiations has been achieved.; For me the main technology breakthrough has been in computers.

_source.definition_text: the air that goes into and out of your lungs
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her breath smelled of garlic.; Then I felt someone's breath on my shoulder...

_source.definition_text: either of the two soft, rounded parts of a woman's chest that produce milk after she has a baby
_source.learnerexamples_text: When a woman becomes pregnant her breasts tend to grow larger.; breast cancer; This person is so special to me because [after I was] born I was drinking milk from her breast.

_source.definition_text: to be breathing quickly because you have been running, walking fast, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He burst into the room, red-faced and out of breath.; I find that shopping is very good exercise too! By the time you have completed the whole High Street, you will be out of breath.

_source.definition_text: to keep air in your lungs and not let it out
_source.learnerexamples_text: How long can you hold your breath under water?; My heart was beating fast. I was holding my breath.

_source.definition_text: If something takes your breath away, you feel surprise and admiration because it is so beautiful or exciting.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The view from the window took my breath away.; The landscape just takes your breath away sometimes.

_source.base_text: catch your breath; get your breath back
_source.definition_text: to rest for a short time until you can breathe regularly again
_source.searchterms_text: breath;catch your breath get your breath back;catch your breath; get your breath back
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's stop here and catch our breath.; Unfortunately, the rooms we stayed in were on the 4th floor. The older people couldn't catch their breath when they finally arrived there!

_source.definition_text: to fill your lungs with air
_source.learnerexamples_text: Take a deep breath and relax.; But if you took a deep breath after reading the question, don't worry.

_source.definition_text: in an excited or anxious way
_source.learnerexamples_text: I waited with bated breath as the results were read out.; Nevertheless, a huge number of scientists carrying out very useful research, [and] composers, actors, [and] artists making us watch their creations with bated breath, do not earn [as much] money as a lot of outstanding sportsmen do.

_source.definition_text: If you say something under your breath, you say it very quietly so that other people cannot hear it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was muttering curses under his breath.; "We must have taken a wrong turn somewhere..." he kept muttering under his breath.

_source.definition_text: someone or something that is new, different, and exciting
_source.searchterms_text: a breath of fresh air;breath;breath of fresh air
_source.learnerexamples_text: Having Eve around has been a breath of fresh air.; The final suggestion is focused on building a leisure centre. Should this be everything the Town Council has promised, it will bring a breath of fresh air.

_source.definition_text: to wait for something to happen, often feeling anxious
_source.learnerexamples_text: While the leaders negotiated, the world held its breath.; They, the critics, the fans and friends and his wife, held their breath and crossed their fingers, hoping to once again hear his enchanting voice.

_source.definition_text: very beautiful or surprising
_source.learnerexamples_text: breathtaking scenery/views; For me it is a very beautiful country, with amazing and breathtaking scenery.

_source.definition_text: to take air into and out of your lungs
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's so airless in here - I can hardly breathe.; Breathe in and now breathe out.; Keep breathing deeply.; The air you will breathe is cleaner than the air in the city.

_source.definition_text: to keep animals for the purpose of producing young animals
_source.learnerexamples_text: His main income comes from breeding cattle.; We can keep animals, breed them, observe, and protect [them].

_source.definition_text: to cause something to develop, especially something bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: He believes that movies like this breed violence.; The question arises: who is right - those who love and cherish history or those for whom the above-mentioned familiarity breeds contempt?

_source.definition_text: a type of dog, sheep, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This rare breed of sheep is particularly good for wool.; What's your favourite breed of dog/dog breed?; After she had seen pictures of the show animals, she de[c]ided to buy a small male kitten of the Cornish rex breed.

_source.definition_text: a light and pleasant wind
_source.learnerexamples_text: a cool breeze; She let the gentle breeze cool her face.; It was not that hot and we had a cool breeze as we cycled downhill.

_source.definition_text: money or a present given to someone so that they will do something for you, usually something dishonest
_source.learnerexamples_text: The politician was accused of accepting bribes from businessmen. ; Because we don't like to wait, it is very common to jump in the queues or give bribes to people in charge.

_source.definition_text: to try to make someone do something for you by giving them money, presents or something else they want
_source.learnerexamples_text: He bribed immigration officials and entered the country illegally.; She considers presents to be a means of bribing her in order to love you.

_source.definition_text: a small, hard, rectangular block used for building walls and houses
_source.learnerexamples_text: a brick wall; Future homes might not be built out of bricks at all!

_source.definition_text: when someone is offered money or a present so that they will do something, usually something dishonest
_source.learnerexamples_text: bribery and corruption; They treat bribery as something natural - as it was in the last political system.

_source.definition_text: a woman who is getting married
_source.learnerexamples_text: He returned from New York with his lovely new bride.; The bride and groom posed for pictures outside the church.; The day of the wedding, I took lots of pictures of the bride and the groom.

_source.definition_text: a structure that is built over a river, road, railway, etc. to allow people and vehicles to cross from one side to the other
_source.learnerexamples_text: We drove across/over the bridge.; The Brooklyn Bridge spans the East River from Brooklyn to Manhattan.; We can see Bogaz bridge from [the] window.

_source.definition_text: something that connects two groups, organizations, etc. and improves the relationship between them
_source.learnerexamples_text: After the war they tried to build bridges with neighbouring countries.; It is difficult to prevent this but we must do our best to build bridges between countries.

_source.definition_text: lasting only a short time or using only a few words

_source.definition_text: for a short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: We chatted briefly about the weather.; In this essay, I shall briefly look at the advantages and disadvantages of ow[n]ing a car.

_source.definition_text: using only a few words
_source.learnerexamples_text: world news in brief; In brief, I have had a marvellous week.

_source.definition_text: full of light, shining
_source.learnerexamples_text: bright sunshine; The rooms were bright and airy.; The lights are too bright in here - they're hurting my eyes.; It was bright and sunny.

_source.definition_text: strong in colour
_source.learnerexamples_text: Leslie always wears bright colours.; He said hello and I felt my face turn bright red.; I will be using bright orange for my bedroom.

_source.definition_text: clever
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were bright children, always asking questions.; She was enthusiastic and full of bright ideas and suggestions.; Rony had the bright idea of calling the firemen.

_source.definition_text: happy or full of hope
_source.learnerexamples_text: You're very bright and cheerful this morning!; She's an excellent student with a bright future.; I think I'm [a] very bright kind of person, friendly with lots of energ[y].

_source.definition_text: with a lot of strong colour or light
_source.learnerexamples_text: brightly coloured clothes; a brightly lit room; The sun was shining brightly over the white mountain tops.

_source.definition_text: to find good things in a bad situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Look on the bright side - no one was badly hurt.; I am quite self-confident and I usually look on the bright side, as I am not keen on pessimistic thoughts.

_source.definition_text: extremely good or enjoyable
_source.learnerexamples_text: Oh, brilliant! My parcel's arrived.; "Did you like the film?" "I thought it was brilliant."; These presents were brilliant!

_source.definition_text: extremely clever
_source.learnerexamples_text: a brilliant mathematician; He is [an] engineering student and he is brilliant in his stud[ies].

_source.definition_text: full of light or colour
_source.learnerexamples_text: The sky was a brilliant blue.; It was 11:15 so I thought "they won't come" but suddenly a brilliant light bath[ed] me.

_source.definition_text: to take someone or something with you when you go somewhere
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Shall I bring anything to the party?" "Oh, just a bottle."; Bring me that knife/Bring that knife to me.; Did you bring an umbrella with you?; Please bring old clothes with you.

_source.definition_text: in a very skillful way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He seems to do everything brilliantly - piano playing, skiing, sailing.; Although they are not very famous like JULIE BLOOM, they sang brilliantly.

_source.definition_text: to cause happiness/luck/peace, etc.

_source.definition_text: to make something finish
_source.learnerexamples_text: The stories in the newspaper brought her career to a sudden end.; At the end of the year 2002 a great construction was brought to an end.

_source.base_text: bring a lump to your throat
_source.definition_text: to make you feel such strong emotion that you want to cry
_source.searchterms_text: bring;bring a lump to your throat;bringing;brings;brought
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was a very moving speech, and it brought a lump to my throat.; This devastating image brought a lump to John's throat.

_source.base_text: bring out the best in sb

_source.definition_text: to change a decision or opinion
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you change your mind about coming tonight, just give me a call.; When I first met him I didn't like him but I've changed my mind.; After the first lesson, I changed my mind.

_source.definition_text: when something becomes different, or the result of something becoming different
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let me know if there's any change in the situation.; We're living in a time of great change.; They've made a lot of changes to the house.; Really, this bedroom needs a big change.

_source.definition_text: to start talking about a different subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd tried to explain the situation, but he just changed the subject.; Well, changing the subject, I accidentally broke your beautiful vase. I'm really sorry, I'll try to find [another] vase that looks similar.

_source.definition_text: the money which is returned to someone who has paid for something which costs less than the amount that they gave
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think you've given me the wrong change.; First of all, I helped selling tickets and drinks and there I realized how bad my maths is - I took such a long time to give back the change!

_source.definition_text: when you stop having or using one thing and start having or using another
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've told the school about our change of address.; This country needs a change of government.; The reason for the change of class was mainly the teacher.

_source.definition_text: money which is coins rather than notes
_source.learnerexamples_text: She gave me £5 in change.; My dad always used to carry a lot of loose/small change in his pocket.; He asked me if I had any change.

_source.definition_text: a set of clean clothes you can put on if you need to take off the ones you are wearing
_source.searchterms_text: a change of clothes;change;change of clothes;changes
_source.learnerexamples_text: Make sure you bring a change of clothes.; If you want you can bring an extra change of clothes so we can get wet.

_source.definition_text: something which is pleasant or interesting because it is unusual or new
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's nice to see her smile for a change.; "Shall we eat in the garden?" "Why not - it'll make a change."; We've always had a red car - it's time we had a change!; Last year the college had a sports day so this year we should have a party in a disco for a change.

_source.definition_text: If you have a change of heart, you change your opinion or feelings about something.
_source.searchterms_text: a change of heart;change;change of heart;changes
_source.learnerexamples_text: At first he said he wouldn't help us, but he seems to have had a change of heart.; The narrator didn't tell her big secret to Inder Lal and after a change of heart she decides to keep the baby.

_source.definition_text: often changing, or likely to change
_source.learnerexamples_text: The weather was very changeable last summer.; I must say that summers here are a bit mild and changeable.

_source.definition_text: a television station
_source.learnerexamples_text: a cable/terrestrial channel; a music/movie/news/shopping/sports channel; the news on Channel 4; She switched/turned to another channel to watch the football.; First of all, I enjoy watching news [o]n international channels like Aljazeera, CNN, Alhurra and BBC.

_source.definition_text: a way of communicating with people or getting something done
_source.learnerexamples_text: a channel of communication ; Please make your request through the proper channels.

_source.definition_text: to use money or energy for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've channelled all our resources into this project.; In the same way that it shouldn't take the place of more important matters, there shouldn't be so much money channelled into it, especially when we want to see it as sport rather than business, and when there are so many other much fairer ends for that money.

_source.definition_text: a state of total confusion with no order
_source.learnerexamples_text: Snow and ice have caused chaos on the roads.; Ever since our secretary walked out, the office has been in a state of total chaos.; There was chaos at the school.

_source.definition_text: in a state of chaos
_source.learnerexamples_text: a chaotic situation; Consequently, in order to improve the chaotic traffic situation it is advisable to choose other means of transport as mentioned above.

_source.definition_text: a small church, or a room used as a church in a building
_source.learnerexamples_text: There is a small chapel in the grounds of the house.; On [one] occasion we were taken to a small chapel that was in such a state of dilapidation that it was not worth climb[ing] the stairs.

_source.definition_text: one of the parts that a book is divided into
_source.learnerexamples_text: Read Chapter 3 before class tomorrow.; I promise you that I will read chapter 10 of the book, and I will make a resume for you.

_source.definition_text: a person represented in a film, play or story
_source.learnerexamples_text: The film revolves around three main characters.; She had Mickey Mouse or some other cartoon/Disney character on her sweater.; He made his name as a character actor.; My favourite character was Gandalf but Lucie preferred Morween, the young elf maiden.

_source.definition_text: the combination of qualities and personality that makes a person different from others
_source.learnerexamples_text: Politeness is traditionally part of the British character.; It would be very out of character of her to lie.; One of the joys of being a parent is watching the child's character develop.; It's not in his character to be jealous.; Mary had a strong character and faced her uncle with great courage.

_source.definition_text: qualities that are interesting or unusual
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hotel of character; There [are] many very old house[s] with a lot of character and charm, [which are] just perfect for a photographer.

_source.definition_text: an interesting or funny person whose behaviour is different from most people's
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your granny's a real character.; Mr Brown is a great character.

_source.definition_text: a particular kind of person
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unpleasant character; John was a gentle character, [rather] shy, but full of joy and happiness.

_source.definition_text: a typical or noticeable quality of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Unfortunately a big nose is a family characteristic.; Sentimentality seems a characteristic of all the writers of that period.; The male bird displays several characteristics which distinguish him from the female.; Orwell gives the animals human characteristics and we can identify with them.

_source.definition_text: a letter, sign, or number that you use when you are writing or printing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Chinese characters; However, [the] poems are written in old Japanese characters which are difficult to understand.

_source.definition_text: typical of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Grey stone is characteristic of buildings in that area.; With characteristic generosity, she offered to pay for us all.; But to be honest, food is the only feature which will stay as a characteristic aspect of a country.

_source.definition_text: to ask an amount of money for something, especially a service or activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: How much/What do you charge for delivery?; The bank charged commission to change my traveller's cheques.; They charge you $20 just to get into the nightclub.; The local museum doesn't charge for admission.; Be careful while you are in Brazil because sometimes people charge really high prices for everything just because you are a tourist.

_source.definition_text: If the police charge someone, they accuse them officially of a crime.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's been charged with murder.; While Jem is accused of [a] minor crime, Joss is charged with smuggling.

_source.definition_text: to attack someone or something by moving forward quickly
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bull lowered its horns and charged.; The violence began when the police charged at a crowd of demonstrators.; They had water bombs and water pistols at the ready. They started charging down the field towards the fire and once in range everyone thew their balloon as far as they could.

_source.definition_text: to put electricity into something
_source.learnerexamples_text: My mobile needs charging.

_source.definition_text: the amount of money that you have to pay for something, especially for an activity or service
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's no charge for children under ten.; There's an admission charge of £5.; They fixed my watch free of charge.; It is free of charge and will give me a idea of this sport.

_source.definition_text: to be the person who has control of or is responsible for someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's in charge of a team of 20 people.; Who's in charge of organizing the music for the party.;  I talk[ed] to the man who was in charge and [he] convince[d] me that it was safe, so I did it.

_source.definition_text: to take control of or make yourself responsible for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was happy to let her take charge of the holiday arrangements.; I am 21 years old which means that I can take charge of school children.

_source.definition_text: a formal police statement saying that someone is accused of a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: The 19-year-old will be appearing in court on Thursday where she will face criminal charges.; He has been arrested on a charge  of murder.; The police brought a charge of theft against him.; He decided on the spot that if Paul was to return all the money he wouldn't press charges so he called his parents and asked them to find out where he was.

_source.definition_text: to complain officially about someone in a court of law
_source.learnerexamples_text: The family decided not to press charges against him.; He decided on the spot that if Paul was to return all the money he wouldn't press charges so he called his parents and asked them to find out where he was.

_source.definition_text: a natural power which some people have to influence or attract people
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is a respected politician but he lacks charisma.; I admire peop[l]e with heart and soul, with that real charisma which can only blossom in highly intelligent and spiritual people - this is what we call `intense personality'.

_source.definition_text: having a natural power to influence and attract people
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her mother was a very charismatic woman.; Some charismatic people have a great influence on others, and they are highly respected or praised.

_source.definition_text: an official organization that gives money, food, or help to people who need it, or money, food, or help that is given to people who need it
_source.learnerexamples_text: UNICEF is an international charity.; She does a lot of work for charity.; She does a lot of charity work.; People tend to give to charity at Christmas time.; Money from the sale of these cards will go to local charities.

_source.definition_text: kindness towards other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: an act of charity; It is undeniable that nowadays the whole world is suffering [from] the lack of good personalit[y] models to follow. Models that [ar]e able to show the importance of charity, humility and other qualities so old-fashioned in our age.

_source.definition_text: a quality which makes you like or feel attracted to someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a woman of great charm; The building has a certain charm.; I had to use all my charms to get them to lend us the hall.; It's an extremely severe and rugged sort of landscape with its own very special charm.

_source.definition_text: an object that you keep or wear because you believe that it is lucky
_source.learnerexamples_text: a lucky charm ; Consequently, "the treasures" I took there were nothing but all the little gifts and lucky charms I had received from my boyfriend and friends.

_source.definition_text: to attract someone or persuade someone to do something because of your charm
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were charmed by his boyish manner.; She arrived in time for the ball held that night, and everybody was charmed by her looks and manners.

_source.definition_text: pleasant and attractive
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's very charming.; It's a charming little village.; He's charming, but he's too talkative and not romantic enough.

_source.definition_text: a drawing which shows information in a simple way, often using lines and curves to show amounts
_source.learnerexamples_text: a sales chart; Now I can create special charts at home.

_source.definition_text: an official list of the most popular songs each week
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're currently at the top of the charts with their single 'Enough'.; She get[s] to the people's hearts by music and she is now [at] the top [of the] charts with the song "Love me".

_source.definition_text: to run after someone or something in order to catch them
_source.learnerexamples_text: The dog was chasing a rabbit.; She was chasing after her two-year-old son.; I could feel that the man was chasing after me.

_source.definition_text: to run after a person or animal to make them leave a place
_source.searchterms_text: chase;chase sb/sth away/off/out etc;chase sb/sth away/off/out, etc.;chased;chases;chasing
_source.learnerexamples_text: I chased the cat away.; But one day, Napoleon said that his rival Snowball was a spy of the farmers and chased him away.

_source.definition_text: to try very hard to get something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are hundreds of graduates chasing very few jobs.; I was tired and for the first time I started to take notice [of] the smirks on peoples faces as I walked past them, the silent laughter and I saw myself through their eyes; I was an old fool, chasing a r[i]dic[u]lous, flimsy dream.

_source.definition_text: to talk to someone in a friendly and informal way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She spends hours on the phone chatting to her friends.; We were just chatting about what we did last weekend.; Whenever I walk in, I always find the two of them chatting away.; We were eating, drinking and chatting at the party.

_source.definition_text: to have a conversation with someone who is online at the same time as you are by typing messages
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were chatting till well past midnight.; I can surf [the] Internet and chat with some friends.

_source.base_text: chat sb up or chat up sb
_source.definition_text: to talk to someone in a way that shows them that you are sexually attracted to them
_source.searchterms_text: chat;chat sb up or chat up sb
_source.learnerexamples_text: He spends hours in cafés, chatting up the waitresses.; Then he started to chat her up.

_source.definition_text: a friendly, informal conversation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Give me a call and we'll have a chat sometime.; I had a chat with my boss today about a possible salary increase.; Then we can go to Starbucks Café to have a chat after the film.

_source.definition_text: a television or radio programme where people are asked questions about themselves
_source.learnerexamples_text: I saw her on a chat show last week.; But I'm very interested in politics, so I really enjoy political and chat shows.

_source.definition_text: liking to talk
_source.learnerexamples_text: My sister is very chatty.; Both Mr Brown and Peter are chatty and not afraid of [the] camcorder.

_source.definition_text: A piece of writing that is chatty has a friendly and informal style.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a chatty letter/style; To be more specific, the articles will include events taken from our college life, written in a humorous, chatty way in order to help them see life in its positive aspect.

_source.definition_text: costing little money or less than is usual or expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got a cheap flight at the last minute.; Food is usually cheaper in supermarkets.; Children and the elderly are entitled to cheap train tickets.; The scheme is simple and cheap to operate.; The house rent is very cheap.

_source.definition_text: low in price and quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: I bought some cheap wine to cook with.; [The] "luxury hotel" from the advertis[e]ment happened to be a dirty, cheap hotel with no lift (notice that all the rooms were located on the 4th floor) and no service.

_source.definition_text: to behave in a dishonest way in order to get what you want
_source.learnerexamples_text: Anyone caught cheating will be immediately disqualified from the exam.; She was caught cheating in her French exam.; He cheats at cards.; She also didn't want to cheat during the exam because it wouldn't be fair to anyone.

_source.definition_text: to have a secret sexual relationship with someone who is not your usual sexual partner
_source.learnerexamples_text: She found out that Jeremy had been cheating on her.; In Cancun, I met another cute guy and I cheated on my boyfriend with him but that was just an affair, that did not mean anything to me.

_source.definition_text: to examine something to make sure it is correct or the way it should be
_source.learnerexamples_text: Always check your oil, water and tyres before taking your car on a long trip.; I always check (that) I've shut the windows before I leave the house.; After I'd finished the exam, I checked my answers for mistakes.; The doctor will call next week to check on your progress.; I think I left it in your bedroom. Can you check, please?

_source.definition_text: to find out about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I rang them yesterday to check when they were arriving.; If you're near the garage, could you check whether the car's ready?; I called the company to check whether I really had won the jackpot.

_source.definition_text: to ask someone for permission to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to stay overnight, but I need to check with my parents.; I'll be there at 4.00 the next day which will be the 5th. Would you check with your neighbours again, please?

_source.definition_text: to go to the desk at an airport, so that you can be told where you will be sitting and so that your bags can be put on the aircraft
_source.learnerexamples_text: Passengers are requested to check in two hours before the flight.; I had to check in at 2.15 pm.

_source.definition_text: to say who you are when you arrive at a hotel so that you can be given a key for your room
_source.searchterms_text: check;check in/check into sth;check in/check into sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please would you check in at the reception desk and sign your name in the book.; We checked in at the hotel and we all went to bed early that night.

_source.definition_text: to try to discover how something is progressing or whether someone is doing what they should be doing
_source.searchterms_text: check;check (up) on sth;check up on sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: My boss is always checking up on me.

_source.base_text: check sth out or check out sth
_source.definition_text: to examine something or get more information about it in order to be certain that it is true, safe, or suitable
_source.searchterms_text: check;check sth out or check out sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: We'll need to check out his story.; Can you please check it out and let me know who caused such a[n] awful mistake.

_source.definition_text: to leave a hotel after paying and returning your room key
_source.learnerexamples_text: We checked out of/from our hotel at 5 a.m. to catch a 7 a.m. flight.; [On] the last day we decided to stay in the hotel because we had to check out at noon.

_source.base_text: check sth out or check out sth
_source.definition_text: to go to a place in order to see what it is like
_source.searchterms_text: check;check sth out or check out sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's check out that new dance club.; If cooking is not your favourite task or you enjoy eating out, check out the college cant[een].

_source.definition_text: an examination of something in order to make certain that it is correct or the way it should be
_source.learnerexamples_text: The soldiers gave their equipment a final check before setting off.; We do safety checks on all our electrical equipment.;  Security checks have become really strict at the airport.; I have to do some medical checks [on] my dog because I think it is very sick and may have a problem [with its] throat.

_source.definition_text: the place at an airport where you show your ticket so that you can be told where you will be sitting
_source.learnerexamples_text: A representative from the tour company will meet you at the check-in.; I'll meet you at the check-in desk.; After we had finished [having coffee], we went to the check-in.

_source.definition_text: the place at an airport where you show your ticket so that you can be told where you will be sitting
_source.learnerexamples_text: A representative from the tour operator will meet you at the check-in.; I'll meet you by the check-in counter.; After we had finished [having coffee], we went to the check-in.

_source.definition_text: the place in a shop, especially a large food shop, where you pay for your goods
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your fruit and vegetables will be weighed at the checkout.; She works on the checkout at the local supermarket.; Your visit to the shop concludes in a long queue to the checkout (where you can easily spend another 30 minutes), where they will suck out some money from your account.

_source.definition_text: the place on a website where you order and pay for goods
_source.learnerexamples_text: After you've chosen what you want, click here to proceed to checkout.

_source.definition_text: the soft part of your face which is below your eye and between your mouth and ear
_source.learnerexamples_text: rosy cheeks; The tears ran down her cheeks.; He kissed her on both cheeks.; I kissed him on the cheek and I left him.

_source.definition_text: slightly rude or showing no respect, but often in a funny way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's got such a cheeky grin.; Don't be so cheeky!; Don't get angry, but I think your husband is a very cheeky man!

_source.definition_text: to give a loud shout of approval or encouragement
_source.learnerexamples_text: Everyone cheered as the winners received their medals.; He was cheering for the other side.; When she had finished, she felt satisfied and so did the audience who cheered for Louise.

_source.base_text: cheer sb on or cheer on sb
_source.definition_text: to shout loudly in order to encourage someone in a competition
_source.searchterms_text: cheer;cheer sb on or cheer on sb
_source.learnerexamples_text: The race was tough, but I could hear all my friends cheering me on.;  People rush to the stadiums and gyms to cheer on their favourites or spend long hours in front of the TV with their fingers crossed hoping for a win.

_source.definition_text: a shout of approval or encouragement
_source.learnerexamples_text: His speech was drowned out by cheers.; They were welcomed onto the stage in their home town by deafening cheers from their fans.

_source.definition_text: If someone cheers up, or something cheers them up, they start to feel happier.
_source.searchterms_text: cheer;cheer up (sb) or cheer (sb) up;cheer up sb or cheer sb up
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was ill so I sent her some flowers to cheer her up.; Cheer up! It's not that bad!; She went shopping to cheer herself up.; My sister tried to cheer me up but she couldn't.

_source.definition_text: happy and positive
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's usually fairly cheerful.; You're in a cheerful mood this morning.; She manages to stay cheerful despite everything.; Her fiancé is very kind and cheerful.

_source.definition_text: describes a place or thing that is bright and pleasant and makes you feel positive and happy
_source.learnerexamples_text: The doctor's waiting room was bright and cheerful with yellow walls and curtains.; We can have [a] mixed colour[ed] carpet to make the reception area more cheerful.

_source.definition_text: in a cheerful way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She walked down the road, whistling cheerfully.; But Mr Robertson recognised Jane and greeted her very cheerfully.

_source.definition_text: the state of being happy or bright and pleasant to look at
_source.learnerexamples_text: His cheerfulness made us all feel better.; Bright colours are identified with cheerfulness and happiness and dark colours with sadness or feeling down.

_source.definition_text: a friendly expression said just before you drink an alcoholic drink
_source.learnerexamples_text: Cheers! To your good health.

_source.definition_text: used to mean 'goodbye'
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Bye." "Cheers, see you next week."; See you later, cheers.

_source.definition_text: used to mean 'thank you'
_source.learnerexamples_text: "I've bought you a drink." "Cheers, mate."

_source.definition_text: a food made from milk, which can either be firm or soft and is usually yellow or white in colour
_source.learnerexamples_text: a slice of cheese;  goat's cheese; I like soft French cheeses such as Brie and Camembert.; I prefer hard cheeses, like Cheddar.; cheese and biscuits

_source.definition_text: a skilled and trained cook who works in a hotel or restaurant, especially the most important cook
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is one of the top chefs in Britain.; She is the head chef at the Waldorf-Astoria.; I want to study cooking, because I want to be a chef.

_source.definition_text: a basic substance that is used in chemistry or produced by chemistry
_source.learnerexamples_text: The government has pledged to reduce the amount of chemicals used in food production.; Each year, factories release millions of tonnes of toxic chemicals into the atmosphere.; There are a lot of chemicals and sewage in the river Dollmitz and the lakes, too.

_source.definition_text: relating to chemicals
_source.learnerexamples_text: a chemical reaction; chemical weapons; The chemical industry produces such things as petrochemicals, drugs, paint and rubber.; In the latter many chemical reactions may be reproduced to show the students the final compounds generated.

_source.definition_text: a shop where you can buy medicines, make-up and products used for washing yourself
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you call in at the chemist and get some plasters?; We [can] meet [at] the bus stop, in front of the chemist.

_source.definition_text: a person who studies chemistry, or a scientist who works with chemicals or studies their reactions
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is he a chemist or a physicist?; I ha[d] been working in a factory because I am [a] chemist, but one day I decided to change my work [and] my life.

_source.definition_text: the scientific study of substances and the different ways in which they react or combine with other substances
_source.learnerexamples_text: She studied chemistry at university.; the chemistry of the ozone layer; a chemistry department/laboratory; On the day of her birthday, I will ask her to help me with my homework for chemistry (she is really smart).

_source.definition_text: a piece of paper printed by a bank that you use instead of money to pay for things
_source.learnerexamples_text: I wrote him a cheque for £50.; I don't have any cash on me, so could I pay by cheque?; Please make your cheques payable to The Brighter Toyshop Ltd.; I'll send you the cheque next week.

_source.definition_text: a small, round, soft red or black fruit with a single hard seed in the middle
_source.learnerexamples_text: cherry trees; There was a big cherry tree, and there, on the top, was Trouble [the cat]!

_source.definition_text: a game that two people play by moving differently shaped pieces around a board of black and white squares
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you play chess?; a chess player/set; My favourite hobby is playing chess.

_source.definition_text: the front part of your body, between your neck and your waist, containing your heart and your lungs
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was shot in the chest.; Peter has a very hairy chest.; She went to the doctor complaining of chest pains.; She tried to get her weapon, but then a bullet hit her chest like a hammer.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone about something that you have been worried or angry about for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tell me what's wrong - you'll feel better if you get it off your chest.; Chris is always caring and lends you his ear if there's something you need to get off your chest.

_source.definition_text: a strong, usually wooden, container with a lid, used for keeping things in
_source.learnerexamples_text: a treasure chest; The woman opened a heavy wooden chest and produced the book, after trying to sweep off a little of the dirt.

_source.definition_text: a piece of furniture for keeping clothes in
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need a chest of drawers for Oliver's bedroom.; I bought a chest of drawers and put it next to the door.

_source.definition_text: to crush food into smaller, softer pieces with the teeth so that it can be swallowed
_source.learnerexamples_text: This meat is difficult to chew.; You don't chew your food enough - that's why you get indigestion.; Next, when you eat something, please chew [it] for a long time.

_source.definition_text: to repeatedly bite something without swallowing it
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was chewing gum.; Our dog loves a bone to chew (on).; She sat in the dentist's waiting room, nervously chewing (at) her nails.; Students couldn't chew bubble-gum, smoke or eat swe[e]ties in school, but they do now.

_source.definition_text: a sweet that you chew but do not swallow
_source.learnerexamples_text: Would you like a piece/stick of chewing gum?; Some visitors [to the zoo] feed them with forbidden things like sugar or they give them chewing gum.

_source.definition_text: a type of bird kept on a farm for its eggs or its meat
_source.learnerexamples_text: A male chicken is called a cock and a female chicken is called a hen.

_source.definition_text: most important or main
_source.learnerexamples_text: The chief problem we have in the area now is the spread of disease.; The weather was our chief reason for coming here.; This is the chief argument of those who do not agree with zoos.

_source.definition_text: the meat of a chicken
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're having roast/fried chicken for dinner.; I'd like to eat chicken and chips.

_source.definition_text: the person in charge of a group or organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: a police chief; A new chief of the security forces has just been appointed.; I saw her one day, and she [told] me that she had been promoted to chief of section.

_source.definition_text: highest in rank
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is the chief economic adviser to the government.; Bob Wilson, the chief accountant, had resigned.

_source.definition_text: a boy or girl who is not yet an adult, or a son or daughter of any age
