_source.definition_text: a place where something official, usually a document, is checked
_source.learnerexamples_text: passport/immigration control; I kissed my parents and went to passport control.

_source.definition_text: the ability to be calm
_source.learnerexamples_text: It took a lot of control to stop myself hitting him.; If you think you [are doing] something wrong during your test you shouldn't [start] panic[k]ing and losing your control.

_source.definition_text: causing disagreement or discussion
_source.learnerexamples_text: a controversial issue/decision/speech/figure; The book was very controversial.; From my point of view it is a very controversial issue.

_source.definition_text: a lot of disagreement and argument about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There is a lot of controversy over mobile phone towers.; Travelling abroad to work has been a matter of controversy.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being convenient
_source.learnerexamples_text: the convenience of credit cards;  I like the convenience of living so close to the shops.; I think the first reason is its convenience. [...] Just by sitting in front of it, you can enjoy TV program[me]s.

_source.definition_text: at a time that is convenient to you
_source.learnerexamples_text: We can meet at your convenience.; I look forward to hearing from you at your earliest convenience.

_source.definition_text: something that makes life easier
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fortunately, the house has every modern convenience.; Thus, we have many facilities and conveniences in comparison with the past.

_source.definition_text: easy to use or suiting your plans well
_source.learnerexamples_text: We could meet at either place - whichever is more convenient for you.; A bike's a very convenient way of getting around.; I find it more convenient to be able to do my banking by phone.; What would be a convenient time for me to come round?; If it would be possible for you, I can attend another class at any time which is convenient for you.

_source.definition_text: near or easy to get to
_source.learnerexamples_text: My new house is more convenient for the station.; It is near the train station [so] it is very convenient to get there.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is convenient
_source.learnerexamples_text: The house is conveniently situated near the station and the shops.; First of all, your group has been booked into the Palace Hotel, which is conveniently situated in the centre of Nymegen.

_source.definition_text: a large formal meeting of people who do a particular job or have a similar interest, or a large meeting for a political party
_source.learnerexamples_text: the national Democratic convention; Where are they holding their party convention?; Conference facilities: Being completely renovated, the historic building of Edessa's Cultural Association is the ideal place for a modern scientific convention.

_source.definition_text: a usual and accepted way of behaving or doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: In many countries it is the convention to wear black at funerals.; Nowadays, people tend to avoid traditions and conventions.

_source.definition_text: traditional and ordinary
_source.learnerexamples_text: conventional behaviour/attitudes/clothes; conventional medicine/farming; I find his art rather dull and conventional.; The accommodation wasn't bad, however our rooms were quite small and conventional.

_source.definition_text: what most people believe
_source.learnerexamples_text: These ideas about childcare go against conventional wisdom on the subject.; Thus, against conventional wisdom, I think that while a lot of adult problems are caused by money or the lack of it, it is really the ability to deal with money and to see money as a means rather than an end.

_source.definition_text: a talk between two or more people, usually an informal one
_source.learnerexamples_text: a conversation about football.; I had a strange conversation with the bloke who's moved in upstairs.; But every day we have [a] spelling test and [a] conversation with our teacher or in pairs.

_source.definition_text: to have a conversation
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can just about hold a conversation in Italian.; I know the grammar and many different expressions, and I can hold a conversation with other people.

_source.definition_text: when the appearance, form, or purpose of something is changed
_source.learnerexamples_text: the country's conversion to democracy ; Solar power is the conversion of the sun's energy into heat and electricity.; This 'magic' conversion of energy can be performed in several ways, which result in different degrees of 'dignity' or 'cleanness' for the resulting electrons, freely running through our cables.

_source.definition_text: to change the appearance, form, or purpose of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could we convert the small bedroom into a second bathroom?; What's the formula for converting pounds into kilos?; Even some medieval castles have been converted into museums.

_source.definition_text: to change to a new religion, belief, etc., or to make someone do this
_source.learnerexamples_text: When did he convert to Islam?; Frederica converted to Catholicism and devoted her life to mentally ill children.

_source.definition_text: to communicate information, feelings, or images to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: She always conveys a sense of enthusiasm for her work. ; Being an Ambassador for Youth bears lot of responsibility, not only because the person must be an outstanding character and widely well-known, but also because they must behave accordingly and be able to convey a positive message.

_source.definition_text: to decide officially in a court of law that someone is guilty of a particular crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was convicted of murder.; Consequently he was convicted of robbery and murder and was sentenced to 20 years in prison.

_source.definition_text: when someone is officially found to be guilty of a particular crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: He already had two convictions for burglary. ; The conviction of all three protesters caused anger in the local community.; Besides, she had no previous convictions so nobody believed that such a pretty, intel[l]igent and polite woman could do any harm to anybody.

_source.definition_text: a strong opinion or belief
_source.learnerexamples_text: religious/moral convictions ; a deep/strong conviction; In spite of the fact that I respect their convictions, I totally disagree with this viewpoint.

_source.definition_text: to persuade someone or make them certain
_source.learnerexamples_text: She tried to convince me that I needed a new car.; I hope this will convince you to change your mind.; He managed to convince the jury of his innocence.; She was the one who convinced me to go, and I am glad she did.

_source.definition_text: certain
_source.learnerexamples_text: My boyfriend says I'd enjoy a walking holiday, but I'm not convinced.; I'm convinced (that) she is lying.; I'm convinced that I would benefit from this experience in the future.

_source.definition_text: able to make you believe that something is true or right
_source.learnerexamples_text: a convincing argument/explanation; I didn't find the ending of the film very convincing.; The school didn't give us a real and convincing explanation for this.

_source.definition_text: to prepare food and usually heat it
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't cook meat very often.; Who's cooking this evening?; He cooked us an enormous meal./He cooked an enormous meal for us.; I would like you to cook Camerounian traditional foods (Ndole, Pistache, Couscous, Khaki).

_source.definition_text: someone who prepares and cooks food
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's a wonderful cook.; For example my mother wake[s] up at 4am. She is [a] cook like me.

_source.definition_text: a piece of information stored on your computer which contains information about all the Internet documents you have looked at
_source.learnerexamples_text: You need to enable cookies to use this website.

_source.definition_text: a large box-shaped device which is used to cook and heat food either by putting the food inside or by putting it on the top
_source.learnerexamples_text: a gas/electric cooker; For instance I've got my television, radio, computer, a small cooker, a bed, a desk and a sink.

_source.definition_text: preparing and cooking food, or a particular way of preparing and cooking food
_source.learnerexamples_text: My mother always hated cooking.; Who does the cooking in your house?; I love my dad's cooking.; I really like it because I love cooking and also baking.

_source.definition_text: used when you like something or agree to something
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've got your own apartment? Cool!; "We'll meet at ten, then?" "Cool."; That's very exciting. Cool!

_source.definition_text: good, stylish, or fashionable
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was a really cool gig.; She's really cool.; I got this mega cool T-shirt.

_source.definition_text: slightly cold, but not too cold
_source.learnerexamples_text: cool water; a nice cool breeze; Sometimes a cool wind blows [in Bodrum].

_source.definition_text: calm and not emotional
_source.learnerexamples_text: She seemed cool and confident.; I remember saying to myself that "this little boy will survive" and after that I felt totally cool and calm and did what had to be done.

_source.definition_text: unfriendly
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was very cool towards us.; I encouraged him to tell me what was going on and I could hardly believe [it] when he explained the reason why he had been treating me in a cool manner.

_source.definition_text: to become less hot, or to make someone or something become less hot
_source.searchterms_text: cool;cool down/off (sb/sth) or cool (sb/sth) down/off;cool down/off sb/sth or cool sb/sth down/off
_source.learnerexamples_text: She waited until her coffee had cooled down and then took a sip.; We went for a swim to cool off.; The pool is a very popular place to cool down [in].

_source.definition_text: to become less hot, or to make something become less hot
_source.learnerexamples_text: Allow the bread to cool before slicing it.; In the summer many people were delighted by fountains which cooled the air.

_source.definition_text: to remain calm in a difficult situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: To be successful in business, you need to keep a cool head in negotiations.; Kevin managed to keep a cool head and took over the navigation.

_source.definition_text: to suddenly become very angry
_source.learnerexamples_text: She lost her cool and started shouting.

_source.definition_text: to become calmer, or to make someone become calmer
_source.searchterms_text: cool;cool down/off (sb/sth) or cool (sb/sth) down/off;cool down/off sb/sth or cool sb/sth down/off
_source.learnerexamples_text: Just leave her to cool off and then talk to her.; It seemed to me that you were stressed. If I were you, I would cool down a little.

_source.definition_text: to remain calm
_source.learnerexamples_text: You did well to keep your cool in all that panic.; Whatever the problem is, keep your cool, don't panic.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being cold
_source.learnerexamples_text: the coolness of the breeze; The coolness of the coach made me ill.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being calm
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was admired for his coolness under pressure.; Finally, a successful person should have [their] own style and opinion to distinguish from other people, enough patience to wait for important opportunities, a certain coolness to "survive" critical situations, and last but not least, a good deal of luck, which often decides whether you are successful or not.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being unfriendly
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was a little insulted by her coolness towards him.; James eyed her with a mixture of contempt and admiration for her coolness.

_source.definition_text: to help someone or do what they ask
_source.learnerexamples_text: I find it very hard to dress my two-year-old when she refuses to cooperate.; Moreover, I am in favour of rules at school because it is very important for children to learn how to cooperate with others.

_source.definition_text: to work together with someone in order to achieve the same aim
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Spanish authorities cooperated with the British police in finding the terrorists.; Several companies are cooperating in the relief effort.; Lime has become a sort of monster, with no consideration for life any more, and Martins decides to cooperate with the police to catch and kill him.

_source.definition_text: willing to help or do what people ask
_source.learnerexamples_text: I found them very cooperative.; You can rely on me - I love children and I am energetic and cooperative.

_source.definition_text: when you work together with someone or do what they ask you
_source.learnerexamples_text: This documentary was made with the cooperation of Rails UK.; There's very little cooperation between the two countries.; We thank you in advance for your cooperation.; The clubs work in close cooperation  with the Football Association.; Thank you in advance for your cooperation in this respect.

_source.definition_text: a reddish-brown metal used especially for making wire and coins, or the reddish brown colour of this metal
_source.learnerexamples_text: copper wire/pipes; Rosie's hair shone like copper in the sunlight.; Its domes are made of pure copper, inside there's a big bell called "Zygmunt".

_source.definition_text: to deal successfully with a difficult situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: How does she cope with three small children and a job?; It was too stressful and eventually he just couldn't cope.; Tyres generally don't cope well on wet roads.; Moreover she can't cope with life.

_source.definition_text: to produce something that is similar or exactly the same as something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: They've copied the basic design from the Japanese model and added a few of their own refinements.; Copy the file onto disk.; I will copy the CD on[to] my computer.

_source.definition_text: to cheat by looking at and using someone else's work
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was always copying from/off other children, but never got caught.; I'm certain she thought we had copied in the test.

_source.definition_text: to behave like someone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: He tends to copy his brother in the way he dresses.; He has to eat salads now, in [the] hope [that] the kids'll copy his attitudes and eat fresh and healthy food instead of sweets and unhealthy st[u]ff.

_source.definition_text: a single book, newspaper, etc. of which many have been produced
_source.learnerexamples_text: Over a million copies of the book have been sold.; The single with her new song sold more than 15 million copies, now she was a powerful star.

_source.definition_text: something that has been made to be exactly like something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: This painting is only a copy - the original hangs in the Louvre.; I always keep a copy of any official or important letters that I send off.; Could you make a copy of this for tomorrow's meeting, please?; For covering the work I missed, I will ask May on Thursday if I can borrow her exercise book and make a copy.

_source.definition_text: a hard, usually pink or white substance produced by a type of very small sea animal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a coral reef; The main [attraction] of the place is scuba diving, due to the excellent visibility of the water and the impressive coral reefs which surround the island.

_source.definition_text: the most important part of a system or principle
_source.learnerexamples_text: core values ; Better health care was at the core of the senator's campaign.; The aim of this paper is to respond to a call for proposals [from] a TV company which is planning to launch a programme called "Making the World a Better Place" and to select the group of people which represents the core idea of this programme.

_source.definition_text: the hard, central part of certain fruits, such as apples, which contains the seeds
_source.learnerexamples_text: Peel the apples and remove the cores.; So there it was, hidden in nature, occasionally trampled by a stray dog with no other companion than old cans and apple cores.

_source.definition_text: a crop of grain, or the seed from this crop used to make flour or feed animals
_source.learnerexamples_text: fields of corn; [My sister] is a farmer and we have to plant yams, corn, beans and other crops.

_source.definition_text: a part of a larger area, often somewhere quiet or far away
_source.learnerexamples_text: He lives in a beautiful corner of northern California.; Special buses and trams were allocated to give people a lift to the shopping centre practically from any corner of the city.

_source.definition_text: going to happen soon
_source.learnerexamples_text: Christmas is round the corner and I still haven't bought any presents.; With the FIFA World Cup just around the corner, there certainly is a lot of excitement buzzing in the air.

_source.definition_text: the point, area or line which is formed by the meeting of two lines, surfaces, roads, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Click the icon in the bottom right-hand corner of the screen.; There's a postbox on the corner of the street.; I've got a bruise where I hit my leg against the corner of the table.; They live just around/round the corner - so we see them all the time.; It's at the corner of East Street and Beach Street.

_source.definition_text: a difficult situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had been in a tight corner before and had always managed to cope.; It is a great pressure, requiring a lot of effort and sense of humour but does work in most cases, helping to find the best way out of a tight corner.

_source.definition_text: relating to a large company or group
_source.learnerexamples_text: corporate finance; This proposal highlights advisable amendments to the ABC Company's management structure, namely the marketing department, in view of unforeseen corporate losses.

_source.definition_text: a large company or group of companies that is controlled together as a single organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: a multinational corporation; the British Broadcasting Corporation; She didn't want to work for a big corporation where everything was so impersonal.; Since I was a child, I've always dreamed about being a car designer in a large and powerful corporation like Ferrari, Porsche, Mercedes-Benz, etc.

_source.definition_text: a dead person's body
_source.learnerexamples_text: There were several corpses in the building.; Evian and I just stood there and gazed at the corpse for a few hours.

_source.definition_text: to show someone the mistakes in something they have said or written
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our teacher normally corrects our pronunciation.; Until now, I have never had someone really teaching me and correcting my mistakes.

_source.definition_text: accurate, or having no mistakes
_source.learnerexamples_text: a correct answer; Check that you have the correct information.; Is that the correct spelling?; "Your name is Angela Black?" "That is correct."; I must learn more [from] English people [so] that I hear correct English.

_source.definition_text: suitable for a particular situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: correct behaviour; I think that is the correct option because I really like this [kind of] film!

_source.definition_text: to make a mistake or problem right or better
_source.learnerexamples_text: The new software finds and corrects any errors on the hard disk.; For example if I have to write a formal letter or something like this, I use my 'PC' because the paper looks nicer and [the] computer corrects my mistakes.

_source.definition_text: a change made to something in order to correct or improve it, or when you make such a change
_source.learnerexamples_text: I made some corrections before handing in my essay.; She was disappointed to see her essay returned with a mass of corrections in red ink.; My new teacher is friendlier and he is more careful [with his] correction [of] the work and exams we do.

_source.definition_text: in a correct way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have I pronounced your name correctly?; I don't speak English correctly.

_source.definition_text: to be the same or very similar
_source.learnerexamples_text: The money I've saved corresponds roughly to the amount I need for my course.; The American FBI corresponds to the British MI5.; His story of what happened that night didn't correspond with the witness's version.; Therefore, I would like to ask you for my entrance fee, as this evening did not correspond to your advertisement.

_source.definition_text: similar or related
_source.learnerexamples_text: Draw a line between the words with corresponding meanings.; In terms of the consequences for society as a whole, an increase in life expectancy might pose problems if the percentage of old people increases without being accompanied by a corresponding increase in the birth rate.

_source.definition_text: to communicate with someone by writing letters
_source.learnerexamples_text: They had corresponded ever since the war.; Dear Tom It would be wonderful to see you because we've been corresponding for a long time but I've never had [the] pleasure [of meeting] you.

_source.definition_text: a long passage in a building or train
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her office is at the end of the corridor.; The invigilator left the room and walked down the corridor looking for some help.

_source.definition_text: dishonest or illegal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a corrupt government ; I am not saying he is corrupt - I don't believe that - but he com[m]ands many corrupt people.

_source.definition_text: to make someone or something become dishonest or immoral
_source.learnerexamples_text: He became corrupted by power and money. ; Maybe wealth can corrupt people's mind[s] and make people weak.

_source.definition_text: when you cause someone or something to become dishonest or immoral
_source.learnerexamples_text: the corruption of innocent young children; The contrast between those two groups was getting bigger and bigger and it ended up [in] a destructive war, destructive doesn't refer only to deaths and city damage but also to the corruption of morals.

_source.definition_text: dishonest or immoral behaviour, usually by people in positions of power
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was arrested for corruption and bribery.; I think that both have lost respect because of corruption.

_source.definition_text: consisting of people and things from many different countries
_source.learnerexamples_text: London is a very cosmopolitan city.; I chose London because it's a cosmopolitan city, and very near to the other European countries.

_source.definition_text: the amount of money that you need to buy or do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The cost of building materials has risen.; The cruise ship was built at a cost of $400 million.; Software is included at no extra cost.; The supermarket chain announced that it was cutting the cost of all its fresh and frozen meat.; The cost of living has gone up.

_source.definition_text: something that you give or lose, in order to get or achieve something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: He rescued four people at the cost of his own life.; She finally got the job she wanted, but at great personal cost.; It's not worth getting into an argument with Tim, as I learned to my cost.; We wanted to travel by car and, to my cost, my friend began to drive the car.

_source.definition_text: If something must be done at all costs, it is very important that it is done.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have to succeed at all costs.; One thing was sure: he was convinced [he had] to save Anne's life at all costs.

_source.definition_text: If something costs an amount of money, you must pay that amount to buy or do it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: How much did your bike cost?; The trip will cost you $1000.;  It costs a lot to buy a house in this part of London.; It cost me £200 just to get it fixed.; How much does it cost?

_source.definition_text: to cause someone to lose or destroy something valuable
_source.learnerexamples_text: Drinking and driving costs lives.; His affairs cost him his marriage.; However, many people are talking about car accidents which cost human lives.

_source.definition_text: a set of clothes worn in order to look like someone else, especially for a party or a film or play
_source.learnerexamples_text: actors in costume; a clown costume; The children were dressed in Halloween costumes.; Everything becomes alive with music and dancing, and everybody wears amazing costumes.

_source.definition_text: the set of clothes typical of a particular country or period of history
_source.learnerexamples_text: Japanese national costume; You also can take some terrific [ph]otographs of national costumes, hear music and take part in dances.

_source.definition_text: comfortable and warm
_source.learnerexamples_text: This room is nice and cosy in the winter.; He showed me into a cosy little room.; I have a very tiny but cosy bedroom.

_source.definition_text: a small house, usually in the countryside
_source.learnerexamples_text: They live in a country cottage, with roses round the door.; I live in a typical Norwegian cottage with a huge fireplace, and everything is natural and simple.

_source.definition_text: cloth or thread made from the fibres of the cotton plant
_source.learnerexamples_text: a shirt made of pure cotton;  a simple cotton dress; a reel of cotton ; Normally, I would prefer my blouses to be made of cotton or silk as these materials make me [feel] comfortable.

_source.definition_text: to force air out of your lungs through your throat with a short loud sound
_source.learnerexamples_text: The smoke made me cough.; I coughed all night long.; I kept coughing, my nose kept running!

_source.definition_text: when you cough or an illness that makes you cough
_source.learnerexamples_text: a dry cough; Emily has a nasty cough.; Because of swimming so much I got a terrible cough and so I had to be sent back to school so that I could be treated properly.

_source.definition_text: used as the past form of 'can' to talk about what someone or something was able to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: When I was younger I could stay up all night and not get tired.; It was so noisy that we couldn't hear ourselves speak.; I couldn't find the information [either] but I phoned the school.

_source.definition_text: used for making a suggestion
_source.learnerexamples_text: We could go for a drink after work tomorrow, if you like.; You could always call Susie and see if she might babysit.; I could take you to a nice hotel.

_source.definition_text: used as a more polite form of 'can' when asking someone to provide something or do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you lend me £5?; Could you turn the music down a little, please?; Could you please send it?

_source.definition_text: used to talk about what will possibly happen or is possibly true
_source.learnerexamples_text: She could arrive any time now.; A lot of crime could be prevented.; This new drug could be an important step in the fight against cancer.; This could be a big advantage but on the other [hand], books contain more details and sometimes some parts of the book are cut out [in] the film.

_source.definition_text: used as a more polite form of 'can' when asking for permission
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could I speak to Mr Davis, please?; Excuse me, could I just say something here?; Could I bring you the missing work [to the] next class?

_source.definition_text: used to talk about things that possibly happened in the past or might possibly have happened by some time in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: She could have been killed.; Let's go to the coast anyway - the rain could have stopped by the time we get there.; Then they thought about the situation and tried to [develop] a theor[y] about what could have happened with the dead body and who could be the murderer.

_source.definition_text: used to express certainty that something in the past was impossible or didn't happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: He couldn't have damaged your bike - he was with me all evening.; That book couldn't have been on sale last week - it's only come out today!; The blood froze in our veins, and we were all sure that it couldn't have been anything but a ghost!

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that someone is not interested in or worried about something or someone
_source.searchterms_text: could;i/he etc couldn't care less;i/he, etc. couldn't care less
_source.learnerexamples_text: I couldn't care less what people think.; There was hunger, there was poverty and the king couldn't care less about his people['s] well-being.

_source.definition_text: the group of people elected to govern a particular area, town or city, and organize services for it
_source.learnerexamples_text: Edinburgh City Council; The local council has/have decided not to allocate funds for the project.; The town/city council is/are responsible for keeping the streets clean.; Rubbish collecting needs to be arranged more regularly by the city council.

_source.definition_text: the job or process of listening to someone and giving them advice about their problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: a counselling service; As well as providing [a] speci[a]list counselling service by experienced social work[er]s, each member of the society needs to create [a] warm welcoming atmosphere for those who once were [rejected by] the society.

_source.definition_text: someone whose job is to listen to people and give them advice about their problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: I saw a counsellor to help me with my anxiety.; It is a burden to society, which has to find a way to create jobs, to employ counsellors to help problem unemployed and to watch out for the safety of the society.

_source.definition_text: to see how many people or things there are
_source.learnerexamples_text: The teachers counted the students as they got on to the coach.; Count your money carefully to make sure it's all there.; We're still waiting for the votes to be counted (up).; I counted them and there were 5 suitcases.

_source.definition_text: to say numbers in their correct order
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you count to ten in French?; What he told me is "If you have any wishes, count 1 to 100 every Sunday for one month".

_source.definition_text: to be important
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've always believed that happiness counts more than money.; My opinion doesn't count for anything around here.; It wasn't romantic, there were no flowers but Carla knew [that] what counts is in the h[e]art.

_source.definition_text: to be accepted or allowed as part of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've been to sixteen different countries, but I only spent half an hour in Luxembourg, so that doesn't really count.

_source.definition_text: to think of someone or something in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She counted Tim as her closest friend.; You should count yourself lucky you weren't hurt.; In a way, I think I should count myself very lucky.

_source.definition_text: to include something or someone in a calculation
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are 1500 people at my school, counting teachers.; It was not until I married Paul that I began to receive a bunch of telephone calls from my closest relatives, not counting my mother because she had [already] become a part of our house.

_source.definition_text: to include someone in an activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you're going for a pizza, you can count me in.; I can always count her in. She is always there by my side.

_source.definition_text: to have confidence in someone because you know they will do what you want

_source.definition_text: to expect something to happen and make plans based on it
