_source.definition_text: when someone performs or presents something to the public for the first time
_source.learnerexamples_text: She made her debut as a pianist in 1975.;  This is the band's debut album.; Pavarotti's grand debut took place in the Royal Theatre of Reggio Emilia.

_source.definition_text: a period of ten years, especially a period such as 1860 to 1869, or 1990 to 1999
_source.learnerexamples_text: The building was due to be knocked down decades ago.; Life has centred around fast food chains during the last decade and continues to do so.

_source.definition_text: Decaffeinated tea or coffee is made by removing the caffeine.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could I have a decaffeinated coffee, please?

_source.definition_text: when something decays
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many of the buildings had fallen into decay.; Furthermore, by having tourism, the authorities of the country will be obliged to rest[ore] any monuments which have fallen into decay.

_source.definition_text: to become gradually damaged or to cause something to become gradually damaged
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sugar makes your teeth decay.; Pollution has decayed the surface of the stonework on the front of the cathedral.; The historic buildings are starting to decay.

_source.definition_text: someone who has died
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police have not yet informed the family of the deceased.; The deceased was a 19-year-old girl who had run away from home some months ago.

_source.definition_text: dead
_source.learnerexamples_text: the deceased man's belongings; A picture of a deceased family member brings back lots of memor[ies].

_source.definition_text: to make someone believe something that is not true
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company deceived customers by selling old computers as new ones.; The sound of the door closing deceived me into thinking they had gone out.; So if you don't want to feel deceived or offended, think twice before you decide to go shopping.

_source.definition_text: the twelfth and last month of the year
_source.learnerexamples_text: 23(rd) December/December 23(rd); Their baby was born last December.; Jonathan finishes his course next December.; My parents got married in/during December.; It was one of the coldest Decembers ever.

_source.definition_text: of a satisfactory quality or level
_source.learnerexamples_text: He earns a decent salary.; I haven't had a decent cup of coffee since I've been here.; I think it's a decent place for us to stay for a night.

_source.definition_text: honest and morally good
_source.learnerexamples_text: Decent people have had their lives ruined by his behaviour.; She should do the decent thing and apologize.; In fact, it had such [a] bad reputation that nobody "decent" went there any longer.

_source.definition_text: If something is deceptive, it makes you believe something that is not true.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Appearances can be deceptive.; One should also remember another common, albeit wise phrase: appearances can be deceptive.

_source.definition_text: when you make someone believe something that is not true
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was found guilty of obtaining money by deception. ; On the other hand, his deception means that he betrayed his own nation.

_source.definition_text: to be the reason or situation that makes a particular result happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: This match will decide the tournament.; At any rate, science will decide whether it is better to live longer.

_source.definition_text: to choose something after thinking about several possibilities
_source.learnerexamples_text: They have to decide by next Friday.; I don't mind which one we have - you decide.; In the end, we decided to go to the theatre.; She decided (that) she would retire to the country.; I can't decide what to do.

_source.definition_text: a choice that you make about something after thinking about several possibilities
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has had to make some very difficult decisions.; The company will reach/come to/make a decision shortly.; Let me have a/your decision by next week.; It was his decision to leave.; We need to take a lot of factors into account in our decision-making.

_source.definition_text: the thing that helps to make the final decision
_source.learnerexamples_text: Cost was the deciding factor in choosing these builders.; Personally, I think the quality of teachers, school reputation and facilities should be the deciding factor for parents [for] which schools their children should be educated in.

_source.definition_text: able to make decisions quickly and confidently, or showing this quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: You need to be more decisive.; a decisive reply; They were attractive, handsome, brave and decisive men.

_source.definition_text: strongly affecting how a situation will progress or end
_source.learnerexamples_text: a decisive goal/victory; Seeing that advertisement was a decisive moment in my life.; Recently, our Board of Executives has taken a decisive step: from now on, our clothes will also be available for purchase on the Internet!

_source.definition_text: the flat area of a ship or boat that is not covered
_source.learnerexamples_text: We sat on deck until it was dark.; When I woke up and went on the deck, I saw the skipper who [was coming] back from the village in the small boat.

_source.definition_text: in a decisive way
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to act decisively.; Putting your foot down quickly and decisively before things really get out of hand seems sensible.

_source.definition_text: an announcement, often one that is written and official
_source.learnerexamples_text: a declaration of independence; Indochina is a French film that deals with the colonial period in Indochina from the Second World War to the country['s] declaration of independence.

_source.definition_text: to announce something publicly or officially
_source.learnerexamples_text: They declared their support for the proposal.; America declared war on Japan in 1941.; The country declared independence in 1952.; We should declare [the city centre] a pedestrian zone.

_source.definition_text: to officially tell someone the value of goods you have bought, or the amount of money you have earned, because you might have to pay tax
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you got anything to declare?

_source.definition_text: to gradually become less or worse
_source.learnerexamples_text: His interest in the project declined after his wife died.; The party's popularity has declined in the opinion polls.; It had slightly declined to about 88 per cent in 1992.

_source.definition_text: to refuse politely
_source.learnerexamples_text: I invited him to the meeting but he declined.; He declined my offer.; We thank you for your offer of accommodation, but we decline it.

_source.definition_text: when something becomes less in amount, importance, quality or strength
_source.learnerexamples_text: industrial decline; Home cooking seems to be on the/in decline.; a sharp decline in sales; She seemed to be recovering and then she went into a decline.; For the 25-34 age group, a decline can be seen from 2006 to 2010.

_source.definition_text: to add attractive things to an object or place, often for a special day or period
_source.learnerexamples_text: They decorated the wedding car with ribbons and flowers.; The church always is decorated with beautiful flowers and other things.

_source.definition_text: to put paint or paper on the walls or other surfaces of a room
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're going to decorate the kitchen next week.; I hate the smell of paint when I'm decorating.; It is all decorated in blue.

_source.definition_text: when the walls or other surfaces of rooms or buildings are covered with paint or paper
_source.learnerexamples_text: This place is badly in need of decoration.; I will start with the new decoration [of] my bedroom next week.

_source.definition_text: something that you put on something to make it look attractive or special, or the activity of putting things on something to make it look more attractive or special
_source.learnerexamples_text: Christmas/party/table/cake decorations; He's good at cake decoration.; In November I joined a day course to learn how to make Christmas decorations.

_source.definition_text: to become less, or to make something become less
_source.learnerexamples_text: During the summer months, rainfall decreases.; The aim to satisfy different interests should not [allow] the quality [to] decrease.

_source.definition_text: made to look attractive
_source.learnerexamples_text: a decorative display of plants and flowers; a mirror in a decorative frame; It seems that the decorative role of clothes will have disappeared by the year 2050.

_source.definition_text: a reduction
_source.learnerexamples_text: There has been a steady decrease in the number of visitors.; Their yellow and black stripe has a mysterious beauty (which is the main reason for the huge decrease [in the] tiger population).

_source.definition_text: to give most of your energy and time to something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has dedicated her life to helping others. ; I have been interested in these matters but due to my lack of time, I haven't been able to dedicate myself to this investigation.

_source.definition_text: believing that something is very important and giving a lot of time and energy to it
_source.learnerexamples_text: a dedicated teacher; I myself am a totally dedicated sports fan and I believe that basketball is the greatest sport on this earth.

_source.definition_text: designed to be used for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: a dedicated news channel; I require a 2 bedroomed flat with a dedicated parking space.

_source.definition_text: to say that something you have made or done is to show your love or respect for someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: This book is dedicated to my daughter.; This story is dedicated to my sister to whom I can only feel deep admiration.

_source.definition_text: when you are willing to give a lot of time and energy to something because you believe it is very important
_source.learnerexamples_text: She thanked the staff for their dedication and enthusiasm.; Sacrifice and self-denial are cornerstones, together with dedication and commitment to a good cause.

_source.definition_text: when an amount or a part of something is taken away from a total, or the amount that is taken
_source.learnerexamples_text: tax deductions; After the deduction of 5% administration expense and 10% entertainment cost, we contributed the remaining 85% of the surplus to the local hospital.

_source.definition_text: to decide that something is true using the available information
_source.learnerexamples_text: From the contents of his shopping basket, I deduced that he was single.; Two important results are deduced from these figures: living standards in the U.K. have improved dramatically over the last century, and women can be expected to live longer than men.

_source.definition_text: when you decide something using the available information
_source.learnerexamples_text: I worked out the facts by a process of deduction.; My deductions obviously went further, and I found relie[f in] thinking that neither [was] the story real nor [had] the lost diary even existed.

_source.definition_text: to judge or consider something in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: The book was deemed to be unsuitable for children. ; Were it not for the fact that we regard our job as adequately paid and providing sufficient free time, it could not be deemed a satisfactory one.

_source.definition_text: having a long distance from the top to the bottom
_source.learnerexamples_text: a deep river/sea/lake ; The water's not deep here - look, I can touch the bottom.; The water's only ankle-/knee-/waist-deep, so we'll be able to get across the river easily.; That place [is] good for families too, because [the] water is not so deep but warm.

_source.definition_text: A deep colour is strong and dark.
_source.learnerexamples_text: deep purple; He is tall and has got black hair and beautiful deep brown eyes.

_source.definition_text: A deep sound is low.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a wonderfully deep voice ; "I'm not Gary," a strange and deep voice answered, "I'm someone who wants to warn you that tomorrow, you are going to die."

_source.definition_text: A deep feeling or experience is very strong.
_source.learnerexamples_text: deep regret ; Their son has been a deep disappointment to them.; I fell into a deep depression, and took an extremely long time to recover.

_source.definition_text: to fill your lungs with air
_source.learnerexamples_text: Take a deep breath and relax.; But if you took a deep breath after reading the question, don't worry.

_source.definition_text: one metre/6 ft, etc. from the top to the bottom, or from the front to the back
_source.searchterms_text: deep;deeper;deepest;one metre/6 ft etc deep;one metre/6 ft, etc. deep
_source.learnerexamples_text: This end of the pool is two metres deep.; Her father's friend, who is a professional scuba-diver, invited her to do her first immers[i]on on the reefs, 15 met[res] deep.

_source.definition_text: when someone is sleeping in a way that makes it difficult to wake them up
_source.learnerexamples_text: He fell into a deep sleep.; And then, he fell to a deep sleep, putting his sack next to him.

_source.definition_text: serious and difficult for most people to understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: a deep and meaningful conversation; I think we really need to go back to the classics to re[ce]ive something from the deep thinkers.

_source.definition_text: giving all of your attention to what you are thinking or talking about, and not noticing anything else
_source.learnerexamples_text: I noticed that Ali and Ben were deep in conversation.; He was deep in thought, chewing on something brown and rectangular.

_source.definition_text: a long way into something from the top or outside
_source.learnerexamples_text: They travelled deep into the forest.; He thrust his hands deep in(to) his pockets.; I just fall deep into the story, into the writer's own world.

_source.base_text: throw sb in at the deep end
_source.definition_text: to make someone start a new and difficult job or activity without helping them or preparing them for it
_source.searchterms_text: deep;deeper;deepest;throw sb in at the deep end
_source.learnerexamples_text: My first job was to organise a huge conference - they really threw me in at the deep end!; Sometimes we can be thrown in at the deep end and have qualms about making a decision.

_source.definition_text: If you know or feel something deep down, you are certain that it is true, or you feel it strongly although you do not admit it or show it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Deep down, I knew that I was right.; No, because I [feel] deep down that it's wrong to put animals behind bars.

_source.definition_text: If a feeling or a problem goes deep, it is very strong or serious and has existed for a long time.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hostility between the two nations runs deep.

_source.definition_text: to become worse or stronger, or to make something become worse or stronger
_source.learnerexamples_text: The economic crisis has deepened.; My frustration was deepened by the fact that the day before I had written in the diary some libellous remarks concerning my parents.

_source.definition_text: if someone's knowledge or understanding deepens, it increases.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It certainly helped to deepen my understanding of the situation.; Furthermore, not only can travelling give you an opp[o]rtunity to make a lot of friends, but your knowledge about this world could be broadened and deepened by travelling.

_source.definition_text: extremely or strongly
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm deeply grateful to you.; He found her comments deeply irritating/annoying/offensive.; We don't want to get too deeply involved with these people.; After 20 years of marriage, they're still deeply in love.; I was deeply impressed by the long-term cooperation between the zoo and the school.

_source.definition_text: a large, wild animal that is sometimes hunted for food and has antlers (= long horns) if it is male
_source.learnerexamples_text: a deer park ; It would be even nicer if there would be some wildlife in the par[k], like deer, walking free all over.

_source.definition_text: to cause someone or something to fail
_source.learnerexamples_text: The proposal to change the rules was narrowly defeated by 201 votes to 196.; I'm afraid anything that involves language learning has always defeated me.; But it was useless, Tina's friends had defeated their plan, and her.

_source.definition_text: to win a victory over someone in a fight, war or competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: Napoleon was defeated by the Duke of Wellington at the battle of Waterloo.; If we can defeat the Italian team, we'll be through to the final.; I still remember when Marcelo became [number] 1 in 1998 after he defeated Andre Agassi in the final of the "fifth Grand Slam".

_source.definition_text: when someone or something is made to fail
_source.learnerexamples_text: At the last General Election, they suffered a massive defeat.; The company was not ready to admit defeat.; After long negotiations with the police, Linda admitted defeat and gave up.

_source.definition_text: when someone loses against someone else in a fight, war or competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: After their defeat in battle, the soldiers surrendered.; Norwich City have suffered their worst defeat of the season.; The whole team will face serious problems, which may lead to big defeats.

_source.definition_text: a fault or problem with someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: genetic defects;  A mechanical defect caused the plane to crash.; There are also people that are overweight and it is not their own fault, because they suffer from genetic defects.

_source.definition_text: not in good condition or not working correctly
_source.learnerexamples_text: defective goods; The electric instal[l]ations are defective, some locks are broken, and the ceil[ing] leaks. Under these conditions, it's no wonder the library has no visitors.

_source.definition_text: the part of a sports team which tries to prevent the other team from scoring points
_source.learnerexamples_text: I play best in defence.; I did basketball exercises for defence.

_source.definition_text: protection or support against attack, criticism or infection
_source.learnerexamples_text: When Helen criticized me, Chris came/rushed to my defence.; She argued strongly in defence of her actions.; A good diet helps build the body's natural defences.; Movie stars like Brigitte Bardot started strong campai[g]ns against zoos as part of wider battles in defence of animal rights.

_source.definition_text: the weapons and military forces that a country uses to protect itself against attack
_source.learnerexamples_text: Government spending on defence is increasing.; the defence industry; [The] USA spent only 2% of money on education; it spent quite a large amount of money on defence (18%).

_source.definition_text: the lawyers in a court who work in support of the person who is accused of a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was cross-examined by the defence.; a defence lawyer; One good turn deserves another so Anne decided to influence somehow [the] counsel for the defence.

_source.definition_text: to support someone or something that is being criticized
_source.learnerexamples_text: The newspaper's editor defended his decision to publish the photos.; They are fighting to defend their beliefs/interests/rights.; Do we know a lot of people nowadays who would be able to take the risk of being a prisoner for 10 or 20 years "just" to defend his beliefs?

_source.definition_text: to protect someone or something from being attacked, especially by fighting
_source.learnerexamples_text: How can we defend our homeland if we don't have an army?; I'm going to karate lessons to learn how to defend myself.; White blood cells help defend the body against infection.; In the fourth one, you learn to defend yourself by doing Karate and in the last section, you could learn fencing.

_source.definition_text: to try to show in a court that someone is not guilty of a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has hired two lawyers to defend him in court.; An in[n]ocent man is arrested and the court ap[p]oints an attorney to defend him.

_source.definition_text: someone in a sports team who tries to prevent the other team from scoring points, goals, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Brazilian attack put France's defenders under pressure.; I'm mostly a defender, so scoring a goal for the first time gave me great pleasure!

_source.definition_text: a mistake or fault in something so that it is not good enough
_source.learnerexamples_text: Parents are complaining of serious deficiencies in the education system.; By studying the effects of rain and ways to handle the expected amount of water, one can plan the laying out of the new roads and correct the deficiencies in the present ones.

_source.definition_text: quick to protect yourself from being criticized
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's very defensive about his weight. ; And because the traveller's own value system is challenged, he reacts in a defensive way.

_source.definition_text: when you do not have enough of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a vitamin deficiency; Anaemia, protein deficiency and vitamin deficiency [are] common problem[s] in vegetarians.

_source.definition_text: the amount by which the money that you spend is more than the money that you receive
_source.learnerexamples_text: a budget deficit; Unfortunately, this could not be fulfilled by the government due to a huge budget deficit.

_source.definition_text: to say exactly what something means, or what someone or something is like
_source.learnerexamples_text: In the dictionary 'reality' is defined as 'the state of things as they are, rather than as they are imagined to be'.; Your duties are clearly defined in the contract.; I guess you would have to define the word 'fit' to answer that question.

_source.definition_text: certain, fixed and not likely to change
_source.learnerexamples_text: The date for the meeting - is that definite?; We need a definite answer by tomorrow.; I'm really excited about your definite plans to come.

_source.definition_text: the grammatical name for the word 'the' in English, or the words in other languages which have a similar use
_source.learnerexamples_text: 'The City', referring to the financial area of London, takes a definite article.

_source.definition_text: without any doubt
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you definitely decided to go to America?; He definitely said he'd be here.; So if I were you, I would definitely stay in the city.

_source.definition_text: used after an adverb in short, negative replies
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Do you think the work will be finished by June?" "Definitely not."; That's nice, but do you think that money is all that matters? Definitely not!

_source.definition_text: how clear an image of something is in a photograph or on a screen
_source.learnerexamples_text: high-definition TV; There is a slight loss of definition in the picture quality on transfer.; And, do not forget to appreciate the keyboard work from the legendary Tony Banks, and the spectacular guitar-playing from Mike Rutherford, all of them surrounded by three huge high-definition screens.

_source.definition_text: an explanation of the meaning of a word or phrase
_source.learnerexamples_text: a dictionary definition; What is the definition of 'mood'?; He tried to give a definition of friendship.

_source.definition_text: to refuse to obey someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Some of these children openly defy their teachers.; Jack was the only one, or the most conspic[u]ous of all, to defy him.

_source.definition_text: certain, clear, and not likely to change
_source.learnerexamples_text: a definitive answer; I know many people who offer easy and definitive answers to every question.

_source.definition_text: to be impossible to believe/describe/explain, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: His attitude defies belief. ; The horror of th[ose] endless days, when the whole family was as if in suspension not knowing the final diagnosis, defies any description.

_source.definition_text: a unit for measuring temperature, shown by the symbol ° written after a number
_source.learnerexamples_text: Water boils at 212 degrees Fahrenheit and 100 degrees Celsius/Centigrade.; Today it is very windy and too cold for bathing, just about 15 degrees.

_source.definition_text: a qualification given for completing a university course
_source.learnerexamples_text: "What degree did you do at York?" "Geography."; She's got a physics degree/a degree in physics from Oxford.; I completed my languages degree course at U.P.N University.

_source.definition_text: an amount or level of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: This job demands a high degree of skill.; A good society depends on the degree to which people are able to trust each other.; Can you imagine the degree of pollution you absorb in crossing London every morning by bicycle?

_source.definition_text: to make something happen at a later time than originally planned or expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: My plane was delayed by an hour.; Could we delay the meeting a few days?; The bus was delayed and I decided to go on foot.

_source.definition_text: a small level or amount of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was some degree of truth in what she said.; The plan involves a degree of risk, but it is worth trying.; Nevertheless, some degree of freedom is obviously necessary for [the] healthy development of a young individual.

_source.definition_text: when you have to wait longer than expected for something to happen, or the time that you have to wait
_source.learnerexamples_text: An accident caused long delays on the motorway.; There has been a delay in the book's publication.; It was terrible at Heathrow airport because my flight had a delay of over two hours.

_source.definition_text: to cause someone or something to be slow or late
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was delayed by traffic.; The roads were crowded with a lot of traffic, so I got really delayed.

_source.definition_text: immediately
_source.learnerexamples_text: This problem needs to be dealt with without delay.; Firstly, the programme began on time at midday without delay.

_source.definition_text: someone who is sent somewhere to represent a group of people, especially at a meeting
_source.learnerexamples_text: The delegates were all given badges to wear.; I participated at the opening of the new Arts Centre as a delegate from my college.

_source.definition_text: to give someone else part of your work or some of your responsibilities
_source.learnerexamples_text: He needs to learn to delegate or he'll never get everything done.; Let me call him Mr. X. His success is based on various qualities of modern leadership: he delegates as much responsibility as possible to subordinates and gives them all competence to carry out their tasks.

_source.definition_text: a group of people who have been chosen to represent a much larger group of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: a delegation of Chinese officials; For instance, two weeks ago I had to go to Kiev to work as a translator with a delegation at the Ukrainian Central Bank.

_source.definition_text: to remove something, especially from a computer's memory
_source.learnerexamples_text: All names have been deleted from the report.; I didn't take notice of [the email] and deleted it again.

_source.definition_text: done intentionally or planned
_source.learnerexamples_text: a deliberate attack/insult/lie;  This was a deliberate attempt to mislead us.; I'm sure that his deliberate intention with this was to make us get closer.

_source.definition_text: soft, light or gentle
_source.learnerexamples_text: a delicate flavour; a delicate shade of pink; She liked his delicate skin and his body's warmth.

_source.definition_text: intentionally
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm sure he says these things deliberately to annoy me.; Many of them choose the bicycle deliberately, just to have at least a small amount of exercise before and after [the] hours they spend sitting at their desks.

_source.definition_text: needing to be handled with great care or skill
_source.learnerexamples_text: I need to speak to you about a rather delicate matter/question.; The pay negotiations have reached a delicate point/stage.; Repairing damaged nerves is a very delicate operation/process.; Being aware of the two proposals our local government is considering in order to solve the apparently unavoidable matter of traffic in our beloved city, I feel compelled to offer my views on such a delicate subject.

_source.definition_text: easy to damage or break
_source.learnerexamples_text: delicate china; Delicate plants need to be kept in a greenhouse during the winter.; Although you told me I can make use of anything, I'd like to make sure that it isn't a problem to use such delicate things as the computer and the CD player?

_source.definition_text: having a thin, attractive shape
_source.learnerexamples_text: delicate hands; Suddenly a shadow moved among the trees and a surprisingly beautiful and delicate woman walked towards me.

_source.definition_text: having a very pleasant taste or smell
_source.learnerexamples_text: a delicious cake; The delicious smell of freshly-made coffee came from the kitchen.; This wine is delicious.; I love it because they make delicious hamburgers.

_source.definition_text: (something or someone that gives) great pleasure, satisfaction or happiness
_source.learnerexamples_text: The children screamed with delight.; My sister's little boy is a real delight.; I read your letter with great delight.; He seems to take great delight in teasing his sister.; At midnight fireworks covered the concert hall and I, as well as the rest of [the] spectators, felt excitement and delight.

_source.definition_text: very pleased
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're delighted with our new house.; I was delighted at/by your news.; I'm absolutely delighted that you can come.; We'd be delighted to come to dinner on Friday.; I've just seen your letter and I'm really delighted to have won the first prize in your competition.

_source.definition_text: very pleasant, attractive, or enjoyable
_source.learnerexamples_text: We had a delightful evening.; A table was laid with a lot of delightful food and a beautiful cake was in the centre of it.

_source.definition_text: to take things such as goods, letters and parcels to people's houses or places of work
_source.learnerexamples_text: Mail is delivered to our office twice a day.; The shop is delivering our new bed on Thursday.; You have to deliver newspapers to the town centre's shops.

_source.definition_text: to speak formally to a group of people
_source.searchterms_text: deliver;deliver a speech/talk etc;deliver a speech/talk, etc.;delivered;delivering;delivers
_source.learnerexamples_text: The priest delivered a passionate speech against war.; Then, he delivered a speech to the public.

_source.definition_text: when things such as goods, letters, or parcels are taken to people's houses or places of work
_source.learnerexamples_text: a delivery van ; We get two deliveries of mail a day.; You can pay for the carpet on delivery.; We expect to take delivery of our new car next week.; I called for a delivery [from] Pizza Hut and after that went to study.

_source.definition_text: to achieve or do something that you have promised to do, or that people expect you to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company failed to deliver the high-quality service that we expect.; I can also help as a team-leader to help others to deliver the right services.

_source.definition_text: to need something such as time or effort
_source.learnerexamples_text: This job demands a high level of concentration.; I would say that driving a car demands a lot of responsibility.

_source.definition_text: to ask for something in a way that shows that you do not expect to be refused
_source.learnerexamples_text: I demanded an explanation.; I demand to see the manager.; She demanded that he return the books he borrowed from her.; I demand a full refund or I will be forced to take this matter further.

_source.definition_text: a strong request
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can't give in to children's demands all the time.; The government is unlikely to agree to the rebels' demands for independence.; They received a final demand for payment.; Of course only when my demands are logical.

_source.definition_text: a need for something to be sold or supplied
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was little demand for tickets.; I believe we [have] to stop the demand for ivory!

_source.definition_text: wanted or needed in large numbers
_source.learnerexamples_text: Good teachers are always in demand.; Nevertheless, people will always use cars and vehicles, so petrol will always be in demand.

_source.definition_text: needing a lot of time, attention or energy
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's a very demanding child.; a demanding job ; Although the job was demanding I enjoyed it.

_source.definition_text: a system of government in which people elect their leaders, or a country with this system
_source.learnerexamples_text: The early 1990s saw the spread of democracy in Eastern Europe.; From then on it represented democracy and freedom until Hitler took over power in January 1933.

_source.definition_text: to completely destroy a building, especially in order to use the land for something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: A number of houses were demolished so that the supermarket could be built.; The building was demolished, and so was the dream of a house of the[ir] own.

_source.definition_text: based on the principles of democracy
_source.learnerexamples_text: We must accept the results of a democratic election.; If we regard ourselves as modern people, we must be democratic enough to release them.

_source.definition_text: to show that an idea or argument is wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: He completely demolished my argument.

_source.definition_text: to show or prove that something exists or is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: These problems demonstrate the importance of strategic planning.; These figures clearly demonstrate the size of the economic problem facing the country.; Research has demonstrated that babies can recognize their mother's voice very soon after birth.; The results were amazing, the group man[a]ged to demonstrate that the learning capacity increased a lot with respect to traditional methods.

_source.definition_text: to march or stand with a group of people to show that you disagree with or support someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thousands of people gathered to demonstrate against the new proposals for universities.; Maybe the RSPCA should demonstrate, to show that it's not [accept]able. We have to stand up for their rights! Yesterday I heard that animal rights activists have met the prime minister.

_source.definition_text: to show something and explain how it works
_source.learnerexamples_text: The teacher demonstrated how to use the equipment.; He's got a job demonstrating kitchen equipment in a department store.; I could demonstrate to people how to create compost pits and use kitchen waste to generate compost for their gardens.

_source.definition_text: to express or show that you have a feeling, quality, or ability
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has demonstrated a genuine interest in the project.; As a result, he does not allow himself to demonstrate any emotion apart from anger.

_source.definition_text: when a group of people march or stand together to show that they disagree with or support something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: The students are holding a demonstration to protest against the increase in their fees.; Protesters staged an anti-war demonstration in front of the US embassy.; There were many demonstrations and violence.

_source.definition_text: showing how to do something, or how something works
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let me give you a demonstration of how the camera works.; a cooking demonstration; Some of our workers will give you a demonstration on how they produce, step by step, some of the world's best-known rings and necklaces.

_source.definition_text: when you say that something is not true
_source.learnerexamples_text: a denial of his guilt; Although everyone past forty claims to be reli[e]ved not to be twenty anymore, most of them miss the excitement of the days when everything was less serious, when fun was [a] top priority and responsibilities lost somewhere close to denial.

_source.definition_text: proof that something exists or is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: This disaster is a clear demonstration of the need for tighter controls.; Most women are now allowed to wear trousers and this is a demonstration of the change of women's role in society throughout the years.

_source.definition_text: thick, strong, cotton cloth, often blue in colour, used especially for making jeans
_source.learnerexamples_text: a denim jacket and jeans; If you have time to go shopping you could buy me a pair of blue denim jeans (size 30).

_source.definition_text: with a lot of things close together
_source.learnerexamples_text: England was once a densely wooded country.; Mexico City is one of the most densely populated cities in the world.; It's densely populated and with that the ugliness [of] densely populated places follows.

_source.definition_text: thick and difficult to see through
_source.learnerexamples_text: dense fog ; a dense forest; "Don't [be afraid] and don't run" shouted someone from the dense forest.

_source.definition_text: relating to the teeth
_source.learnerexamples_text: dental treatment ; In Kingsthorp you have lots of GPs and dental surger[ie]s.

_source.definition_text: the number of people or things in a place when compared with the size of the place
_source.learnerexamples_text: The area has a high population density.; However, the factors of population density and transport systems in some regions must not be ignored during this analysis.

_source.definition_text: someone who examines and repairs teeth
_source.learnerexamples_text: You should have your teeth checked by a dentist at least twice a year.; She is a dentist and can speak several languages.

_source.definition_text: to say that something is not true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Neil denies that he broke the window, but I'm sure he did.; Neil denies breaking the window.; We cannot deny that technology has changed our lives.

_source.definition_text: to not allow someone to have or do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her request for time off work was denied.; No one should be denied a good education.; The goalkeeper denied him his third goal.; I was denied the opportunity of learning French at school.; Should wild animals be kept in cages, and denied their freedom so that we can have the pleasure of watching them at zoos?

_source.definition_text: a substance that you put on your body to prevent or hide unpleasant smells
_source.learnerexamples_text: I always use deodorant.; On the other hand, men require regular supplies of shaving lotions, shampoo, deodorant, and many more [things] too.

_source.definition_text: to go away or leave, especially on a journey
_source.learnerexamples_text: The plane departs at 6.00 a.m.; The train for London departs from Platform 2.; The boat departs from King's Bridge.

_source.definition_text: a large shop divided into several different parts, each of which sells different things
_source.learnerexamples_text: First we'll go to May's department store, because things are so cheap [there].

_source.definition_text: a part of an organization such as a school, business or government which deals with a particular area of study or work
_source.learnerexamples_text: the geography department/the department of geography; The accounts department is/are having a Christmas party this week.; the Department of Health and Social Security; Then we went down to [the] Design and Technology department and [the] English department.

_source.definition_text: used to say that you are not certain about something because other things affect your answer
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Are you coming out tonight?" "It depends where  you're going."; It depends how you want to spend your holidays.

_source.definition_text: when someone or something leaves a place, especially to start a journey to another place
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are several departures for Paris every day.; Our departure was delayed because of bad weather.; departure time ; Now I am just waiting for the day of departure.

_source.definition_text: If something depends on someone or something, it is influenced by them, or changes because of them.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The choice depends on what you're willing to spend.; But, [o]n the other hand, you should explain to your parents what you want to do because you know that your decision depends on what they say.

_source.definition_text: to need the help and support of someone or something in order to exist or continue as before
_source.learnerexamples_text: She depends on her son for everything.; The country depends heavily on foreign aid.; I don't want to depend on my parents any more.

_source.definition_text: when you need someone or something all the time in order to exist or continue
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our society needs to reduce its dependence on the car.; The dependence on oil is a menace because oil reserves will disappear and because at this time we have no other invention to replace it.

_source.definition_text: to trust someone or something and know that they will help you or do what you want or expect them to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can always depend on Michael in a crisis.; I'm depending on you to keep your promise.; You can't always depend on the trains arriving on time.; I hope you'll let me join your foundation because I could be a member you can depend on.

_source.definition_text: needing the support of something or someone in order to continue existing or operating
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has three dependent children.; It's very easy to become dependent on sleeping pills.; If I went to school by car I would be dependent on my father.

_source.definition_text: to represent someone or something in a picture or story
_source.learnerexamples_text: The cartoon depicts the president as a vampire. ; A picture depicts an image that allows us different feelings, depending on the moment and the sensations we experienced while the picture was shot.

_source.definition_text: influenced by or decided by something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The amount of tax you pay is dependent on how much you earn.; The benefits for a traveller will be dependent upon the purpose for which someone travels.

_source.definition_text: a payment that you make immediately when you decide to buy something, as proof that you will really buy it
_source.learnerexamples_text: They've put down a deposit on a house.; How many days in advance do we have to make our reservation? I also wonder if there is a deposit that we have to pay.

_source.definition_text: an amount of money that you pay into a bank
_source.learnerexamples_text: to make a deposit; Now, you can [make a] deposit, have a record of your expenses, transfer funds from one account to another and even pay your credit card .

_source.definition_text: a layer of a substance that has developed from a natural or chemical process
_source.learnerexamples_text: deposits of iron ore; When these foods are taken in excess quantities, the digestive system converts the bits that are useful to the body and the rest are stored as fat deposits in different parts of the body.

_source.definition_text: to put money into a bank or valuable things into a safe place
_source.learnerexamples_text: She deposited $150,000 in a Swiss bank account.; Now, you can deposit [money], have a record of your expenses, transfer funds from one account to another and even pay your credit card.

_source.definition_text: an amount of money that you pay when you rent something, and that is given back to you when you return it without any damage
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did you get your deposit back?; I told the estate agent I was interested, paid my deposit and moved in within a week.

_source.definition_text: unhappy and without hope for the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: He seemed a bit depressed about his work situation.; She became deeply depressed when her husband died.; I felt depressed and decided to go to live in another city.

_source.definition_text: A depressed country, area, or economy does not have enough jobs or business activity.
_source.learnerexamples_text: an economically depressed area; Our area is getting closer to a depressed area rather than a peaceful and nice one.

_source.definition_text: making you feel unhappy and without hope for the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: I find this weather so depressing.; Her letter made depressing reading.;  It was very depressing watching the news on television tonight.;  It's depressing to think that we've got five more years of this government!; It was really depressing, seeing people drinking and having fun [when] I just had to work.

_source.definition_text: when you feel very unhappy, or a mental illness that makes you feel very unhappy and anxious for long periods
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you suffer from depression, it's best to get professional help.; My mum always worried about my sister because of her shyness and depression.

_source.definition_text: a time when there is not much business activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: The stock market crash marked the start of a severe depression.; We are just coming out of a financial depression, and companies have had to lay off thousands of people.

_source.definition_text: the state of not having enough of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: sleep deprivation; Often it has been seen that children suffering from extreme deprivation in their childhood can become deviant as they grow up.

_source.definition_text: not having enough food, money, and the things that you need to have a normal life
_source.learnerexamples_text: children from deprived backgrounds ; It is true that possibly, because of a deprived childhood in which every purchase had to be considered carefully, a person learns to manage his finances.

_source.definition_text: to take something, especially something necessary or pleasant, away from someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: He claimed that he had been deprived of his freedom/rights.; You can't function properly when you're deprived of sleep.; We shouldn't deprive our music fans of this wonderful event, that can only enrich our city's cultural life.

_source.definition_text: the distance down either from the top of something to the bottom, or to a distance below the top surface of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: the depth of a lake/pond; There are very few fish at depths below 3000 metres.; The river froze to a depth of over a metre.; But suddenly Laura did not feel any fear anymore and within a second she jumped into the air and fell into the endless depth of the Grand Canyon.

_source.definition_text: when you have serious qualities or the ability to think seriously about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Terry lacks depth - he's a very superficial person.; Her writing shows astonishing depth.; Jo has hidden depths.; I think that the main reason why someone has to read this book twice is the strength and depth of the two main characters: Donald Woods and Steve Biko.

_source.definition_text: in a very detailed way
_source.learnerexamples_text: With access to the Internet, students can do their homework in greater depth.; I would love to learn English in more depth during the summer.

_source.definition_text: not having the knowledge, experience, or skills to deal with a particular subject or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: When they start talking about philosophy, I'm completely out of my depth.; It was my first day of school. What I can remember is that I really felt out of my depth: my parents were so happy that I couldn't succeed in telling them that I was terribly frightened and that [the only] thing that I wanted was my doll.

_source.definition_text: how much someone knows or feels about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was amazed at the depth of his knowledge.; More and more people seem to take refuge in the depth of his philosophy now.

_source.definition_text: someone who has the second most important job in an organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: the deputy Prime Minister ; If you would like to have [a] teacher on your side, for general questions, I would propose our deputy principal Mr Brown.

_source.definition_text: to get a positive feeling or advantage from someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: derive;derive comfort/pleasure etc from sth;derive comfort/pleasure, etc. from sth;derived;derives;deriving
_source.learnerexamples_text: I derive great pleasure from gardening.; Last but not least, it is a fact that people derive pleasure from being in a position to have the things they desire and can afford to buy.

_source.definition_text: to come from or be developed from something
_source.searchterms_text: derive;derive (sth) from sth;derive sth from sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: The name derives from Latin.; From another chart, we can have a clear understanding of nuclear power's contribution to different European countries. 78.0% [of] electricity production [is] derived from nuclear power in France.

_source.definition_text: to go or come down
_source.learnerexamples_text: The path descended steeply into the valley.; Jane descended the stairs.; Paul slowly descended to the river and sat down on the grassy bank.

_source.definition_text: to be related to a person or creature that lived a long time ago
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her father is descended from Greek royalty.

_source.definition_text: someone who is related to someone who lived a long time ago
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is a descendant of Queen Victoria.; Someone born poor in the country will never have a chance to heighten his social status, and generations later, his descendants will be poor as well.

_source.definition_text: to say or write what someone or something is like
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you describe your bag?; He described the painting in detail.; Let me describe (to you) how it happened.; She described Gary as shy.; I would like to describe the food from my country.

_source.definition_text: something that tells you what something or someone is like
_source.learnerexamples_text: Write a description of your favourite seaside resort.; Your essay contains too much description, and not enough discussion of the issues.; She has given the police a very detailed/full description of the robber.; Here's a description of [my bedroom].

_source.definition_text: a large, hot, dry area of land with very few plants
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Sahara Desert; They were lost in the desert for nine days.; I'm on holiday in Tunisia near "Djerba". Yesterday morning I [saw] many camels in the desert.

_source.definition_text: If a place is deserted, it has no people in it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a deserted street; Too often have I seen deserted city centres caused by loss of trade, centres subject to graffiti, dirt and vandalism.

_source.definition_text: If you deserve something good or bad, it should happen to you because of the way you have behaved.
_source.learnerexamples_text: After all that hard work, you deserve a holiday.; Chris deserves our special thanks for all his efforts.; I hope they get the punishment they deserve.; They certainly deserved to win that match.; I wish you happiness, you deserve it.

_source.definition_text: the art of making plans or drawings for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's an expert on kitchen/software design.; He's studying design at college.; You know that my subject is design.

_source.definition_text: a pattern or decoration
_source.learnerexamples_text: a floral design; Last year I made and sold more than 200 pairs of knitted socks and because of that I got a prize from The Swedish Handcraft Company for [the] wonderful and original design on my socks.

_source.definition_text: the way in which something is planned and made
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't like the design of this kettle.; The building was originally Victorian in design.; a serious design fault ; The car has some excellent design features.; I was looking to find a good bicycle with a nice design.

_source.definition_text: a drawing which shows how an object, machine, or building will be made
_source.learnerexamples_text: Engineers are working on the new designs.; To finish some of your designs on time you could take them home and continue them there or you could work for longer in your office.

_source.definition_text: to draw or plan something before making it
_source.learnerexamples_text: Who designed this building/dress/furniture?; This range of clothing is specially designed for shorter women.; It was built in 1570 and designed by [the] Italian architect Morando.

_source.definition_text: to have been planned or done for a particular purpose
_source.searchterms_text: be designed for/to do sth;be designed for/to do sth ;design;designed;designing;designs
_source.learnerexamples_text: This dictionary is designed for advanced learners of English.; These measures are designed to reduce pollution.; The end-of-conference party is designed to give rough ideas about many different cultures.

_source.definition_text: someone who draws and plans how something will be made
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fashion/software designer; After five months, she was working as a co-designer with the best Italian designer, although she was just a student.

_source.definition_text: made by a famous or fashionable designer
_source.learnerexamples_text: designer jeans/sunglasses; I can't afford designer labels/designer label clothes.; People like designer clothes like Armani, Chanel [and] so on.

_source.definition_text: worth having and wanted by most people
_source.learnerexamples_text: Reducing class sizes in schools is a desirable aim.; It's regarded as a highly desirable job.; The house is in a very desirable area of the city.; It is desirable that they include showers, although a bath tub would be nice, too.

_source.definition_text: a strong feeling that you want something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I certainly have no desire to have children.; There is a strong desire for peace among the people.; She had a strong desire to go back to her home country before she died.; Several people have expressed a desire to see the report.; I had such a desire to go to the disco that I decided to go even without [my] parents' permission.

_source.definition_text: the effect/result/shape, etc. that is wanted
_source.searchterms_text: desired;desired effect/result/shape, etc.;the desired effect/result/shape etc;the desired effect/result/shape, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her medicine seems to have had the desired effect.; The sentence had had the desired effect of calming down the clients.

_source.definition_text: to want something
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can have whatever you desire.; Indeed, the location of this hotel will allow all of us to do whatever we desire.

_source.definition_text: a type of table that you can work at, often one with drawers
_source.learnerexamples_text: an office/school desk; She sat at her desk writing letters.; He had a pile of papers on his desk.; There [is] a television, a stereo, a computer, a big bed and a desk with a chair.

_source.definition_text: a computer screen that contains icons that represent files, programs and other features of the computer
_source.learnerexamples_text: The menu bar with its windows is one of the features of the desktop.

_source.definition_text: a computer that is small enough to fit on a desk
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can download from my desktop to my mobile phone.; The computer I bought is a beautiful, new, white desktop.

_source.definition_text: a feeling of having no hope
_source.learnerexamples_text: a mood/sense of despair; They're in the depths of despair over/about the money they've lost.; Almost in despair, I came out of the bathroom and tried my best to look for a candle.

_source.definition_text: extremely worried or frightened and ready to do anything to change the bad situation you are in
_source.learnerexamples_text: The doctors made one last desperate attempt/effort to save the boy's life.; They made a desperate appeal for help.; I was almost desperate, trying to think about any possible solution to my problem, but the more I thought, the bigger was my problem, because hours went by.

_source.definition_text: A desperate situation is very serious or bad.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The economy is in a really desperate situation.; In desperate situations one may even think that our only task in this world is to face and try to overcome everyday problems.

_source.definition_text: needing or wanting something very much
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are desperate for help.; He was desperate to tell someone his good news.; She was 19 and in desperate need of a boyfriend.

_source.definition_text: in a way that shows you are frightened and ready to try anything to change a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: They fought desperately for their lives.; He desperately tried to keep the stalking sharks at bay, but he couldn't succeed.

_source.definition_text: extremely or very much
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was desperately ill.; I'm not desperately keen on football.; He was desperately in love with her.; They desperately wanted a child.; I desperately need a bicycle as a bicycle competition is going to take place in our city.

_source.definition_text: the state of being desperate
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was overcome by a sense of desperation.; Many are driven to desperation and turn to stealing to survive.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something happened or is true, although something else makes this seem not probable

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a situation which is surprising in relation to something that is true or happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company has been forced to reduce its price, despite the fact that the offer has been very popular.; The advantages of the kind of life that people ha[d] years ago is that they could eat more fruit and vegetables than us. However, there are advantages for us too, because despite the fact that we eat more fast food, we do more exercise than they [did].

_source.definition_text: sweet food eaten after the main part of a meal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a dessert fork/spoon;  For dessert there's apple pie, cheesecake or fruit.; If you make the main course, I'll make a dessert.; I always order a t-bone steak with salad, and for dessert a piece of chocolate cake.

_source.definition_text: the place where someone or something is going
_source.learnerexamples_text: We arrived at our destination tired and hungry.; His letter never reached its destination.; The Caribbean is a popular tourist/holiday destination.; The journey to the destination lasted about an hour.

_source.definition_text: a power that some people believe controls what will happen in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: Nick said it was destiny that we met.; If anybody ever asked me if I believed in destiny, I would hesitate.

_source.definition_text: the things that will happen to someone in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: At last she feels in control of her own destiny.; It was our parents' destiny, it is our destiny and is going to be our children's destiny, too.

_source.definition_text: when something is destroyed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many people are very concerned about the destruction of the rainforests.; Unusually high winds left a trail of destruction over southern Britain.; weapons of mass destruction; With the ongoing industrialisation and, for example, the destruction of the rain forest men have taken or destroyed the natural places of several hundred species all over the world.

_source.definition_text: to damage something so badly that it does not exist or cannot be used
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most of the old part of the city was destroyed by bombs during the war.; The accident seemed to have completely/totally destroyed his confidence.; The film described a terrible period of our history when a lot of people died and a lot of cities were destroyed.

_source.definition_text: a detached building is one that is not joined to another building
_source.learnerexamples_text: They have a detached 5-bedroom house in Surrey.; I live in a detached house in the countryside with my two friends, who are married.

_source.definition_text: If someone is detached, they do not feel involved with someone or emotional about something.
_source.learnerexamples_text: As a nurse, I see some very distressing things, but I try to stay detached.; Whereas Olivia was very much attracted by and interested in India's mysteries, Douglas had a much more detached view of India.

_source.definition_text: information about someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've sent off for the details of a job I saw advertised in the paper.; They haven't given me any details yet.; A police officer took down the details of what happened.; Here are the details you asked for.

_source.definition_text: including or considering all the information about something or every part of something

_source.definition_text: one of many facts or pieces of information about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She insisted on telling me every single detail.; We don't know the full/precise details of the story yet.; Consequently we [want] to know every single detail about them and their lives.

_source.definition_text: to tell or include all the facts about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I won't go into detail over the phone, but I've been having a few health problems recently.; The longer document goes into more detail about the experiments.; In one of his books he really goes into detail [about] how children treat other children [who] have difficulties with their "new" [language].

_source.definition_text: to discover or notice something, especially something that is difficult to see, hear, smell, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Some sounds cannot be detected by the human ear.;  This special camera can detect bodies by their heat.; The kind of contamination that can be detected and observed most easily is the air pollution.

_source.definition_text: giving a lot of information
_source.learnerexamples_text: A witness gave a detailed description of the man.; We ran until we arrived at the police station where we gave a detailed description of that man and what had happened.

_source.definition_text: someone, especially a police officer, whose job is to discover information about a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: a private detective; detective stories ; I know that you love detective stories.

_source.definition_text: to become worse
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her condition deteriorated rapidly.; Otherwise, the situation will deteriorate more and more.

_source.definition_text: when someone continues trying to do something, although it is very difficult
_source.learnerexamples_text: Andy Murray will need great determination and skill to win this match.; Mandela tried to better the political situation of South Africa [-] he was strong enough to fight, he had determination.

_source.definition_text: to discover the facts or truth about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The doctors are still unable to determine what is wrong.; You can use a simple test to determine whether the paint contains lead.; Our feelings about the issue led our class to direct a survey among local residents in Fordham, in order to determine statistically how often the latter use Greendale Park.

_source.definition_text: wanting to do something very much, and not letting anyone stop you
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm determined to get this piece of work finished today.; She's sure to get the job she wants - she's a very determined person.; I am determined to study computer engineering and pursue my education oversea[s].

_source.definition_text: to decide what will happen
