_source.definition_text: in grammar, a word which is used before a noun to show which particular example of the noun you are referring to
_source.learnerexamples_text: In the phrases 'my first boyfriend' and 'that strange woman', the words 'my' and 'that' are determiners.

_source.definition_text: something that stops people doing something because they are afraid of what will happen if they do
_source.learnerexamples_text: They've installed a security camera as a deterrent to thieves.; I also think that the assistance that the state provides acts as a deterrent in the sense that, in Britain for example, the income support or family credit can actually be higher than what some people can earn in a week of hard work: so, what is the point of working?

_source.definition_text: harmful or damaging
_source.learnerexamples_text: a detrimental effect; The truth is that the situation [in] which we now find ourselves due to the industrialisation of countries has reached crisis point and will probably have a detrimental effect on the environment in the years to come.

_source.definition_text: making someone very shocked and upset
_source.learnerexamples_text: Despite the devastating news, no one is giving up hope.; It can be really devastating for such [a] person to experience it.

_source.definition_text: very shocked and upset
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was devastated when her husband died.; They were devastated by the terrible news.; To begin with, everyone was devastated [at] how long we had to wait at the airport, as the flight to Dublin was late.

_source.definition_text: causing a lot of damage or destruction
_source.learnerexamples_text: The fire has had a devastating effect on the local wildlife.; We are all aware of the devastating impact that factories have on the environment, not to mention the cars whose numbers multipl[y] day-by-day.

_source.definition_text: serious damage caused by a violent event
_source.learnerexamples_text: The tornado has already left a trail of devastation through four states from Nebraska to Missouri.; As you might know, this is one of the few green areas that has survived the devastation suffered by our town during the past five years.

_source.definition_text: to make something new such as a product
_source.learnerexamples_text: Scientists are developing new drugs all the time.; The company is spending $650 million on developing new products/technology.; With more free time we can develop new tec[h]nology, learn more about ourselves and the world that surrounds us.

_source.definition_text: to (cause something to) grow or change and become more advanced
_source.learnerexamples_text: The baby develops inside the mother for nine months.; Over time, their acquaintance developed into a lasting friendship.; This exercise is designed to develop the shoulder and back muscles.; I'm looking for a job which will enable me to develop my skills/talents.; Therefore it's an important tool that is used to develop new friendships.

_source.definition_text: If you develop an illness or problem, or if it develops, you start to suffer from it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The study showed that one in twelve women is likely to develop breast cancer.; She's developed some very strange habits lately.; They often developed the same symptoms as can be seen among mentally disturbed human beings.

_source.definition_text: to start to happen or exist
_source.learnerexamples_text: Further problems may develop if you do not deal with this now.; But it's not only financial problems which can develop as a result of more people living longer in a society.

_source.definition_text: describes a country or region of the world with an advanced level of technology, industry, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a developed country/nation ; To conclude I would like to say that the gover[n]ments of all developed countries wouldn't have been so concerned about [the] so-called "problem 2000" if the computer had not been so important for modern society.

_source.definition_text: someone whose job is to create new products, especially computer products such as software
_source.learnerexamples_text: We mostly use developers based in India.; For example, we may have the top website developers in China, but quite often the[ir] skills are [restrict]ed by poor IT infrastructures.

_source.definition_text: describes a country or region of the world which is poor and has few industries
_source.learnerexamples_text: the developing world/countries/nations; Nowadays, both developed and developing countries spend a lot of money on computeriz[ation].

_source.definition_text: someone who buys land or buildings to improve them and sell them for more money
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the land was bought up by developers.; In some cities these days, a lot of building developers bought spaces above some shops to either develop [them] as a business or develop them as flats.

_source.definition_text: when someone or something grows or changes and becomes more advanced
_source.learnerexamples_text: healthy growth and development; The programme traced the development of popular music through the ages.; a development project in Pakistan; There are some machines which have helped in my development, and others which help to make my life easier.

_source.definition_text: the process of developing something new
_source.learnerexamples_text: the development of new drugs; Mr Berkowitz is in charge of product development.; Owing to the great speed of technological development, people need to lead a faster life.

_source.definition_text: something new that happens and changes a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: an important development in the fuel crisis; Phone me if there are any new developments.; There have been impressive developments in technology lately.

_source.definition_text: when something starts to happen or exist
_source.learnerexamples_text: Smoking encourages the development of cancer.; The aims taken into account [i]n the establishment of the "Health fund" are varied and cover different areas such as the education of the general public on the issues of health itself, [and] the threat posed by the development of cancer and Aids, etc.

_source.definition_text: a piece of equipment that is used for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: an electronic device; Rescuers used a special device for finding people trapped in collapsed buildings.; I have much more time for many other things during the day thanks to [the] devices modern technology offers us.

_source.definition_text: an evil being, often represented in human form but with a tail and horns
_source.learnerexamples_text: This film is about a devil who meets a priest.

_source.base_text: leave someone to their own devices
_source.definition_text: to leave someone to do what they want to do
_source.searchterms_text: device;devices;leave someone to their own devices
_source.learnerexamples_text: With both parents out at work, the kids were often left to their own devices.; The moment teenagers leave school, they are left to their own devices.

_source.definition_text: someone who behaves badly
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's an absolute devil!; It must be with my younger brother, that little devil, Diana thought, so she went to his room and opened every drawer, but she could find nothing.

_source.definition_text: to design or invent something such as a system, plan, or piece of equipment
_source.learnerexamples_text: She devised a plan to make money.; We need to devise an interactive internet language programme by reinforcing our computer facility and replenishing necessary items.

_source.definition_text: to use time, energy, etc. for a particular purpose
_source.searchterms_text: devote;devote sth to sb/sth;devote sth to sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He resigned from his job to devote more time to his family.; At that time, everyone should have devoted their life to the nation.

_source.definition_text: to use a space or area for a particular purpose
_source.searchterms_text: devote;devote sth to sb/sth;devote sth to sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most of the magazine was devoted to celebrity gossip.; And we ha[ve] come [up with] the idea of building a drama theatre at our college and a new department for our library devoted to music.

_source.definition_text: extremely loving or caring very much about someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a devoted fan/husband/wife; Lucy is devoted to her cats.; I am devoted to reading and I can say this book is wonderful.

_source.definition_text: to spend all your time or energy doing something that you think is important
_source.searchterms_text: devote;devote yourself to sth;devote yourself to sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He retired in 1814 to devote himself to social reforms.; Bosses do not like women of such marital status, because there is a threa[t] that they will have not enough time to devote themselves to their professional work.

_source.definition_text: to say what is wrong with someone who is ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was diagnosed with/as having cancer last year.; I wasn't prepared at all when my parents sat me down to tell me that my mother had been diagnosed with cancer.

_source.definition_text: when a doctor says what is wrong with someone who is ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's the diagnosis?; Lung cancer was the diagnosis.

_source.definition_text: a simple picture showing what something looks like or explaining something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The teacher drew a diagram showing how the blood flows through the heart.; The first diagram tells us that the number of Japanese tourist[s] travelling abroad increased dramatically from about 5 million in 1985 to about 11 million in 1990.

_source.definition_text: to make a telephone call to a particular number
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can I dial this number direct, or do I have to go through the operator?; Dial 0 for the switchboard.; So he picked up the phone and dialled the number written in the letter.

_source.definition_text: a form of a language that people speak in a particular part of a country
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're speaking a local dialect.; Mrs Haefele, the owner and cook of this inn, serves the meals personally and if you are lucky, you [may] understand a bit of her Swabian dialect.

_source.definition_text: (a) conversation which is written for a book, play or film
_source.learnerexamples_text: The play contained some very funny dialogue.; Act Two begins with a short dialogue between father and son.; However, she shows her courage during her first dialogue with Joss.

_source.definition_text: a formal discussion between countries or groups of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to enter into a dialogue with these people.; The way I see it, history has proven that authority without dialogue leads to rebellion, and I do not see rebellion as a way to improvement, but as a symbol of failure.

_source.definition_text: an extremely hard valuable stone which is used in jewellery, and in industry for cutting hard things
_source.learnerexamples_text: a diamond ring/necklace ; He had worked in the diamond mines of South Africa.; She found a gorgeous diamond ring on her finger.

_source.definition_text: a shape with four straight sides of equal length, forming two opposite angles which are wide and two which are narrow
_source.learnerexamples_text: Joe's socks had diamond patterns on them.

_source.definition_text: an illness in which your solid waste is more liquid than usual, and comes out of your body more often
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has got diarrhoea.; He is completely different from Ralph; he is fat, has asthma, diarrhoea, and suffers from acute shortsight[e]dness.

_source.definition_text: a book in which a person writes a private record of events, thoughts, feelings, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I write down my thoughts in my diary every night.; I've kept a diary since I was a little girl.; The best one is a diary: my aunt gave it to me. It like it because I can write my feelings in it.

_source.definition_text: a book containing spaces for all the days and months of the year, in which you write down your future arrangements, meetings, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll check my diary and see when I'm free.; Don't forget to write the date of the meeting in your diary.; My diary is important for me because [it has] all my friend's ad[d]ress[es].

_source.definition_text: a small object with six equal square sides, each with between one and six spots on it, used in games
_source.learnerexamples_text: Roll the dice to see who starts the game. ; The dice were rolling and my luck was [in].

_source.definition_text: to cut food into small, square pieces
_source.learnerexamples_text: diced onions ; There are trays of cut lettuce, leaf lettuce, cut tomato, diced tomato, all kinds of relishes, cheese with bacon spread, barbecue, or whatever you like.

_source.definition_text: to decide or control what happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: The weather will dictate where we hold the party.; Since the dawn of time people of all religions have considered that there is a higher power that dictates their destiny.

_source.definition_text: a book that contains a list of words in alphabetical order with their meanings explained or written in another language, or a similar product for use on a computer
_source.learnerexamples_text: a French-English/English-French dictionary; a bilingual/monolingual dictionary; To check how a word is spelt, look it up in a dictionary.; Andrew, I think I left my new dictionary in your house last night.

_source.definition_text: to stop living or existing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Twelve people died in the accident.; She died of/from hunger/cancer/a heart attack/her injuries.; It is a brave person who will die for their beliefs.; Our love will never die.; The pen is very important for me because my grandfather g[a]ve it to me before he died.

_source.definition_text: to be extremely eager to have or do something
_source.searchterms_text: be dying for/to do sth;be dying for/to do sth ;die;died;dies;dying
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm dying to hear your news.; I'm dying for a cup of tea.; Now I have to leave you because I'm dying for a pizza!

_source.definition_text: If something, especially noise or excitement, dies down, it gradually becomes less loud or strong until it stops.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She waited for the laughter to die down before she spoke.; Even the best materials wouldn't be able to avoid the deafening noise which does not ever die down.

_source.definition_text: fuel used in the engines of some vehicles, especially buses and trucks
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to stop for some diesel.; Secondly, if the price of petrol is increased, people will buy cars that run on diesel.

_source.definition_text: to become more and more rare and then disappear completely
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dinosaurs died out about 65 million years ago.; A second point is that [a] lot of animals are going to die out because of pollution.

_source.definition_text: the type of food that someone usually eats
_source.l_topic_text_text: body and health, food and drink
_source.learnerexamples_text: a healthy/balanced diet; The children seem to exist on a diet of burgers and chips.; You can try our fresh farm food, which [is] very good for your diet.

_source.definition_text: to be not like something or someone else, either physically or in another way
_source.learnerexamples_text: The twins look alike, but they differ in personality.; His views differ considerably from those of his parents.; The findings of the various studies differ greatly/widely.; People's opinions on this matter differ widely.

_source.definition_text: when someone eats less food, or only particular types of food, because they want to become thinner or for medical reasons
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm going on a diet next week and hope to lose two kilos before Christmas.; The doctor put me on a low-salt diet to reduce my blood pressure.; I'm on a serious diet, and I have to exercise.

_source.definition_text: the way in which two people or things are not the same
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's the difference between an ape and a monkey?; I will not find the same one and of course John will notice the difference.

_source.definition_text: to improve a situation (a lot)
_source.searchterms_text: difference;differences;make a (big) difference;make a big difference
_source.learnerexamples_text: Exercise can make a big difference to your health.; It wouldn't make a big difference in my life, but it would be good.

_source.definition_text: the amount by which one thing is different from another
_source.learnerexamples_text: a(n) age/price/temperature difference; There's a big difference in age between them.; This age difference was too big!

_source.definition_text: a disagreement or different opinion
_source.learnerexamples_text: They must try to resolve their differences peacefully.; Caroline and her husband had had an argument last week, but as he was going to be away for a few days, they had finally settled their differences.

_source.base_text: make no difference/not make any difference
_source.definition_text: to not be important or change a situation
_source.searchterms_text: difference;differences;make no difference/not make any difference
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can ask him again if you like, but it won't make any difference - he'll still say no.; It makes no difference where you put the aerial, the TV picture's still bad.; Does it make any difference, some might ask?

_source.definition_text: not the same
_source.learnerexamples_text: She seems to wear something different every day.; We're reading a different book this week.; Emily is very/completely different from her sister.; That's totally different to my experience at school.; There are many different types/kinds of bacteria.

_source.definition_text: to notice a difference between two things
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't tell the difference between an American and a Canadian accent.; Not only will their critical sen[s]e atrophy but also they will not be able to tell the difference between what is right and wrong.

_source.definition_text: to understand or notice how two things or people are different from each other
_source.learnerexamples_text: He can't differentiate between blue and green.; The person would learn how to differentiate his needs from his wants and would value hard work.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about separate things or people of the same type
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had to go to three different shops to find the book she wanted.; I have three different teachers for three different things, one for the grammar, [an]other for the lis[ten]ing and finally [one] for my writing.

_source.definition_text: to make someone or something different
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to differentiate ourselves from the competition.; Consumerism is reflected through this need, leading to a non-stop purchasing of products and services which will differentiate us from the mass.

_source.definition_text: in a different way
_source.learnerexamples_text: We want to do things differently.; Are girls treated differently?; I had always pictured it quite differently.

_source.definition_text: not friendly or easy to deal with
_source.learnerexamples_text: The manager is difficult to deal with/a difficult person to deal with.; His wife is a very difficult person.; Please children, don't be so difficult!; I'm not a difficult person and I can cook very [well].

_source.definition_text: when something is not easy to do or understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: a difficult problem/choice/task ;  It will be very difficult to prove that they are guilty.; Many things make it difficult for women to reach the top in business.; He finds it extremely difficult being a single parent.; This book is very important because I have a difficult exam next Friday.

_source.base_text: put sb in a difficult position
_source.definition_text: to cause someone to be in a difficult situation
_source.searchterms_text: difficult;put sb in a difficult position
_source.learnerexamples_text: When two of your best friends argue it puts you in a very difficult position.; I know that I will put you in a difficult position with my absence but I must leave.

_source.definition_text: when something is not easy to do or understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: We finished the job, but only with great difficulty.; The difficulty of the task excited them.; She had great difficulty finding a job.; They would have difficulty in sleeping outdoors.

_source.definition_text: to break up and move soil using a tool, a machine or your hands
_source.learnerexamples_text: Digging (in) the garden is good exercise.; I started digging, but it was useless.

_source.definition_text: something that is not easy to deal with
_source.learnerexamples_text: financial difficulties; to have/experience difficulties; children with learning difficulties; As you know my family has financial difficulties and we can't afford this.

_source.definition_text: to form a hole by moving soil
_source.learnerexamples_text: The tunnel was dug with the aid of heavy machinery.; The dog was digging a hole to hide its bone in.; I was ready to dig a hole and jump into it, because when you are at that age and your best friend's father sees you kissing your boyfriend in the dark, [it is] just the most embarr[a]ssing thing which can happen to you.

_source.definition_text: to change food in your stomach into substances that your body can use
_source.learnerexamples_text: I need some time to digest my dinner.; Most families are also trying to eat a bit less meat, because meat is very hard to digest.

_source.definition_text: to think about new information carefully in order to understand it
_source.learnerexamples_text: You need to give me time to digest this report.; Also I found the lectures about how to write CVs very useful although if the groups were smaller, it would have made the information easier to digest.

_source.definition_text: when your body changes food in your stomach into substances that it can use
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has problems with his digestion.; Afterwards, I had some serious digestion problems, and no medical care was available.

_source.definition_text: using an electronic system that changes sounds or images into signals in the form of numbers before it stores them or sends them
_source.learnerexamples_text: digital data; a digital recording; digital TV; It has amazing digital effects.

_source.definition_text: showing information in the form of an electronic image
_source.learnerexamples_text: a digital clock/display; a digital watch; The alarm clock was flashing with the annoying digital zeros.

_source.definition_text: a type of camera that records images that you can use and store on a computer
_source.learnerexamples_text: These days almost everyone uses a digital camera.; I got lots of gifts, including a digital camera!

_source.definition_text: calm, serious, and behaving in a way that makes people respect you
_source.learnerexamples_text: a quiet, dignified woman; In the book "The remains of the day" we get to know the very dignified butler, Stevens, and his relationship with Miss Kenton.

_source.definition_text: calm and serious behaviour that makes people respect you
_source.learnerexamples_text: He behaved with great dignity and courage. ; This includes a feeling of self satisfaction, happiness, honour, respect and dignity.

_source.definition_text: If it is beneath your dignity to do something, you think you are too important or from too high a class to do it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She felt that it was beneath her dignity to wear a name badge.; He thought it was beneath his dignity to talk about his master's decisions and ideas.

_source.definition_text: a situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two different things you could do
_source.learnerexamples_text: The President is clearly in a dilemma about/over how to tackle the crisis.; She faces the dilemma of disobeying her father or losing the man she loves.; a moral/ethical dilemma; Actually I think it's a typical female dilemma: we try to do many things by ourselves and at the same time!

_source.definition_text: not bright or clear
_source.learnerexamples_text: He could hardly see her in the dim light.; As well as such drawbacks, the lighting is too dim to browse around and some light tubes are permanently off.

_source.definition_text: when you can remember something slightly, but not very well
_source.searchterms_text: a dim memory/recollection etc;a dim memory/recollection, etc.;dim;dim memory/recollection, etc.;dimmer;dimmest
_source.learnerexamples_text: I have a dim memory of meeting her at a party.; I really regret having lost it for now I have only dim recollections of my past.

_source.definition_text: a particular part of a situation, especially something that affects how you think or feel
_source.learnerexamples_text: Music has added a new dimension to my life.; I had never felt this way before, it was like being part of another life, another dimension!

_source.definition_text: to become less bright, or to make something become less bright
_source.learnerexamples_text: He dimmed the lights and turned up the music.; The light was carefully dimmed by the waiter as they order[ed] their food: they both chose their special enchiladas.

_source.definition_text: a measurement of the length, width, or height of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The dimensions of the photo should be no larger than 30cm by 20cm.; Also I [want to] take a big mirror, the dimensions are 0.70 x 1.20 m.

_source.definition_text: to become less, or to make something become less
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your pain should diminish gradually after taking these tablets. ; As one student I've asked said, if we manage to keep cars out of town, air pollution will considerably diminish.

_source.definition_text: the main meal of the day that people usually eat in the evening
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were just having (our) dinner.; We had some friends round for dinner on Saturday.; a romantic candlelit dinner; I can come to dinner tomorrow at 7 o'clock.

_source.definition_text: a room in which meals are eaten
_source.learnerexamples_text: We ate in the dining room.; I think I left it in the dining room.

_source.definition_text: a very large animal that used to live millions of years ago
_source.learnerexamples_text: So why did the dinosaurs die out?; It was attacked by an enormous dinosaur and died.

_source.definition_text: to put something into a liquid for a short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dip the fish in the batter, then drop it into the hot oil.; She dipped her toe into the pool to see how cold it was.; I recommend little sandwiches, chips and other things to dip [into sauces].

_source.definition_text: to become lower in level or amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: The number of students taking sciences has dipped sharply.; Cinema attendance in th[is] age group dipped to 88%.

_source.definition_text: a qualification from a school, college or university, or an official document showing that someone has completed a course of study
_source.learnerexamples_text: a diploma in marketing; My best present was a diploma [from] the University of Cambridge.

_source.definition_text: dealing with the relationships between governments
_source.learnerexamples_text: international diplomacy ; I studied International Relations and Diplomacy.

_source.definition_text: an official whose job is to represent one country in another, and who usually works in an embassy
_source.learnerexamples_text: a Spanish/British diplomat; The owner of the restaurant was a diplomat, and he invited the refugees to eat at the restaurant.

_source.definition_text: skill in dealing with people well and not upsetting them
_source.learnerexamples_text: She showed great tact and diplomacy in the meeting.; And if a dispute ar[ose], he managed to solve it with great diplomacy and with the result that nobody in the end felt offended.

_source.definition_text: relating to diplomacy or diplomats
_source.learnerexamples_text: diplomatic relations; The price has been arranged by the Argentine an[d] English Governments, that have now entered diplomatic relations.

_source.definition_text: good at dealing with people without upsetting them
_source.learnerexamples_text: That's a very diplomatic answer.; We may have to be diplomatic and tactful, but we also must be honest and firm.

_source.definition_text: in a way that deals well with people without upsetting them
_source.learnerexamples_text: He phrased his question very diplomatically.; Even though this issue is usually settled diplomatically, there still remains [a] considerable amount of criticism to be faced.

_source.definition_text: going straight from one place to another without stopping or changing direction
_source.learnerexamples_text: a direct route/line ; Is there a direct train to Edinburgh?; I'm looking for a direct flight from Zurich to Botswana.

_source.definition_text: with no other person or thing involved or between
_source.learnerexamples_text: She decided to take direct control of the project.; Have you any direct experience of this kind of work?; He left as a direct result/consequence of what she said.; There is a direct link/connection between smoking and lung cancer.; I think that there are huge dangers today such as war, violence, crime, pollution, etc. that have a direct influence on our lives.

_source.definition_text: saying clearly and honestly what you think
_source.learnerexamples_text: a direct answer; He preferred to give me [a] hint rather than a direct answer.

_source.definition_text: to tell the actors in a film or play what to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: He wanted to give up acting and start directing (his own films).; 'Jaws' was directed by Steven Spielberg.; We plan to see an action film which was directed by Tarantino.

_source.definition_text: to show or tell someone how to get to a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you direct me to the manager's office please?; He directed me to a room where other guests were waiting.

_source.definition_text: to aim something at someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: direct;direct sth against/at/towards etc sb/sth;direct sth against/at/towards, etc. sb/sth;directed;directing;directs
_source.learnerexamples_text: The demonstrators' anger was directed at the police.; In these circumstances it is important, however, that alte[r]native options are provided (e.g. efficient and affordable train services) and that economic measures (such as increased prices) are directed at those who really cause the most environmental costs.

_source.definition_text: to organize and control the way something is done
_source.learnerexamples_text: He directed the building of the new art gallery.; Obviously they will work in the com[m]ercial department, under the supervision of Lorenzo Soboli, the person who is in charge of directing that section.

_source.definition_text: the way that someone or something is moving or facing
_source.learnerexamples_text: "No, go that way," I said, pointing in the opposite direction.; He was going in the direction of the bedroom.; They drove away in opposite directions.; I walked for hours in the same direction I [had] walked before.

_source.definition_text: towards someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: She keeps looking in my direction.; I didn't know why she was talking to me but suddenly she walked in my direction and told me: "I need to know your name".

_source.definition_text: control or instructions
_source.learnerexamples_text: Under his direction the company has doubled its profits.; I am writing to you on behalf of the Social Club of our language school to express some complaints that we had from several students concerning our recent visit to the Science and Technology Museum which is under your direction.

_source.definition_text: the way that someone or something changes or develops
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our careers have gone in very different directions.; At school and at home young people are supposed to take responsibility for their actions and choose a direction for their life.

_source.definition_text: with no other person or thing involved or in between

_source.definition_text: a difficult and important plan
_source.learnerexamples_text: Putting on the concert will be a joint enterprise between the two schools.; She succeeded in whatever enterprises she undertook all [through] her life and even the death of her husband did not prevent her from carrying on.

_source.definition_text: when someone is enthusiastic and willing to do something new and clever, although there are risks involved
_source.learnerexamples_text: The scheme shows imagination and enterprise.; I am talking about a frank and sincere young lady with enterprise.

_source.definition_text: to keep a group of people interested or enjoying themselves
_source.learnerexamples_text: We hired a magician to entertain the children.; Most children's television programmes aim to educate and entertain at the same time.; You should sing in a pub to entertain people.

_source.definition_text: someone whose job is to entertain people by singing, telling jokes, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've hired a children's entertainer for the party.; You could hire some entertainers.

_source.definition_text: funny and enjoyable
_source.learnerexamples_text: an entertaining story/film/talk ; His books aren't particularly well-written, but they're always entertaining.; It is obvious that some people prefer reading books, [while] others claim that watching films is much more entertaining.

_source.definition_text: shows, movies, television, or other performances or activities that entertain people
_source.learnerexamples_text: There is live entertainment in the bar every night.; There's not much in the way of entertainment in this town - just the cinema and a couple of pubs.; You can find cinemas, discos and night clubs for entertainment.

_source.definition_text: a feeling of energetic interest in a particular subject or activity and an eagerness to be involved in it
_source.learnerexamples_text: One of the good things about teaching young children is their enthusiasm.; After the accident he lost his enthusiasm for the sport.; I am filled with enthusiasm about [spend]ing two weeks at Camp California in the U.S.A.

_source.definition_text: showing enthusiasm
_source.learnerexamples_text: You don't seem very enthusiastic about the party - don't you want to go tonight?; I've got a lot of friends who are really enthusiastic about cycling and we often go cycling [together].

_source.definition_text: in an enthusiastic way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She responded very enthusiastically to the idea.; She accepted my suggestion enthusiastically.

_source.definition_text: whole or complete, with nothing missing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Between them they ate an entire cake.; He'd spent the entire journey asleep.; On behalf of the entire school, I would like to put forward a num[b]er of suggestions in regard to the improvement of the reception area.

_source.definition_text: completely
_source.learnerexamples_text: I admit it was entirely my fault.; I'm not entirely convinced it will work.; The company is run almost entirely by middle-aged men.; I would like to do something entirely different before I start to study again.

_source.definition_text: to give someone the right to do or have something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm entitled to apply for citizenship.; Being unemployed entitles you to free medical treatment.; In conclusion, I believe that I am entitled to a partial refund.

_source.definition_text: something which exists apart from other things
_source.learnerexamples_text: They want the area recognized as a separate political entity.; Even if these qualities are also quite useful in team sports, where the whole team works as an entity, a spirit of co-operation and teamwork is also needed in order to achieve the effective coexistence of all the players of the team.

_source.definition_text: to give something a particular title
_source.learnerexamples_text: a lecture entitled "Language, Learning and Literacy"; In June, [the] club arranged a slide show and talk which was entitled 'Walking In The Black Hills'; this was very informative and the students had lots of tips for hill walking.

_source.definition_text: a door, gate, etc. by which you can enter a building or place
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are two entrances - one at the front and one round the back.; They must have used the back entrance to the building.; I'll meet you at the main entrance.; From my house you can get there by bus. There's a special one, and it'll take you up to the entrance of the park.

_source.definition_text: the right to enter a place or join an organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: Entrance is free, but you have to pay for your drinks.; If you've [got] membership, you don't need to pay for entrance. You only pay for the drinks and the food.

_source.definition_text: when someone comes into or goes into a place, especially in a way that makes people notice them
_source.learnerexamples_text: The whole room went quiet when he made his entrance.; Or, you could imagine yourself prancing about in your Ferrari, Lotus, Lamborg[h]ini, basic limousine, whatever, in the heart of the town, going to a party where everybody who is anybody is there, and the means of transportation would be by helicopter or by boat, to avoid traffic and, at the same time, to make an outstanding entrance.

_source.definition_text: the right or ability to come into or go into a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was refused entry.; A flock of sheep blocked our entry to the village.; I can't go down that street - there's a 'No entry' sign.; There's free entry to the exhibition for students after 6 pm.

_source.definition_text: a separate piece of information that is recorded in a book such as a dictionary, or on the Internet
_source.learnerexamples_text: They've updated a lot of the entries on the website.; As his illness progressed, he made fewer entries in his diary.; Later I got my own entry on their Clan-home-page.

_source.definition_text: when you join an organization or take part in a competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are there lots of exams for entry into the legal profession?; Have you filled in your entry form yet?; You can do anything in this club from football to chess. If you ever come to visit, I could organise an entry form [for] you.

_source.definition_text: a piece of work that you do to try to win a competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: There have been a fantastic number of entries for this year's poetry competition.; the winning entries

_source.definition_text: a flat paper container for a letter
_source.learnerexamples_text: She ripped open the envelope.; Last night I left an envelope in your house.

_source.definition_text: the air, land and water where people, animals and plants live
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're not doing enough to protect the environment from pollution.; The new road may cause damage to the environment.; The first lesson was enjoyable - we had to talk about the environment.

_source.definition_text: the conditions that you live or work in and the way that they influence how you feel or how effectively you can work
_source.learnerexamples_text: The office is quite bright and airy - it's a pleasant working environment.; As a parent you try to create a stable home environment.; They need to live in a friendly environment with their relatives and their friends.

_source.definition_text: relating to the environment
_source.learnerexamples_text: People are becoming far more aware of environmental issues.; As you know, I went to Canada in order to take part in an environmental conference.

_source.definition_text: someone who tries to protect the natural environment from being damaged
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is a well-known environmentalist.; Others also, especially environmentalists, suggest that we should turn to electric-powered engines which are environmentally friendly, as these air pollutants bring about the thinning of the ozone layer.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is related to the environment
_source.learnerexamples_text: environmentally damaging chemicals; We need our industries to work in an environmentally responsible way.; All these [things] were made possible because we have the world's most dedicated and environmentally adaptable government, spearheaded by Lee Kuan Yew decades ago.

_source.definition_text: not harmful to the environment
_source.learnerexamples_text: environmentally-friendly washing powder; A lot was said about creating more environmentally-friendly products.

_source.definition_text: to imagine something happening, or think that something is likely to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police don't envisage any trouble at the festival.; We envisage the size of the branch to be around 50 people to start with and expect to grow circa 20% a year.

_source.definition_text: to imagine something happening, or think that something is likely to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: He envisioned a partnership between business and government.; From the childhood, when you are only a kid, you envision you[r]self getting married and quite naturally it is a great feeling when you do get married.

_source.definition_text: to wish that you had something that someone else has
_source.learnerexamples_text: I envy her ability to talk to people she's never met before.; I don't envy you the job of cooking for all those people.; I really envy you, Pete.

_source.definition_text: the feeling that you wish you had something that someone else has
_source.learnerexamples_text: I watched with envy as she set off for the airport.; Sam, your last letter has filled me with envy.

_source.definition_text: to wish very much that you had something that another person has
_source.searchterms_text: (be) green with envy;be green with envy;envy
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sam's got a job in the south of France and we're all green with envy!; The more successful players' salary makes the others green with envy.

_source.definition_text: to be liked and wanted by someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her new office was the envy of the whole company.; I enjoy being the envy of my friends as I take it out of its case and show it off.

_source.definition_text: a single event or group of related events
_source.learnerexamples_text: This latest episode in the fraud scandal has shocked a lot of people.; The drugs, the divorce and the depression - it's an episode in his life that he wants to forget.; This little episode happened when I was seven years old.

_source.definition_text: one of the single parts into which a story is divided, especially when it is broadcast on the television or radio
_source.learnerexamples_text: I missed the first episode.; I watch[ed] the news and one episode of "Friends".

_source.definition_text: the same in amount, number or size
_source.learnerexamples_text: The sides are of equal length.; One litre is equal to 1.76 imperial pints.; We are a well-mixed class with equal numbers of boys and girls, all about 20 years old.

_source.definition_text: the same in importance and deserving the same treatment
_source.learnerexamples_text: All people are equal, deserving the same rights as each other.; They've got a long way to go before they achieve equal pay/opportunities for men and women.; Then Napoleon did whatever he wanted to do under the motto of "all animals are equal", which was false.

_source.definition_text: someone or something that has the same importance as someone or something else and deserves the same treatment
_source.learnerexamples_text: The good thing about having her as a boss is that she treats us all as equals.; We must respect and treat them as our equals.

_source.definition_text: the right of different groups of people to have a similar social position and receive the same treatment
_source.learnerexamples_text: equality between the sexes;  racial/sexual equality; That's why I think people who fight to defend equality are amazing, especially Nelson Mandela because he spen[t] part of his life in jail for that.

_source.definition_text: fairly and in the same way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Everyone should be treated equally.; In [the] festival, all the performers were treated equally.

_source.definition_text: into amounts or parts that are the same size
_source.learnerexamples_text: She shared the money equally between the four children.; The obligations should be divided equally between the members of the gro[u]p.

_source.definition_text: to consider one thing to be the same as or equal to another thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many people equate wealth with happiness.; Because we live in a capitalist world where the notions of good life and happiness are largely, if not solely, equated with material prosperity, to achieve them requires the above listed qualities.

_source.definition_text: to the same degree or level
_source.learnerexamples_text: an equally important question; She did equally well in the competition last year.; I think the choice of a good organization, which can provide good facilities and social conditions, along with good teaching, is equally important.

_source.definition_text: when you show that two amounts are equal using mathematical symbols
_source.learnerexamples_text: In this equation, x = 6.; I would like to address the issue [using] a very simple equation of economics: Demand = supply.

_source.definition_text: to provide someone or something with what is needed for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're raising money to equip the hospital.; The new trains are equipped with all the latest technology.; We were equipped with crampons, ropes, ice axes, gloves, sunglasse[s] and so on.

_source.definition_text: the set of necessary tools, clothing, etc. for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: office/camping/kitchen equipment;  electrical equipment; This is a really useful piece of equipment.; You can rent equipment or take your own.

_source.definition_text: equal in amount, value, importance, or meaning
_source.learnerexamples_text: The UK's Brit Awards are roughly equivalent to the Oscars.; They go to the same school and I daresay that the same percentage of girls does the Abitur (equivalent to the English GCE A level).

_source.definition_text: something that has the same value, importance, size, or meaning as something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: She won the equivalent of $5 million.; As well as this I have passed the Cambridge First Certificate exam and another exam in Spain which is the equivalent of FCE.

_source.definition_text: a period of time in history that is special for a particular reason
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Clinton era; the post-war era; They had worked for peace during the long era of conflict.; The fall of the Berlin wall marked the end of an era.; The world is paddling through the era of technology.

_source.definition_text: to destroy or completely get rid of something such as a social problem or a disease
_source.learnerexamples_text: The government claims to be doing all it can to eradicate corruption.; Homelessness is not going to be eradicated unless we acknowledge that it is not anything else but a symptom of the imperfection of the society in which we live.

_source.definition_text: If soil, stone, etc. erodes or is eroded, it is gradually damaged and removed by the sea, rain, or wind.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The coastline is slowly being eroded by the sea.; The areas of Sayago - in the Spanish province of Zamora - and Tras-os-Montes, in Portugal, are joined by a natural border: the river Duero and the rocky canyon that has been eroded for millions of years by the action of the water.

_source.definition_text: to gradually destroy a good quality or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Reports of corruption have eroded people's confidence in the police.; Competition can erode a child's confidence.

_source.definition_text: when soil, stone, etc. is gradually damaged and removed by the sea, rain, or wind
_source.learnerexamples_text: soil/coastal erosion ; Deforestation changes the climate and natural ability to stop soil erosion also plays a role here.

_source.definition_text: when a good quality or situation is gradually destroyed
_source.learnerexamples_text: There has been a gradual erosion of confidence in the government. ; For one [thing], shopping can cause an erosion in family values. Children now tend to give more importance to material things.

_source.definition_text: the amount by which a calculation can be wrong but still produce a good result
_source.learnerexamples_text: a margin of error of 5 percent ; It might be true that what is considered to be healthy or unhealthy changes over time, however, [as] science progresses the margin of error becomes smaller, and experts are then able to have a more accurate and precise say on all matters, including health.

_source.definition_text: a mistake
_source.learnerexamples_text: He admitted that he'd made an error.; The letter contained a number of typing errors.;  Human error has been blamed for the air crash.; The document was destroyed in error by the police.; There are a lot [of] factual errors in this article.

_source.definition_text: a way of learning the best way to do something by trying different methods
_source.learnerexamples_text: There aren't any instructions with it - it's just a matter of trial and error.; If you don't know the past, you're liable to live through it again as instead of deriving the lessons from someone else's experiences, you'll have to learn them the hard way, by trial and error.

_source.definition_text: If a volcano erupts, it suddenly throws out smoke, fire, and melted rocks.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The volcano erupted last year.; Earth can easily be seen as a volcano which can suddenly erupt.

_source.definition_text: moving stairs that take people from one level of a building to another
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll meet you by the up/down escalator on the second floor.; Shall we use the lift or take the escalator?; The newly decorated section is fairly modern [in] style with escalators and touch-screen ticket machine[s].

_source.definition_text: to succeed in getting away from a place where you do not want to be
_source.learnerexamples_text: The two prisoners escaped from prison last night.; There were reports that a lion had escaped from its cage at a nearby zoo.; You also get to meet people there, interesting people - for example, I met a really weird guy who claims to have escaped from an asylum, twice!

_source.definition_text: If something such as a name escapes you, you cannot remember it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The name of her book escapes me at the moment.; My first teacher was an elderly woman (her name escapes me now), who had worked in that school for many years.

_source.definition_text: to avoid a dangerous or unpleasant situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was lucky to escape serious injury.; Chelsea only just escaped defeat in the second round of the cup.; Happily they were found by some hunters and escaped with minor injuries.

_source.definition_text: If something escapes your notice or attention, you do not notice or see it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Nothing that goes on in this office escapes her attention.; It has hardly escaped the attention of anyone that the football World Cup is coming up, and it seems that virtually everybody has something to say about this event or about international sports competitions in general.

_source.definition_text: something that helps you to forget about your usual life or problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: I love old movies - they're such an escape from the real world.; Going on holiday is a great idea and I think it's the best way to relax and have fun, but it would also be an escape from the daily routine and a break from your tiring job.

_source.definition_text: If you have a narrow escape, you only just avoid danger.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He had a narrow escape when a falling tree crushed his car.; Ralph will have a narrow escape: he is saved by the arrival of a ship which has at last come to rescue them all.

_source.definition_text: when someone succeeds in getting out of a place or a dangerous or bad situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: He made his escape on the back of a motorbike.; an escape route; Being impatient in the jail, Tom planned for his escape.

_source.definition_text: very much or particularly
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's not especially interested in sport.; I chose this especially for your new house.; I loved the show, especially the dancing.; I like sports, especially playing basketball.

_source.definition_text: for one particular person, purpose, or reason
_source.learnerexamples_text: I cooked this meal especially for you.; I remember the taste of the pineapple cake that you baked especially for me and your home-made goos[e]berry wine.

_source.definition_text: a short piece of writing about a particular subject, especially one done by students
_source.learnerexamples_text: For homework I want you to write an essay on endangered species.; I could write an extra essay.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize the most important idea or quality of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: In essence, its purpose is to contain information.; In essence, homelessness means that you don't have a home and because of this you are living on the streets.

_source.definition_text: the basic or most important idea or quality of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The essence of his argument is that we should not eat meat.; But growth is in the essence of every living being, and it is a part of the educational process, as the child grows older, that parents learn to "let go".

_source.definition_text: very important and necessary
_source.learnerexamples_text: Government support will be essential if the project is to succeed.; Computers are an essential part of our lives.; Water is essential for/to living things.;  It is essential that our prices remain competitive.; For the experiment to be valid, it is essential to record the data accurately.

_source.definition_text: the most basic and important
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's one essential point I think you've forgotten.; There is an essential difference between Germans from Germany and native Germans from abroad.

_source.definition_text: relating to the most important characteristics or ideas of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's essentially a dictionary but it differs in one or two respects.; What he's saying is essentially true.; Although we are essentially a rock band, we integrate elements of traditional Indian music (such as sitar).

_source.definition_text: to start a company or organization that is likely to continue for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: The brewery was established in 1822.; The first restaurant, which was established 10 years ago, is called Paris.

_source.definition_text: to start having a relationship or communicating with another person, company, country, or organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: The two countries have only recently established diplomatic relations.; [As] everyone knows, English is called "the universal language", which is used in all the airports of the world, to establish communication between the airports and the planes that arrive from all over the world.

_source.definition_text: to put someone or something into a successful and lasting position
_source.learnerexamples_text: He quickly established himself as a talented actor.; In fact, after ending his career as a football player, Pele managed to establish himself as a successful businessman.

_source.definition_text: to find out information or prove something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police are trying to establish how he died.; In summary, it is difficult to establish how people cho[o]se to buy what they buy.

_source.definition_text: to decide something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our first step must be to establish priorities for the weeks ahead.; As well as this, parents have to establish clear guidelines in relation to expenditure.

_source.definition_text: a business or other organization, or the place where an organization operates
_source.learnerexamples_text: an educational/religious establishment; Even if you do not enjoy novel eating experiences, this establishment is worth a visit due to its architecture and atmosphere.

_source.definition_text: a large area of land in the country which is owned by a family or an organization and is often used for growing crops or raising animals
_source.learnerexamples_text: a country estate; There is a special law in Sweden which allows everyone to wander [through] any private estate unless one causes harm.

_source.definition_text: when an organization, school, business, etc. is started
_source.learnerexamples_text: the establishment of a new national bank; That explains the establishment of various fast-food restaurants in our countries, which spread in a[n] incredibly quick way, and have changed our eating habits in a short time.

_source.definition_text: to guess the cost, size, value, etc. of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Government sources estimate a long-term 50% increase in rail fares.; They estimate that the journey will take at least two weeks.;  It was difficult to estimate how many trees had been destroyed.; The number of dead is estimated at over three hundred.; I estimate it will take only 7 minutes to walk from the conference center to the hotel.

_source.definition_text: a group of houses or factories built in a planned way
_source.learnerexamples_text: a housing estate; an industrial estate; I live [o]n a big housing estate.

_source.definition_text: guessed
_source.learnerexamples_text: an estimated cost/value ; My estimated [time of] arrival [at] Heathrow airport is nine o'clock in the morning and my flight number is OK 1312.

_source.definition_text: a guess of what the size, value, amount, cost, etc. of something might be
_source.learnerexamples_text: The number of people who applied for the course was 120 compared with an initial estimate of between 50 and 100.; This is only a rough estimate.

_source.definition_text: ideas and beliefs about what type of behaviour is morally right and wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: a code of ethics; the ethics of genetic engineering; By experiencing difficult situations in life, they become wiser and they never forget their values and ethics.

_source.definition_text: a belief or idea that influences the way you think or behave
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has a very strong work ethic.; Though I am no longer a bel[ie]ver, I agree with the whole religious ethic, and I shall transmit it to my children.

_source.definition_text: relating to what is right or wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: The book raises some serious ethical questions.; In spite of this, I am not in favour of euthanasia and I even think that mercy killing holds severe ethical problems.

_source.definition_text: relating to a particular race of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: ethnic minorities ; Over 98% of the population are ethnic Chinese.

_source.definition_text: morally correct and good
_source.learnerexamples_text: He dealt with this case in a completely professional and ethical manner.; It's not so much a problem of funds now, for I and my husband earn our living easily, but the question [of] how to bring across those moral and ethical values I believe in, namely reliability, honesty, self-confidence, to a certain degree endurance and discipline, paired with friendly and polite manners.

_source.definition_text: the unit of money used in most European Union countries; €
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most hotels are priced between a hundred and two hundred euros a night.; The price is 50 euro.

_source.definition_text: to consider or study something carefully and decide how good or bad it is
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need time to evaluate the proposal.; The aim of this report is to evaluate and describe how successful our College Film Club has been so far.

_source.definition_text: the act of considering something carefully and deciding how good or bad it is
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was no evaluation of the risks involved.; She carried out an evaluation of their services.; And that is what counts in the evaluation of job candidates.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize the fact that something does not happen or is not true
_source.learnerexamples_text: "I never cry." "Not even when you hurt yourself really badly?"; Nobody spoke, not even the children.; We tried to fish, but didn't catch a thing, not even a shoe!

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize a comparison
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her last film was even better.; The next 36 hours will be even colder, with snow showers just about everywhere.; I think Alex is going to be even taller than his father.; It's even more difficult to find work.; When I saw her getting off the train I really was close to break[ing] down because she looked even more beautiful.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize something that is surprising
_source.learnerexamples_text: Everyone danced - even Mick.; It's a very difficult job - it might even take a year to finish it.; You were the only one who wasn't there, even Marcelo was there!

_source.definition_text: whether or not
_source.learnerexamples_text: Even if you take a taxi, you'll still miss your train.; I often go to parks, with or without the children, even if the weather is not good.

_source.definition_text: although
_source.learnerexamples_text: Even though he left school at 16, he still managed to become a millionaire.; He still smokes even though he's got asthma.; They didn't give up hope even though they were tired and wet to the bone.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that something surprising is true despite what you have just said
_source.learnerexamples_text: Car prices have gone down a lot, but even so, we couldn't afford to buy one.; I'm sure many of [these things] happened due to bad luck, but even so, there are some arrangements that, I bel[ie]ve, can easily be improved.

_source.definition_text: the part of the day between the afternoon and the night
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm working late this evening.;  In the evenings, I like to relax.; What are you doing tomorrow evening?; We usually go to the cinema on Friday evenings.; I work in a restaurant and only get one evening off a week.

_source.definition_text: to not make money but also not lose money
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company only managed to break even this year.; Company C does not seem to be doing well. In the year 2000, it just seems to be breaking even.

_source.definition_text: something that happens, especially something important or unusual
_source.learnerexamples_text: Local people have been shocked by recent events in the town.; The police are trying to determine the series of events that led up to the murder.; I like this book because I like the description of historical events.

_source.definition_text: a race, party, competition, etc. that has been organized for a particular time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Over two thousand people took part in the event.; They stage big sporting events here.; They organize a lot of social events.; When there are parties or important social events, I usually choose a dress to wear.

_source.definition_text: if something happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: An airbag could save your life in the event of an accident.; In the event of bad weather, it would be wise to plan an alternative to the boat trip, for example a visit of Buckingham Palace or the Houses of Parliament.

_source.definition_text: the way in which a situation develops, especially a sudden or unexpected change
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were all shocked by this tragic turn of events.; She was not prepared for such an unexpected turn of events!

_source.definition_text: full of interesting or important events
_source.learnerexamples_text: a very eventful day/journey; She informed me of her exciting and eventful life in London in her letters, which made me decide to follow suit in order to study English.

_source.definition_text: whatever happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm not sure if I'm coming on Friday, but in any event, I'll see you next week.; In any event, it is incumbent upon all of us to carefully plan our travel matters, so as to take advantage of their several benefits.

_source.definition_text: happening or existing at the end of a process or period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: the eventual winner of the competition; Finally, the most important consequence - and in some way quite a perverse one - is that setting the island on fire leads to the boys' eventual rescue; so, pure destruction here means [c]atharsis (speaking in terms of drama).

_source.definition_text: at any time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you ever been to London?; If you're ever in Cambridge, do give me a ring.; Nothing ever happens here in the evenings.; The smell is worse than ever.; [It] is the most beautiful place I've ever seen.

_source.definition_text: in the end, especially after a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Eventually they reached an agreement.; He eventually got round to fixing the bike.; Anyway Pat eventually apologized to me.

_source.definition_text: almost never
_source.learnerexamples_text: We hardly ever go out these days.; My bedroom hardly ever looks tidy.

_source.definition_text: continuously since that time
_source.learnerexamples_text: We met at school and have been friends ever since.; He's been depressed ever since he got divorced.; The pen was given [to me] by my father on my birthday and I have treasured it ever since.

_source.definition_text: always in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm not going to live here for ever.; My friend was leaving the city for ever and [going] to a city in another country.

_source.definition_text: a very
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's ever such a good dancer.; The psychiatrist was a very nice young girl that helped me ever such a lot.

_source.definition_text: very
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was ever so kind of you to meet us at the airport.; It was ever so kind of you to take the trouble and make room for us although we arrived quite unexpectedly.

_source.definition_text: better/faster/happier, etc. than at any time before
_source.searchterms_text: better/faster/happier etc than ever;better/faster/happier, etc. than ever;ever
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is running faster than ever.; First of all, I would like to thank you for your invitation to the new opening of Longridge Arts Centre, the centre looks better than ever and I enjoyed the arts exhibition that is on now.

_source.definition_text: always changing/growing/increasing, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: ever;ever changing/growing/increasing, etc.;ever-changing/growing/increasing etc;ever-changing/growing/increasing, etc.;everchanging/growing/increasing, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We live in an ever-changing world.; In our ever-changing society, in the affluent cities of the Western world, life moves at such a fast pace that parents are the reflection and the result of our times, the cogs of a large, rather uncontrollable wheel.

_source.definition_text: each one of a group of people or things
_source.learnerexamples_text: Every time I go to London I get caught in a traffic jam.; Ten pence is donated to charity for every bottle sold.; She ate up every (single) bit of her fish.; Every shop say[s] M[e]rry Xmas in front of the shop.

_source.definition_text: used to show that something is repeated regularly
_source.learnerexamples_text: He goes to Ireland every summer.; Computers can perform millions of calculations every second.; Every four minutes a car is stolen in this city.; Every few kilometres we passed a burnt out truck at the side of the road.; The conference takes place every other/second year.

_source.definition_text: sometimes, but not often
_source.learnerexamples_text: We still meet up every now and then.; Each day choose 10 new words and learn them by heart. In a week you will have learned 70 new words, and in a year 3640, a lot of words. Please, do not forget to repeat them every now and then.

_source.definition_text: as much as is possible
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to wish you every success in your new job.; She has every reason to be unhappy after losing her job and her home.; You had every opportunity to make a complaint.; Every effort is being made to minimise civilian casualties.; She has every right to be proud of her tremendous achievements.

_source.definition_text: sometimes, but not often
_source.learnerexamples_text: He went into town every so often to buy supplies.; Elizabeth and others visited her every so often until [one] day she left them.

_source.definition_text: happening one day/week, etc but not the next
_source.searchterms_text: every;every other day/week etc;every other day/week, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Alice goes to the gym every other day.; The rubbish is collected every other day, which is quite often.

_source.definition_text: every person
_source.learnerexamples_text: Everyone agreed with me.; Everyone involved in the accident has been questioned by the police.; Would everyone who wishes to attend the dinner let me know by Friday afternoon?; I had dressed up but everyone else was wearing jeans.; Almost everyone went to the party.

_source.definition_text: every person
_source.learnerexamples_text: Everybody thought it was a good idea.; I've received replies from everybody but Jane.; Goodbye, everybody - see you next week.; I'm sorry, but you'll just have to wait your turn like everybody else.; I was so happy, [because] everybody had a good time.

_source.definition_text: all things
_source.learnerexamples_text: The thieves took everything.; You can't blame him for everything.; Everything looks so much nicer in the sunshine.; Is everything all right, Angela?; The fish wasn't very fresh, but everything else tasted good.

_source.base_text: do everything in your power to do sth
_source.definition_text: to do everything that you are able and allowed to do in order to achieve something
_source.searchterms_text: do everything in your power to do sth;everything;everythings
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've done everything in my power to help him. ; I think of myself as an open-minded and cheerful person and if I get the job I will do everything in my power to make sure your visitors will have a great time at the theme park.

_source.definition_text: to be the most important part of someone's life
_source.learnerexamples_text: His children mean everything to him.; Money isn't everything.; I think that every person has a different opinion, but for me, money and fame isn't everything in life.

_source.definition_text: in or to every place
_source.learnerexamples_text: I looked everywhere for my keys.; Everywhere I look I see things that remind me of Brendan.; We had to stay in a hotel outside the town as everywhere else was fully booked.; I love the teddy bear because it's soft and I can take it with me everywhere.

_source.definition_text: information that is given or objects that are shown in a court of law to help to prove if someone has committed a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was arrested despite the lack of evidence against him.; My new neighbour murdered his wife and although the circumstan[t]i[a]l evidence against him was enormous, the case was dismissed because of the lack of some clinching piece of evidence.

_source.definition_text: something that makes you believe that something is true or exists
_source.learnerexamples_text: evidence of global warming; There is no evidence that the theory is true.; New evidence suggests/shows this argument is flawed. ; There is scientific evidence that the drug is addictive.;  All the evidence points to a substantial rise in traffic over the next few years.

_source.definition_text: obvious to everyone and easy to see or understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: The full extent of the damage only became evident the following morning.;  From the smell it was evident that the drains had been blocked for several days.; In conclusion, it is evident that it is better to do shopping in big supermarkets or shopping centres than small local shops in terms of time, money, working hours and family life.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is easy to see
_source.learnerexamples_text: He evidently likes her.; There are, evidently, points in favour and points against.

_source.definition_text: something that is very bad and harmful
_source.learnerexamples_text: Drug-addiction is one of today's great social evils.; The theme of the play is the battle between good and evil.; It is not simply [the] confronting of good and evil.

_source.definition_text: very cruel, bad or harmful
_source.learnerexamples_text: an evil monster; These people are just evil.; She is a very dark and evil person who can't forget the first Mrs. de Winter.

_source.definition_text: the way in which living things change and develop over millions of years
_source.learnerexamples_text: Darwin's theory of evolution; I think it is good to have zoos, but we shouldn't try to control natural evolution as we have done until now.

_source.definition_text: a gradual process of change and development
_source.learnerexamples_text: the evolution of language; [Leonardo's] studies and projects on mechanics puzzle us and foresee the future evolution of science and technology.

_source.definition_text: to develop or make something develop, usually gradually
_source.learnerexamples_text: rapidly evolving technology ; This device has evolved from being a large machine into the size of a notebook.

_source.definition_text: completely correct in every detail
_source.learnerexamples_text: The exact distance is 1.838 metres.; I'm afraid I can't give you exact details.; The exact location of the factory has yet to be decided.; They've lived here a long time - 25 years to be exact.; I am looking forward to your next letter to know the exact time of your [arrival].

_source.definition_text: used when you are giving or asking for information that is completely correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: The journey took exactly three hours.; Where are you staying exactly?; I don't know exactly what time I'll arrive.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize what you are saying
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've found some shoes that are exactly the same colour as that dress.; Do exactly what I tell you and no-one will get hurt!; That's exactly why I didn't go.; That is exactly one of the reasons [why] I decided to join a new English class.

_source.definition_text: something you say when you agree completely with someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Surely they should have told us about this problem sooner?" "Exactly!"

_source.definition_text: used to say that something is not completely true
_source.learnerexamples_text: "So you gave her your book?" "Not exactly, I lent it to her."

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that someone or something does not have a particular quality
_source.searchterms_text: exactly;not exactly easy/new/rich etc;not exactly easy/new/rich, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's face it, we're not exactly rich, are we?; The Hotel Royal was not exactly luxurious.

_source.definition_text: when you describe something as larger, better, worse, etc. than it really is
_source.learnerexamples_text: a slight/gross exaggeration of the facts ; You wrote about "a sudden downpour of rain" which was a huge exaggeration.

_source.definition_text: to make something seem larger, better, worse, etc. than it really is
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't exaggerate - it didn't cost that much!; Without exaggerating, I would like to mention that she is dependable and trustworthy but also tactful and supportive.

_source.definition_text: an official test of how much you know about something, or how well you can do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: How many pupils are sitting/taking the geography exam this term?; I failed my physics exam, but I passed chemistry.; exam papers ; exam results ; I will take my exam on December 8.

_source.definition_text: an exam
_source.learnerexamples_text: a written examination; We try to improve our English, because we must pass [the] P.E.T. examination to complete our studies.

_source.definition_text: when someone looks at or considers something carefully in order to discover something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a medical examination; I had to have a medical examination when I started my new job.; The evidence is still under examination.; I thought it was paint at first, but on closer examination I realised it was dried blood.; Finally we went to the hospital for a medical examination and fortunately we were all right.

_source.definition_text: to look at or consider a person or thing carefully and in detail in order to discover something about them
_source.learnerexamples_text: She picked up the knife and examined it closely.; He was examined by a doctor as soon as he arrived.; Experts are examining the wreckage for clues about the cause of the explosion.; I examined both of them and finally I discovered [that it] was a virus changed genetically in order to kill people.

_source.definition_text: to test someone to see how much they know or how well they can do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: You'll be examined in three main areas: speaking, listening, and reading comprehension.; Be prepared, not only in the [areas] you will be examined in.

_source.definition_text: someone who tests how much you know about something, or how well you can do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The writing paper is marked by trained examiners.; When the examiner said that I had passed, I could not believe it.

_source.definition_text: something which is typical of the group of things that is being talked about
_source.learnerexamples_text: This painting here is a marvellous example of her work.; Could you give me an example of the improvements you have mentioned?; This is a very good/typical example of medieval Chinese architecture.; Look at the example before you do the exercise.; I like rap music, one example of that is El Santo.

_source.definition_text: to do something in a good way so that other people might try to copy you
_source.learnerexamples_text: Try to set a good example to the children.; It sets a good example for other museums.

_source.definition_text: used to give an example of the type of thing you mean
