_source.learnerexamples_text: I like soft fruit, for example peaches and plums.; Some people, students for example, can get cheaper tickets.; Also he likes to do sports, for example swimming and c[ycl]ing.

_source.definition_text: someone or something that is very good and should be copied
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is a very good example to the rest of the class.; You are a shining example for you[r] colle[a]gues.

_source.definition_text: a very good example of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is a prime example of what happens when communication is poor.; In this context in the analyses of Piggy's character, it strikes me as a first spontaneous impression that he personifies the typical proper schoolboy who will later on undoubtedly grow up to be the prime example of a good and responsible citizen.

_source.definition_text: to be more than a particular number or amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sales have exceeded $1 million so far this year.; Our administration costs didn't exceed 5%, the other 10% were the pure costs of the entertainment.

_source.definition_text: to be much bigger or better than expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: The location of the apartment exceeded our expectations.; They might exceed our expectations with the top-quality cuisine, which is fine as long as it is value for money; we don't want an unaffordable canteen.

_source.definition_text: to drive faster than you are allowed to according to the law
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was caught exceeding the speed limit.; There are three ground rules you have to follow: stop at stop-signs, don't exceed the speed limit and don't be in the way of other cars.

_source.definition_text: to be very good at something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Paula always excelled in languages at school.; If a school is successful, it will provide opportunities for the child to excel in other areas such as the creative arts, like music, dance, painting and drama, and also sports.

_source.definition_text: to do something better than you usually do
_source.learnerexamples_text: The British team have excelled themselves this year to reach the finals.; As far as the acting is concerned, the interaction between the lead actors is amazing while Catherine Zeta Jones excels herself in the highly demanding role of the client.

_source.definition_text: extremely good
_source.learnerexamples_text: The food was excellent.; Her car is in excellent condition.; The fall in interest rates is excellent news for borrowers.; I had an excellent supper and danced with Nat.

_source.definition_text: not including a particular fact, thing or person
_source.learnerexamples_text: The museum is open daily except Mondays.; It's cool and quiet everywhere except in the kitchen.; Everyone was there except for Sally.; All of my friends came except you.

_source.definition_text: used to give a reason why something is not possible or true
_source.learnerexamples_text: I want to go, except that I'm tired.; She would have passed the exam, except that she was ill on the day.

_source.definition_text: someone or something that is not included in a rule, group or list or that does not behave in the expected way
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are exceptions to every rule.; I like all kinds of films with the exception of horror films.; Her books are always entertaining and this one is no exception.; You must report here every Tuesday without exception.; The animals looked so sad to me. So I decided to set them free, all of them, without exception.

_source.definition_text: to not treat someone or something according to the usual rules
_source.learnerexamples_text: They don't usually take cheques, but they said they'd make an exception in my case.; Unfortunately, they were not flexible enough to make an exception, but on the other hand we know about the problem now and can avoid it in the future.

_source.definition_text: to be annoyed or insulted by something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took exception to being asked to sweep the floor.; I hope you will not take exception to my words, but I think that this course of action is rather foolish and illogical.

_source.definition_text: extremely good
_source.learnerexamples_text: He really is an exceptional student.; This trip constitutes an exceptional challenge for me.

_source.definition_text: very unusual and not likely to happen very often
_source.learnerexamples_text: Visitors are only allowed in exceptional circumstances.; However, there are always some exceptional circumstances in which they fail to understand what is appropriate for them.

_source.definition_text: extremely
_source.learnerexamples_text: an exceptionally gifted student; Jacky Chan is an exceptionally hardworking person who won't let anything bring him down and he has a great sense of humour which is why most people like him.

_source.definition_text: more of something than is usual or needed
_source.learnerexamples_text: An excess of oil on the markets has caused prices to fall sharply.;  He earns in excess of £60,000 a year.; We should change our behaviour and buy what we need and not in excess, giving the children a pattern to follow.

_source.definition_text: to do something too much
_source.learnerexamples_text: He occasionally has a beer, but he never drinks to excess. ; We eat and drink to excess only to face the consequences later on.

_source.definition_text: more than is usual or allowed
_source.learnerexamples_text: We had to pay £100 for excess baggage. ; Most students feel that they need to get rid of excess energy at the end of the day and also convey that they are hampered by the fact that not enough sports facilities are available.

_source.definition_text: more than is necessary or wanted
_source.learnerexamples_text: They accused the police of using excessive force.; On the other hand the excessive use of mobile telephones ha[s given] us the excuse to decrease our face to face contact.

_source.definition_text: when you give something to someone and they give you something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: an exchange  of ideas/information ; They were given food and shelter in exchange for work.; So, it was a very interesting exchange of ideas.

_source.definition_text: an arrangement by which students and teachers from one country go to stay with students and teachers in another country
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you going on the French exchange this year?; His name is Rob and, [like] me, [he] applied to the student exchange program.

_source.definition_text: to give something to someone and receive something similar from them
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's traditional for the two teams to exchange shirts after the game.; We exchanged addresses and telephone numbers.; She moved to another part of town and we forgot to exchange our addresses.

_source.definition_text: to take something back to the shop where you bought it and change it for something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: Goods can only be exchanged on production of the original receipt.; Could I exchange this shirt for a larger size?

_source.definition_text: If two people exchange looks, opinions, views, etc., they look at each other, talk to each other, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: exchange;exchange looks opinions views etc;exchange looks, opinions, views, etc.;exchanged;exchanges;exchanging
_source.learnerexamples_text: The group meets every month to exchange their views on a book they have all read.; You can exchange opinions with them as to the way of life in Japan and your country.

_source.definition_text: the rate at which the money of one country can be changed for the money of another country
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Money Ready Reckoner gives the exchange rate for any country you plan to visit and shows how much currency you will get.; I looked around and saw a shop with the notice "Currency exchange". I decided to [go] in [to find out] the exchange rate.

_source.definition_text: feeling very happy and enthusiastic
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you getting excited about your holiday?; An excited crowd waited for the singer to arrive.; I am very excited!

_source.definition_text: in an excited way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She ran excitedly down the hall to greet her cousins.; We talked excitedly about it all the way home.

_source.definition_text: when people feel very happy and enthusiastic
_source.learnerexamples_text: The competition is causing a lot of excitement.; If you want excitement, you should try parachuting.; However, if you are looking for fun and excitement, I would go for the city.

_source.definition_text: making you feel very happy and enthusiastic
_source.learnerexamples_text: an exciting film/match ; You're going to Africa? How exciting!; I enjoyed [the game] very much, because it was very exciting.

_source.definition_text: to say something suddenly and loudly because you are surprised, annoyed, excited, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: "How terrible!" she exclaimed. ; Then he would exclaim, "What a wonderful selection," with a robust laugh.

_source.definition_text: a punctuation mark (!) used at the end of a sentence that expresses surprise, excitement or shock
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her emails are full of exclamation marks.; The day was wonderful as I got two A's with [an] exclamation mark.

_source.definition_text: to not allow someone or something to take part in an activity or enter a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: Women are still excluded from the club.; Sometimes the range of sports offered is small and they feel excluded from some sports because they are not fit enough or the sport is too violent.

_source.definition_text: to intentionally not include something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The insurance cover excludes particular medical conditions.; Thus, excluding the cost of organising the day, we were able to give 85% of what we earned to the hospital.

_source.definition_text: expensive and only for people who are rich or of a high social class
_source.learnerexamples_text: an exclusive club/hotel/shop ; an exclusive part of town; We can also discern sophisticated, exclusive shops with expensive clothes in the city centres.

_source.definition_text: not shared with another person, organization, newspaper, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: an exclusive interview ; They don't have a personal life anymore because of this and photographers are following them everywhere because they want to take an exclusive picture, so they can earn a lot of money with it when a magazine wants to buy it.

_source.definition_text: not including something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The price of the meal is exclusive of drinks.; Preferred areas are [mainly] in North, North West, South East and South West London with a budget of £800 per month exclusive of Council Tax and Bills.

_source.definition_text: only
_source.learnerexamples_text: an exclusively female audience; In addition, the reduced price mentioned refers exclusively to UK students, which caused significant problems.

_source.definition_text: used to politely get someone's attention
_source.learnerexamples_text: Excuse me, does this bus go to Oxford Street?; While I was waiting for my fast food, someone knocked my shoulder. I turn[ed and saw] a girl about my age. I asked: - Excuse me, did you call me?

_source.definition_text: used to say sorry for something that you do without intending to
_source.learnerexamples_text: Oh, excuse me, did I take your seat?; Excuse me, I'm going to miss the English class tomorrow.

_source.definition_text: to forgive someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please excuse me for arriving late - the bus was delayed.; Please excuse my appearance - I've been painting.; I hope you'll excuse me now, I have to do my homework.

_source.definition_text: to be given as a reason for someone's bad behaviour, so that it does not seem so bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: Nothing can excuse that sort of behaviour.; Their main goals are to save the animals and/or to show the animals to the public in order to make us take an interest in the animals and in ecology. I think that these purposes can excuse [the fact] that the animals are locked up, if they [have] enough space and [are] treated very well.

_source.definition_text: a reason that you give to explain why you did something wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: What was his excuse for being late?; He'd better have a good excuse for not being here!; I've never known him to miss a meeting - I'm sure he'll have an excuse.; There's no excuse for that sort of behaviour.; I had no excuse to give [for] being late with this report.

_source.definition_text: a false reason that you give to explain why you do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Nick was just looking for an excuse to call her.; Any excuse for a holiday!; Also shopping for clothes is an excuse to go out with girls!!

_source.definition_text: to kill someone as a legal punishment
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was executed for murder.; She might even have had some cruel aspects in her personality for she did not hesitate to execute traitors.

_source.definition_text: to do something, such as follow a plan or order
_source.learnerexamples_text: to execute a deal/plan; When he controls the work of the other staff members, he wants to find out [whether] they executed their duties perfectly.

_source.definition_text: relating to making decisions and managing businesses
_source.learnerexamples_text: an executive director; So I am now an executive director, I have a job and I know very important people in the Romanian Government.

_source.definition_text: to be or give a typical example of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: This painting perfectly exemplifies the naturalistic style which was so popular at the time.; Okonkwo serves to exemplify to the reader the consequences that the Igbo people were suffering.

_source.definition_text: someone who has an important job in a business
_source.learnerexamples_text: a company executive; The main reason why I attended this conference was to learn how international companies select their employees and how I could improve my qualifications as a finance executive.

_source.definition_text: physical activity that you do to make your body strong and healthy
_source.l_topic_text_text: body and health, people: actions, shopping
_source.learnerexamples_text: You really should take more exercise.; Swimming is my favourite form of exercise.; I do stomach exercises most days.; I can also [take some] exercise with the bicycle.

_source.definition_text: a set of actions that a group of soldiers do to practise their skills
_source.learnerexamples_text: The cadets are out on military exercises.; I am not opposed to military exercises, but such a noisy activity cannot be tolerated in a world in which environmental protection should be promoted by everybody, [including] the army.

_source.definition_text: a short piece of written work which you do to practise something you are learning
_source.learnerexamples_text: The book has exercises at the end of every chapter.; It's a new book and it has all [the] nece[s]sary exercises for secondary school.

_source.definition_text: to do physical activities to make your body strong and healthy
_source.l_topic_text_text: body and health, people: actions, shopping
_source.learnerexamples_text: She exercises most evenings, usually by running.; A work-out in the gym will exercise all the major muscle groups.; It's funny how I heard about that; I was at the gym with Sarah, we were exercising when we heard Tom talking about it with John.

_source.definition_text: to use a power, right, or ability
_source.learnerexamples_text: You should always exercise your right to vote.; However, if you believe that nothing can be done, I have to inform you that we will exercise our legal rights and take action against you.

_source.definition_text: the waste gas from a vehicle's engine
_source.learnerexamples_text: exhaust fumes ; Therefore, it might cause a great deal of pollution because of exhaust fumes.

_source.definition_text: to make someone very tired
_source.learnerexamples_text: The long journey exhausted the children.; I think that the students were expecting to be given a job that would actually improve their English and not just exhaust them physically.

_source.definition_text: the pipe that waste gas from a vehicle's engine flows through
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car needs a new exhaust.; There are traffic jams and it becomes a real hell to drive or simply to walk (because of the noise and pollution of exhaust pipes).

_source.definition_text: extremely tired
_source.learnerexamples_text: By the time they reached the summit they were exhausted.; Exhausted, they fell asleep.; When we got back home I was absolutely exhausted.

_source.definition_text: making you feel extremely tired
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've had an exhausting day.; We will also have the opportunity to drink a coffee or have a snack after an exhausting day in the swimming pool!!

_source.definition_text: when you are extremely tired
_source.learnerexamples_text: She felt ill with exhaustion.; The tennis star is said to be suffering from exhaustion.; Eighty kilometres is a pretty long distance and there is a threat that our trip would turn out to be a gruelling experience because of physical exhaustion.

_source.definition_text: complete and including everything
_source.learnerexamples_text: an exhaustive account of the incident; I think this report is exhaustive and that we can rely on this institution, should other colleagues be sent on a similar course there.

_source.definition_text: to show objects such as paintings to the public
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's exhibiting her roses at the local flower show.; One of the most important pictures of Van Gogh will be exhibited at the London Museum during the summer holidays.

_source.definition_text: to show a feeling, quality, or ability
_source.learnerexamples_text: The crew exhibited great courage when the plane crashed. ; I consider my father a successful man because he exhibits all the qualities I've mentioned above.

_source.definition_text: an object such as a painting that is shown to the public
_source.learnerexamples_text: a museum exhibit ; Apart from that, there are English-speaking tourist guides in museums and historical sites, so that visitors can enjoy them and understand what the exhibits are.

_source.definition_text: when objects such as paintings are shown to the public
_source.learnerexamples_text: to see/visit an exhibition; an exhibition centre ; There's a new exhibition of sculpture on at the city gallery.; We went to the Royal Academy to see the Kandinsky exhibition.

_source.definition_text: when someone has to leave their home and live in another country, often for political reasons
_source.learnerexamples_text: He spent the war years in exile in New York.;  The King was forced into exile.; In the exhibition I would like to depict the years he has spent in exile in India, a neighbouring country of Tibet.

_source.definition_text: to be present or real
_source.learnerexamples_text: Poverty still exists in this country.; Ghosts don't exist anyway.; Buses will not exist any more and everyone will have his own car and his own computer too.

_source.definition_text: to live in difficult conditions
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can't exist without water for more than a week.; It's hard to exist without water, so there were long queues to our local wells.

_source.definition_text: when something or someone exists
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many people question the existence of God.; According to modern cosmology, the Universe came into existence about fifteen billion years ago.; The theatre company that they started is still in existence today.; The book gives explanations about all these popular beliefs about ghosts and their supposed existence among living people.

_source.definition_text: describes something that exists now
_source.learnerexamples_text: The existing church was built in the sixteenth century.; The existing laws are inadequate.; The computer upgraded most of the existing inventions, and made them more efficient, faster and [more user-friendly].

_source.definition_text: a particular way of life
_source.learnerexamples_text: We could have a much more peaceful existence in the countryside.; People from all over the world emigrated to the fifth continent and it was believed that they would have a better existence there.

_source.definition_text: the door or gate which you use to leave a public building or place
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fire exit; an emergency exit; the main exit; I'll meet you tonight [at] the exit of Wood Green station.

_source.definition_text: a road which you use to leave a motorway or roundabout
_source.learnerexamples_text: Take the third exit at the next roundabout.; You should take the motorway from Palermo to Mazzara and take the third exit.

_source.definition_text: to stop using a program on a computer
_source.learnerexamples_text: Press escape to exit the game.

_source.definition_text: unusual, interesting and often foreign
_source.learnerexamples_text: exotic flowers/fruits ; Even if you do not have any cooking skills you can enjoy exotic meals.

_source.definition_text: to increase in size or amount, or to make something increase in this way
_source.learnerexamples_text: The air in the balloon expands when heated.; They expanded their retail operations during the 1980s.; I would like to expand my library.

_source.definition_text: when something increases in size or amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: These years saw the rapid expansion of the software industry.; More effective ways includ[e] the construction of bridges [in] heavy traffic areas and the expansion of METRO to even more areas of Athens.

_source.definition_text: to think or believe that something will happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: We are expecting a lot of applicants for the job.; I expect (that) she'll be very angry.; He didn't expect to see me.; I expect that it is going to be sunny because in the hotel there is a swimming-pool.

_source.definition_text: to be waiting for someone or something to arrive
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm expecting a letter from my sister.; I wasn't expecting any message.

_source.definition_text: to think that someone should behave in a particular way or do a particular thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: You will be expected to work some weekends.; You have to satisfy your boss [but] you do not have to do more than you are expected to.

_source.definition_text: used to show that you think something is likely to be true
_source.learnerexamples_text: I expect Isabel's told you about me?; "Will you be coming to the party?" "I expect so."

_source.definition_text: to be going to have a baby
_source.searchterms_text: be expecting (a baby);be expecting a baby;expect;expected;expecting;expects
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm expecting our first baby in May.; When I was nine or ten years old, my mother was expecting a baby.

_source.definition_text: when you expect good things to happen in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: The holiday lived up to all our expectations.; I have high expectations for this job.; We did so well - beyond all our expectations.; The talks given by writers were up to my expectations and it was a pleasure to attend all of them.

_source.definition_text: to be much bigger or better than expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: The location of the apartment exceeded our expectations.; They might exceed our expectations with the top-quality cuisine, which is fine as long as it is value for money; we don't want an unaffordable canteen.

_source.definition_text: thought likely to happen or be true
_source.learnerexamples_text: The expected power cuts never happened.; I went into the theatre on time but became a little bit angry [at having to] wait until 20:15, forty-five minutes after the expected starting time.

_source.definition_text: the total amount of money that a government or person spends
_source.learnerexamples_text: The government's annual expenditure on arms has been reduced. ; First of all, and it is the most obvious solution, government expenditure on subsidies for [the] homeless should increase.

_source.definition_text: an organized journey, especially a long one for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: Shackleton led several expeditions in the Antarctic.; I was with my father on Mount Tahan [and] I had the best time of my life during this expedition.

_source.definition_text: the money that you spend on something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Buying a bigger car has proved to be well worth the expense.; We've just had a new garage built at great expense.; It's silly to go to the expense of buying new clothes when you don't really need them.; You have to pay/cover your own medical expenses.; We couldn't afford the expense of a new car [at] that time.

_source.definition_text: in order to make someone look stupid
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stop making jokes at my expense.; But despite his intellectual superiority, Piggy was subject to derision because of his physical outward appearance and the group of boys played jokes at his expense.

_source.definition_text: If you do one thing at the expense of another, doing the first thing harms the second thing.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He spent a lot of time at work, at the expense of his marriage.; Unfortunately one is usually done at the expense of the other.

_source.definition_text: money that you spend when you are doing your job, that your employer will pay back to you
_source.learnerexamples_text: travel expenses; They pay us two hundred pounds a week, plus expenses.; They actually helped me a lot with relocation and even reimbursed my travel expenses.

_source.definition_text: costing a lot of money
_source.learnerexamples_text: expensive jewellery; He buys very expensive clothes.; It's expensive to run a car.; She has expensive tastes.; My mother bought the glass for me last year and it's very expensive.

_source.definition_text: knowledge that you get from doing a job, or from doing, seeing, or feeling something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has a lot of teaching experience.; You become more confident in your work as you get more experience.; Do you have any experience of working with children?; I know from experience that you can't trust him.; In my experience, people smile back if you smile at them.

_source.definition_text: something that happens to you that affects how you feel
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had a rather unpleasant experience at the dentist's.; My trip to Australia was an experience I shall never forget.; It was a great experience, we talked for 3 hours about lots of thing[s].

_source.definition_text: If you experience something, it happens to you, or you feel it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We experienced a lot of difficulty in selling our house.; It was the worst pain I'd ever experienced.; We had three fantastic days [- the best] we have ever experienced.

_source.definition_text: a test, especially a scientific one, that you do in order to learn something or to discover whether something is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Some people believe that experiments on animals should be banned.; Scientists are carrying out/doing experiments to test the effectiveness of the new drug.; In the chemistry lab experiments are often set up.

_source.definition_text: having skill or knowledge because you have done something many times
_source.learnerexamples_text: an experienced teacher; She is very experienced in marketing.; You can go to the nearest village, where you can [do a] mountain walk led by experienced guides.

_source.definition_text: to try something in order to discover what it is like
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did he ever experiment with drugs?; Last year I started to take a lot of black and white photos and I wanted to follow the process all the way through so I bought an enlarger. I was now able to experiment with all sorts of te[chniq]ues.

_source.definition_text: to do an experiment
_source.learnerexamples_text: Experimenting on mice can give us an idea of the effect of the disease in humans.; Firstly, scientists are the best contributors [for a] better world around us being smarter and hard-working, gaining knowledge and experimenting in laborato[ries].

_source.definition_text: relating to tests, especially scientific ones
_source.learnerexamples_text: The two scientists used very different experimental methods.; But in my opinion this is no excuse to discard the findings of numerous well-educated nutritionist[s] and food specialists who devote long [h]ours to researching the eating habits of the people of the world, who sift through data from times gone by to find out about our predecessors' habits and who build and test hypotheses in strictly controlled experimental conditions.

_source.definition_text: someone who has a lot of skill in something or a lot of knowledge of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a computer/gardening/medical expert; He's an expert on Japanese literature.; My "personal" trainer is Peter, he is a real expert in running.

_source.definition_text: having or showing a lot of knowledge or skill
_source.learnerexamples_text: The centre provides expert advice for people with financial problems.; What's your expert opinion?; We're not expert cyclists and we could [get] tired before we get to the Mountain Hostel.

_source.definition_text: If a legal document or agreement expires, you can no longer use it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your contract expired six months ago.; My rental contract expired last month and I wanted to find a bigger place, which I am delighted to say I did.

_source.definition_text: to make something clear or easy to understand by giving reasons for it or details about it
_source.learnerexamples_text: If there's anything you don't understand, I'll be happy to explain.; The teacher explained the rules to the children.; Our guide explained where the cathedral was.; He explained how the machine worked.; Please could you explain why you're so late.

_source.definition_text: the details or reasons that someone gives to make something clear or easy to understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: What was her explanation for why she was late?; Could you give me a quick explanation of how it works?; There must be some kind of explanation.

_source.definition_text: showing or talking about sex or violence in a very detailed way
_source.learnerexamples_text: an explicit film; One is not supposed to watch explicit movies under the age of 16 [nor] drink alcohol under the age of 18.

_source.definition_text: clear and exact
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was very explicit about her plans.; He made no explicit references to Tess.; Rules have to be explicit and well explained so that they [can] be strictly followed.

_source.definition_text: If something such as a bomb explodes, it bursts with noise and force, and if you explode it, you make it burst with noise and force.
_source.learnerexamples_text: A bomb exploded at one of London's busiest railway stations this morning.; He was driving so fast that his car tyre exploded.; A bomb had exploded and that boy rescued me from the accident.

_source.definition_text: to treat someone unfairly for your own advantage
_source.learnerexamples_text: Laws exist to stop companies exploiting their employees.; I suppose those people are often exploited and do not have real friends with whom they can share feelings and emotions. Therefore I believe being a famous person is also synon[y]mous [with] being lonely.

_source.definition_text: a journey to a place to find out about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Livingstone was the first European to make an exploration of the Zambesi river. ; She's always loved travel and exploration.; In the near future robots will take part in space exploration, as well as ocean exploration.

_source.definition_text: to use or develop something to your advantage
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to make sure that we exploit our resources as fully as possible.; John would certainly exploit this unique opportunity and meet the interviewer's expectations easily.

_source.definition_text: to go around a place where you have never been in order to find out what is there
_source.learnerexamples_text: The best way to explore the countryside is on foot.; The children have gone exploring in the woods.; You can walk and explore in the jungle.

_source.definition_text: to find out more about something, often something that you might do in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're exploring the possibility of buying a holiday home.; It is a great camera and I still [have] not explore[d] all [the] possibilities it holds.

_source.definition_text: when something such as a bomb explodes
_source.learnerexamples_text: Forty people were killed in the explosion.; The fire was thought to have been caused by a gas explosion.; I was doing my homework when I heard an explosion.

_source.definition_text: when something increases suddenly by a large amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: the recent population explosion ; The factors leading to this population explosion in cities of the world might vary from country to country and city to city, but there is one common demominator - the quest for a better life.

_source.definition_text: An explosive situation or subject causes strong feelings, and may make people angry or violent.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a highly explosive political issue; Moreover, there are some explosive issues that give them food for thought, such as the environmental pollution, and the poverty.

_source.definition_text: An explosive substance or piece of equipment can cause explosions.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The explosive device was hidden in a suitcase.; an explosive mixture of oil vapour and oxygen; The small piece of an explosive material caused chaos in the streets of London.

_source.definition_text: a substance or piece of equipment that can cause explosions
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was caught smuggling explosives into the building.; It was in this background of events that Riyaz Mohammed drove a van loaded with a thousand kilos of explosives into the US embassy compound in Nairobi, Kenya, causing the deaths of hundreds of Kenyans and dozens of American citizens.

_source.definition_text: to send goods to another country for sale
_source.learnerexamples_text: French cheeses are exported to many different countries.; Our clothes sell so well in this country that we have no need to export.; And of course, while Italy is exporting pizza, spaghetti and food like that, Italian people are able to try different food from foreign countries, like hamburger[s], Chinese food, or pudding.

_source.definition_text: a product that you sell in another country or the business of selling products in another country
_source.learnerexamples_text: Coffee is one of Brazil's main exports.; The export of ivory is now strictly controlled.; India grows tea for export.; We are planning to develop our export market.; At present I work for a Multinational company as export officer.

_source.definition_text: to experience something or be affected by something because you are in a particular situation or place
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was the first time I'd been exposed to violence.; Also, with television, we might be exposed to violence in some films and advertisements, which does not happen [if] we read a book.

_source.definition_text: to make public something bad or dishonest
_source.learnerexamples_text: The review exposed widespread corruption in the police force.; The newspaper story exposed him as a liar.; If I do not receive full satisfaction, I will expose your operation by writing to the newspaper.

_source.definition_text: when someone experiences something or is affected by it because they are in a particular situation or place
_source.learnerexamples_text: There is a risk of exposure to radiation.; Many young children now have exposure to computers in the home.; Due to exposure to low temperatures throughout the tour I developed pneumonia and had to be admitted to hospital on arrival [in] London.

_source.definition_text: to show what you think or how you feel using words or actions
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm simply expressing my opinion.; I would like to express my thanks for your kindness.; I'm sorry, I'm not expressing myself very clearly.; Words can't express how happy I am.; Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to express my dissatisfaction about the show you presented two weeks ago at your theatre.

_source.definition_text: the look on someone's face, showing what they feel or think
_source.learnerexamples_text: facial expressions; He had such a sad expression on his face.; I could tell from her expression that something serious had happened.; He had a funny expression on his face.

_source.definition_text: a word or phrase
_source.learnerexamples_text: He uses a lot of informal expressions.; 'A can of worms' is an expression which means 'a difficult situation'.; With th[ese] kind[s] of videos, they could learn words and expressions used every day by normal people talking to normal people.

_source.definition_text: when you show what you think or how you feel using words or actions
_source.learnerexamples_text: He wrote her a poem as an expression of his love.; We've received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.;  Freedom of expression is a basic human right.; It's better to give expression to your anger, rather than hiding it.; It always thrilled me, the energy and expression this dance had.

_source.definition_text: showing your feelings
_source.learnerexamples_text: expressive language; a very expressive face; Ann was a beautiful girl with wonderful hair and expressive brown eyes.

_source.definition_text: very beautiful or perfect
_source.learnerexamples_text: a garden of exquisite flowers; On the forefinger of my left hand they can see the most exquisite diamond ring that they ever did see.

_source.definition_text: to make something bigger or longer
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have plans to extend our house.; They've extended their range of products.; The existing lighting loop would be extended and [the] capacity of the illumination would be increased.

_source.definition_text: to make an activity, agreement, etc. last for a longer time
_source.learnerexamples_text: They have extended the deadline by one week.; A lot of shops have extended their opening hours.; I need to extend my visa.; If we decide to extend our stay for two more days, does the offer still stand?

_source.definition_text: to continue or stretch over a particular area of land or period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: a mountain range that extends down the Italian peninsula; Will the building work extend into next week?

_source.definition_text: extra time that you are given to do or use something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've applied for an extension to my visa.

_source.definition_text: a telephone that is connected to the main telephone in an office or other large building
_source.learnerexamples_text: Call me on extension 3104.; For further information call 990-643 extension 93.

_source.definition_text: something that has developed as a result of something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: The book is an extension of ideas he set out in an earlier article.; So we might say the computer is the extension of our brain.

_source.definition_text: large in amount or size
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fire had caused extensive damage to the building.; This is probably the most extensive modern art collection in Europe.; The school has extensive grounds. ; The motorway was in need of extensive repairs.; Both events received extensive coverage in the newspapers.

_source.definition_text: mainly
_source.searchterms_text: extent;to a great/large etc extent;to a great/large, etc. extent
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their anger was to a large extent justified.; As we all know, TV, video and cinema have replaced books to an enormous extent.

_source.definition_text: the size or importance of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are just beginning to realize the full extent of the damage.; Her face was injured to such an extent that we didn't recognize her.; Rosie's teacher was impressed by the extent of her knowledge.; The River Nile is over 6500 kilometres in extent.; [For the] past couple of decades, TV has been diffused in Japan to such an extent that nowadays, one household is likely to have more than 2 TV sets that [show] a wide range of programmes nearly 24 hours [a day].

_source.base_text: to some extent/to a certain extent
_source.definition_text: in some ways
_source.searchterms_text: extent;to some extent/to a certain extent
_source.learnerexamples_text: To some extent, she was responsible for the accident.; I agree with you to a certain extent.; To a certain extent, this point of view seems to be very respectable.

_source.definition_text: the degree to which something happens or is likely to happen
_source.searchterms_text: extent;extent to which;the extent to which
_source.learnerexamples_text: The research should show the extent to which these changes are being implemented.; Several factors determine the extent to which a person's character may influence our own opinions and even our way of life, such as the time spent with that particular person, or the importance that figure has in our li[v]es.

_source.definition_text: the outside part of something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: The exterior of the house was painted white.; Thus, it is best for the management to improve the look of this building as other buildings in this area have a better looking exterior than ours.

_source.definition_text: relating to the outside part of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: the external walls of the house; This cream is for external use only.; If you see all this external decoration, you will probably fall in love [with] this art.

_source.definition_text: coming from or relating to another country, group, organization, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most news magazines have a section devoted to external affairs.; All exams are marked by an external examiner.

_source.definition_text: If a type of animal is extinct, it does not now exist.
_source.learnerexamples_text: These creatures could soon be extinct.; We are destroying the Earth by polluting it and we do not realise [this], and the thing is, we will not do so until we have made some species become extinct and we have damaged it all.

_source.definition_text: when a type of animal no longer exists
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many species of animal are threatened with extinction.; I wholeheartedly suggest that it should be returned to nature and to the turtles, as they face extinction after the loss of their natural home.

_source.definition_text: more, or more than usual
_source.learnerexamples_text: She babysits to earn a bit of extra cash.; He needs extra help with his English.; The price includes travel and accommodation but meals are extra.; You only have to bring an extra t-shirt.

_source.definition_text: more
_source.learnerexamples_text: They pay her extra to work nights.; Will there be any special events that cost extra?

_source.definition_text: something that you can get with something else if you pay a little more money
_source.learnerexamples_text: A sunroof is an optional extra on this model of the car.; The DVD contains many extras.

_source.definition_text: to remove or take out something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The oil which is extracted from olives is used mainly for cooking.; The tooth was eventually extracted.; I'm really sorry, but I can't come on the day before because I need to have my teeth extracted.

_source.definition_text: an actor in a film who does not have a main part and usually plays someone in a crowd
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was an extra in the crowd scene.; A theatre troop at the beginning of a new project is more often than not a flabbergasting rabble of actors, technicians, extras, back-stage workers and so forth.

_source.definition_text: a short part of a book, poem, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They published an extract from his autobiography.; The number of copied and read articles or book extracts ha[s] increased steadily.

_source.definition_text: very special, unusual or strange
_source.learnerexamples_text: He told the extraordinary story of his escape.; She was an extraordinary young woman.; On the next day there was an extraordinary thunderstorm!

_source.definition_text: very
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is, it must be said, extraordinarily beautiful.; Besides, the trip will be extraordinarily helpful for my course at school.

_source.definition_text: costing too much, or spending a lot more money than you need to
_source.learnerexamples_text: the extravagant lifestyle of a movie star; In some extreme cases, young people are known to have extravagant lifestyles and wasteful spending habits.

_source.definition_text: the most unusual or the most serious possible
_source.learnerexamples_text: extreme weather conditions ; In extreme cases, the disease can lead to blindness.; It seems to be an extreme case but it is a fact that modern children have no more contact with animal life.

_source.definition_text: very large in amount or degree
_source.learnerexamples_text: extreme pain/danger/wealth ; This time I promise that I will take extreme caution [with] your things.

_source.definition_text: having such strong opinions or beliefs that most people cannot agree with you
_source.learnerexamples_text: extreme views; the extreme right/left; Consequently, I can now express my disagreement [with] both articles, mostly because of the extreme opinions they [cont]ain.

_source.definition_text: very, or much more than usual
_source.learnerexamples_text: They played extremely well.; She's extremely beautiful/intelligent.; The film was extremely funny.

_source.definition_text: a sport or activity that is exciting and dangerous
_source.learnerexamples_text: I love most extreme sports, such as bungee jumping and white-water rafting.; You can go camping, climb mountains or learn a lot of extreme sports.

_source.definition_text: someone who has such strong opinions or beliefs that most people cannot agree with them
_source.learnerexamples_text: political/religious extremists; Be[ar]ing in mind all these strict rules my children have to follow they seem to be bound to become anarchic extremists.

_source.definition_text: someone who is very confident and likes being with other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is an extrovert.; She is an extrovert, a sociable person, who loves talking to people and is always ready to sacrif[i]ce her free time to make them happy.

_source.definition_text: one of the two organs in your face, which you use to see with
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has no sight in his left/right eye.; She's got beautiful green eyes.; He closed his eyes and went to sleep.; I like her long brown hair and blue eyes.

_source.definition_text: to be very surprised when you see someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw what he was wearing.; Well, this church was extremely simple [o]n the outside, but when I got inside it, I couldn't believe my eyes.

_source.definition_text: to watch or look after someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you keep an eye on this pan of soup for a moment?; You have to supply [e]verything they need and keep an eye on them all the time.

_source.definition_text: in someone's opinion
_source.learnerexamples_text: In my parents' eyes, I'll always be a child.; To answer your question right away, the boat trip is highly recommendable in my eyes!

_source.definition_text: to be good at noticing a particular type of thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your son has a very good eye for detail.; She's got an eye for details but a mind like anybody else's.

_source.base_text: can't keep/take your eyes off sb/sth
_source.definition_text: to be unable to stop looking at someone or something because they are so attractive or interesting
_source.searchterms_text: can't keep/take your eyes off sb/sth;eye;eyes
_source.learnerexamples_text: He couldn't take his eyes off her all night.; Her daughter, Lourdes Maria, is such a pretty little girl that I couldn't take my eyes off her.

_source.base_text: keep an eye out for sb/sth
_source.definition_text: to watch carefully for someone or something to appear
_source.searchterms_text: eye;eyes;keep an eye out for sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep an eye out for the delivery van.; Although individually we try to deliver the best care possible for our individual patients, we do keep an ear or an eye out for the other members of the team that day.

_source.definition_text: to choose to ignore something that you know is wrong or illegal
_source.searchterms_text: eye;eyes;turn a blind eye (to sth);turn a blind eye to sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Restaurant staff often took food home, and their boss turned a blind eye.; Nevertheless, we can't turn a blind eye to this reality.

_source.definition_text: to be famous and often featured in the media
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her new role means that she will be in the public eye.; But being famous also means that you are always in the public eye, which is a major drawback.

_source.definition_text: to get someone's attention by looking at them
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tried to catch her eye, but she had already turned away.; All of a sudden she caught my eye and smiled in a sad way.

_source.definition_text: to be attractive or different enough to be noticed by people
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was the colour of his jacket that caught my eye.; Dear Sir, I am writing regarding your newly published article about nutrition, which immediately caught my eye as I was reading your magazine.

_source.definition_text: to look at someone in a direct way, without showing fear or shame
_source.learnerexamples_text: Look me in the eye and say that you didn't steal it.; One day she looked me in the eyes with a sharp deep look - never have I seen such a deep look - and asked me what was happening and I told her.

_source.definition_text: If two people see eye to eye, they agree with each other.
_source.searchterms_text: eye;eyes;see eye to eye (with sb);see eye to eye with sb
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our teachers don't always see eye to eye with the headmaster.; Although I agree with some of the statements given by the young people, I do not see eye to eye with all of their viewpoints.

_source.definition_text: If someone cries their eyes out, they cry a lot about a problem or situation.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She cried her eyes out when he left her for another girl.; It wasn't an easy decision to make. Melanie spent many nights crying her eyes out in bed and trying to convince herself that she wasn't doing the right thing.

_source.definition_text: to watch carefully for someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: eye;eyes;keep your eyes peeled (for sb/sth);keep your eyes peeled for sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep your eyes peeled, he should be here any minute.; Ever since, I try to keep my eyes peeled for anything similar.

_source.base_text: in the blink of an eye
_source.definition_text: extremely quickly
_source.searchterms_text: eye;eyes;in the blink of an eye
_source.learnerexamples_text: In the blink of an eye, he was gone.; And for all those who keep nagging about losing their favourite regular programmes during such an event, be patient: TV routine will be back into your living rooms in the blink of an eye.

_source.definition_text: when people look at each other, for instance when they are talking to each other
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was very little eye contact between them.; I tried to avoid having eye contact with people just because of this humility.

_source.definition_text: to watch carefully for someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: eye;eyes;keep your eyes open (for sb/sth);keep your eyes open for sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep your eyes open for anything unusual.; It has helped us identify and successfully combat many a nutritional hazard, keeping our eyes open to immoderate consumption of some substances and its effects.

_source.definition_text: If something can be seen by the naked eye, it is big enough to be seen without special equipment.
_source.learnerexamples_text: These bugs are so tiny you cannot see them with the naked eye.

_source.definition_text: in your imagination or memory
_source.learnerexamples_text: In my mind's eye, she remains a little girl of six although she's actually a grown woman.; He sees her in his mind's eye, running around barefoot, laughing and squealing, wading in the water and running back out, screaming, trying to get away from the breaking waves.

_source.definition_text: the thin line of hair that is above each eye
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's got really bushy eyebrows.; He woke up and cleaned off the blood from his injured eyebrow.

_source.definition_text: to move your eyes so that they are looking up, usually to show surprise or disapproval
_source.learnerexamples_text: When I asked her when she thought the building work would be finished, she just rolled her eyes.; This attitude is obvious when, for instance, shop assistan[ts] show no patience for the slower reaction of elderl[y] [people]; when nobody offers a seat to an older person in [an] overcrowded tube; when we roll our eyes about older people's desire for quiet, etc.

_source.definition_text: one of the short hairs which grow from the edge of your eyelids
_source.learnerexamples_text: false/long eyelashes

_source.definition_text: the piece of skin that covers your eyes when you close them
_source.learnerexamples_text: His eyelids drooped with tiredness.

_source.definition_text: the ability to see
_source.learnerexamples_text: My eyesight is getting worse.; I had some trouble with my eyesight, so he advised me to wear glasses and not to strain my eyes.

_source.definition_text: the basic way in which a society or other social group is organized
_source.searchterms_text: fabric;fabric of sth;fabrics;the fabric of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: The family is part of the fabric of society. ; You cannot infringe individual liberties and ban the purchase of cars - it would go against the very fabric of modern society.

_source.definition_text: cloth
_source.learnerexamples_text: a light/woollen fabric ; Lifestyle-changing fashion Do small pieces of coloured fabric really have the might to change how people live their lives?

_source.definition_text: extremely good
_source.learnerexamples_text: They've got a fabulous house.; We had an absolutely fabulous holiday.; Everybody admitted that the entertainment was absolutely fabulous.

_source.definition_text: the front part of the head, where the eyes, nose and mouth are, or the expression on this part
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's got a long, thin face.; She had a worried expression on her face.;  She has got brown [e]yes, [a] round face and wh[ite] s[k]in.

_source.definition_text: If you accept something at face value because of the way it first looks or seems, you do so without thinking carefully about it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can't just accept everything you read in the newspapers at face value.; These results should not be taken at face value - careful analysis is required to assess their full implications.; People are assessed at face value [by] the type of cars they drive.

_source.definition_text: to show with your face that you do not like someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Joe made a face when he saw what was for lunch.; Making a face, I slapped my forehead.

_source.definition_text: to become less respected by others because of something you did
_source.learnerexamples_text: The party has lost face with the public by abandoning their original policy on education.; However, many popular people like Pierce Brosnan managed to keep their lives out of the press and yet be present to meet public demand without losing face.

_source.definition_text: to manage to stop yourself from smiling or laughing
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can never play jokes on people because I can't keep a straight face.

_source.definition_text: used when you are describing how a situation seems on the surface
_source.learnerexamples_text: On the face of it, it seems like a bargain, but I bet there are hidden costs.; On the face of it, both sides have valid arguments, and it's a difficult balancing act to manage.

_source.definition_text: while having to deal with a difficult situation or problem
_source.learnerexamples_text: She refused to leave him, in the face of increasing pressure from friends and family.; No doubt, it was rather difficult to like Enid X. She was hardly likely to arouse sympathy in anybody even in the face of death.

_source.definition_text: something someone does that insults or upsets you
_source.searchterms_text: a slap in the face;face;faces;slap in the face
_source.learnerexamples_text: After all that hard work, losing my job was a real slap in the face.; My father noticed that and decided it was high time to take me down a peg or two. He used to work as a volunteer in hospital for children dying for cancer. One day, he took me there. It was like a slap in the face - suddenly I saw a different world. It was a bleak world, without smiles and happy faces.

_source.definition_text: to be the opposite of what is usual or accepted
_source.learnerexamples_text: These recommendations fly in the face of previous advice on safe limits of consumption.; But when we have a look outside our wonderful world, we can easily see that this argument flies in the face of the facts.

_source.definition_text: If you face a problem, or a problem faces you, you have to deal with it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is one of the many problems faced by working mothers.; Passengers could face long delays.; You're faced with a very difficult choice there.; Grandparents are experienced people and they can help their child[ren] to avoid a lot of problems which they have faced.

_source.definition_text: to be or turn in a particular direction
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our house faces north/south/east/west.; She turned to face him.; The café faces (towards) the sea.; There is a desk [to] the right of the room which faces my bed.

_source.definition_text: to accept that something unpleasant is true and start to deal with the situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think Phil has to face the fact that she no longer loves him.; We have to face facts here - we simply don't have enough money.; He's dying but he refuses to face the truth.; But Mary has a strong personality, she faces the facts.

_source.definition_text: to not want to do something or deal with someone, often because it is difficult or unpleasant
_source.searchterms_text: can't face sb/sth/doing sth;can't face sb/sth/doing sth ;face;faced;faces;facing
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't face walking up all those steps again.; I knew someone had to tell her but I couldn't face it.; How can I face him now that he knows what I've done?; Everybody at [the] swimming pool was laughing about me. I couldn't face my family.

_source.definition_text: to accept punishment or criticism for something bad that you have done
_source.learnerexamples_text: At the end of the day I had to go home and face the music.; Teenagers who live with their parents have to face the music about the long bills their parents receive monthly!

_source.definition_text: something that you say before you say something that is unpleasant but true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's face it, none of us are getting any younger.; Let's face it, a life with [no] physical and mental exercise is something none of us relishes.

_source.definition_text: to accept that a difficult situation exists
_source.searchterms_text: face;face up to sth;face up to sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Eventually, he faced up to his money problems.; She has to face up to the fact that he's not coming back.; However, she had to face up to the fact that it was her duty to question the serial killer, to find out what his motives were.

_source.definition_text: directly, meeting someone in the same place
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to talk face to face.; I need to talk to her face to face.

_source.definition_text: of or on the face
_source.learnerexamples_text: facial expressions/hair ; I can still recall the doctor's facial expression when he announced the exciting news [to me].

_source.definition_text: involving two people who are meeting in the same place
_source.learnerexamples_text: a face-to-face meeting

_source.definition_text: to make something possible or easier
_source.learnerexamples_text: I will do everything in my power to facilitate the process.; I found that the presentations and talks about CVs and letters of application were really useful, [but] we should have been divided into smaller groups to facilitate conversation.

_source.definition_text: the buildings, equipment and services provided for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: childcare facilities;  sports facilities; The city has more facilities than the countryside.

_source.definition_text: something that you know is true, exists, or has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't know all the facts about what happened.; I'm not angry that you took my car - it's just the fact that you didn't ask me first.; I knew for a fact that she was lying.; I love this book, because it's about history facts and it['s] very interestin[g].

_source.definition_text: a part of a system or machine which makes it possible to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: an overdraft facility; I would suggest free Internet access as an extra facility in our library.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize what is really true, or to give more information
_source.learnerexamples_text: We met Rebecca for lunch. In fact, we spent the whole afternoon with her.; I was told there were some tickets left but in fact they were sold out.; The club has its own small clubhouse, with many things in it. For example, there was a big pinball-game and some computers. In fact it was the best clubhouse I've ever seen.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a situation which is surprising in relation to something that is true or happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company has been forced to reduce its price, despite the fact that the offer has been very popular.; The advantages of the kind of life that people ha[d] years ago is that they could eat more fruit and vegetables than us. However, there are advantages for us too, because despite the fact that we eat more fast food, we do more exercise than they [did].

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize what is really true, or to give more information
_source.learnerexamples_text: I thought she was Portuguese, but in actual fact she's Brazilian.; Nowadays almost all people own a car and in actual fact more and more people have been facing death as a consequence of careless driving.

_source.definition_text: real events and experiences, not things that are imagined
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's sometimes hard to separate fact from fiction.

_source.definition_text: used to give more information, or to correct something that has been said
_source.learnerexamples_text: John plays golf professionally. As a matter of fact, he has just won a big competition.; "So you're from Cambridge?" "No, as a matter of fact, I'm from Bristol."; I think it would be better to choose somewhere outdoors. As a matter of fact, I prefer the open air and the sunlight!

_source.definition_text: used to tell someone that something is the truth
_source.searchterms_text: fact;fact (of the matter) is;facts;the fact (of the matter) is;the fact of the matter is
_source.learnerexamples_text: I wouldn't usually ask for your help, but the fact is I'm desperate.; You may find [it] unusual for a woman to play football, but the fact is I'm Brazilian and in Brazil [it] is really common.

_source.definition_text: the thing that helps to make the final decision
_source.learnerexamples_text: Cost was the deciding factor in choosing these builders.; Personally, I think the quality of teachers, school reputation and facilities should be the deciding factor for parents [for] which schools their children should be educated in.

_source.definition_text: one of the things that has an effect on a situation, decision, event, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Money was an important factor in their decision to move.; Price is an important/key/major factor in the success of any product.;  economic factors; [Modern technology] is another important factor which affects our life.

_source.definition_text: a building or set of buildings where large amounts of goods are made using machines
_source.learnerexamples_text: a car/shoe factory; He works in a paint factory.; a factory worker/manager ; My friend Martin works at a factory.

_source.definition_text: a particular department at a college or university, or the teachers in that department
_source.searchterms_text: english/law/science, etc. faculty;faculties;faculty;the english/law/science etc faculty;the english/law/science, etc. faculty
_source.learnerexamples_text: He works in the law faculty.; I graduated from Warsaw University, where I studied [in] the faculties of applied linguistics and journalism.

_source.definition_text: to become less bright, strong or clear, or to make something become less bright, strong or clear
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you hang your clothes out in the bright sun, they will fade.; My suntan is already fading.; They arrived home just as the light was fading.; The music began to fade.; The sun had faded the blue walls.

_source.definition_text: to gradually become less strong or clear and then disappear
_source.learnerexamples_text: With time, memories of that painful summer would fade away.; These memories would never fade away, she knew it.

_source.definition_text: to not pass a test or exam
_source.learnerexamples_text: A lot of people fail their driving test the first time.; If she doesn't work she'll fail all her exams.; "How was your chemistry exam?" "Awful! I think I've failed."; I was told most people fail the exam two or three times.

_source.definition_text: to not be successful
_source.learnerexamples_text: She moved to London in the hope of finding work as a model, but failed.; He failed in his attempt to break the record.; This method of growing tomatoes never fails.; I tried to make him give up, but all my attempts failed.

_source.definition_text: to not do what is necessary or expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: He failed to turn up for football practice yesterday.; He failed to mention that we wouldn't be paid for the work.; Your advertisement also failed to mention the fact that there w[ere] no discounts.

_source.definition_text: to stop working normally, or to become weaker
_source.learnerexamples_text: Two of the plane's engines had failed.; The sound system failed.

_source.definition_text: used to say that you do not accept something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I fail to see why you cannot work on a Sunday.; I fail to understand why they still refuse to use this media; it could possibly be the main solution to the present problems [in] the library.

_source.definition_text: when you do not do something that you are expected to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: Failure to pay within 14 days will result in interest being charged.; It was his failure to return her phone call that told her that something was wrong.

_source.definition_text: when someone or something does not succeed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their attempt to climb Everest ended in failure.; I'm a bit of a failure at making cakes.; I feel such a failure.; David told her that the reason [for] his failure was her, because she used to press him and she couldn't accept that he wanted to be an actor.

_source.definition_text: when something does not work, or stops working as well as it should
_source.learnerexamples_text: All trains were delayed due to a power failure.; He died of heart/liver failure.; [There] has been a power failure but it will be solved in [a] few minutes.

_source.definition_text: slight and not easy to notice, smell, hear, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a faint sound/noise/smell ; She gave me a faint smile.; I heard a faint sound.

_source.definition_text: to feel very weak and as if you might fall down
_source.learnerexamples_text: Seeing all the blood made me feel faint.; Starting to feel faint, Fred quickly roused himself and ran out of the hotel as quickly as he could.

_source.definition_text: to suddenly become unconscious for a short time, usually falling down
_source.learnerexamples_text: He faints at the sight of blood.; I nearly fainted in the heat.; The young girl was about to faint.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that you do not know something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I haven't the faintest idea what you're talking about.; Some twenty years ago, when I left my parents' home to go and live on my own, I was [given] four mugs. By whom? I haven't the faintest idea.

_source.definition_text: having pale skin or a light colour of hair
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's got fair hair and blue eyes.; He's fair-haired.; She is a pretty girl with long fair hair and she has beautiful eyes.

_source.definition_text: treating everyone in the same way, so that no one has an advantage
_source.learnerexamples_text: That's not fair! You always go first!; It's not fair to make me do all the work.; a fair trial; I can't spend all my time with one child - it wouldn't be fair on the others.; Even though she thought her m[u]m wasn't being fair, she decided to go and try to have a nice day with her family.

_source.definition_text: used for saying that you can understand and accept someone's opinion or decision
_source.learnerexamples_text: "He says he'll only work on Sunday if he gets paid extra." "Fair enough."; Most of the streets are open [to] cars and therefore people tend to escape to a little area around the pedestrian streets. Fair enough, but it make[s] those streets terribly overcrowded.

_source.definition_text: acceptable, reasonable or right
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fair deal ; He offered a fair price for the car.; That's a fair comment/question.; You may ask yourself: "What do you do in a club?" Well, it's a fair question!!!

_source.definition_text: not very good but not very bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her German is very good, but her knowledge of French is only fair.; As for grammar, listening and writing skills, they were only fair.

_source.definition_text: quite a large amount, distance, size, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: a fair amount/distance/size etc;a fair amount/distance/size, etc.;fair;fair amount/distance/size, etc.;fairer;fairest
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's still a fair bit of work to be done on the house.; Of course it is important to find a job we enjoy and which leaves us a fair amount of free time, but it is equally important to find a job that pays the bills, especially nowadays.

_source.definition_text: behaviour that is fair, honest, and does not take advantage of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: The public needs to feel a sense of fair play from the government.; He still believes in justice or just the rule of fair play.

_source.definition_text: an event outside where you can ride large machines for pleasure and play games to win prizes
_source.learnerexamples_text: The children spent all their money on rides at the fair.; For example in the morning we can go to a fair, like Six Flags. I think that it will be exciting.

_source.definition_text: an event where people show and sell goods or services relating to a particular business or hobby
_source.learnerexamples_text: a trade fair; Starting on 18th May 2003, the Birmingham NEC hosted the annual British trade fair.

_source.definition_text: more than average, but less than very
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fairly big family; She's fairly tall.; We get on fairly well.; I saw her fairly recently.; The weather was fairly warm.

_source.definition_text: If you do something fairly, you do it in a way which is right and reasonable and treats people equally.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He claimed that he hadn't been treated fairly by his employers.; Officials will ensure that the election is carried out fairly.

_source.definition_text: when you treat everyone in the same way, so that no one has an advantage
_source.learnerexamples_text: He believes in fairness and decency.; I think you have not treated us with fairness and truthfulness and therefor[e] I do think that an apology in the newspaper would be in order.

_source.definition_text: great trust or confidence in something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has no faith in modern medicine.; You'll be fine - I have great faith in you.; After the trial, his family said they had lost all faith in the legal system.; We must do our best to help [these children] to have faith in their future.

_source.definition_text: strong belief in a god or gods
_source.learnerexamples_text: Even in the bad times she never lost her faith.; Her faith in God was shattered when her baby died.; It's my faith that keeps me going.; Your story about Christianity was very interesting and I was shocked at your deep faith in God.

_source.definition_text: a particular religion
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Muslim/Christian/Jewish faith; a multi-faith society; Everybody was praying, asking for help according to their faith or religion.

_source.definition_text: loyal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a faithful friend ; They are faithful supporters of the Labour Party.; His faithful old dog accompanied him everywhere he went.; An ideal pet should be a faithful friend [to] people, especially [to] its owner.

_source.definition_text: If your husband, wife, or partner is faithful, they do not have a sexual relationship with anyone else.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a faithful husband; They remained faithful to each other throughout their long marriage.; Making a commitment to be faithful to another, and to love a person for the rest of your life is no small thing.

_source.definition_text: not changing any of the original details, facts, style, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Does the film adaptation stay faithful to the novel?; Working with deconstruction in music, he remained faithful to his main motto: Be yourself, express yourself, never repeat or imitate.

_source.definition_text: used to end a formal letter to someone whose name you do not know
_source.learnerexamples_text: Yours faithfully, Katherine Smith; Yours faithfully, SAMSON LAM (READER)

_source.definition_text: not real, but made to look or seem real
_source.learnerexamples_text: fake fur; a fake passport; On the walls there are paintings which are very artistic - one of them is a fake Picasso.

_source.definition_text: a copy of something that is intended to look real or valuable and deceive people
_source.learnerexamples_text: Experts say that the painting is a fake.; Many of the pictures taken are fakes.

_source.definition_text: someone who pretends to have particular skills or qualities so that they can deceive people or get their admiration
_source.learnerexamples_text: He said he was a doctor, but we soon realized he was a fake.; So, after all he was a fake!

_source.definition_text: to copy something in order to deceive people
_source.learnerexamples_text: The documents had been faked.; People liked it so much that another author, using the [pseudonym] of "Arellaneda", faked Cervante's novel by writing a second part.

_source.definition_text: to pretend that something has happened when it has not or to pretend to have a feeling that you do not have
_source.learnerexamples_text: They faked illness to avoid having to work.; He said he was feeling sick, but he was just faking it.; This situation lasted about two years until Caroline had a great idea: they would fake their death and run away to live a quiet life on a secret island they would have bought under an alias.

_source.definition_text: to move down towards the ground, sometimes by accident
_source.learnerexamples_text: The path's very steep, so be careful you don't fall.; He fell badly and broke his leg.; I fell down the stairs and injured my back.; He fell to his death climbing the Matterhorn.; By winter, all the leaves had fallen off the trees.

_source.definition_text: to become lower in size, amount or strength
_source.learnerexamples_text: Demand for new cars has fallen recently.; The standard of his work has fallen during the year.; The temperature could fall below zero overnight.; Average temperatures fell by ten degrees.; The pound has fallen to its lowest-ever level against the dollar.

_source.definition_text: to start to sleep or become ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: I fell asleep on the sofa watching TV.; I planned to go with my cousin but unfortunately she fell ill, so I had to go with my friend.

_source.definition_text: to start to love someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was 20 when I first fell in love.; I fell in love with David.

_source.definition_text: If an event or joke falls flat, it fails to have the effect that you wanted, such as making people laugh.
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the jokes in his speech fell flat.; The cultural visits fell flat [in comparison] to their expectations, although the sightseeing tour of Willstown was, as the students said, "fascinating".

_source.definition_text: used to say that it is becoming dark
_source.learnerexamples_text: When darkness fell, I began to feel worried.; He greeted the worms and the slugs, and as darkness fell he retired to the shelter he had built for the night.

_source.definition_text: to be defeated and start to be controlled by a different leader
_source.learnerexamples_text: In 1453 the city fell to the Turks.

_source.definition_text: to become worse, or start to be in a bad situation or condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: Education standards are continuing to fall.; Empty for 30 years, the building had fallen into ruin.; This impressive, massive 18th-century building which accommodated the Town Hall until recently (5 years ago) has now fallen into disuse.

_source.definition_text: to hang down
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her long blonde hair fell softly over her shoulders.; She had gorgeous black hair falling down her back, a creamy complexion and a figure models dream of.

_source.definition_text: If advice or a request falls on deaf ears, people ignore it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our pleas for help fell on deaf ears.; His cry for help and for a more meaningful relationship between himself and Mildred invariably fell on deaf ears.

_source.definition_text: When events or details that you did not understand before fall into place, they become easy to understand.
