_source.learnerexamples_text: When Jo told me she had a twin sister, everything fell into place.

_source.definition_text: to be hurt or deceived by something or someone bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: He fell prey to a gang of criminals pretending to be council officials.; As young people do not have experience in living independently in society and are not fully aware of social problems such as drugs and violence, they may easily fall prey to adults who would like to exploit them.

_source.definition_text: to not reach a particular level, but only by a small amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sales for the first half of this year fell just short of the target.; Furthermore, it cannot be denied that public transport falls short of the target set during the planning process.

_source.definition_text: to break into pieces
_source.learnerexamples_text: My poor old boots are falling apart.; It looks like it [is] going to fall apart any day.

_source.definition_text: to fail to achieve something
_source.learnerexamples_text: His behaviour falls short of what we expect.; She just fell short of the grades she needed.; This routine was really wearing me out, but, I didn't want to fall short of my parents' expectations.

_source.definition_text: to use someone or something when other things have failed, or when there are no other choices
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've been saving up the past few years, to have something to fall back on.; Moreover, in an emergency, you can fall back on my neighbours.

_source.definition_text: to start having problems that you cannot deal with
_source.learnerexamples_text: The deal fell apart because of a lack of financing.; Their marriage fell apart when she found out about her husband's affair.; All her dreams and wishes fell apart.

_source.definition_text: to fall onto the ground
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our apple tree fell down in the storm.; He stumbled and fell down.; When I got up in the morning, I slip[ped] on a piece of soap and fell down.

_source.definition_text: to suddenly have strong romantic feelings about someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: She fell for a tall, handsome Frenchman when she was on holiday in Paris.; I saw a handsome boy [and] I fell for him.

_source.definition_text: to argue with someone and stop being friendly with them
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's fallen out with her sister.; They fell out over money.; My husband always blame[s] me and we fall out over my incapacity to cook.

_source.definition_text: If someone or something falls over, they fall to the ground or onto their side.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She tripped and fell over.; The fence fell over in the wind.; I nearly fell over because the corridor was very dark.

_source.definition_text: If a plan or agreement falls through, it fails to happen.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our plans to go on holiday together fell through when Jamie became ill.; All our plans fell through and I hope it will never happen to me again.

_source.definition_text: when the size, amount or strength of something gets lower
_source.learnerexamples_text: the recent fall in the price of petrol; a fall in the unemployment rate; We could hear the rise and fall of voices in the other room.; There is a fall in job vacancies.

_source.definition_text: when someone or something falls down to the ground, often without intending to or by accident
_source.learnerexamples_text: He had a nasty fall and hurt his back.; The boulder smashed several small trees during its fall.; I was terrified and I heard the noise of a fall just by my side.

_source.definition_text: when a city, government, leader, etc. loses power or control
_source.learnerexamples_text: the fall of communism; After the fall of the previous system everything changed.

_source.definition_text: not true or correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: a false name; false information; The rumour later turned out to be false.; You'll get a false impression/idea of the town if you only visit the university.; I must say that the advertisement for the show included a lot of false information.

_source.definition_text: not real, but made to look or seem real
_source.learnerexamples_text: false eyelashes/teeth ; false documents; Asking what made her do so she answered that she had forgotten her false teeth, without which she couldn't have faced the fire-brigade.

_source.definition_text: not sincere or expressing real emotions
_source.learnerexamples_text: false promises; I hate the way he smiles at everyone. It's so false.; The actor is really getting on my nerves because he is so selfish and so false.

_source.definition_text: easy to recognize because of being seen, met, heard, etc. before
_source.learnerexamples_text: There were one or two familiar faces.; The house looked strangely familiar, though she knew she'd never been there before.; The street was familiar to me.; Someone started to wave and then I saw a familiar face.

_source.definition_text: when you are known by many people because of your achievements, skills, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She first rose to fame as a singer at the age of 16.; She moved to London in search of fame and fortune.; It is certain that these people have fame, fortune and success, and that many of them are very rich.

_source.definition_text: to know something or someone well
_source.searchterms_text: be familiar with sth/sb;be familiar with sth/sb ;familiar
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry, I'm not familiar with your poetry.; I'm familiar with many kinds of sports activities such as ball games, recreation games, swimming and Japanese budo-karate, judo etc.

_source.definition_text: to teach someone more about something new, or try to understand more about it yourself
_source.learnerexamples_text: We spent a few minutes familiarizing ourselves with the day's schedule.; The presenter should be acting as a teenager in order to familiarise the youth of the area with the programme immediately.

_source.definition_text: a group of people who are related to each other, such as a mother, a father, and their children
_source.learnerexamples_text: A new family has/have moved in next door.; I come from a large family - I have three brothers and two sisters.; He hasn't any family.; He's American but his family come/comes from Ireland.; This film is good family entertainment.

_source.definition_text: the children of a family
_source.learnerexamples_text: Single parents have to raise a family on their own.; Paul and Alison are hoping to start a family soon.; Some people also want to [have] a family because they want to be a father or a mother.

_source.definition_text: when people living in a particular area do not have enough food for a long time causing suffering and death
_source.learnerexamples_text: The floods were followed by a terrible famine.; Pictures of the famine in Africa or the defor[e]station of the Amazon raise important issues for humanity as a whole, urging us to be more active citizens.

_source.definition_text: known and recognized by many people
_source.learnerexamples_text: a famous actor ; New York is a city famous for its theaters and nightlife.; It is the most famous place in Edinburgh.

_source.definition_text: someone who admires and supports a person, sport, sports team, etc.
_source.l_topic_text_text: arts and media, people: personality, shopping
_source.learnerexamples_text: More than 15,000 Liverpool fans attended Saturday's game.; He's a big fan of country music.; I'm a fan of rock music.

_source.definition_text: something that is used to move the air around so that it feels cooler, such as a machine or an object that you move with your hand
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was no air conditioning, just a ceiling fan turning slowly.; Since it's quite hot here I brought a fan. I have to use it at night otherwise I can't get to sleep.

_source.definition_text: someone whose interest in something or enthusiasm for something is extreme
_source.learnerexamples_text: a religious fanatic; fitness/exercise fanatics; This can give way to fanatics, religious or politic[al], who may easily influence the frustrated masses into doing something they would under other circumstances refrain from.

_source.definition_text: to want to have or do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you fancy a drink this evening?; I didn't fancy swimming in that water.; Do you fancy eating at the restaurant together?

_source.definition_text: to feel sexually attracted to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: I fancied him the first time I saw him.; He had 3 very nice boys and everybody in my class knew that I fancied his youngest son Nicolai.

_source.definition_text: used at the beginning of a sentence to show that you are surprised or shocked by something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fancy seeing you here!; Fancy meeting a man who looked like an ancient knight!

_source.definition_text: extremely good
_source.learnerexamples_text: You look fantastic in that dress.; We had a fantastic time.; They've won a holiday? How fantastic!; The beaches here are fantastic!

_source.definition_text: extremely
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're fantastically rich.; They're doing fantastically well.; We spent three fantastically romantic days later.

_source.definition_text: at, to or from a great distance in space or time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is the station far away?; She doesn't live far from here.; How far away does your mother live?; How far is it from Australia to New Zealand?; Bournemouth is not far from Poole.

_source.definition_text: a situation or event that you imagine, which is not real or true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Steve's favourite fantasy was to own a big house and a flashy car.;  sexual fantasies; She retreated into  a fantasy world, where she could be anything she wanted.; Reading a book stimulates one's fantasy and imagination.

_source.definition_text: until now
_source.learnerexamples_text: So far we've made thirty-two thousand pounds.; So far I like it here very much.

_source.definition_text: used to say that you think something is true, but cannot be sure
_source.learnerexamples_text: As far as I know, he's never been in trouble with the police.; As far as I know, accommodation at Camp California is in tents or log cabins.

_source.definition_text: very much
_source.learnerexamples_text: This car is far better than our old one.; It cost far more (money) than I could afford.; He loses his temper far too often.; I'd far rather/sooner go to the theatre than watch a DVD.; I think restaurant B is far better than restaurant A.

_source.base_text: as far as sb is concerned
_source.definition_text: used to say what someone's opinion is
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's all over as far as I'm concerned.; As far as I am concerned, Bernard is similar to him.

_source.base_text: as far as sth is concerned
_source.definition_text: used to say what you are talking about
_source.learnerexamples_text: As far as sport is concerned, I like tennis and football.; As far as studying abroad is concerned, I totally agree with this idea.

_source.definition_text: by a great amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are by far the best students in the class.; I have travelled to many countries, but New Zealand is by far the best.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something has gone well until now
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's the first time I've done any decorating, but so far so good.; So far so good, only no one told us they held this point of view before the actual christening took place.

_source.definition_text: certainly not something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The situation is far from clear.; The quality of catering was far from ideal as well, as a meal in a hamburger restaurant can hardly be called a typical English lunch.

_source.definition_text: used to tell someone that something is certainly not true
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's not handsome - far from it.; The Hotel Royal cannot be considered as being luxury - far from it - i.e. our rooms were dirty and situated [o]n the 4th floor without a lift.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about how true something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: How far do politicians represent the views of ordinary people?; How far and to what extent would the characteristics we are born with influence our future development in life?

_source.base_text: go so far as to do sth
_source.definition_text: to take the extreme action of doing something
_source.searchterms_text: far;farther;farthest;further;furthest;go so far as to do sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He even went so far as to stop her using the telephone.; Our present course of action may go so far as to cause irrevers[i]ble damage not only to our planet but also to the people living upon [it].

_source.definition_text: certainly not doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Far from being pleased, he was embarrassed by the praise.; Far from asking you to close the airport, which would be quite an irrational request, I am suggesting that you should take some action to improve the situation.

_source.definition_text: to behave in a way that upsets or annoys other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's said some stupid things in the past, but this time he's gone too far.; Lucia let her speak and calmly said: "You really have gone too far this time."

_source.definition_text: not happening or existing very often
_source.learnerexamples_text: Opportunities like this are few and far between.; Jobs in those days were few and far between and for a number of years he was alternating between temporary jobs and unemployment benefit.

_source.definition_text: to be very different from something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The princess's world was far removed from reality.; It is the same problem with planned excursions to street markets in Asia, souks in Arabia or even tribes that are far removed from industrialized life in Papua New Guinea or the rainforest of Brazil.

_source.definition_text: describes the part of something that is most distant from the centre or from you
_source.learnerexamples_text: His office is at the far end of the corridor.; The children ran to the far side/corner of the room.; The dark spot at the far end of the wall seemed to be coming after her this time.

_source.base_text: be a far cry from sth
_source.definition_text: to be very different from something
_source.searchterms_text: be a far cry from sth;far;farther;farthest;further;furthest
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her luxury mansion is a far cry from the house she grew up in.; The museum was a far cry from what we expected. Not only were the machines really old and should have been replaced a long time ago, but they were boring as well.

_source.definition_text: a long distance away
_source.learnerexamples_text: faraway places; They trans[port] me to faraway places and to a magic world.

_source.definition_text: used to describe political groups whose opinions are very extreme
_source.learnerexamples_text: He belongs to a far right group.

_source.definition_text: an expression on someone's face that shows that they are not thinking about what is happening around them
_source.learnerexamples_text: He had a faraway look in his eyes.; But her most noticeable feature[s] are her large [brown] eyes and her happy smile. Yet, sometimes you could see a faraway look in her eyes.

_source.definition_text: the money that you pay for a journey on a vehicle such as a bus or train
_source.learnerexamples_text: Air/Bus/Train fares are going up again.; In fact, there are buses (number 843 and 845) which go [to] my village but the bus fare is very expensive for me.

_source.definition_text: an area of land with fields and buildings, used for growing crops and/or keeping animals as a business
_source.learnerexamples_text: farm animals ; It's very important because I'm going to a farm this weekend and there's nothing to do.

_source.definition_text: someone who owns or looks after a farm
_source.learnerexamples_text: a sheep farmer; The farmer was very friendly and we [spent] the day with him.

_source.definition_text: the activity of working on a farm or organizing the work there
_source.learnerexamples_text: modern farming practices; I am interested in farming and hope to own a farm one day.

_source.definition_text: to interest someone a lot
_source.learnerexamples_text: Science has always fascinated me.; What fascinates me about it is that this style of music allows the artist to bring in crazy new ideas such as African or Indian rhythms.

_source.definition_text: extremely interested
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were fascinated by his stories. ; I am sure you will be fascinated by his work and his multi-faceted character.

_source.definition_text: extremely interesting
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fascinating person/place ; I found the movie fascinating.; You can enjoy not only Hungarian food but also fascinating Hungarian music.

_source.definition_text: when you find someone or something fascinating
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her fascination with fashion started at an early age.; Anyhow, even if you can't grasp the deep meaning behind [the] words, its beautiful rhyme and r[h]ythm will exert a fascination on you.

_source.definition_text: a style that is popular at a particular time, especially in clothes, hair, make-up, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Long hair is back in fashion for men.; Fur coats have gone out of fashion.; She always wears the latest fashions.; I like this present because I love clothes and fashion.

_source.definition_text: making and selling clothes
_source.learnerexamples_text: the fashion industry ; fashion magazines ; When I'm tired, I like reading fashion magazines.

_source.definition_text: popular at a particular time
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fashionable nightclub/restaurant ; fashionable clothes ;  It's no longer fashionable to smoke.; There are some fashionable cafes, restaurants and museums.

_source.definition_text: moving or happening quickly, or able to move or happen quickly
_source.learnerexamples_text: fast cars ; a fast swimmer; Computers are getting faster all the time.; The fast train to London takes less than an hour.; I like fast music very much.

_source.definition_text: a very quick way of achieving or dealing with something
_source.searchterms_text: a fast track (to sth);a fast track to sth;fast;fast track (to sth);faster;fastest
_source.learnerexamples_text: These intensive courses claim to offer a fast track to wealth and success.; If I ever found a job which lives up to these expectations, I would consider myself on [a] fast track already.

_source.definition_text: moving or happening quickly
_source.learnerexamples_text: We ran as fast as we could.; The accident was caused by people driving too fast in bad conditions.; I rode my bike home as fast as I could.

_source.definition_text: in a firm or tight way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He tried to get away, but she held him fast.; Thankfully, there are those who still cling to such age-old values as personal contentment and growth, regarding them as the anchors which hold happiness fast.

_source.definition_text: completely asleep
_source.learnerexamples_text: I looked into her room but she was still fast asleep.; Karen's grandson walks into the room to find her fast asleep on her favourite chair.

_source.definition_text: the busy and exciting way of life that a successful person has
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fed up with life in the fast lane, Jack gave up his job and moved to the countryside.; Finally, should you ask why people are not happier than before, the answer is that nowadays they spend more hours on work than before, because modern life is mostly a life in the fast lane.

_source.definition_text: quickly and in large numbers
_source.learnerexamples_text: Calls were coming in thick and fast by the end of the programme.

_source.definition_text: to close or fix something together, or to become closed or fixed together
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fasten your seat belt.; This shirt fastens at the back.; She fell fast asleep and only woke to the sound of the announcement: "Ladies and gent[le]men fasten your seat belts [-] in a couple of minutes we will be landing in Kingston".

_source.definition_text: to fix one thing to another
_source.searchterms_text: fasten;fasten sth on/to/together etc;fasten sth on/to/together, etc.;fastened;fastening;fastens
_source.learnerexamples_text: He fastened the rope to a tree.

_source.definition_text: hot food that can be served very quickly because it is already prepared
_source.learnerexamples_text: fast food restaurants; We don't eat lots of fast food, us[ual]ly I cook every day.

_source.definition_text: Someone who is fat weighs too much.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He eats all the time but he never gets fat.; She is tall and [a] little b[i]t fat.

_source.definition_text: a solid or liquid substance that is taken from animals or plants and used in cooking
_source.learnerexamples_text: This product contains no animal fat.; I only use vegetable fats in cooking.; They should also consum[e] as much salad as they can, due to the fact that it does not contain fat.

_source.definition_text: A fatal illness or accident causes death.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This illness is fatal in almost all cases.; the fatal shooting of an unarmed 15-year-old; Paul received a fatal shot in [the] head.

_source.definition_text: Fatal actions have very bad effects.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He made the fatal mistake/error of believing what they told him.; That was a fatal mistake because that [person] was my teacher and he wasn't so pleased about my behaviour.

_source.definition_text: what happens to someone, especially something bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: We want to decide our own fate.; His fate is now in the hands of the jury.; No one as powerless as him deserves this fate.

_source.definition_text: a power that some people believe decides what will happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: When we met again by chance in Cairo, I felt it must be fate.; Fate has brought us together.; But, little we did know what fate had in store for us.

_source.definition_text: your male parent
_source.learnerexamples_text: My father took me to watch the football every Saturday.; I got it from my father and mother.

_source.definition_text: the father of your husband or wife
_source.learnerexamples_text: My father-in-law was a banker. ; My father-in-law, I'm pretty sure, [will] be able to answer all your questions.

_source.definition_text: Fatty foods contain a lot of fat.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Try to cut down on eating fatty foods.; There is a greater reliance on fast food and fatty foods.

_source.definition_text: If something bad that has happened is someone's fault, they are responsible for it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She believes it was the doctor's fault that Peter died.; It's not my fault she didn't come!; "It's my fault" I said and he answered "Never mind, it's all ok".

_source.definition_text: responsible for something bad that has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was at fault and I would like to apologize.; I really felt at fault.

_source.definition_text: something that is wrong with something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car has a serious design fault.; They think the fire was caused by an electrical fault.; I went out of the house and I saw that the other houses had not got any lights, so it was not an electrical fault.

_source.definition_text: something that is wrong with someone's character
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has many faults, but dishonesty isn't one of them.; He had a fault: he talked a lot.

_source.definition_text: to criticize someone or something, especially without good reasons
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was always finding fault with our work.; Sometimes I take offence at their trying to find fault with me and I am not allowed to answer back.

_source.definition_text: perfect, or without any mistakes
_source.learnerexamples_text: a faultless performance; Children also need to be taught that parents are not faultless and the best way to teach a child to apologise is by doing it oneself after having treated the child [unfairly].

_source.definition_text: not working correctly or not in perfect condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: faulty brakes/goods ; Big supermarkets always [give] you a complete refund if an item is of poor quality or faulty.

_source.definition_text: something that you do to help someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: She rang up to ask me a favour.; Could you do me a favour - could you give this to Sean, please?; Could you do me a favour?

_source.definition_text: to agree with or approve of a plan or idea
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most people are in favour of reducing traffic in cities.; I am certainly in favour of h[o]lding the music festival next year.

_source.definition_text: If you refuse or get rid of someone or something in favour of someone or something else, you choose them instead.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They dropped him from the team in favour of a much younger player.; The city council should revise the airport project [... and] change the current location of the airport in favour of a more isolated area.

_source.definition_text: If something is in your favour, it helps you to win or succeed.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Both sides have strong arguments in their favour.; Unfortunately the weather conditions were not in our favour, but the rain only lasted a few minutes and did not look at all like a downpour.

_source.definition_text: to choose or prefer one possibility
_source.learnerexamples_text: These are the running shoes favoured by marathon runners.; This development probably would not be really favoured by individuals either, as most people use their own car to do the shopping mostly and just to go on their daily business.

_source.definition_text: showing that you like or approve of someone or something, or making you support or approve of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She made a very favourable impression on us.; It is the first thing people see from our village and if their first impression is favourable, they will feel like going further into the village.

_source.definition_text: making something more likely to be successful
_source.learnerexamples_text: We had favourable weather conditions for the sailing competition. ; As far as bringing up my own children is concerned, I would like to follow my mother in the above-mentioned aspects (I feel I had a rare opportunity to be raised in extremely favourable conditions).

_source.definition_text: best liked or most enjoyed
_source.learnerexamples_text: "What's your favourite colour?" "Green."; My favourite food is pasta.; my favourite band/book/film ; My favourite food is rice and curry.

_source.definition_text: a thing that someone likes best or enjoys most
_source.learnerexamples_text: How clever of you to buy chocolate chip cookies - they're my favourites.; We are going to see a thriller film, they are my favourites.

_source.definition_text: the person, animal or thing that is most likely to win a competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Dallas Cowboys are now favourites to win.; Her novel was the favourite to win the prize, but the judges chose differently.

_source.definition_text: to send a document using a fax machine
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fax me your reply/Fax your reply to me.; I will ask one of my classmate[s] to fax me the work you [set], and I will try to do it.

_source.definition_text: a strong, unpleasant feeling that you get when you think that something bad, dangerous, or frightening might happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: her fear of snakes;  Shaking/Trembling with fear, she handed over the money to the gunman.; There are fears that the disease will spread to other countries.; Fears for her safety are growing.; The low profit figures simply confirmed my worst fears.

_source.definition_text: because you are worried about something/doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I didn't want to move for fear of waking her up.; No one dared to turn around for fear of being bitterly disappointed.

_source.definition_text: to be worried or frightened that something bad might happen or might have happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: Police fear (that) the couple may have drowned.;  It is feared (that) as many as two hundred passengers may have died in the crash.; Lots of changes which may occur during these next fifty years [might] make us fear that our sons' and grandsons' lives will not be as happy as ours.

_source.definition_text: to be frightened of something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most older employees fear unemployment.; What do you fear most?; I've always feared the dark.

_source.definition_text: to worry that something very bad will happen or that something very bad has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: When there was no sign of the children, the rescuers feared the worst.; Her parents had been quar[re]lling constantly now for almost half [a] year, and she feared the worst.

_source.definition_text: frightened or worried
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many women are fearful of travelling alone. ; My mother is a very fearful person and when I was playing with other children in the sea I could not stand [it] when she interrupted our game all the time with the same words: "Do not do that and do not do this, it is to[o] dangerous."

_source.definition_text: not frightened of anything
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fearless fighter; It is something which associates [i]n my mind with extreme, fearless guys who tend to live on the edge of life, always searching for new strong feelings and a 'dose of adrenaline'.

_source.definition_text: possible to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: a feasible plan; It may be feasible to clone human beings, but is it ethical?; In the context of Singapore, where land is scarce and [the] widening or building of more roads is just not feasible, we have no choice but to choose what is best for everyone.

_source.definition_text: a large meal, especially to celebrate something special
_source.learnerexamples_text: a wedding feast; Finally, they have a feast with a lot of food and wine.

_source.definition_text: to eat a lot of food and enjoy it very much
_source.learnerexamples_text: We feasted on fried chicken, ice cream, and chocolate cake.; Some people think that travelling entails feasting on typical food and buying lots of clothes.

_source.definition_text: an act or achievement that shows great skill or strength
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Eiffel Tower is a remarkable feat of engineering.; It can be argued that, on this level, sport is close to becoming a form of art but it is undoubtedly a feat of strength just to have qualified [in] an event of this kind.

_source.definition_text: used when you want to emphasize that an act or achievement is very difficult
_source.learnerexamples_text: Learning to ski at 60 is no mean feat!; There was an interesting discussion about whether it was harder or easier for them to enter the world of cinema, given their famous names. Both said that it was no mean feat because people were more demanding as [to] their abilities.

_source.definition_text: one of the soft, light things that grow from and cover a bird's skin
_source.learnerexamples_text: I found a peacock's feather. ; Birds were cleaning their feathers [and singing] morning songs, monkeys were jumping [at] the top of an old tree in the corner of the mon[aste]ry yard.

_source.definition_text: a typical quality, or an important part of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The town's main features are its beautiful mosque and ancient marketplace.; Our latest model of phone has several new features.; He explained the features of the new product to the rest of his colleagues.

_source.definition_text: Someone's features are the parts of their face that you notice when you look at them.
_source.learnerexamples_text: His eyes are his best feature.; They have similar figures, [and] the features of their faces are nearly the same.

_source.definition_text: a special article in a newspaper or magazine, or a special television programme
_source.learnerexamples_text: a double-page feature on global warming; As a regular reader of the student magazine 'Uni', I read with particular interest last week's feature on political thrillers.

_source.definition_text: to include someone or something as an important part
_source.learnerexamples_text: The film features James Dean as a disaffected teenager.; This week's broadcast features a report on victims of domestic violence.; My favourite song is "Candy Shop", by 50 Cent, featuring Olivia.

_source.definition_text: the second month of the year, after January and before March
_source.learnerexamples_text: 28(th) February/February 28(th); I was born on the fifth of February/February the fifth.; We moved house last February.; We are moving house next February.; Building work is expected to start in February.

_source.definition_text: annoyed or bored by something that you have experienced for too long
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm fed up with my job.; He got fed up with all the travelling he had to do.; I'm sure that the whole world is fed up with Mozart.

_source.definition_text: an amount of money that you pay to do something, to use something, or to get a service
_source.learnerexamples_text: university/college fees; an entrance/registration fee; Due to the fact that the centre is new and very big, the fee is quite high, about a hundred euros for three months.

_source.definition_text: extremely weak
_source.learnerexamples_text: She became too feeble to get out of bed.; Most of the times, the owner is a decrepit and feeble old man, who can hardly hear you, but who can be a magnificent narrator.

_source.definition_text: to give food to a person, group or animal
_source.learnerexamples_text: I usually feed the neighbour's cat while she's away.; Let's feed the kids first and have our dinner after.; If you feed your dog on cakes and biscuits, it's not surprising he's so fat.; You can also ride horses and feed animals like rabbits, birds and hamsters.

_source.definition_text: not very good or effective
_source.learnerexamples_text: a feeble argument/excuse; Some of the passengers began to pray under their breath, in a feeble attempt to suppress their panic.

_source.definition_text: to supply something such as information to a person or a machine, especially in a regular or continuous way
_source.learnerexamples_text: We fed them false information about our plans.; Nicola fed the pages into the photocopier.; For heaven's sake, the strike lasted for three weeks not three years. [...] They feed you with lies.

_source.definition_text: If an animal or a baby feeds, it eats.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The caterpillars feed on cabbage leaves.; In the same way, animals killed plants and fed on them.

_source.definition_text: information or opinions about something, such as a new product, that provide an idea of whether it is successful or liked
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you had any feedback from customers about the product?;  positive/negative feedback; I am writing to you to give you feedback about [the] social programme.

_source.definition_text: to experience something physical or emotional
_source.learnerexamples_text: "How are you feeling?" "Not too bad, but I've still got a headache."; My eyes feel really sore.; I'm feeling really happy today!; I feel embarrassed about making so many mistakes.; I like Prague, because it is place where I feel good.

_source.definition_text: to have a feeling or idea about something that you have experienced even though it is not true
_source.learnerexamples_text: I feel as if I've known you for ages.; It feels like I've been here forever and yet it's only been three months.; I feel like I've been here for ages.

_source.definition_text: to have a wish for something, or to want to do something, at a particular moment
_source.searchterms_text: feel;feel like sth/doing sth;feel like sth/doing sth ;feeling;feels;felt
_source.learnerexamples_text: I feel like going for a swim.; I feel like a nice cool glass of lemonade.; "Are you coming to aerobics?" "No, I don't feel like it today."; He was so rude I felt like hitting him.; The weather is warm and I feel like swimming.

_source.definition_text: to seem to be similar to a type of person, thing, or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: My feet feel like blocks of ice.; I felt like a fool when I saw what everyone else was wearing.; In front of these big towers, I feel like a tiny insect!

_source.definition_text: to think something or have an opinion
_source.learnerexamples_text: I feel (that) I should be doing more to help her.; Do you feel very strongly about this?; I feel certain I'm right.; The more he got close to this man, the more he felt sure it was Chris, who died in a car crash in April 1972.

_source.definition_text: to feel sympathy for someone because they are in a difficult situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: I feel so sorry for the children - it must be really hard for them.; Anyway, I feel sorry for her and I wonder: what would I do if I were her?

_source.definition_text: to touch something, especially with your hands, in order to examine it
_source.learnerexamples_text: I felt his head and it was hot.; Just feel how cold my hands are!; I was feeling around in my bag for the keys.; I tried to open the heavy door; I could feel the iron bar with my almost frozen fingers.

_source.definition_text: to feel happy and confident in a place or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: After a month she felt at home in her new job.; I explained: "I was in Manchester for just 10 month[s] and [during] that time the people from there made me feel at home [so] I feel proud to have the accent."

_source.definition_text: If a place, situation, etc., feels different, strange, etc., that is how it seems to you, or that describes your experience of it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It felt strange to see him again after so long.; The house feels empty without the children.; It felt strange and yet so wonderful to ski in the summer!

_source.definition_text: to be aware of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I could feel them watching me.; I could feel the silence.

_source.definition_text: to feel that you should do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He felt compelled to resign from his job.; As a member of the International Student's Sports Club, I felt compelled to write this article in answer to the previous article about how today's youth is putting sports and healthy activities aside.

_source.definition_text: to feel very weak and as if you might fall down
_source.learnerexamples_text: Seeing all the blood made me feel faint.; Starting to feel faint, Fred quickly roused himself and ran out of the hotel as quickly as he could.

_source.definition_text: emotion
_source.learnerexamples_text: a feeling of joy/sadness ; The feeling of loneliness was suddenly too much for him.; Her performance seemed to me completely lacking in feeling.; When I'm walking alone I can think about all my feelings, combine them into one and the name of this feeling is love.

_source.definition_text: an idea that something is true or exists
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had the strange feeling that we had met before.; I got the feeling that she was unhappy with the arrangement.; When I saw the policeman['s] face I got a bad feeling about this man. He d[id]n't look like a cop but he was [dressed] like one, so I decide[d] to stay away from this guy.

_source.definition_text: Your feelings are your beliefs and emotions, especially those influenced by other people.
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can't hide your feelings from me.; I didn't want to hurt his feelings, so I didn't tell him what she'd said about him.; I can't explain my feelings.

_source.definition_text: when you feel something physical
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got this odd feeling in my stomach.; My toes were so cold that I'd lost all feeling in them.; After one hour I was home and still had the feeling of warm rain touching my skin.

_source.definition_text: an opinion or belief
_source.learnerexamples_text: My feeling is that we had better act quickly or it will be too late.; My feeling is that we shou[l]d simply buy what we want to buy [and] not what we are prompted to buy.

_source.definition_text: when people are upset or angry with each other
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't want to cause any bad feeling between us.; For those who can't afford to shop, this might cause them to envy and harbo[u]r ill feeling [towards] those they can see are enjoying and splurging.

_source.definition_text: describes someone who has the same job or interests as you, or is in the same situation as you
_source.learnerexamples_text: She introduced me to some of her fellow students.; Our fellow travellers were mostly Spanish-speaking tourists.; In conclusion, I have to declare that [I] myself and my fellow students will be available to help [with] this short video.

_source.definition_text: belonging or relating to women, or to the sex that can produce eggs or have babies
_source.learnerexamples_text: a female athlete/employee; female cats/elephants; She was voted the best female vocalist.; All my female friends at school say that he is [an] attractive young man.

_source.definition_text: a female animal or person
_source.learnerexamples_text: The kitten was actually a female, not a male.; Females represent 40% of the country's workforce.; We all know the problems that [are] cause[d] [by] having animals kept in a zoo: females refuse the males, or they become mad [from] the lack of freedom.

_source.definition_text: a wood, wire or metal structure which divides or goes around an area of land
_source.learnerexamples_text: a garden fence; I looked around to make sure that no-one saw me and jumped [over] the fence.

_source.definition_text: showing qualities that people generally think are typical of women
_source.learnerexamples_text: a feminine voice;  feminine beauty; When my grandmother was a young women, it was a must for her to wear a dress or at least a skirt and a very feminine blouse.

_source.definition_text: to take care of yourself without help
_source.learnerexamples_text: When you go away to college, you have to learn to fend for yourself.; For such people to be able to provide for their families and fend for themselves, they have to work irrespective of how they do the job.

_source.definition_text: a boat that regularly carries passengers and often vehicles across an area of water
_source.learnerexamples_text: a car ferry; We're going across to France by/on the ferry.; We took the ferry to Calais.; We are planning to go to the "Red Island", which is just 15 minutes from Rovigno by ferry.

_source.definition_text: Fertile land or soil produces a lot of healthy plants.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They settled in the fertile river valleys.; We had an enormous backyard with the most fertile soil where we grew all sorts of vegetables.

_source.definition_text: a series of special events, performances, etc. that often takes place over several days
_source.learnerexamples_text: a folk/pop/rock festival; The Aldeburgh Festival is held every year in June.; the Cannes Film Festival; I d[e]cided to go to that city because of the film festival that was going to happen.

_source.definition_text: a special day or period when people celebrate something, especially a religious event
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Jewish festival of Hanukkah; I like to dress up traditional[l]y during festivals.

_source.definition_text: to go to another place to get something or someone and bring them back
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you fetch my glasses for me from the other room, please?; I have to fetch my mother from the station.; I'll come and fetch you at 7 o'clock.

_source.definition_text: when people are very excited about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Election fever has gripped the nation.; It was then when they started to build enormous buildings and skyscrapers all around. The "building fever" had started.

_source.definition_text: when someone's body temperature rises because they are ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's got a headache and a high/slight fever.; I understood that she was alone with her brother and he has [a] fever.

_source.definition_text: some, or a small number of
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll be ready in a few minutes.; I need to get a few things in town.; We've been having a few problems with the new computer.; "How many potatoes do you want?" - "Oh, just a few, please."; I've met a few of his friends.

_source.definition_text: quite a large number of
_source.learnerexamples_text: I know quite a few people who've had the same problem.; We played quite a few games and we had prizes for the winner of each of the games.

_source.definition_text: a small number, not many or not enough
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is among the few people I can trust.; Very few people can afford to pay those prices.; Few of the children can read or write yet.; We get few complaints.; According to the survey, as few as 10% of us are happy with our jobs.

_source.definition_text: not happening or existing very often
_source.learnerexamples_text: Opportunities like this are few and far between.; Jobs in those days were few and far between and for a number of years he was alternating between temporary jobs and unemployment benefit.

_source.definition_text: the substance in plants which cannot be digested and helps food pass through your body
_source.learnerexamples_text: Broccoli is a good source of fibre.; We try to eat less fat and more fibre, like oats, instead of sandwiches with butter and cheese.

_source.definition_text: something that is not true or real
_source.learnerexamples_text: Nobody knows whether his statement is fact or fiction.; Everything she had said turned out to be a complete fiction.; With regret I have to admit that [the] lively social programme was a total fiction and the only thing participants could do was to find and make friend[s] oneself, as I did.

_source.definition_text: literature and stories about imaginary characters and events
_source.learnerexamples_text: The book is a work of fiction and not intended as a historical account.; a writer of children's fiction; In his fiction, one can detect traces of different literary schools.

_source.definition_text: existing only in fiction
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fictional character; What he is especially known and admired [for] are his fictional but memorable characters, which became almost archetypes in literature.

_source.definition_text: an area of land used for growing crops or keeping animals
_source.learnerexamples_text: corn fields; The cows were all standing in one corner of the field.; You could spend hours walking in wonderful forests and fields.

_source.definition_text: an area of grass used for playing sport
_source.learnerexamples_text: the school playing/sports field; a football/hockey/rugby field; They filmed our sports fields and our classroom.

_source.definition_text: an area of study or activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's an expert in the field of biochemistry.; This time [it] is the case of telecommunications, tomorrow it will be the time of advances in the field of medicine.

_source.definition_text: the people who are competing in a race, activity, or business
_source.learnerexamples_text: We lead the field in genetic research.; Brian Moore leads the field with a style that can only be called immaculate.

_source.definition_text: an area of land covered with or containing a lot of a particular substance
_source.learnerexamples_text: a gas/oil field; The upper part of the volcano is a vast field of black lava.; They searched for meteorites on the frozen ice fields of Antarctica.; Our tour took also us to see the lower fields; from where the tour bus stops [to] the end of the lava fields, which is in the sea, it takes about t[h]irty minutes walking.

_source.definition_text: violent or angry
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fierce dog ; a fierce attack/battle ; Two men were shot during fierce fighting last weekend.; This may surprise some of you who have always thought of [the] tiger as a fierce and dangerous beast.

_source.definition_text: showing strong feeling or energetic activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: The expansion plans will face fierce opposition/resistance from environmentalists.; There is fierce competition to join the Special Branch.; Nowadays, family life importance is a matter that arouses fierce passions.

_source.definition_text: very strong or powerful
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fierce winds/storms battered the coast all weekend.; Fire fighters had to retreat from the fierce heat.; The need for darkness was justified by the fierce thunderstorm, which seemed likely to smash the house into pieces.

_source.definition_text: the number 15
_source.learnerexamples_text: thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen; "How many books were returned?" "Fifteen."; She's invited fifteen children to her party.; It is fifteen years old and it is in good condition.

_source.definition_text: one of five equal parts of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: One fifth is the same as 20 percent.

_source.definition_text: 5th written as a word
_source.learnerexamples_text: the fifth floor of the building; Tomorrow is the fifth of September.; This is [the] fifth Harry Potter book.

_source.definition_text: the number 50
_source.learnerexamples_text: forty, fifty, sixty; They were travelling at fifty miles an hour.; There were fifty guests at my party.

_source.definition_text: to be aged between 50 and 59
_source.searchterms_text: (be) in your fifties;be in your fifties;fifty
_source.learnerexamples_text: He retired when he was still in his fifties.; Despite being in my fifties I am healthy and in good shape.

_source.definition_text: the years from 1950-1959
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many new towns were built in the fifties.; I love bands from the fifties, sixties, seventies... and most of the radio stations seem to forget that the music has a history and it is always nice to remember past songs, because a good song will always be a good song.

_source.definition_text: to use physical force to try to defeat another person or group of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: Two men were fighting outside the park.; Sam's always fighting with his little brother.; She was very tired and afraid, so I decided to help her [by] going to the "Blue Forest", and I remember I fought with the wizards.

_source.definition_text: to take part in a war
_source.learnerexamples_text: Millions of young men fought in World War One.; He fought in the Spanish Civil war and in World War II.

_source.definition_text: to try hard to stop something bad happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: He fought against racism.; New measures have been introduced to fight crime.; The other great advantage is that it is a nice way of fighting against pol[l]ution.

_source.definition_text: to argue
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've got to stop fighting in front of the children.; Then I became angry again because although I spent my day doing nothing, I didn't buy a present for my sister, and when I went home we f[ou]ght.

_source.definition_text: to try hard to achieve something you want or think is right
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are fighting for their freedom.; He had to fight hard to keep his job.; All of them [were] fighting for their cause.

_source.definition_text: when people use physical force to hurt or attack others
_source.learnerexamples_text: Jeff's always getting into/starting fights.; The older boys broke up the fight.; He put up a fight when the police tried to arrest him.; My son got into a fight on his way from the school to the house and he had a black eye.

_source.definition_text: when you use a lot of effort to achieve or stop something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Join us in our fight for freedom!; We must continue the fight against homelessness.; He died last week after a long fight with cancer.; This year has brought some good news in the fight to save the whales.; I was sitting like every evening in my armchair, reading my favorite book "My fight for Irish freedom" and suddenly the lights went out.

_source.definition_text: an argument
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't want to have a fight over this.; I had a fight with my mother and she told me off in front of my friends.

_source.definition_text: when people fight, especially in a war
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fierce fighting has continued all day.; [Kung-fu] is not only a way of fighting, it is also a way of life.

_source.definition_text: the symbol for a number or an amount expressed in numbers
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you read this figure? Is it a three or an eight?; Write the amount in both words and figures.; I looked quickly down the column of figures.; He earns a six-figure salary.; More than 5,000 were present, so I don't understand why you mention the figure 2,000.

_source.definition_text: the shape of someone's body, usually an attractive shape
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's got a good figure.; She has long blond hair and blue eyes. She has a good figure.

_source.definition_text: a particular type of person, often someone important or famous
_source.learnerexamples_text: Lincoln was a major figure in American politics.; She is an important figure in Argentina.

_source.definition_text: a person that you cannot see clearly
_source.learnerexamples_text: I could see two tall figures in the distance.; Suddenly a figure appeared in front of us.

_source.definition_text: numbers from 0 to 9/numbers from 10 to 99, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't know exactly how many times the train has been late this month, but it's certainly in double figures.

_source.definition_text: a number that expresses an amount, especially in official documents
_source.learnerexamples_text: Government figures show a rise in unemployment.; They do not have any avenues of change until they migrate to cities, which only 15% of villagers do in Pakistan according to government figures.

_source.definition_text: a picture or drawing in a book or document, usually with a number
_source.learnerexamples_text: Look at the graph shown in Figure 2.; Figure 1 demonstrates the use of electricity in England in summer and winter.

_source.base_text: figure out sth/sb or figure sth/sb out
_source.definition_text: to finally understand something or someone
_source.searchterms_text: figure;figure out sth/sb or figure sth/sb out
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't figure out why he did it.; I find him really odd - I can't figure him out at all.; I couldn't figure out what had happened.

_source.definition_text: to decide something after thinking about it
_source.learnerexamples_text: I figured that it was time to tell her the truth.; Everything around us is constantly cutting down on budget, leaving fewer and less attractive work places, so I figure the best way to actually obtain a job is to go after something you're truly passionate about.

_source.definition_text: a collection of information such as text, pictures or computer programs stored together electronically with a single name
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's the file name?; I'm going to copy/save this file.; I need the computer to save all my file[s].

_source.definition_text: a collection of information and documents about someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a study file; The school keeps files on all its students.; I think I've left the file near the table in the drawing room.

_source.definition_text: If people or things fill a space, there are a lot of them in it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dark clouds filled the sky.; The streets were filled with tourists.; Suddenly clouds filled the sky with darkness.

_source.definition_text: to make a container or space full, or to become full
_source.learnerexamples_text: I filled the bucket with water.; I drank my tea while the bath was filling.; It was really hot, even for a summer day, but we were refreshed by a beautiful waterfall that we stopped [at] to fill our water bottle.

_source.definition_text: If light, sound, or a smell fills a place, you can easily notice it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The smell of smoke filled the room.; The class was filled with the sound of laughing.

_source.definition_text: to give a job or position to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry, the job/position/post/vacancy has already been filled.; We would prefer to fill the position with a recent graduate.; Suppose if ten people retire from an organization, the vacancies are filled by bringing up the middle management and their previous positions will be filled be lower management.

_source.definition_text: to make someone feel very angry/happy/proud, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: fill;fill sb with anger/joy/pride etc;fill sb with anger/joy/pride, etc.;filled;filling;fills
_source.learnerexamples_text: The thought of losing him filled her with fear.; Nobody was talking and the 50 passengers were filled with terror.

_source.base_text: fill in/out sth or fill sth in/out
_source.definition_text: to write the necessary information on an official document
_source.searchterms_text: fill;fill in/out sth or fill sth in/out
_source.learnerexamples_text: to fill in/out a form/questionnaire ; Please fill in my form.

_source.definition_text: to provide something that people need or want
_source.learnerexamples_text: The new nursery is really filling a need.; I had nearly finished my study and had an idea to start a small software company, filling a gap in the market that was overlooked by the larger I.T. companies.

_source.definition_text: to become full, or to make something become full
_source.searchterms_text: fill;fill up (sth) or fill (sth) up;fill up sth or fill sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: The seats in the hall were filling up fast.; Could you fill that bucket up with water for me?; I bought that [couch] just to fill up the space left.

_source.definition_text: a story shown in moving pictures, shown at the cinema or on television
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's your favourite film?; We took the children to see a film.; I hate people talking while I'm watching a film.; He made over thirty films.; a film critic/director/producer

_source.definition_text: a thin layer of something on a surface
_source.learnerexamples_text: A thick film of dust covered the furniture.; The walls were covered with a thin film of water.

_source.definition_text: to record moving pictures with a camera, usually to make a film
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most of the scenes were filmed in a studio.; They filmed for a week in Spain.; So he had put it into his cupboard which was [just] open and the burglar hadn't noticed the camera which filmed all his actions.

_source.definition_text: a film director, especially an independent one who has control over how the film is made
_source.learnerexamples_text: one of the industry's top film-makers.; The plot [i]s about a film-maker and his difficulties [in] finish[ing] his last film.

_source.definition_text: to gradually appear
_source.learnerexamples_text: The sunlight filtered through the bedroom curtains.; Outside, the moonlight filtered through the leaves of the roadside trees like a sheet of burnished silver.

_source.definition_text: to pass a liquid or gas through a piece of equipment in order to remove solid pieces or other substances
_source.learnerexamples_text: The water was filtered to remove any impurities.; The sun's rays, filtered through the black lenses, seemed harmless.

_source.definition_text: to gradually become known
_source.learnerexamples_text: News is filtering in of an earthquake in Mexico.; At first I didn't realise what Nicole was saying, because she spoke French. Then the message slowly filtered down - Pregnant.

_source.definition_text: a piece of equipment that you pass a liquid or gas through in order to remove particular substances
_source.learnerexamples_text: a coffee filter; Finally, the governments of all countries should implement heavy pecuniary punishments to the factory owners who do not use special filters on their chimneys or on their waste systems.

_source.definition_text: extremely dirty
_source.learnerexamples_text: Wash your hands, they're filthy!; Creaking, worn-out beds, dripping taps and filthy rugs have nothing in common with 'luxury'!

_source.definition_text: last in a series or coming at the end of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a final warning/offer ; the final paragraph ; West Ham scored in the final minute.; The game is in its final stages.; I need them imm[e]diately as my final exam is [the] day after tomorrow.

_source.definition_text: rude or offensive
_source.learnerexamples_text: filthy language/jokes ;  Smoking is a filthy habit. ; As far as books are concerned, pornography and filthy language is evident everywhere, to lure people to buy these books.

_source.definition_text: If a decision, agreement, or answer is final, it will not be changed or discussed any more.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The committee's decision is final.; It was the sort of statement that you know is final, and Mr. Cameron perceived this.

_source.definition_text: the last in a series of games, races or competitions, usually the one in which the winner is chosen
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're in the final.; Last year we got through to the final.; The men's basketball final will be on Sunday.; We were in the final, but we lost.

_source.definition_text: after a long time or some difficulty
_source.learnerexamples_text: We finally got home at midnight.; After months of looking he finally found a job.; Well, I have finally decided that I will paint my room blue.

_source.definition_text: used especially at the beginning of a sentence to introduce the last point or idea
_source.learnerexamples_text: Finally, I'd like to thank everyone for coming this evening.; Finally, I want you to say hi [to] everybody and I am looking forward to see[ing] you.

_source.definition_text: the money which a person, company or country has
_source.learnerexamples_text: We keep a tight control on the organization's finances.; She needs to sort out her finances.; First of all, we should budget our finances better.

_source.definition_text: the control of how large amounts of money should be spent
_source.learnerexamples_text: the finance minister; You need to speak to someone in the finance department.; The finance committee controls the school's budget.; Therefore we decided to invite a minist[er] of finance to explain it.

_source.definition_text: to provide the money needed for something to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: The local authority has refused to finance the scheme.; I [am] apply[ing] for this job because I want to earn some money to finance my study.

_source.definition_text: relating to money or how money is managed
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're having a few financial difficulties at the moment. ; a financial adviser ; The person described himself as a financial officer of a South African government and needs a contact person in Switzerland to transfer 200 m dollar[s].

_source.definition_text: in a way that relates to money or how money is managed
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's still financially dependent on his parents.; They advise them or help them financially.

_source.definition_text: to discover something or someone that you have been searching for
_source.learnerexamples_text: I couldn't find Andrew's telephone number.; Police found the missing girl at a London railway station.; Has Mick found himself a place to live yet?; I can't find my cd, can you bring some music please?

_source.definition_text: to discover something by chance
_source.learnerexamples_text: I found some money in my coat pocket.; The body was found by a man walking his dog.; Miss Murphy said that she had found my diary in a street near the airport.

_source.definition_text: to become aware that something exists or has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: We came home to find (that) the cat had had kittens.; I found (that) I could easily swim 1000 metres.; I found that the food inside there is very nice.

_source.definition_text: to think or feel a particular way about someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: find;find sb/sth easy/boring/funny etc;find sb/sth easy/boring/funny, etc.;finding;finds;found
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you find Clive difficult to talk to?; She doesn't find it easy to talk about her problems.; I find living in the city quite stressful.; I found her very helpful.; I found it very amusing.

_source.definition_text: to have or get enough money/time, etc. to do something
_source.searchterms_text: find;find the money/time etc;find the money/time, etc.;finding;finds;found
_source.learnerexamples_text: Where do you find the money to do all these things?; I hope you will keep fit and find the time to do everything.

_source.definition_text: to become aware that you have gone somewhere or done something without intending to
_source.searchterms_text: find;find yourself somewhere/doing sth;find yourself somewhere/doing sth ;finding;finds;found
_source.learnerexamples_text: I suddenly found myself making lunch.; The most embarassing moment of my life [was] when, during a school trip to Paris, a friend of mine and I went to the wrong room and found ourselves in front of our teacher who, having had a shower, was looking for his glasses.

_source.definition_text: to exist or be present somewhere
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many plant and animal species are found only in the rainforests.; Vitamin C is found in citrus fruit.; An example might be the [k]oala bear, which could be found almost everywhere in Australia not so long ago.

_source.definition_text: to judge that someone is guilty or not guilty in a law court
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was found guilty of murder.; To the surprise of everyone in the village, the judge found her guilty but didn't send her to jail because he thought she should take care of Linda, who had no other relatives.

_source.definition_text: to criticize someone or something, especially without good reasons
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was always finding fault with our work.; Sometimes I take offence at their trying to find fault with me and I am not allowed to answer back.

_source.definition_text: to find shared beliefs, interests or ideas
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's difficult for me to find any common ground with my dad.; The bottom line is we have to find some common ground and some balance between development and nature...

_source.definition_text: to get information about something, or to learn a fact for the first time
_source.searchterms_text: find;find out (sth) or find (sth) out;find out sth or find sth out
_source.learnerexamples_text: How did you find out about the party?; I'll just go and find out what's going on outside.; We need to find out why he's late.; Too late, she found out that the train had been cancelled.; If my mother finds out she'll kill me!

_source.definition_text: well, healthy, or happy
_source.learnerexamples_text: "How are you?" "I'm fine, thanks."; I felt terrible last night but I feel fine this morning.; I'm fine.

_source.definition_text: used to agree with a suggestion, idea, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Shall we meet at 8 o'clock?" "Yes, that's fine."; OK that's fine. We['ll] meet at 8pm.

_source.definition_text: good or good enough
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Is this soup hot enough?" "Yes, it's fine."

_source.definition_text: sunny and not raining
_source.learnerexamples_text: If it's fine tomorrow, we could have a picnic.; Today the weather is fine and warm.

_source.definition_text: excellent or much better than average
_source.learnerexamples_text: fine wines; This building is the finest example of its type.; There [we] will be served a fine dinner.

_source.definition_text: thin or made of very small pieces
_source.learnerexamples_text: fine, brown hair; fine sand; They got their hands on some anthrax bacteria, grew them in petri dishes and with all her knowledge in biology managed to make anthrax spores. Her friends ground the clumps of spores into fine particles.

_source.definition_text: an amount of money that you must pay for breaking a rule or law
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had to pay a fine.; a parking fine; The maximum penalty is a $1000 fine.; If found guilty, he faces a heavy fine.; She was made to pay a fine and she wasn't sent to prison.

_source.definition_text: to charge someone an amount of money as a punishment for not obeying a rule or law
_source.learnerexamples_text: Drivers who break the speed limit can expect to be fined heavily.; They fined him $100 for using threatening behaviour.; Besides, you can be fined by the police.

_source.definition_text: very well or without any problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: "How did your exam go?" "It went fine, I think."; The car was working fine yesterday.; The couple was great and everything went fine.

_source.definition_text: into small pieces
_source.learnerexamples_text: Finely chop the onion.

_source.definition_text: one of the long thin separate parts of the hand, including your thumb
_source.learnerexamples_text: He noticed her long delicate fingers.; I cut my finger chopping vegetables last night.; Then my mother brought the cake and while she was lighting the candles she burnt her finger.

_source.base_text: keep your fingers crossed/ cross your fingers
_source.definition_text: to hope that things will happen in the way that you want them to
_source.searchterms_text: finger;fingers;keep your fingers crossed/ cross your fingers
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's keep our fingers crossed that she gets the job.; We're crossing our fingers and hoping that the weather stays fine.; Wish me luck, Winnie," she sighed "keep your fingers crossed, please".

_source.base_text: have/keep your finger on the pulse
_source.definition_text: to be/stay familiar with the most recent changes or improvements
_source.searchterms_text: finger;fingers;have/keep your finger on the pulse
_source.learnerexamples_text: The situation changes daily, so you've got to keep your finger on the pulse.; It wouldn't be clever to hire people who are completely ignora[nt] about music and they must constantly keep their finger on the pulse of [the] music industry.

_source.definition_text: to understand exactly why a situation is the way it is
_source.learnerexamples_text: Something was wrong, but I couldn't put my finger on it.; Something sinister about the picture, he felt, but he couldn't put his finger on what made him [think this].

_source.definition_text: If you have something at your fingertips, you can get it and use it very easily.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He had all the information needed at his fingertips.; An Internet connection literally means having the world at your fingertips.

_source.definition_text: the hard part that covers and protects the top of the end of your finger
_source.learnerexamples_text: dirty/long fingernails; She had bright red fingernails.; Half way through dinner we had discussed almost everything about him: his lips, fingernails, how he would look in swimming pants, how he would dance etc.

_source.definition_text: to end
_source.learnerexamples_text: The meeting should finish around four o'clock.; The play finishes with a song.; He goes to college at 9 am and finishes [at] 1 pm.

_source.definition_text: to complete something, or come to the end of an activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll call you when I've finished my homework.; Please place your questionnaire in the box when you've finished.; She finished the concert with a song from her first album.; Have you finished reading that magazine?; I have finished my course.

_source.definition_text: to eat, drink or use something completely so that none remains
_source.learnerexamples_text: He finished his coffee and left.; We finished the pie last night.; After Maria finished her coffee, she got the man's phone and left the cafe.

_source.definition_text: to be in the first/second, etc. winning position at the end of a race or competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her horse finished fourth.; I finished third; it is good even if we were only 7.

_source.definition_text: to complete the last part of something that you are doing
_source.searchterms_text: finish;finish off (sth) or finish (sth) off;finish off sth or finish sth off
_source.learnerexamples_text: I want to finish off this essay before I go to bed.; I am going to finish off with the sad story about the exam that we didn't get to take.

_source.definition_text: to end a romantic relationship with someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Paula's just finished with her boyfriend after three years.; I lived in the United States for three year[s], and when I moved to Brazil, I had to finish with my boyfriend.

_source.definition_text: the end of a race, or the last part of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a close finish; They replayed the finish in slow motion.; We [had] a race and I [came] second [at] the finish.

_source.definition_text: from the beginning of something to its end
_source.learnerexamples_text: I enjoyed the film from start to finish.; I found out that the service itself should last at least one and half hour[s] from start to finish.

_source.definition_text: having a limit or end
_source.learnerexamples_text: We only have a finite amount of time to complete this task.; Some analysts suggest that the price increase is due to the facts that petrol is a finite resource which could become unavailable in the next 20-30 years.

_source.definition_text: to start burning
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car crashed and caught fire.; One of the new machines that I had brought from Germany had caught fire.

_source.definition_text: heat, light, and flames that are produced when something burns
_source.learnerexamples_text: The library was badly damaged in the fire.; It is thought that the fire was started deliberately.; It took the firefighters three hours to put out the fire.; How many historic buildings are damaged by fire each year?; Yesterday I bought very cool clothes. [...] I bought them because yesterday all my shoes and T-shirts were burned [in] a fire.

_source.definition_text: a small controlled fire that is used for heating or cooking
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's very cold in here - should I light a fire?; We built a fire on the beach.; We put up our tents and made a small fire.; In the evenings we sat down [o]n the grass round a fire and talked to each other.

_source.definition_text: If something is on fire, it is burning when it should not be.
_source.learnerexamples_text: If your home was on fire and you could save only one thing, what would it be?; A lot of bu[i]ldings were on fire.

_source.definition_text: the shooting of guns and other weapons
_source.learnerexamples_text: The soldiers opened fire.; Suddenly, one of the thieves opened fire.

_source.definition_text: to be criticized
_source.learnerexamples_text: The government has come under fire for closing the hospital.

_source.definition_text: to be involved in an activity that could be dangerous
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're playing with fire if we continue with genetic modification of our food.; Stop playing with fire or World War 3 might come in [the] shape of a nuclear war.

_source.base_text: set fire to sth; set sth on fire
_source.definition_text: to make something start burning, usually to cause damage
_source.searchterms_text: fire;fires;set fire to sth set sth on fire;set fire to sth; set sth on fire
_source.learnerexamples_text: Enemy troops set fire to the village.; At this point nothing made sense anymore, so I just watched while Jake set the car on fire.

_source.definition_text: to cause a weapon to shoot bullets, arrows or missiles
_source.learnerexamples_text: He fired his gun into the air.; He fired three shots.; Someone started firing at us.; Without warning he started firing into the crowd.; Martins found Lime on an iron staircase and fired a last shot, killing Lime.

_source.definition_text: to make someone very excited or interested in something
_source.learnerexamples_text: His paintings really fired my imagination.; The newspaper article on education that I read really fired my imagination and urged me to think about the points raised.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone they must leave their job
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was fired after she was caught stealing from her employer.; He was fired from his last job for poor performance.; She has just been fired as editor of the newspaper.; Last month I was fired from my job in a bank.

_source.definition_text: an organization that is in charge of preventing and stopping unwanted fires
_source.learnerexamples_text: Call the fire brigade.; By that time the fire brigade had arrived - luckily som[e] neighbour had phoned them.

_source.definition_text: a person whose job is to stop fires from burning
_source.learnerexamples_text: His cousin works as a firefighter.; We could see firefighters and ambulances coming from all over the premises!

_source.definition_text: a space in the wall of a room where you can have a fire, or the structure around this space
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was a large fireplace in the living room.; They were sitting in front of the fireplace, in a tiny cottage.

_source.definition_text: the building where fire engines are kept and firefighters wait for emergencies
_source.learnerexamples_text: We visited our local fire station.; I only saw M[r]. Bean from my class[room] window - they were filming him running to the fire station.

_source.definition_text: a small object that explodes to produce a loud noise and bright colours, often used to celebrate special events
_source.learnerexamples_text: a firework display ; When it gets dark we'll let off/set off the fireworks.; What time do the fireworks start?; We have spent three days [at] Disneyland, watching fireworks every night.

_source.definition_text: certain or fixed and not likely to change
_source.learnerexamples_text: We don't have any firm plans for the weekend yet.; I'm a firm believer in equal rights.; It is my firm belief that I would use all the experience I have.

_source.definition_text: not soft, but not completely hard
_source.learnerexamples_text: A firm bed is better for your back.

_source.definition_text: strict and making certain that people do what you want
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've got to be firm with children.; Being an officer, my father was rather firm with my sister and me.

_source.definition_text: strong and tight
_source.learnerexamples_text: a firm handshake/grip ; Of course there will be moments where you have to mark out a border to the child by a firm grip on his arm or a slap on his bottom, but it shouldn't have to happen very often.

_source.definition_text: a company or business
