_source.learnerexamples_text: He works for a law firm called Neil and Vigliano.; He's just started working for an accountancy firm/a firm of accountants in Bristol.; I have to improve my knowledge of English because I have the opportunity to work for an English law firm.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is certain or fixed
_source.learnerexamples_text: I firmly believe that we must take action on this.; I firmly believe that some of the things you mentioned are wrong.

_source.definition_text: strongly; in a way that will not become loose
_source.learnerexamples_text: Make sure the rope is firmly attached before attempting to climb down it.; Slowly but firmly I grab[b]ed the door handle, took another quick glance in the room, and turned it.

_source.definition_text: coming before all others
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is my first trip to New York.; Karen was the first person to arrive.; We met for the first time yesterday.; My first day in college is Monday.

_source.definition_text: most important, top
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sheila won first prize in the photo competition.; It was good because my cousin played and won the first prize.

_source.definition_text: when you first see or hear about something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was love at first sight!; It may, at first sight, seem a surprising choice.; It was love at first sight!

_source.definition_text: before everything or everyone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can come out tonight, but I've got to do my homework first.; I have to go to [the] dentist first!

_source.definition_text: at the start of a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Why did you invite her in the first place?; In the first place, you were unknown people for me, but now you are my special foreign friends.

_source.definition_text: before doing anything else
_source.learnerexamples_text: First of all, we swam 200 metres in the pool. ; First of all, I bought a new t-shirt, [a] cool jacket and jeans. After that, I went to the athletic[s] store.

_source.definition_text: used to introduce the first idea, reason, etc. in a series
_source.learnerexamples_text: First of all, I'd like to ask you a few questions about your childhood.; First of all, thanks for your letter.

_source.definition_text: used to introduce the first idea, reason, etc. in a series
_source.learnerexamples_text: First, I want to thank my parents.; First, I want to say "Thank you!"

_source.definition_text: for the first time
_source.learnerexamples_text: When did you first meet each other?; I first heard the song on the radio.; I first heard of it [o]n the radio and then I saw a leaflet about it.

_source.definition_text: at the beginning of a situation or period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: At first I thought she was unfriendly, but actually she's just shy.; At first, when I arrived I was very nervous because I didn't know anyone, but then a girl started talking to me and I felt better.

_source.definition_text: more than anything else
_source.learnerexamples_text: In spite of being elected to office, she remains first and foremost a writer.; First and foremost it is my longing to help others with what they cannot do for themselves.

_source.definition_text: to be the most important person or thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her career always comes first.; They do not take the time to sit down and enjoy being with their family. The work comes first, and the family next.

_source.definition_text: to consider someone or something to be the most important thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most couples put their children first when sorting out their problems.; On the other hand, we forget about our personality and the worth that we have as individuals; we put our wishes first, [rather] than what we really need in life.

_source.definition_text: the first person or thing to do or be something, or the first person or thing mentioned
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tonight sees the first of three documentaries about cancer.; She was one of the first to arrive.; He is the first to admit that much of his success is due to his good looks.; I prefer the first because it's an exciting story of a cat that escapes from a dangerous house lived [in] by an aggressive dog.

_source.definition_text: to be something that has never happened before
_source.learnerexamples_text: Man walking on the moon was a first in space history.

_source.definition_text: on the first floor
_source.learnerexamples_text: a first-floor flat/apartment/office

_source.definition_text: the floor of a building that is directly above ground level
_source.learnerexamples_text: She works on the first floor.; My bedroom is on the first floor.

_source.definition_text: the language that someone learns to speak first
_source.learnerexamples_text: Madeleine's first language is French, but she also speaks German fluently.; Originally I come from Germany and therefore my first language is German.

_source.definition_text: the personal name that was given to you when you were born and that is not your family's name
_source.learnerexamples_text: It can be rude to call someone by their first name if they are much older or more important than you.; After that he asked the students to introduce themselves, and he easily learned the first name[s] of the student[s] and addressed them [by] their first name except me and it really annoyed me.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to the first thing in a list
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are two very good reasons why we can't do it. Firstly, we don't have enough money, and secondly, we don't have enough time.; I think it [would] suit us, firstly because it is good work experience, [and] secondly [because] we can get discounts on books and CDs.

_source.definition_text: an animal that lives only in water and swims using its tail and fins
_source.learnerexamples_text: Several large fish live in the pond.; Sanjay caught the biggest fish I've ever seen.; We are going to go to an even larger (no, the largest) river to catch fish next week!!

_source.definition_text: the form of a verb or pronoun that is used when people are speaking or writing about themselves. For example, 'I' and 'we' are first person pronouns.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Autobiographies are written in the first person.

_source.definition_text: fish eaten as food
_source.learnerexamples_text: fried fish; I don't eat fish or meat.; My favourite food is fish.

_source.definition_text: someone who catches fish as a job or as a hobby
_source.learnerexamples_text: Local fishermen are finding it difficult to make a living.; His father was a fisherman and he died working just a few days before he was born, so the child had never met him.

_source.definition_text: to try to catch fish
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're fishing for tuna.; In the countryside the air is pure and you can fish in lakes or walk in fields.

_source.definition_text: the sport or job of catching fish
_source.learnerexamples_text: My dad loves to go fishing.; salmon fishing; Fishing is still their main source of income.; We can go fishing or hunting.

_source.definition_text: to be the right size or shape for someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: That jacket fits you perfectly.; These jeans don't fit me any more.; I can't find a lid to fit this jar.; Sometimes I like the style and colour but when I wear them I see that they don't fit me.

_source.definition_text: a hand closed into a ball with the fingers and thumb curled tightly together
_source.learnerexamples_text: He banged his fist down angrily on the table.; He slammed his fists against the door and yelled out several times but to no response.

_source.definition_text: If people or things fit somewhere, or if you can fit them somewhere, that place is big enough for them.
_source.searchterms_text: -tt-;fit;fit (sth) in/into/through/under, etc.;fit sth in/into/through/under etc;fit sth in/into/through/under, etc.;fits;fitted;fitting;tt
_source.learnerexamples_text: How many people can you fit in your car?; This radio is small enough to fit into my pocket.; The desk has to be very small and has to fit into the corner, because there is not much space left in my bedroom.

_source.definition_text: to put or fix something somewhere
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the carpets we sell are fitted free.; You ought to fit a smoke alarm in the kitchen.; The air pollution could be reduced if car manufacturers and companies made [people] fit effective filters on car exhausts and factory chimneys.

_source.definition_text: to be the same as or like something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She seems to fit the police description.; The ac[c]ommodation I [had] during the trip didn't fit the description in the advertisement and neither did the restaurants or the cultural activit[ie]s.

_source.definition_text: to feel that you belong to a particular group and are accepted by them
_source.learnerexamples_text: He doesn't fit in with the other pupils in his class.; How shall they behave in order to fit in?

_source.definition_text: to be suitable for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The punishment should fit the crime.; You ought to put on a formal dress or suit to fit the atmosphere.

_source.definition_text: If one thing fits in with another thing, they look pleasant together or are suitable for each other.
_source.searchterms_text: fit;fit in with sth;fit in with sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a very nice sofa but it doesn't fit in with the rest of the room.; Modern buildings don't fit in [with] the architecture of our village.

_source.definition_text: If something fits in with a situation, idea, method, etc., it is suitable and works successfully as part of it.
_source.searchterms_text: fit;fit in with sth;fit in with sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Changing location fits in with their plans to expand the business.; In conclusion, I think your wedding day should be about you and your partner and the wedding celebrations should fit in with your combined ideas and cultures and wants to make it a memorable occasion for you and not to satisfy other people.

_source.definition_text: healthy and strong, especially as a result of exercise
_source.learnerexamples_text: I joined a gym to get fit.; I jog to keep fit.; You need to be very fit to go mountain climbing.; I'm on holiday in Miami [and] I've seen a lot of very fit people.

_source.definition_text: of a good enough quality or suitable type for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is this water fit to drink?; She's not in a fit state to drive.; It has undergone restoration recently and is now fit to serve as a perfect example of [a] model and modern British college library.

_source.base_text: do sth as you see/think fit
_source.definition_text: to do something that you feel is the right thing to do, although other people might disapprove
_source.searchterms_text: do sth as you see/think fit;fit;fitter;fittest
_source.learnerexamples_text: You must spend the money as you see fit.; Do as you think fit!

_source.definition_text: the number 5
_source.learnerexamples_text: Five, four, three, two, one, blast-off!; I work five days a week.; I will finish work at five o'clock.

_source.definition_text: the condition of being physically strong and healthy
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm trying to improve my fitness by cycling to work.; I specially like fitness lessons.

_source.definition_text: to repair something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They couldn't fix my old computer, so I bought a new one.; I had an accident [yesterday] and I need to fix my car.

_source.definition_text: to decide a certain and exact date, time, place, price, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Shall we fix a time for our next meeting?; They haven't fixed a date for the wedding yet.; If you are busy at that time, you can call them to fix a new date.

_source.definition_text: to fasten something in position so that it cannot move
_source.searchterms_text: fix;fix sth onto/to/under etc;fix sth onto/to/under, etc.;fixed;fixes;fixing
_source.learnerexamples_text: We fixed the bookcase to the wall.; The seat was not fixed to the flo[o]r properly.

_source.definition_text: to arrange a meeting, date, event, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can we fix up a date for the next meeting?; The date of this event should be aranged soon. Perhaps if you tell us when it is more conve[ni]ent for you, we will fix up the date according to your answer.

_source.definition_text: If your eyes are fixed on something, you are looking at it continuously.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I kept my eyes fixed on his face.; Dozens of eyes were fixed on the sun-burnt, leaden coloured face of the guide, beaming with anticipation.

_source.definition_text: arranged or decided already and not able to be changed
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fixed price ; fixed interest rates; Usually you have a fixed time to listen [to] live music, but what if you are not able to go to the concert?

_source.definition_text: a piece of cloth with a special design and colours, that is the symbol of a country or a group, or has a particular meaning
_source.learnerexamples_text: the French flag; Flags of all twenty-seven countries are flying outside the building.; The guard waved his flag and the train pulled away from the station.; And about my present from the USA: I really would like to have an authentic American flag, to decorate my bedroom ceiling.

_source.definition_text: a natural ability to do something well
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has a flair for languages.; She's an artist with a flair for promotion.

_source.definition_text: hot, bright, burning gas produced by something on fire
_source.learnerexamples_text: The flames grew larger as the fire spread.; When the fire engine arrived the house was already in flames.; We were standing by the window and the flames were [getting] nearer and nearer.

_source.definition_text: when you do something in an exciting and interesting way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He played with great imagination and flair.; If I must describe the service I should say that it is superb: the gentle waiters serve with flair as if it was a culinary cabaret.

_source.definition_text: to suddenly start burning
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car plunged down a hill and burst into flames.; When we turned it on, it burst into flames and before we could exti[n]guish it, the fire destroyed my desk.

_source.definition_text: to shine brightly and suddenly, or to make something shine in this way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stop flashing that light in my eyes!; The lightning flashed and distant thunder rolled.; You'd better slow down, that car was flashing (its lights) at you.; As they were driving back, a light flashed, a crash sounded, then screams.

_source.definition_text: to appear for a short time, or to make something appear for a short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: An icon flashed up on the screen.

_source.definition_text: to move somewhere fast
_source.learnerexamples_text: The motorcycle flashed past us and around the corner.; The image flashed across my screen.; But one day an idea flashed through her mind.

_source.definition_text: a sudden bright light
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bomb exploded in a flash of yellow light.; At the same moment, that piece of unknown stuff sent towards me a flash of very bright light!

_source.definition_text: a piece of camera equipment that produces a bright light when you take a photograph in a dark place
_source.learnerexamples_text: Flash photography is not permitted anywhere in the museum.

_source.definition_text: a sudden experience of something such as a feeling or idea
_source.learnerexamples_text: a flash of anger; I had a flash of inspiration.

_source.definition_text: immediately, or very quickly
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll be back in a flash.; He took it and, in a flash, he came up to the surface.

_source.definition_text: when you suddenly remember something that happened in the past, often something bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: She suffered from flashbacks for years after the accident.; Margaret started to remember, yes; a sudden flashback brought her to the twenties, when she was still her mamma's little girl, all innocence and curls.

_source.definition_text: part of a film or book that goes back in time to something that happened before the main story began
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are several flashbacks to the character's childhood.; Another way of increasing the reader's interest is the par[al]lelism of both stories and the flashbacks she is always giving us to explain Olivia's experiences.

_source.definition_text: a set of rooms for living in which are part of a larger building and are usually all on one floor
_source.learnerexamples_text: a furnished/unfurnished flat; a block of flats; to buy/rent/move into/move out of a flat; They have a house in the country and a flat in London.; I live in a flat.

_source.definition_text: level and smooth, with no curved, high, or hollow parts
_source.learnerexamples_text: An ice rink needs to be completely flat.; Roll out the pastry on a flat surface.; Much of the countryside in East Anglia is very flat.; The countryside is very flat and for this kind of holiday it's really perfect!!

_source.definition_text: If a tyre, ball, etc. is flat, it does not contain enough air.
_source.learnerexamples_text: When I got to the car, I discovered I had a flat tyre.; I found my bicycle with a flat tyre and realised I would be late instead of early.

_source.definition_text: If a drink is flat, it does not contain enough bubbles of gas.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This lemonade is flat.

_source.definition_text: Flat shoes do not raise your feet far from the ground.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Wear flat shoes - you'll be on your feet all day.; In your last letter you wanted me to tell you about clothes. Well, as you know I'm tall so I always wear flat shoes in light colours like white, light green and blue.

_source.definition_text: in a level position, often against another surface
_source.learnerexamples_text: Lay the cloth flat across the table.

_source.definition_text: If an event or joke falls flat, it fails to have the effect that you wanted, such as making people laugh.
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the jokes in his speech fell flat.; The cultural visits fell flat [in comparison] to their expectations, although the sightseeing tour of Willstown was, as the students said, "fascinating".

_source.definition_text: to fall over so that your face hits the ground, often in an embarrassing way
_source.learnerexamples_text: I stepped on the ice and fell flat on my face.; You can guess what happened next - I fell flat on my face right in the mud and I have never felt more embarrassed in my life!

_source.definition_text: to become flat or to make something become flat
_source.learnerexamples_text: Roll out the dough into balls and flatten them slightly. ; Another thing they accomplished was to stop people cutting [down] trees because they wanted to flatten [the] land.

_source.definition_text: the number 4
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most animals have four legs.; We need four people to make up a team.; He works four days and has four days off.

_source.definition_text: a structure that forces water up into the air as a decoration
_source.learnerexamples_text: There is a beautiful fountain in the middle of the square.; The place I enjoyed the most was the park, because it had a nice atmosphere with all those happy kids, and the most terrific fountain I've ever seen.

_source.definition_text: the number 14
_source.learnerexamples_text: twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen; Her baby is fourteen months old.; Several days ago I had my birthday and I am now fourteen.

_source.definition_text: 4th written as a word
_source.learnerexamples_text: My birthday is on the fourth of December.; Daniel finished fourth in the race.; The new art class is in classroom A [o]n the fourth floor.

_source.definition_text: a wild animal like a dog with red-brown fur, a pointed nose, and a long, thick tail
_source.learnerexamples_text: A fox came in the night and killed the chickens.; One day, the fox attacked his animals and he shouted as much as he could.

_source.definition_text: a very small number or amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fraction of a second; Both of them hit the wall almost at the same time but, against Hall's prediction, Popou was better by a fraction of a second.

_source.definition_text: physically or emotionally weak
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fragile little girl; She seemed to be so fragile with an everlasting smile on her face.

_source.definition_text: easily broken, damaged, or destroyed
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fragile china cup; a fragile economy; The majority of these countries still have a very fragile economy.

_source.definition_text: a pleasant smell
_source.learnerexamples_text: the delicate fragrance of roses; We were inundated with the fresh air, an untold fragrance mixed with the warm breeze and the unique-styled buildings.

_source.definition_text: with a pleasant smell
_source.learnerexamples_text: fragrant flowers; From his terrace you can see the marvellous sea of Dublin Bay and appreciate the fragrant odour of the beautiful flowers that embellish the place.

_source.definition_text: a border which surrounds and supports a picture, door or window
_source.learnerexamples_text: a picture/window frame; I'm going to buy picture frames to put the pictures in and I'll put them on the wall, around my table.

_source.definition_text: not strong or healthy
_source.learnerexamples_text: a frail old lady; Looking at her, she was frail and looked confused.

_source.definition_text: the basic structure of a building, vehicle or piece of furniture that other parts are added onto
_source.learnerexamples_text: a bicycle frame; In my bedroom is a big bed with a wood frame and a comfortabl[e] matt[ress].

_source.definition_text: the way someone feels at a particular time
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was in a much more positive frame of mind today.; Naturally, these are more difficult factors to cope with for older people, but it just happens to anyone if you're not in the right frame of mind.

_source.definition_text: a system of rules, ideas, or beliefs that is used to plan or decide something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a legal framework for resolving disputes; the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages; They were all trying to do their best in the rigid framework of the existing system (one of them even succeeded in making the difference).

_source.definition_text: done in a fast and excited way and not calm or organized
_source.learnerexamples_text: a frantic search; Fred started to shiver as frantic images of the past flashed through his mind.

_source.definition_text: used when giving an honest and direct opinion, often one that might upset someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Quite frankly, I think this whole situation is ridiculous.; I'm asking this because quite frankly, it's the part of the festival that my friend and I enjoyed the most.

_source.definition_text: very worried or frightened
_source.learnerexamples_text: frantic calls for help; I got home to find Joe frantic with worry.; Donna's mother had heard her frantic shouts, and now said soothingly: "Have you forgotten Elaine has spent the night at her friend's house?"

_source.definition_text: when someone does something illegal in order to get money
_source.learnerexamples_text: credit card fraud; Michael was completely speechless when he realized that Claire had all the proof of the fraud he had [committed].

_source.definition_text: someone or something that deceives people by pretending to be someone or something that they are not
_source.learnerexamples_text: She claimed to be a journalist, but she was just a fraud.; My marriage was a fraud, a case of b[i]gamy.

_source.definition_text: dishonest and illegal
_source.learnerexamples_text: fraudulent insurance claims; This vice increases more and more as fanatics spend more money for sport-related topics, and so, most valuable players become more expensive and then they begin to be involved in cheating and fraudulent activities.

_source.definition_text: not busy doing anything
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you free this evening?; I don't have much free time.; I am free this afternoon.

_source.definition_text: not in prison
_source.learnerexamples_text: He will soon be a free man again.; I will [regret it] for the rest of my life, because I wanted to be a free man...

_source.definition_text: not limited or controlled
_source.learnerexamples_text: a free society ; Am I free to leave now?; People should be free to say what they think.; The agreement gives companies free access to the markets of member countries.; The plan was this: they would call the police, which would trap the man so the child would be free to return to his mother.

_source.definition_text: not costing any money
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got some free cinema tickets.; Members all receive a free copy of the monthly newsletter.; We will install your washing machine free of charge.; You don't have to bring any money because it is free.

_source.definition_text: not being used by anyone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is this seat free?; The hall was full of people and no seat was free.

_source.definition_text: to allow someone to leave prison or to allow a person or animal to escape
_source.learnerexamples_text: He opened the cage and set the birds free.; To sum up, animals should be set free and live as they should live in nature.

_source.definition_text: not containing or having anything harmful or unpleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: a life free from pain; We can start to grow new plants so that our environment looks fresh and enchanting and free from pesticides and sicknesses as well.

_source.definition_text: permission to make your own decisions about how you want to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The students were given a free hand as far as designing their product was concerned.; But unlike my parents, I wouldn't give my children a free hand in solving their problems.

_source.definition_text: without cost or payment
_source.learnerexamples_text: Children under five travel free.; He offered to do it for free.; I get tickets for free.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is not tied, limited, or controlled
_source.learnerexamples_text: The horse broke free and ran away.; If animals were born free, why [do] they have to live in a prison?

_source.definition_text: to escape from someone or something that is controlling you
_source.learnerexamples_text: She tried to break free from the social conditioning of her upbringing.; I would like to revisit there one day as it's firmly connected to my ad[o]lescence, when I struggled to break free from my peers, [and] tried to establish my own identity.

_source.definition_text: to suddenly escape or become separate from something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The prisoner broke free while the guards weren't looking.

_source.definition_text: to allow someone to leave a prison or place where they have been kept
_source.learnerexamples_text: After a ten-hour siege the gunman agreed to free the hostages.; We were taken hostage by a bank robber but the police came and freed us.

_source.definition_text: the condition or right of being able or allowed to do, say, think, etc. whatever you want to, without being controlled or limited
_source.learnerexamples_text: Children are allowed much more freedom these days.; I felt such a sense of freedom, up in the hills alone.; At university, you have the freedom to do what you want.; Everyone should be allowed freedom of choice.; [The car] gives some freedom of choice: I can move quick[ly] from one place to another, I don't waste time on public transport and in winter [it] protects me from [the] cold and rain.

_source.definition_text: a situation in which you are not suffering because of something unpleasant or harmful
_source.learnerexamples_text: freedom from fear/poverty; Despite our modern medicine and the progress it has made within the last century, there is no guarantee of freedom from disease or freedom from illness.

_source.definition_text: without being controlled or limited
_source.learnerexamples_text: For the first time in months she could move freely.; Exotic foods are freely available in supermarkets.; She freely admits that she was partly to blame.; We encourage the victims to talk freely about their experiences.; We have always been able to speak freely with each other and this letter is no exception.

_source.definition_text: If something freezes or is frozen, it becomes hard and solid because it is very cold.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Water freezes at a temperature of 0°C.; The ground had frozen hard/solid.; When the lake freezes (over), we can go skating on it.; Sometimes the roads [ar]e frozen and the cars cannot pass.

_source.definition_text: to make food last a long time by making it very cold and hard
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll freeze any food that's left over.; Most soups freeze well.

_source.definition_text: to feel very cold
_source.learnerexamples_text: Without a sleeping bag, you would freeze to death out there on the mountainside.; The weather is warm in the summer but when the winter comes... get ready to freeze!

_source.definition_text: to suddenly stop moving, especially because you are frightened
_source.learnerexamples_text: She saw someone outside the window and froze.; I froze with terror.

_source.definition_text: a large container operated by electricity in which food can be frozen and stored
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's some ice cream in the freezer.; It is about that beautiful vase you had on the freezer in the kitchen.

_source.definition_text: extremely cold
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's absolutely freezing in here - can I close the window?; They survived for four hours in the freezing water.; After walking through the snow, my feet were freezing.; At the moment, I am here in England and it is absolutely freezing.

_source.definition_text: happening often
_source.learnerexamples_text: a frequent visitor to the US; The most frequent cause of death is heart attack.; I am a frequent visitor to your cinema and I really like the films you show.

_source.definition_text: when you are so excited, nervous, or anxious that you cannot control what you are doing
_source.learnerexamples_text: She hit him in a frenzy of rage.; For the next thirty-two hours, a frenzy took hold of the house.

_source.definition_text: Fresh food has been produced or collected recently and has not been frozen, dried, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: fresh fruit/vegetables/fish/bread ; Sometimes they go to the sea to get really fresh fish.

_source.definition_text: often
_source.learnerexamples_text: frequently asked questions; I see him quite frequently.; The buses run less/more frequently at certain times.; I met a beautiful girl and now we are seeing each other frequently, about twice a week.

_source.definition_text: new or different from what was there before
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're looking for fresh ideas.; We need to take a fresh look at the problem.; They decided to move abroad and make a fresh start.; In fact, it was the chance of a new life, the opportunity to make a fresh start.

_source.definition_text: smelling clean or feeling pleasantly cool
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fresh smell/breeze ; The water was wonderfully fresh.

_source.definition_text: air outside buildings or away from the city that is clean and cool
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's go outside and get some fresh air.; I think [it] would be better [to] go to the south east to the countryside and have a nice relaxing time with lots of fresh air.

_source.definition_text: Fresh skin looks healthy.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fresh complexion; Her eyes were blue and she had a beautiful fresh complexion.

_source.definition_text: recently made, done, arrived, etc., and especially not yet changed by time
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was a fresh fall of snow during the night.; Some people like the smell of fresh paint, but I don't.; The events of last year are still fresh in people's minds.; I don't know if it is the most embar[r]assing moment of my life, but it is still fresh in my memory and I get embar[r]assed every time I think of it.

_source.definition_text: having a lot of energy and not feeling tired
_source.learnerexamples_text: We got up the next day feeling fresh and relaxed.; Before the test, you should have your breakfast with a cup of coffee to make yourself feel fresh.

_source.definition_text: water from lakes, rivers, etc. that has no salt in it
_source.learnerexamples_text: These fish live in fresh water.; You find stunning white beaches, clear, fresh water lakes, isolated tropic islands, reef, rainforests, buzzing cities, challenging mountain range, bush, outback - and the desert.

_source.definition_text: someone or something that is new, different, and exciting
_source.searchterms_text: a breath of fresh air;breath of fresh air;fresh;fresher;freshest
_source.learnerexamples_text: Having Eve around has been a breath of fresh air.; The final suggestion is focused on building a leisure centre. Should this be everything the Town Council has promised, it will bring a breath of fresh air.

_source.definition_text: disagreement or dislike caused by people having different opinions
_source.learnerexamples_text: There’s less friction in relationships when you use teamwork.; Money spen[t] on shopping can also be the cause of friction or arguments between husbands and wives.

_source.definition_text: the day of the week after Thursday and before Saturday
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you want to go to the theatre on Friday?; I love Fridays because I leave work early.; The class is on Friday, from 2 to 4 p.m.

_source.definition_text: a large container that uses electricity to keep food cold
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't forget to put the milk back in the fridge.; I think they are in the kitchen, near the fridge.

_source.definition_text: cooked in hot oil or fat
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fried egg; My favourite food is fried pork.

_source.definition_text: someone who you know well and like
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's my best/closest friend - we've known each other since we were five.; He's a family friend/friend of the family.; This restaurant was recommended to me by a friend of mine.; Bob is an old friend of mine.; [At the] weekend she is free [so] she goes out with friends.

_source.definition_text: a person you write to on an Internet site
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've just added Adam as a friend on Facebook.

_source.definition_text: to begin to know and like someone
_source.searchterms_text: friend;friends;make friends (with sb);make friends with sb
_source.learnerexamples_text: He finds it difficult to make friends.; He's made friends with a boy in his class called Alex.; Although I didn't know anyone in this club, I immediately made friends with Maria and Rosaria.

_source.definition_text: to know and like someone
_source.searchterms_text: be friends (with sb);be friends with sb;friend;friends
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've been friends with Jo for years.; He was really happy too, so we began to be friends.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being friendly
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was the friendliness of the people that struck me.; Your description of the people, their everyday life, their characters and their friendliness reflects that you really had an excellent time here.

_source.definition_text: behaving in a pleasant, kind way towards someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: a friendly face/smile; Our neighbours have always been very friendly to/towards us.; I think I'd prefer a pen-friend from America, because they are very friendly, aren't they?

_source.definition_text: to know and like someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her brother is quite friendly with my brother.; The teacher is friendly with the students, but a bit [strict] at the same time.

_source.definition_text: when two people are friends
_source.learnerexamples_text: a close friendship; I value her friendship above anything else.; I hope our friendship will become stronger and maybe he should become my boyfriend!

_source.definition_text: a sudden feeling of shock and fear
_source.learnerexamples_text: That dog gave me a terrible fright.;  She screamed in fright when she saw him.; She suddenly realised she was being followed, so, speechless with fright, began to stride along back to her car.

_source.definition_text: to make someone feel fear
_source.learnerexamples_text: He frightens me when he drives so fast.; The noise frightened me to death.; I have no interest in lizards. Whatever their characters are, their appearance always frightens me.

_source.definition_text: making you feel fear
_source.learnerexamples_text: a frightening thought; a frightening film; I like frightening films, so I'm going to buy it.

_source.definition_text: feeling fear or worry
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you frightened of spiders?; I was frightened (that) you would fall.; She gets frightened when he shouts at her.; The policewoman found a frightened child in the hut.; We were both frightened and didn't know what to do.

_source.definition_text: the outside edge of an area, group, or subject and not the main part
_source.learnerexamples_text: the southern fringe of the city; the radical fringe of the party; He is on the fringe of society.

_source.definition_text: hair that is cut short and straight at the top of someone's face
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her fringe was nearly in her eyes.; She had [a] long fringe over her forehead that almost covered her pale blue eyes.

_source.definition_text: a small, green animal with long back legs for jumping that lives in or near water
_source.learnerexamples_text: The frogs down at the lake were making a lot of noise.; That was my favourite place, because there were ducks, some frogs, and many butterflies as well as birds.

_source.definition_text: not belonging to the main part of a group, activity, or subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: fringe politics/theatre ; Unfortunately it seems to have won "new" currency in view of the latest events directed against foreigners, minorities and fringe groups.

_source.definition_text: used to show the origin of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Where are you from?" "I'm from Italy."; I come from Spain.; I wonder who this card is from.; She comes from Poland.

_source.definition_text: used to show the place where someone or something starts
_source.learnerexamples_text: What time does the flight from Amsterdam arrive?; The wind is coming from the north.; She sent me a postcard from Majorca.; She took her hairbrush from her handbag and began to brush her hair.; So did you really walk all the way from Bond Street?

_source.definition_text: used to show the time when something starts or the time when it was made or first existed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Drinks will be served from seven o'clock.; The price of petrol will rise by 5p a gallon from tomorrow.; Most of the paintings in this room date from the seventeenth century.; The museum is open from 9.30 to 6.00 Tuesday to Sunday.; It's from 5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.

_source.definition_text: used to show the distance between two places
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's about two kilometres from the airport to your hotel.; We're about a mile from home.; I[t']s about 3 kilometres from the city centre.

_source.definition_text: used to show the material of which something is made
_source.learnerexamples_text: juice made from oranges and mangoes; The present I love[d] the most was a cute little cat that [is] made from glass.

_source.definition_text: used when you are saying how similar or different two things, people or places are
_source.learnerexamples_text: University is very different from school.; His opinion could hardly be more different from mine.; The two sisters are so similar that it's almost impossible to tell one from the other.; His clothes are very different from everyone else['s].

_source.definition_text: used to show the cause of something or the reason why something happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was rushed to hospital but died from his injuries.; You could tell she wasn't lying from the fear in her voice.; Many people have died from car accidents.

_source.definition_text: used to show a change in the state of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Things went from bad to worse.; She has been promoted from manager to director.; On the other hand the number of animals living in freedom, for example the number of tigers, elephants and lions in Africa or Asia, is decreasing more and more, because their living conditions have gone from bad to worse.

_source.definition_text: used to show the position of something in comparison with other things, or the point of view of someone when considering a matter or problem
_source.learnerexamples_text: From the restaurant there is a beautiful view of Siena.; She was talking from her own experience of the problem.; From our point of view, we do not see how these changes will benefit the company.; The job was hard, but from my point of view, it was worth [it].

_source.definition_text: If something moves from side to side, it moves from left to right and back again repeatedly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: swinging from side to side; I began to understand it when I went [to] Kenya in 1986, because I had the wonderful chance to look at the animals in their natural [surroundings], without being in a cage, walking nervously from side to side.

_source.definition_text: used to show what someone is not allowed to do or know, or what has been stopped happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's been banned from driving for six months.; For many years, the truth was kept from the public.; Wouldn't it be better if cars were banned from the Central Business District in order to avoid traffic jams and stress[?]

_source.base_text: a week/six months/ten years, etc. from now
_source.definition_text: a week/six months/ten years, etc. after the time when you are speaking
_source.searchterms_text: a week/six months/ten years etc from now;a week/six months/ten years, etc. from now;from;week/six months/ten years, etc. from now
_source.learnerexamples_text: Who knows what we'll all be doing five years from now?; Have you ever thought about what clothes will look like in 100 years from now?

_source.definition_text: sometimes but not often
_source.learnerexamples_text: From time to time I still think of her.; I wash the dishes from time to time (I sometimes try to avoid this unpleasant duty) and clean our house.

_source.definition_text: starting then, that day, etc. and continuing into the future
_source.searchterms_text: from;from then/that day etc on;from then/that day, etc. on
_source.learnerexamples_text: From then on, he began to keep all her letters and cards.; They were good friends from that day on.; It happened like a miracle, suddenly I could speak quite well and I had lots of friends and from then on, I had a very nice time and I lived the best experience I've ever live[d] in my short life.

_source.definition_text: from the beginning of something to its end
_source.learnerexamples_text: I enjoyed the film from start to finish.; I found out that the service itself should last at least one and half hour[s] from start to finish.

_source.definition_text: completely
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've searched the house from top to bottom and still can't find it.; Very often we can see someone in black, from top to bottom, or in white.

_source.definition_text: If you do something from scratch, you do it from the beginning.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We didn't have any furniture of our own so we had to start from scratch.; That means you don't have to start from scratch with your teacher.

_source.definition_text: the part of something that is furthest forward
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was standing right at the front.; Do you want to sit in the front, next to me?; Thomas plays in the front. He makes nearly all the goals [for] our team.

_source.definition_text: the side of something that is most important or most often seen because it faces forward
_source.learnerexamples_text: The front of the museum is very impressive.; You need to write the address clearly on the front of the envelope.; There was coffee on the front of his shirt.; If you want to come with me, call me or come [to] the front of the Rialto [at] 8:45 am - I will be there.

_source.definition_text: close to the front part of something, or where someone can see or hear you
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's parking space in front of the hotel.; Please don't use bad language in front of the children.; There are four villas in front of our building.

_source.definition_text: further forward than someone or something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car in front suddenly stopped and I went into the back of it.; She started talking to the man in front of her.; As the concert finished, I heard someone call my name. I beli[e]ved it was my imagination or perhaps a dream because I couldn't see anyone in front, behind or opposite me.

_source.definition_text: in or at the front of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: the front door/garden; the front page of the newspaper; One of his front teeth is missing.; I'd like two seats in the front row.; So let's meet at the front gate, at 9:15 pm.

_source.definition_text: a line or border between two countries
_source.learnerexamples_text: They placed guards on the frontier.; He took it and escaped towards the German frontier.

_source.definition_text: with the back part of something where the front should be
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've got your trousers on back to front.; Therefore, the government needs to cut expenditure and as a result of this, health faciliti[es] will only be accessible for rich people. Then we are back to front.

_source.definition_text: the limits of what is known or what has been done before in an area of knowledge or activity
_source.searchterms_text: frontier;frontiers;frontiers of sth;the frontiers of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: the frontiers of science and technology; Introduction: throughout history, scientists, artists and other people tried hard to push back the frontiers of knowledge, in order to succeed in making [or] creating something that all humankind will ben[e]fit from somehow.

_source.definition_text: a thin, white layer of ice that forms on surfaces at night when it is very cold, or a time when the temperature is very cold and water freezes
_source.learnerexamples_text: When I woke up this morning the ground was covered with frost.; There was a frost last night.; There were a lot of hard frosts that winter.; Thirdly, you do not have to worry about rain, wind, frost or other bad weather conditions.

_source.definition_text: to make your face show that you are annoyed or worried by moving your eyebrows
_source.learnerexamples_text: She frowned when I mentioned his name. ; She looked at him and frowned, strange, but he smiled back.

_source.definition_text: to think that something is wrong and that you should not do it
_source.learnerexamples_text: Smoking is frowned upon in many public places. ; Talking being very often frowned upon in the Zen gardens, consequently it is peaceful and so you can fully relax and completely empty your head.

_source.definition_text: Frozen food has been made so that it will last a long time by freezing.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We don't have any fresh vegetables, only frozen peas.; Nowadays, we do not need anymore to spend hours cooking, we just put some frozen food in the microwave, and in a few minutes our meal is ready.

_source.definition_text: the expression on your face when you frown
_source.learnerexamples_text: He looked at me with a puzzled frown. ; If you are truly devoted to your health, logic thus dictates that you will be sitting at the dinner table with an empty plate - and certainly a frown on your face.

_source.definition_text: If a person, or a part of their body is frozen, they are very cold.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is there any heating in here? I'm frozen!; After walking through the snow, my feet were frozen stiff.; I was frozen, [but] after a second I had a big silly smile on my face.

_source.definition_text: turned into ice
_source.learnerexamples_text: They skated over the frozen lake.

_source.definition_text: something such as an apple or orange that grows on a tree or a bush, contains seeds, and can be eaten as food
_source.learnerexamples_text: fresh fruit; dried fruit; fruit juice; I eat three or four pieces of fruit a day.; I like exotic fruit, like mangoes and papayas.

_source.definition_text: If something that someone does bears fruit, it produces successful results.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our decision is just beginning to bear fruit.;  Although a new hotel and conference centre would greatly improve the image of our town, I consider it a costly investment that might not bear fruit.

_source.definition_text: the good result of someone's work or actions
_source.searchterms_text: fruit;fruit(s) of sth;fruits;the fruit(s) of sth;the fruits of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: This book is the fruit of 15 years' research.; People work very hard to obtain their salaries or wages, so after earning their salaries they need to enjoy the fruits of their hard labour and shopping is one way of doing that.

_source.definition_text: annoyed because things are not happening in the way that you want, or in the way that they should
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm very frustrated at/with my lack of progress.; Fans are frustrated by their lack of success this season.; What, however, made us very frustrated was that there was no opportunity for us to take an exam at the end of this month.

_source.definition_text: producing good or useful results
