_source.learnerexamples_text: There is general concern about rising crime rates.; There seems to be general agreement on this matter.; The decision has already been made by general agreement.

_source.definition_text: not detailed, but including the most basic or necessary information
_source.learnerexamples_text: These leaflets contain some general information about the school.; It's a very general description.; I've got a general idea of how it works.; By seeing the film, we are able to understand the general idea of the story.

_source.definition_text: including a lot of things or subjects and not limited to only one or a few
_source.learnerexamples_text: general knowledge ; To improve the general knowledge of the students, it might be a good idea to offer more newspapers than magazines.

_source.definition_text: usually, or in most situations
_source.learnerexamples_text: In general, men are taller than women.; In general, the weather here stays sunny.; In general, when anybody in my country [has a] wedding, the families invite all fri[e]nds and n[eighbours] to the wedding.

_source.definition_text: considering the whole of someone or something, and not just a particular part of them
_source.learnerexamples_text: So, apart from the bad ankle, how are you in general?; I think that I, as well as people in general, would have been more depressed if we didn't have light.

_source.definition_text: when someone says something very basic that is often true but not always true
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a sweeping generalization to say that girls read more than boys.; As the organizer of the International Student's Sports Club, I feel inclined to report from [my] own experience that such a generalisation is not appropriate.

_source.definition_text: to say something very basic that is often true but not always true
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can't generalize about a continent as varied as Europe.; Anyway, even though it's hard to generalise, it seems clear that people don't want to work, and want to enjoy themselves without working.

_source.definition_text: usually, or in most situations
_source.learnerexamples_text: I generally wake up early.; I generally prefer reading newspapers, but I don't dislike books.

_source.definition_text: considering the whole of someone or something, and not just a particular part of them
_source.learnerexamples_text: My health is generally very good.; Generally, Athens has a lot of things to do.

_source.definition_text: by most people, or to most people
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is generally believed to be their best player.; It is generally acknowledged that it depends on the zoo because sometimes the animals are loved and sometimes hated.

_source.definition_text: to cause something to exist
_source.learnerexamples_text: The new development will generate 1500 new jobs.; This film has generated a lot of interest.; Football generates every kind of emotion: happiness, sadness, and above all passion.

_source.definition_text: to produce energy
_source.learnerexamples_text: The wind farm may be able to generate enough electricity for 2000 homes.; In France, for instance, more than three-quarters of [all] electricity is generated from nuclear power.

_source.definition_text: all the people in a society or family who are approximately the same age
_source.learnerexamples_text: the older/younger generation; This is the story of three generations of women.; Some people say that cell phones are a bad influence on the younger generation.

_source.definition_text: a period of about 25 to 30 years, the time it takes for children to become adults and take the place of their parents in society
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our family has lived in this village for generations.; A generation ago, home computers were almost unknown.; Salzburg is a beautiful medieval town - it has got a wonderful cathedral, which was built by entire generations of Italian artisans.

_source.definition_text: the production of energy in a particular form
_source.learnerexamples_text: electricity generation from wind and wave power; [T]he energy generation crisis Brazil is having to deal with [is well known].

_source.definition_text: a product when it is at a particular stage of development
_source.learnerexamples_text: a new generation of computers; I can sum up the most important things that changed my li[f]e are the telephone, the computer, the portable phone and of course [the] new generation of television.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being generous
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her friends take advantage of her generosity.; Anna, thank you again for your generosity.

_source.definition_text: larger than usual or than expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: a generous discount for students; a generous portion; To sum up, I must correct the conclusion in your article, as the event did come up to the organisers' expectations, [rais]ing a generous amount of money to donate to the hospital.

_source.definition_text: willing to give other people money, help, kindness, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's been very generous with her time.; I like her because she is a generous, kindly, interesting person.

_source.definition_text: in a generous way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please give generously to Children in Need.; I can't think of any other person who opens her house so generously as you do!

_source.definition_text: relating to genes
_source.learnerexamples_text: a rare genetic disorder ;  genetic research ; Mendel thought that basically it is the genetic material which is responsible for the future development of a child.

_source.definition_text: having had some of the genes changed by a scientific process
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are opposed to genetically modified food.; Despite the fact that the European Union prohibited genetically modified products in its countries, we are still using pesticides, causing pollution and food poisoning.

_source.definition_text: the scientific study of the parts of cells which control particular characteristics (genes)
_source.learnerexamples_text: Next year, I'll be studying genetics.; We use technology in order to save human live[s] and to explore strange new worlds, such as genetics.

_source.definition_text: someone who is extremely intelligent or extremely good at doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Einstein was a genius. ; And what about Mozart - poor little genius!

_source.definition_text: the quality of being extremely intelligent or extremely good at doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Einstein's genius ; Nothing is more common than unrewarded genius and mis[used] talents.

_source.definition_text: kind, calm and careful not to upset or hurt anyone
_source.learnerexamples_text: My mother was such a gentle, loving person.; Mani is very kind and gentle.

_source.definition_text: not violent, severe or strong
_source.learnerexamples_text: gentle exercise ; a gentle breeze; The weather is sunny, the gentle breeze is pure and fresh.

_source.definition_text: A gentle slope or climb is not steep.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was a fairly gentle climb to the summit.; THE TOUR Trained guides lead people across gentle slopes towards thick woods displaying a wide variety of birds and animal life.

_source.definition_text: a polite word for 'man'
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ladies and gentlemen, the show is about to begin.; So she walked up on the stage and started speaking steadily into the microphone: "Ladies and gentlemen...." This is how the story ended.

_source.definition_text: calmly, kindly or softly
_source.learnerexamples_text: He held the baby gently in his arms.; Now I am older and I speak to my mother very gently.

_source.definition_text: If a person or their feelings are genuine, they are sincere and honest.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They showed genuine sympathy for our situation.; On the other hand, it is well known in environmental management that strategies that work via [the] people's purse are often the only way to motivate people who have little genuine interest in environmental problems (or just too many other concerns).

_source.definition_text: If something is genuine, it is really what it seems to be.
_source.learnerexamples_text: genuine leather; The bicycle is [a] genuine Shimano bicycle.

_source.definition_text: in a genuine or sincere way
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm genuinely sorry for the extra work this has caused.; We are all genuinely interested in English literature.

_source.definition_text: the study of the physical surface of the Earth and all regions of the world
_source.learnerexamples_text: a degree in geography and economics; I left my geography book at your house yesterday.

_source.definition_text: the study of rocks and soil and the physical structure of the Earth
_source.learnerexamples_text: a book about geology; I have graduated from school and I am now studying geology at the University of Greece.

_source.definition_text: the beginning of something
_source.searchterms_text: germ;germ of sth;germs;the germ of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: the germ of a brilliant idea ; Going back to the scene at More's home, we now understand why this is the germ of the subsequent development of the play.

_source.definition_text: a very small living thing that causes disease
_source.learnerexamples_text: Wash your hands before cooking so that you don't spread germs. ; I am more careful with cleaning up and taking care of my baby. It was amazing the way they spoke about germs and dust.

_source.definition_text: A gerund is a noun made from the form of a verb that ends with -ing, for example 'fishing' in 'John loves fishing.'
_source.learnerexamples_text: We learned about gerunds today.

_source.definition_text: a movement you make with your hand, arm, or head to express what you are thinking or feeling
_source.learnerexamples_text: He made a rude gesture at the crowd. ; Review - The Body Speaks [...] In the second part, you are taught how to read the gestures, voice, [and] hesitations, and analyse them.

_source.definition_text: something you do to show people how you feel about a person or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: It would be a nice gesture to invite her to dinner. ; Dear Sir, I am the secretary of the Student Committee in Bringtown College and I am writing to thank you for your kind gesture [in] inviting me to the opening of the new Arts Centre.

_source.definition_text: to point at something or express something using your hand, arm, or head
_source.learnerexamples_text: He gestured towards the window. ; She gestured to the hall's expensive Persian carpets and the extensive collection of French Impressionists hanging on the walls.

_source.definition_text: to obtain or buy something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll get some bread on the way home.; Did you get the tickets for the concert?; We could get the afternoon ticket.

_source.definition_text: to receive or be given something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got some lovely presents on my birthday.; I got a letter from Stefano.; Did you get my email?; I got your note.

_source.definition_text: to reach or arrive at a particular place
_source.searchterms_text: get;get here/there/home/to work etc;get here/there/home/to work, etc.;gets;getting;got;gotten
_source.learnerexamples_text: We got home later than usual.; I didn't get to work till nine o'clock.; I had a good time at your house last night but when I got home I realized I had forg[o]tten my bag!

_source.definition_text: to travel somewhere in a bus, train, taxi or other vehicle
_source.searchterms_text: get;get a bus/train/taxi etc;get a bus/train/taxi, etc.;gets;getting;got;gotten
_source.learnerexamples_text: Shall we get a taxi to the station?; You can get the train.

_source.definition_text: to go somewhere and bring back someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Wait here while I get the car.; I'll go and get Sophie from the station.; Could you get me my keys from upstairs?; I decided [to] go on with my plan and get my father's car.

_source.definition_text: to begin a legal relationship with someone as their husband or wife
_source.learnerexamples_text: They got married in April.; She was going to get married, and I was invited to the wedding.

_source.definition_text: to become ill or develop an illness
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm getting another cold.; I was angry, and I got a cold!

_source.definition_text: to start to be cold/ill/late, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your coffee's getting cold.; It's getting late.; It's getting late so I should finish now.

_source.definition_text: to become more ill, unpleasant, difficult, severe, etc. than before
_source.learnerexamples_text: My cold seems to be getting worse.; If the rain gets any worse, we'll have to stop walking.; I thought, it couldn't get worse.

_source.definition_text: to have something done to you. This is sometimes used instead of the usual passive structure.
_source.searchterms_text: get;get caught/killed/told off etc;get caught/killed/told off, etc.;gets;getting;got;gotten
_source.learnerexamples_text: He got killed in the war.; She got told off in class for not paying attention.; I got bitten during the walk.; Two weeks ago many people at school got injured because of an explosion, so a TV company came to film what the school is like now ...

_source.definition_text: to produce an answer or result that is not correct, or to say or write something that is not correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got most of the answers wrong.; The newspapers got the story completely wrong.

_source.definition_text: to do a task, or to arrange for someone to do a task for you
_source.searchterms_text: get;get sth painted/repaired etc;get sth painted/repaired, etc.;gets;getting;got;gotten
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you get the kids dressed?; I need to get my hair cut.; You must get that form sent off.; First I have to go to the doctor and then I have to get my teeth checked by the dentist.

_source.definition_text: to contact someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please get in touch if you ever come back to Madrid.; Get in touch soon.

_source.definition_text: to move to a different place or into a different position
_source.learnerexamples_text: I saw her getting into his car.; They [said] that I got into a car by myself (they thought that I had believed the story).

_source.definition_text: to deal with or answer a ringing telephone, a knock on the door, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you get the phone, Al?; Someone's at the door - could you get it?

_source.definition_text: to spend time with someone or something so that you gradually learn more about them
_source.searchterms_text: get;get to know sb/sth;get to know sb/sth ;gets;getting;got;gotten
_source.learnerexamples_text: The first couple of meetings are for the doctor and patient to get to know each other.; I'll need a few weeks to get to know the system.; I hope you can come here and get to know him.

_source.definition_text: to throw something away or give something to someone because you no longer want it
_source.learnerexamples_text: We must get rid of some of those old books.; Do you think I'd better get rid of the sofa and place the bookshelf [there]?

_source.definition_text: to end something unpleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't seem to get rid of this headache.; [The] first step is to get rid of smoking.

_source.definition_text: to make something happen, or make someone or something do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't get my computer to work!; I'll get Ben to fix your bike.; We must get the councillors to change their minds.

_source.definition_text: to annoy someone, especially by doing something again and again
_source.learnerexamples_text: If we spend too much time together, we end up getting on each other's nerves.; Sometimes, receiving a phone call can disturb very important events in [a person's] life, but [it] also get[s] on people's nerves when you use it in a public place like a train...

_source.definition_text: to develop an opinion about a situation because of something that you notice
_source.searchterms_text: get;get the feeling/idea/impression etc;get the feeling/idea/impression, etc.;gets;getting;got;gotten
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got the feeling that she was quite angry about the situation.; I disagree with some points you mentioned and would like to share the impression I got from that popular holiday report during my two-week trip.

_source.definition_text: to have the chance to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I never got to meet her.; I did get to meet a musician, a singer named Anouk.

_source.definition_text: to understand or hear something
_source.learnerexamples_text: That joke that he told - did you get it?

_source.definition_text: to make an effort to control your emotions and behave more calmly
_source.searchterms_text: get;get a grip (on yourself);get a grip on yourself;gets;getting;got;gotten
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stop panicking and get a grip on yourself!; The best thing to do was to talk to people who were not doing the test rather than building up my anxiety. However, I did not do this and it almost resulted in a disaster, but I got a grip on myself and just barely passed.

_source.definition_text: to annoy someone, especially by doing something again and again
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please stop making that noise! It really gets on my nerves.; My neighbour is always quarrel[l]ing with his wife. It['s] getting on my nerves!

_source.definition_text: to make someone leave
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was useless at her job so we had to get rid of her.; Improving your English on your own (or a self-guide [on] how to get rid of your English teacher!)

_source.definition_text: to make sure that you completely understand a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let me get this straight - am I paying for this?; Next time you should try to get your facts straight.

_source.definition_text: to organize your activities so that you can make progress
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's so disorganized - I wish she'd get her act together.; He was determined to get his act together and try to find a solution to his problem.

_source.definition_text: If something gets you nowhere, it does not help you to succeed.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Bad manners will get you nowhere.; As this is a loophole in [the] law system, it's creating a conflict between house-owners and squatters and getting them nowhere.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone about something that you have been worried or angry about for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tell me what's wrong - you'll feel better if you get it off your chest.; Chris is always caring and lends you his ear if there's something you need to get off your chest.

_source.definition_text: to do something unpleasant to someone because they have done something unpleasant to you
_source.searchterms_text: get;get your own back (on sb);get your own back on sb;gets;getting;got;gotten
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got my own back by putting a frog in her bed.; There, Kingshaw has the opportunity to get his own back by pushing Hooper down the wall, but he doesn't dare because he is not as cruel as Hooper.

_source.definition_text: to do something difficult or unpleasant as soon as you can so that you do not have to worry about it any more
_source.searchterms_text: get;get sth over (and done) with;get sth over and done with;gets;getting;got;gotten
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got all my apologies over and done with at the beginning of the meeting.; Not to mention that he knew that he had to get his degree over and done with before he started making serious decisions.

_source.definition_text: used when you do not want someone to think that you do not like someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't get me wrong, I like her, but she can be very annoying.; Don't get me wrong, I love my aunts, I really do, but not as houseguests.

_source.definition_text: to hurry
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're leaving in five minutes, so get moving!; "Oh, look at the time, we must get moving!"

_source.definition_text: to hurry
_source.learnerexamples_text: Come on, get a move on!; 'All the lights will be switched off in 28 minut[e]s, so I have to get a move on' I said to myself, as I started to write on a new piece of paper.

_source.definition_text: to become difficult to control
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was the end of term and the children were getting a little out of hand.; A few solutions can prevent this problem from getting out of hand.

_source.definition_text: to learn how to do something, especially if it is not obvious or simple
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've never used one of these before. - Don't worry, you'll soon get the hang of it.; It was quite hard to get the hang of it, as I didn't have any knowledge of English.

_source.definition_text: to begin
_source.learnerexamples_text: The film festival gets underway on 11th July.

_source.definition_text: used to say that someone understands a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Oh right, I get the picture.; If you use a photograph though, you can be sure that everyone will get the picture (pun intended) and pro[b]ably remember the person you're talking about next time they see him.

_source.base_text: get across sth or get sth across
_source.definition_text: to manage to make someone understand or believe something
_source.searchterms_text: get;get across sth or get sth across
_source.learnerexamples_text: We tried to get our point across, but he just wouldn't listen.; This is the message that we want to get across to the public.; I am going to get across several ideas to improve the look of our town.

_source.definition_text: If you ask someone what they are getting at, you are asking them what they really mean.
_source.searchterms_text: be getting at sth;be getting at sth ;get
_source.learnerexamples_text: What do you think the poet is getting at in these lines?; The point I'm getting at is that you have to understand that young people look at sport like school: it's something you do that makes you feel good afterwards and computer games are something you do when you have some spare time.

_source.definition_text: to be able to reach or get something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've put the cake on a high shelf where the kids can't get at it.

_source.definition_text: to leave or escape from a place or person, often when it is difficult to do this
_source.learnerexamples_text: We walked to the next beach to get away from the crowds.; [A] bicycle is a means of making new friends, and getting away from [your] daily routine.

_source.definition_text: to succeed in not being criticized or punished for something
_source.searchterms_text: get;get away with sth;get away with sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: If I thought I could get away with it, I wouldn't pay any tax at all.; When the police arrived, the criminals had already disappeared: they got away with this murder.

_source.definition_text: to go somewhere to have a holiday, often because you need to rest
_source.learnerexamples_text: I just need to get away for a few days.; I spent a wonderful week in your flat. I've enjoyed the peace of getting away, you know I needed it.

_source.definition_text: to return to a place after you have been somewhere else
_source.learnerexamples_text: When we got back to the hotel, Ann had already left.; If you get back in time, you can come with us.; Will call you when I get back.

_source.base_text: get back sth or get sth back
_source.definition_text: to be given something again that you had before
_source.searchterms_text: get;get back sth or get sth back
_source.learnerexamples_text: He went next door to get his ball back.; Don't lend him money, you'll never get it back.; He hoped that he would get back his suitcase.

_source.definition_text: to talk to someone, usually on the telephone, to give them some information they have asked for or because you were not able to speak to them before
_source.learnerexamples_text: I need to get back to Gary about his new computer.; I am awfully sorry for having been slow in getting back to you.

_source.definition_text: to make someone feel unhappy
_source.learnerexamples_text: All this uncertainty is really getting me down.; But when I had finally reached the bottom of the valley seeing the whole ski group staring at me, the embarras[s]ment got me down.

_source.definition_text: to start doing something seriously and with a lot of attention and effort
_source.learnerexamples_text: Before we get down to business, I'd like to thank you all for coming today.; Let's get down to business!

_source.definition_text: to succeed in entering a place, especially a building
_source.learnerexamples_text: They must have got in through the bathroom window.; First of all there was queue [of] about 350 metres to get in and everybody was very impa[t]ient.

_source.definition_text: to arrive at a place at a particular time
_source.learnerexamples_text: My flight gets in at 9.45 p.m.; When does Elaine get in?

_source.definition_text: to succeed in being chosen or elected
_source.learnerexamples_text: He wanted to go to Cambridge but he didn't get in.; I need to pass PET CAMBRIDGE exam to get in, [and] my degree course starts this Septem[b]er.

_source.definition_text: to become interested in an activity or subject, or start being involved in an activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: How did you get into journalism?; Taking everything into account, I truly believe that "Ethnos" is the most suitable newspaper to be placed in the library [...] for every student who would like to learn Greek deeply and get into the Greek culture and civilisation.

_source.definition_text: to succeed in being chosen or elected
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's got into Oxford.; I'm a professional player and maybe I could get into the team of this club.

_source.definition_text: to go onto a bus, train, aircraft or boat
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think we got on the wrong bus.; Last Saturday I was running to get on the bus, but my schoolbag was open and the diary fell [out].

_source.definition_text: to leave a bus, train, aircraft or boat
_source.learnerexamples_text: We should get off at the next stop.; Then get off the bus in Obdland Village [and] walk up the road.

_source.definition_text: to manage or deal with a situation, especially successfully
_source.learnerexamples_text: How are you getting on in your new flat?; Please let me know how you [are] getting on in your new school.

_source.definition_text: to have a good relationship
_source.learnerexamples_text: He doesn't get on with his daughter.; I get on well with most of her friends.; I couldn't get on with my teacher.

_source.definition_text: to continue doing something, especially work
_source.learnerexamples_text: Get on with your homework.; I must go and get on with my homework.

_source.definition_text: to leave a closed vehicle, building, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll get out when you stop at the traffic lights.; Suddenly the lights went out and I was there, desper[ately] trying to find a way to get out of the house!

_source.definition_text: to go out to different places and meet people in order to enjoy yourself
_source.learnerexamples_text: She doesn't get out so much now that she's got the baby.; Since Internet, e-mails and mobile phones were invented, fewer people get out and meet friends.

_source.definition_text: to avoid doing something that you do not want to do, especially by giving an excuse
_source.searchterms_text: get;get out of sth/doing sth;get out of sth/doing sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: If I can get out of going to the meeting tonight I will.; I must go to Tokyo on business that Wednesday afternoon. This is a kind of step up for me and I can't get out of it.

_source.definition_text: to escape from or leave a place, or to help someone do this
_source.learnerexamples_text: I left the door open and the cat got out.; They got the hostages out from the rebel base without injury.; "Don't panic, now, Lorraine", he answered me. "He may be a little .... um, eccentric, but I'm sure he'll get us out of here fine."

_source.definition_text: to get better after an illness, or feel better after something or someone has made you unhappy
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's still getting over the flu.; It took her months to get over the shock of Richard leaving.; First of all, she had had to get over the deaths of three close relatives in the last three years.

_source.definition_text: to be very shocked or surprised about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't get over how different you look with short hair.; I can't get over how quickly you wrote to me.

_source.definition_text: to do something that you have intended to do for a long time
_source.searchterms_text: get;get round to sth;get round to sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: I still haven't got round to fixing that tap.; I'm sorry I haven't written to you earlier. I had my exams at the Institute so I just couldn't get round to this.

_source.definition_text: to finish doing or using something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We got through a whole jar of coffee last week.

_source.definition_text: to succeed in an examination or competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: She got through her exams without too much trouble.; I know you want to get through your exams.

_source.definition_text: You ask where people or things have got to when they have not arrived or are not where you expect them to be and you want to know where they are.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I wonder where my glasses have got to.; Where's Annabel got to? She should be here by now.

_source.definition_text: to deal with a difficult or unpleasant experience, or to help someone do this
_source.searchterms_text: get;get (sb) through sth;get sb through sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't know how I got through the first couple of months after Andy's death.; We'll get you through this, Karen.; You see, my friend, how li[f]e can be a bit difficult but people manage to get through it.

_source.definition_text: to succeed in making someone understand or believe something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I just don't seem to be able to get through to him these days.; He should make the lesson interesting and should manage to get through to children.

_source.definition_text: to make someone feel upset or angry
_source.learnerexamples_text: I know he's annoying but you shouldn't let him get to you.; But they are overprotective and it gets to me very much.

_source.definition_text: to meet in order to do something or spend time together
_source.learnerexamples_text: A few of us are getting together next week for a drink.; During [a] Chinese wedding cer[e]mony, new couples wear traditional clothes and hold a party for friends and families getting together.

_source.definition_text: to stand up
_source.learnerexamples_text: The whole audience got up and started clapping.; When I got up on my feet again I reached out my arm to get a hold on something, but there w[as]n't anything to hold on to.

_source.definition_text: to wake up and get out of bed, or make someone do this
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had to get up at five o'clock this morning.; Could you get the kids up?; My friend gets up early.

_source.definition_text: the spirit of a dead person
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you believe in ghosts?; We saw a horror film. It was about ghosts and vampires!

_source.definition_text: to do something, often something that other people would disapprove of
_source.searchterms_text: get;get up to sth;get up to sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's been getting up to all sorts of mischief lately.; I wonder what those two got up to yesterday?; They were playing happily and they failed to notice me, so I realised that they were not getting up to anything.

_source.definition_text: an imaginary man who is much bigger and stronger than ordinary men
_source.learnerexamples_text: The story is about a friendly giant.; People have always seen him as a "big friendly giant", always ready to help those who are in need.

_source.definition_text: extremely large
_source.learnerexamples_text: a giant spider; Harry Potter fought with the giant snake and he won.

_source.definition_text: a very large and important company or organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: a media/software giant; In less than 15 years Bill Gates has built up his own company from scratch and turned it into a computer giant.

_source.definition_text: a present or something which is given
_source.learnerexamples_text: a wedding gift; The guitar was my father's gift. It is the best gift I've ever received.

_source.definition_text: a natural ability or skill
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has a gift for design.; He understands the thought processes of children quite well, and has a gift for making difficult concepts understandable to youngsters, which obviously means he would be a very good supervisor.

_source.definition_text: A gifted person has a natural ability or is extremely intelligent.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a gifted athlete; a school for gifted children; Roger Federer is a young and extremely gifted tennis player.

_source.definition_text: to laugh in a nervous or silly way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She started giggling and couldn't stop. ; Clara, a thin woman in her late fifties, giggled and her usually so flabby lips trembled as she did so.

_source.definition_text: a large African animal with a very long neck and long legs
_source.learnerexamples_text: Giraffes are the tallest land animals.; Animals like elephants, giraffes and exotic birds must be free. How would you feel living inside a cage?

_source.definition_text: a female child or young woman
_source.learnerexamples_text: Two girls showed us round the classrooms.; We have three children - a boy and two girls.; She has one girl.

_source.definition_text: a group of female friends
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm going out with the girls tonight.;  We w[ere] dancing all night at the club [and] I really enjoyed my time with the girls.

_source.definition_text: a woman or girl who someone is having a romantic relationship with
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've never met his girlfriend.; I danced with my mother and my girlfriend Maria.

_source.definition_text: a female friend of a girl or woman
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's going out with her girlfriends tonight.; I buy clothes once a month, and I usually go shopping with my mother or my girlfriends.

_source.definition_text: to provide someone with something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her parents gave her a car for her birthday.; Can you give me a date for another appointment?; Can you give this book to Andrea?; Yesterday was my birthday and my mother gave me a small dictionary.

_source.definition_text: to put something near someone or in their hand so that they can use it or look at it
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you give me that pen?; He poured a cup of coffee and gave it to Isabel.; We gave the monkeys some bananas to eat and played with them.

_source.definition_text: to telephone someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Why don't you just give him a call?; [If] you have other questions, you can give me a call.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you give Jo a message?; The woman refused to give her name.; She gave me some really useful advice.; I really hope you can give me some advice.

_source.definition_text: to allow someone to have a right or an opportunity
_source.learnerexamples_text: We didn't really give him a chance to explain.; I'll see you at seven o'clock to give you the chance to explain.

_source.definition_text: to have a party
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're always giving parties.; He's a very nice guy, and I would like to give him a surprise party.

_source.definition_text: to produce or cause something
_source.learnerexamples_text: What you said has given me an idea.; The sudden noise gave me quite a shock.; This announcement will give hope to millions of sufferers.; I hope this [will] give you an idea of what I like.

_source.definition_text: to allow someone or something a particular amount of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm nearly ready - just give me a few minutes.; Do you think you would be able to give me 2 hours more on Friday?

_source.definition_text: to pay someone a particular amount of money for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I gave him £20 for his old camera.

_source.definition_text: to perform an action
_source.learnerexamples_text: She gave a cry. ; He gave her a kiss on the cheek.; She gave me a big hug.; When he saw me, he gave me a big, warm hug and a sweet kiss.

_source.definition_text: to perform or speak in public
_source.searchterms_text: gave;give;give a performance/speech etc;give a performance/speech, etc.;given;gives;giving
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tony gave a great speech to open the conference.; We would be very happy if you [could] come to our school and give a speech.

_source.definition_text: When a woman or an animal gives birth, she produces a baby from her body.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She gave birth to twins.; The most important person in my life is the person who gave birth to me, my mother.

_source.definition_text: to not do an activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think I'll give aerobics a miss this evening.; For this reason, I don't encourage you to buy the Spanish version of these CDs. I think you should give it a miss. Kind regards

_source.definition_text: to cause something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bacteria live in the human body but do not give rise to any symptoms.; That visit gave rise to a fruitful discussion in which various opinions were voiced and here are some comments on them.

_source.definition_text: to stop in order to allow other vehicles to go past before you drive onto a bigger road
_source.learnerexamples_text: You must give way at this junction.; Of course, you have to remember to give way to the pedestrians, to respect the signs and to push on the brake when you see a red light.

_source.definition_text: to promise someone something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Paolo gave me his word that he wouldn't tell anyone.; I give you my word that it will never happen again.

_source.definition_text: to express strong anger or another strong feeling
_source.learnerexamples_text: He gave vent to the frustration that had been building up inside him.; It's a great fallacy that giving vent to our emotion will be a solution to the problem itself and will lead to anything at all.

_source.definition_text: If something gives way, it falls because it is not strong enough to support the weight on top of it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Suddenly the ground gave way under me.; Fred's voice trailed off as he felt his legs give way beneath him.

_source.definition_text: to change into something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her excitement quickly gave way to horror.; This friendship gave way to love, but it was a really difficult situation, after all she was the Managing Director's daughter.

_source.definition_text: to criticize someone and make them feel guilty about something they have done
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ever since I missed the goal, the other players have been giving me a hard time.; I'm not saying that I wasn't normal or anything, I just gave my family a hard time sometimes.

_source.base_text: give away sth or give sth away
_source.definition_text: to give something to someone without asking for payment
_source.searchterms_text: give;give away sth or give sth away
_source.learnerexamples_text: The shop is giving away a sample pack to every customer.; She decided to give away everything she had and go to a place where nobody could find her.

_source.base_text: give away sth or give sth away
_source.definition_text: to tell people something secret, often without intending to
_source.searchterms_text: give;give away sth or give sth away
_source.learnerexamples_text: The party was meant to be a surprise, but Sharon gave it away.; It was always the same; she would meet with her neighbours afterwards and give my secrets away.

_source.base_text: give back sth or give sth back
_source.definition_text: to return something to the person who gave it to you
_source.searchterms_text: give;give back sth or give sth back
_source.learnerexamples_text: Has she given you those books back yet?; Please give it back to me tomorrow.

_source.base_text: give in sth or give sth in
_source.definition_text: to give a piece of written work or a document to someone for them to read, judge or deal with
_source.searchterms_text: give;give in sth or give sth in
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you given that essay in yet?

_source.definition_text: to finally agree to what someone wants, after refusing for a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: He nagged me so much for a new bike that eventually I gave in.; What you should do is talk to your parents and explain your problem to them. [Your] parents may give in!

_source.definition_text: to accept that you have been defeated and agree to stop competing or fighting
_source.learnerexamples_text: She knew she'd lost the argument but she wouldn't give in.; You'll never guess the answer - do you give in?

_source.base_text: give out sth or give sth out
_source.definition_text: to give something to a large number of people
_source.searchterms_text: give;give out sth or give sth out
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please give these worksheets out, Maria.; I've said I'll give out leaflets for them in town.; At the concert, what I had to do was to give out refreshments to the audience.

_source.base_text: give up sth or give sth up
_source.definition_text: to stop doing a regular activity or job
_source.searchterms_text: give;give up sth or give sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're going to give up our sports club membership after this year.; I believe that you should continue sports rather than music for as you mentioned in your letter you have always done sports and you can't give all that up for music classes.

_source.definition_text: If you give up a habit, such as smoking, or something such as alcohol, you stop doing it or using it.
_source.searchterms_text: give;give up (sth) or give (sth) up;give up sth or give sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: I gave up smoking two years ago.; Don't offer him a cigarette, he's trying to give up.; The reason why he is not happy could be that he can't give up drinking so much and it gets him down.

_source.definition_text: pleased and happy
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm glad that you came.; I'm so glad to see you.; I'm very glad to hear that.

_source.base_text: give up (sth/doing sth) or give (sth) up
_source.definition_text: to stop doing something before you have completed it, usually because it is too difficult
_source.searchterms_text: give;give up (sth/doing sth) or give (sth) up;give up sth/doing sth or give sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've given up trying to persuade Sara to come - she's just not interested.; I had to give up halfway through the race.; The most important thing is that you should keep doing it. Don't give up!!

_source.definition_text: very willing to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's always glad to help.; I know him personally and I'm sure he'll be very glad to help you.

_source.definition_text: to be grateful for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was glad of a few days off before going back to work.; We are glad of the changes [at] the Sports Centre even if the changes do not solve all [the] problems.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being attractive, exciting and special
_source.learnerexamples_text: the glamour of Hollywood ; The red carpet, the glamour, the glitter, the fame are things we all dream about at one point or another [in] our lives.

_source.definition_text: to look somewhere for a short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: He glanced at his watch.; From my seat [at] the café table I was glancing at this man when suddenly two men in black jackets, and wearing sunglasses ran and tackled the stranger, knocking him out.

_source.definition_text: to read something quickly
_source.learnerexamples_text: She glanced through the newspaper.; As you know, I always like glancing at some international newspapers.

_source.definition_text: a quick look
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had a quick glance around the restaurant but couldn't see him.; Just have a glance at the enclosed menu.

_source.definition_text: If you see something at a glance, you see it very quickly or immediately.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He could tell at a glance that something was wrong.; You could tell at a glance that Peter was a loner.

_source.definition_text: strong, bright light that hurts your eyes
_source.learnerexamples_text: I get a lot of glare from my computer screen.; As often as not, pressing the switch gave no result or yielded the glare of a naked bulb.

_source.definition_text: a long, angry look
_source.learnerexamples_text: She gave me an angry glare.; His glare [said] everything; she was the worst thing that had ever happened to the school.

_source.definition_text: to look at someone in an angry way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She glared at him and stormed out of the room.; You open the door and "Surprise!!": [it's] your mother and father, who ha[ve] just arrived from the country to spend the weekend with you. You glare at your mother, imagining that.

_source.definition_text: a hard transparent substance that objects such as windows and bottles are made of
_source.learnerexamples_text: broken glass; a glass jar/vase ; The present I love[d] the most was a cute little cat made from glass.

_source.definition_text: a container made of glass that is used for drinking
_source.learnerexamples_text: Would you like a glass of water?; After the film we can visit [a] restaurant for [a] glass of wine.

_source.definition_text: a piece of equipment with two transparent parts that you wear in front of your eyes to help you see better
_source.learnerexamples_text: a pair of glasses; She was wearing glasses.; Roger, I think I have left my glasses in the kitchen.

_source.definition_text: when you see something or someone for a very short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: He caught/got a glimpse of her as she got into the car.; If you go to Canada, like I did, you will enjoy great camping in the Rockies and might even catch a glimpse of the famous bears.

_source.definition_text: relating to the whole world
_source.learnerexamples_text: a global disaster ; the global problem of nuclear waste; the global economy; The improvement of electronics and global communications has made it possible to keep [in] close contact with friends all over the world.

_source.definition_text: the process by which businesses operate in many different countries and the culture of different countries becomes more similar
_source.learnerexamples_text: the globalization of big brands; the globalisation of fashion; Thanks to globalisation, fast food has arrived [in] Argentina, as almost everywhere in the world.

_source.definition_text: in a way that relates to the whole world
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company has to be able to compete globally.; Since I went to Canada, I realized we should think about environmental pollution globally.

_source.definition_text: a gradual increase in world temperatures caused by polluting gases
_source.learnerexamples_text: Very few people now deny that global warming is caused by humankind.; Also, due to global warming, sea levels might rise and [the] risk of flooding will also rise.

_source.definition_text: the world
_source.learnerexamples_text: This event is being watched by 200 million people around the globe. ; He has given numerous speeches around the globe, in which he always captivated the audience.

_source.definition_text: when people praise and respect you for achieving something important
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was my idea, but she got all the glory.; This point of view states that it is more fulfilling for a single person to achieve a goal on [their] own, without having to share the glory with other people and that by doing it alone, one really feels that [one] has achieved something.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being very impressive or beautiful
_source.learnerexamples_text: The castle has been restored to its former glory. ; Two years ago, the state, helped by the community of the island, gave birth to an ambitious plan to restore this beach to its former glory.

_source.definition_text: a soft, warm light
_source.learnerexamples_text: the warm glow of the moon ; The sun was setting, leaving a pink glow on everything it touched and the air smelled like fresh-cut grass.

_source.definition_text: a piece of clothing which covers your fingers and hand
_source.learnerexamples_text: a pair of gloves; Remember to bring gloves as well.

_source.definition_text: when your face feels or appears warm and healthy
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sam's face had lost its rosy glow.; After about three weeks of using this product by Morway Company, you will notice that your face looks softer and has a natural healthy glow.

_source.definition_text: to produce a soft, warm light
_source.learnerexamples_text: toys which glow in the dark; You can safely invest [i]n juggling equipment that glows in the dark, has flashing lights - or even that is set afire before starting to juggle [with] it.

_source.definition_text: to have a warm and healthy appearance
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her eyes were bright and her cheeks were glowing.; While the tourists were getting dressed, Ingrid, a tall middle-aged woman, checked the humidity of her armpits and that reminded her of the sentence: "Horses sweat, men perspire, women glow."

_source.definition_text: to feel very happy, proud, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Glowing with pride, she showed me her painting.; I never use it, of course, but just knowing I possess it makes me glow with happiness.

_source.definition_text: a substance used to stick things together
_source.learnerexamples_text: Put a bit of glue on both edges and hold them together. ; On the contrary, sometimes, with the help of our teachers, we had to fix them using "emergency" solutions and materials, such as sellotape and glue.

_source.definition_text: to stick something to something else with glue
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you think you can glue this vase back together? ; That is why my father glued and nailed the back of it so nobody could ever open the frame.

_source.definition_text: to be watching something, especially television
_source.learnerexamples_text: The kids were glued to the TV all morning. ; In general, it can be said that the modern mass obsession with television has led to the fact that more people now[a]days lead a sedentary way of life, not to mention [their being] couch potatoes, glued to the screen [for] most of their leisure time.

_source.definition_text: to move or travel somewhere
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to go to Japan.; He went into the house.; Are you going by train?; Does this train go to Newcastle?; Where did Helena go?

_source.definition_text: to move or travel somewhere in order to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's go for a walk.; I have to go and pick the kids up now.; I also have a dog and I like to go for a walk with [him].

_source.definition_text: to visit shops in order to buy things
_source.learnerexamples_text: We went shopping in town last Saturday.; We often go shopping.

_source.definition_text: to go somewhere to do a particular activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: We went skating yesterday.; We're going camping on Friday.; I'd like to go swimming.

_source.definition_text: to intend to do or be something
_source.searchterms_text: be going to do/be sth;be going to do/be sth ;go;goes;going;gone;went
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm going to call her tonight.; I'm going to be a dancer when I grow up.; I'm going to paint my bedroom yellow.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something is expected to happen in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's going to snow tonight.; They're going to have their first baby in June.; I think it's going to rain [tomorrow].

_source.definition_text: to empty the body of urine or solid waste, usually using a toilet to do so
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's going to be a long journey, kids, so if you want to go to the toilet do so now.; I left my watch at your house last night. [...] I went to [the] toilet and put it on the basin.

_source.definition_text: to develop in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: My exams went really well.; "How did your interview go?" - "Rather badly!"; Something's gone wrong with my computer.; I hope everything is going well.

_source.definition_text: to develop problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: Something's gone wrong with my computer.; Despite all that went wrong, there was something I really enjoyed. It was visiting the Diamond Cave.

_source.definition_text: to disappear or no longer exist
_source.learnerexamples_text: The food had gone by the time we got to the party.; When I turned round, the man had gone.; When I came to take my suitcase, it had gone!

_source.definition_text: If two things go, they match each other.
_source.learnerexamples_text: That top doesn't go with these trousers.; This jacket and skirt don't go together do they?

_source.definition_text: to become bald/blind/grey, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He went bald in his twenties.

_source.definition_text: If a road, path, etc. goes in a particular direction, it leads there.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This road goes to Birmingham.

_source.definition_text: to have a particular tune or words
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't remember how his latest song goes.

_source.definition_text: If time goes, it passes.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The day went very quickly.; But the time went so quickly and now I am in my early sixties [with] a lot of spare time.

_source.definition_text: to make a particular sound or movement
_source.learnerexamples_text: A cat goes 'Miaow'.; "Your dog's behaving oddly!" - "He goes like that when he wants some food."

_source.definition_text: to work in the right way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did you get the car going?

_source.definition_text: If someone goes red, their face becomes red because they are embarrassed or angry.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He kissed her on the cheek and she went bright red. ; When Paul saw the girl who had got blond hair and bluish eyes, his face suddenly went red.

_source.definition_text: to tell or include all the facts about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I won't go into detail over the phone, but I've been having a few health problems recently.; In one of his books he really goes into detail [about] how children treat other children [who] have difficulties with their "new" [language].

_source.definition_text: If something goes without saying, it is obvious or generally accepted.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It goes without saying that smoking is harmful to your health.; It goes without saying that I will participate!

_source.definition_text: If two things go hand in hand, they exist together and are connected with each other.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Prosperity goes hand in hand with investment.; Traffic and pollution go hand in hand.

_source.definition_text: to provide what someone needs for a short period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dinner is at eight, but I had an apple to keep me going.; Because of health concerns, advertisements lately show the people in Holland how important it is to have a good breakfast and that it will keep you going the whole day.

_source.definition_text: to continue to become more successful
_source.learnerexamples_text: The business is going from strength to strength.; To sum up, I believe that if the suggestions outlined above are put into action our magazine will go from strength to strength.

_source.definition_text: to gradually become worse
_source.learnerexamples_text: After his wife died, his health started to go downhill.; He had been going downhill in the last few days and so his death came as no surprise.

_source.definition_text: If there is a particular amount of time to go, that time remains.
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are only two weeks of term to go.; Right now this example is very realistic, and as I have just been told there is only 15 min to go, my stress level, I have to admit, is too high.

_source.definition_text: to do something too much, or to be too excited about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think people go overboard with presents at Christmas.; While no one should restrict their eating habits to the point eating is no longer a pleasure, but rather a chore, it is important not to go overboard, completely disregarding the advice of nutrition experts.

_source.base_text: go out of your way to do sth
_source.definition_text: to try very hard to do something pleasant for someone
_source.searchterms_text: go;go out of your way to do sth;goes;going;gone;went
_source.learnerexamples_text: He went out of his way to make us feel welcome.

_source.base_text: go so far as to do sth
_source.definition_text: to take the extreme action of doing something
_source.searchterms_text: go;go so far as to do sth;goes;going;gone;went
_source.learnerexamples_text: He even went so far as to stop her using the telephone.; Our present course of action may go so far as to cause irrevers[i]ble damage not only to our planet but also to the people living upon [it].

_source.definition_text: to do something because you are expected to do it and not because you want to
_source.learnerexamples_text: These days when we go out, I feel as though he's just going through the motions.; She went through the motions of every-day-life without enthusiasm.

_source.definition_text: to behave in a way that upsets or annoys other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's said some stupid things in the past, but this time he's gone too far.; Lucia let her speak and calmly said: "You really have gone too far this time."

_source.definition_text: to do or accept what other people are doing because it is the easiest thing to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: Just relax and go with the flow!; At this stage of her progress towards knowing herself better she has accepted that life is a mu[dd]le and that to a certain extent one has to go with the flow.

_source.definition_text: If something goes against the grain, you would not normally do it because it would be unusual or morally wrong.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It goes against the grain to throw all this food away.; She tries to dodge George because she is afraid of admitting the fact that she loves him. It simply goes against the grain.

_source.definition_text: If the level of something, especially a price, goes through the roof, it increases very quickly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The price of corn has gone through the roof recently.; Try extreme sports and feel your adrenaline levels going through the roof!

_source.definition_text: continuing to be successful or healthy after a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: The club was set up in 1987, and it's still going strong.; He's 93 and still going strong!; I am proud of him and happy that he is still going strong.

_source.definition_text: to start to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We now have permission to go ahead with the project.; The vote will go ahead today as planned.; I felt depressed under my parents' pressure, but I had something stronger deep inside of me saying that I should go ahead with my [plan].

_source.definition_text: something that you say to someone to allow them to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Can I borrow your book?" - "Yes, go ahead."; Everyone needs something sweet from time to time. Go ahead but don't eat it too often, eat more fruit and veg[e]tables!

_source.definition_text: to leave a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: Just go away and leave me alone, will you?; [A] big dog appeared. We were very scared. However, the dog went away and we [were able to] spend a beautiful day, walking, and breathing clean air.

_source.definition_text: to leave your home in order to spend time in a different place
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're going away for a few weeks in the summer.; You must have time to rest, to go for a walk, to go away on holiday ... and you don't have to give any explanation about it.

_source.definition_text: to return to a place where you were or where you have been before

_source.learnerexamples_text: It's been raining hard all day. ;  She kicked the ball as hard as she could. ; It was a clo[u]dy day, the wind [was] blow[ing] hard, and the city was quiet.

_source.definition_text: certainly not

_source.definition_text: almost not, or only a very small amount

_source.definition_text: the physical and electronic parts of a computer, rather than the programs
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to include new hardware in our budget.; Computer technology keeps improving all the time and consume[r]s like me and you definitely have to pay our money to keep our personal computer up to date and able to work with new computer software that require[s] [better and better] performance of computer hardware.

_source.definition_text: hurt or damage
_source.learnerexamples_text: Smoking can cause serious harm to the lungs. ;  Alan would never do anyone any harm. ; Missing a meal once in a while never did anyone any harm.; She was frightened by the experience but she came to no harm.; It is true that the car does us harm.

_source.definition_text: doing a job seriously and with a lot of effort
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's a very hard-working student.; I think I am suitable for the job because, apart from all [the] above, I am hard-working, well-educated and imaginative.

_source.base_text: there's no harm in doing sth
_source.definition_text: used to say that something is not a bad thing to do and could possibly have a good effect
_source.searchterms_text: harm;there's no harm in doing sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: I suppose there's no harm in trying.; There is no lack of go[o]d language schools and there is no harm in trying another one the next time.

_source.definition_text: to hurt someone or damage something

_source.definition_text: causing harm

_source.definition_text: not able or not likely to cause harm
_source.learnerexamples_text: Taken in small doses, this drug is completely/totally harmless. ; In conclusion, cars are not as harmless as they look so we must stop using them so much.

_source.definition_text: not likely to shock or upset people or to cause problems

_source.definition_text: when people are peaceful and agree with each other, or when different things seem right or suitable together
_source.learnerexamples_text: living together in peace and harmony ; I would like to think my children are going to live in a lovely world where the human being [will] be able to live in peace and harmony with the environment.

_source.definition_text: very cold, dangerous, or unpleasant and difficult to live in
_source.learnerexamples_text: harsh conditions; Furthermore, I have been trained for a year in living in harsh conditions.

_source.definition_text: a pleasant sound in music, made by playing or singing a group of different notes together
_source.learnerexamples_text: The choir sang in perfect harmony.; Their voices produced beautiful harmonies.; Having some singing knowledge myself, I can say their performance was excellent: the tune was maintained all through the concert, the r[hyth]m was also carefully kept and the[y] sounded in perfect harmony.

_source.definition_text: cruel, unkind, or unpleasant in a way that seems unfair
_source.learnerexamples_text: harsh criticism/punishment;  Taking him out of the game was a bit harsh.; Sorry if I sounded so harsh in the letter but I felt it was important to make these points.

_source.definition_text: too strong, bright, loud, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: harsh chemicals/lighting; It only contains herbs and plant extracts so it would not be too harsh a product for the skin and will not destroy the skin's natural defences.

_source.definition_text: in a harsh way
_source.learnerexamples_text: I thought she'd been treated rather harshly.; The public television is harshly criticised for joining the commercial flow of the private stations and targeting large audiences, instead of presenting more ambitious programmes of high quality.

_source.definition_text: when crops are cut and collected from fields
_source.learnerexamples_text: the grain/potato/grape harvest; We had a good/bad/poor harvest this year.; Well I can tell you about our annual harvest festival.

_source.definition_text: something you wear to cover your head, for fashion or protection
_source.learnerexamples_text: a straw hat; a woolly hat; I want to wear this hat when I go to [my] grandmother's house.

_source.definition_text: to dislike someone or something very much
_source.learnerexamples_text: Kelly hates her teacher.; She hated the winter.; I hate it when you do that.; I have always hated speaking in public.; I love rock and techno but I hate rap.

_source.definition_text: a strong dislike for someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hate and bigotry can only make our lives more difficult.; Feelings of hate and disgust may fill us, but we may love somebody. Many people say that love and hate go together.

_source.definition_text: an extremely strong feeling of dislike
_source.learnerexamples_text: What is very clear in these letters is Clark's passionate hatred of his father.; The motive for this shocking attack seems to be racial hatred.; The producers create situations involving different feeling[s] [such] as love, hatred, anger, fear,...

_source.definition_text: an amount of something that has been stolen or that is owned illegally
_source.learnerexamples_text: a haul of arms/drugs ; Because of the loud noise of the running engine, she wasn't aware of the man behind her grabbing the smaller bag and turning round ready to escape with his haul.

_source.definition_text: to pull something somewhere slowly and with difficulty
_source.learnerexamples_text: They hauled the piano into the living room. ; "When I'm finished, you can jump whenever you like. Remember to hold on to each other, and we'll haul you up when it's all over."

_source.definition_text: If an unpleasant memory or feeling haunts you, you think about or feel it often.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fighting in Vietnam was an experience that would haunt him for the rest of his life.; Thirty years after the fire he is still haunted by images of death and destruction.; And so John remained alone, haunted by the terrible loss.

_source.definition_text: If a ghost haunts a place, it appears there often.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They say that the house is haunted by the soldier's ghost.; [The castle] is 500 years old, and it is said to be haunted by a lady ghost.

_source.definition_text: used with the past participle of another verb to form the present and past perfect tenses
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you seen Roz? ;  I've passed my test. ;  He hasn't visited London yet. ;  I'd met his wife before. ;  It would have been better to tell the truth.

_source.definition_text: to need to do something or be forced to do something
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have (got) to do sth;have (got) to do sth ;have got to do sth;have got to do sth ;having

Yest[e]rday I went to the doctor and he said that I've got to stay at home for three days.

_source.definition_text: used when you are telling someone how to do something
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have (got) to do sth;have got to do sth;having
_source.learnerexamples_text: You have to wait for the green light and then record your voice.;  You've got to type in your name, then your password. ; To get to my house, you have to get bus [number] 30 to town, [and] there you have to get bus [number] 15 to Spring Bank.

_source.definition_text: used to say that you feel certain that something is true or will happen
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have (got) to do/be sth;have got to do/be sth;having
_source.learnerexamples_text: Interest rates have to come down at some point.; There's (=there has) got to be a better way of doing this.; There has to be a solution to this.

_source.definition_text: to own or possess
_source.learnerexamples_text: They have a big house.; He has blue eyes.; I've got two brothers.; He's got a degree.; She has a lot of experience.

_source.definition_text: If you have a particular illness, you suffer from it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got a cold.; Have you ever had measles?; I know you had [the] flu.

_source.definition_text: to eat or drink something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had prawns and rice for lunch.; Can I have a drink of water?; Let's have a coffee before the film.; When are we having dinner?; I have dinner [at] 5 pm.

_source.definition_text: to give birth to a baby
_source.learnerexamples_text: Elaine had a baby girl yesterday.; She had got married and had had a baby without telling me!

_source.base_text: have fun/a nice time/a problem, etc.
_source.definition_text: to experience something
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have fun/a nice time/a problem etc;have fun/a nice time/a problem, etc.;having
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have a nice day!; We had a great time in Venice.; We had a few problems finding the house.; Did you have any luck finding a present for Annie?; We played a lot of games and had fun.

_source.definition_text: used with nouns to say that someone does something
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have a rest/shower/walk etc;have a rest/shower/walk, etc.;having
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can I have a quick shower? ;  Let's have a walk along the river. ; If you want you can have a shower after play[ing] tennis.

_source.definition_text: to pay someone to do something for you
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have sth cleaned/cut/repaired etc;have sth cleaned/cut/repaired, etc.;having
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm having my hair cut this afternoon.; I've had my watch mended.; We're having the house painted next month.; My mother is having her car repaired.

_source.definition_text: If you have something stolen/taken, etc. someone takes something that belongs to you.
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have sth stolen/taken etc;have sth stolen/taken, etc.;having
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had her car stolen last week.; I had my bag taken.; He told me over the phone that he had arrived in London with his wife, but shortly after the arrival, he had ha[d] his wallet stolen in the underground station.

_source.definition_text: used to say that someone is holding something, or that someone or something is with them
_source.learnerexamples_text: He had a pen in his hand.; She had a little boy with her.; Maria had the phone in her hand.

_source.definition_text: to cause something to be in a particular state
_source.learnerexamples_text: He had dinner ready by the time we got home.; We had the tent up within ten minutes.; We had everything ready in case of an emergency or a chaos situation.

_source.definition_text: to not know
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Where's Serge?" "I've no idea."; I have no idea about how his children are.

_source.definition_text: If you have someone over/round, etc. you arrange for someone to visit you in your home.
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have sb over/round/to stay etc;have sb over/round/to stay, etc.;having
_source.learnerexamples_text: We had Justyna and Al round for dinner last week.; I'd like to thank you once more for having me round [to] your house.

_source.definition_text: to arrange for someone to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you wait, I'll have someone collect it for you.; I'll have my secretary call her this afternoon.; I would like to request you, as a manager, to either have someone fix the problem with the microwave or simply replace it.

_source.definition_text: to be completely unable to guess, understand, or deal with something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I haven't a clue what you're talking about.; I haven't a clue about it.

_source.definition_text: to talk to someone for a short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could I have a word (with you) about the sales figures?; Perhaps you would have a quiet word with Simon about the problem.; The nurse sitting beside me said to me, 'Your mother would like to have a word with you,' then she went out.

_source.base_text: have nothing to do with sb/sth
_source.definition_text: to have no connection or influence with someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have nothing to do with sb/sth;having

_source.base_text: have nothing to do with sb
_source.definition_text: If something is or has nothing to do with you, you have no good reason to know about it or be involved with it.
_source.searchterms_text: had;has;have;have nothing to do with sb;having
_source.learnerexamples_text: I wish he wouldn't offer advice on my marriage - it's nothing to do with him.; The party was horrible: the guests were all talking about things that had nothing to do with me.

_source.definition_text: to have a reason not to like someone or something

_source.definition_text: to dislike someone and want to cause problems for them
_source.learnerexamples_text: She really has it in for me - I don't know what I've done to offend her.; Only then did she realise that somebody had it in for her.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that you do not know something

_source.base_text: have (got) on sth or have (got) sth on

_source.searchterms_text: have;have (got) on sth or have (got) sth on;have got on sth or have got sth on
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's got a red shirt on.; I loved that dress you had on last night.; I looked [over] my shoulder and there was Nora as white as the dress she had on.

_source.definition_text: something that is dangerous

_source.definition_text: dangerous
_source.learnerexamples_text: hazardous chemicals ; They are faced with hazardous chemical reactions when trying to gain new knowledge and therefore people should be very grateful to them.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a man, boy or male animal that has already been mentioned
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't ask Andrew, he won't know.; There's no need to be frightened - he's a very friendly dog.; He is from Hungary.

_source.definition_text: the part of the body above the neck which contains your brain, eyes, nose, mouth, ears, etc. and on which your hair grows

_source.definition_text: the person in charge of a school
_source.learnerexamples_text: You'll have to ask the head for permission.; If I can't do my homework, my teacher will sen[d] me to [the] head teacher.

_source.definition_text: the person who is in charge of an organization or a part of an organization

_source.definition_text: the mind and mental abilities

_source.definition_text: to remain calm in a difficult situation

_source.definition_text: to stop being calm in a difficult situation

_source.definition_text: to laugh/shout/scream, etc. very much and very loudly

_source.definition_text: to move in a particular direction

_source.definition_text: to be in charge of a group, organization, etc.

_source.definition_text: to be at the front or top of something

_source.definition_text: the main stories in newspapers, on television, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: That story made headlines all over the world.

_source.definition_text: the place from where an organization is controlled

_source.definition_text: the person in charge of a school

_source.definition_text: If a wound or broken bone heals, it becomes healthy again, and if something heals it, it makes it healthy again.

_source.definition_text: the condition of your body

_source.definition_text: the set of services provided by a country or an organization for treating people who are ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: A large proportion of these taxes go towards providing health care.; Healthcare workers are some of the lowest paid people in the country.; In Britain, the NHS provides free health care for every citizen.

_source.definition_text: physically strong and well

_source.definition_text: good for your health

_source.definition_text: successful and strong

_source.definition_text: an untidy pile of things

_source.definition_text: a lot of something

_source.definition_text: to listen to someone or something

_source.definition_text: If you hear from someone, you get a letter, a message, or a telephone call from them, or they tell you something.

_source.definition_text: to be told some information

_source.definition_text: If you have heard of someone or something, you know that that person or thing exists.

_source.definition_text: the organ in your chest that sends the blood around your body
_source.learnerexamples_text: heart disease/failure; He's got a weak/bad heart.; My father [is] going to have heart s[u]rgery.

_source.definition_text: someone's deepest feelings and true character

_source.definition_text: the centre of something or the most important part of something
_source.searchterms_text: heart;heart of sth;hearts;the heart of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: The demonstrators will march through the heart of the capital.; A disagreement about boundaries is at the heart of the dispute.; This restaurant is in the heart of Tepec, and it is open from 10.00am to 6.00pm except on Friday.

_source.definition_text: a shape that is used to mean love

_source.definition_text: used to say that you feel something very strongly

_source.definition_text: so that you can remember all of something

_source.definition_text: used to say what you really think

I have to admit that it was only a [sensi]ble decision, because deep in my heart I knew I want[ed] to learn English.

_source.definition_text: to make someone feel extremely sad
_source.learnerexamples_text: She really broke his heart when she left.; It breaks my heart when I hear the terrible things that have been said about him.; I saw them kissing each other. That was it - when I saw that scene, it broke my heart.

_source.definition_text: used to say what someone is really like
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm just a kid at heart.; I also thought that she was brave at heart.

_source.definition_text: If you take criticism or advice to heart, you think about it seriously, often because it upsets you

_source.definition_text: to tell someone your secret thoughts and feelings

_source.definition_text: to stop believing that you can succeed

_source.definition_text: If something is dear to someone or dear to their heart, it is very important to them.

_source.definition_text: If you have a change of heart, you change your opinion or feelings about something.

_source.definition_text: a serious medical condition in which the heart does not get enough blood, causing great pain and often leading to death
