_source.definition_text: relating to events or people in the past, or to the study of history
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many important historical documents were destroyed when the library was bombed.; She specializes in historical novels set in eighteenth-century England.; Budapest is very beautiful with a [lot] of historical buildings and churches.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is connected to history
_source.learnerexamples_text: The film makes no attempt to be historically accurate.; Historically, there have always been close links between France and Scotland.; Well, maybe this brief description of my travel in time is not historically accurate; nevertheless I hope that you have enjoyed yourself reading it as much as I did writing it, and I hope you will consider it worth[y] of publication in your magazine.

_source.definition_text: the whole series of events in the past which relate to the development of a country, subject, or person
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Civil War was a terrible time in American history. ;  What do you know about the history of jazz? ; I liked it very much because it [was] about Chinese history.

_source.definition_text: the study of events in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's very interested in modern European history. ;  a history book ; Dear Nicolas, I think I left my history book in your house.

_source.definition_text: If you have a history of a particular problem or illness, you have already suffered from it.
_source.searchterms_text: a history of sth;histories;history;history of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: a man with a history of drug addiction; The characteristic we are born with is to a certain level affected by genetic factor[s] e.g. if a mother has a history of depression her daughter or son will also have higher chance [of] get[ting] depression.

_source.definition_text: to touch someone or something quickly and with force using your hand or an object in your hand
_source.learnerexamples_text: She hit him on the head with her tennis racket. ; Teachers are not allowed to hit their pupils.; When I went in, somebody hit me with a pan!

_source.definition_text: to touch someone or something quickly and with force, usually causing injury or damage
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car went out of control and hit a wall. ;  She hit her head on the pavement when she fell. ; He hit a boy on the main road [but] fortun[ate]ly the boy was ok[a]y.

_source.definition_text: to affect something badly
_source.learnerexamples_text: The economy has been hit by high unemployment. ; Penalties for parking in [the] wrong place can really hit you in [the] po[c]ket.

_source.definition_text: to reach a place, position, or state
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our profits have already hit $1 million.; Having already hit the 50% boundary in 1991, we still see that the teachers' salaries experienced a significant rise.

_source.definition_text: If an idea or thought hits you, you suddenly think of it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The idea for the book hit me in the middle of the night.; I climbed out of the shower, staggered into my room and then it hit me! "My diary! For crying out loud, that's it!"

_source.definition_text: If people hit it off, they like each other and become friendly immediately.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Carla and Nina didn't really hit it off.; They hit it off immediately.

_source.definition_text: to become very angry and start shouting
_source.learnerexamples_text: If I'm late again he'll hit the roof.; Be careful, if you make too much noise he'll hit the roof.

_source.definition_text: a thing or person that is very popular or successful
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Beatles had a string of number-one hits in the 1960s.; Your cake was a real hit at the party - everyone loved it.; They've just released a CD of their greatest hits.; The group RADIANT played their big hits [from the] 1980s for an hour.

_source.definition_text: a request to see a document on the Internet that is then counted to calculate the number of people looking at the page
_source.learnerexamples_text: There have been over 10,000 hits on the site since Wednesday.

_source.definition_text: to get free rides in someone's vehicle, by standing next to the road and waiting for someone to pick you up
_source.learnerexamples_text: We hitchhiked from Paris to Milan. ; We hitchhike[d] to the nearest city.

_source.definition_text: using or involved with the most recent and advanced electronic machines, computers, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This database system is an affordable, hi-tech solution.; With the development of science and technology, many new inve[ntions] have entered our life, especially some hi-tech products.

_source.definition_text: an activity that you enjoy and do regularly when you are not working
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ben's hobby is restoring old motorcycles.; My hobby is playing the guitar.

_source.definition_text: a team game played on grass where you hit a small ball with a long, curved stick
_source.learnerexamples_text: I play hockey every Saturday.; We played hockey and fo[o]tball.

_source.definition_text: to have something in your hand or arms
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was holding a glass of wine. ;  She held the baby in her arms. ;  They were holding hands and kissing. ; Can you hold the bag while I open the door?; I like to hold [the cat] tightly because her [fur] is so soft and lovely.

_source.definition_text: to keep something in a particular position
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you hold the door open, please? ;  Hold your hand up if you know the answer. ;  They held a gun to his head. ; Suddenly, the girl found herself in front of the man, [who was] holding a gun against her forehead.

_source.definition_text: to organize an event
_source.learnerexamples_text: to hold talks/an election; A music festival is held there in July.; Every evening the concerts are held in the open air, so you can have lots of fun.

_source.definition_text: to contain or be able to contain something
_source.learnerexamples_text: This jug holds exactly one pint.; One bag won't hold all of the shopping - we'd better take two.; Modern computers can hold huge amounts of information.; Big companies which hold a huge amount of information would not be able to work without a computer.

_source.definition_text: to keep someone in a place so that they cannot leave
_source.learnerexamples_text: The terrorists held him hostage for 18 months.; I was held prisoner in a tiny attic room.; All around the world animals are held as prisoners in zoos.

_source.definition_text: to keep air in your lungs and not let it out
_source.learnerexamples_text: How long can you hold your breath under water?; My heart was beating fast. I was holding my breath.

_source.definition_text: to have a particular job, position, or qualification
_source.learnerexamples_text: She held the post of treasurer. ; In fact 90% males hold the skilled vocational diploma where[as] only 10% females hold the same degree.

_source.definition_text: to wait for something to happen, often feeling anxious
_source.learnerexamples_text: While the leaders negotiated, the world held its breath.; They, the critics, the fans and friends and his wife, held their breath and crossed their fingers, hoping to once again hear his enchanting voice.

_source.definition_text: to believe something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They held the view that physical punishment was good for children.; Nowadays, some people hold the opinion that children who do not have good living conditions are better prepared to deal with the problems which they will encounter later on.

_source.definition_text: to have a particular position in a competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: to hold the world record; The team held the lead until the 89th minute.; Nowadays she is an excellent sportswoman, she holds the world record.

_source.definition_text: to have a conversation
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can just about hold a conversation in Italian.; I know the grammar and many different expressions, and I can hold a conversation with other people.

_source.definition_text: to keep someone interested in something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The film held my attention from beginning to end.; The recent protest about our canteen held my attention.

_source.definition_text: to be as successful as other people or things
_source.learnerexamples_text: Alison could always hold her own in political debates.; An average IT company in the UK is only 30% female so it is vital to be comfortable in the company of so many men, and to be able to hold your own against them in meetings and discussions.

_source.definition_text: If you say that an argument doesn't hold water, you mean that it can't possibly be true.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry, but what you are suggesting just doesn't hold water!;  It remains to us to prove that the opinions of some scientists are far-fetched and don't hold water.

_source.definition_text: to like or respect someone less because they have done something wrong or behaved badly
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was his mistake but I won't hold it against him.; When my Dad was about sixteen, he had to get a job. [...] My uncle on the other hand was al[lowe]d to study until he was 21. They have never held it against each other, as far as I know.

_source.definition_text: to prevent someone or something from moving forward
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police held back the protesters.; At last, the guards were able to temporarily hold them back.

_source.base_text: hold back sth or hold sth back
_source.definition_text: to not tell everything you know about something
_source.searchterms_text: hold;hold back sth or hold sth back
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think she suspected I was holding something back.; To be honest, I am holding back a lot more things [that are] special about the cottage, because I want you to come and have a look.

_source.definition_text: to prevent someone or something from making progress
_source.learnerexamples_text: She felt that having children would hold her back.; For years, nothing could hold her back, and she didn't realize how her huge amount of self-confidence prevented her from seeing life as it really was.

_source.base_text: hold back sth or hold sth back
_source.definition_text: to stop yourself showing an emotion
_source.searchterms_text: hold;hold back sth or hold sth back
_source.learnerexamples_text: She couldn't hold back the tears.; In the last scenes, I could not hold back my tears any longer and I just burst into tears.

_source.definition_text: to keep a job
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's difficult for mothers to hold down a full-time job.; I don't know how long I'd manage to hold down a job that I d[id]n't like, and that d[id]n't bring me anything other than money.

_source.definition_text: to wait before doing something
_source.searchterms_text: hold;hold off (sth/doing sth);hold off sth/doing sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: We'll hold off making a decision until we hear from Nick.

_source.definition_text: to wait for a short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hold on, I'll check in my diary.; I've a lot of good stories to tell you about so hold on.

_source.definition_text: something you say when you are confused or surprised by something that you have just heard or read and want to understand it
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hold on, if Sara's not coming, why are we booking a table for six?

_source.definition_text: to hold something or someone firmly with your hands or arms
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hold onto the rope and don't let go.; I take my poetry book with me all the time to hold onto something so important to me.

_source.definition_text: to think that something is likely to succeed or have a good result
_source.learnerexamples_text: Few people hold out any hope of finding more survivors.; To be honest, I don't hold out much hope that this problem will ever be solved, because homelessness doesn't affect MPs personally.

_source.base_text: hold up sb/sth or hold sb/sth up
_source.definition_text: to make something or someone slow or late
_source.searchterms_text: hold;hold up sb/sth or hold sb/sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: We got held up by the traffic.; Then I was held up in a traffic jam.

_source.definition_text: when you hold something or someone, or the way you do this
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep a tight hold on your tickets.; When I got up on my feet again, I reached out my arm to get a hold on something, but there w[as]n't anything to hold on to.

_source.definition_text: to start holding something or someone
_source.searchterms_text: catch/get/grab/take hold of sth/sb;catch/get/grab/take hold of sth/sb ;hold;holds
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took hold of one end of the carpet and tugged.; I just managed to grab hold of Lucy before she fell in the pool.; I'm scared!" said Nora trembling, as she took hold of my arm.

_source.definition_text: to obtain something, or to manage to speak to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got hold of a copy at the local library. ;  I rang three times, but couldn't get hold of her. ; I had also forgotten to remind my friends and teachers to bring their own knife and fork to our lunch, but fortunately one of my friends managed to get hold of some spare knives and forks.

_source.definition_text: power or control over something or someone
_source.searchterms_text: a hold on/over sth/sb;hold;hold on/over sth/sb;holds
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their company has a strong hold on the computer market.; They send the money directly to his father and now have a hold on Chen.

_source.definition_text: If a plan or activity is on hold, it will not be done until a later time.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The project is on hold until we get more money.; What's more, it might, intentional[l]y or not, raise awareness on issues that might have been put on hold by authorities, such as the legalization of soft drugs.

_source.definition_text: waiting to speak to someone on the telephone
_source.learnerexamples_text: His secretary put me on hold.; The day after, I called your office and after being put on hold, the person answering the phone was unwilling to come up with a proper reply.

_source.definition_text: a time when you do not have to go to work or school
_source.learnerexamples_text: a public holiday; I'll be on holiday from Monday for two weeks.;  My aunt looks after us during the school holidays. ; Yes, I w[ould] like to go with you, because it is our school holiday.

_source.definition_text: a hollow space in something, or an opening in a surface
_source.learnerexamples_text: a bullet hole ;  There's a hole in the roof. ;  We dug a hole to plant the tree. ; I like wearing jeans with holes in them, they look cool.

_source.definition_text: having a hole or empty space inside
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hollow shell/tube ; He had taken the dark red leather-bound book to his hideout in the forest, an old oak tree with a hollow trunk, where he used to play alone.

_source.definition_text: a long visit to a place away from where you live, for pleasure
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's book a skiing/walking holiday. ;  Are you going on holiday this year? ; We [are] going to Greece this summer for [a] holiday.

_source.definition_text: If something someone says rings hollow, it does not sound true or sincere.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He said he was pleased, but his words rang hollow.; Everything rang hollow to her, so she decided to follow him in order to understand what had happened and her fiancé became so friendly and understanding.

_source.definition_text: without meaning or real feeling
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hollow victory ;  a hollow laugh ; These celebrities tend to encourage a lifestyle that, at first, may be extremely appealing, specially to children and teenagers, but it is nothing [more] than pure hollow hedonism.

_source.definition_text: relating to a religion or a god
_source.learnerexamples_text: the holy city of Jerusalem ; I'd like to go inside and see for myself but only the holy priests are allowed to be in there and only [on] special occasions.

_source.definition_text: the place where you live or feel you belong
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tried to ring him, but he wasn't at home. ;  We sold our home in London and moved to Scotland. ;  He left home when he was eighteen. ; I was actually born in New Zealand, but I've lived in England for so long that it feels like home now.; That's why I love my home.

_source.definition_text: to feel happy and confident in a place or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: After a month she felt at home in her new job.; I explained: "I was in Manchester for just 10 month[s] and [during] that time the people from there made me feel at home [so] I feel proud to have the accent."

_source.definition_text: the place where you usually find something or someone, or where they come from
_source.searchterms_text: home;home of sth/sb;homes;the home of sth/sb
_source.learnerexamples_text: France, the home of good food; Every golfer - and those watching golf - know, that the home of golf is St. Andrews in Scotland.

_source.definition_text: a place where people who need special care live
_source.learnerexamples_text: a children's home; My grandmother lives in a home now.; However, I am also experienced with elderly people because I worked in an old people's home for about 3 months in the summer 1997.

_source.definition_text: to behave in a relaxed way in a place, as if it was your own home
_source.learnerexamples_text: Take off your coat and make yourself at home.; Please relax and make yourself at home and help yourself.

_source.definition_text: to the place where you live
_source.learnerexamples_text: He didn't come home until midnight.; I went home to visit my parents.; I must go home at midnight because I have to travel tomorrow.

_source.definition_text: a family in which the parents do not now live together
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many of these children come from broken homes.; The development of the modern society has brought with it a growing number of broken homes, divorces and economic problems which have directly affected the parent-child relationship.

_source.definition_text: at or in the place someone lives
_source.learnerexamples_text: Will you be home tomorrow evening?; I'll not be home this afternoon.

_source.definition_text: without a place to live
_source.learnerexamples_text: 10,000 people were made homeless by the floods.; As a result, there are a lot of homeless people in our local community.

_source.definition_text: people who are homeless
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're opening a new shelter for the homeless.; The money spen[t] on the royal family could be used for something else like building houses for the homeless.

_source.definition_text: the state of being homeless
_source.learnerexamples_text: The government is trying to tackle homelessness.; Unemployment is a major problem today and it leads more and more people on[to] the path of poverty and homelessness.

_source.definition_text: work which teachers give students to do at home
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you done your homework yet? ; history/maths/science homework; I like doing my homework.

_source.definition_text: sincere and telling the truth
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you want my honest answer/opinion, I think your hair looks awful. ; I tell everything to my mother in order to be honest.

_source.definition_text: not likely to lie, cheat, or steal
_source.learnerexamples_text: an honest man ; She had an honest face.; I know it is an illusion, but I want to think that in the world there are some honest people.

_source.definition_text: used to express your real opinion
_source.learnerexamples_text: To be honest, I didn't really enjoy the party. ; To be honest with you, I don't think it will be possible.; To be honest, I do hate shopping for clothes.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that you are telling the truth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thanks, but I honestly couldn't eat another piece of cake. ; Honestly, I did not know what to do, I wanted to cry.

_source.definition_text: in an honest way
_source.learnerexamples_text: They have always dealt honestly and fairly with their customers.; If we want to answer [this question] honestly and sincerely, we should think about [the] advantages and disadvantages that keeping animals in zoos results [in].

_source.definition_text: the quality of being honest
_source.learnerexamples_text: I appreciate your honesty.; He's an extraordinary person and the TV viewers will love him because of his good sense of humo[u]r and his honesty.

_source.definition_text: used when you are saying what you really think or feel about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: In all honesty, I'd rather not go.; It is easy to say that government funding should be raised to make classes smaller and materials more relevant, but in all honesty, Danish schools are working very well indeed.

_source.definition_text: a sweet, sticky food that is made by bees
_source.learnerexamples_text: We had a mug of tea and toast spread with honey.; For breakfast they eat bread with butter, jam or honey.

_source.definition_text: a holiday taken by two people who have just got married
_source.learnerexamples_text: We went to Paris on our honeymoon.; Where did you spend your honeymoon?

_source.definition_text: when people respect you because you have done what you believe is honest and right, or the quality of doing this
_source.learnerexamples_text: a man of honour; We fought for the honour of our country.; Your health is worth much more than your honour.

_source.definition_text: in order to celebrate or show great respect for someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: honour;honoured;honouring;honours;in honour of sb/sth;in honour of sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: a banquet in honour of the president; Finally we went to Corinth, where there are a lot of ancient sanctuaries which were built in honour of their gods.

_source.definition_text: something which makes you feel proud and pleased
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's an honour to be team captain. ;  I had the great honour of meeting the King. ; It would be a pleasure and an honour for me.

_source.definition_text: part of a piece of clothing which can be pulled up to cover the top and back of the head
_source.learnerexamples_text: The coat has a hood.; He was wearing a black hood.

_source.definition_text: proud and pleased because you have been given respect or asked to do something special
_source.learnerexamples_text: I am honoured to accept your invitation.; We would be honoured if you would join us for the day.; We would be honoured if you could present the prizes at this event.

_source.definition_text: to like or start to like doing something very much and want to do it all the time
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's completely hooked on computer games.; It is such a great change to listen to well-known singers for those who are hooked on rock music.

_source.definition_text: a curved piece of metal or plastic used for hanging something on, or a similar object used for catching fish
_source.learnerexamples_text: a coat/picture hook; a boat hook; a fish hook; A few moments later she took out a rope, which had a hook on one end.

_source.definition_text: If a small animal, bird, or insect hops, it moves by jumping on all of its feet at the same time.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Rabbits were hopping across the field. ; I advise a quite different restaurant, in a more peaceful area; it is a pavil[i]on facing Monstsouris garden, where you can see birds hopping and flying through the tre[e]s, and swans on the lake.

_source.definition_text: to jump on one foot or to move about in this way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He hopped across the room.; He was not to be able to stand still and seemed to be hopping and leaping with his violin while playing.

_source.definition_text: to go somewhere quickly or get into or out of a vehicle quickly
_source.learnerexamples_text: to hop on a plane/train ; The next thing that happen[s] is that everyone hops in their cars and drives to the restaurant where they have dinner.

_source.definition_text: to want something to happen or be true
_source.learnerexamples_text: I hope (that) the bus won't be late. ;  We had hoped for better weather than this. ;  "Do you think it's going to rain?" "I hope not!" ;  "Is he coming?" "I hope so." ; I hope you can come next time.

_source.definition_text: a positive feeling about the future, or something that you want to happen or be true
_source.learnerexamples_text: a message full of hope ;  What are your hopes for the future? ;  Don't give up hope - I'm sure he'll be fine. ;  Young people are growing up in our cities without any hope of getting a job. ; Ten minutes later I started to tell [them] how brave [they were] and how we fought when there was no hope.

_source.definition_text: to intend to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dad hopes to retire next year. ; With this new class I hope to make progress.

_source.definition_text: because you want something good to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: She went to Paris in the hope of improving her French.; They wrote to the Prime Minister in the hope that he would help.; Not only would I want to travel back to understand Hitler's incredible success, but also in the hope of thwarting his plans.

_source.definition_text: the best/last/only person or thing that can help you and make you succeed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Doctors say his only hope is a transplant.; My spirits sank at the same time [as] the water, our last hope of survival, did.

_source.definition_text: to think that something is likely to succeed or have a good result
_source.learnerexamples_text: Few people hold out any hope of finding more survivors.; To be honest, I don't hold out much hope that this problem will ever be solved, because homelessness doesn't affect MPs personally.

_source.definition_text: feeling positive about a future event or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was hopeful about the outcome of the meeting.; They were hopeful of a successful agreement.; I'm hopeful (that) we can reach a compromise.; I know that it is quite impossible to find it [i]n a big town like mine, but I am [still] hopeful.

_source.definition_text: If something is hopeful, it gives you reason to believe that what you want to happen will happen.
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are hopeful signs that she will make a full recovery.; The hopeful atmosphere darkened somewhat.

_source.definition_text: used, often at the start of a sentence, to express what you would like to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hopefully it won't rain.; Hopefully we'll be in Norwich by early evening.; Hopefully he likes me, too.

_source.definition_text: in a hopeful way
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Are there any tickets left?" she asked hopefully.; I'll be waiting hopefully for your letter.

_source.definition_text: without hope
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hopeless situation; They searched for survivors but it was hopeless.; She was depressed and felt totally hopeless about the future.; When my uncle heard about my new hobby, he bought me a chess-computer to train for my first real match. At the moment I'm trying to win against it but I think it is hopeless.

_source.definition_text: very bad at a particular activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm hopeless at sports.; He's a hopeless cook.

_source.definition_text: extremely, or in a way that makes you lose hope
_source.learnerexamples_text: hopelessly lost; They met at university and fell hopelessly in love.; It's never easy to be young and hopelessly in love.

_source.definition_text: the line in the distance where the sky seems to touch the land or sea
_source.learnerexamples_text: We could see a large ship on the horizon.; The view from here is also very beautiful and I remember that when I looked out over the sea, I could see the boats dotted around between the bay and the horizon.

_source.definition_text: to increase the number of things that you know about, have experienced, or can do
_source.learnerexamples_text: Travelling certainly broadens your horizons.; Overall, I can say the conference was a success and definitely broadened my horizons.

_source.definition_text: likely to happen soon
_source.learnerexamples_text: Economic recovery is on the horizon.; Often this is justified as [a] result of society being collective[ly] afraid that a shortage of fuel is on the horizon.

_source.definition_text: level and flat, or parallel to the ground or to the bottom of a page
_source.learnerexamples_text: a horizontal line/stripe ; Years are projected along the horizontal axis.

_source.definition_text: a piece of equipment used to make a loud sound as a warning or signal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a car/fog horn ;  The taxi driver sounded/beeped his horn. ; How happy I was, hearing the sound of a car horn.

_source.definition_text: a curved musical instrument that you blow into to make a sound
_source.learnerexamples_text: He blew his horn.; At last, when the first notes came out of the or[c]hestra, a spotlight showed the enormous figure of Ludwig van Mill strolling in the forest, blowing his horn and grinning at the trees.

_source.definition_text: one of the two hard, pointed growths on the heads of cows, goats, and some other animals
_source.learnerexamples_text: These cows have curved horns.; Far in the south of Chile, you will find the smallest deer of the world called "Pudù". It is only 25 cm. tall, doesn't have big horns and eats fruit.

_source.definition_text: very unpleasant or bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's got a horrible cold.; What's that horrible smell?; That was a horrible thing to say!; I got a really nice T-shirt from Janeth, and a horrible pair of socks from Simon.

_source.definition_text: very shocked
_source.learnerexamples_text: When I told him all the money was gone, he was absolutely horrified. ; When we arrived at the Riverside Lodge I was horrified to find out that there were no ramps in the building.

_source.definition_text: extremely shocking
_source.learnerexamples_text: She sustained horrifying injuries in the attack. ; Evading his unknown captors he is faced with a horrifying proposition.

_source.definition_text: a film or story that entertains people by shocking or frightening them
_source.learnerexamples_text: I love reading horror stories.; I'll buy a DVD called "Scream", it's a horror movie - you know I love scary movies.

_source.definition_text: a strong feeling of shock or fear
_source.learnerexamples_text: She watched in horror as the car skidded across the road. ; The thought of speaking in front of so many people fills me with horror.; I then realized to my absolute horror, that I had forgotten the present.; I approached the door but to my horror, it was locked.

_source.definition_text: a large animal with four legs, which people ride on or use for carrying things or pulling vehicles
_source.learnerexamples_text: to ride a horse; a horse and cart; I also like to be with horses.

_source.definition_text: A hospitable person or place is friendly, pleasant, and welcomes visitors.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We always find them very hospitable.; First of all, the families you will be staying with are exceptionally hospitable, always willing to show you round in the local area.

_source.definition_text: a place where ill or injured people go to be treated by doctors and nurses
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got to go (in)to hospital to have an operation.; She spent a week in hospital last year.; She works in a hospital.

_source.definition_text: when people are friendly and welcoming to guests and visitors
_source.learnerexamples_text: The local people showed me great hospitality.; Our members were ever so pleased with the families and your kind hospitality.

_source.definition_text: someone who invites people to a meal or a party, or to stay in their home
_source.learnerexamples_text: We thanked our hosts for the lovely evening.; My host family looked after me very well during my month in London.; My experience [of] liv[ing] with a host family was very good, so I suggest we should look for a nice place for both of us.

_source.definition_text: a large number of people or things
_source.searchterms_text: a host of sth;host;host of sth;hosts
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got a whole host of questions to ask you.; In this day and age, we can buy Nike clothes, H[ead & Shoulders] shampoos and a host of other products in the UK as well as other places in the world.

_source.definition_text: someone who introduces the guests on a radio or television programme
_source.learnerexamples_text: a talk show host; For a lot of youngsters some television hosts are regarded as role models because they are famous and do not seem to have problems with anything at all.

_source.definition_text: If a place hosts an event, people there arrange it and it happens there.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The town hosts an annual jazz festival.; Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing on behalf of my town which has been short-listed to host an international conference next year.

_source.definition_text: someone who is kept as a prisoner and may be hurt or killed in order to force other people to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Three hostages died in the attack.; The most extraordinary bond, however, develops between two of the hostages, namely Mr. Hosokawa himself and the American opera singer Roxanne Coss.

_source.definition_text: to catch or keep someone as a prisoner
_source.learnerexamples_text: Two tourists were held hostage by terrorists.; At the party, however, things take an unexpected turn when all the visitors are taken hostage by a group of terrorists.

_source.definition_text: a place like a cheap hotel, where you can live when you are away from home or have no home
_source.learnerexamples_text: a youth hostel;  a hostel for the homeless; We'll stay in a hostel [be]cause it's cheap and we'll use public transport.

_source.definition_text: unfriendly and not liking or agreeing with something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Some politicians were very hostile to the idea. ; She is not hostile or aggressive.

_source.definition_text: unpleasant or not suitable for living or growing
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hostile climate ; They live and work in very hostile conditions.; However, they do not realize that they have to survive in a hostile environment, living in unsafe and unhealthy slums.

_source.definition_text: unfriendly, angry behaviour that shows that you dislike someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: hostility towards outsiders; As Edmund's cruelty and hostility towards Charles intensified, and Charles' attempts to escape failed, his unhappiness increased, which led to his ultimate self-destruction.

_source.definition_text: having a high temperature
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hot sunny day; hot weather; a hot drink/meal; It's too hot in here, can we turn down the heating?; Bake the cake in a hot oven, about 220°C, for 30 minutes.

_source.definition_text: Hot food contains strong spices which cause a burning feeling in your mouth.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hot curry; hot and spicy food; Here we have many restaurants to go [to], so it's hard to have a favourite, but we sometimes go to [the] Delhi restaurant, which serve[s] Indian food, because we like meals [that are] hot [with] various spices.

_source.definition_text: a subject which people discuss and have strong feelings about
_source.learnerexamples_text: The legalization of drugs is a hot topic.; Whether to compete or to cooperate has become a hot issue in today's society, both in public and private.

_source.definition_text: exciting or interesting
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hollywood's hottest new actress; That would mean that Bill Gates is the hottest celebrity on earth, but he is not.

_source.definition_text: a place where you pay to stay when you are away from home
_source.learnerexamples_text: a 4-star hotel; We stayed in/at a hotel on the seafront.; hotel guests; Cracow offer[s] a lot of very nice hotels, restaurant[s] and pubs.

_source.definition_text: a period of 60 minutes
_source.learnerexamples_text: The exam lasted an hour and a half.; The journey took about three hours.; There are 24 hours in a day.; How many hours' sleep do you need?; I'll be back in an hour's/two hours' time.

_source.definition_text: a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I spent hours doing my homework. ; They kept us waiting for hours and hours.; We spent hours talking, but at ten o'clock he [took] me home.

_source.definition_text: very late at night, until early morning, or almost all the time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our neighbours are up till all hours every night, playing loud music.; This causes traffic jams at all hours of the day.

_source.definition_text: the hours between midnight and the time that the sun rises
_source.learnerexamples_text: I usually wake up in the early hours.; After the firework display, villagers start dancing again until the early hours.

_source.definition_text: done or happening every hour
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's an hourly bus service into town.; A nurse checked him at hourly intervals.

_source.definition_text: for each hour
_source.learnerexamples_text: an hourly rate/wage; I'll also call the shop and ask [about] the hourly rate and the working hours.

_source.definition_text: once every hour
_source.learnerexamples_text: Trains stop here hourly.; This train runs hourly and takes about 90 minutes to Kassel which is the second stop.

_source.definition_text: a building where people live, usually one family or group
_source.learnerexamples_text: a three-bedroomed house; to buy/rent a house; We went to my aunt's house for dinner.; Come to my house for dinner tomorrow.

_source.definition_text: the people watching a performance or the area where they sit
_source.learnerexamples_text: The actors played to a full house.

_source.definition_text: to provide space for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The museum houses a huge collection of paintings.; Her study houses a really huge collection of books on history, architecture, [and] geography of the places we have been to.

_source.definition_text: to give a person or animal a place to live
_source.learnerexamples_text: This development will house over 100 families.; In short, if more emphasis is put on social skills and benefits become easier to obtain, then homelessness could be reduced - except for the persons who cannot be housed because of their deviant behaviour.

_source.definition_text: a family or group of people who live together in a house
_source.learnerexamples_text: By the 1960s, most households had a TV.; household chores; household expenses; In Japan, for example, the vast majority of households have at least one car nowadays.

_source.definition_text: a woman whose work is inside the home, doing the cleaning, cooking, etc., and who usually does not have any other job
_source.learnerexamples_text: My grandmother was the perfect housewife.; I have also enjoyed "Desperate housewives", "the O.C" and of course "the Oprah show" recently.

_source.definition_text: the work of keeping a house clean and tidy
_source.learnerexamples_text: I hate doing housework.; I ran out of vegetables and cans, [and] as I was not at home the housework wasn't done, and the children almost destroy[ed] my furniture.

_source.definition_text: buildings for people to live in
_source.learnerexamples_text: a shortage of local housing; The problems with housing can be improved by building more council houses, which can be bought at lower prices, or giving subsidies to first [time] buyers.

_source.definition_text: used to ask someone if they are well and happy
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Hi, Lucy, how are you?" "Fine, thanks, how are you?"; Dear Ramesh, How are you?

_source.definition_text: used to ask or talk about quantity, size, or age
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you know how many people are coming?;  How much was that dress? ;  How big is the house? ;  How old are they? ; How much does it cost?

_source.definition_text: used to ask or talk about the way something happens or is done
_source.learnerexamples_text: How do we get to the town from here?; How did you hear about the concert?; How does this machine work?; Roz doesn't know how to ride a bicycle.; How can/could he be so stupid?

_source.definition_text: used to make a suggestion
_source.learnerexamples_text: How about a drink? ;  How about going to the cinema? ; How about going on Monday evening?

_source.definition_text: used to ask or talk about what an experience or event was like
_source.learnerexamples_text: How was your flight?; How did you find the lecture?; How did you like the concert?; How was your birthday?

_source.definition_text: used to ask about someone's health
_source.learnerexamples_text: How is your mother?; How are you feeling this morning?; How are you feeling? I hope you are feeling better.

_source.definition_text: used for emphasis
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't tell you how pleased I am that you came.; How nice to see you!; I was amazed at how quickly she finished.; It's quite amazing how quickly she could change my reason to learn English.

_source.definition_text: used to ask for someone's opinion on a particular subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: So the town was nice - how about the food?; I don't like shopping with my mum because she wants me to wear weird clothes. How about you?

_source.definition_text: a formal greeting for someone that you have not met before
_source.searchterms_text: how;how do you do;how do you do?
_source.learnerexamples_text: "I'm Jack Stewart." "How do you do? I'm Angela Black."

_source.definition_text: said to mean that something is strange/stupid, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: how;how strange/stupid/weird etc is that;how strange/stupid/weird, etc. is that?
_source.learnerexamples_text: I found my keys in the fridge - how stupid is that?; The best thing is that my current rent is only 2/3 of the old flat and the landlord is paying the facility bills and council tax for me. How good is that?

_source.definition_text: used to ask why or how something has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: How come you didn't go to the party?; Off the record: How come that your reporter can print such lies when knowing they are perhaps hurting certain people in this important matter?

_source.definition_text: used to express anger about something someone has done
_source.searchterms_text: how;how dare she/you etc;how dare she/you, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: How dare you talk to me like that!; How dare you call that high standards?!

_source.definition_text: used to talk about how true something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: How far do politicians represent the views of ordinary people?; How far and to what extent would the characteristics we are born with influence our future development in life?

_source.definition_text: used to say that it does not make any difference how cold/difficult/slowly, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're not going to get there in time, however fast we drive. ; However hungry I am, I never seem to be able to finish off a whole pizza.; If Emma likes something she'll buy it however much it costs.; I'll see you after the show and give you £20 for the tickets, or however much they cost.; We think that we are careful and that we can avoid traffic accidents, but however careful we may be, some other people might be careless and hit us.

_source.definition_text: used when you are about to say something which is surprising compared with what you have just said
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is one possible solution to the problem. However, there are others.; There may, however, be other reasons that we don't know about.; I will be very happy to go fishing and swimming in the lake like the last time. However, if you don't want to do it, it's not a problem for me.

_source.definition_text: in whatever way
_source.learnerexamples_text: However you look at it, it's still a mess.; You can do it however you like, it really doesn't matter.; However you do it, the important part is that you relax.

_source.definition_text: to put your arms around someone and hold them tightly, usually because you love or like them
_source.learnerexamples_text: They hugged each other when they met at the station.; Emily hugged her teddy bear tightly to her chest.; She sat on the floor hugging her knees.; We walked in the street together and spoke [to] each other [for] more than for four hours and at the end we hugged and kissed.

_source.definition_text: when you put your arms around someone and hold them tightly
_source.learnerexamples_text: Come here and give me a big hug.; We always exchange hugs and kisses when we meet.; The singer of the band ,"Green Day" was coming to[wards] me. [He] took my hand and then gave me a hug.

_source.definition_text: extremely large
_source.learnerexamples_text: They live in a huge house.; The costs involved in building a spacecraft are huge.; A huge number of people attended.; I live in a huge old house in the suburbs with my family.

_source.definition_text: to sing without opening your mouth
_source.learnerexamples_text: She walked around the house, humming a song.; Secretly, when nobody can hear them, they hum a little tune or whistle a melody, their faces beam, and their hearts grow warm.

_source.definition_text: relating to people or their characteristics
_source.learnerexamples_text: the human body; human behaviour; The fault was due to human error.; As for me, the last good programme I saw was [a] scientific episode about [the] abilities of the human brain.

_source.definition_text: to not be perfect
_source.learnerexamples_text: Of course Tom makes mistakes - he's only human.;  In theory, it is easy to say "We should learn from the mistakes of the past" but is it easy to do so in practice? Many people would say "No" to this question, as we are only human.

_source.definition_text: connected with improving people's lives and reducing suffering
_source.learnerexamples_text: The UN is sending humanitarian aid to the refugees.; Indeed, the conflicts in the Balkans are so deeply rooted and complex that they can be likened to a political quagmire: once you go in, a withdrawal of humanitarian aid and military forces becomes difficult to undertake.

_source.definition_text: a man, woman or child
_source.learnerexamples_text: The greatest damage being done to our planet today is that being done by humans.; The programm[e]s I have enjoyed recently were about w[h]ales, sharks and humans.

_source.definition_text: all people
_source.learnerexamples_text: The massacre was a crime against humanity.; All humanity enjoys the numerous advances in modern technology and [in] our day, life [has become] more interesting and eas[ier].

_source.definition_text: kindness and sympathy towards others
_source.learnerexamples_text: Mother Teresa was famous for her compassion and humanity.; When he sees Faber's intelligence and humanity, he is once more convinced of the fact that books are a good thing and that they should be preserved rather than destroyed and he decides to fight for this.

_source.definition_text: the condition of being human
_source.learnerexamples_text: War robs these people of their humanity.; At last they will be back home, but they are sure that nobody could give them again that humanity that the war took away.

_source.definition_text: the basic rights that every person should have, such as justice and freedom to say what you think
_source.learnerexamples_text: international laws protecting human rights; My main interest is the way of li[f]e during the so-called French Period; that period is very important for the foundation of human rights and the way parl[ia]ment ought to work.

_source.definition_text: not proud or not believing that you are important
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's very humble about his success.; I am aware that this may be perceived by some people as a naive point of view, as such humble values are becoming less and less popular in today's materialistic world.

_source.definition_text: poor or of a low social rank
_source.learnerexamples_text: She rose from humble beginnings to become Prime Minister.; As a result of it, he never forgot his humble origins in a small region of Spain.

_source.definition_text: used to give your opinion about something, often when you are sure you are right
_source.learnerexamples_text: In my humble opinion, that's the wrong decision.; In my humble opinion, there's no such thing as a uniform celebrity, good, bad or otherwise.

_source.definition_text: Humid air or weather is hot and slightly wet.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's very humid today.; [The] north of Iran is wet but [the] south of Iran is humid and hot.

_source.definition_text: making you feel stupid or ashamed
_source.learnerexamples_text: a humiliating defeat; How humiliating it had been to have her parental abilities questioned.

_source.definition_text: made to feel stupid or ashamed
_source.learnerexamples_text: She felt completely humiliated. ; Never again in my life have I felt so miserable and humiliated.

_source.definition_text: the quality of not being proud or not thinking that you are better than other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: Try to show a little humility.; This growing shopping mania is also said to create an increasingly materialistic society; hence, our children grow up forgetting the basic values of life - simplicity, integrity, humility and plain hard work.

_source.definition_text: the ability to understand funny things and to be funny yourself
_source.searchterms_text: a sense of humour;humour;humours;sense of humour
_source.learnerexamples_text: Carol has a wicked sense of humour.; Most of them have an incredible sense of humour so we laugh a lot when we go there.

_source.definition_text: funny, or making you laugh
_source.learnerexamples_text: a humorous book ; To be more specific, the articles will include events taken from our college life, written in a humorous, chatty way.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being funny
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's a lot of humour in her work.; The film is really exciting with a bit of humour.

_source.definition_text: the way you are feeling, or your mood
_source.learnerexamples_text: good humour ; My mother was the tenderest and the most amiable mother one could have and my father was the man I mostly "loved", thanks to his good humour and his gentle manner.

_source.definition_text: a lot
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hundreds of people wrote in to complain.; When she came back to reality she could see hundreds of people applauding..

_source.definition_text: the number 100
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've driven a/one hundred miles in the last two hours.; "How many children are there in the school?" "About three hundred."; That dress costs hundreds of pounds.; It cost nine hundred yuan at least.

_source.definition_text: the feeling you have when you need to eat
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't believe that that enormous meal wasn't enough to satisfy your hunger.; By about 9 o'clock she started to feel faint from/with hunger.; It [wa]s [what] I expected, a baby crying f[rom] hunger.

_source.definition_text: when you do not have enough food
_source.l_topic_text_text: body and health, food and drink
_source.learnerexamples_text: All over the world, people die of hunger every day.; Many changes are coming and many problems are coming too, because overpopulation, contamination, pollution, hunger, [and] poverty besides come with this technological revolution and that is something that the human being will have to solve soon.

_source.definition_text: a strong wish for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hunger for success/knowledge; The most important factor when learning English is the hunger for knowledge, the hunger for the unknown.

_source.definition_text: wanting or needing food
_source.learnerexamples_text: By four o'clock I felt/was really hungry.; The boys are always hungry when they get home from school.; She often goes hungry herself so that her children can have enough to eat.;  I'm very happy [about] this dinner, because after w[or]k I'm so hungry.

_source.definition_text: to have a strong wish for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The journalists were hungry for more details of the accident.; I am always fascinated with people who are well-educated and do not stop being hungry for information.

_source.definition_text: to chase and kill wild animals
_source.learnerexamples_text: Some animals hunt at night.; Cats like to hunt mice and birds.; As I was saying, you can also go to jungle hotels - comfortable hotels in the middle of the forest, just crossing the Amazon River, where you can keep in touch with nature, feed monkeys and even "hunt" alligators (all sizes, believe me!).

_source.definition_text: to search for something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've hunted all over the place, but I can't find that book.; They are still hunting for the missing child.; I've hunted high and low for my gloves.; Police are hunting the terrorists who planted the bomb.; You don't have to hunt for a place to park your car and to worry what will happen when you're out of gas.

_source.definition_text: a search for something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: After a long hunt we finally found a house we liked.; The hunt for the injured climber continued throughout the night.; What is more, it helps to face problems which could occur during the hunt for a "lifetime" job.

_source.definition_text: the sport of chasing and killing animals
_source.learnerexamples_text: deer hunting; She's very much against hunting of any sort.; And of course hunting won't be allowed.

_source.definition_text: to move or do things more quickly than normal, or to make someone do this

_source.definition_text: to do something more quickly
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hurry up or we'll miss the train.; When I arrived, the other [basketball] club members [were] already dressed, so I had to hurry up.

_source.definition_text: the need to move or do things more quickly than normal

"Yes, I'm not in any hurry/I'm in no hurry."; Are you in a hurry to leave?; What's (all) the hurry (for)/Why (all) the hurry - we've got plenty of time.; "I'll let you have this back next week." "That's all right, there's no (great) hurry/there isn't any (great) hurry ."

_source.base_text: hurry up sb/sth or hurry sb/sth up
_source.definition_text: to make someone do something more quickly, or to make something happen sooner
_source.searchterms_text: hurry;hurry up sb/sth or hurry sb/sth up;hurry up sb/sth or hurry sb/sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you hurry the children up, or their dinner will get cold?

_source.definition_text: to cause pain
_source.learnerexamples_text: Simon hurt his knee playing football.; Emma hurt herself when she fell off her horse.; I hurt myself one week ago so I can't help you but pupils can [put out] chairs and the [other] furniture.

_source.definition_text: to cause emotional pain to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: She criticized my writing quite severely and that hurt.; He was badly hurt by the end of his marriage.; I didn't mean to hurt your feelings.; My heart was hurt and nobody will [be able to] repair the damage.

_source.definition_text: If a part of your body hurts, it feels painful.
_source.learnerexamples_text: My eyes really hurt.; It hurts to walk on it.; I'[m going to] see the dentist, because my tooth is hurting and I really need to go.

_source.definition_text: injured or in pain
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let me help you up. Are you hurt?; Put that knife away before someone gets hurt.; Several people were seriously/badly hurt in the explosion.; There was an accident on the motorway but fortunately nobody was seriously hurt.

_source.definition_text: upset or unhappy

_source.definition_text: the man a woman is married to
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've never met Fiona's husband.; On Sunday afternoon[s], she goes with her husband and her son to the swi[m]ming pool.

_source.definition_text: a small, simple building, often made of wood
_source.learnerexamples_text: a mountain hut; a row of beach huts; Finally, we reached a hut near a river, where we stayed until the following day, when we returned home by bus.

_source.definition_text: very clean, so that bacteria cannot spread
_source.learnerexamples_text: hygienic conditions ; That was not only extremely uncomfortable, but also inconvenient and not very hygienic.

_source.definition_text: the process of keeping things clean, especially to prevent disease
_source.learnerexamples_text: health and hygiene regulations ;  dental/personal hygiene ; The ones that need medical services at home have hardly [got] anyone, and no one has helped them with personal hygiene.

_source.definition_text: a mark (-) used to join two words together, or to show that a word has been divided and continues on the next line
_source.learnerexamples_text: There should be a hyphen in 'short-sighted'.

_source.definition_text: when someone pretends to believe something that they do not really believe or that is the opposite of what they do or say at another time

_source.definition_text: a suggested explanation for something which has not yet been proved to be true

_source.definition_text: If someone is hysterical, they cannot control their feelings or behaviour because they are extremely frightened, angry, excited, etc.

_source.definition_text: used when the person speaking or writing is the subject of the verb

_source.definition_text: water that has frozen and become solid

_source.definition_text: to make people feel more relaxed in a social situation

_source.base_text: be the tip of the iceberg

_source.definition_text: a sweet food made from frozen milk or cream, sugar and a flavour
_source.learnerexamples_text: chocolate/vanilla ice cream; I like chocolate and ice cream with fruit.

_source.definition_text: a game played on ice in which two teams try to hit a small hard object into a goal using long curved sticks

_source.definition_text: to suggest or show something, without saying it directly
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you implying (that) I'm fat?; I'm not implying anything about your cooking, but could we eat out tonight?; I detected an implied criticism of the way he was treated.; I am not implying that the other options will not be to our advantage but I think that this one is what we really need.

_source.definition_text: If one thing implies another, the first thing shows that the second is likely to exist or be true.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Socialism implies equality.; Such mergers do unfortunately imply a massive loss of jobs, not only in Europe but also all over the world.

_source.definition_text: not polite
_source.learnerexamples_text: It is impolite to point at people.; Besides, [the] serving speed was too slow and some waiters were even impolite to customers.

_source.definition_text: used to show that the name of something tells you something about it
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Long Room, as its name implies, runs the entire length of the house.; Sour Sweet, as the name implies, is originally a Chinese restaurant.

_source.definition_text: to buy or bring in products from another country
_source.learnerexamples_text: We import a large number of cars from Japan.; Moreover they say we must be independent of the Near East countries from whom we import oil.

_source.definition_text: a product which is imported from another country
_source.learnerexamples_text: Japanese/American imports; cheap imports from Asia; Furthermore, cheap imports from the newly industrialised countries ha[ve] also contributed to the increase in car ownership.

_source.definition_text: how important someone or something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your views are of great importance to us.; The report stresses the importance of fresh food in a diet.; He emphasized the importance of following safety procedures.; The company recognizes the importance of regular staff training.; Now I know the importance of electricity.

_source.definition_text: when you import something into a country
_source.learnerexamples_text: a ban on the import of beef; One of them, which is the most important for a government, is the import of foreign money.

_source.definition_text: having a lot of power, influence or effect
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was one of the most important writers of that period.; an important person/decision; Recently I've read [two] good books, "La Coscienza di Zeno" and "Uno, Nessuno e Centomila", that are written by Svevo and Pirandello, two of the most important writers of the XX century in Italy.

_source.definition_text: valuable, useful or necessary
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think his career is more important to him than I am.; What are the most important ideas in this text?;  It's important for children to learn to get on with each other.;  The important thing is to keep the heat low or the sugar will burn.; This is not important for me.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is important
_source.learnerexamples_text: If we served more soft drinks, there would be fewer hangovers and, more importantly, fewer drink-driving incidents.; Lastly, and most importantly, what is the cost?

_source.definition_text: to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received
_source.learnerexamples_text: Very high taxes have recently been imposed on cigarettes.; Judges are imposing increasingly heavy fines for minor driving offences.; The council has imposed a ban on alcohol in the city parks.; [An]other advantage is that local governments could receive more money as they impose a fine or ask for a congestion charge.

_source.definition_text: to force someone to accept something, especially a belief or way of living
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't want them to impose their religious beliefs on my children.; We must impose some kind of order on the way this office is run.; Above all, never allow others to impose their ideas on you.

_source.definition_text: when something is impossible
_source.learnerexamples_text: What you're asking just can't be done - it's an impossibility.; Simple tasks like watching television or listening to music become an impossibility when every five minutes or so they get drowned in a sea of noise.

_source.definition_text: If an action or event is impossible, it cannot happen or be done.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was impossible to sleep because of the noise.; It seems impossible that I could have walked by without noticing her.; He made it impossible for me to say no.; I tried to find it but it was impossible!

_source.definition_text: very difficult to deal with
_source.learnerexamples_text: You just can't reason with her, she's absolutely impossible.; We found ourselves in an impossible situation.; I couldn't help laughing at the impossible situation that had resulted from the combination of my personal musings by the side of this wishing-well, and the boy's very straightforward and impulsive character.

_source.definition_text: to cause someone to admire or respect you
_source.learnerexamples_text: He tried to impress me with his extensive knowledge of wine.; All groups did their best to impress the public and every group played professionally.

_source.definition_text: feeling admiration or respect for someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was impressed by her professionalism.; He seemed suitably impressed by our efforts.; I am really impressed by your offer to paint me.

_source.definition_text: the way that something seems, looks or feels to a particular person
_source.learnerexamples_text: It makes/gives/creates a very bad impression if you're late for an interview.; He likes to give the impression (that) he's terribly popular and has loads of friends.; I was afraid of being late or saying something wrong because I really wanted to make a good impression on this man.

_source.definition_text: an idea, feeling or opinion about something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: I didn't get much of an impression of the place because it was dark when we drove through it.; What was your impression of Charlotte's husband?; I don't tend to trust first impressions.; When I first met him I got/had the impression that he was a shy sort of a guy.; You can look back fifty years to get an impression of what changes have happened.

_source.definition_text: Someone or something that is impressive makes you admire and respect them.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's a very impressive public speaker.; That was an impressive performance from such a young tennis player.; an impressive collection of modern paintings; There are some very impressive buildings in the town.; I thi[n]k that the Westfield Music Festival was really impressive.

_source.definition_text: to think or understand a particular stated thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was under the impression (that) you didn't get on too well.; He was under the mistaken impression (that) you were married.; I am under the impression that people generally exercise a little, but if they eat the wrong food every day, it won't help.

_source.definition_text: to put someone in prison or keep them as a prisoner
_source.learnerexamples_text: Taylor was imprisoned in 2005 for burglary.; DMX was a criminal and was imprisoned.

_source.definition_text: when someone is kept in a prison
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was sentenced to five years' imprisonment. ; My brother, John, is just 16 years old, but was sentenced to two years' imprisonment for dealing [in] drugs.

_source.definition_text: to get better or to make something better
_source.learnerexamples_text: I thought the best way to improve my French was to live in France.; Her health has improved dramatically since she started on this new diet.; I'd like to have a pen-friend in Scotland, because [it] is very important for me to improve my English.

_source.definition_text: better than before
_source.learnerexamples_text: improved performance/results;  a new and improved recipe; Emergency centres like hospitals [and] clinics must have the most improved medical devices to [provide] excellent [care] for the citizens.

_source.definition_text: when something gets better or when you make it better
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's been a big/great/huge/major/noticeable improvement in her work this term.; Sadly, Olivia's health has shown no improvement.; Just twenty to thirty minutes riding every day gives you a considerable improvement in your general state of health.

_source.definition_text: a change to something that makes it better
_source.learnerexamples_text: home improvements; It would be a pleasure for me to give you some tips on improvements to the cinema.

_source.definition_text: If there is room for improvement, something can be made better.
_source.learnerexamples_text: His work isn't bad but there's still some room for improvement.; She is Polish, aged 29 and can speak English pretty well, but there is still room for improvement, that's why she wants to spend a year in England, looking after children in an English-speaking family.

_source.definition_text: a sudden feeling that you must do something, without thinking about the results
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her first impulse was to run away.; He is, therefore, a sort of intellectual and represents the force of reason as opposed to the violent impulses of the other boys.

_source.definition_text: suddenly and without thinking first
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tend to act on impulse.; I'm seeing Milly as a capricious girl who, like most teenagers, enjoy[s] buying, although I think that she buys on impulse.

_source.definition_text: Impulsive people do things suddenly, without planning or thinking carefully, but because they want to.
_source.learnerexamples_text: In an impulsive gesture, he threw his arms around her.; Anyway, the fact is that Hara struck me as a quite silly, impulsive and excessively spontaneous girl with no serious intellectual skills and spirit.

_source.definition_text: inside or towards the inside of a container, place or area
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's milk in the fridge.; Is Mark still in bed?; They live in an old cottage.; How much is that coat in the window?; What's that in your hand?

_source.definition_text: during part or all of a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're going to Italy in April.; I started working here in 2007.; Life in the 19th century was very different from what it is now.; She was a brilliant gymnast in her youth.; I haven't had a decent night's sleep in years/ages.

_source.definition_text: needing or using no more time than a particular amount of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you finish the job in two weeks?; Dinner will be ready in ten minutes.; She could get that essay done in a couple of hours if she really tried.; My bedroom isn't too big, so we will finish in 1 hour.

_source.definition_text: forming a part of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He used to be the lead singer in a rock band.; There are too many spelling mistakes in this essay.; I've been waiting in this queue for ages.; My sister sings in a pop group.

_source.definition_text: close to the front part of something or where someone can see or hear you
_source.learnerexamples_text: He parked the car in front of the house.; We can meet in front of the museum.

_source.definition_text: wearing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you recognize that man in the grey suit?; She's always dressed in red.; [T]he man has to be dressed in black.

_source.definition_text: before a particular time, or before doing a particular thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you're going to come, please let me know in advance.; I can help you if you want to book your room in advance.

_source.definition_text: early or at the right time
_source.learnerexamples_text: We arrived in time to catch the train.; If I [don']t come back in time you can put [a] note on my desk.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize what is really true, or to give more information
_source.learnerexamples_text: We met Rebecca for lunch. In fact, we spent the whole afternoon with her.; I was told there were some tickets left but in fact they were sold out.; The club has its own small clubhouse, with many things in it. For example, there was a big pinball-game and some computers. In fact it was the best clubhouse I've ever seen.

_source.definition_text: further forward than someone or something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car in front suddenly stopped and I went into the back of it.; She started talking to the man in front of her.; As the concert finished, I heard someone call my name. I beli[e]ved it was my imagination or perhaps a dream because I couldn't see anyone in front, behind or opposite me.

_source.definition_text: liking someone very much and having romantic or sexual feelings for them
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you ever been in love?; I think I am in love with him.

_source.definition_text: experiencing an emotion or condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's in a bad/good mood this morning.; You're in great danger.; He's living in luxury in the south of France.; I hope you are in a good mood today, because we are planning to go to Cinepolis.

_source.definition_text: arranged or divided in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: We all sat down in a circle.; The desks were arranged in rows of ten.; Discounts are available to people travelling in large groups.; The books on these shelves are arranged in alphabetical order.; We often work in groups where we can talk in English.

_source.definition_text: as well (as)
_source.learnerexamples_text: In addition to his flat in London, he has a villa in Italy and a castle in Scotland.; In addition, I saw a wonderful programme about Aborigines.

_source.definition_text: finally, after something has been thought about or discussed a lot
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were thinking about going to Switzerland, but in the end we went to Austria.; And in the end he invited me to visit him at his house in Miami!

_source.definition_text: completely and with nothing missing
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bill must be paid in full by the end of the month.; Unfortunately, I wasn't able to read the e-mail in full, but as I underst[oo]d, he wanted to apologise [for] what had happened between us many years ago.

_source.definition_text: including or considering all the information about something or every part of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We haven't discussed the matter in detail yet.; The book described her sufferings in great detail.; I'm really sorry that I didn't write back earlier, but to make up for this I will answer your questions in detail!

_source.definition_text: usually, or in most situations
_source.learnerexamples_text: In general, men are taller than women.; In general, the weather here stays sunny.; In general, I like wearing informal clothes, like blue jeans and T-shirts, but sometimes I like wearing formal clothes too.

_source.definition_text: beginning from now

_source.definition_text: crying
_source.learnerexamples_text: I found him in tears in his bedroom.; By the end of it, Mary Anne was nearly in tears.

_source.definition_text: considering the whole of someone or something, and not just a particular part of them
_source.learnerexamples_text: So, apart from the bad ankle, how are you in general?; I think that I, as well as people in general, would have been more depressed if we didn't have light.

_source.base_text: in order (for sb/sth) to do sth
_source.definition_text: with the purpose of achieving something
_source.searchterms_text: in;in order (for sb/sth) to do sth;in order for sb/sth to do sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He came home early in order to see the children before they went to bed.; She worked all summer in order to save enough money.; As you certainly remember, last year I spent three month[s] in England in order to improve my English.

_source.definition_text: to agree with or approve of a plan or idea
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most people are in favour of reducing traffic in cities.; I am certainly in favour of h[o]lding the music festival next year.

_source.definition_text: divided into two equal parts
_source.learnerexamples_text: Cut the potatoes in two.; Divide the dough in half and roll it out into two circles.; They were very surprised when they found the gold was cut in half.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize what is really true, or to give more information
_source.learnerexamples_text: I thought she was Portuguese, but in actual fact she's Brazilian.; Nowadays almost all people own a car and in actual fact more and more people have been facing death as a consequence of careless driving.

_source.definition_text: expressed or written in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: They spoke in Russian the whole time.; Why not do a rough answer in pencil first?; Complete the form in (black) ink.; I also speak in English during the break.

_source.definition_text: especially
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you looking for anything in particular?; I've read a lot of books recently, and in particular I liked: "Eleven minutes" and "Veronica decides to die", written by Paulo Coelho.

_source.definition_text: involved or connected with a particular subject or activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: a degree in philosophy; advances in medical science; I never knew you worked in publishing.; He is my age and we have the same tastes in music and art.

_source.definition_text: because of a possibility of something happening, being needed, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't think I'll need any money but I'll bring some just in case.; Bring a map in case you get lost.; I have my mobile with me just in case.

_source.definition_text: used to give another reason for something you are saying, or that you have done
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't want to go and in any case, I haven't been invited.; I suggest that you should in any case leave your car at home and take buses or other public means of transport.

_source.definition_text: when something happens, or in preparation for when something happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: We keep a bucket of water backstage, in case of fire.; It is about how to rescue people in case of an accident or a natural disaster.

_source.definition_text: because of the mentioned situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's no coffee left? In that case I'll have tea.; You could try [k]ayaking. In that case, of course, you need to pay for the equipment.

_source.definition_text: used when referring to something that is done as a result of something else
