_source.definition_text: used to show the total amount of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Some of the children came, so there were 15 of us in all.; Secondly, even though most people like[d] [the] group RADIANT, they [only] played for 35 minutes in all.

_source.definition_text: using only a few words
_source.learnerexamples_text: world news in brief; In brief, I have had a marvellous week.

_source.definition_text: in someone's opinion
_source.learnerexamples_text: In my parents' eyes, I'll always be a child.; To answer your question right away, the boat trip is highly recommendable in my eyes!

_source.definition_text: used to introduce the last part of a speech or a piece of writing
_source.learnerexamples_text: In conclusion, I would like to thank our guest speaker for her fascinating talk.; In conclusion, swimming is an enjoyable form of exercise and an excellent way to keep fit.; In conclusion, music, TV and clothes are very important in a young person's life and can reflect each person's character.

_source.definition_text: used to say what something is about
_source.learnerexamples_text: I am writing in connection with the above job advertised in The Daily Press on Monday 12th February.; A man has been arrested in connection with last month's murder.; Dear Mrs Brown, I am writing in connection with a surprise birthday party for your husband, Mr Brown.

_source.definition_text: at a suitable time in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: The results will be sent to you in due course.; I look forward to hearing from you in due course.

_source.definition_text: used to explain what something means in a different way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He said he's too busy - in other words he isn't interested.; They had had a great time before and had drunk too much alcohol. In other words, they were totally drunk.

_source.definition_text: towards someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: She keeps looking in my direction.; A player kicked the ball in my direction and I started to think about what I was going to do to catch that ball.

_source.definition_text: An agreement that is in writing is official and is proof of that agreement.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please confirm your reservation in writing.; I [am] tell[ing] you in writing that I would like to help you.

_source.definition_text: without telling other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: For years they met in secret.; We met in secret when Mary was busy.

_source.definition_text: if vegetables or fruit are in season, they are available and ready to eat.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Asparagus is in season at the moment.; They celebrate Halloween in October when pumpkins are in season, that's why in the decorations they include them very often; most of the people carve the pumpkins and put some lights inside.

_source.definition_text: feeling good/excited/unhappy, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: in;in good/high/low etc spirits;in good/high/low, etc. spirits
_source.learnerexamples_text: The whole class was in good spirits that day.; I was in high spirits until I got my paper back.

_source.definition_text: in order to celebrate or show great respect for someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: in;in honour of sb/sth;in honour of sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: a banquet in honour of the president; Finally we went to Corinth, where there are a lot of ancient sanctuaries which were built in honour of their gods.

_source.definition_text: because of
_source.learnerexamples_text: In view of recent events, we have decided to cancel the meeting.; In view of what happened, I would advise you not to try to mislead people like this [again].

_source.definition_text: at the start of a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Why did you invite her in the first place?; In the first place, you were unknown people for me, but now you are my special foreign friends.

_source.definition_text: instead of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Try adding fruit to your cereal in place of sugar.; In the advertisement, it [said] that Danny Brook was starring, but in place of him there was a different actor and he was really disap[p]ointing.

_source.definition_text: If you do something in person, you go somewhere to do it yourself.
_source.learnerexamples_text: You have to collect the document in person.; I am looking forward [to] meeting you in person.

_source.definition_text: If something is true in practice, this is the real situation.
_source.learnerexamples_text: In practice, the new laws have had little effect. ; When you leave school, you have knowledge but you do not know how to use it in practice.

_source.definition_text: in a place where nobody else can hear you or see what you are doing
_source.learnerexamples_text: The meeting was held in private. ; I agree that th[is] should be in private.

_source.definition_text: happening or being done now

_source.definition_text: about or relating to something

_source.definition_text: when compared with something

_source.definition_text: in a particular way, or in many ways

_source.definition_text: as an answer to

_source.definition_text: available in a shop
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you have the book in stock at the moment?; I would like to tell you that I am quite satisfied with the cinema and its customer service, but there is of course some [room] for improvement - for example referring to the cafe, which on the one hand has in stock a huge variety of groceries, but [which] on the other hand [is very] dark.

_source.definition_text: one after another without a break

_source.definition_text: one after another

_source.definition_text: used to talk about a period in the past

_source.definition_text: as a result of something that is part of a series of events

_source.definition_text: in order to collect money for a group of people who need it

_source.definition_text: in the way described by a rule, law, or wish

_source.definition_text: in large amounts

_source.definition_text: working together with

_source.definition_text: wanted or needed in large numbers

_source.definition_text: to be famous and often featured in the media

_source.definition_text: the particular way in which something appears or exists

_source.definition_text: because you want something good to happen

_source.definition_text: used to say what you really think

_source.definition_text: to help someone and give them an advantage

_source.definition_text: If you do something in moderation, you do not do it too much.

_source.definition_text: to have difficulty making a decision

_source.definition_text: not taking help or money from other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: Grandma's very independent and does all her own shopping and cooking.; I've always been financially independent.; I'm an independent person, and I like to be.

_source.definition_text: not influenced or controlled in any way by other people, events or things
_source.learnerexamples_text: an independent enquiry/organization ; The group is independent of any political party.; The film programme is excellent, as you show a large variety of independent films that are not the usual mainstream films and block busters.

_source.definition_text: An independent country is not governed or ruled by another country.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Belize became fully independent from Britain in 1981.; Tibet, once an independent country, is now part of China.; After 1918, our city again became [the] capital of [an] independent state.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is independent
_source.learnerexamples_text: The two scientists both made the same discovery independently, at roughly the same time.; Each part of the organization operates independently of the others.; What students should understand is the existence of links among apparently different subjects and the impossibility of studying them independently or, [worse], studying one and neglecting the others.

_source.definition_text: an alphabetical list, such as one printed at the back of a book showing which page a subject, name, etc. is found on
_source.learnerexamples_text: Try looking up 'heart disease' in the index.; The negative point of the book was its lack of an index.

_source.definition_text: to show that something exists or is likely to be true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Recent evidence indicates that the skeleton is about 3 million years old.; Exploratory investigations have indicated large amounts of oil below the sea bed.; In fact, the study also indicates that time spent on watching TV has surged, especially during the last decade.

_source.definition_text: to say something or give a signal to show what you mean or what you intend to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please indicate which free gift you would like to receive.; She indicated to me (that) she didn't want me to say anything.; I have just received your letter informing me that I won a two week holiday at Camp California, so I am writing to you to indicate my preferences [regarding] travel and accommodation.

_source.definition_text: a sign showing that something exists or is likely to be true
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are strong indications that the case will be referred to the Court of Appeal.; Unfortunately, after the equipment was installed and plug[g]ed into [the] mains, black smoke came out of the back, which in my opinion is an indication of a failure of some sort.

_source.definition_text: a sign showing what someone means or what they intend to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: Helen's face gave no indication of what she was thinking.; Rumour had it that Peter secretly brought roses early every morning to her doorstep, as an indication of his love for her.

_source.definition_text: something that shows what a situation is like
_source.learnerexamples_text: Commodity prices can be a useful indicator of inflation.; The right-wing thinkers claim that unemployment is one of the indicators in [the] economy, displaying lack of balance between industrial output and citizens' demands.

_source.definition_text: when you do not care about something or have any particular opinions about it
_source.learnerexamples_text: an air of indifference; On the other hand, there were some voices expressing their indifference towards money.

_source.definition_text: not caring about or interested in someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are indifferent to the plight of the unemployed.; Being a resident of our area yourself, you may not be entirely indifferent to the plans of the local authorities concerning the construction of a new supermarket.

_source.definition_text: not directly caused by or connected with something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Indirect effects of the fighting include disease and food shortages.; At school, children should follow many rules. For example, they should finish their homework [and] respect other students' opinion[s]. From these experience[s], children can experience social life in indirect ways, and can learn how to be good members of society.

_source.definition_text: done or caused in a way that is not obvious
_source.learnerexamples_text: indirect taxes/costs; an indirect criticism; According to some experts there are just two solutions: delaying the age of retirement or increasing indirect taxes such as VAT.

_source.definition_text: completely necessary
_source.learnerexamples_text: an indispensable tool/guide; She quickly became indispensable to him.; We should not be led to believe that [computers] are the indispensable ingredient to our well-being, [though] neither should we deny their wide-ranging potential.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is not direct
_source.learnerexamples_text: She still controls the company indirectly, through her son.; This indirectly improves the quality of life and people will feel re-energised.

_source.definition_text: considered separately from the other things in a group
_source.learnerexamples_text: Read out the individual letters of each word.; Well, this place is [a group of] small individual islands and there are[n't] many things that you can do [in] the capital city as it's so small and crowded.

_source.definition_text: obviously and certainly true
_source.learnerexamples_text: an indisputable fact; It is an indisputable fact that young people do not have any anxieties as far as housework is concerned because every house is equipped with labour-saving devices.

_source.definition_text: given to or relating to one particular person or thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: We deal with each case on an individual basis.; We all have an individual password.; The first lesson started with an individual presentation.

_source.definition_text: a person, especially when considered separately and not as part of a group
_source.learnerexamples_text: We try to treat our students as individuals.; Every individual has rights which must never be taken away.; I can work as part of a team but also as an individual.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being different from others
_source.learnerexamples_text: The houses had no character and no individuality.; As an intellectual, he refuses to annihilate his individuality and degenerate into savagery.

_source.definition_text: a person with a particular characteristic
_source.learnerexamples_text: a ruthless individual; These are all hard-working individuals.; I realise that his character has changed a little with the passing of time; I can understand that he is nervous and that has turned into a selfish individual who only cares about himself.

_source.definition_text: happening, used or situated inside a building
_source.learnerexamples_text: indoor sports/activities; an indoor swimming pool; We played a lot of indoor games at the party.

_source.definition_text: separately rather than with others
_source.learnerexamples_text: I spoke to them all individually.; The sweets are individually wrapped.; This has the additional advantage that students can work individually on what seems to be most necessary for them.

_source.definition_text: into or inside a building
_source.learnerexamples_text: Come indoors, it's cold outside.; Spring bulbs can be grown indoors.; I love being indoors, eating or watching TV.

_source.definition_text: to let yourself do or have something that you enjoy but which may be bad for you
_source.learnerexamples_text: They indulged in a bit of gossip.; Go on, indulge yourself! Have another chocolate.; Eating disorders of various kinds are certainly not unknown to our culture, yet we seem to be less concerned about what we shouldn't do than what we tend to indulge ourselves in.

_source.definition_text: connected with industry, or having a lot of industry and factories, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: industrial expansion; an industrial landscape; He has an industrial background.; I am sure that both ideas will improve the look of our industrial town.

_source.definition_text: to let someone do or have anything they want
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their children are dreadfully indulged.; In an attempt to give them instant gratification, their parents do their utmost to fulfill their wishes and as a consequence of this, children become utterly indulged.

_source.definition_text: the process of developing industries in a country
_source.learnerexamples_text: Japan's rapid industrialization; With industrialization and economic development, Hong Kong people's standards of living have also improve[d] dramatically.

_source.definition_text: Industrialized countries have a lot of industry.
_source.learnerexamples_text: the industrialized nations; The role of women has changed during the past 100 years but there are still a lot of changes needed not only in developing countries but also in industrialized countries like Germany.

_source.definition_text: Industrious people work hard.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is good at his work and very industrious.; The society wouldn't be as advanced as it is unless we had well educated, efficient and industrious workers.

_source.definition_text: the people and activities involved in one type of business
_source.learnerexamples_text: the gas/electricity industry; the tourist industry; manufacturing industries; The computer industry has been booming.; As you know, I would like to work in [the] tourism industry, so I thought this course could be good to improve my English.

_source.definition_text: the production of goods in factories
_source.learnerexamples_text: trade and industry; industry and commerce; The city needs to attract more industry.; If you are interested in local industry, there is the Prefectural Local Industry museum.

_source.definition_text: Inefficient people or things waste time, money or effort, and do not achieve as much as they should.
_source.learnerexamples_text: an inefficient heating system; The conditions in the coaches are poor with the leg room only for small children, the safety belts broken, and an inefficient air-conditioner.

_source.definition_text: not suitable for eating
_source.learnerexamples_text: The meat was inedible.; The fruit was rotten, the sandwich inedible.

_source.definition_text: when some groups in a society have more advantages than others
_source.learnerexamples_text: inequality between the sexes; She was surrounded by poverty and inequality and grew more and more dissatisfied with the Government's policies, whether internal or foreign.

_source.definition_text: certain to happen and unable to be avoided or prevented
_source.learnerexamples_text: The accident was the inevitable consequence/result/outcome of carelessness.; Strikes always cause some problems but sometimes they are inevitable.

_source.definition_text: in a way that cannot be avoided
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their arguments inevitably end in tears.; Should you, my humble reader, happen to reach fame and fortune, try never to forget that appearing always as an ordinary human being would inevitably grant you more empathy from the people surro[u]nding you.

_source.definition_text: without much experience or knowledge of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Abigail Kennedy was young and inexperienced.; The advertisement said that Danny Brook was one of the starring actors but he was replaced by another extremely disappointing and inexperienced actor.

_source.definition_text: cheap but of good quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: inexpensive children's clothes; It has far more advantages than the countryside, starting with the excellent accommodation, which is inexpensive and easy to find.

_source.definition_text: so strange or unusual that you cannot understand or explain it
_source.learnerexamples_text: To me his behaviour was quite inexplicable.; Although for inexplicable reasons she can be really stubborn sometimes, I admire her courage to admit her mistakes and apologize.

_source.definition_text: when you are a baby or a very young child
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their fourth child died in infancy.; The young musician filled my days of infancy with 'London Bridge is Falling Down.'

_source.definition_text: Something that is in its infancy has only just begun to develop.
_source.learnerexamples_text: In the 1950s, space travel was in its infancy.

_source.definition_text: a baby or very young child
_source.learnerexamples_text: Mothers and infants were allowed to board the plane first.; The cells are extremely active while we are infants, but as we grow older, their efficiency weakens.

_source.definition_text: If a computer virus infects a computer, it harms it
_source.learnerexamples_text: My computer was infected by a virus.; With CLEAN-MAIL, you can protect your computers from getting infected with viruses effectively: virus-mails are deleted before they even arrive at your mailbox.

_source.definition_text: to give someone a disease
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thousands of people were infected with the virus.; It was only a small clinic, that refused to give attention to a group of young people all infected with AIDS.

_source.definition_text: a disease in a part of your body that is caused by bacteria or a virus
_source.learnerexamples_text: a serious infection; a throat infection; Bandage the wound to reduce the risk of infection.; He told me that she was suffer[ing] from [a] kidney infection.

_source.definition_text: If a place, wound, or substance is infected, it contains bacteria or other things that can cause disease.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The wound became infected.; infected water/meat; When the water got too badly infected, your mind could not ignore it any more and got sick.

_source.definition_text: Infectious laughter or feelings quickly spread from one person to another.
_source.learnerexamples_text: infectious enthusiasm; I have found that feelings and emotions are infectious and people tend to be happier with people who are fun-loving and take life less seriously.

_source.definition_text: An infectious disease can be passed from one person to another.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hepatitis is an infectious disease.; For example, epidemic[s] of major infectious diseases like cholera or meningitis carry the risk of transferring the focus of infection to any part of the world.

_source.definition_text: to guess that something is true because of the information that you have
_source.learnerexamples_text: I inferred from the number of cups that he was expecting visitors.; From the above, it can be inferred that the major causes of land degradation var[y] according to regions.

_source.definition_text: not good, or not so good as someone or something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've never felt inferior to anyone.; They're selling inferior products at inflated prices.; Young girls often feel inferior to boys in the same class.

_source.definition_text: someone who is considered to be less important than other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: She considered me her inferior.; Broadly speaking, he appears to be an inferior, a non-human, in the opinion of the other boys.

_source.definition_text: when someone feels they are not as good as other people or when something is not as good as another thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: With these talented sisters, I always had a feeling of inferiority.; Critics suggest that these policies have not benefited poor black Americans, that they have impeded the development of social problems and that they have inhibited black Americans and other discriminated groups through a deep sense of inferiority.

_source.definition_text: extremely large or great
_source.learnerexamples_text: an infinite variety/number of options; She took infinite care with the painting.; An overwhelming selection of goods, shops [and] even types of shopping has provided us with an infinite number of products to choose from.

_source.definition_text: very or very much
_source.learnerexamples_text: Travel is infinitely more comfortable now than it used to be.; It would be infinitely preferable for the people to park their cars in the multi-storey car park.

_source.definition_text: the basic form of a verb that usually follows 'to'
_source.learnerexamples_text: In the sentences 'I had to go' and 'I must go', 'go' is an infinitive.; 'Go' is the infinitive form.

_source.definition_text: the rate at which prices increase, or a continuing increase in prices
_source.learnerexamples_text: high/low inflation; the rate of inflation; 3% inflation; In this country of high inflation we could save some money.

_source.definition_text: the power to affect how someone thinks or behaves, or how something develops
_source.learnerexamples_text: The drug companies can have a lot of influence on doctors.; At the time she was under the influence of her father.; Picasso had a big influence on art in the twentieth century.; Today's computers have a massive influence on the whole [of] society.

_source.definition_text: If someone or something is a bad/good influence on someone, they have a bad/good effect on them.
_source.searchterms_text: be a bad/good influence (on sb);be a bad/good influence on sb;influence;influences
_source.learnerexamples_text: Television can be a bad influence on children.; Some people say that cell phones are a bad influence on the younger generation.

_source.definition_text: to affect or change how someone or something develops, behaves or thinks
_source.learnerexamples_text: Were you influenced by anybody at the beginning of your career?; What influenced you to choose a career in nursing?; Our life has been influenced by modern technology.

_source.definition_text: having a lot of influence
_source.learnerexamples_text: an influential figure in modern jazz ; Although not being directly involved in global politics anymore, he is still a very powerful and influential person.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: If he calls me again, I shall inform the police.; I informed my boss that I was going to be away next week.; This letter is to inform you that I will not be able to attend tomorrow's class due to medical issues.

_source.definition_text: the arrival of a lot of people or things at the same time
_source.learnerexamples_text: The 1990s saw an influx of foreign players into British football.; Countries are known mainly for their history, that is why there is an influx of tourists in places with historical interest.

_source.definition_text: to give someone information about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Patients should be informed about the risks.; Anyway, once a month I read gossip magazines and every day I read newspapers to be informed.

_source.definition_text: not formal or official
_source.learnerexamples_text: The two groups agreed to hold an informal meeting.; He's the ideal sort of teacher - direct, friendly and informal.; 'Hi' is an informal way of greeting people.; The dress-code is informal but neat and there'll be plenty of drinks and snacks.

_source.definition_text: in an informal way
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's an outdoor party, so dress informally.; We dress casually and very informally and you often see body piercings and tat[t]oos being displayed around the place.

_source.definition_text: facts about a situation, person, event, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: to find out/get information; Do you have any information about/on train times?; I read an interesting bit/piece of information in the newspaper.;  For further information, please contact your local library.; We have reliable information that a strike is planned next month.

_source.definition_text: containing a lot of useful facts
_source.learnerexamples_text: a very informative lecture; There were presentations from many different industries, some of them very informative and entertaining.

_source.definition_text: the basic systems and services, such as transport and power supplies, that a country or organization uses in order to work effectively
_source.learnerexamples_text: The war has badly damaged the country's infrastructure.; It is very easy to build homes but at the same time forgetting to upgrade the infrastructure and facilities.

_source.definition_text: a food that is used with other foods in the preparation of a particular dish
_source.learnerexamples_text: The list of ingredients included 250g of almonds.; The chef had used good, fresh ingredients.

_source.definition_text: one of the parts of something successful
_source.learnerexamples_text: Trust is an essential ingredient in a successful marriage.; In my opinion it is clear that with these "ingredients" you can make an interesting video about [daily] life at our school.

_source.definition_text: to live in a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: an area inhabited by artists and writers; The Cranleigh housing estate has [only] been built recently and is mainly inhabited by young families with teenage children who wanted to escape from the rush and the traffic of the city to the pleasant suburb[an] refuge that Cranleigh offers.

_source.definition_text: a person or animal that lives in a particular place
_source.learnerexamples_text: a city of 5 million inhabitants; I think that the town has about 2000 inhabitants in winter.

_source.definition_text: existing as a natural and basic part of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The desire for freedom is inherent in all people.; However, it is important to bear in mind the inherent pressures that come with fortune and fame.

_source.definition_text: to receive money or possessions from someone after they have died
_source.learnerexamples_text: Who will inherit the house when he dies?; All her children will inherit equally.; I wouldn't mind if it was just a scratch to any other [piece of ] furniture but I couldn't contain myself when my mother burst into tears looking at a broken leg of an antique chair inherited from my grandfather.

_source.definition_text: money or possessions that someone gives you when they die
_source.learnerexamples_text: Nick has sold off much of his inheritance.; When they first moved in they seemed to all of us like a "typical" family, not very wealthy but managing to live in the neighbourhood due to the inheritance they had received from Gina's mother.

_source.definition_text: to have the same physical or mental characteristics as one of your parents or grandparents
_source.learnerexamples_text: Miranda has inherited her father's red hair. ; Her grandparents were from Sweden, and she had inherited blond hair and blue eyes from them.

_source.definition_text: a feeling of embarrassment or worry that prevents you from saying or doing what you want
_source.learnerexamples_text: The whole point about dancing is to lose all your inhibitions.; Secondly, parents are the closest and most easily accessible wealth of knowledge. Children lose their inhibitions and freely ask their curious questions.

_source.definition_text: extremely cruel
_source.learnerexamples_text: the inhuman treatment of prisoners; Not very long ago, when some of us thought it wasn't possible anymore, the same terrible inhuman mistakes as in the past [were happening].

_source.definition_text: the first letter of a name, especially when used to represent a name
_source.learnerexamples_text: He wrote his initials, P.M.R., at the bottom of the page.; Paul M. Reynolds refused to say what the initial "M" stood for.; They carved their initials into a tree.; It was black and my initials [were] inside it.

_source.definition_text: first, or happening at the beginning
_source.learnerexamples_text: My initial reaction was one of anger.; Initial reports say that seven people have died, though this has not yet been confirmed.; All this may seem trivial [and] unimportant to an ordinary man addicted to his TV-set, forgetting the initial impulse that made him cho[o]se this way [of life].

_source.definition_text: at the beginning
_source.learnerexamples_text: Initially, most people approved of the new scheme.; The damage was far more serious than initially believed.; He initially disagreed with his wife but after much persuasion, he finally gave in.

_source.definition_text: to make something begin
_source.learnerexamples_text: The reforms were initiated by Gorbachev.; He initiated a restoration of the sports centre in the town where he lives and he donates money [to] charity regularly.

_source.definition_text: a plan or activity that is done to solve a problem or improve a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: a new government initiative to reduce crime; The peace initiative was welcomed by both sides.; Any government as well as grass root initiative will have an effect on pollution problems, but firstly, we need to change our society's overall mentality.

_source.definition_text: the ability to make decisions and do things without needing to be told what to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need someone who can work on their own initiative.; I shouldn't always have to tell you what to do - use your initiative.; She showed a lot of initiative.; It is difficult to judge whether you [show] more initiative than the others or not.

_source.definition_text: to be the first person to do something that solves a problem or improves a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Jackson had taken the initiative and prepared a report.; I took the initiative to contact Sue Wilton, who is the manager of the restaurant "El Plato".

_source.definition_text: when someone puts a drug into your body using a needle
_source.learnerexamples_text: an injection of insulin; This visit was only to be the beginning of it all, as numerous trips to the hospital, fertility clinics, pills and injections soon became a part of their lives together.

_source.definition_text: when a large amount of money is provided for a plan, service, organization, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The university has welcomed the $5 million cash injection.; There are few areas such as the information technology, library resources and overseas visits, that need this financial injection.

_source.definition_text: to hurt a person, animal or part of your body
_source.learnerexamples_text: A bomb exploded at the embassy, injuring several people.; She fell and injured her shoulder.; He was badly/seriously injured in the crash.; Nobody from my family was injured, so that was one good [piece] of news.

_source.definition_text: damage to someone's body in an accident or an attack
_source.learnerexamples_text: a head/back/knee injury; a serious/slight injury; Injuries to the spine are common amongst these workers.; They were lucky to escape (without) injury.; Professional footballers can also have serious injuries during their life as [a] footballer.

_source.definition_text: hurt or physically harmed
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was told to stay in bed to rest her injured back.; Zoos can take care of injured animals and help them.

_source.definition_text: to make someone's bad situation worse by doing something else to upset them
_source.learnerexamples_text: To add insult to injury, we had to pay for the damage!; To add insult to injury, such an approach often turns out to be counterproductive.

_source.definition_text: a situation or action in which people are treated unfairly
_source.learnerexamples_text: the fight against racial injustice; the injustices of the legal system; Adults enjoy the stories too, because it somehow reflects the society that we live in, and how justice is always [on] the stronger side than injustice.

_source.definition_text: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has an innate desire to win.; His innate ability to act as a motivator for other people has helped him obtain excellent leadership skills.

_source.definition_text: a coloured liquid that you use for writing, printing, or drawing
_source.learnerexamples_text: a bottle of ink; blue/black/red ink; Please write in ink, not in pencil.; The book is printed in three different coloured inks.; Her father had shown her once how to write with an invisible ink.

_source.definition_text: on the inside or near the middle of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Leading off the main hall is a series of small inner rooms.; Even in the inner city, streets are dark and don't give the feeling of safety after sunset.

_source.definition_text: Inner feelings or thoughts are ones that you do not show or tell other people.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sarah always seemed to have a deep sense of inner peace.; Every now and then everybody feels an inner call for changes, and one of [those] changes might be a journey somewhere in the world.

_source.definition_text: when someone is not guilty of a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: She pleaded her innocence, but no one believed her.;  She fought to prove her son's innocence. ; They were released after seven years in jail and were determined to prove their innocence and find the real murderer.

_source.definition_text: when someone does not have much experience of life and does not know about the bad things that happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: the innocence of childhood; She has a childlike innocence which I find very appealing.; From the day we're born, our awareness of the world and its people increases. With it comes knowledge and capability but also the loss of innocence.

_source.definition_text: not guilty of committing a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: He firmly believes that she is innocent of the crime.; The plan works: the jury thinks that the wife is a notorious liar and her husband is found innocent.

_source.definition_text: not having much experience of life and not knowing about the bad things that can happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: an innocent young woman; She is so innocent and doesn't understand anything which is happening around [her].

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that someone who was hurt had done nothing wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: Several innocent civilians were killed in the bombing.; While Jem was ste[a]ling horses, his brother was a murderer of innocent people.

_source.definition_text: not intended to harm or upset anyone
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was an innocent mistake.; It was an innocent comment/remark, I didn't mean to hurt his feelings.; On the spur of the moment, I advised him to try it and that's what turned a[n] innocent episode into a nigh[t]mare.

_source.definition_text: in an innocent way
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Have I done something wrong?" she asked innocently.; He said he had obtained the television innocently, not knowing it had been stolen.; Denny had innocently [turned on] the light to see if there was anything of interest in the other room.

_source.definition_text: using new methods or ideas
_source.learnerexamples_text: an innovative approach to programme making; Problems like this will probably app[ea]r again and again but we have to beli[e]ve that they can be solved in an innovative way.

_source.definition_text: a new idea or method that is being tried for the first time, or the use of such ideas or methods
_source.learnerexamples_text: the latest innovations in education; There was a barrage of creativity and innovation rarely seen in human history.

_source.definition_text: ideas, money, effort, etc. that you put into a process or acitivity in order to help it succeed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Input from students is used to develop new and exciting courses.; I could go on but my intention was to give you some input to stimulate your brain!

_source.definition_text: very many, or too many to count
_source.learnerexamples_text: innumerable problems; Due to the fact that sport is given a lot of importance in Switzerland, there are innumerable facilities available.

_source.definition_text: information that is put into a computer or the act of putting information into a computer
_source.learnerexamples_text: Data input is carried out by a team based overseas.

_source.definition_text: to ask for information
_source.learnerexamples_text: Shall I inquire about the price of tickets?; She rang up to inquire when her car would be ready.; "Where are we going?" he inquired politely.; "Say Mary, when did the war beg[i]n?", inquired the old lady.

_source.definition_text: a question that you ask when you want more information
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've been making inquiries about/into the cost of a round-the-world ticket.; Dear Sue, I apologize for not responding to your letter for so long, but I didn't forget to make some inquiries relating to the job in the Water Sports Centre.

_source.definition_text: an official process to discover the facts about something bad that has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: a judicial inquiry; Citizens have demanded a full inquiry into the government's handling of the epidemic.; I am very much surprised that such [problems] had not been foreseen by the public inquiry.

_source.definition_text: the process of asking questions in order to get information
_source.learnerexamples_text: Inquiry into the matter is pointless - no one will tell you anything.; Upon inquiry, it became clear it was in Tim's possession, more precisely in his diary.

_source.definition_text: very silly or stupid
_source.learnerexamples_text: an insane decision; It was an insane idea to accom[m]odate me so far away from the school (approximately four miles).

_source.definition_text: seriously mentally ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hospital for the criminally insane; It seemed as if she had become insane but it was only a way of surviving an impossible situation.

_source.definition_text: a small creature with six legs, for example a bee or a fly

_source.definition_text: a feeling of being lonely
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had this awful sense of isolation.; Unemployment can lead to isolation.

_source.definition_text: a subject or problem which people are thinking and talking about
_source.learnerexamples_text: environmental/moral/personal issues; As employers we need to be seen to be addressing these issues sympathetically.; You're a student so this should be a very important issue for you.

_source.definition_text: the newspaper, magazine, etc. that is produced on a particular day/week/month

_source.definition_text: to disagree with what someone says or writes

_source.definition_text: most important in what is being discussed

_source.definition_text: to officially say something or give someone something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The office will be issuing permits on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.; The school issued a statement about its plans to the press./The school issued the press with a statement about its plans.; Finally, the doctors issued an ultimatum.

_source.learnerexamples_text: I liked it in Scotland.; It's unlikely that she'll arrive on time.; It costs less if you travel at the weekend.; It's [a] nice place.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about the time, date, weather or distances
_source.learnerexamples_text: What time is it?; It was October, so it was quite cold.; It rained all day.; It rained and rained and rained and it really didn't want to stop raining.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize one part of a sentence

_source.definition_text: used as the subject of verbs such as 'seem', 'appear' and 'look'

_source.definition_text: information technology: the use of computers and other electronic equipment to store and send information

_source.definition_text: used to say the name of a person or thing when the person you are speaking to does not know

_source.definition_text: to want to do something very much

_source.definition_text: a single thing in a set or on a list

_source.definition_text: a piece of news on television or radio, or in a newspaper

_source.definition_text: a list of places that you plan to visit on a journey

_source.definition_text: belonging to or relating to something that has already been mentioned

_source.definition_text: the reflexive form of the pronoun 'it'

_source.definition_text: used to put emphasis on a word

_source.definition_text: used emphasize that something is true of one particular thing but that other things may have to be considered

_source.definition_text: a place where criminals are kept as a punishment

_source.definition_text: a short coat

_source.learnerexamples_text: strawberry/raspberry jam; a jar of apricot jam; First we [can] eat some snacks: cheese, jam, toast...

_source.definition_text: something that is stuck in a machine or that prevents the parts of a machine from moving

_source.definition_text: a glass container used for storing food
_source.learnerexamples_text: a jar of coffee/honey; a jam jar; I've already bought them a jar of "Dulce de leche", that I'm sure they will love.

_source.definition_text: the lower part of your face which moves when you open your mouth

I'm a computer operat[o]r. I'm not his wife. It is not my job.

_source.definition_text: now or very soon
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm just coming!; The doctor will be with you in just a minute/moment/second.

_source.definition_text: only; simply
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Would you like another drink?" "OK, just one more."; It was just a joke.; The film is not just about love.; Just because you're older than me doesn't mean you can tell me what to do.; It was just a dream...

_source.definition_text: almost not
_source.learnerexamples_text: This dress only just fits!; We arrived at the airport just in time to catch the plane.; The airplane will arrive at midday, just in time for lunch.

_source.definition_text: exactly or equally
_source.learnerexamples_text: This carpet would be just right for the dining room.; The twins look just like each other.; Things turned out just as I expected.; You've got just as many toys as your brother.; I can't help you just now.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize something you say
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's just dreadful what happened to her.; I just can't bear it!; That is my best place - it is just wonderful.

_source.definition_text: more or less; almost
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Can you see the stage?" "Yes, just about."; I've just about finished painting the living room.; I was just about 2 months [older].

_source.base_text: be just about to do sth
_source.definition_text: to be going to do something very soon
_source.searchterms_text: be just about to do sth;be just about to do sth ;just
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was just about to phone you.; I was so amazed that I didn't realize I was just about to fall into the lake.

_source.definition_text: equally bad/good/tall/clever, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: just;just as bad/good/tall/clever etc as sb/sth;just as bad/good/tall/clever, etc. (as sb/sth);just as bad/good/tall/clever, etc. as sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's just as talented as his brother.; Everywhere he went was just as good as he expected.

_source.definition_text: a little before/over/under, etc. something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: She left just before Michael.; It costs just under £10.; Last autumn I bought a new flat in Siedke which I moved into just before New Year's Eve.

_source.definition_text: used to say that it is lucky that something happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's just as well we brought an umbrella.; It is just as well that my friends had cars to give me a lift to the school.

_source.definition_text: at the same time as
_source.learnerexamples_text: She woke up just as we got there.; Just as I was turning on the radio somebody knocked at the door.

_source.base_text: I/you/we, etc. will just have to do sth
_source.definition_text: used to say that there is nothing else someone can do
_source.searchterms_text: i/you/we etc will just have to do sth;i/you/we, etc. will just have to do sth;just
_source.learnerexamples_text: You'll just have to wait.; We will just have to wait and see.....

_source.definition_text: fair or morally right
_source.learnerexamples_text: a just society; He is really involved in what he is doing and does not fear [facing] the difficulties if it is to defend a just cause.

_source.definition_text: behaviour or treatment that is fair and morally correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's no justice in the world when people can be made to suffer like that.; The winner has been disqualified for cheating, so justice has been done.; Both of them symbolize courage, [a] love of justice, [and a] fight for freedom, which makes them look like heroes.

_source.definition_text: the system of laws which judges and punishes people
_source.learnerexamples_text: The justice system in this country consists of a series of law courts at different levels.; The police are doing all they can to bring those responsible for the bombing to justice.; They are victims of a miscarriage of justice.; I hope by the time I [am] out of prison, [the] justice [system] will have changed.

_source.base_text: do sb/sth justice; do justice to sb/sth
_source.definition_text: to show the best or real qualities of something or someone
_source.searchterms_text: do sb/sth justice do justice to sb/sth;do sb/sth justice; do justice to sb/sth;justice;justices
_source.learnerexamples_text: This postcard doesn't do justice to the wonderful scenery.; No words can do justice to the indignation that I feel.

_source.definition_text: having a good reason
_source.learnerexamples_text: justifiable anger; Thus, we can understand that this attitude to reading is, to some extent, justifiable.

_source.definition_text: a reason for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's no justification for treating her so unfairly.; Unfortunately that day, I took the diary with me, although there was no justification for taking it because I was just going to visit my grandparents and I had no intention of staying there more than one day.

_source.definition_text: to give or to be a good reason for
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't really justify taking another day off work.; Are you sure that these measures are justified?; The fact that you want to be the best in your job does not justify your attitude.

_source.definition_text: fair or having a good reason
_source.learnerexamples_text: justified criticism; He's perfectly justified in asking for a salary increase.; Finally, I would strongly recommend that steps are taken to remedy matters and feel we are justified in requesting partial compensation.

_source.definition_text: If you justify yourself, you give a good reason for what you have done.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was the only thing that I could do - I don't have to justify myself to anyone.; How we can justify ourselves, when we are completely against captivity?

_source.definition_text: a large Australian animal that moves by jumping on its back legs
_source.learnerexamples_text: Kangaroos are a danger on the roads.; Furthermore it has been my dream since I was five years old to see a kangaroo and play with it.

_source.definition_text: by, for, or relating to young people
_source.learnerexamples_text: juvenile crime ; Among many aspects of crime, researchers have been keenly studying juvenile crime.

_source.definition_text: very interested or enthusiastic
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's a keen tennis player.; She's keen on (playing) tennis.; We are both quite keen on sailing and skiing.

_source.definition_text: wanting to do something very much
_source.learnerexamples_text: The shop is keen to attract new customers.; He is very keen to write [a] report about crime.

_source.definition_text: very good or well developed
_source.learnerexamples_text: a keen sense of smell; Furthermore, she has a keen sense of humour and does not mind a practical joke, which is an advantage with children.

_source.definition_text: to have something permanently or for the whole of a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you want this photograph back or can I keep it?; I can't keep the sofa because [it] is too big.

_source.definition_text: to regularly store something in a particular place
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep sth in/on etc;keep sth in/on, etc.;keeping;keeps;kept
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep medicines in a locked cupboard.; We'll keep your application on file.; All my homework sheets were kept in that file.

_source.definition_text: to (cause to) stay in a particular place or condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: I wish you'd keep quiet.; I like to keep busy.; Keep left/right at the traffic lights.; It was difficult for us to keep warm, as the house had no heating.; He goes jogging twice a week to keep fit.

_source.definition_text: to continue doing something without stopping, or to do it repeatedly
_source.learnerexamples_text: He keeps trying to distract me.; I kept hoping that he'd phone me.; I don't know why I wanted to meet her so much but my heart just kept telling me to go after her.

_source.definition_text: to communicate or continue to communicate with someone, for example by email or telephone
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've kept in touch by email for the last five years.; Please keep in touch with me.

_source.definition_text: to delay someone or prevent them from doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's very late, what's keeping him?; She kept me talking on the phone for half an hour.; Don't let me keep you from your work.

_source.definition_text: to not tell anyone a secret/ about something secret
_source.learnerexamples_text: Mr Brown apparently delayed the announcement, and managed to keep it secret from the entire cabinet.; I [had] loved Sean since sixth grade but I was keeping it a secret.

_source.definition_text: to be late so that someone has to wait for you
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry to have kept you waiting.; The dentist kept me waiting for ages.; A week later, when we were going to have our second lesson, she kept us waiting for almost an hour.

_source.definition_text: to do what you have promised to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: James kept his promise and repaid all of the money he had borrowed.; She didn't keep her promise and she ruined my life.

_source.definition_text: to write something down in order to remember it
_source.learnerexamples_text: Remember to keep a record of how much you spend.; Furthermore, a computer helps us to keep records by saving file[s].

_source.definition_text: to watch or look after someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you keep an eye on this pan of soup for a moment?; You have to supply [e]verything they need and keep an eye on them all the time.

_source.definition_text: If food or drink keeps, it remains fresh.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Once opened, this product will keep for three days if refrigerated.

_source.definition_text: to have and look after animals
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our neighbours keep chickens.; It is cruel to keep dogs, cats, [and] birds in flats.

_source.definition_text: to stay with someone so that they are not alone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Come and keep me company, Isabel.; I wish you came and kept me company.

_source.definition_text: to remember to consider someone or something that may be useful in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll keep you in mind if another job comes up. ; But we should keep in mind that books improve our vocabulary and, what's more, our imagination.

_source.definition_text: to continue to know about someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He changes jobs so often I can’t keep track any more.; Be sure to keep track of the time so you won't be late.; Trying to keep track of these changes by translating them would be an inappropriate task.

_source.definition_text: to do what you said you would do
_source.learnerexamples_text: He agreed to come and I'm sure he'll keep his word.; It turned out that the company that had been hired to organize it did not keep their word.

_source.definition_text: to provide what someone needs for a short period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dinner is at eight, but I had an apple to keep me going.; Because of health concerns, advertisements lately show the people in Holland how important it is to have a good breakfast and that it will keep you going the whole day.

_source.definition_text: to provide enough money for someone to live
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't keep a family on that salary.; The economy ha[d] been developed and people could earn money in order to keep the family.

_source.base_text: keep an eye out for sb/sth
_source.definition_text: to watch carefully for someone or something to appear
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep an eye out for sb/sth;keeping;keeps;kept
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep an eye out for the delivery van.; Although individually we try to deliver the best care possible for our individual patients, we do keep an ear or an eye out for the other members of the team that day.

_source.definition_text: to remain calm
_source.learnerexamples_text: You did well to keep your cool in all that panic.; Whatever the problem is, keep your cool, don't panic.

_source.definition_text: to move or develop at the same speed as someone or something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have to keep pace with the changing times.; It was first published a century ago and what amazes people most is that [it] keeps pace with the development of the country without leaving out references to our history and tradition.

_source.definition_text: to make certain that someone always knows what is happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep me posted on anything that happens while I'm away.; We will keep our members posted on the best eating places in town.

_source.definition_text: to watch carefully for someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep your eyes open (for sb/sth);keep your eyes open for sb/sth;keeping;keeps;kept
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep your eyes open for anything unusual.; It has helped us identify and successfully combat many a nutritional hazard, keeping our eyes open to immoderate consumption of some substances and its effects.

_source.definition_text: to try not to be noticed
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has kept a low profile since the divorce.; Finally, I believe that the best way to handle these issues is to try to keep a low profile at all times and to remain indifferent to gossip.

_source.definition_text: to be able to pay for your food, clothing and somewhere to live
_source.learnerexamples_text: His wages are barely enough to keep body and soul together.; Not only does he keep body and soul together, but he is [o]n good terms with his wife.

_source.definition_text: to watch carefully for someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep your eyes peeled (for sb/sth);keep your eyes peeled for sb/sth;keeping;keeps;kept
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep your eyes peeled, he should be here any minute.; Ever since, I try to keep my eyes peeled for anything similar.

_source.definition_text: to manage to stop yourself from smiling or laughing
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can never play jokes on people because I can't keep a straight face.

_source.base_text: keep your fingers crossed/ cross your fingers
_source.definition_text: to hope that things will happen in the way that you want them to
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep your fingers crossed/ cross your fingers;keeping;keeps;kept
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's keep our fingers crossed that she gets the job.; We're crossing our fingers and hoping that the weather stays fine.; Wish me luck, Winnie," she sighed "keep your fingers crossed, please".

_source.definition_text: to remain calm in a difficult situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: To be successful in business, you need to keep a cool head in negotiations.; Kevin managed to keep a cool head and took over the navigation.

_source.definition_text: to have just enough money to live or to continue a business
_source.learnerexamples_text: With extra income from private sponsorship, the club is just about managing to keep its head above water.; I also started to realise how much she had on her plate, how very little help she had and how, at times, she had to struggle just like me to keep her head above water.

_source.definition_text: to not talk about something that is secret
_source.learnerexamples_text: It might be wise to keep this quiet for a while.; They tried to keep it quiet but, somehow, half the village knew about the news in a few days.

_source.definition_text: to succeed in staying calm and not becoming angry
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't discuss this with you unless you promise to keep your temper.; He never offends people and he keeps his temper even if someone insults him.

_source.definition_text: to make sure that someone gives all their attention to what they are doing and is ready for anything that might happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have random inspections to keep everyone on their toes.

_source.definition_text: to continue working hard at something difficult
_source.learnerexamples_text: Learning a language is hard but you've just got to keep at it.; Despite the fact that it requires patience, one should not work oneself up into a frenzy but keep at it.

_source.definition_text: to not go somewhere or near something, or to prevent someone from going somewhere or near something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I told them to keep away from the edge of the cliff.; The traffic must be kept away from the centre of our town.

_source.definition_text: to not go near something, or to prevent someone or something from going past a particular place
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police struggled to keep the crowd back.

_source.definition_text: to not tell someone everything you know about a situation or an event
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was sure she was keeping something back.

_source.base_text: keep down sth or keep sth down
_source.definition_text: to stop the number, level, or size of something from increasing
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep down sth or keep sth down
_source.learnerexamples_text: I have to exercise to keep my weight down.; That's also a way of keeping down the many accidents we have from fast cycling.

_source.definition_text: to prevent someone or something from doing something
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep sb/sth from doing sth;keep sb/sth from doing sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Try to keep the children from throwing food all over the floor.; I really must say that I do not agree [with] introduc[ing] an entrance fee, as this would keep many students from coming to the sports centre.

_source.definition_text: to not tell someone about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is there something you're keeping from me?; They kept it from me.

_source.definition_text: to make a child stay inside, often as a punishment, or to make someone stay in hospital
_source.learnerexamples_text: She kept the children in as it was so cold.

_source.definition_text: to not go onto an area, or to stop someone or something going onto an area
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep (sb/sth) off sth;keep (sb/sth) off sth ;keep sb/sth off sth;keep sb/sth off sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep off the grass.

_source.definition_text: to stop something touching or harming someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep sth off (sb/sth);keep sth off sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He put a cloth over the food to keep the flies off.

_source.definition_text: to continue to do something, or to do something again and again
_source.learnerexamples_text: She kept on asking me questions the whole time.; I kept on looking for him outside my building and in the park, but I still [haven't found] him.

_source.definition_text: to not go into a place, or to stop someone or something from going into a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: The building was unsafe so they put up a sign saying 'Danger - Keep out'.

_source.definition_text: If you keep something to yourself, you do not tell anyone else about it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She usually keeps her opinions to herself.; She kept her thoughts to herself, her best friend being her diary.

_source.definition_text: If you keep to a plan/subject/path, etc., you stay with it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We must keep to the agenda or the meeting will take too long.; I wish you'd keep to the point!; She kept to the main roads and was home before dark.; I suffer from stomach-ache and have to keep to a diet.

_source.base_text: keep up sth or keep sth up
_source.definition_text: to not allow something that is at a high level to fall to a lower level
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep up sth or keep sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep up the good work!; Make sure you eat properly - you've got to keep your strength up.; I joined because I wanted to keep up [my] English and also, to learn some more.

_source.definition_text: to increase or make progress at the same speed as something or someone else so that you stay at the same level as them
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep up (with sth);keep up with sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Prices have been rising very fast and wages haven't kept up.; We need more and more of our natural [resources] to be able to keep up with the rise in population.

_source.definition_text: to move at the same speed as someone or something that is moving forward so that you stay level with them
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep up (with sb/sth);keep up with sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was walking so fast I couldn't keep up with her.; Unfortunately he was too fast and I couldn't keep up with him.

_source.definition_text: to be able to understand or deal with something that is happening or changing very fast
_source.searchterms_text: keep;keep up (with sb/sth);keep up with sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's important to keep up with international news.; I live in London and I have to keep up with Turkish news for my job.

_source.definition_text: to continue without stopping or changing or to continue something without allowing it to stop or change
_source.learnerexamples_text: People are having difficulties keeping up the repayments on their loans.; The reason why a person becomes homeless is that he or she is not able to pay the rent or fails to keep up the mortgage payments.

_source.definition_text: a person who takes care of animals or is in charge of valuable objects, a building, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a zoo keeper; a lighthouse-keeper; Tina was confused because she wasn't a dragon keeper, so normal[l]y dragons didn't speak with her.

_source.definition_text: a covered metal or plastic container with a handle and a shaped opening for pouring, used for boiling water
_source.learnerexamples_text: If I have an electric kettle in my bedroom, I won't need to go to the kitchen.

_source.definition_text: short for goalkeeper
_source.learnerexamples_text: The keeper intends to stay with the club until the end of next season.; He is a very good keeper - before he play[ed] football, he was in a karate club.

_source.definition_text: a piece of metal cut into a particular shape that is used for opening or closing the lock of a door, starting a car engine, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: car/door/house keys; I left my keys at your house.

_source.definition_text: a list of answers to an exercise or game
_source.learnerexamples_text: See key to Test 3 on page 176.

_source.definition_text: one of the parts that you press with your fingers on a computer or musical instrument to produce letters, numbers, symbols or musical notes
_source.learnerexamples_text: Press the shift key to write in capital letters.; piano keys; What is more, you can get the information you need in just one second by pressing the "enter" key [o]n a computer.

_source.definition_text: a way of explaining or achieving something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hard work is the key to success.; To those who say that money can't buy happiness I answer that money is a key to happiness.

_source.definition_text: very important in influencing or achieving something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was a key figure in the international art world.; a key factor in tackling the problem; Unfortunately one day I decided that it was time to become more independent and I didn't ask a key question.

_source.definition_text: to be very important in influencing or achieving something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Early diagnosis is key to your chances of surviving.; Distribution is key to achiev[ing] economic growth and the positioning of domestic and imported goods.

_source.base_text: key in sth or key sth in
_source.definition_text: to put information into a computer using a keyboard
_source.searchterms_text: key;key in sth or key sth in
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got all the data now but it still needs to be keyed in.; Just key in the appropriate information and in a few seconds you will receive prices and conditions.

_source.definition_text: a set of keys that you press to use a computer
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got a new keyboard and mouse for my computer.; COMPUTER [FOR SALE] It's one year old so I [will] give you the monitor and keyboard.

_source.definition_text: an electrical musical instrument similar to a piano, or the set of keys on a piano or similar musical instrument
_source.learnerexamples_text: Steve plays keyboards, drums, and saxophone.; I play two instruments, so I can help you with the concert, playing guitar or keyboard.

_source.definition_text: to hit someone or something with the foot, or to move the feet and legs suddenly and violently
_source.learnerexamples_text: I kicked the ball as hard as I could.; He was accused of kicking a man in the face.; I picked up a ball and kicked it, [and] the dog ran after it with the phone still in his mouth.

_source.definition_text: to start to be effective or to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: The new tax rate kicks in next month.; It is at this time that the hormones start to kick in resulting in most of them having to suffer the side effects.

_source.definition_text: to be very annoyed with yourself for doing something stupid or wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: I could have kicked myself for saying that.; Nevertheless what kept me kicking myself was that this time my partner was in danger as well.

_source.definition_text: When you kick off a discussion or activity, you start it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Shall we kick off the session with a presentation from Lisa?

_source.definition_text: When a football match or other event kicks off, it starts.
_source.learnerexamples_text: What time does the match kick off?

_source.definition_text: to force someone to leave a place or organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: His wife kicked him out.; He will kick you out of his house without thanking you.

_source.definition_text: the action of kicking something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She gave him a kick under the table to shut him up.; We [practiced] shooting, passing the ball to each other, and [taking a] corner kick.

_source.definition_text: a special feeling of excitement and energy
_source.learnerexamples_text: She gets a kick out of performing live.; I really get a kick out of anything which concerns magic.

_source.definition_text: one of the two organs in your body which remove waste from the blood and produce urine
_source.learnerexamples_text: kidney failure/disease; Her kidneys didn't work well enough to keep her healthy and someone had to be found who could give one of his kidneys to her.

_source.definition_text: a child
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took the kids to the park while I was working.; Even small kids came and had fun.

_source.definition_text: to cause someone or something to die
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her parents were killed in a plane crash.; Smoking can kill.; Food must be heated to a high temperature to kill harmful bacteria.; I like it because you must kill a lot of monsters.

_source.definition_text: used to say that someone will be very angry with someone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dad will kill me for being late.; It's very important to find it because if not my mother will kill me!

_source.definition_text: to do something while you are waiting for something else to happen or have nothing else to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: We killed time playing video games.; When you are at home alone and have nothing to do, you can kill time watching television.

_source.definition_text: to cause you a lot of pain or effort
_source.learnerexamples_text: My feet are killing me.; It wouldn't kill you to tidy up occasionally.; I didn't have enough room to move and the seat belt was broken so when we finally arrived [in] Edinburgh my back was killing me.

_source.definition_text: to stop an activity or experience completely
_source.learnerexamples_text: His remark killed the conversation.

_source.definition_text: someone who kills another person
_source.learnerexamples_text: Police are still hoping to find the dead woman's killer.; I opened the window to take a breath of fresh air and I saw the man again, the killer, smoking a cigarette and looking at me.

_source.definition_text: when a person is murdered
_source.learnerexamples_text: a series of brutal killings; During the film there were a lot of explosions, killings and action scenes.

_source.definition_text: a kilogram
_source.learnerexamples_text: a 200 kilo block of concrete; We danced a lot, and I think everybody has lost 2 kilos.

_source.definition_text: a unit of mass equal to 1000 grams, or 2.2 pounds
a unit of measurement equal to 1000 metres
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's five kilometres [from] my house.

_source.definition_text: a type of thing or person
_source.learnerexamples_text: What kind of music do you like?; Today's vehicles use two kinds of fuel - petrol and diesel.; Her travel company was the first of its kind.; My favourite kind of music is rock.

_source.definition_text: used to show that what you have just said is only an example from a larger group of things
_source.learnerexamples_text: I like pasta, pizza - that kind of thing.; I enjoy that kind of thing, going to buy presents.

_source.definition_text: many different types of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The cupboard contained all kinds of strange things.; To help, I could bring all kinds of CDs.

_source.definition_text: used to describe something approximately
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a kind of shed.; He was kind of half laughing and half crying.; I know that the Frene Hotel is kind of expensive, but it's just for one night so I think we can make it.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about something when you are not sure of its exact type
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has some kind of disability.; You should try joining some kind of club.

_source.definition_text: used to describe someone or something that is completely different from other people or things
_source.learnerexamples_text: My Dad was one of a kind - funny, kind and generous.; Pele is indeed one of a kind and can be considered a model for youngsters.

_source.definition_text: generous, helpful and thinking about other people's feelings
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's a very kind and thoughtful person.; It's really kind of you to help us.; Please be kind to your sister!; [I]t's very kind of you to find an Australian pen-friend for me!

_source.definition_text: in a kind way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stella has very kindly offered to help out with the food for the party.; He answers my simple questions kindly.

_source.definition_text: to not like something that someone says or does

_source.definition_text: the quality of being kind
_source.learnerexamples_text: love and kindness; Thank you again for your kindness and hospitality.

_source.definition_text: (the title of) a male ruler of a country, who holds this position because of his royal birth
_source.learnerexamples_text: King Richard II; the kings and queens of England; The French kings lived at Versailles.

_source.definition_text: the best or most important person in a particular activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's the new king of pop music.; He is the king of football, which is not at all an exag[g]eration, even though he is retired now.

_source.definition_text: a country ruled by a king or queen
_source.learnerexamples_text: the kingdom of Sweden; The kingdom Chosun lasted until the beginning of [the] 20th century.

_source.definition_text: all animals or plants considered together
