_source.definition_text: to press your lips against another person's lips or skin to show love or affection
_source.learnerexamples_text: She kissed him on the mouth.; He kissed the children good night/goodbye.; I danced, drank a lot and kissed a girl.

_source.definition_text: an act of kissing someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Give your granny a big kiss.; a kiss on the lips; Then she gave me her address and gave me a sweet kiss.

_source.definition_text: a set of clothes worn for sport
_source.learnerexamples_text: football kit; Yesterday when I came to your house, I left my tennis kit.

_source.definition_text: a collection of things kept in a container for a particular use
_source.learnerexamples_text: a first-aid/tool kit; I would rather buy a big travel kit, including a first-aid kit.

_source.definition_text: a room where food is kept, prepared and cooked and where the dishes are washed
_source.learnerexamples_text: We usually eat breakfast in the kitchen.; the kitchen table; a new fitted kitchen ; I think my bag is in your kitchen.

_source.definition_text: a toy made from paper or cloth which flies in the air on a long string
_source.learnerexamples_text: We spent the morning flying a kite in the local park.; I got a lot of presents: a kite, a ball, shoes, a T-shirt, trousers, jeans, and a dog.

_source.definition_text: a young cat
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our cat's had two kittens.

_source.definition_text: to go down into, or stay in, a position where one or both knees are on the ground
_source.learnerexamples_text: She knelt (down) beside the child.; He knelt in front of the altar and prayed.; Robert knelt down by her, prono[u]ncing the simple words "Will you marry me?"

_source.definition_text: the middle part of your leg where it bends
_source.learnerexamples_text: a knee injury; The baby was crawling around on its hands and knees.; He got/went down on his knees in front of the altar.; He entered the living room drunk and with blood over his knee.

_source.definition_text: a sharp tool, usually with a metal blade and a handle, used for cutting and spreading food or other substances, or as a weapon
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fish/butter/steak knife; I prefer to use a knife and fork.; He drew/pulled a knife and stabbed her.; I want to sell a beautiful old knife, because it doesn't cut anything.

_source.definition_text: women's underwear that covers the bottom
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was one time when Pat and I had a fight. It all started when I accident[al]ly took the wrong bag back to my house, and there w[ere] lad[ies'] knickers inside.

_source.definition_text: to make clothes, etc. by using two long needles to connect wool or another type of thread into joined rows
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's forever knitting.; She's busy knitting baby clothes.; My granny knitted me some gloves/knitted some gloves for me.; I would really like to learn how to knit sweaters and hats.

_source.definition_text: a round handle, or a round button on a machine
_source.learnerexamples_text: a door knob ;  Turn the black knob to switch on the radio. ; It's so obvious that when we turn a knob on or when we switch on something [and] there is no electricity, we are at a loss!

_source.definition_text: to repeatedly hit something, making a noise
_source.learnerexamples_text: She knocked on the window to attract his attention.; There's someone knocking on/at the door.; Please knock before entering.; On Monday, a person knocked on my door.

_source.definition_text: to hit, especially forcefully, and cause to move or fall
_source.learnerexamples_text: He accidentally knocked the vase off the table.; She knocked her head against the wall as she fell.; She took a hammer and knocked a hole in the wall.; Falling down, I knocked my head on the pa[v]ement.

_source.definition_text: to hit someone with a vehicle and injure or kill them
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was knocked down by a bus.; The man explained that Lime was knocked down by a car and that he died immediately.

_source.definition_text: to make someone become unconscious, usually by hitting them on the head
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was knocked out halfway through the fight.; Chris knocked him out with a strong punch without doubting that he was a criminal.

_source.definition_text: to destroy a building or part of a building
_source.learnerexamples_text: They've knocked down the old cinema.; Since many of the office building are almost empty I also think that we should have them knocked down and replaced by green parks or other areas where no cars are to be allowed.

_source.definition_text: to defeat a person or team in a competition so they cannot take part any more
_source.learnerexamples_text: The French team were knocked out in the semi final.

_source.definition_text: to hit or push something or someone, especially accidentally, so that they fall to the ground or onto their side
_source.learnerexamples_text: I knocked a bottle of wine over while I was reaching for a dish.; He banged into me so hard that he nearly knocked me over.; I knocked over the girl's cup, which was still full of milk.

_source.definition_text: a place where one or more pieces of string, rope, etc. have been tied
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tie a knot in the rope.; The man was always wearing a shabby coat and a big red scarf which was tied in a very complicated knot.

_source.definition_text: to get married
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're planning to tie the knot in April.; She was going to tie the knot in July.

_source.definition_text: to have knowledge or information about something in your mind
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Where did he go?" - "I don't know."; "What does it cost?" - "Ask Kate. She'll know."; She knows the name of every kid in the school.; I don't know anything about this.; We don't know when he's arriving.

_source.definition_text: used to ask someone to tell you a piece of information
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you know the time?; Do you know where the Post Office is?; Do you know why?

_source.definition_text: to be able to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you know how to ski?; I only know a little Spanish.; Some people know how to play the guitar.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let me know if you're coming to the party.; I just want to let you know that we are going to use blue paint because I really like blue.

_source.definition_text: to be certain
_source.learnerexamples_text: I know (that) she'll be really pleased to hear the news.; I don't know whether I should tell her or not.; I can't find the information, but I know the class is on Tuesday.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize what you are saying, or used before you start to talk about someone or something, or used as something to say while you are thinking what to say next
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm not stupid, you know!; You know the bookshop next to the bank? Well, it's closing down.; It's, you know, supposed to be a surprise on her birthday.

_source.definition_text: to be familiar with or have experience and understanding of
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've known Daniel since we were at school together.; She grew up in Paris so she knows it well.; I've seen the film 'Casablanca' so many times that I know a lot of it by heart.; Knowing Sarah, she'll have done a good job.; I knew him in London, and when I knew him I was very happy.

_source.definition_text: to spend time with someone or something so that you gradually learn more about them
_source.searchterms_text: get to know sb/sth;get to know sb/sth ;knew;know;knowing;known;knows
_source.learnerexamples_text: The first couple of meetings are for the doctor and patient to get to know each other.; I'll need a few weeks to get to know the system.; I hope you can come here and get to know him.

_source.definition_text: If you know a subject, you are familiar with it and understand it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you know about computers?; If you want to know more about Peruvian history, I recommend you [visit] the city because you can see the old houses and museum[s].

_source.definition_text: used to say that you think something is true, but cannot be sure
_source.learnerexamples_text: As far as I know, he's never been in trouble with the police.; As far as I know, accommodation at Camp California is in tents or log cabins.

_source.definition_text: to have the intelligence or judgment not to do something
_source.searchterms_text: knew;know;know better (than to do sth);know better than to do sth;knowing;known;knows
_source.learnerexamples_text: She should have known better than to eat so much. No wonder she feels sick now.; I should have known better but I had to tell it to someone.

_source.definition_text: used when you agree with something someone has just said
_source.learnerexamples_text: "It's a lovely day, isn't it?" "I know - let's hope it lasts."

_source.definition_text: very soon
_source.learnerexamples_text: We'll be there before you know it.; It is a bit dark inside and especially in winter, it is dark before you know it.

_source.definition_text: used when you have an idea
_source.learnerexamples_text: I know - let's go to Helen's house.

_source.definition_text: to know everything about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He knows the system inside out.; The participants got to know Britain inside out and they are happy with the knowledge they gained.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something could be possible although it does not seem likely
_source.learnerexamples_text: You never know - you might win the lottery.; You never know, maybe I'll find something interesting and I'll change my point of view.

_source.definition_text: used when you are saying something that someone already knows
_source.learnerexamples_text: As you know, we have been trying to contact him.; As you know, I am in New York.

_source.definition_text: to guess something correctly
_source.learnerexamples_text: I should have known he wouldn't come.; I should have known that he wouldn't understand.

_source.definition_text: to have enough experience not to do something stupid or something that will not achieve anything
_source.learnerexamples_text: I thought she'd listen to me - I should have known better.; Surely two grown-ups should have known better than to shout at each other at the top of their lungs.

_source.definition_text: to be the most suitable person to have responsibility and make important decisions
_source.learnerexamples_text: When it comes to dealing with my own son, I think I know best.; How true is that expression "Father knows best". If my father [was alive] today he would probably be laughing his head off.

_source.base_text: know what you are talking about
_source.definition_text: to understand a subject because of your experience
_source.searchterms_text: knew;know;know what you are talking about;knowing;known;knows
_source.learnerexamples_text: He doesn't know what he's talking about - he's never even been to Africa.; I beli[e]ve that you don't really know what you're talking about.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about part of a story that happens in a sudden and surprising way
_source.searchterms_text: knew;know;knowing;known;knows;next thing i knew;the next thing i knew

_source.definition_text: to have heard of something or someone and have a little information about them

_source.definition_text: to know a lot about a subject, or to be very good at doing something

_source.definition_text: information and understanding that you have in your mind

_source.definition_text: showing that you know what another person is really thinking
_source.learnerexamples_text: He smiled knowingly.; On staring at the picture, he saw two women smiling enigmatically, rather knowingly.

_source.definition_text: used to say that you think that something is true, but cannot be sure
_source.searchterms_text: knowledge;to (the best of) my knowledge;to the best of my knowledge

_source.definition_text: something that a lot of people know

_source.definition_text: knowing a lot

_source.definition_text: knowledge about something which is good enough to be useful
_source.searchterms_text: a working knowledge of sth;knowledge;working knowledge of sth

_source.definition_text: recognised or known about by most people

_source.definition_text: to be called

_source.definition_text: one of the parts of your finger where it bends

_source.definition_text: a laboratory
_source.learnerexamples_text: a science/computer lab; a lab technician; There are computer labs too.

_source.definition_text: a company which produces goods for sale, the goods themselves, or the company's name or symbol

_source.definition_text: to fix a small piece of paper or other material to something which gives information about it

_source.definition_text: to describe the qualities of someone or something using a word or phrase, usually in a way that is not fair

_source.definition_text: an activity that is hard work but which you do because you enjoy it
_source.searchterms_text: a labour of love;labour;labour of love;labours

_source.definition_text: a boy or young man

_source.definition_text: a piece of equipment which is used to reach high places, consisting of short steps fixed between two long sides

_source.definition_text: a large area of water which has land all around it

_source.definition_text: a young sheep, or the flesh of a young sheep eaten as meat

_source.definition_text: a piece of equipment that produces light
_source.learnerexamples_text: a table/bedside lamp; an oil lamp; I think it is next to the lamp.

_source.definition_text: an area of ground, especially when used for a particular purpose such as farming or building

_source.definition_text: the surface of the Earth that is not sea

_source.definition_text: a country

_source.definition_text: a man who you rent a room or house from

_source.definition_text: an event which is famous or important in the history of something

_source.definition_text: a building that you can easily recognize, especially one that helps you to know where you are

_source.definition_text: the appearance of an area of land, especially in the countryside

_source.definition_text: secret information that has intentionally been told to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: There have been several leaks to the press.

_source.definition_text: to move the top part of your body in a particular direction
_source.searchterms_text: lean;lean (sth) back/forward/out, etc.;lean sth back/forward/out etc;lean sth back/forward/out, etc.;leaned;leaning;leans;leant
_source.learnerexamples_text: She leaned forward and whispered in my ear.; He was leaning out of the window.; Lean your head back a bit.; John loved figures, combining them into long lines, counting them and solving difficult problems. And he had a secret. He saw numbers in different colours. [...] John tried to hide his papers with a book but Mr. Robinson leaned forward and whispered: "My number one is always red".

_source.definition_text: to rest against something for support, or to move something into this position
_source.searchterms_text: lean;lean (sth) against/on sth;lean sth against/on sth;leaned;leaning;leans;leant
_source.learnerexamples_text: She leaned her head on his shoulder.; His spade was leaning against the fence.; She turned around and saw this boy leaning against the wall.

_source.definition_text: to try to make someone do what you want by threatening or persuading them
_source.learnerexamples_text: I suspect that he took the decision because he was leant on.; Piggy is the most intelligent boy of the group, but he doesn't have the streng[th] to apply his ideas to the situation they are living [in], that is why he leans on Ralph (the perfect leader-type, as he sees him).

_source.definition_text: to accept the chance to have or do something with enthusiasm
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd leap at the opportunity to work in Japan. ; I was offered a job abroad, a hig[h]ly paid one, and I decided to leap at the chance and avail myself [of] this Godsent opportunity!"

_source.definition_text: to suddenly move somewhere
_source.searchterms_text: leap;leap into/out of/up etc;leap into/out of/up, etc.;leaped;leaping;leaps;leapt
_source.learnerexamples_text: He leapt out of his car and ran towards the house. ;  I leapt up to answer the phone. ; At the split second the man rings the bell, there are over a 100 people suddenly leaping up from behind the desk.

_source.definition_text: a sudden improvement or increase
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was a big leap in profits last year. ;  This represents a great leap forward in technology. ; Ultimately, we could be taking a "giant leap" towards technological excellence.

_source.definition_text: If progress or growth happens in leaps and bounds, it happens very quickly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her Spanish has come on in leaps and bounds this year.; To begin with, it is undeniable that technology, which is developing in leaps and bounds, has contributed to the wide range of goods that we enjoy nowadays.

_source.definition_text: to make yourself remember a piece of writing by reading it or repeating it many times
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't know how actors manage to learn all those lines.; We were told to learn Portia's speech by heart for homework.; He was a very famous and popular actor. He's very funny and he shows us very useful tricks to [help us] learn our roles.

_source.definition_text: to get knowledge or skill in a new subject or activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: They learn Russian at school.; "Can you drive?" "I'm learning."; I've learned a lot about computers since I started work here.; I'm learning to play the piano.; First you'll learn (how) to use this machine.

_source.definition_text: to be told facts or information that you did not know
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were all shocked to learn of his death.; I later learnt (that) the message had never arrived.; I only learnt about the accident later.; I was pleased to learn that you are coming to Switzerland.

_source.definition_text: to start to understand that you must change the way you behave
_source.learnerexamples_text: She'll have to learn that she can't have everything she wants.; She soon learnt not to contradict him.; He's not afraid to learn from his mistakes.; I am sure that the organis[e]rs will learn from their mistakes and that next year you will enjoy it.

_source.definition_text: someone who is getting knowledge or a new skill
_source.learnerexamples_text: learners of English; She is very shy, so her Japanese didn't improve very rapidly, but she was a very industrious learner.

_source.definition_text: the process of getting knowledge or a new skill
_source.learnerexamples_text: language learning; This technique makes learning fun.; For the first month in her new job she was on a steep learning curve.; Th[ese] events are not only to entertain students, they are also a part of the learning process, as by communicating with each other, students learn the language.

_source.definition_text: as much as, or more than, a number, amount, distance, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It will cost at least £500.; You'll have to wait at least an hour.; I can write at least once a week.

_source.definition_text: even if nothing else happens or is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you can't manage to clean the whole house, at least make sure the kitchen is clean.; We could go shopping or at least go and have an ice-cream somewhere.

_source.definition_text: something that you say when you are telling someone about an advantage in a bad situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a small house but at least there's a garden.; It is not impressive but at least it has some things that I like.

_source.definition_text: used to reduce the effect of a statement
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've met the President - at least, he shook my hand once.; But after years of developing my slalom, I wanted to learn something new, [s]o, I started Hot-Dogging. Hot-Dog is great fun. At least, people say so.

_source.definition_text: less than anything or anyone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: I chose the least expensive dish on the menu.; This group is the least likely of the four to win.; Disaster struck when we least expected it.; It was the answer she least wanted to hear.; Every day was the same and I thought that nothing w[ould] change but I was wrong - something changed and that something happen[e]d on the day I least expected it to.

_source.definition_text: something that you say to introduce the last person or thing on a list
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is Jeremy, this is Cath and, last but not least, this is Eva.; And, last but not least, some complaints were made [about] the entertainment the café provides.

_source.definition_text: especially
_source.learnerexamples_text: The whole trip was fascinating, not least because of the people I met.; We are all human beings but we are all different, not least because of a different cultural background.

_source.definition_text: less than anyone or anything else
_source.learnerexamples_text: He contributed least to the workshop.; I like the green one least of all.; He's the relative I like (the) least.; Giving her a bed for the night was the least I could do.; Taking you to the airport was the least I could do for such a good friend.

_source.definition_text: not at all
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't mind staying at home, not in the least.; Educating two children was not so easy a task, not in the least!

_source.definition_text: not less than, and probably much more than
_source.learnerexamples_text: At the very least, you should apologize.; We should earn £500 at the very least.; Thus, I trust you will agree that at the very least I deserve a letter of explanation from you and a substantial refund of my money.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that you could have said something in a much stronger way
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were surprised, to say the least.; You get slightly bored, to say the least.

_source.definition_text: the smallest amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: She earns the least money of all of us.; I spent the least time on the third question.; My favourite way to travel is by plane, because I think that the most important point when you are travelling is to arrive [at] your destination in the least time.

_source.definition_text: the skin of animals that is used to make things such as shoes and bags
_source.learnerexamples_text: a leather jacket/belt/handbag; And I g[o]t teddy bears, a cool leather jacket, and a pretty bag.

_source.definition_text: to go away from a place or a situation, either permanently or for a temporary period
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bus leaves in five minutes.; I'll be leaving at seven o'clock tomorrow.; He left the house by the back door.; She left the group of people she was with and came over to speak to us.; "Does Trevor still work there?" "No, he left last month."

_source.definition_text: to put something in a place and forget to take it with you when you go
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hey, you've left your keys on the table.; That's the second umbrella I've left on the train!; I think I have left my umbrella in the bathroom.

_source.definition_text: to put something in a place where it will stay
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can leave your bags at reception.; Why don't you leave the kids with me on Friday?; Can you take my sunglasses and leave [them] in my house today?

_source.definition_text: to put something somewhere for another person to have later
_source.learnerexamples_text: I left some sandwiches for them to have later.; Can I leave a message for Sue?; I will leave a short message for you.

_source.definition_text: to not use all of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They'd eaten all the cake but they'd left some biscuits.; Are there any sandwiches left?; If you're having a bath, make sure you leave enough hot water for the rest of us.; Could you please help me to find out if there [are] any place[s] left [on the course].

_source.definition_text: to cause something to stay in a particular condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: Leave that chair where it is.; Don't leave any lights on, will you?; I'll have to go back - I think I've left the iron on.; You can leave the window open.; And I heard my husband shouting: "Mag, do you always have to leave all the lights on?"

_source.definition_text: to end a relationship with a husband, wife, or partner and stop living with them
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll never leave you.; She left him for a younger man.; Jose, who is a bus driver, was very unhappy, because his girlfriend [had] left him.

_source.definition_text: to stop speaking to or annoying someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Leave me alone! I'm trying to work.; I asked [him] to leave me alone and [un]plugged the phone.

_source.definition_text: to produce a particular, often bad, situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Far from improving things, the new law has left many people worse off than before.; Storms have left areas of Britain without electricity.; The family were left homeless.; He was born on a ranch in Jalisco, the fourth of eight children, and when the youngest was only six months old, my grandfather died, leaving the family penniless.

_source.definition_text: to do something later that you could do immediately
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't leave your packing till the night before you go.; I'll leave these letters till Monday.; Don't leave it too late.; They left booking their holiday till/to the last minute.; I left it until the following day since I was too worn out to go on.

_source.definition_text: to arrange for someone to receive something after you die
_source.learnerexamples_text: He left his nieces all his money./He left all his money to his nieces.; "I hate him", Jane thought, "and [I wonder] why on earth Uncle John left him all his money and the most beautiful estate in our country with this old manor house, in which all my ancestors were born."

_source.definition_text: If you leave something or someone doing something, you allow them to continue doing it, or they continue doing it when you go away.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I left the children watching television.; She also has the tendency to leave the children doing what they want, sometimes without realising the consequen[c]es.

_source.base_text: leave someone to their own devices
_source.definition_text: to leave someone to do what they want to do
_source.searchterms_text: leave;leave someone to their own devices;leaves;leaving;left
_source.learnerexamples_text: With both parents out at work, the kids were often left to their own devices.; The moment teenagers leave school, they are left to their own devices.

_source.base_text: leave behind sb/sth or leave sb/sth behind
_source.definition_text: to leave a place without taking someone or something with you
_source.searchterms_text: leave;leave behind sb/sth or leave sb/sth behind
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were in a hurry and I think I must have left my keys behind.; He got out of the country, but had to leave his wife and son behind.; I know you must be disappointed [at] having to move, leaving all your friends behind, but it's OK, I'm sure you'll make new ones.

_source.definition_text: to do everything that you can in order to achieve something or to find someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Both sides have vowed to leave no stone unturned in the search for peace.; She has left no stone unturned so as to reach her [goal], always asserting her assets and views with conviction.

_source.definition_text: time allowed away from work for holiday or illness
_source.learnerexamples_text: How much annual/paid leave do you get?; She's (gone) on leave.; I've asked if I can take a week's unpaid leave.; It was from him, her lover, and told her that he was on leave and would come to visit her.

_source.base_text: leave out sb/sth or leave sb/sth out
_source.definition_text: to not include someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: leave;leave out sb/sth or leave sb/sth out
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can leave the butter out of this recipe if you're on a low-fat diet.; I've made a list of names - I hope I haven't left anyone out.; None of the other children play with her, and I think she feels rather left out.; She felt so left out.

_source.definition_text: a formal talk on a serious or specialist subject given to a group of people, especially students
_source.learnerexamples_text: We went to a lecture on Italian art.; Who's giving the lecture this afternoon?; The film will start at 9.30pm, so you could reach us after your lectures at the university in the pub near the cinema.

_source.definition_text: to give a formal talk to a group of people, often at a university
_source.learnerexamples_text: She travelled widely throughout North America lecturing on women's rights.; For ten years, she lectured in law.; He was also lecturing at the local university and really knew what he was talking about in respect to the underwater world.

_source.definition_text: a long white and green vegetable that smells and tastes similar to an onion
_source.learnerexamples_text: leek soup; I had some roasted chicken pieces with some leek and broccoli and roasted potatoes and Jan had his favourite spaghetti with cream sauce.

_source.definition_text: someone who teaches at a university or college
_source.learnerexamples_text: a lecturer in psychology ; In addition, my lecturers can't give me particular explanations for my questions.

_source.definition_text: to the side of your body that is west when you are facing north
_source.learnerexamples_text: Turn left at the lights.; When you go out of Kilburn station, you turn left and you go straight.

_source.definition_text: on or towards the side of your body that is to the west when you are facing north
_source.learnerexamples_text: His left eye was heavily bandaged.; Tomorrow I must to go to the doctor because of my left leg, I can't walk any more.

_source.definition_text: on or to the left of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's a sign on the left-hand side.; When the bus arrives at City Hall, you can jump out, and my house is [on the] left-hand side by City Hall.

_source.definition_text: the left side of your body, or the direction towards this side
_source.learnerexamples_text: First I'll introduce the speaker sitting on my left.; Take the first/second/third on the left.; It's the shop to the left of the pub.; It's on the left.

_source.definition_text: relating to the belief that wealth and power should be shared equally
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is interested in left-wing politics.; Women's politics are usually followed by the left-wing parties in Austria.

_source.definition_text: one of the parts of the body of a human or animal that is used for standing and walking
_source.learnerexamples_text: My legs were tired after so much walking.; He broke his leg skiing.; The horse broke its front leg in the fall.; He has broken his leg and I must look after him.

_source.definition_text: money or property that you receive from someone after they die
_source.learnerexamples_text: An elderly cousin had left her a small legacy.; So, soon after I agreed to receive the great legacy from my great aunt with joy, I realised that a problem would occur accordingly.

_source.definition_text: a situation that was caused by something from an earlier time
_source.learnerexamples_text: The war has left a legacy of hatred.; Many of his novels deal with the social and political problems facing his country, including the difficulty of the post-colonial legacy.

_source.definition_text: relating to the law
_source.learnerexamples_text: legal advice; a legal obligation/requirement; your legal rights; Unless I hear from you within ten days, I shall have to take legal advice on the matter.

_source.definition_text: allowed by the law
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is abortion legal in your country?; Can anybody say how any enterprise should or must work? Is it legal?

_source.definition_text: a legal process in a court
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are planning to take legal action against the company.; If we do not get a satisfactory answer to this letter, apologising and offering the compensation that the students deserve, we will have no other option but to take legal action.

_source.definition_text: as stated or allowed by the law
_source.learnerexamples_text: Children under sixteen are not legally allowed to buy cigarettes.; He already had a driving licence, so by that time he could legally drive his own Ferrari.

_source.definition_text: a famous person
_source.learnerexamples_text: a living legend; Jazz legend, Ella Fitzgerald, once sang in this bar.; The audience at the London Palladium was much more quiet, partly because we were in a theatre, partly because everyone was spe[e]chless in front of such a living legend.

_source.definition_text: an old story or set of stories from ancient times
_source.learnerexamples_text: The dance was based on several Hindu legends.; She is writing a thesis on Irish legend and mythology.; Legend has it that he always wore his boots in bed.; You know I'm fond of medieval tales and legends, so while we're in Scotland, let's visit a haunted castle!

_source.definition_text: from a legend
_source.learnerexamples_text: a legendary Greek hero ; The last article concerned Hercules, the legendary hero.

_source.definition_text: famous for being excellent
_source.learnerexamples_text: the legendary guitarist Jimi Hendrix;  He became editor of the legendary Irish journal, 'The Bell'. ; If I went back to the beginning of [the] 70s, then I would probably have [had] a chance to work with Bill Gates and his 'legendary crew'.

_source.definition_text: a law or a set of laws
_source.learnerexamples_text: The government has promised to introduce legislation to limit fuel emissions from cars.; And while governments have taken measures to reduce emission of fuels into the atmosphere and prevent toxic waste from being discharged into the oceans, the existing legislation is not rigorously enforced.

_source.definition_text: reasonable and acceptable
_source.learnerexamples_text: He claimed that the restaurant bill was a legitimate business expense.; Not even when he mentioned acts of violence as a legitimate way of ach[ie]ving one's goals did she react.

_source.definition_text: allowed by law
_source.learnerexamples_text: The army must give power back to the legitimate government.; After all, Ralph has the conch, which symbolizes legitimate power, and has been democratically elected.

_source.definition_text: the time when you are not working
_source.learnerexamples_text: leisure activities; Most people only have a limited amount of leisure time.; The town lacks leisure facilities such as a swimming pool or squash courts.; Reading is my favourite leisure activity. I've already read fifteen books this year.

_source.definition_text: an oval, yellow fruit that has sour juice
_source.learnerexamples_text: lemon juice; For this recipe you need the juice of two lemons.; Would you like a slice of lemon in your tea?; We drink juice and tea with lemon.

_source.definition_text: a cold drink with a lemon flavour that is sweet and has bubbles
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like a glass of lemonade, please.; We drank lemonade and talked about you.

_source.definition_text: If a bank lends money, it gives money to someone who then pays the money back in small amounts over a period.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bank refuses to lend to students.; The bank agreed to lend him $5000.

_source.definition_text: to give something to someone for a short period of time, expecting it to be given back
_source.learnerexamples_text: She doesn't like lending her books.; If you need a coat I can lend you one/lend one to you.; I like pop music, and I can lend you some pop music cds.

_source.definition_text: the measurement or distance of something from one end to the other
_source.learnerexamples_text: The boat is ten metres in length.; The length of the bay is approximately 200 miles.; The new one has a length of 2.10 metres.

_source.definition_text: to be suitable for a particular purpose
_source.searchterms_text: lend;lend itself to sth;lend itself to sth ;lending;lends;lent
_source.learnerexamples_text: The novel's complex, imaginative style does not lend itself to translation.; Last but not least, the fact that he managed to reconquer the realm of rock music for the German tongue lends itself to be[ing] displayed, together with similar efforts by bands like Aurhefu, who achieved a similar "resurrection" for the Welsh language.

_source.definition_text: the amount of time something takes
_source.learnerexamples_text: the length of a film/speech/play; He is unable to concentrate on his work for any length of time.; We will need you to start the talk at 7:00 p.m. with a length of one hour.

_source.definition_text: the amount of writing in a book or document
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's written books of various lengths on the subject.; All of your essays will be about the same length.

_source.base_text: the length and breadth of sth
_source.definition_text: in every part of a place
_source.searchterms_text: length;length and breadth of sth;lengths;the length and breadth of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: They travelled the length and breadth of Scotland together.; It is the reason that we can easily see the foreigners wandering [the] length and breadth [of] the museum being unaware of the origin of items they look at.

_source.definition_text: If you talk about something at length, you talk for a long time.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We discussed both topics at length.; Since we have already arranged for your family to come to stay in my home and discussed the arrangements at length and in detail, I will no longer bother you with terms of payment and other information that, judging by your letter, seems to be quite irrelevant.

_source.definition_text: to not allow someone to become too friendly with you
_source.searchterms_text: (keep sb) at arm's length;keep sb at arm's length;length;lengths
_source.learnerexamples_text: I always had the feeling she was keeping me at arm's length.; At first she keeps them at arm's length, but Mr Emerson is direct and advises Lucy to behave in a more natural way instead of doing what some old ladies say.

_source.definition_text: to become longer or to make something longer
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are plans to lengthen the school day.; Furthermore, I suggest [...] that you lengthen the stay in Cambridge which was definitely too short.

_source.definition_text: continuing for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: a lengthy discussion/process; Many airline passengers face lengthy delays because of the strike.; It is worth watch[ing] because it is a really lovely story and you can gain a lot of optimism from it by realising that problems are not always as big as they seem to be, but as it is a soap opera it is extremely lengthy.

_source.definition_text: a large wild cat that has yellow fur with black spots on it and lives in Africa and southern Asia
_source.learnerexamples_text: We saw leopards in their natural habitat.; We saw different kinds of animals like a leopard, a buffalo and so on.

_source.definition_text: A lenient punishment is not severe.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He asked the judge to pass a lenient sentence.; The Court had been too lenient towards his detested father.

_source.definition_text: not as much
_source.learnerexamples_text: Exercise more and eat less.; Getting out of bed in summer is less difficult than in winter.; I prefer summer [clothes] because they're less heavy than the winter ones.

_source.definition_text: almost or approximately
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've more or less finished work on the house.; He more or less admitted he'd done it.; The new window will cost £500 more or less.; I will [now] give you some information, so that you know more or less what you can expect.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that someone is not interested in or worried about something or someone
_source.searchterms_text: i/he etc couldn't care less;i/he, etc. couldn't care less;less
_source.learnerexamples_text: I couldn't care less what people think.; There was hunger, there was poverty and the king couldn't care less about his people['s] well-being.

_source.definition_text: not as much
_source.learnerexamples_text: We must try to spend less money.; I drink less coffee than I used to.; All the clothes cost me £60.50 so now I have less money.

_source.definition_text: not as much
_source.learnerexamples_text: I earn less than my brother.; My books cost less than the regular price.

_source.definition_text: to become less or to make something less
_source.learnerexamples_text: Exercise and a healthy diet lessen the chance of heart disease.; Strengthen the legs and it lessens the strain on the knees.; Should you give back the students' money and take into consideration our complaints, I am sure that you will lessen our disappointment.

_source.definition_text: an experience which teaches you how to behave better in a similar situation in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: There is a lesson for all parents in this tragic accident.; My parents made me pay back all the money and it was a lesson I never forgot.; We can learn important lessons from this disaster.; I think he learned a valuable lesson.

_source.definition_text: a period of time when a teacher teaches people
_source.learnerexamples_text: How can we make science lessons more interesting?; She has never had/taken any acting lessons.; He gives French lessons.; One lesson take[s] 45 minutes.

_source.definition_text: to punish someone so that they will not behave badly again
_source.learnerexamples_text: The next time she's late, go without her. That should teach her a lesson.; He didn't want to hurt Diane just teach her a lesson.

_source.definition_text: to decide not to do something again because it has caused you problems in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm not going out without my umbrella again - I've learnt my lesson!; She learnt her lesson and she won't go out before [an] exam any more.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone something
_source.searchterms_text: let;let sb know (sth);let sb know sth;lets;letting
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you still come on Friday? Please let me know.; I'll let you know when we've fixed a date for the meeting.; Please let me know as soon as possible.

_source.definition_text: something that you say when you are making a suggestion
_source.learnerexamples_text: After the film, let's go out to dinner.; Let's not argue.; Let's go shopping.

_source.definition_text: to allow someone to do something, or to allow something to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: She wanted to go but her parents wouldn't let her.; He decided to let his hair grow long.; Let your shoes dry completely before putting them on.; I'm letting you stay up late, just this once.; Don't let it worry you.

_source.definition_text: to stop holding someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: let;let go (of sb/sth);let go of sb/sth;lets;letting
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hold onto the rope and don't let go!; I let go of the feather and it floated to the ground.; I kicked that man as hard as I could and it worked - he let go of my mouth to hold between his legs and then I screamed with a voice w[h]ich could only be compared [to] Tarzan's.

_source.definition_text: to allow someone or something to move to a particular place
_source.searchterms_text: let;let sb/sth in/past/through etc;let sb/sth in/past/through, etc.;lets;letting
_source.learnerexamples_text: They won't let us past the gate.; The roof lets in a lot of rain.; I had got so drunk that I could not control myself, so the doorman would not let me in.

_source.definition_text: to stop thinking about or being angry about the past or something that happened in the past
_source.searchterms_text: let;let go (of sth);let go of sth;lets;letting
_source.learnerexamples_text: I have tried to let go of the past.; You've been storing up these feelings for years, and it's time to let go now.; It was obvious to me that he had had a hard time letting go of the past.

_source.definition_text: something that you say when you are offering to help someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let me carry your cases.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that something is more impossible than another thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: You couldn't trust her to look after your dog, let alone your child.; We are surrounded by amazing pieces of technology which we do not fully understand, let alone use to their full capacity.

_source.definition_text: something that you say when the truth is unpleasant but must be accepted
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's face it, we're not getting any younger.; Let's face it, we live in an era dominated by machines.

_source.definition_text: to relax when you should be careful or ready to deal with something

_source.definition_text: able to cause death

_source.definition_text: a written message that you send to someone, usually by post

_source.definition_text: a plant with large green leaves, eaten raw in salads

_source.definition_text: a symbol that is used in written language and that represents a sound in that language

_source.definition_text: the amount or number of something

_source.definition_text: someone's ability compared to other people

_source.definition_text: flat or horizontal

_source.definition_text: legally responsible

_source.base_text: be at liberty to do sth

_source.learnerexamples_text: a public/university library; a library book; It's important because I want some books from the library, [and] without [a] library card [I] can't take any [out].

_source.definition_text: to be in or move your body into a horizontal position

_source.definition_text: a cover on a container, which can be lifted up or removed

_source.definition_text: to be on a particular surface

_source.definition_text: to be in a particular place or position

_source.definition_text: If responsibility, blame, a decision, a choice, etc. lies with someone, they have responsibility, must make the decision, etc.

_source.definition_text: to move into a position in which your body is flat, usually in order to sleep or rest

_source.definition_text: to say or write something which is not true in order to deceive someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you lying to me?; Don't trust her - she's lying.; I suspect he lies about his age.; She lied [to] me and said she could not come with me because she had work.

_source.definition_text: something that you say which you know is not true

_source.definition_text: everything which is alive
_source.learnerexamples_text: human/marine/plant life; Recently, I've enjoyed watch[ing] programmes about sea life.

_source.definition_text: the time between a person's birth and their death

_source.definition_text: a way of living

_source.definition_text: the manner in which a person lives

_source.definition_text: the existence of a person

_source.definition_text: energy or enthusiasm

_source.definition_text: for the whole of someone's life

_source.base_text: a matter of life and/or death

_source.definition_text: for all of your life

_source.definition_text: If something happens as a matter of course, it always happens as part of the normal process or system.
_source.searchterms_text: a matter of course;matter;matter of course;matters
_source.learnerexamples_text: Babies were tested for the disease as a matter of course.; The transform[ation] has succeeded so far and caused enormous changes in ordinary life as a matter of course, including eating habits.

_source.base_text: it's only a matter of time

_source.searchterms_text: it's only a matter of time;matter;matters
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's only a matter of time before someone gets killed on this road.; In my opinion it is only a matter of time before it is decided to [put] an end to this country being a kingdom.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that something cannot be changed

_source.definition_text: If a subject is no laughing matter, it is serious and not something that people should joke about.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This weather is no laughing matter.; Anna and Tom knew this was no laughing matter.

_source.definition_text: If something is a matter of confidence/luck/waiting, etc., that is what you need for it to happen.

_source.definition_text: a particular type of substance or thing

_source.base_text: a matter of life and/or death

_source.searchterms_text: a matter of life and/or death;matter;matter of life and/or death;matters

_source.definition_text: used in expressions describing how small an amount or period of time is

_source.definition_text: the smallest amount that is allowed, needed, or possible

_source.learnerexamples_text: coal/salt mining; My company deals mostly with the mining, processing and benefic[i]ation of magnesite ore. Most of our final products are sold abroad.

_source.definition_text: a member of the government in Britain and many other countries who is in charge of a particular department or has an important position in it

_source.definition_text: a government department which is responsible for a particular subject

_source.definition_text: not important or serious

_source.definition_text: making someone believe something that is untrue
