_source.definition_text: a building where you can look at important objects connected with art, history, or science
_source.learnerexamples_text: a museum of modern art; the Natural History Museum; We sometimes go to [a] museum.

_source.definition_text: a type of fungus with a short stem and a round top, some types of which can be eaten
_source.learnerexamples_text: pasta with wild mushrooms; They usually buy wine and prepare a traditional Polish [meal] like cabbage with mushrooms and sausages.

_source.definition_text: a pattern of sounds that is made by playing instruments or singing, or a recording of this
_source.learnerexamples_text: classical/pop/dance/rock music; a beautiful piece of music; What sort of music do you listen to?; He plays really good music.; I just like making music.

_source.definition_text: to accept punishment or criticism for something bad that you have done
_source.learnerexamples_text: At the end of the day I had to go home and face the music.; Teenagers who live with their parents have to face the music about the long bills their parents receive monthly!

_source.definition_text: related to music
_source.learnerexamples_text: musical instruments; Mozart's musical compositions include symphonies and operas.; If you need a musical instrument, I can bring my guitar but unfortunately I won't be able to play it because I have never learn[t] it.

_source.definition_text: good at playing music
_source.learnerexamples_text: She comes from a very musical family.; [These] people are very musical and, therefore, you will find folk songs and even unique dances.

_source.definition_text: a play or film in which singing and dancing tell part of the story
_source.learnerexamples_text: a Broadway musical; A Little Night Music is one of Sondheim's greatest musicals.; It is always a great opportunity to enjoy a musical when you go on holiday to London.

_source.definition_text: in a way that relates to music
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a school for musically gifted children.; Musically speaking, this band has a lot of talent.; Not that I was musically gifted or wanted to become a pianist, it was just the fact that I loved music that led my step there.

_source.definition_text: someone who plays a musical instrument, often as a job
_source.learnerexamples_text: a talented jazz/classical musician ; The concert features dancers, singers and musicians of all nationalities.; The movie is about two musicians that had to dress like women to escape from the gangsters of Chicago.

_source.definition_text: used to say that it is necessary or important that something happens or is done
_source.learnerexamples_text: Meat must be cooked thoroughly.; I must get some sleep.; You mustn't show this letter to anyone else.; Luggage must not be left unattended.; We must be there at 7 o'clock in the morning.

_source.definition_text: used to show that you think something is very likely or certain to be true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Harry's been driving all day - he must be tired.;  It must have been very upsetting for her.; There's no food left - they must have eaten it all.;  She must be very wealthy.; I must have been seven years old at that time.

_source.definition_text: used to show that you think it is a good idea for someone to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: You must come and stay with us some time.; We must meet for lunch.; You must come with me when you are in Germany.

_source.definition_text: a thick, spicy yellow or brown sauce often eaten in small amounts with meat
_source.learnerexamples_text: a teaspoon of mustard; You just ask for what you want put in it - ham, eggs, salad, chicken, mustard, etc.

_source.definition_text: to speak quietly so that your voice is difficult to hear, often when complaining about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was muttering (away) to himself.;  He muttered something about the restaurant being too expensive.; "Emile Zola is the best writer", he muttered.

_source.definition_text: When two or more people have a mutual feeling, they have the same opinion about each other.
_source.learnerexamples_text: mutual admiration/respect;  He doesn't like her, and I suspect the feeling's mutual.; It will hugely contribute to better understanding between the parties as well as add to a mutual respect and trust.

_source.definition_text: When two or more people have a mutual friend or interest, they have the same one.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Andrew and Jean were introduced to each other by a mutual friend.; They need someone who would help their dead, but still living, bodies look good and they find a victim - their mutual lover (Bruce Willis).

_source.definition_text: belonging to or relating to the person who is speaking or writing
_source.learnerexamples_text: my parents; my name; my jacket;  Tom's my older son.; It wasn't my fault.

_source.definition_text: the reflexive form of the pronouns 'me' or 'I'
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've bought myself a new coat.; I caught sight of myself in the mirror.; Yes, I thought to myself, it's time to take a holiday.; I enjoyed myself a lot.

_source.definition_text: alone or without anyone's help
_source.learnerexamples_text: I couldn't carry all the luggage by myself.; I spent the night all by myself.; I made this chair myself.; I want to paint my bedroom, but it [is] hard for me to do this by myself.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize 'I' as the subject of a sentence
_source.learnerexamples_text: I myself don't like a heavy meal at lunchtime.;  I'll tell her myself.; Dear editor of 'The Student Tourist Guidebook' [I am writing] regard[ing] your latest student tourist guidebook, which I myself found very useful on my latest trip to Lampton.

_source.definition_text: for my use only
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll have the flat all to myself this weekend.; I need a couple of hours to myself.; This is because if I live[d] in a triple-storey [house], I would get a room all to myself.

_source.definition_text: strange or unknown, and not explained or understood
_source.learnerexamples_text: a mysterious stranger;  the mysterious death of her son; He died in mysterious circumstances, and there is still a possibility that it was murder.; He went to the Hotel because he wanted to find out who was the person that had sent him a mysterious letter a few days ago.

_source.definition_text: something strange or unknown which has not yet been explained or understood
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unsolved mystery; How the massive stones were brought here from hundreds of miles away remains a mystery.;  He never gave up hope that he would solve the mystery of his son's disappearance.;  He's out of work, so how he pays his rent is a mystery to me. ; I have chosen this film because it has mystery in it and a lot of fun!!

_source.definition_text: in a way that is mysterious
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Perhaps, and perhaps not," she said mysteriously.; Mysteriously, the light came on, although no one was near the switch.; Mysteriously, their character always dies tragically or goes abroad and [is] never seen again.

_source.definition_text: an ancient story about gods and brave people, often one that explains an event in history or the natural world
_source.learnerexamples_text: ancient myths;  the gods and goddesses of Greek and Roman myth; I spent three days there thinking about myths and legends and having a lot of fun.

_source.definition_text: an idea that is not true but is believed by many people
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a myth that men are better drivers than women.; There is this myth that when you are on [holiday] you should spend your whole time at the beach, practically doing nothing.

_source.definition_text: a thin piece of metal with a sharp end, used to join pieces of wood together
_source.learnerexamples_text: a three-inch nail; I stepped on a nail sticking out of the floorboards.;  Hammer a nail into the wall and we'll hang the mirror from it.; Sometimes in food given to animals by visitors you can find pieces of glass, nails or even poison.

_source.definition_text: the hard surface at the end of your fingers and toes
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stop biting your nails!; nail clippers; a nail file; She went to the hairdresser to have her hair cut, to the nails shop to have her nails done and finally she made her face up.

_source.definition_text: If someone is naive, they believe things too easily and do not have enough experience of the world.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was much younger then, and very naive.; It might sound a bit idealistic and naive, but I think this concept of communication will make the world a better place.

_source.definition_text: not wearing clothes
_source.learnerexamples_text: a naked man; naked bodies; He was naked to the waist.; The children were half naked.; I cried out in anger and that was a mistake, because the girls turned around and looked at me, standing there naked.

_source.definition_text: A naked feeling or quality is not hidden, although it is bad.
_source.learnerexamples_text: naked aggression; This programme presents the naked truth about Brazil, this so called "Tropical Paradise".

_source.definition_text: If something can be seen by the naked eye, it is big enough to be seen without special equipment.
_source.learnerexamples_text: These bugs are so tiny you cannot see them with the naked eye.

_source.definition_text: the word or words that a person, thing or place is known by
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Hi, what's your name?" "My name's Diane."; Please write your full name and address on the form.; What's the name of that mountain in the distance?; That would be a good name for a dog.; The students were listed by name and by country of origin.

_source.definition_text: If bad things are done in the name of something, they are done in order to help that thing succeed.
_source.learnerexamples_text: So much blood has been spilt in the name of religion.; Recently, a Swedish priest compared homosexuality to cancer, and he did it in the name of religion.

_source.definition_text: the reputation that someone or something has
_source.learnerexamples_text: She went to court to clear her name.; Their actions gave British football a bad name in Europe at that time.; They're trying to restore the good name of the manufacturer.; He's the only one concerned about the good name of the family.

_source.definition_text: to become famous or respected by a lot of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's been trying to make a name for himself in the music business.; Secondly, only [a] few sportsmen and sportswomen manage to make a name for themselves and get to the top.

_source.definition_text: to use impolite or unpleasant words to describe someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: He said the other children were calling him names.; He had never called me names or told me off.

_source.definition_text: used to show that the name of something tells you something about it
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Long Room, as its name implies, runs the entire length of the house.; Sour Sweet, as the name implies, is originally a Chinese restaurant.

_source.definition_text: to give someone or something a name
_source.learnerexamples_text: We named our dogs 'Shandy' and 'Belle'.; A man named Dennis answered the door.; She is named Maryam.

_source.definition_text: to say what something's or someone's name is
_source.learnerexamples_text: In the first question you had to name three types of monkey.; He couldn't name his attacker.; Not only "Tandoori dishes" but all the [dishes] are tasty, to name some there [are] Chinese, North Indian, and many others.

_source.definition_text: to choose someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Just name the time and the place and I'll be there.; Name your conditions/terms/price.; Ms Martinez has been named (as) the new Democratic candidate.; He has [been] named as the best Latin singer and he has [won] two Grammys.

_source.definition_text: something that you say which means anything you say or choose
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've never seen such a wide selection. You name it, they've got it.; Courses vary from languages, management, computer- related fields to fitness, yoga, karate classes [and] all [the] different hobbies you might be interested in such as painting on silk or on wood, pottery, carving and the like. You name it, they have it at ECM.

_source.definition_text: used when you are going to give more detail about something you have just said
_source.learnerexamples_text: She learned an important lesson from failing that exam, namely that nothing is ever certain.; This network is used by the four most used means of transport in our city (namely, bus, car, bicycle and motorcycle) and has been plagued by problems such as potholes, poor drainage and poor use (or lack!) of traffic signs.

_source.definition_text: a short sleep
_source.learnerexamples_text: He likes to have/take a nap after lunch.; He usually takes a nap after lunch and at night goes to bed about 10.00 p.m.

_source.definition_text: a story or description of a series of events
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a moving narrative of wartime adventure.; It is a happy ending, however, only because the narrative stops at this point.

_source.definition_text: Narrow things measure a small distance from one side to the other.
_source.learnerexamples_text: narrow streets; a narrow bridge/passage/gap; a narrow face; narrow feet; You will also see narrow streets with pubs and small cafes everywhere.

_source.definition_text: the person who tells the story in a book, film, play, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The narrator is a fisherman.; Leo Colston is the narrator and chief character through whose eyes we dive into the story.

_source.definition_text: If you have a narrow escape, you only just avoid danger.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He had a narrow escape when a falling tree crushed his car.; Ralph will have a narrow escape: he is saved by the arrival of a ship which has at last come to rescue them all.

_source.definition_text: limited to a small area of interest, activity or thought
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has narrow interests.; It was regarded as a very narrow interpretation of the law.; People leave home with a narrow outlook and it doesn't seem to broaden.

_source.definition_text: to become less or to make something become less
_source.learnerexamples_text: to narrow the gap between rich and poor; I tend to believe that every country should join together, as only by discussing and sorting out some measures will [we] be able to narrow the gap that nowadays exists among countries all over the world.

_source.definition_text: to become less wide or to make something less wide
_source.learnerexamples_text: The road has been narrowed to one lane.; His eyes narrowed angrily.; Driving as well as parking has become a difficult task in Copenhagen City as the City Council [has] over the last [few] years deliberately cut down the numbers of parking places, raised the fees and narrowed the roads and streets.

_source.definition_text: to make something, for example a list or a choice, smaller and clearer by removing the things that are less important
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've managed to narrow the list down to four.; My hobbies were narrowed down to reading books, listening to some music and that's all.

_source.definition_text: not willing to accept new ideas or opinions different from your own
_source.learnerexamples_text: My family are very narrow-minded.; He is a bit narrow-minded and at first he'll drive you crazy but once you get to know him, he'll be good company.

_source.definition_text: only by a small amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: He narrowly escaped death in the accident.; She narrowly missed winning an Oscar.; They narrowly escaped crash[ing] with the car in [the]opposite lane.

_source.definition_text: bad or unpleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: a nasty shock/surprise; There's a nasty smell in here.; He had a nasty cut above the eye.; She has a nasty habit of picking on people in meetings.; Inside there were three samples of a nasty purple liquid.

_source.definition_text: unkind
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't be so nasty to your brother - he's four years younger than you!; I though that it was a nasty joke made by a friend, but the ad[d]ress of the sender did not match with any that I knew.

_source.definition_text: very angry or violent
_source.learnerexamples_text: When I asked for the money, he turned really nasty.; He can sometimes be very nasty and say and do horrible things on and [off] the pitch.

_source.definition_text: a country or the people living in a country
_source.learnerexamples_text: the industrial nations; All the nations of the world will be represented at the conference.; Practically the whole nation watched the ceremony on television.; At that time, everyone should have devoted their life to the nation.

_source.definition_text: relating to or typical of a whole country and its people
_source.learnerexamples_text: a national holiday; Britain has more than ten national newspapers.; The company's national headquarters is in Rome.; The children were wearing traditional national costume/dress.; The government's view is that raising taxes now would not be in the national interest.

_source.definition_text: If you have American/British/Swiss, etc. nationality, you are legally a member of that country.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has British nationality.; He has dual nationality.; What nationality are you?; At the International School they have pupils of 46 different nationalities.; My friend [was] born in Norway, but his nationality is Polish.

_source.definition_text: existing or happening in all parts of a particular country
_source.learnerexamples_text: a nationwide network/chain of shops; a nationwide survey; The nationwide blackout was the first in the past decade.

_source.definition_text: in all parts of a country
_source.learnerexamples_text: Schools nationwide are experiencing a shortage of teachers.; On Thursday, Friday or Saturday you could visit the annual festival, which is well-known nationwide for the music, costumes and dance of the local people.

_source.definition_text: Your native town or country is the place where you were born.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She returned to live and work in her native Japan.; She's a native Californian.; I am good, because in my native country, Austria, I worked in a cinema.

_source.definition_text: relating to the first people to live in an area
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Aborigines are the native inhabitants of Australia.; the native population; native customs and traditions; I am very happy to tell you about my trip to the Amazon forest native inhabitants museum.

_source.definition_text: the first language that you learn
_source.learnerexamples_text: French is his native tongue.; My native language is Russian but I speak English fluently and I have been learning Latin for two years.

_source.definition_text: Native animals or plants live or grow naturally in a place, and have not been brought from somewhere else.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a large bird native to Europe

_source.definition_text: someone who has spoken a particular language since they were a baby, rather than having learnt it as a child or adult
_source.learnerexamples_text: All our teachers are native speakers of English.; a native-speaker dictionary; My knowledge in foreign languages ha[s] to get better and the best way to do [that] is to get in contact with native speakers.

_source.definition_text: Something that is natural exists or happens because of nature, not because it was made or done by people.
_source.learnerexamples_text: natural ingredients; a natural substance; He died from natural causes.; Floods and earthquakes are natural disasters.; People say that breast-feeding is better than bottle-feeding because it's more natural.

_source.definition_text: normal or expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: Of course you're upset - it's only natural.;  It's natural that you should feel anxious when you first leave home.;  It's quite natural to experience a few doubts just before you get married.; So, of course, it was quite a natural thing for me to learn [to] driv[e] a car as early as possible, and that was at the age of 18 when one could apply for a driving licence.

_source.definition_text: If you have a natural characteristic, it is something you have been born with.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a natural talent; She's a natural athlete/blonde.; Also my natural talent for entertaining people together with my past experience should be very useful working at [the] new theme park.

_source.definition_text: in a normal way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Relax and try to behave naturally.; As a result they can't behave naturally at all and become sick.

_source.definition_text: as you would expect
_source.learnerexamples_text: Naturally, he was very disappointed.; Naturally we had to take his word for it.

_source.definition_text: having been born with a characteristic
_source.learnerexamples_text: naturally aggressive/funny/slim; Clarisse McClellan is a spontane[o]us and naturally curious teenager who even enjoys simple things.

_source.definition_text: happening or existing as part of nature and not made or done by people
_source.learnerexamples_text: A healthy body will be able to fight off the illness naturally without the use of medicine.; He has naturally blonde hair.; Sometimes people say women are naturally stronger tha[n] men.

_source.definition_text: all the plants, creatures, substances, and forces that exist in the universe, which are not made by people
_source.learnerexamples_text: her love of nature; This new technique of artificially growing cells copies what actually happens in nature.; a nature article/book/programme; It's a nice place to relax and enjoy nature.

_source.definition_text: someone's character
_source.learnerexamples_text: As a child Juliana had a lovely nature - everyone liked her.;  It's not really in her nature to be aggressive.; He is by nature inclined to be rather lazy.; Jane wasn't very suspicious by nature, but there was something weird in that.

_source.definition_text: type
_source.learnerexamples_text: What exactly is the nature of your business?; I don't like hunting and things of that nature.; He claims that he did not improve his English because of the nature of the job.

_source.definition_text: When children are naughty, or their behaviour is naughty, they behave badly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: You naughty boy!; Now that's naughty - you mustn't throw food on the floor!; Our boss treats us all like naughty schoolchildren.; But some naughty students in my class were throwing paper aeroplanes when the teacher was writing something on the board.

_source.definition_text: relating to the navy
_source.learnerexamples_text: a naval base/officer; It is irrefutable that naval areas are in most cases abandoned by their governments.

_source.definition_text: very dark blue
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was wearing a navy blue sweater.; I think I will buy [a] navy blue carpet and black and blue furniture.

_source.definition_text: the part of a country's armed forces which is trained to operate at sea
_source.learnerexamples_text: My brother is an officer in the Navy.; Gabriel joined the navy in 1997.; a navy ship/vessel; Best of all, not only am I familiar [with the] life-style on a ship but I also know a lot of things about ship[s] because I was in the navy.

_source.definition_text: close in distance
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is there a train station near here?; We were near the exit.; The hotel is near the airport.; Don't come too near me - you might catch my cold.; Which bus stop is nearest (to) your house?

_source.definition_text: close in time
_source.learnerexamples_text: He arrived near the end of the lesson.; It was nearer four when we finally arrived.; We can decide which route to take nearer the time.

_source.definition_text: almost in a particular state or condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: The runners looked near exhaustion.; I was near (to) tears at one point during the film.; This is the nearest I've ever got to winning anything.; He came near to punching him.; It is strictly related to the fact that the old possess a vast amount of experience and are nearer to death.

_source.definition_text: not close in distance, time, amount or quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: The house was nowhere near the sea.; It's nowhere near time for us to leave yet.; I'm nowhere near finishing the book - I'm only half-way through it.; He's nowhere near as tall as his sister.; Although people are well aware of the current situation in Switzerland, they prefer looking at other countries and comparing us to them (we are nowhere near as fat as them).

_source.definition_text: used in questions and negatives to mean 'close to being or doing something'
_source.learnerexamples_text: The house isn't anywhere near ready.; We could not have gone anywhere near 5000 miles because all our minibuses were broken down - we even stayed in one place for 8 days.

_source.definition_text: close in distance
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was standing just near enough to hear what they were saying.; Don't come any nearer.; And they are getting nearer, I must run for my life.

_source.definition_text: close in time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her birthday was getting nearer and I still hadn't bought her a present.; As the date of his operation drew near, he became more and more anxious.; I would appreciate very much if you could reply as soon as possible, as the school holiday is drawing near.

_source.definition_text: close in distance
_source.learnerexamples_text: Where's the nearest post office?; Dear Dan, My friends and I have decided to go to the nearest cinema, the one which is in The Mall, three blocks from here.

_source.definition_text: at a time that is not far away
_source.learnerexamples_text: Space travel may become very common in the near future.; I look forward to receiving your reply in the near future.

_source.definition_text: similar in characteristics or quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: My pocket knife is the nearest thing to a weapon that I have.; I couldn't get any cream cheese so I bought the nearest equivalent that I could find.

_source.definition_text: not far away
_source.learnerexamples_text: If there's a cafe nearby, we could stop for a snack.; I noticed a policeman standing nearby.; We can go swimming, [and] visit some of the bea[u]tiful castles nearby.

_source.definition_text: not far away
_source.learnerexamples_text: We stopped at some nearby shops to buy some food.; The nearby towns are lovely, very calm.

_source.definition_text: almost
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's been nearly three months since my last haircut.; I've nearly finished that book you lent me.; She's nearly as tall as her father now.; They'd eaten nearly everything before we arrived.; It was so funny - we nearly died laughing.

_source.definition_text: tidy and clean
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your house is always so neat - how do you manage it with three children?; She likes everything neat and tidy.; You've got such neat handwriting.; I always go to this restaurant because it's neat and clean.

_source.definition_text: a lot less
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's not nearly as expensive as I thought.; There are not nearly enough jobs to go round.; However this is not nearly enough, since we are restricted when it comes to us[ing] nuclear power [and] there is always a constant search for other energy sources.

_source.definition_text: in a tidy way
_source.learnerexamples_text: neatly dressed; a neatly folded pile of clothes; The performers are all neatly dressed.

_source.definition_text: used in negatives to mean 'in every case' or 'therefore'
_source.learnerexamples_text: That's not necessarily true.; The fact that something is cheap doesn't necessarily mean it's of low quality.; You may love someone without necessarily wanting to marry them.; The most important point in a job interview is to give a good impression, which does not necessarily mean how you look.

_source.definition_text: the need for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's no financial necessity for her to work.; Sewing is something I do out of necessity, not for pleasure.; Therefore, the most important lesson to learn is to acknowledge the necessity of education and the str[uggle] to make it happen.

_source.definition_text: needed in order to achieve something
_source.learnerexamples_text: If necessary, we can change the dates of our trip.; We don't want to take any more luggage with us than is necessary.;  I won't stay any longer than necessary.; He lacks the necessary skills for the job.; Is it necessary to give so much detail?

_source.definition_text: something you need
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most people seem to consider a car a necessity, not a luxury.; Mobile phones first appeared as a necessity in worldwide communications because, as the different business domains began to expand, the need [for] information and detailed facts about numerous aspects have emerged.

_source.base_text: be a pain in the neck
_source.definition_text: to be annoying
_source.searchterms_text: be a pain in the neck;neck;necks
_source.learnerexamples_text: My brother can be a real pain in the neck sometimes.; He's adorable although sometimes he can really be a pain in the neck (don't tell him I wrote this.)

_source.definition_text: the part of the body which joins the head to the shoulders
_source.learnerexamples_text: He had the thickest neck I'd ever seen.; She wore a gold chain around her neck.; I was really shocked when I noticed it wasn't on my neck.

_source.definition_text: If two people who are competing are neck and neck, they are very close and either of them could win.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The two runners were neck and neck coming into the last lap.; It was [a] really neck and neck match that took my breath away every second.

_source.definition_text: the part of a piece of clothing that goes around your neck
_source.learnerexamples_text: a polo-neck/V-neck jumper; When she was walking down the street feeling elated by the success of the business meeting, a gorgeous thirtyish man wearing [a] beige polo neck swiftly appro[a]ched and turned towards her and smiled, revealing strong white teeth.

_source.definition_text: a piece of jewellery that you wear around your neck
_source.learnerexamples_text: a gold/silver necklace; Dear Elaine, The party was wonderful and I got the necklace which I wanted so much.

_source.definition_text: If you need something, you must have it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I need some new shoes.; Babies need constant care.; He needs an operation.; I need you to help me choose an outfit.; I badly need a rest from all this.

_source.definition_text: If you need to do something, it is necessary to do it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I need to do some shopping on my way home from work.; I need to go to the toilet.; Do we need to go with her?; I need to l[earn] Engl[i]sh.

_source.base_text: don't need to do sth/needn't do sth
_source.definition_text: used in order to say that someone does not have to do something or should not do something
_source.searchterms_text: don't need to do sth/needn't do sth;need;needed;needing;needs

_source.definition_text: If you do or achieve something against all the odds, you succeed although you were not likely to.
_source.searchterms_text: against all (the) odds;against all the odds;odds
_source.learnerexamples_text: We won the game against all odds. ; The stormy waters and heavy winds were a great challenge, and almost deemed it impossible for me to succeed, but against all odds I managed to defeat my fears.

_source.definition_text: a group of small objects of different types which are not valuable or important
_source.learnerexamples_text: I use this box to keep odds and ends in.

_source.definition_text: to not agree with someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: His remark was at odds with our report. ; Young people are inexperienced as far as the world is concerned and thus they are frequently at odds with their family.

_source.definition_text: belonging or relating to someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a friend of mine; the colour of her hair; part of the problem; employees of the company; The name of my friend is Maria.

_source.definition_text: a smell, often one that is unpleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: body odour; It was stale and had a decidedly offensive odour.

_source.definition_text: used after words which show an amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: a kilo of apples; loads of food; hundreds of people; most of them; none of them

_source.definition_text: containing
_source.learnerexamples_text: a bag of sweets; a bottle of beer; a book of short stories; sacks of rubbish; I like cups of tea, I like noodles, but I don't like beef.

_source.definition_text: used with numbers, ages and dates
_source.learnerexamples_text: an essay of 500 words; a boy of six; the 14th of February 2005; The class started [on] the 2nd of June at half past five.

_source.definition_text: used to say 'yes' and emphasize your answer
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Can you help me?" "Of course!"; Yes of course I can come.

_source.definition_text: used in expressions showing position
_source.learnerexamples_text: the top of his head; the back of your dress; on the corner of the street; the front of the queue; I've never been north of Edinburgh.

_source.definition_text: showing someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a map of the city centre; a photo of my boyfriend; Tony gave me a photo of Henry.

_source.definition_text: used when comparing related things
_source.learnerexamples_text: Best of all I liked the green one.; Worst of all was the food!; He's the best looking of the three brothers.; I think that of all his films it's my favourite.; The best of all was a necklace.

_source.definition_text: used to say 'no' and emphasize your answer
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Do you mind if I borrow your pen?" "Of course not."; "Pardon. You said your [u]ncle's will? Would you mind explaining [that], please?" "Of course not!"

_source.definition_text: used to show who or what does something
_source.learnerexamples_text: the works of Shakespeare; the arrival of the rainy season; the music of the flute; They often cover the music of "The Beatles" or "The Rolling Stones".

_source.definition_text: showing a reason or cause
_source.learnerexamples_text: He died of cancer.; But, three months later, after walk[ing] in the rain he died of pneumonia.

_source.definition_text: used after an adjective when judging someone's behaviour
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was very nice of you to think of us.; It was a bit mean of him to mention her weight.; Thank you so much for my present. How thoughtful of you.; It was most thoughtful of you to invite us and I warmly appreciate your hospitality.

_source.definition_text: used to show that what you are saying is obvious or already known
_source.learnerexamples_text: Of course, the Olympics are not just about money.; Of course, I met many new people.

_source.definition_text: about or relating to
_source.learnerexamples_text: Speaking of Elizabeth, here she is.; Let us consider the events of the last five months.; We know very little of her childhood.; Speaking of sightseeing, many thought that visiting other sights - like the Folk Museum - should not be compulsory.

_source.definition_text: If you do something of your own accord, you choose to do it and no one else forces you.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She left of her own accord.; She would go alone, but it was something that was chosen of her own accord.

_source.definition_text: not at work
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had six months off after my son was born.; I'm going to take/have some time off to work on my house.; She was off sick last week.; I will take a day off on Friday.

_source.definition_text: used with actions in which something is removed or removes itself from another thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Take your jacket off.; One of my buttons has come off.; She's had all her hair cut off.; I left the lid off.; I took off my ring.

_source.definition_text: not operating or being used
_source.learnerexamples_text: Make sure the computers are all off before you go home.; I tr[i]ed to contact my neighbour, but his phone was off and nobody was at home.

_source.definition_text: If a price has a certain amount of money off, it costs that much less than the usual price.
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can get some money off if you pay cash.; There's 40% off this week on all winter coats.; There was $40 or $50 off most jackets in the shop.; He promised me 30% off the price, so I'm going to buy the TV and the CD player from him.

_source.definition_text: away from a place or position
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm just off to the shops.; Keep the dog on the lead or he'll just run off.; If we can get off early tomorrow morning we'll avoid most of the traffic.; I'm off now - see you tomorrow.; She's off to Canada next week.

_source.definition_text: far in distance or time
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can see the village off in the distance.; My holidays seem a long way off.; The exams are so far off that I'm not even thinking about them yet.; Allow me to start by saying that one day, which may l[ie] not so far off in the future, people will visit the buildings which were formerly known as "Educational Institutions" like we visit museums to gape at the sheer size of the Dinosaurs...

_source.definition_text: down or away from a place or position
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the leaves had dropped off the tree.; He fell off his bike.; I still remember the way your brother fell off the lad[d]er that day.

_source.definition_text: used with actions in which something is removed or removes itself from another thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't get the lid off this jar.; Has anyone taken a book off my desk?; Could you cut me a small piece off that white cheese?; Take your feet off the seat.; Next month, I'm going to change my bedroom. I'll take the photographs off the wall.

_source.definition_text: If someone such as a doctor or a soldier is off duty, they are not working.
_source.learnerexamples_text: What time are you off duty tomorrow?; Sometimes I come off duty at ten p.m.

_source.definition_text: near to a building or place
_source.learnerexamples_text: an island off the coast of Spain; He spent all night off the coast, (unfinished)

_source.definition_text: If an area is off limits, you are not allowed to enter it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most of the palace is off limits to the public.; The only place that was off limits for us was on the other side of the mountain, because it was too dangerous.

_source.definition_text: If you say something off the record, you do not want the public to know about it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Off the record, ministers are saying the president must resign.; Off the record, how come that your reporter can print such lies when knowing they are perhaps hurting certain people in this important matter?

_source.definition_text: in a place where few people go
_source.learnerexamples_text: I prefer to take my holiday somewhere off the beaten track.; Furthermore, in areas off the beaten track, there [are] not even police sometimes.

_source.definition_text: If food or drink is off, it is not now fresh and good to eat or drink.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This milk smells off.; Who knows if the food isn't off?

_source.definition_text: stopped or given up
_source.learnerexamples_text: The wedding's off - she's decided she's too young to settle down.; It's all off between Philippa and Mike.; The boat trip is off because of the weather.; On that day, she had written him a big long letter and told him that it was all off, for she didn't love him any longer.

_source.definition_text: a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: Driving without a licence is an offence.; a serious/minor offence; a criminal offence; He committed several serious offences.; It's the third time that he's been convicted of a drug offence.

_source.definition_text: when something rude makes someone upset or angry
_source.learnerexamples_text: I really didn't mean to cause/give any offence - I was just stating my opinion.; Do you think he took offence at what I said about his hair?; If you don't mind, I'd rather go on my own - no offence, but I think it would be better.; Now, about that organisation of yours. What is it actually doing? No offence, I just wonder are you saving nature or just writing articles about it?

_source.definition_text: to make someone upset or angry
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think she was a bit offended that she hadn't been invited to the party.; He looked a offended when you called him middle-aged.; If the sight of a few dirty dishes offends you, then I think you've got problems!; I know that she was not offended but I will never forget my stupid question.

_source.definition_text: someone who has committed a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: first-time offenders;  sex offenders; young offenders; The ticket fare is very reasonable, [and] there [are] always police p[a]tro[l]ling around, protecting the people from offenders.

_source.definition_text: likely to make people angry or upset
_source.learnerexamples_text: This programme contains language that some viewers might find offensive.; He told some really offensive sexist jokes.; Dear Sir/Madam, The review on the Westfield Music Festival was both offensive and incorrect.

_source.definition_text: to say that you are willing to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Paul has offered to help us move house.; "I'll do the cooking, " he offered.; Dear Robbie, Thank you for offering to help me paint my bedroom.

_source.definition_text: to ask someone if they would like something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They've offered me a job.; Can I offer you a drink?; I feel bad that I didn't offer them any food.; Someone should offer that old lady a seat.; He offered me a contract and asked me to go to his music studio to record a CD.

_source.definition_text: to give or provide something
_source.learnerexamples_text: to offer advice; We are now offering you the chance/opportunity to buy the complete set of DVDs at half price.; Did he offer any explanation for his strange behaviour?; Rome offers good nightlife so after visiting [the] museum, we'll be able to go to [the] disco.

_source.definition_text: to say that you will pay a particular amount of money
_source.learnerexamples_text: I offered him £500 for the car.; Police have offered a $1,000 reward for information.; My company will offer 20 percent more than the minimum wage that exists for the same type of work in Canada.

_source.definition_text: a cheap price or special arrangement for something you are buying
_source.learnerexamples_text: This special offer ends on Friday.; Are these jeans still on offer?; We found a £12 offer to Leeds Castle including bus transfer and entrance ticket for the castle.

_source.definition_text: when you ask someone if they would like something
_source.learnerexamples_text: an offer of help; a job offer; to accept/refuse an offer; "If you like I can do some shopping for you." "That's a very kind offer."; Thank you very much for your offer.

_source.definition_text: available
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were amazed at the range of products on offer.; You should find out about the services on offer.; The swimming pool is also on offer [to] tourists. Another advantage of the hotel is that it is not far from the cent[re].

_source.definition_text: an amount of money that you say you will pay for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The highest offer anyone has made so far is £150.

_source.definition_text: a room or building where people work
_source.learnerexamples_text: I didn't leave the office until eight o'clock last night.; the director's office; office workers; office equipment; I go to the office on foot.

_source.definition_text: a room or building where you can get information, tickets, or a particular service
_source.learnerexamples_text: a ticket office; the tourist office; I suggest [we] meet at 4.50 p.m, in the ticket office.

_source.definition_text: an important job in an organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: Some people think he has been in office for too long.; She held the office of mayor for eight years.; The former Polish prime minister was a woman - Hanna Suchocka - and she was able to remain in office for 15 months, in the time when the life expectancy of governments in Poland is about half a year.

_source.definition_text: a police officer
_source.learnerexamples_text: a uniformed officer; They sent me an officer: Officer McDonald, from the anti-mafia department.

_source.definition_text: a person who has a position of authority in an organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: a customs/prison officer; I work as [a] customs officer and [in] this job I meet a lot of foreign people every day.

_source.definition_text: someone with an important job in a military organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: a naval officer; an army officer; He was an officer in [the] army.

_source.definition_text: approved by the government or someone in authority
_source.learnerexamples_text: the official language of Singapore; an official document; There is to be an official inquiry into the incident.; The queen will attend the official opening of the theatre in June.; I have worked as an official translator in [the] British Embass[y] in Seoul.

_source.definition_text: An official explanation or statement is one that is given, but which may not be true.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The official reason for the delay is bad weather.; Well, this was the official reason to explain his stay, [but] the truth - which I had learned later - was that Martin was a broken man.

_source.definition_text: known by the public
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their engagement is now official.; Inflation has fallen below 2%, and that's official.; It was now official, she was the most beautiful girl of the school.

_source.definition_text: relating to the duties of someone in authority
_source.learnerexamples_text: an official visit; The two episodes in the book 'The colour of blood' that I've decided to write about are Cardinal Benn and Prime Minister meeting at the official residence, and the fatal mass in honour [of] the blessed martyrs.

_source.definition_text: a person who has a position of responsibility in an organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: a UN official; a government/trade-union official; Neither Olivia nor her husband, Douglas, are Indian, but Douglas is a British official in India.

_source.definition_text: formally and in a way agreed to or arranged by people in positions of authority
_source.learnerexamples_text: The new hospital was officially opened yesterday.; The royal engagement was announced officially this morning.; If I could travel back to any place and time in history, I would choose the day when Wor[l]d War II was officially declared over.

_source.definition_text: slightly unpleasant or worrying so that you do not want to get involved in any way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's slightly aggressive, which a lot of people find a bit off-putting when they first meet him.; Therefore, it's quite off-putting to stay in Hong Kong for higher education.

_source.definition_text: If one thing offsets another thing, it has the opposite effect and so creates a more balanced situation.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The costs have been offset by savings in other areas.; During the interview, she tried to offset the bad impression she was sure she had made.

_source.definition_text: the child of a person or animal
_source.learnerexamples_text: to produce offspring; Now, seven years into a relationship with a woman that eventually became my wife and mother of my offspring, I sit back and recall with selfish and secret pleasure the sheer number of different wom[e]n I have been out with between these two absolute landmarks in my love life.

_source.definition_text: many times or regularly
_source.learnerexamples_text: I often shop there.;  How often do you wash your hair?; I don't often drink spirits.; I don't see him very often.;  It's not often that you meet someone who you're instantly attracted to.

_source.definition_text: If something often happens or is often true, it is normal for it to happen or it is usually true.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Brothers and sisters often argue.; Headaches are often caused by stress.; Christmas is often mild in Britain.; Very often, people link classical music to Austrian or German [composers], [such] as Mozart or Handel, but rarely to England and genius[es] [such] as Haydn and Purcell.

_source.definition_text: sometimes, but not often
_source.learnerexamples_text: He went into town every so often to buy supplies.; Elizabeth and others visited her every so often until [one] day she left them.

_source.definition_text: used to express different emotions, such as surprise, disappointment and pleasure, often as a reaction to something someone has said
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Jack can't come after all." "Oh dear, Emma will be sad to hear that."; "He's been married three times." "Oh, really? I didn't know that!"; "I'm afraid I can't come to the party." " Oh, that's a shame."; Is that for me? Oh, you're so kind!; "I'm sorry I forgot to ring you." "Oh, don't worry."

_source.definition_text: introduces an idea that you have just thought of, or something that you have just remembered
_source.learnerexamples_text: Oh, I've just thought of a problem.; Oh, and don't forget to lock the back door.; Oh yeah, someone phoned for you while you were out.; Oh, and don't forget to show up in old clothes, ok?

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize how surprised, angry, shocked, etc. you are
_source.learnerexamples_text: Oh my God! The car's been stolen.; Oh my god, your sister is getting married!

_source.definition_text: a thick liquid produced from plants that is used in cooking
_source.learnerexamples_text: olive/sunflower/vegetable oil; Hi Fatima, I think you can bring some potatoes, olive oil and lettuce.

_source.definition_text: a thick liquid that comes from under the Earth's surface that is used as a fuel and for making parts of machines move easily
_source.learnerexamples_text: an oil company; engine oil; He is working in a big oil company called Agip.

_source.definition_text: to work late into the night
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had to burn the midnight oil to get the essay finished.; My examinations were nearing and I was always burning the midnight oil.

_source.definition_text: used when agreeing to do something or when allowing someone to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Could you pick me up from the station?" "OK, what time?"; "I'll pay you back tomorrow." "Okay, no problem."; OK. See you for dinner!

_source.definition_text: used to check that someone understands something or that they agree to something
_source.learnerexamples_text: So I'll get the food and you can get the drink, OK?; I'll see you at six-thirty, okay?; Don't forget to wear [an] old shirt and jeans, okay?

_source.definition_text: used as a way of showing that you are going to take action, start speaking or start something new
_source.learnerexamples_text: OK then, if you're ready we'll start.; Okay, let's go.

_source.definition_text: not ill, damaged, upset, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you OK? You look a bit pale.; How's Paola? Is she okay after her fall yesterday?; "Is everything OK with you?" "Yes, fine."; I'll just check that the car's okay - that was a bit of a bang!; Hi, Ramesh What are you doing? Are you OK?

_source.definition_text: allowed or acceptable
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is it OK if I bring a friend to the party?; Is it okay to smoke in here?; If it's okay by/with you, I'll leave the shopping till tomorrow.; Dear Ally, It's okay that you couldn't come.

_source.definition_text: good or good enough
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is your food OK?; "Did you have a good meal last night?" "It was okay, though I've had better."; Her voice is OK, but it's nothing special.; I hope the new trousers you bought are OK.

_source.definition_text: in a satisfactory way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Everything was going OK until the printer stopped working.; Did you sleep okay?; I just phoned to make sure that you got there okay.; Finally the day finished OK.

_source.definition_text: having lived or existed for many years
_source.learnerexamples_text: an old man; an old house; We're all getting older.; I was shocked by how old he looked.; I'm too old to be out clubbing every night.

_source.definition_text: used to describe or ask about someone's age
_source.learnerexamples_text: How old is your father?; Rosie's six years old now.; He's a couple of years older than me.; She is 23 years old.

_source.definition_text: from a period in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: I saw my old English teacher last time I went home.; He's bought me a smart new camera to replace my old one.; She showed me her old school.; I saw an old boyfriend of mine.; My old one is [a] Nokia.

_source.definition_text: someone who you have known and liked for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I met an old friend who I was at college with.; Do you remember my old friend Jack?

_source.definition_text: a period in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: In the old days large families were much more common.

_source.definition_text: something or someone you have seen or heard many times before
_source.searchterms_text: old;older;oldest;same old arguments/face/story, etc.;the same old arguments/face/story etc;the same old arguments/face/story, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Every day I see the same old faces.; Politicians repeat the same old arguments time and time again.; I think that it is the same old story with media all over the world that they tend to present the news in [an] exaggerated manner.

_source.definition_text: not modern
_source.learnerexamples_text: old-fashioned clothes/ideas/furniture; She's a bit old-fashioned in her outlook.; But I don't like clothes with stripes, because I think that's a little old-fashioned.

_source.definition_text: a small green or black fruit with a bitter taste that is eaten or used to produce oil
_source.learnerexamples_text: olive oil; olive trees ; In [the] countryside there are some hills, some sunflowers, olive trees and many medieval town[s] on the hills to visit!

_source.definition_text: a food made with eggs that have been mixed and fried, often with other foods added
_source.learnerexamples_text: a cheese/mushroom omelette; I want to make many cakes and omelettes!

_source.definition_text: when something has not been included that should have been
_source.learnerexamples_text: Measures to control child employment are a glaring omission from this legislation.; There are some serious errors and omissions in the book.; Finally, I think it would be an omission if I didn't mention the children that live in poverty and die from starvation and diseases every day.

_source.definition_text: to not include something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was omitted from the list of contributors to the report.; The Prince's tour conveniently omitted the most deprived areas of the city.; The advertisement had omitted some important facts about the school, like the rare possibility of taking the exam, the problems with transport, the lack of advertised social activities.

_source.definition_text: to not do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She omitted to mention where she was going. ; Thus, no-one else could fill the gap if they omit to teach their children basic principles of living [in] society.

_source.definition_text: used to show the day or date when something happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many shops don't open on Sundays.; What are you doing on Friday?; My birthday's on the 30th of May.; I go to college on Monday and Wednesday.

_source.definition_text: on or onto a surface
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ouch, you're standing on my foot!; I dropped my pen on the floor.; Look at all the books on your desk!; We put all of our medicine on a high shelf.; Your suitcase is on top of the wardrobe.

_source.definition_text: covering, touching, attached to or hanging from something
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've got blood on your shirt.; Which finger do you wear your ring on?; We could hang this picture on the wall next to the door.; Dogs should be kept on their leads at all times.; I like my bedroom, because there are [a] lot of windows, two armchair[s], a lamp next to the bed, a table under the window, [and] some pictures on the wall.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a place when giving directions
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our house is the first on the left after the post office.; Take the first turning on the right.; My house is the first one on the left.

_source.definition_text: used for showing some methods of travelling
_source.learnerexamples_text: I love travelling on trains.; She'll be arriving on the five-thirty bus.; We went to France on the ferry.; I will travel on a train and then I will take [a] taxi to your home.

_source.definition_text: in a particular place
_source.learnerexamples_text: the diagram on page 22; They lived on a farm.; I live on a farm in the Emmental.

_source.definition_text: used to show the way in which something is recorded or broadcast
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's on television tonight?; When's the film coming out on DVD?; At the party, we watched films on television.

_source.definition_text: used to show what money or time is used for
_source.learnerexamples_text: She refuses to spend more than £20 on a pair of shoes.; I've wasted too much time on this already.; I love it and I spend all my time on it.

_source.definition_text: available at a reduced price
_source.learnerexamples_text: I love that dress but I'm waiting until it's on sale before I buy it.; I bought a nice t-shirt and a pair of shorts. I bought them because they're comfortable and cheap: they were on sale. I spent 15€.

_source.definition_text: walking
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you going by bicycle or on foot?; It isn't far away from the main building [-] it's about 15 minutes on foot.

_source.definition_text: available to buy in a shop, on the Internet, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The video and book are now on sale.; I went window shopping with my friends yesterday and I saw this beautiful skirt on sale.

_source.definition_text: about
_source.learnerexamples_text: a book on plants; Her thesis is on Italian women's literature.; The other one is a book on dogs and cats.

_source.definition_text: using something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I do all my household accounts on computer.; Chris is on drums and Mike's on bass guitar.; I'm on the phone.; I was in the pizza shop to order some food for my family and I was on the phone.

_source.definition_text: next to or along the side of a place or area
_source.learnerexamples_text: Cambridge is on the River Cam.; Our house was on Sturton Street.; Strasbourg is on the border of France and Germany.; Dan, We are going to the cinema that is on Arocena street.

_source.definition_text: on a boat, train, aircraft, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: There were 230 people on board the plane.; I also love travelling by plane because you can have a snack on board.

_source.definition_text: If something is on fire, it is burning when it should not be.
_source.learnerexamples_text: If your home was on fire and you could save only one thing, what would it be?; A lot of bu[i]ldings were on fire.

_source.definition_text: not early or late
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got to school on time. ; So, I will not be on time for my English class tomorrow.

_source.definition_text: intentionally
_source.learnerexamples_text: I didn't do it on purpose, it was an accident. ; I didn't do it on purpose; it was dark and I just walked into it.

_source.definition_text: If something is on display, it is there for people to look at.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many old aircraft are on display at the museum at the moment.; There were some new musical instruments on display.

_source.definition_text: generally
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've had a few problems, but on the whole we're very happy.; On the whole I don't like watching television.

_source.definition_text: alone
_source.searchterms_text: (all) on your own;all on your own;on
_source.learnerexamples_text: I like living on my own.; On Wedn[e]sday morning I went on my own to see [the]Vatican.

_source.definition_text: without any help
_source.searchterms_text: (all) on your own;all on your own;on
_source.learnerexamples_text: I did my buttons up all on my own, Mummy.; Maybe I can do the missing work on my own.

_source.definition_text: because of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He doesn't eat any dairy products on account of the diet he is following.; On account of its location, it is always busy.

_source.definition_text: used to show something which is used as food or fuel
_source.learnerexamples_text: What do frogs live on?; Does this radio run on batteries?; All new cars run on unleaded fuel w[h]ich is a benefit to the environment.

_source.definition_text: used to show what happens as a result of touching or hitting against something
_source.learnerexamples_text: You'll cut yourself on that knife if you're not careful.; I hit my head on the shelf as I was standing up.; Suddenly I hit my head on the bed as the man was talking.

_source.definition_text: used to give your opinion after you have considered all the facts about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: On balance, I'd prefer to come straight home.; On balance, no matter how important or useful computers may be, they will never replace the pleasure of re-reading familiar pages of your favourite books.

_source.base_text: on behalf of sb or on sb's behalf
_source.definition_text: If you do something on behalf of someone, you do it for them or instead of them.
_source.searchterms_text: on;on behalf of sb or on sb's behalf
_source.learnerexamples_text: On behalf of the entire company, I would like to thank you for all your work.; Unfortunately, George cannot be with us today so I am pleased to accept this award on his behalf.; I am writing on behalf of our college English club members to welcome you [to] our city.

_source.definition_text: only if
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll come with you on condition that we're back before midnight.; I would like to do this on condition that you will not mention my name [on] the website.

_source.definition_text: in addition to something else that is bad
