_source.definition_text: If someone such as a doctor or a soldier is on duty, they are working.
_source.learnerexamples_text: What time are you on duty tomorrow?; I was on duty in front of the major's house with another soldier.

_source.base_text: on the one hand ... on the other hand
_source.definition_text: used when you are comparing two different ideas or opinions
_source.searchterms_text: on;on the one hand ... on the other hand;on the one hand on the other hand
_source.learnerexamples_text: On the one hand, computer games develop many skills, but on the other, they mean kids don't get enough exercise. ; On the one hand, I know from my experience that it's much easier in life if you know more about everything, but on the other hand, I'd say that if someone [had given] me a chance (when I was kid) to study what I enjoy[ed], probably I'd have more possibility to develop my skills.

_source.definition_text: available
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were amazed at the range of products on offer.; You should find out about the services on offer.; The swimming pool is also on offer [to] tourists. Another advantage of the hotel is that it is not far from the cent[re].

_source.definition_text: having something as a reason
_source.learnerexamples_text: Marks are awarded on the basis of progress and performance.; On the basis of the points mentioned above, it is a foregone conclusion that young people do not face any severe problems.

_source.definition_text: to be a member of a group or organization
_source.searchterms_text: be on a committee/panel etc;be on a committee/panel, etc.;on
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's on the playgroup committee.; How many people are on your staff?; She's a researcher on a women's magazine.; As a student on the committee w[h]ich organises this, I have to say that there have been some problems with the experience, and also that some changes should be made in order to make a better programme.

_source.definition_text: to be quick to understand and react to things
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's over ninety, but she's still on the ball.; When you're at Sants station, you'll need to be on the ball to find the tube.

_source.definition_text: because of a particular reason
_source.learnerexamples_text: You cannot discriminate on the grounds of religion.; I refused on the grounds that it was too risky.; I am convinced that it is better than Southside College on the grounds that a great mass of students are satisfied.

_source.definition_text: on television or radio
_source.learnerexamples_text: The radio station is on air from 6.00 a.m.; It is on air at 8.30 p.m. every Thursday and Saturday.

_source.definition_text: waiting to speak to someone on the telephone
_source.learnerexamples_text: His secretary put me on hold.; The day after, I called your office and after being put on hold, the person answering the phone was unwilling to come up with a proper reply.

_source.definition_text: If a plan or activity is on hold, it will not be done until a later time.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The project is on hold until we get more money.; What's more, it might, intentional[l]y or not, raise awareness on issues that might have been put on hold by authorities, such as the legalization of soft drugs.

_source.definition_text: likely to happen soon
_source.learnerexamples_text: Economic recovery is on the horizon.; Often this is justified as [a] result of society being collective[ly] afraid that a shortage of fuel is on the horizon.

_source.definition_text: If something is on the increase, it is happening more often.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Violent crime is on the increase.; [The] number of motorists is on the increase everywhere in the world.

_source.definition_text: If something is on loan, someone is borrowing it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Both paintings are on loan from the city museum.; For example, you can always take out on loan any video you like from our cent[re].

_source.definition_text: If a film or television programme is made on location, it is made at a place suitable to the story.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The movie was shot on location in Kenya.; We can't help mentioning the nice shots on location.

_source.definition_text: driving or travelling, usually over a long distance
_source.learnerexamples_text: We'd been on the road for 48 hours. ; I have experienced sitting behind a steering wheel on the road for many years.

_source.definition_text: making progress and likely to succeed
_source.learnerexamples_text: A fighter from Edinburgh is on track to become world heavyweight boxing champion.; We've got a lot of work to do but we're on the right track.; The sales teams are well on track and bringing [in] new customers every day.

_source.definition_text: being shown to the public
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her designs are currently on show at the Museum of Modern Art.; One of the facilit[ies] that really make[s] a difference is the Art Gallery, with its great exhibition on show, as well as the Art Library.

_source.definition_text: to have something with you
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you have your driving licence on you?

_source.base_text: be on the verge of sth/doing sth
_source.definition_text: to be going to happen or do something very soon
_source.searchterms_text: be on the verge of sth/doing sth;on
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company is on the verge of financial disaster.; I was on the verge of depression, when I decided to take the control of my own life.

_source.definition_text: inside a factory, office building, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are two restaurants on site.; They provide on-site childcare facilities for employees.; A small period of training on site is required a few days before the beginning of the job itself and how many interesting people you will meet!

_source.base_text: on no account; not on any account
_source.definition_text: not for any reason or in any situation
_source.searchterms_text: on;on no account not on any account;on no account; not on any account
_source.learnerexamples_text: On no account must these records be changed.; Mary did not want Martin to leave on any account, let alone move to a foreign country.

_source.base_text: be on the brink of sth
_source.definition_text: to be in a situation where something bad is going to happen very soon
_source.searchterms_text: be on the brink of sth;on
_source.learnerexamples_text: The two countries are on the brink of war.; By the end of the 21st century, Earth was on the brink of destruction. The atmosphere was polluted, the seas were poisoned, the animals were just a distant memory.

_source.definition_text: to be likely to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you think marriage is on the cards?

_source.definition_text: at that exact time
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have to leave at 7.30 on the dot.; He gave him an address and told him to be there at six on the dot.

_source.definition_text: to be extremely happy and excited
_source.learnerexamples_text: After I heard I'd got the job, I was on cloud nine!; But now, after the promise in which both said "yes", she was on cloud nine.

_source.definition_text: sometimes, but not often
_source.learnerexamples_text: I only drink alcohol on occasion.; As I am writing this I am begin[n]ing to conclude that there are very few disadvantages of banning private cars, only that for individuals it is far easier and [more] conven[i]ent to use a private car and not rely on our public transport, which can be on occasions very unreliable.

_source.base_text: be on the verge of sth/doing sth
_source.definition_text: to be going to happen or to do something very soon
_source.searchterms_text: be on the verge of sth/doing sth;on
_source.learnerexamples_text: a company on the verge of financial disaster; I was on the verge of depression, when I decided to take control of my own life.

_source.definition_text: If two people are on the same wavelength, they have the same way of thinking and it is easy for them to understand each other.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We chatted occasionally, but I never really felt we were on the same wavelength.; We were on the same wavelength and we therefore started our own research.

_source.definition_text: If someone's job, reputation, life, etc. is on the line, they may lose it.
_source.searchterms_text: (be) on the line;be on the line;on
_source.learnerexamples_text: If we don't win the contract, all our jobs are on the line.; The person who hopes to achieve success shouldn't be afraid of taking risks and sometimes putting his or her career on the line for the sake of gaining much bigger benefits.

_source.definition_text: to be nervous or worried
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sorry for shouting - I'm a bit on edge today.; I was consequently on edge all the time and was not able to have fun as much as the others did.

_source.definition_text: used when you are describing how a situation seems on the surface
_source.learnerexamples_text: On the face of it, it seems like a bargain, but I bet there are hidden costs.; On the face of it, both sides have valid arguments, and it's a difficult balancing act to manage.

_source.definition_text: to be ready to deal with something difficult that might happen
_source.searchterms_text: be on (your) guard;be on your guard;on
_source.learnerexamples_text: Companies were warned to be on their guard for suspicious packages.; However, we should be on guard, so as not to let the things escape our control.

_source.definition_text: If someone is in form or on form, they are feeling or performing well, and if they are off form they are not feeling or performing well.
_source.searchterms_text: be on (good) form;be on good form;on
_source.learnerexamples_text: Harry was on good form last night.

_source.definition_text: suddenly and without thinking first
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tend to act on impulse.; I'm seeing Milly as a capricious girl who, like most teenagers, enjoy[s] buying, although I think that she buys on impulse.

_source.base_text: on the part of sb; on sb's part
_source.definition_text: done or experienced by someone
_source.searchterms_text: on;on the part of sb on sb's part;on the part of sb; on sb's part
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is a major sacrifice on the part of the unions.; The accident was caused by carelessness on the instructor's part.; It seems that international sports competitions have always tended to attract a great amount of interest on the part of the media and have consistently been popular with sports fans the world over.

_source.definition_text: near to someone or something, and ready to help or be used when necessary
_source.learnerexamples_text: Extra supplies will be on hand, should they be needed.; From their point of view, they can always have you on hand whenever they need help, which is the most important part in their formative years.

_source.definition_text: in addition to your main job
_source.learnerexamples_text: She does a bit of bar work on the side.; At work, they gave her the worst jobs to do. She knew she didn't have much choice but she still tried to find something else on the side.

_source.definition_text: If you refuse to do something on principle, you refuse to do it because you think it is morally wrong.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She doesn't wear fur on principle.; They granted themselves a little celebration: it was time to keep the promise made four years before; so they bought some bottles of wine and got drunk (the[y] who, on principle, never drank alcohol).

_source.base_text: on the spur of the moment
_source.definition_text: If you do something on the spur of the moment, you do it suddenly, without planning it.
_source.searchterms_text: on;on the spur of the moment
_source.learnerexamples_text: On the spur of the moment we decided to go to London for the day.; In reality, many people buy things on the spur of the moment only to discover later that they, in fact, do not [meet] their expect[at]ions.

_source.definition_text: immediately
_source.learnerexamples_text: I accepted the job on the spot.; And when it was Meredith's turn to tell her about her impending wedding, she felt she was going to have a heart attack on the spot.

_source.definition_text: at the start of a new and important time or development
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're on the threshold of a new era in European relations.;  On the threshold of the third millen[n]ium, there is no stopping progress.

_source.definition_text: If you have something on, you are wearing it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's got a black coat on.; Why don't you put your new dress on?; And I want you to put on some baggy clothes, so that you'll feel comfortable while working.

_source.definition_text: into a bus, train, plane, etc. or onto a horse
_source.learnerexamples_text: The train suddenly started moving as I was stepping on.; Her horse began to move as soon as she was on.

_source.definition_text: happening or planned
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm busy tomorrow, but I've got nothing on the day after.; I've got a lot on at the moment.; Do you know what's on at the cinema?; Is the party still on for tomorrow?

_source.definition_text: performing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Hurry up with the make-up - I'm on in ten minutes.; The audience cheered as the band came on.; My faith in youth started to fade but then a boy named Josh came on.

_source.definition_text: working or being used
_source.learnerexamples_text: The heating has been on all day.; For example, the staff shouldn't leave the lights [on] and the heating's on when they don't need to use it.

_source.definition_text: in a way which results in forward movement
_source.learnerexamples_text: You cycle on and I'll meet you there.; Move on, please, and let the ambulance through.; I had just got [o]n the subway when it stopped and didn't move on.

_source.definition_text: one single time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I went sailing once, but I didn't like it.; I go swimming once a week.; We have lunch together once a month.; Once a year we all get together.; I can write to him once a week.

_source.definition_text: in the past, but not now
_source.learnerexamples_text: This house once belonged to my grandfather.; Computers are much cheaper nowadays than they once were.; I once went to England and I love the style of the clothes and how people dress there!

_source.definition_text: again
_source.learnerexamples_text: Once again I'm left with all the washing-up!; Once again I'm sorry.

_source.definition_text: one more time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to visit the colleges once more before we leave.; On Friday I will see him once more.

_source.definition_text: immediately
_source.learnerexamples_text: I knew at once that I'd like it here.; She called for an ambulance which came at once.

_source.definition_text: used at the beginning of a story to mean a long time ago
_source.learnerexamples_text: Once upon a time there was a beautiful princess.; Once upon a time there was a very poor family.

_source.definition_text: at the same time
_source.learnerexamples_text: They all started talking at once.; The study centre is really small and all the students talk at once.

_source.definition_text: sometimes but not often
_source.searchterms_text: (every) once in a while;every once in a while;once
_source.learnerexamples_text: We do go to the beach once in a while.; She did not say very much except for "oh" and "yes, yes" every once in a while.

_source.definition_text: used to mean that something is happening that does not usually happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: For once, the bus came on time.; We would take lots of pictures, and play our own instruments, and if we get lucky enough, we would even touch the very stones and for once be embraced by magic itself.

_source.definition_text: completely and finally
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's get to the bottom of this matter once and for all!; Now I was sure that my wife had left me once and for all.

_source.definition_text: suddenly
_source.learnerexamples_text: All at once he stood up and walked out of the room.; All at once, everything started to work again.

_source.definition_text: as soon as
_source.learnerexamples_text: Once I've found somewhere to live I'll send you my address.; Remember that you won't be able to cancel the contract once you've signed.; I'll write back soon once I know exactly when I can visit you.

_source.definition_text: the number 1
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've got three bags and I've only got one.; one hundred and ninety-one people; Four parcels came this morning, but only one was for Mark.; Paint one side, leave it to dry, and then paint the other.; She has got three da[ug]hters and one son.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a particular person or thing in a group that has already been talked about
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got a few books on Chinese food. You can borrow one if you like.; Which one would you like?; Would you make a copy for everybody in the office and a few extra ones for the visitors.; "Which cake would you like?" "The one at the front."; There were lots of people standing watching, and not one of them offered to help.

_source.definition_text: each other
_source.learnerexamples_text: How can they reach an agreement if they won't talk to one another?; We know one another from Poland.

_source.definition_text: separately
_source.learnerexamples_text: Eat them one at a time.; The story was a horrible one but it had a harmless ending. The mad man kills one at a time, but in the end, the producer of the film says: "Cut, we'll take everything once again."

_source.definition_text: separately, one after the other
_source.learnerexamples_text: One by one the old buildings in the city have been demolished and replaced with modern tower blocks.; They entered the room one by one.; So, he decides to investigate his death and he meets Harry's friends, one by one, to [find out] how he died, but they tell him different stories.

_source.definition_text: combined into a single thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a vacation and art course all in one.; The internet is like combining a television, a telephone and an airplane all in one.

_source.definition_text: many, in a series, especially with very little time between them
_source.learnerexamples_text: They had four children one after another.; She ate the chocolates one after the other until the box was finished.; Little parties organised one after another by [the] represent[ative]s of different countries gave me [an] opportunity to try the French, Spanish or Japanese special[tie]s.

_source.definition_text: any person in general
_source.learnerexamples_text: One ought to respect one's parents.; One can learn the beauty of the Greek language by simply reading the headings and will [soon] find that "The Step" is the best newspaper of all.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a particular person or thing in a group
_source.learnerexamples_text: One drawback is the cost of housing in the area.;  One of our daughters has just got married.; Our organization is just one of many charities that are providing famine relief in the region.; One of my presents was a dog!

_source.definition_text: used to talk about something that happened in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: One day, I came home to find my windows smashed.; One day, I was reading an interesting book when someone called me.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a particular occasion while avoiding stating the exact moment
_source.learnerexamples_text: I met him one day in the park.; One night we stayed up talking till dawn.; He was attacked as he was walking home from work late one afternoon.; One afternoon, my mum called me asking what I was doing.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a time in the future which is not yet decided
_source.learnerexamples_text: Why don't we meet for lunch one day next week?; I'd like to go skiing one Christmas.; I would be very glad if Enrico could stay with you one summer.

_source.definition_text: used when saying there is no other person or thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's the one person you can rely on in an emergency.; This may be your one and only opportunity to meet her.; My final guest on tonight's show needs no introduction. Please welcome the one and only Michael Jordan!; Often it's the one and only possibility for young children to see wild animals or unknown animals from the other side of the world in real life.

_source.definition_text: a single thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you think five of us will manage to squeeze into the one car?; There's too much data to fit onto just one disk.; I think we should paint the bedroom all one colour.; I would recommend just the one hotel: Riverside Hotel, which offers great value.

_source.definition_text: a few

_source.definition_text: in some way that is not stated
_source.learnerexamples_text: One way or another these bills have to be paid.; Everyone at the party was related in one way or another.; All of them made a big difference [to] our personal life and have affected it one way or another.

_source.definition_text: at some time in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to go to Berlin again one day.; I hope one day I can become like that.

_source.definition_text: in any way that is possible
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have to make a decision one way or the other about what needs to be done.; Our transportation system nowadays is also very well organised and there is a wide range of buses, subways, etc. with which you can reach your destination one way or the other.

_source.definition_text: used to describe someone or something that is completely different from other people or things
_source.learnerexamples_text: My Dad was one of a kind - funny, kind and generous.; Pele is indeed one of a kind and can be considered a model for youngsters.

_source.definition_text: the reflexive form of the pronoun 'one' when it refers to the person speaking or people in general
_source.learnerexamples_text: How else should one protect oneself and one's family? ; One must ask oneself: "Why is this happening?"

_source.definition_text: a round vegetable with layers that has a strong taste and smell
_source.learnerexamples_text: I always cry when I'm chopping onions.; Fry the onion and garlic for about two minutes.; This is cooked cab[b]age with beef, wild mushrooms and onion.

_source.definition_text: still happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: an ongoing investigation/process/project; No agreement has yet been reached and the negotiations are still ongoing.; To sum up, we are extremely positive about the club's future and its ongoing success.

_source.definition_text: describes products, services or information that can be bought or used on the Internet
_source.learnerexamples_text: online banking/shopping; an online newspaper/magazine/dictionary; I like it very much, because I can play online games now.

_source.definition_text: not more than a particular size or amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's only 13.; These shoes only cost £20.; He only passed one of his exams.; It's only four o'clock and it's already getting dark.; This is only ten minutes by car.

_source.definition_text: bought, used, etc. using the Internet
_source.learnerexamples_text: I ordered them online.; Why don't you go online and see what you can find?; When we went back home, I went online and checked my e-mails.

_source.definition_text: not anyone or anything else
_source.learnerexamples_text: Only Sue and Mark came to the meeting.; This club is for members only.; Only food bought at the café may be eaten here.; Only Marco, Anna, Sue and Nick came.

_source.definition_text: not in any other place
_source.learnerexamples_text: At present these televisions are only available in Japan.; These birds are only found in New Zealand.; I think animals, just as human beings, can only live in their natural habitat.

_source.definition_text: used to mean that something happened very recently
_source.learnerexamples_text: I only arrived half an hour ago.; They only put the roof on last week.; People were leaving and I'd only just arrived.; We'd only just set off when the car broke down.; I am really sorry I didn't write back earlier but I have only just got back from holiday.

_source.definition_text: used when you want to say how doing something simple would make it possible to avoid something unpleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: If only she'd listen to what he's saying, I'm sure they could work it out.; If only I had been more careful.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something is not important, or that you did not mean to upset someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't worry - it's only a scratch.; I was only joking.; I was only trying to help.; It was only a dream!

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize what you are hoping or wishing for
_source.searchterms_text: i only hope (that) ... /i only wish ... (that);i only hope that ... /i only wish ... that;i only hope that /i only wish  that;only
_source.learnerexamples_text: I only hope you know what you're doing.; I only wish that they would keep in touch more regularly.; I only hope I can have the chance to see her too.

_source.definition_text: used to say that more than one thing is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Not only did he turn up late, he also forgot his books.; If this project fails it will affect not only our department, but also the whole organization.; Not only did she introduce me to her friends but she also introduced me to her brother.

_source.definition_text: to not be perfect
_source.learnerexamples_text: Of course Tom makes mistakes - he's only human.;  In theory, it is easy to say "We should learn from the mistakes of the past" but is it easy to do so in practice? Many people would say "No" to this question, as we are only human.

_source.definition_text: used to say that there are limits to something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's only so much help you can give someone.; The effects of a longer life span have many side ef[f]ects such as an increase in the world's population and, since there is only so much food, m[any] more people are st[ar]ving to death.

_source.definition_text: used to mean that there are not any others
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is our only chance.; I was the only person on the train.; Is this really the only way to do it?; The only thing that matters is that the baby is healthy.; It was the only thing I could do under the circumstances.

_source.definition_text: used to introduce a statement which explains why something you have just said cannot happen or is not completely true

_source.definition_text: used to show that you are starting to talk about a different subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: How did we get onto this subject?; Let's move onto another topic!

_source.definition_text: used to show movement into or on a particular place

_source.definition_text: available for business or serving customers
_source.learnerexamples_text: The supermarket is open till 10.00 p.m.; Our phonelines are open until 9 pm.; They are open all day and all night.

_source.definition_text: beginning at a time and continuing after it
_source.searchterms_text: from the 1870s/march/6.30 pm, etc. onwards;from the 1870s/march/630 pm etc onwards;onwards
_source.learnerexamples_text: From June onwards, they began to meet regularly.; A growth to about 10% is expected around 2030 and an immense growth from 2030 onwards (from 10% to 27%).

_source.definition_text: not closed or fastened
_source.learnerexamples_text: an open door/window; An open suitcase lay on her bed.; You left the packet open.; Someone had left the window wide open.; The door was open!

_source.definition_text: An open area of land has no buildings on it or near it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: large open spaces; From the garden there was a marvellous view over open countryside.; I need to be outside in open spaces.

_source.definition_text: An open person is honest and does not hide their feelings.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's quite open about his weaknesses.; I wish you'd be more open with me, and tell me what you're feeling.; She has an honest, open face.; I was grateful to my flatmate who told me I should be open about myself.

_source.definition_text: to wait until you know all the facts before you form an opinion about something or judge someone

_source.definition_text: to come from a particular place, person or cause, or to begin during a particular period

_source.definition_text: an attractive object that is used as a decoration in a home or garden
_source.learnerexamples_text: There were glass ornaments on the shelf.; Expensive products such as necklaces and decorative ornaments are highly represented, much to the joy of the more wealthy people in the town.

_source.definition_text: a child whose parents have died

_source.learnerexamples_text: an orthodox Jewish family; the Russian/Greek Orthodox Church; Her ancestors were orthodox Jews and Rabbis.

_source.definition_text: If ideas or methods are orthodox, most people think they are correct, usually because they have existed for a long time.
_source.learnerexamples_text: orthodox medicine; Despite both being healthy people something appeared to be wrong after following all the orthodox methods to conceive a child.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about the remaining members of a group or items in a set

_source.definition_text: as well as the person or thing already mentioned

_source.definition_text: the opposite side or end of something

_source.learnerexamples_text: Put the chair at the other end of the desk.; The man was waiting on the other side of the street.; I'll move my bed to the other side of my room.

_source.definition_text: different from the thing or person already mentioned

The girl asked: "Is there any other way the Man [can] hurt us?"

_source.definition_text: used to introduce an explanation that is simpler than the one given earlier

_source.definition_text: referring to a day, week, etc. in the recent past without saying exactly when it was

_source.definition_text: used when you cannot or do not want to be exact about the information you are giving

_source.definition_text: happening one day/week, etc but not the next

_source.definition_text: different from or except

_source.definition_text: except for the thing you have just said

This means I have to keep all my things under the bed. Other than that, I would like a big beautiful garden because I love nature.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a person or thing which belongs to a group or set that you have already talked about

_source.definition_text: used to show that each person in a group of two or more people does something to the others

_source.definition_text: people in general, not including yourself

_source.definition_text: more ones

_source.definition_text: used after an order or suggestion to show what the result will be if you do not follow that order or suggestion

_source.definition_text: different to what has just been stated

_source.definition_text: except for what has just been referred to
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bike needs a new saddle, but otherwise it's in good condition.; The poor sound quality ruined an otherwise splendid film.; This seemed the high point of an otherwise dull and disorganised event.

_source.definition_text: used to say that you expect something to be true or that you expect something to happen

_source.definition_text: used to say or ask what is the correct or best thing to do

_source.definition_text: used to show that something belongs to or is connected with the person who is speaking and one or more other people

_source.definition_text: belonging to or relating to us

_source.definition_text: alone or without anyone else's help

_source.definition_text: the reflexive form of the pronoun 'we'

_source.definition_text: not in the place where you usually live or work, especially for a short time

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a period of time when someone goes away from home for a social activity

_source.definition_text: used to show movement away from the inside of a place or container

_source.definition_text: able to be seen

_source.definition_text: available to buy or see

_source.definition_text: to the point where something is removed or disappears

_source.definition_text: If you say or read something out loud, you say or read it so that other people can hear you.

_source.definition_text: not accurate

_source.base_text: the ins and outs of sth
_source.definition_text: the details of a particular subject
_source.searchterms_text: ins and outs of sth;out;the ins and outs of sth

_source.definition_text: outside

_source.definition_text: used to show movement away from the inside of a place or container

_source.definition_text: not in a job

_source.definition_text: without a job

_source.definition_text: unusual or different

_source.definition_text: to be of extremely good quality

_source.definition_text: If someone's actions or words are out of line, they are not suitable or acceptable.

_source.definition_text: If something is out of the question, it is not possible or not allowed.

_source.definition_text: old and no longer useful, correct or fashionable

_source.definition_text: to know little about what has recently happened

_source.definition_text: a strong feeling of anger or shock

_source.definition_text: not in a building

_source.definition_text: to repair and decorate a building that is old and in bad condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has a business renovating old buildings.; We should also renovate the library and extend the opening hours.

_source.definition_text: the act of repairing and decorating a building that is old and in bad condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: They spent all their savings on the renovation of an old cottage.; Dear Principal, In response to your memo, I am writing to provide you with some suggestions concerning the renovation of [the]Sports Centre, on behalf of the member of the student committee.

_source.definition_text: famous
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Lake District is renowned for its beauty.;  Maria Sandoral is a talented young artist who, at the age of 23, has far more background than a lot of artists. [...] She is renowned for her restless attitude, and for her deep interest in the field.

_source.definition_text: the amount of money that you pay to live in a building that someone else owns
_source.learnerexamples_text: I pay a higher rent than the other tenants because my room is bigger.; Rents here are very high/low.; I think I have left my wallet in your house. Please look for it and call me because I have to pay the rent tomorrow.

_source.definition_text: to pay money to live in a building that someone else owns
_source.learnerexamples_text: He'll be renting an apartment until he can find a house to buy. ;  I have rent[ed] a flat in Camden Town.

_source.definition_text: to pay money to use something for a short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: We could rent a car for the weekend. ; I rented a car from a garage so that I could get about.; If you want, you can rent a car.

_source.definition_text: to allow someone to pay you money to live in your building
_source.learnerexamples_text: I rented out my house and went travelling for a year. ; My Dad has a cottage which he rents (out) to tourists.; My uncle is trying to rent his house.

_source.definition_text: to organize something again in order to improve it
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's completely reorganized his schedule for the week.; We must focus our programme more [on] cultural exchange and less [o]n work; the students gained very little in this six weeks [so] we must reorganise this to improve the experience.

_source.definition_text: to fix something that is broken or damaged
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're repairing the holes in the road at last.;  I must get my bike repaired.; The garage said the car was so old it wasn't worth repairing.; I had my car repaired.

_source.definition_text: to improve a bad situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: It will take a long time to repair relations between the two countries.; The German government was not able to repair the damage caused by the crisis.

_source.definition_text: something that you do to fix something that is broken or damaged
_source.learnerexamples_text: My car is in the garage for repairs.; The repairs to the roof will be expensive.; My father sent it to the workshop for repair.

_source.definition_text: to be in good/bad condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most of the building is in very bad repair.; Cinemas and restaurants are necessary for all and we should also bear in mind that the existing sports facilities need renovation because they aren't in good repair.

_source.definition_text: to pay back money that you have borrowed
_source.learnerexamples_text: He had to sell his car to repay the loan.; We could make a deal, so that I could repay my debts.

_source.definition_text: to do something kind for someone who has done something to help you
_source.learnerexamples_text: What can I do to repay you for your kindness?; It's always a ple[a]sure to see you and I hope I'll be able to repay your hospitality if you ever come to visit us in Cambridge.

_source.definition_text: to say or do something more than once
_source.learnerexamples_text: He repeated the number.;  The test must be repeated several times. ;  "I don't know!" he repeated. ; Would you mind repeating what you just said?; I'd like to repeat that interesting visit.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone something that someone else has told you
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please don't repeat what I've just told you to anyone else.; He had written he was sorry, he should not have done it, he wished he had not repeated what I told him, he would never do something like that again...

_source.definition_text: done or happening more than once
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has refused repeated requests to be interviewed.; There were so many people and so many repeated questions and so much noise at home.

_source.definition_text: many times
_source.learnerexamples_text: He telephoned repeatedly, begging her to return. ; The European Union has repeatedly stressed the importance of language learning.; Once you pick up the new words and learn something, you need to say it repeatedly otherwise you will easily forget [it].

_source.definition_text: when something is repeated
_source.learnerexamples_text: We don't want a repetition of last year's disaster. ; This could in fact lead to a repetition of the mistakes of the past, when the paralyzed United Nations were, due to the small number and influence of neutral countries, a mere bystander to the risky arms-race fought out between the two nuclear superpowers.

_source.definition_text: doing or saying the same thing several times, especially in a way that is boring
_source.learnerexamples_text: a repetitive job; My grandparents used to say to my mum: "How can you wear it?! It hardly covers your b[o]ttom! When I was young..." (This is the beginning of a sentence when it starts to be little bit boring and extremely repetitive!)

_source.definition_text: to get something new because the one you had before has been lost or damaged
_source.learnerexamples_text: We'll have to replace this carpet soon.; I promised to replace the plate that I'd dropped.; I'm very sorry about it [but] don't worry because I bought another one to replace it.

_source.definition_text: to start using another thing or person instead of the one that you are using now
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're thinking of replacing our old TV with a new one. ; The factory replaced most of its workers with robots.; And I'm going to replace the desk, because I [don't] have enough [sp]ace to put a computer onto it.

_source.definition_text: to start to be used instead of the thing or person that is being used now
_source.learnerexamples_text: This system will replace the old one.; Tourism has replaced agriculture as the nation's main industry.; We felt very disappointed when we discovered that Danny had been replaced by an unknown and really bad actor.

_source.definition_text: to put something back in the place where it usually is
_source.learnerexamples_text: She picked up the books and carefully replaced them on the shelf.; Jane jumped up and carefully replaced the photo on the desk.

_source.definition_text: the thing or person that replaces something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: The agency sent a replacement for the secretary who resigned.;  It's not going to be easy to find a replacement for you.; But the people responsible for the concert did their best to find [a] replacement.

_source.definition_text: to answer
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Where are you going?" I asked. "Home," he replied.;  "I don't understand," she replied.; I replied that it was 12 o'clock.;  He didn't reply to my email. ; Please reply as soon as possible.

_source.definition_text: the process of replacing something with something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: the replacement of existing computer equipment; replacement windows; But by using much larger desks, we will be able to use the equipment more efficiently and this will reduce the cost for the replacement of broken equipment.

_source.definition_text: to describe a recent event or situation, especially on television, radio, or in a newspaper
_source.learnerexamples_text: Jo Smith reports on recent developments. ;  She reported that the situation had changed dramatically.;  A woman outside the shop reported seeing the gun. ; The assassination was reported in all the newspapers.; You reported that other performers were second-rate.

_source.definition_text: an answer
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her reply was short and unfriendly. ;  Have you had a reply to your email? ;  In reply to their questions, she just shrugged.;  She sent me an email in reply.; I asked why, but he made/gave no reply.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone in authority that something has happened, especially an accident or crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: He should have reported the accident immediately. ;  Have you reported the fault to a technician? ; Of course I reported it at the train station, but they couldn't find it [when] they s[ea]rched the train.

_source.definition_text: a description of an event or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: a news/weather report; a company's financial report; a report on climate change; I gave a report of the theft to the insurance company.; I'll be handing you a report [on] Chapter 7 the next day.

_source.definition_text: If something has reportedly happened or is reportedly a fact, people say it has happened or is true.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Two students were reportedly killed and several wounded. ; Some types of birds have reportedly become extinct in the area.

_source.definition_text: someone whose job is to discover information about news events and describe them on television, radio, the Internet, or in a newspaper
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's a reporter for the local newspaper.; The reporters t[alke]d about her life, where she was born, [and] who her parents [are].

_source.definition_text: to be equal to something
_source.learnerexamples_text: In practice the figure represents a 10% pay cut.;  The cancellation of the new road project represents a victory for protesters.; It [means] rec[y]cling 90% of the office material that we usually use. This represents a profit to the company which [would be] given to the employees, so they are motivated.

_source.definition_text: to officially speak or do something for someone else because they have asked you to
_source.learnerexamples_text: The union represents over 200 employees.; They chose a famous lawyer to represent them.; We hereby inform you that we have subsequently commen[c]ed proccedings aimed at hiring a la[wy]er to represent our party in court, should such a step be necessary.

_source.definition_text: to be the person from a country, school, etc. that is in a competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was chosen to represent France at the Olympics.; I was very fond o[f] swimming so I was glad that I was the one to be picked to represent my swimming team at that particular comp[e]tition.

_source.definition_text: to be a sign or symbol of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The crosses on the map represent churches.; I think the sea represents life and the sacrifice[s] we [make].

_source.definition_text: to show someone or something in a particular way, especially when this is done to influence other people's opinions
_source.learnerexamples_text: In the article, they were represented as evil exploiters of children.; Piggy, one of the main characters of the book Lord of the Flies, by William Golding, is represented as the typical fat boy with glasses.

_source.definition_text: the way someone or something is shown
_source.learnerexamples_text: an accurate representation of country life; Mildred is an establishment pet, the representation of the current society they are living in.

_source.definition_text: speaking or doing something officially for another person
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can he afford legal representation?; An old politician whose name I do not recall once said "Taxation without representation is t[y]ranny" - nowadays this concept might be extended to corruption itself.

_source.definition_text: someone who speaks or does something officially for another person or group of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: The firm has two representatives in every European city.; Dear Mr Robertson, My name is ... and I am a student representative.

_source.definition_text: criticism of someone, especially for not being successful or not doing what is expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was a hint of reproach in his voice.; The article gave the impression that the teachers were above/beyond reproach.; Before they turned of[f] the light, he saw disappointment and reproach in their eyes.

_source.definition_text: to criticize someone for not being successful or not doing what is expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've no reason to reproach yourself.; I know I shouldn't reproach myself for not giving her money.

_source.definition_text: to make a copy of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The diagram is reproduced by permission of the original author.; MI5 operates two computers, one for word processing and another for scanning and reproducing prints, drawings and photos.

_source.definition_text: to repeat something so that it is the same as before
_source.learnerexamples_text: The new design unfortunately reproduced some of the problems of the earlier model.; We were unable to reproduce the results of our earlier research.; I overcame this by listening to tapes and by trying to reproduce the native speaker's sounds and stresses.

_source.definition_text: If people, animals, or plants reproduce, they produce babies or young animals or plants.
_source.learnerexamples_text: These organisms reproduce by dividing.; Primitive man had a few aims in life like to be born, to reproduce and die, and among them there were two other important priorities, to hunt and to eat.

_source.definition_text: a copy of something, especially a painting
_source.learnerexamples_text: The picture is a reproduction of a Manet.; It would be great if the park provided some flight simulators and a reproduction of a space shuttle (so that people get a feeling of how it is to be an astronaut).

_source.definition_text: the process of producing babies or young animals and plants
_source.learnerexamples_text: We are learning about reproduction in biology.; What will happen if we live longer but we don't slow down the reproduction of our species?

_source.definition_text: an animal which produces eggs and uses the heat of the sun to keep its blood warm
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tom liked the reptiles, especially the snakes and the lizards.; Even though the northern part of Italy has undergone rapid industrialisation, there remain large areas of wild uninhabited ground where a great number of wild animals (birds, reptiles, large mammals) can live.

_source.definition_text: a country with no king or queen but with an elected government
_source.learnerexamples_text: France is a republic.; Unfortunately in ancient Greece, although the notion of the republic and democracy were invented and quite successfully developed there, not being a noble citizen could be cruelly disappointing and painful.

_source.definition_text: known to be good and honest
_source.learnerexamples_text: a reputable organization; I believe such a reputable company [as] you[rs] will not refuse to accept the responsibilities and prompt action will be taken in due course.

_source.definition_text: the opinion that people have about someone or something based on their behaviour or character in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company has a worldwide reputation for quality.;  Both hotels have a good reputation.; He quickly earned a reputation as an entertaining speaker.; My country has a great reputation for food.

_source.definition_text: when you politely or officially ask for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They received hundreds of requests for more information.;  His doctor made an urgent request for a copy of the report.;  An application form is available on request.; The clause was added to the contract at her request.; The manager refused their request to leave work early.

_source.definition_text: to politely or officially ask for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've requested a further two computers. ;  They requested that no photographs be taken in the church. ; Visitors are requested not to walk on the grass.; I have to rent a car [at the] Hertz agency and request information about where the hotel [i]s.

_source.definition_text: to need or demand something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Training to be a doctor requires a lot of hard work.; Please telephone this number if you require any further information.; Skiing down a steep slope requires total concentration.; Weddings are very different in our country and require a lot of [prepara]tion.

_source.definition_text: to officially demand that someone does something
_source.learnerexamples_text: You are required by law to produce a valid passport. ; It may occur in the future that they are required to posses[s] knowledge of something they didn't study at school in order to get a job.

_source.definition_text: something that you must do, or something you need
_source.learnerexamples_text: A good degree is a minimum requirement for many jobs.;  Valid insurance is a legal requirement.; Students who fail to meet the requirements of the course will fail.;  college entrance requirements; If you have any more requirements, please don't hesitate to contact me.

_source.definition_text: when someone is saved from a dangerous or unpleasant situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Lifeboats carry out many rescues every month.;  an unsuccessful rescue attempt; Last Friday I saw one that was about two guys who were lost in the jungle for nine days, and the rescue team found them alive.

_source.definition_text: to save someone from a dangerous or unpleasant situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fifty passengers had to be rescued from a sinking ship.; The government has refused to rescue the company from bankruptcy.; A bomb had exploded and that boy rescued me from the accident.

_source.definition_text: to help someone who is in a difficult situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: I forgot my purse but Anna came to the rescue and lent me some money.

_source.definition_text: when someone studies a subject in detail or tries to find information about a subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: scientific/medical research; a research program/laboratory;  research into language development;  They are conducting research into plant genetics.; I've done some research into the best beaches to visit.

_source.definition_text: to study a subject in detail or to try to find information about a subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: He spent several years researching a rare African dialect.; She's researching possible cures for malaria.; He went online to research flights and hotels.; I had to write an article [called] Protect our Environment so I researched and studied a lot about it using [the] Internet and [the] library to find suitable details.

_source.definition_text: someone who does research as a job
_source.learnerexamples_text: Researchers uncovered new facts about his family.; As researchers find out more about animals, we learn more about them and because of this we learn more about the world.

_source.definition_text: a similarity between two people or things, especially in their appearance
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's a striking resemblance between Diane and her mother.; I must admit that Dick has a strong resemblance to Neolithic Man, but everyone loves him because he is so cheerful and talkative.

_source.base_text: bear a/little/no, etc. resemblance to sth/sb
_source.definition_text: to be similar/not similar/somewhat similar, etc., to something or someone
_source.searchterms_text: bear a/little/no etc resemblance to sth/sb;bear a/little/no, etc. resemblance to sth/sb;resemblance;resemblances
_source.learnerexamples_text: He bears a resemblance to someone I used to know.; The city bears little resemblance to how it was 100 years ago.; The concert bore no resemblance to any other I have been to, firstly due to the location, and secondly thanks to the spontaneity, yet impressive precision of the performance - the two factors which created the unique atmosphere of the event.

_source.definition_text: to look like or be like someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She resembles her father.; After the earthquake, the city resembled a battlefield.; However, the most representative Romanian resorts resemble the ones in the Alps and maybe even exceed them in the respect of popularity among all walks of life and affordability.

_source.definition_text: to feel angry and upset about a situation or about something that someone has done
_source.learnerexamples_text: I resent having to work late.;  He resents the fact that she gets more money than he does.; More specifically, my cousin's husband and his family, neither of whom I knew very well, deeply resented this decision.

_source.definition_text: an arrangement that you make to have a seat on an aircraft, a room in a hotel, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to make a table reservation for two people for 9 o'clock.; Please confirm your reservation in writing by Friday.; I can make a reservation if you want.

_source.definition_text: a feeling of anger about a situation that you think is unfair
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you treat your staff differently, it just causes resentment.; I was pleased by the variety of opinions presented; some of the writers expressed a blind faith that we can still learn from our previous mistakes, while others approached the subject with a surprising resentment of our past.

_source.definition_text: a doubt or a feeling that you do not agree with something completely
_source.learnerexamples_text: I still have reservations about her ability to do the job.; When all my friends wanted to do something "naughty", [like] ringing bells at people's home[s] and running away, I had reservations.

_source.definition_text: to arrange to have a seat on an aircraft, a room in a hotel, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to reserve two seats on the 9:15 to Birmingham. ; I reserved a double room at the Lamb Hotel.; I must go [to] the bus station to reserve seats for the bus [at] 17:30 pm.

_source.definition_text: to not allow people to use something because it is only for a particular person or for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: This space is reserved for ambulances only.; These seats are reserved for the elderly and women with babies.; We will have free tent accom[m]odation in an area reserved for the staff.

_source.definition_text: an area of land where animals and plants are protected
_source.learnerexamples_text: We visited a huge reserve in Kenya.; As soon as we reached Nakuru two days later, we entered the game reserve to have a look around before it got dark.

_source.definition_text: a supply of something that you keep until it is needed
_source.learnerexamples_text: emergency cash reserves; The dependence on oil is a menace because oil reserves will disappear and because at this time we have no other invention to replace it.

_source.definition_text: describes people who keep their feelings or thoughts private rather than showing them
_source.learnerexamples_text: Marcus is more reserved than his brother.; Mrs. James was a reserved and solitary person and she lived according to the way she wished to live.

_source.definition_text: someone who lives in a particular place
_source.learnerexamples_text: a resident of the UK/Australia;  Local residents were angry at the lack of parking spaces.; We will have less anxious residents in cities, who will not hurry to go to work or will not be late home or at the office.

_source.definition_text: a building where someone lives
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Governor's official residence; The two episodes in the book 'The colour of blood' that I've decided to write about are Cardinal Benn and Prime Minister meeting at the official residence, and the fatal mass in honour to the blessed martyrs.

_source.definition_text: living in a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has been resident in Britain for most of her life.; My name is ANA AMURRIO, born in Spain (Madrid) twenty four years ago, and resident in your country since July of [this] year.

_source.definition_text: A residential area has only houses and not offices or factories.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a largely residential area with one or two shops.; 'Varta' is situated in a quiet residential area and could be called 'a family restaurant'.

_source.definition_text: A residential course or job is one where you live at the same place as you study or work.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a residential course so I'll be away for a week.

_source.definition_text: to officially tell your employer that you are leaving your job
_source.learnerexamples_text: She resigned as headteacher.;  Two directors have resigned from the company. ; So Laura stepped into her boss'[s] office, wished him a Merry Christmas and resigned.

_source.definition_text: to make yourself accept something that you do not like because you cannot easily change it
_source.learnerexamples_text: He resigned himself to living alone.; Personally I wouldn't like to be at the age when you can't afford anything except bread and butter and you have to resign yourself to this miserable existence without any hope for [a] brighter future.

_source.definition_text: when you accept something that you do not like because you cannot easily change it
_source.learnerexamples_text: She accepted her illness with calm resignation.; He sighed with resignation and got up.

_source.definition_text: when someone tells their employer that they are leaving their job
_source.learnerexamples_text: a letter of resignation; I handed in my resignation yesterday.; She had been so proud of herself no more than five minutes ago walking out of the editor's office after handing him her letter of resignation.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being resilient
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had the resilience to try again. ; Their resilience had been pushed to the extreme and, but for their sheer longing for a child, they might have given up.

_source.definition_text: strong enough to get better quickly after damage, disappointment, illness, shock, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Growth figures show that the economy is still fairly resilient.; He could not stand the thought of staying away from Bill, he was not that resilient.

_source.definition_text: to stop yourself from doing something that you want to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't resist chocolate.;  I just can't resist reading other people's mail.; How do we resist all these nice snacks, and stay slim?

_source.definition_text: to fight against something or someone that is attacking you
_source.learnerexamples_text: British troops resisted the attack for two days.; The Turkish ci[v]ilization was poorer than [the] Greek ci[v]ilisation and that is one more reason why [the] Greeks had to resist and fight their enemies.

_source.definition_text: when people disagree with a change, idea, etc. and refuse to accept it
_source.learnerexamples_text: resistance to political change; The only resistance comes from Jack, an aggressive and impetuous boy who places facts higher than speech[e]s.

_source.definition_text: when someone fights against someone who is attacking them or competing against them
_source.learnerexamples_text: She didn't put up much resistance.; Their knowledge helped Hitler to prolong his resistance against the overwhelming superiority of the Allies.

_source.definition_text: an organization that secretly fights against an enemy that has taken control of its country
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was active in the resistance.; Despite the fact that [the] Germans were many and much more powerful, they faced many difficulties from the Greek resistance.

_source.definition_text: the ability of your body to not be affected by illnesses
_source.learnerexamples_text: Cold weather may lower the body's resistance to infection.; His physical resistance is exceptional, he is young, in perfect condition, healthy.

_source.definition_text: an official decision that is made after a group or organization have voted
_source.learnerexamples_text: Congress passed a resolution in support of the plan. ; Our branch has submitted a resolution on housing to the conference.; India declared that the UN resolution about the ban on nuclear weapons [wa]s unfair.

_source.definition_text: the solution to a problem
_source.learnerexamples_text: a successful resolution to the crisis ; It might help us to find alternative conflict resolutions.

_source.definition_text: a promise to yourself to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: My New Year's resolution is to do more exercise. ; As a New Year's resolution I decided to save some money in a jar for my husband.

_source.definition_text: when you are very determined to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The training was tough, but his resolve never wavered.;  Daniella's attention was focused on the scene and she was truly enjoying what was going on. This sight toughened Marco's resolve.

_source.definition_text: to solve or end a problem or difficulty
_source.learnerexamples_text: an attempt to resolve the dispute; The student committee greatly appreciate your efforts to resolve our current problems, in particular improving and reconstructing our sports centre.

_source.definition_text: a place where many people go for a holiday
_source.learnerexamples_text: a seaside resort; a ski resort; I am in Kajdussdoset which is a famous holiday resort in Hungary, my country.

_source.definition_text: to do something bad in order to achieve what you want, often because it is the only thing you can do to achieve it
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had to resort to threats to get my money back.; This is caused by a person's basic need for food: If someone can't get enough to eat he might have to resort to stealing.

_source.definition_text: something that you do because everything else has failed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Soldiers were given the authority to shoot, but only as a last resort.; But forcing the child to believe in the way we would like it to believe should be used only as a last resort, after discussion and persuading, not before.

_source.definition_text: something useful that a country, person, or organization has which they can use
_source.learnerexamples_text: natural resources; Britain's mineral resources include oil, coal and gas deposits.; With all the resources on the Net, I don't need to go to the library as often as I used to.

_source.definition_text: good at finding ways to solve problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: When we didn't have much money, we had to be more resourceful.; The tormentor was inventive, clever, resourceful and learned fast how to make the most ordinary objects (a moth, a crow) into a source of overwhelming fear for his victim.

_source.definition_text: when you admire someone because of their knowledge, skill, or achievements
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's an excellent teacher and I have the greatest respect for her.; New teachers have to earn the respect of their students.; I have met some fantastic players, especially George N, an experienced footballer who teaches me a lot about getting respect on and off the field, and he's been of great help to me.

_source.definition_text: when you are polite to someone, especially because they are older or more important than you
_source.learnerexamples_text: You should show more respect for your parents. ; Teachers should be treated with respect.; She has no respect for her boss.; As for people who attend weddings, it's important for them to wear formal clothes to show their respect [for] the new couple.

_source.definition_text: relating to a particular thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: I am writing with respect to your letter of 24 June.; With respect to the ages of the members, they are between fifteen and twenty years old.

_source.definition_text: in a particular way, or in many ways
_source.learnerexamples_text: The school has changed in many respects.; How's your friend Mike? He is in many respects better than [a] computer, isn't he? (Teasing you again, sorry).

_source.definition_text: relating to a particular thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: I include payment in respect of your invoice of May 13th.; Instead of that, we should have more English grammar lessons - some of our English students are very interested in them, especially in respect of their exam this year.

_source.definition_text: to admire someone because of their knowledge, achievements, etc
_source.learnerexamples_text: I respect him for his honesty.; I deeply respect David for what he has achieved.; It's nice to have a friend who respects you and who you respect too.

_source.definition_text: If you respect someone's rights, customs, wishes, etc. you accept their importance and are careful not to do anything they would not want.
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you decide to do otherwise we will, of course, respect your wishes.; But the situation is getting worse because of the decisions of the European Union, which is trying to unif[y] Europe[an] education without respecting the wishes of the students, who are trying to stop this process.

_source.definition_text: large enough or good enough

_source.definition_text: containing a lot of something that is important or valuable

_source.definition_text: people who are rich

_source.definition_text: a lot of money or valuable objects

_source.definition_text: to end something unpleasant

_source.definition_text: to throw something away or give something to someone because you no longer want it

_source.definition_text: to make someone leave

_source.definition_text: a journey riding a bicycle, motorcycle, or horse

_source.definition_text: a journey in a vehicle or train

_source.definition_text: a machine at a fair which moves people up and down, round in circles, etc as they sit in it

_source.definition_text: a time when you experience a lot of problems

_source.definition_text: someone who rides a horse, bicycle, or motorcycle

_source.definition_text: correct or true

_source.base_text: have a/no right to do sth

_source.definition_text: used to express agreement with someone

_source.definition_text: in a correct way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is rightly concerned about the situation.; They quite rightly complained to the manager.; If I remember rightly, there were over 5,000.

_source.definition_text: a round piece of jewellery that you wear on your finger
_source.learnerexamples_text: a wedding ring; He bought her a diamond ring.; Sammy gave me a gold ring, Remi an orange swe[a]ter, Minny a bag and Dominique a red cap.

_source.definition_text: supporting the ideas of parties on the political right

_source.definition_text: not able to change or be changed easily

_source.definition_text: to telephone someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you want anything, just give me a ring.; If you find them, please give me a ring.

_source.definition_text: something that is the shape of a circle

_source.learnerexamples_text: Shane Watson? That name rings a bell.; Its name is Laser - I suppose it rings a bell?

_source.definition_text: to telephone someone who rang you earlier or to telephone someone for a second time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm a bit busy - can I ring you back later?; However, I'll ring back to [get more] information.

_source.definition_text: angry, violent behaviour by a crowd of people

_source.definition_text: to telephone someone

_source.definition_text: to take part in a riot
_source.learnerexamples_text: People were rioting in the streets.; If there [are] a lot of frustrated individuals in an area, they may band together and begin rioting.

_source.definition_text: to behave in a noisy, violent, or wild way without being controlled

_source.definition_text: to remove something by pulling it away quickly

_source.definition_text: to become important, successful, or rich

_source.definition_text: cooked in an oven or over a fire
