_source.definition_text: the surface that covers the top of a building or vehicle
_source.learnerexamples_text: The house has a flat/tiled roof.;  He climbed onto the roof.; Put the luggage on the roof of the car.; It's an old Charentese house, with white walls, a red roof and a small garden, close to the seaside.

_source.definition_text: somewhere to live
_source.searchterms_text: a roof over your head;roof;roof over your head;roofs
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took me in when I didn't have a roof over my head.; As for the new homes for local people it seems to be that it will be of particular importance to homeless people, who will feel that they have a roof over their head without having to pay anything.

_source.definition_text: If the level of something, especially a price, goes through the roof, it increases very quickly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The price of corn has gone through the roof recently.; Try extreme sports and feel your adrenaline levels going through the roof!

_source.definition_text: to become very angry and start shouting
_source.learnerexamples_text: If I'm late again he'll hit the roof.; Be careful, if you make too much noise he'll hit the roof.

_source.definition_text: a part of the inside of a building that is separated from other parts by walls, floor and ceiling
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hotel room; I'd like to book a double/single room.; We're in meeting room 1.; She's upstairs in her room.; She has a lot of flowers in her room.

_source.definition_text: space for things to fit into
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is there enough room for me in the car?; That sofa would take up too much room in the flat.; James took the books off the little table to make room for the television.; In the wardrobe there is no[t] enough room to put all my stuff away.

_source.definition_text: If there is room for improvement, something can be made better.
_source.learnerexamples_text: His work isn't bad but there's still some room for improvement.; She is Polish, aged 29 and can speak English pretty well, but there is still room for improvement, that's why she wants to spend a year in England, looking after children in an English-speaking family.

_source.definition_text: someone who you share a room, apartment, etc. with
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was my roommate while we were at college. ; I was a student and lived together in a flat with my roommate Claudia.

_source.definition_text: the part of a plant that grows under the ground and gets water and food from the soil
_source.learnerexamples_text: These plants have really deep roots.; I have gathered over three hundred species: flowers, roots, leaves and others.

_source.definition_text: the cause of something, usually something bad
_source.searchterms_text: root;root of sth;roots;the root of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: We must get to the root of this problem.; Money is said to be the root of all evil.; Unfortunately none of us has ever tried to find the root of this problem but the influences that it has on the environment are obvious.

_source.definition_text: where someone or something originally comes from
_source.learnerexamples_text: the roots of modern jazz; I think people should know where our European pop and rock music has its roots.

_source.definition_text: very thick string made from twisted thread
_source.learnerexamples_text: We tied the boat to a post with a length of rope.; a coil of rope; A few moments later she took out a rope from her backpack.

_source.definition_text: to learn/know how to do a job or activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: I spent a month in the accounts department, learning the ropes.; Knowing the ropes, he did as usual, but one thing was left out.

_source.definition_text: a flower with a pleasant smell and thorns, that grows on a bush
_source.learnerexamples_text: a rose bush; She sent him a bunch of red roses.; He brought me to a posh restaurant and he gave me a bunch of roses.

_source.definition_text: very positive and happy
_source.learnerexamples_text: The future looks rosy.; In addition, I can see something in his eyes that says his life is not as rosy as it seems.

_source.definition_text: Rosy faces are a healthy pink colour.
_source.learnerexamples_text: rosy cheeks; Not a lot taller than a lot of us, with beautiful bl[ue] eyes and rosy cheeks, she used to called us "Muffins".

_source.definition_text: If vegetable or animal substances rot, they decay, and if something rots them, it makes them decay.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sugar rots your teeth.;  the smell of rotting fish; He told me of how he had c[o]me to see it every day, and seen how all the meat had rotted away and stuff.

_source.definition_text: Rotten vegetable or animal substances are decaying.
_source.learnerexamples_text: rotten eggs/fruit; I'll tell you something - my freezer still smells of rotten fish.

_source.definition_text: A rough surface is not smooth.
_source.learnerexamples_text: rough ground; It was a rough mountain road, covered in stones and huge holes.; I went with some people I kn[ew] from bike competitions, and I [was] impressed with how well they can ride a bike on a rough terrain, w[hereas] I had to go carefully in some tracks.

_source.definition_text: approximate and not exact
_source.learnerexamples_text: Write a rough copy first and check the grammar.;  Can you give me a rough idea of the numbers? ; I lost my personal note-pad where I used to write all my job tasks, my arrangements and the records of my students. I have [even] written the rough copy of some personal letters [there].

_source.definition_text: difficult or unpleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's having a rough time at work. ; He did the mountain-route last year and he says that even he had a rough time.

_source.definition_text: If the sea or weather is rough, there is a lot of strong wind and sometimes rain.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The boat sank in rough seas off the Swedish coast. ; I went to the seaside but I was not allowed to bathe for they said that the sea was too rough.

_source.definition_text: approximately
_source.learnerexamples_text: There has been an increase of roughly 2.25 million.; Roughly speaking, it's 2.25 million.; We have roughly the same tastes.; These are very special cases and roughly speaking, confined to one thing.

_source.definition_text: dangerous or violent
_source.learnerexamples_text: a rough part of town ;  Hockey can be quite a rough game. ; I like him as a football player because he plays fair, not rough.

_source.definition_text: forcefully or violently
_source.learnerexamples_text: He pushed us roughly out of the door.; My mother treated me roughly and unkindly by thrashing or smacking me a[t] any time possible.

_source.definition_text: without taking a lot of care to make something perfect
_source.learnerexamples_text: Roughly chop the tomatoes and add to the onions.; She glanced at the mirror, roughly [brushed] her hair with her fingers and went outside for her car.

_source.definition_text: to or in different parts of a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: The landlord showed me round the house.; I had to go all round town to find a hotel that was open.; Well, she showed me round her hometown and we did some sight-seeing.

_source.definition_text: surrounding or being on all sides of something, or in a circular movement
_source.learnerexamples_text: We sat round the fire.; I put my arm round her.;  She had a scarf round her neck. ; The Moon goes round the Earth.; There [is] a big wood round this lake.

_source.definition_text: to someone's home
_source.learnerexamples_text: Wendy's coming round this afternoon. ; I'll go round and see her later.; So would you come round and see me?

_source.definition_text: with a circular movement
_source.learnerexamples_text: This switch makes the wheels go round.

_source.definition_text: to the opposite direction
_source.learnerexamples_text: She looked round. ;  Turn the car round and let's go home. ; I turned round and I saw that the one who was calling me was the singer!!

_source.definition_text: from one place or person to another
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you pass these forms round, please?

_source.definition_text: in the shape of a circle or ball
_source.learnerexamples_text: a round hole/stone/table/window; a round face; It is on the round table in your room.

_source.definition_text: moving in a circle without stopping
_source.learnerexamples_text: We drove round and round trying to find the hotel.; It's not fun to look at an animal who is bored and only walks round and round.

_source.definition_text: when people clap
_source.learnerexamples_text: The crowd gave him a huge round of applause.; It was unbelievable, there was a round of applause and some people couldn't help crying.

_source.definition_text: the first/second/third/final, etc. stage in a competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was beaten in the first round.; At five o'clock in the afternoon, the second round of the games [will begin].

_source.definition_text: a group of events that is part of a series
_source.learnerexamples_text: a round of interviews ; a new round of talks between the two countries; My life was an endless round of parties, and social events.

_source.definition_text: a circular place where roads meet and where cars drive around until they arrive at the road that they want to turn into
_source.learnerexamples_text: At the roundabout, take the second turning.; Rosewood Avenue is off the first roundabout by Tesco.

_source.definition_text: drinks that you buy for a group of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's your turn to buy the next round.; Rob (her husband) was so happy and in such a splendid mood that he decided to pay [for] a round of beer.

_source.definition_text: the roads or paths you follow to get from one place to another place
_source.learnerexamples_text: an escape route; I'm just planning my route.; What's the best route to the station?;  Crowds gathered all along the route to watch the race.; Each cycle route [is] shown in a different colour, so we didn't lose our way.

_source.definition_text: a method of achieving something
_source.learnerexamples_text: A university education is seen by many as the best route to a good job.; This means that only by presenting them with [a] great variety of opportunities can we be certain that our children will be shaped correctly. Thus, [...] it seems to be the only legitimate and most advantagous route to follow.

_source.definition_text: the things you regularly do and how and when you do them
_source.learnerexamples_text: a daily routine;  He longed to escape the routine of an office job.; There's no set/fixed routine at work - every day is different.; Usually we speak about our daily routine, [and] our plan[s] for the future.

_source.definition_text: done regularly and very boring
_source.learnerexamples_text: a routine check/task; His job is very routine.; Nevertheless, when a job becomes routine (and it usually always does), people seem to reminisce [about] their student years with a sense of disappointment.

_source.definition_text: a straight line of people or things
_source.learnerexamples_text: a row of chairs/houses;  My students sit at desks in rows for most of the time.; Two rows of serv[a]nts stood beside the path which was in front of him with [a] red carpet on it.

_source.definition_text: a line of seats
_source.learnerexamples_text: to sit on the back/front row ;  Isn't that Sophie sitting in the row behind us? ; It is great in my class, there are so many people and they are all nice. I'm sitting in the first row next to Nicole.

_source.definition_text: one after another without a break
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's just won the tournament for the fifth year in a row.; Maradona was the captain of the team, and since he arrived, the team won three championships in a row.

_source.definition_text: to move a boat or move someone in a boat through the water using oars
_source.learnerexamples_text: We rowed to the other side of the lake.; In the end, they had to row all the way back to the beach and it was very late when they got home.

_source.definition_text: relating to a queen or king and their family
_source.learnerexamples_text: the royal family; a royal visit; Chris, Anne and I wanted to visit the royal palace.

_source.definition_text: a loud, angry argument
_source.learnerexamples_text: My parents often have rows.;  a blazing row; The sun was shining, the birds w[ere] singing and all the people were happy, but I was very angry because I [had] had a row with my husband.

_source.definition_text: to press your hand or a cloth on a surface and move it backwards and forwards
_source.learnerexamples_text: She rubbed her hands together to warm them. ;  He rubbed himself dry with a towel. ;  Rub the stain with a damp cloth. ; Paul suddenly saw something. A kind of shadow. He rubbed his eyes but there was nothing.

_source.definition_text: to move a substance backwards and forwards over a surface so that it covers it and goes into it
_source.searchterms_text: -bb-;bb;rub;rub sth into/on etc;rub sth into/on, etc.;rubbed;rubbing;rubs
_source.learnerexamples_text: I rubbed some suntan oil on her back. ;  Rub the butter into the flour.

_source.definition_text: to upset someone by talking to them about something which you know they want to forget
_source.learnerexamples_text: I know your exam results were better than mine - there's no need to rub it in.; Indeed, I wouldn't [want] to rub it in but you have reached seventy or eighty. I don't think you can fend for yourself.

_source.definition_text: a small object which is used to remove pencil marks from paper
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you have a rubber in your pencil case?; We have to bring with us a pencil, many crayons and a rubber.

_source.base_text: rub out sth or rub sth out
_source.definition_text: to remove writing from something by rubbing it with a piece of rubber or with a cloth
_source.searchterms_text: rub;rub out sth or rub sth out
_source.learnerexamples_text: If your line isn't straight, rub it out and start again.; Moreover, all the bad words written on the building's walls should be rubbed out.

_source.definition_text: a strong material that bends easily, originally produced from the juice of a tropical tree, and used to make tyres, boots, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: shoes with rubber soles; Worst [of] all it seems to me is the way some zoos are regarded as places of entertainment like [a] circus, where the people are encouraged to laugh at animals whe[n] they 'perform their funny tricks' like eating bananas, swinging from rubber tyres and so on.

_source.definition_text: things that you throw away because you do not want them
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our rubbish gets collected on Thursdays.; Put the empty box in the rubbish bin.; I took some old furniture to the rubbish dump.; While I [was] walking in the rain along the dark and quiet alleys, I heard a weak cry that sound[ed] like a baby [coming] from a corner with rubbish scattered everywhere.

_source.definition_text: something that is of bad quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's so much rubbish on TV. ; I was t[aught] to believe that recorded music was rubbish compar[ed] to live music.

_source.definition_text: something that is nonsense or wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ignore him, he's talking rubbish.; For example, the advertisement where the worker eats only "Mars" and can work hard after it. It's rubbish.

_source.definition_text: behaving in a way which is not polite and upsets other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: a rude comment/remark;  He complained that a member of staff had been rude to him.;  It would be rude to leave without saying goodbye. ; I thought he [wa]s such a rude man.

_source.definition_text: in a rude way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He rudely pushed past us.; When I made a[n] attempt to speak to the conductor, I was rudely told off and told to stay seated for the rest of the journey.

_source.definition_text: Rude words or jokes relate to sex or going to the toilet.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He taught his little sister a lot of rude words.; She just wanted to shout rude words when finally she recognised her father... standing in front of her.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being rude
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was shocked by her rudeness. ; Many complaints were made about the rudeness of the reception [staff].

_source.definition_text: a soft piece of material used to cover the floor
_source.learnerexamples_text: My dog loves lying on the rug in front of the fire.; There is [a] green rug in the middle of the floor.

_source.definition_text: a sport played by two teams with an oval ball and H-shaped goals
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's a keen rugby fan.; I want to play some rugby and swim in the sea.

_source.definition_text: the broken parts that are left from an old building after it has been destroyed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thousands of tourists wander around these ancient ruins every year.; After that I'm going to travel to Luxor and see [the] ruins.

_source.definition_text: to be in a very bad state
_source.learnerexamples_text: The war left one million people dead and the country in ruins.; When my grandparents were young, Germany lay in ruins.

_source.definition_text: when someone loses everything such as all their money or their job
_source.learnerexamples_text: The collapse of the bank has left many people in financial ruin.; He started his first business some time ago which led to financial ruin.

_source.definition_text: an official instruction about what you must or must not do
_source.learnerexamples_text: to break the rules;  to obey/follow the rules;  You can't smoke at school, it's against the rules.; There're plenty of rules in my high school.

_source.definition_text: to spoil or destroy something completely
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were late and the dinner was ruined.; Her injury ruined her chances of winning the race.; Huge modern hotels have ruined this once unspoilt coastline.; But she didn't keep her promise and she ruined my life.

_source.definition_text: a principle of a system, such as a language or science
_source.learnerexamples_text: the rules of grammar; We did a little exam about tenses and grammar rules.

_source.definition_text: the usual way something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: an exception to the rule; I visit my parents on Sunday, as a rule.; As a rule, children who ride bikes change their bike[s] for cars [when they are older] and are pre[pa]red a little [for] how to behave on the road.

_source.definition_text: a way of calculating something, which is not exact but which will help you to be correct enough
_source.searchterms_text: a rule of thumb;rule;rule of thumb;rules
_source.learnerexamples_text: As a rule of thumb, you need one egg for every 125g flour.; As a rule of thumb, one third of the people working in central Copenhagen [go] by car, one third by public transport, and one third by bike.

_source.definition_text: to allow someone to do something which is not usually allowed
_source.learnerexamples_text: We don't usually let students take books home, but I'll bend the rules on this occasion.

_source.definition_text: when someone is in control of a country
_source.learnerexamples_text: military rule; There have been reports of immense human suffering under his rule.; A XXth century modernist, not only should he be paid honour for his artistry but also for his never cea[s]ing battle against Franco's rule.

_source.definition_text: to influence someone's thoughts or actions
_source.learnerexamples_text: His life is ruled by the demands of his job.; Our Earth has grown overcrowded and every inch of our life is ruled by computers.

_source.definition_text: to be in control of somewhere, usually a country
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were ruled for many years by a dictator.; In the late 60s when Greece was ruled by a military government, many young students fled abroad to escape its cruelty.

_source.definition_text: to be in control of somewhere, usually a country
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were ruled for many years by a dictator.; the ruling party; Cleopatra was the seventh queen of Egypt and ruled until 63 B.C. whe[n] she died.

_source.base_text: rule out sb/sth or rule sb/sth out
_source.definition_text: to decide or state that something is impossible or will not happen, or that something or someone is not suitable
_source.searchterms_text: rule;rule out sb/sth or rule sb/sth out
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police haven't yet ruled out murder.; The police have not ruled him out as a suspect.; Owning a house no longer seems to be a practical future plan and has to be ruled out, which meant that people lost their ultimate goal for working.

_source.definition_text: a flat, straight stick which is used to measure things
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can I borrow your ruler?;  We have to bring with us a pencil and a ruler for the first lesson.

_source.definition_text: the leader of a country
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was the ruler of the country for over 20 years.; Versailles in France and the time of Louis XIV as the ruler would be my place and time I would choose to visit.

_source.definition_text: an official legal decision, usually made by a judge
_source.learnerexamples_text: This ruling has delighted road safety campaigners.; As you certainly will remember, the ruling of the High Court obliges you to keep the level of noise below a certain level depending on the distance of the airport.

_source.definition_text: a fact that a lot of people are talking about although they do not know if it is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Rumours are going round the school about Mr Mason and his assistant.; Someone has been spreading rumours about me.;  I heard a rumour that you were leaving.; However, the press shouldn't create rumours and hunt those people like animals.

_source.definition_text: to move on your feet at a faster speed than walking
_source.learnerexamples_text: He can run very fast. ;  He ran away when I tried to pick him up. ;  We had to run to catch up with him. ;  I run about three miles every morning. ; Children can run ev[e]rywh[e]re.

_source.definition_text: to organize or control something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She ran her own restaurant for five years. ; The social group is run by the residents themselves.; My aunt is always working. She runs her own business.

_source.definition_text: If liquid runs somewhere, it flows.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tears ran down her face. ;  Have you got a tissue? My nose is running. ; The warm urine ran through my underwear, [down] my legs and white socks, into my shoes and floated out on the floor.

_source.definition_text: If trains or buses are running, they are available to travel on.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Trains are still running, despite the snow.; A bus runs three times a day into town.; Buses are running an hour late, because of an earlier accident.; There is an easy way to get to the college: a service bus runs every 15 minutes, [and] the journey takes only 20 minutes.

_source.definition_text: If you run a computer program, you use it on your computer.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did you run a virus check this morning? ; At this point the computer is unable to run any program.

_source.definition_text: If a piece of equipment is running, it is switched on and working, and if you run it, you switch it on and make it work.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The engine is running more smoothly now.; We could start a campaign where people are reminded not to leave their car, lorry or bus engines running for more than one minute if stationary.

_source.definition_text: to publish something in a newspaper or magazine
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the papers are running this story on the front page.; If we run a story on "HIV Symptoms" we could have a very succes[s]ful first issue.

_source.definition_text: to move something along, over, or through something else
_source.searchterms_text: ran;run;run sth along/over/through etc sth;run sth along/over/through, etc. sth;running;runs
_source.learnerexamples_text: She ran her fingers through her hair.; The manly figure that had tried to stop her now kneeled before her body running his finger through her soft blond hair.

_source.definition_text: to be at a particular level
_source.learnerexamples_text: Inflation is now running at 5.8%.; According to the official dat[a], unemployment is running at so high a level that it is even possible that the unemploy[ed] will rebel against the government.

_source.definition_text: If someone, especially a child, runs wild, they behave as they want to and no one controls them.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their nine-year-old son is left to run wild.; My parents decided to move to a small village when I was just a kid. Shortly after we settled [in], my parents decided that I was running wild and that it was time for me to receive some sort of education.

_source.definition_text: If something makes your blood run cold, it frightens you very much.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I heard a tapping on the window which made my blood run cold.; This thought scared me and made my blood run cold.

_source.definition_text: If someone's imagination runs wild, they are not able to control their thoughts.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was getting dark and my imagination was starting to run wild.; Her imagination started to run wild and she set about think[ing] about the dark corridors, the secret passages and the obscure dungeons that the castle might hide.

_source.definition_text: to behave in a noisy, violent, or wild way without being controlled
_source.learnerexamples_text: They allow their kids to run riot.

_source.definition_text: to do something although something bad might happen because of it
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think I'll run the risk of hurting her feelings, and tell her the truth.; They constantly run the risk of losing their physical abilities.

_source.definition_text: to be very busy doing a lot of different things
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm exhausted, I've been running around all morning.; Nowadays people are running around trying to save time wherever they can, when in reality time passes far quicker when we try to save it.

_source.definition_text: to secretly leave a place because you are unhappy there
_source.learnerexamples_text: She ran away from home at the age of 13.; At the age of fourteen, she ran away from home.

_source.base_text: run down sb/sth or run sb/sth down
_source.definition_text: to criticize someone or something, often unfairly
_source.searchterms_text: run;run down sb/sth or run sb/sth down
_source.learnerexamples_text: Whatever the government do, the press will always run them down.; But it's not fair to run down my country's past achievements.

_source.definition_text: to accidentally hit something while you are driving a vehicle
_source.learnerexamples_text: He lost control of the car and ran into a tree.; I had tried to stop my car next to the road but I ran into a signpost.

_source.definition_text: to meet someone that you know when you did not expect to meet them
_source.learnerexamples_text: I ran into Harry on the train.; We ran into an old friend of mine and we decided to have a coffee together.

_source.definition_text: to finish, use or sell all of something, so that there is none left
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've run out of money/ideas/patience.; "Have you got any milk?" - "Sorry, I've run out."; Well, I have run out of time, so I have to stop writing.

_source.definition_text: If a machine runs on a supply of power, it uses that power to work.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The scanner runs on mains electricity and batteries.; Public transport will be quick and free, and run on electric power, so there won't be car pollution.

_source.definition_text: If a supply of something runs out, all of it has been used or it is completely finished.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The milk has run out.; My patience is beginning to run out.; In addition, if you are at home and something you need has run out or broken, you can go to buy it at any time.

_source.definition_text: to repeat something in order to practise it or to make sure that it is correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: I just need to run through my talk.

_source.base_text: run over sb/sth or run sb/sth over
_source.definition_text: to hit someone or something with a vehicle and drive over them, injuring or killing them
_source.searchterms_text: run;run over sb/sth or run sb/sth over
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was run over by a bus.; After a while, his father vanished and a car ran over John and killed him.

_source.definition_text: when you move on your feet at a speed faster than walking, especially for exercise
_source.learnerexamples_text: We go for/do a three-mile run every evening after work.; If you set off at a run, you'll be exhausted later.; Walking is recognized [as] good exercise, or going for a run.

_source.definition_text: If you run up against problems or difficulties, you begin to experience them.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The community centre scheme has run up against strong local opposition.; After running up against a lot of difficulties we managed to reach our hotel.

_source.definition_text: in cricket or baseball, a single point
_source.learnerexamples_text: to score a run; I liked the competition because both the teams played well and they scored good runs

_source.definition_text: at a time that is far away in the future
_source.searchterms_text: in the long run;in the long run;run;runs
_source.learnerexamples_text: It seems a lot of effort but I'm sure it's the best solution in the long run.; It costs a lot of money, but in the long run, it [is] worth [it].

_source.definition_text: when something happens several times without something different happening during that period
_source.searchterms_text: a run of sth;run;run of sth;runs
_source.learnerexamples_text: a run of 10 games without a win; a run of good/bad luck ; Strange though it may seem, he achieved success in every possible field not owing to a run of good luck, but thanks to his outstanding qualities.

_source.definition_text: to suddenly run fast in order to escape from somewhere
_source.learnerexamples_text: When he saw the open door, he made a run for it.; Anna and Tom decided to make a run for it.

_source.definition_text: the sport of moving on your feet at a speed faster than walking

_source.definition_text: to stop someone or something from being killed, injured or destroyed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Wearing seat belts has saved many lives.; He fell in the river but his friend saved him from drowning.; He had to borrow money to save his business.; He was desperately trying to save their failing marriage.; We all need to do our bit to save the planet.

_source.definition_text: to prevent time, money or effort being wasted or spent
_source.learnerexamples_text: You'll save time if you take the car.; Thanks for your help - it saved me a lot of work.; More and more people choose to travel by car, because it saves a lot of time comp[ared] to travelling by public transport.

_source.definition_text: to prevent a player from scoring a goal
_source.learnerexamples_text: He saved two goals in the last minute of the game.

_source.definition_text: to help someone avoid having to do something
_source.searchterms_text: save;save sb (from) doing sth;save sb from doing sth;saved;saves;saving
_source.learnerexamples_text: We'll eat in a restaurant - it'll save you having to cook.; Building a new supermarket along with a multi-storey car park will save city dwellers from having to travel to the sub[u]rbs to buy what they need.

_source.definition_text: the money which you keep in an account in a bank or similar financial organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: He spent all his savings on an expensive car.; I also spent all my savings [o]n executive-looking clothes.

_source.definition_text: when you use or spend less money than you would usually have to
_source.learnerexamples_text: a saving of £20.; I know that it sounds as if the company had to spend a lot of money on retraining, but in the long term this will be a saving.

_source.definition_text: to speak words
_source.learnerexamples_text: "I'd like to go home," she said.; How do you say this word?; She said goodbye to all her friends and left.; "How do you say 'goodbye' in French?"; I couldn't hear what they were saying.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone about a fact, thought, or opinion
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did she say where she was going?; Officials refused to say what had happened.; What did they say about the house?; The doctors say (that) it will take him a few weeks to recover.; She didn't say whether she was coming or not.

_source.definition_text: to give information in writing, numbers or signs
_source.learnerexamples_text: My watch says 3 o'clock.; Can you read what that notice says?; It says in the paper (that) they've found the man who did it.; It says on the bottle to take three tablets a day.; Well yesterday I was reading a new fashion magazine. It says that this summer the best clothes to wear are skirts with different colours!

_source.definition_text: to think or believe
_source.learnerexamples_text: People/They say (that) he's over 100.; "It's going to be a very hot summer." "So they say."; She is a firm leader, too firm, some might say.; People say that it never rains here.

_source.definition_text: used to show that many people believe something about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Drinking plenty of water is said to be good for your skin.; On our way around the lake we would have [the] possibility of visiting a huge medieval castle which is said to be haunted.

_source.definition_text: If something goes without saying, it is obvious or generally accepted.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It goes without saying that smoking is harmful to your health.; It goes without saying that I will participate!

_source.definition_text: to think something but not speak
_source.learnerexamples_text: "I hope she likes me," he said to himself.; I remember saying to myself that "this little boy will survive" and after that I felt totally cool and calm and did what had to be done.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that you could have said something in a much stronger way
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were surprised, to say the least.; You get slightly bored, to say the least.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something seems like a good idea but it would be difficult to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: I want to ask her out, but it's easier said than done.; I know it's easier said than done but you have to try.

_source.definition_text: If it is safe to say something, you are sure it is correct.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think it's safe to say that he'll be the next president.; It is probably safe to say that there are no good books about engineering written in Portuguese so my teachers always use books written in English.

_source.definition_text: as you would expect
_source.learnerexamples_text: Needless to say, it rained the whole time we were there.; Needless to say, bribes are a frequent occur[r]ence.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize other problems you have not talked about
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most wild otters have disappeared from populated areas, to say nothing of wilderness areas.; Indeed would not it be an oversimplification to make one's judgement of the country's national character on the grounds of the amount and the quality of food people eat, to say nothing of the fact that this judgement is usually highly subjective?

_source.definition_text: used when you think that something is probably true or will probably happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: I dare say she'll change her mind.; Invent machines that are beneficial, not harmful, and I dare say life will only get better.

_source.definition_text: a famous phrase that people use to give advice about life
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you heard the saying "Don't count your chickens before they're hatched"? ; But as the saying goes "Time flies when you are having fun".

_source.definition_text: the size or level of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We don't yet know the scale of the problem.; Nuclear weapons cause destruction on a massive scale.; My parents used to entertain friends on a large/small scale.; He leads an evil trade: they [carry out] smuggling on a grand scale and use the inn as a store.

_source.definition_text: a set of numbers, amounts etc., used to measure or compare the level of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Centigrade/Fahrenheit scale; How would you rate his work on a scale of 1 to 5?; In brief, I think it would be a very good idea to create a new scale of [salaries] based on our needs, in which doctors would be [higher] than professional footballers.

_source.definition_text: a piece of equipment for measuring weight
_source.learnerexamples_text: kitchen/bathroom scales

_source.definition_text: how the size of things on a map, model, etc. relates to the same things in real life
_source.learnerexamples_text: a scale of 1:50 000; This map is large scale.; Is the bridge drawn to scale?; He was building a scale model of Concorde.; My f[ri]end gave me a 1/72 scale kit of "Supermarine Spitfire" for my birthday.

_source.definition_text: to quickly read a piece of writing to understand the main meaning or to find a particular piece of information
_source.learnerexamples_text: I scanned the travel brochures looking for a cheap holiday.; So, I suggest that you buy a newspaper called "The Loot", sit down with a strong cup of coffee and scan it.

_source.definition_text: to use a piece of equipment that copies words or pictures from paper into a computer
_source.learnerexamples_text: to scan photos into a computer; Instead of drawing some of our customers document[s] we will just scan them.

_source.definition_text: to look around an area quickly to try to find a person or thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: She scanned the crowd for a familiar face.; She looked at Lisa: her restless eyes were scanning the room while her thin fingers were tapping on the table.

_source.definition_text: a medical examination in which an image of the inside of the body is made using a special machine
_source.learnerexamples_text: a brain scan; John went with Sophie for a scan, John was hoping for a boy and Sophie for a girl.

_source.definition_text: something that shocks people because they think it is morally wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: a financial/political scandal; Their affair caused/created a scandal in the office.; If there is the slightest suggestion/hint of scandal, the public will no longer trust us.;  It's a scandal (that) children could be treated in this way.; Among them are the increasingly popular reality shows and all the daily news about gossip and scandal.

_source.definition_text: a permanent mark left on the body from a cut or other injury
_source.learnerexamples_text: an ugly scar; That burn will leave a nasty scar.; David is a tall man with black curly hair, black eyes, a big nose, [a] beard and a scar on his neck.

_source.definition_text: damage done to a person's mind by a very unpleasant event or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: a psychological scar; A person who [has been] affluent since childhood might be said to not have the emotional scars of experiencing poverty during childhood and might be able to look at the world, and to the life as an adult, in a positive and constructive way.

_source.definition_text: rare or not available in large amounts
_source.learnerexamples_text: scarce resources ; In the context of Singapore, where land is scarce and widening or building of more roads is just not feasible, we have no choice but to choose what is best for everyone.

_source.definition_text: to cause a scar
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was scarred for life by the accident.

_source.definition_text: only just
_source.learnerexamples_text: They had scarcely finished eating when the doorbell rang. ; Scarcely had the ferry reached the shore than the heavy storm abated.

_source.definition_text: when there is not enough of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a scarcity of food/affordable housing; With [a] scarcity of supplies and long training hours, wealthy children will then learn not to take things for granted.

_source.definition_text: to frighten a person or animal
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sudden, loud noises scare me.; You may think that Universal Video has gone mad: re-editing those old-fashioned horror movies that couldn't even scare your 6-year-old sister!

_source.base_text: scare the hell/life/living daylights, etc. out of sb
_source.definition_text: to make someone feel very frightened
_source.searchterms_text: scare;scare the hell/life/living daylights etc out of sb;scare the hell/life/living daylights, etc. out of sb;scared;scares;scaring
_source.learnerexamples_text: You scared the life out of me, creeping up on me like that!; Such gory details scared the living daylights out of each parent in town and, soon after the second dead girl was found, [one] Mary Joe Chavez, supposedly another high-school genius, a [state of] emergency was proclaimed and a thorough investigation followed, proving to be in vain, despite all the effort put into it.

_source.base_text: scare sb/sth away/off or scare away/off sb/sth
_source.definition_text: to make a person or an animal so frightened that they go away
_source.searchterms_text: scare;scare sb/sth away/off or scare away/off sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: She scared off her attacker by screaming.; For example, in the Ionian Islands, people break pots on Friday night in order to scare away evil spirits.

_source.base_text: scare sb away/off or scare away/off sb
_source.definition_text: to make someone worried about doing something or going somewhere so that they decide not to do it or go there
_source.searchterms_text: scare;scare sb away/off or scare away/off sb
_source.learnerexamples_text: The recent bomb attacks have scared away the tourists.; During the dance display and horse show we actually did experience some rainfall, however it was a small shower and it didn't manage to scare off the people and to prevent the organisers from reaching their main goal.

_source.definition_text: frightened or worried
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's scared of spiders.; He's scared to tell her what really happened.; I was scared (that) you might not be there.; I was scared stiff.; She had a scared look on her face.

_source.definition_text: a piece of cloth that you wear around your neck, head, or shoulders to keep warm or for decoration
_source.learnerexamples_text: a knitted/woollen/silk scarf; And my sister gave me a scarf too.

_source.definition_text: frightening
_source.learnerexamples_text: a scary movie/story; It was quite exciting but a little scary.

_source.definition_text: covering a wide area
_source.learnerexamples_text: His toys were scattered all over the floor. ;  There will be scattered showers today. ; Nowadays, families are scattered in all the parts of world, for example, my husband's family is in Australia; so our wedding provided me a chance to spend time with his family and learn about their family traditions,

_source.definition_text: a description of a situation, or of a situation that may develop in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are several possible scenarios.; a horrific/nightmare scenario such as a Third World War; This is a common scenario in developed countries, but third world countries have to deal with another type of homeless pe[rson].

_source.definition_text: a short part of a film, play, or book in which the events happen in one place
_source.learnerexamples_text: the funeral/wedding scene; Juliet dies in Act IV, Scene iii.; If you haven't seen any of th[ese] three "Star Wars" movies, I suggest you do see them tonight or tomorrow. They are great, with [a] lot of action scenes.

_source.definition_text: a view or picture of a place, event, or activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: Lowry painted street scenes.; scenes of everyday life; There were scenes of great joy as the hostages were re-united with their families.; I like especially the scene of the garden with snow in winter.

_source.definition_text: a place where an unpleasant event has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police arrived to find a scene of horrifying destruction.; Evidence was found at the scene of the crime.; She managed to recreate the scene of the crime, saying that she had swallowed a fish bone.

_source.definition_text: when people have a loud argument or show strong emotions in a public place
_source.learnerexamples_text: She made a scene when I told her she couldn't come with us.; She didn't cry, she didn't scream, she didn't make a scene.

_source.definition_text: all the things connected with a particular way of life or activity
_source.searchterms_text: club/gay/music, etc. scene;scene;scenes;the club/gay/music etc scene;the club/gay/music, etc. scene
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's well known on the jazz scene.; Both of them are about the gay and lesbian scene.

_source.definition_text: If something happens behind the scenes, it happens secretly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: A lot of hard work has been going on behind the scenes.; Ms. Bolam knew a lot of things going on behind the scenes, [which were] not [known to] the patients.

_source.definition_text: having views of the attractive, natural things in the countryside
_source.learnerexamples_text: a scenic route ; an area of great scenic beauty ; France is an area of great scenic beauty, famous for its excellent cooking and wine.

_source.definition_text: the attractive, natural things that you see in the countryside
_source.learnerexamples_text: beautiful/breathtaking/spectacular scenery; They stopped at the top of the hill to admire the scenery.; If I were you, I'[d] go [to] the countryside because it's peaceful, quiet, and the scenery is wonderful.

_source.definition_text: doubting that something is true or useful
_source.learnerexamples_text: Scientists remain sceptical about astrology. ;  She was sceptical of the new arrangement. ; Such cases make us rather sceptical about authors of various theories concerning nutrition.

_source.definition_text: a pleasant smell
_source.learnerexamples_text: the sweet scent of orange blossom; Flowers are in bloom and their scent triggers my romantic mood.

_source.definition_text: to arrange that an event or activity will happen at a particular time
_source.learnerexamples_text: The meeting has been scheduled for tomorrow afternoon.; The train is scheduled to arrive at 8.45, but it's running twenty minutes late.; My flight is scheduled to arrive at the airport at 10 o'clock in the morning.

_source.definition_text: a plan that gives events or activities and the times that they will happen or be done
_source.learnerexamples_text: I have a very busy schedule today.; Will the work be completed on schedule?; Everything went according to schedule.; Firstly, the programme beg[a]n exactly on schedule and the first group were KING CUP, not TORRENTS.

_source.definition_text: travelling at a regular time each day or week
_source.learnerexamples_text: a scheduled flight

_source.definition_text: planned to happen at a particular time or on a particular date
_source.learnerexamples_text: This programme will be broadcast half an hour later than the scheduled time.; The scheduled time for the arrival is 5.15 pm.

_source.definition_text: an official plan or system
_source.learnerexamples_text: a training/housing/play scheme; a pension/savings scheme; There's a new scheme in our town for recycling plastic bottles.; Class sizes will increase under the new scheme.; I reject any other possibilities like building a tunnel or a by-Pass, because compared to the Park and Ride scheme, they would be much too expensive.

_source.definition_text: an amount of money given to a person by an organization to pay for their education, usually at a college or university
_source.learnerexamples_text: She got a scholarship to the college.; In addition, is there any scholarship or financial support provided for students to apply [for]?

_source.definition_text: someone who has studied a subject and knows a lot about it
_source.learnerexamples_text: a classics/history scholar; Dr Miles was a distinguished scholar of Russian history.; In the old days a scholar could spend years of his life in search of specific information, which now can be easily and inexpensi[ve]ly found at the click of a button!

_source.definition_text: a place where children go to be educated
_source.learnerexamples_text: a primary/secondary school; Milton Road School; They're building a new school in the village.; She drives the kids to school every morning.; I was at school with Luke's brother.

_source.definition_text: the time that you spend at school
_source.learnerexamples_text: before/after school; School starts at 9 a.m. and finishes at 3.30 p.m.; The school start[s] every day at 9:00 and finish[es] at 14:00.

_source.definition_text: a place where you can study a particular subject
_source.searchterms_text: a dance/language/riding etc school;a dance/language/riding, etc. school;dance/language/riding, etc. school;school;schools
_source.learnerexamples_text: She goes to an acting school on Saturdays.; I went to the dance school in our town.

_source.definition_text: a child who goes to school
_source.learnerexamples_text: The morning bus is usually full of schoolchildren.; To schoolchildren: I want to sell my two-year-old red bike.

_source.definition_text: education at school
_source.learnerexamples_text: Jack didn't receive much formal schooling.; Throughout my schooling I felt that school was a chore, a necessary evil, if you will.

_source.definition_text: the study and knowledge of the structure and behaviour of natural things in an organized way
_source.learnerexamples_text: a science course/lesson; a science graduate/teacher; pure/applied science; recent developments in science and technology; Space travel is one of the wonders of modern science.

_source.definition_text: a particular type of science
_source.learnerexamples_text: computer science; Chemistry, physics, and biology are all sciences.; advances in medical science; In my class, there were 15 girls and 15 boys, who were studying computer science with me, so I knew everybody.

_source.definition_text: stories about life in the future or in other parts of the universe
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is a well-known science fiction writer.; Also, I like to watch fantasy and science fiction films.

_source.definition_text: relating to science, or using the organized methods of science
_source.learnerexamples_text: a scientific discovery/experiment/theory; scientific evidence/research; The project has attracted considerable criticism from the scientific community.; I like programmes about sport and scientific discover[ie]s.

_source.definition_text: using scientific methods
_source.learnerexamples_text: scientifically proven; It is scientifically pro[v]en and well-known that the gas [releas]ed by cars is toxic and quite dangerous to the environment - specially to the ozone layer.

_source.definition_text: someone who studies science or works in science
_source.learnerexamples_text: Scientists are working to create a vaccine for the disease.; NASA admitted yesterday they will send a group of highly trained scientists to Mars in the next two years.

_source.definition_text: a tool for cutting paper, hair, cloth, etc. that you hold in your hand and that has two blades that move against each other
_source.learnerexamples_text: a pair of scissors; Could you pass me the/those scissors, please?; We have to bring scissors, a pencil and a ruler.

_source.definition_text: a small motorcycle
_source.learnerexamples_text: I go to college on my scooter.; I want to sell my scooter.

_source.definition_text: the opportunity to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There is plenty of scope for improvement. ; Some people argue that living longer gives them plenty of scope to do things they have always wanted to do but could not find the time for.

_source.definition_text: how much a subject or situation relates to
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do we know the full scope of the problem yet? ; The scope of this article exceeds the problem of the abuse of females.

_source.definition_text: the number of points someone gets in a game or test
_source.learnerexamples_text: a high/low score; What's the score?; At half time, the score stood at two all.; The final score was 3-0.; We took 4 or 5 exams that day and my friend, Erick and I studied all night to get the best scores.

_source.definition_text: to get points in a game or test
_source.learnerexamples_text: He scored just before half-time to put Liverpool 2-1 ahead.; In American football, a touchdown scores six points.; She scored 18 out of 20 in the spelling test.; I almost scored an own goal.

_source.definition_text: to move or climb quickly but with difficulty, often using your hands
_source.learnerexamples_text: We scrambled up the hill. ; Piggy and [an]other few boys scramble up to the Castle Rock because Piggy wants to have his glasses back.

_source.definition_text: a small piece or amount of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He wrote his phone number on a scrap of paper.; I've read every scrap of information I can find on the subject.; They couldn't find a scrap of evidence against him so he was released without charge.; A group of well-educated boys becomes a savage tri[b]e, killing human beings without a scrap of remorse.

_source.definition_text: old cars and machines that are not now needed but have parts which can be used to make other things
_source.learnerexamples_text: scrap metal ; The car was so badly damaged we could only sell it as scrap.; The last place I would visit was an isolated [building], where some lean mongrel dogs were gnawing on rusty bones, while sniffing round the piles of scrap iron the left side of the building was thick with.

_source.definition_text: to not continue with a plan or idea
_source.learnerexamples_text: That project has now been scrapped.; We therefore propose you scrap your plans for Terminal 5 and instead try to reduce the number of incoming and outgoing flights, by diverting some planes to Luton or Stansted or Gatwick Airport.

_source.definition_text: to rub your skin with your nails, often to stop it itching
_source.learnerexamples_text: My skin was so itchy, I was scratching all night.; He was scratching (at) his mosquito bites.; Hannah scratched her head thoughtfully.

_source.definition_text: to make a slight cut or long, thin mark with a sharp object on a surface or on your skin
_source.learnerexamples_text: I scratched myself on the roses.; We scratched the paintwork trying to get the bed into Martha's room.; People have been scratching their names on this rock for years.; How can this ridiculous man accuse me of scratching his new car, thought Laura.

_source.definition_text: a slight cut or a long, thin mark made with a sharp object
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got all these scratches on my arm from the cat.; I should like to join one of those courses to become more 'professional' in how to repair a scratch on the side [of the boat] or a hole in the sail.

_source.definition_text: to rub a hard surface with a sharp object, often making a noise
_source.learnerexamples_text: The dog's scratching at the door - he wants to be let in.; Something scratched at the door.

_source.definition_text: If you do something from scratch, you do it from the beginning.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We didn't have any furniture of our own so we had to start from scratch.; That means you don't have to start from scratch with your teacher.

_source.definition_text: to not be good enough
_source.learnerexamples_text: She told me my work wasn't up to scratch.; The department has put a procedure in place for staff who don't come up to scratch.; The size of the rooms and their state as well were not really up to scratch.

_source.definition_text: to make a loud, high noise with your voice, or to shout something in a loud, high voice because you are afraid, hurt, or angry
_source.learnerexamples_text: A spider landed on her pillow and she screamed.; Through the smoke, the rescuers could hear people screaming for help.; He was screaming in/with pain and begging for anaesthetic.; They screamed with laughter at her jokes.; Ken screamed (out) a warning telling people to get out of the way.

_source.definition_text: when someone screams
_source.learnerexamples_text: We heard screams coming from their apartment.; Last night, I was cooking and dad was watching tv when, suddenly I heard a scream.

_source.definition_text: the words written for and spoken in a film, play, broadcast or speech
_source.learnerexamples_text: Bruce Robinson wrote the script for 'The Killing Fields'.; I didn't get involved that much in writing a script because it was very hard and the director wrote most of it but the main idea of the background of the stage was m[ine], and I am very proud of it.

_source.definition_text: a flat surface in a cinema or on a television, computer, mobile phone, etc., on which pictures or words are shown
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our television has a 19-inch screen.; Coming to your screens shortly, the amazing adventures of 'Robin Hood'.; Her ambition is to write for the screen.; Write the letter on the computer, then you can make changes easily on screen.; My favourite thing about it is that it has a huge screen and a lot of memory space.

_source.definition_text: a set of letters used for writing a particular language
_source.learnerexamples_text: Arabic/Roman script

_source.definition_text: to move text or an image on a computer screen so that you can look at the part that you want
_source.learnerexamples_text: Scroll down to the bottom of the document.

_source.definition_text: dirty and untidy
_source.learnerexamples_text: scruffy jeans; I don't like to look scruffy.; For example, if it is particularly trendy for kids to wear scruffy bomber jackets and faded jeans there is no point in compelling them to dress our conventional way.

_source.definition_text: when you examine something carefully
_source.learnerexamples_text: Every aspect of her life came under public scrutiny.; Everything is placed under careful scrutiny.

_source.definition_text: a piece of art that is made from stone, wood, clay, etc., or the process of making objects like this
_source.learnerexamples_text: a wooden sculpture; modern sculpture; Tom teaches sculpture at the local art school.; The museum has several life-sized sculptures of people and animals.; But if you have time, you must visit some cities, like Rome or Florence, because there are many historical buildings and museums, with the most important sculptures and pictures [by] famous artist[s] like Michelangelo or Raffaello.

_source.definition_text: a large area of salt water
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Mediterranean Sea; We went swimming in the sea.; The sea was calm/smooth/choppy/rough when we crossed the Channel.; The refugees were at sea for forty days before reaching land.; When we moved to the US, we sent our things by sea.

_source.definition_text: an animal with smooth fur that eats fish and lives near the sea
_source.learnerexamples_text: We could see seals swimming near the coast.; After leaving the Orkney Islands, we went by boat to [the] Shetland Islands, because we wanted to observe the grey seals with their pups that were [o]n the northwest coast.

_source.definition_text: to close an entrance or container so that air or liquid cannot enter or leave it
_source.learnerexamples_text: She quickly sealed up the bottle.; In Egypt, [the] Pyramids are being sealed, because the perspiration of the tourists was ruining the paintings on the walls.

_source.definition_text: to close a letter or parcel by sticking the edges together
_source.learnerexamples_text: to seal an envelope; Jenny, my girlfriend, told me that she sealed the envelope with trembling fingers and then posted it.

_source.definition_text: to try to find someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've searched my bedroom but I can't find my watch.; He searched in his pockets for some change.; Police are still searching the woods for the missing girl.; He searched (in/through) his pockets for some change.; I've searched high and low , but I can't find my birth certificate.

_source.base_text: seal off sth or seal sth off
_source.definition_text: to prevent people from entering an area or building, often because it is dangerous
_source.searchterms_text: seal;seal off sth or seal sth off
_source.learnerexamples_text: Police immediately sealed off the streets.; The police sealed off the main street a few weeks ago because they have been building a new restaurant.

_source.definition_text: to use a computer to find information, especially on the Internet
_source.learnerexamples_text: I searched the Internet to find the best prices for flights to Barcelona.; Before you had to go to a lib[r]ary to finish [your] homework. Now, we just search on the internet.

_source.definition_text: If the police search a place or a person, they look to see if they are hiding anything illegal, such as drugs.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were searched at the airport.; The men were searched for drugs and then released.; The undercover [patrol] searched our car rather roughly, looking for drugs.

_source.definition_text: when you try to find someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: After a long search, they eventually found the missing papers.; The police carried out/conducted/made a thorough search of the house, but they failed to find any drugs.; Joshua instantly thought it could be a bomb, so he organized a search all over the airport.

_source.definition_text: to try to find an answer to a problem

_source.definition_text: to be available for sale at a particular price
