_source.definition_text: to persuade someone that an idea or plan is good
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm currently trying to sell the idea to my boss.

_source.definition_text: to be bought quickly and in large numbers
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their new game is selling like hot cakes.; Books about how to remain young are selling like hot cakes.

_source.definition_text: someone who sells something
_source.learnerexamples_text: flower/newspaper/souvenir sellers; Do you think the seller will accept £96 000 for the house?; It was then my mother remembered a toy seller had been selling toys in the place where we had been waiting in the station and that our suitcase[s] must have got mixed up.

_source.definition_text: If a supply of something sells out, or if it is sold out, there is no more of that thing to buy.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The first issue of the magazine sold out within two days.; All the tickets were sold out and the stadium was nearly full.

_source.definition_text: a mark (;) used to separate parts of a sentence, or items in a list which already has commas
_source.learnerexamples_text: Use a semicolon to separate the groups of items in your list.

_source.definition_text: A semi-detached house has one wall that is joined to another house.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We live in a semi-detached house.; When I was in London I lived in a semi-detached house as well.

_source.definition_text: one of the two games in a sports competition that are played to decide who will play in the final game
_source.learnerexamples_text: Who's in the semi-finals?; She's the youngest player ever to get through to a semi-final.; One Sunday morning we had to play the cup semi-final against [our] great rival.

_source.definition_text: a meeting of a group of people with a teacher or expert for training, discussion, or study of a subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: I attended practically every lecture and seminar when I was a student.; I'm giving a seminar on the latest developments in genetic engineering next week.; a seminar room ; I also need this job because I need money to attend some seminars.

_source.definition_text: to make someone go somewhere
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're sending the children to stay with my parents for a couple of weeks.; The commander has asked us to send reinforcements.; They've sent their son (away) to school in Scotland.; He was trying to explain but she became impatient and sent him away.; We should buil[d] more schools because we only have one, so we have to send our children away and none of us like that.

_source.definition_text: to arrange for something to go or be taken somewhere, especially by post
_source.learnerexamples_text: Juan has just sent me a text message.; Send me an email with your dates.; I'll send her a letter/fax/parcel/postcard next week.; We'll send it by post/airmail.; They sent her flowers for her birthday.

_source.base_text: send shivers/a shiver down your spine
_source.definition_text: to make you feel afraid or excited
_source.searchterms_text: send;send shivers/a shiver down your spine;sending;sends;sent
_source.learnerexamples_text: The sound of his voice sent shivers down my spine.; Simply looking at her sent shivers down his spine - there was the love of his life, the dearest woman on good old Earth, that he's never met before.

_source.definition_text: to cause someone or something to do a particular thing, or to cause something to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: The explosion sent the crowd into a panic.; Watching the television always sends me to sleep.; His untidiness sends her crazy/mad/wild.; The draught from the fan sent papers flying all over the room.; While we were singing a duet by Mendelssohn with my sister, a sweeping movement of my hand sent two pages of music flying towards the first row of seats.

_source.base_text: send sth back or send back sth
_source.definition_text: to return something to the person who sent it to you, especially because it is damaged or not suitable
_source.searchterms_text: send;send sth back or send back sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had to send the shirt back because it didn't fit me.; I usual[l]y order my clothes [on the] Internet. It's fast, easy and you don't have any problems send[ing] them back if they don't fit.

_source.definition_text: to send someone a message asking them to come to see you
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were forced to send for a doctor.; Immediately after his arrival he sent for Beadle.

_source.base_text: send off sth or send sth off
_source.definition_text: to send a letter, document or parcel by post
_source.searchterms_text: send;send off sth or send sth off
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you sent off your application form yet?

_source.base_text: send sth out or send out sth
_source.definition_text: to produce something in a way that causes it to spread out from a central point
_source.searchterms_text: send;send sth out or send out sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: The equipment sent out a regular high-pitched signal.; The torch sends out a powerful beam of light.;  The bushes were sending out new shoots.; On the other side of the lake the placid grazing cows would munch their breakfast as the sun rose on the horizon, sending out a flood of colours across the sky.

_source.definition_text: having a more important job or position than someone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: a senior executive; We work in the same team but she's senior to me.; a senior government minister; She is also extrao[r]dinary in that she graduated from Harvard University and Tokyo University and used to work for the Ministry of the Foreign Affairs as a senior civil servant.

_source.definition_text: relating to people who are older
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can't use a senior ticket during the rush hour - you have to pay full fare.; When I got to the tickets desk before the show to buy my ticket I asked for a senior discount, and the woman told me there were no discounts available as I read on the advertising.

_source.definition_text: a physical feeling, or the ability to physically feel things
_source.learnerexamples_text: a burning sensation; I had no sensation of pain whatsoever.; The disease causes a loss of sensation in the fingers.; When I fel[l] into the water, I was shocked. I couldn't move my right leg, the sensation was horrible.

_source.definition_text: a strange feeling or idea that you cannot explain
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had the odd sensation (that) someone was following me.; Suddenly I had the sensation that something was wrong.

_source.definition_text: done in a way that is intended to shock people
_source.learnerexamples_text: sensational journalism; I think that the journalists desired sensational news far too much and they exaggerated.

_source.definition_text: very exciting or extremely good
_source.learnerexamples_text: a sensational performance; If you are up for some sensational fun, "New York-New York" is your place, with a crazy roller coaster soaring through the lobby and out into open air.

_source.definition_text: a lot of excitement, surprise or interest
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their marriage caused a sensation.; In the poetry, she expressed her sad feeling, thinking of her brother who was in China as a soldier. It caused a sensation.

_source.definition_text: a feeling or understanding about yourself or about a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did you get any sense of what they might do?; Living out in the country gave us a great sense of freedom.; I like to see how people fight for the pri[z]e. I like this sense of compet[it]ion that only sport give[s]!

_source.definition_text: the ability to understand funny things and to be funny yourself
_source.searchterms_text: a sense of humour;sense;sense of humour;senses
_source.learnerexamples_text: Carol has a wicked sense of humour.; Most of them have an incredible sense of humour so we laugh a lot when we go there.

_source.definition_text: good judgment, especially about practical things
_source.learnerexamples_text: I hope they'll have the (good) sense/have enough sense to shut the windows before they leave.;  There's no sense in waiting - the next train isn't for two hours.; People should have the sense to dispose [of] all the waste properly.

_source.definition_text: the ability to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's got a good sense of direction and hardly ever uses a map.; good business sense; Animals are part of nature so they must be free [to] go where their sense of direction [leads them].

_source.definition_text: to have a meaning or reason that you can understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's written me this note but it doesn't make any sense.; Eighty kilometres in the mountains just to [look at] views doesn't make any sense to me.

_source.definition_text: one of the five natural abilities of sight, hearing, touch, smell, and taste
_source.learnerexamples_text: With her keen sense of smell, she could tell if you were a smoker from the other side of the room.; My cold is so bad I've lost my sense of smell/taste.; You can enjoy a flight with all your five senses.

_source.definition_text: one of the possible meanings of a word or phrase
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are not immigrants, at least not in any sense that I understand.; The packaging is green - in both senses of the word.; Security defined in the broad/broadest sense of the term means getting at the root causes of trouble and helping to reduce regional conflicts.; The Empress was an ideal lady in every sense of the word.

_source.definition_text: to be a good thing to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: It makes sense to buy now while prices are low.; Therefore it make[s] sense to use the innovation[s].

_source.definition_text: thinking about something in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: In a sense, he's right.; In a sense this is correct, since you have to leave your natural environment to visit a place where no human being is meant to survive.

_source.definition_text: to understand something that is difficult to understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm trying to make sense of this document.; In fact, it's during his journey that Stevens begins to make sense of his life, of all the years he spent as a butler, as the 'perfect butler' who had to be loyal, silent and discreet.

_source.definition_text: to realize you are wrong or have been behaving stupidly
_source.learnerexamples_text: We talked to her for an hour, but we couldn't make her see sense.; Ralph tries to make Jack see sense by showing him the conch which had been the symbol of leadership and also, friendship.

_source.definition_text: happening or done without a good reason
_source.learnerexamples_text: senseless violence ; Maybe after a thousand years of wars between Poland and Germany both sides have finally decided that fighting and killing is senseless.

_source.definition_text: to feel or experience something without being able to explain exactly how
_source.learnerexamples_text: Although she said nothing, I could sense her anger; He sensed something was about to happen.; He sensed (that) his guests were bored, although they were listening politely.; Could you sense what was likely to happen?; So Monica's aunt somehow subconsciously sensed that something was going to happen.

_source.definition_text: someone's feelings, or the ability to understand what other people feel
_source.learnerexamples_text: his aesthetic sensibility; All the features mentioned above are extremely important but they mean nothing if your offspring lacks kindness, sensibility and ignores his family traditions.

_source.definition_text: in a sensible way
_source.learnerexamples_text: She behaved very sensibly about it.; They very sensibly decided to stay at home.; As time goes [by], these kids quite don't understand the importance of using money sensibly and saving money.

_source.definition_text: showing good judgment
_source.learnerexamples_text: a sensible answer/approach/choice/option; a sensible person; I think the sensible thing to do is phone before you go and ask for directions.;  It would be sensible to take an umbrella.; I know it sounds strange but there's a sensible reason: money talks.

_source.definition_text: able to react very quickly and easily
_source.learnerexamples_text: These scales are very sensitive.; He has a very sensitive nose.; I am very sensitive to noise, especially at night, and tend to catch a cold even in summer.

_source.definition_text: easily upset by the things people say or do
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her reply showed that she was very sensitive to criticism.; He was very sensitive about his scar and thought everyone was staring at him.; Nowadays we are not so sensitive.

_source.definition_text: easy to damage and needing to be protected
_source.learnerexamples_text: I have very sensitive skin.

_source.definition_text: A sensitive subject or situation needs to be dealt with carefully in order to avoid upsetting people.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sex education and birth control are sensitive issues.; The stolen car contained military documents described as very sensitive.; I knew that I could not cry and shout because it was too important and sensitive [a] problem for us.

_source.definition_text: the ability to understand how other people are feeling and to be helpful and kind to them
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police showed great sensitivity in their handling of the case.; It is written with sensitivity, honest[y], sincerity and objectiveness.

_source.definition_text: able to understand what people are feeling and deal with them in a way that does not upset them
_source.learnerexamples_text: I want a man who's kind and sensitive.; Representatives of the company claim their plan will be sensitive to local needs.; In the movie, he plays a concerned and sensitive father trying to bring up two teenage children on his own.; One thing Bobby is good at is that he is bright and sensitive enough to protect you.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being easily upset by things that people say or do
_source.learnerexamples_text: I should have warned you about her sensitivity to criticism.; One of her weaknesses would be her great sensitivity.

_source.definition_text: a group of words, usually containing a verb, that expresses a complete idea
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's very impatient and always interrupts me mid-sentence.; Your conclusion is good, but the final sentence is too long and complicated.; Ev[e]ry lesson, I read and write loads o[f] sentences.

_source.definition_text: a punishment that a judge gives to someone who has committed a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: He got a heavy/light sentence.; The offence carries a jail/prison/life/5-year sentence.; This is even worse th[a]n a real life sentence.

_source.definition_text: to give a punishment to someone who has committed a crime
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was sentenced to life imprisonment.; Soon afterwards he gets imprisoned again and is sentenced to death. Sydney takes his place and is executed instead of him.

_source.definition_text: an opinion that you have because of the way you feel about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: nationalist/religious sentiments ; We would discuss for hours on end, arguing most of the times, and never express our true inner sentiments.

_source.definition_text: related to feelings and memories and not related to how much money something costs
_source.learnerexamples_text: It wasn't an expensive ring but it had great sentimental  value.; It can be the value in money that make[s] people be attached to [a] possession or, rather, a sentimental or symbolic link.

_source.definition_text: showing kind feelings such as sympathy, love, etc., especially in a silly way
_source.learnerexamples_text: a sentimental song; The British are very sentimental about animals.; I do love Lighthouse Family's music - the sentimental lyrics and catchy tune[s] all flow with the black singer's magic voice.

_source.definition_text: not joined or touching anything else
_source.learnerexamples_text: a separate compartment; I try to keep meat separate from other food in the fridge.; But there was no choice, as all my friends that did go were already in separate rooms.

_source.definition_text: not affecting or related to each other
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've asked him to turn his music down on three separate occasions.; I have my professional life and my private life and I try to keep them separate.; Three youths have been shot and killed in separate incidents this month.; She went to Lisbon, and we [ended up] living separate li[v]es.

_source.definition_text: different or new
_source.learnerexamples_text: Use a separate sheet of paper.; The art department and the main college are in two separate buildings.; Yesterday I bought a lot [of] presents, so I needed a separate suitcase.

_source.definition_text: to divide into parts, or to make something divide into parts
_source.learnerexamples_text: I separated the class into three groups.; The north and south of the country are separated by a mountain range.; You can get a special device for separating egg whites from yolks.; The top and bottom sections are quite difficult to separate.; On the other hand, more bins ought to be put in the centre [to] encour[a]ge people to separate their rubbish more carefully.

_source.definition_text: to start to live in a different place from your husband or wife because the relationship has ended
_source.learnerexamples_text: My parents separated when I was four.; But his parents separated and John didn't see h[is] mother again, as well as his sister, after that day.

_source.definition_text: to move apart, or to make people move apart
_source.learnerexamples_text: I shall separate you two if you don't stop talking.; Somehow, in the rush to get out of the building, I got separated from my mother.; Perhaps we should separate now and meet up later.; I noticed that there w[ere] some [people] fighting, and we tried to separate them.

_source.definition_text: when two or more people or things are separated
_source.learnerexamples_text: During the war, many couples had to face long periods of separation.; After many years, the government finally abandoned its apartheid system of racial separation.; One of the most important project[s] is the separation of the rubbish and I think that it has worked, but it could work better.

_source.definition_text: not together
_source.learnerexamples_text: Detectives interviewed the men separately.; I tend to wear the jacket and skirt separately rather than as a suit.; I think we'd better deal with these two points separately.; They were living separately and missing each other.

_source.definition_text: the ninth month of the year, after August and before October
_source.learnerexamples_text: 23(rd) September/September 23(rd); We're leaving for France on September the ninth/the ninth of September.; Claudia started school last September/is starting school next September.; My mother's birthday is in September.; My course started [i]n September.

_source.definition_text: the decision of two people who were married or living together to stop living together
_source.learnerexamples_text: They decided on a trial separation.; We lived for a time in peace but our happiness ceased because of his jealousy and fear [of losing] me, which was the cause of our daylong quarrels. There was no solution apart from separation.

_source.definition_text: a series of related events or things that have a particular order
_source.learnerexamples_text: the sequence of events that led to his death ; They don't emerge from nowhere, as there was a certain sequence of events that has led to them, so having the full picture with past events influencing our present can help us to find efficient solutions.

_source.definition_text: a part of a film or video game that shows one thing that happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: I particularly enjoyed the dream sequence.; However, the rest of the game is not as [polished] as the opening sequence: indeed, it seems that the developers simply re-used the graphical engine of the prequel, without even revamping it: the result is truly disappointing.

_source.definition_text: the order that events or things should happen or be arranged in
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got my slides mixed up and they appeared out of sequence.; It was the fourth summer in sequence that he had chosen this hotel to spend his holiday but this he had never experienced before.

_source.definition_text: calm and quiet
_source.learnerexamples_text: a serene face/smile; I enjoy looking at this image, which bears [the] skill of a 16th century artist: the mother's expression is solemn and tender as she looks at the boy, while Christ's face is completely serene and is lit with a faint smile.

_source.definition_text: a feeling of being calm and happy
_source.learnerexamples_text: She sat there with an air of serenity about her.; She strongly believes that art bring[s] peace, harmony, serenity and tranquillity in their life, which could balance their emotions and help [them] to overcome difficulties.

_source.definition_text: describes a person who repeatedly commits the same serious crime, often using the same method, or a serious crime that is committed repeatedly by one person
_source.learnerexamples_text: She wrote a thriller about a brutal serial killer.; a serial rapist; serial murders/killings; These pictures have never been broadcast because too many important people are involved in these serial killings.

_source.definition_text: a story in a magazine or on television or radio that is told in separate parts over a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm watching a serial set in Yorkshire.; As I have already mentioned the quality of the English language used is exceptional and I would like to congratulate all the pe[ople] that take part in the serial.

_source.definition_text: a group of television or radio programmes that have the same main characters or deal with the same subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: The footballer Paul Gascoigne is to host a Channel 4 television series on soccer skills.; a comedy series; I missed the second episode of the series so I don't know what's going on now.; I like television series like Smallville.

_source.definition_text: several things or events of the same type that come one after the other
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's had a series of tests at the hospital but they can't find anything wrong.; She gave a series of lectures at Warwick University last year on contemporary British writers.; The aim of this report is [to] make a series of suggestions on which lessons and other activities should be filmed.

_source.definition_text: a set of books published by the same company which deal with the same subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: They do a series on architecture throughout the ages.; We read all of Poirot and [the] [Miss] Marple series.

_source.definition_text: A serious problem or situation is bad and makes people worry.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a serious illness; There were no reports of serious injuries.; The new tax regulations have landed some of the smaller companies in serious trouble.; A shortage of space has become a serious problem in a lot of schools.; He's been taken to hospital where his condition is described as serious but stable.

_source.definition_text: A serious person does not laugh often.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I remember her as a very serious child.; Well, the new teacher is very serious, but this is ok.

_source.definition_text: not joking or intended to be funny
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please don't laugh - I'm being serious.; He was wearing a very serious expression and I knew something was wrong.; On the surface it's a very funny novel but it does have a more serious underlying theme.; Is she serious about going to live abroad?; We are taught how to act in both comic and serious parts.

_source.definition_text: needing or deserving your complete attention
_source.learnerexamples_text: That's an interesting job offer - I'd give it some serious consideration if I were you.; We've got some serious talking to do, you and me.; I think it would be worthwhile to give serious thought to these animals.

_source.definition_text: badly or severely
_source.learnerexamples_text: seriously ill/worried; He wasn't seriously injured - he just got a few cuts and bruises.; She is seriously ill with cancer.

_source.definition_text: in a way that shows that you are not joking
_source.learnerexamples_text: Seriously now, did he really say that or are you just being silly?; You're not seriously thinking of leaving, are you?; Seriously, Tom, I have noticed that you get angry very easily since your examinations started.

_source.definition_text: to consider a person, subject or situation to be important or dangerous and worth your attention or respect
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police have to take any terrorist threat seriously.; You don't take anything seriously, do you? It's all one big joke to you.; She wants to be taken seriously as an actress.; These young actors take themselves so seriously!; I hope you take my suggestions seriously.

_source.definition_text: someone who works and lives in someone else's house doing their cooking and cleaning, especially in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: They employed more than 50 servants.; In this book, the author [includ]es a detailed description of [the] two main characters: the rich English master PHILEAS FOGG and his French servant PASSEPARTOUT.

_source.definition_text: to help customers and sell things to them in a shop
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you being served?; I also learnt a lot about how to serve c[u]st[o]mers and how to use a till.

_source.definition_text: to give someone food or drink, especially guests or customers in a restaurant or bar
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do they serve meals in the bar?; Breakfast is served in the restaurant between 7 and 9.; We arrived at the hotel and were served with champagne and strawberries.; All recipes in this book will serve 4 to 5 people.; Serve the tarts hot with custard or whipped cream.

_source.definition_text: to be useful as something
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a very entertaining film but it also serves an educational purpose.; The spare bedroom also serves as a study.; He hopes his son's death will serve to warn others about the dangers of owning a gun.; Nothing serves to explain the violent fighting we have seen recently.; As for replanting, it will serve to rejuvenate our forests around Agrinio.

_source.definition_text: to do work that helps society, for example in an organization such as the army or the government
_source.learnerexamples_text: to serve in the army; to serve on a committee/jury; He served as mayor for 5 years.; He always wanted to serve his country.; Women in the former GDR [ha]d the same rights and had to fulfill nearly the same duties (except the duty to serve in the army) as men.

_source.definition_text: to be in prison for a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Williams, 42, is serving a four-year jail sentence.; It all came to me in prison where I was serving [a] two-year sentence.

_source.definition_text: to have a use
_source.learnerexamples_text: These small village shops serve a very useful purpose.; They introduced meetings at Miss Kenton's parlour which were held every evening and served [the] purpose of discussing house running.

_source.definition_text: a central computer from which other computers get information
_source.learnerexamples_text: a network/file server; It was my boss, [who] said "I'm in Australia, and I can't read my e-mail, the server at work crashed.

_source.definition_text: a system or organization that provides something that people need
_source.learnerexamples_text: the ambulance/health/postal/prison service; They provide a free bus service from the station.; We hope to be operating a normal service as soon as possible.; I told him to phone the after-sales service.

_source.definition_text: when people help you and bring you things in a place such as a shop, restaurant, or hotel
_source.learnerexamples_text: The only trouble with this café is that the service is so slow.; I think the Cinemark is the best cinema because it has good service and it is cheap.

_source.definition_text: an amount of money charged for serving a customer in a restaurant, which is often paid directly to the waiter
_source.learnerexamples_text: There is a 10% service charge included in the bill.; Does the bill include service?; The thing which annoyed me the most was [that] they have a 20% service charge, but I refused to pay it because there w[as] no service.

_source.definition_text: the armed forces, or work done in the armed forces
_source.learnerexamples_text: He joined the air force in 1964 and spent ten years in the service.; Most of my family were in the services.; All men under thirty-five were told to report for military service within three days.; Service personnel are subject to the Official Secrets Act.; He finished his military service, and now he was on his way to his family, who had been waiting for him for a long time.

_source.definition_text: a government department that is responsible for a particular area of activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: the diplomatic service; the security services; I was employed in the security service.

_source.definition_text: a period of time or a meeting arranged for a particular activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: The 21-year-old runner twisted his ankle in a training session last Friday.; As the heads of state gathered, the press were allowed in for a photo session.; Last week we had the normal two training sessions and a game against another club.

_source.definition_text: the time you spend working for an organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: He retired last week after 25 years' service.; In my mind he is the perfect candidate, because due to his long service in the U.S. Army, where superiors are obliged to take care of their subordinates, he was in contact with young people from all kinds of ethnic [backgrounds] and social classes.

_source.definition_text: If a story, film, etc. is set in a particular time or place, the action in it happens in that time or place.
_source.learnerexamples_text: 'West Side Story' is set in New York in the late 1950s.; It was an adventure story and I liked it a lot because it was set in Australia.

_source.definition_text: to fix a date or time for something
_source.searchterms_text: set;set a date/time (for sth);set a date/time for sth;sets;setting
_source.learnerexamples_text: Juan and Maria have set a date for their wedding - it's going to be on August 31.; Has a time been set for the meeting yet?; I'm going to miss your class tomor[r]ow, but we can set a date to cover the work on.

_source.definition_text: When the sun sets, it moves down in the sky until it cannot be seen.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.; I loved the thin fog before the sun set.

_source.definition_text: to cause something or someone to be in the stated condition or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: It is believed that the building was set on fire deliberately.; She set fire to her neighbour's house.; After years in prison, the men who had wrongfully been found guilty of the bombing were finally set free.; A modern zoo must be [like] a forest, without cages, and the animals must be set free.

_source.definition_text: to make a piece of equipment ready to be used
_source.learnerexamples_text: The heating is set to come on at 5.00 p.m.; Have you set the video recorder?; I usually set my watch by the time signal on the radio.; He set the alarm for 7.00 a.m.; I had forgotten to set the alarm clock the previous night and by the time I got up it was already 9 o'clock.

_source.definition_text: if something is set somewhere, it is in that place or position
_source.learnerexamples_text: The campsite is set in the middle of a pine forest.; Our house is set back from the road.; The camp is set in a beautiful place in the heart of nature, with lots of opportunities to get out of the camp if you want to.

_source.definition_text: to give someone something to do or achieve
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our teacher has set us a lot of homework.; He's set himself the goal/target of making his first million by the time he's 30.; I suggest it [would] be a good idea to set more projections next year.

_source.definition_text: to do something in a good way so that other people might try to copy you
_source.learnerexamples_text: Try to set a good example to the children.; It sets a good example for other museums.

_source.definition_text: to establish the best achievement so far in a sport or competition
_source.learnerexamples_text: Bolt has set a new world record.

_source.definition_text: to decide the level of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The interest rate has been set at 5%.; In addition to all this, I must point out that our agreement regarding the student discount on all tickets was set at 10%, not 5%, as you mentioned on your handout.

_source.definition_text: to establish guidelines, standards, etc. that must be followed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our school sets very high standards and most students achieve them.; But I do know that even though my parents were indulgent, affectionate and warm, they still quite clearly set standards on how I was supposed to behave.

_source.definition_text: to go into a place or onto a piece of land
_source.learnerexamples_text: He told me never to set foot in his house again.; I dream of being the first one to set foot on a white sandy beach, to admire a new kind of vegetation: cranberry bushes, sweet potatoes, wild turkeys, a different climate; how scary and exciting at the same time!

_source.definition_text: to put something somewhere
_source.searchterms_text: set;set sth down/on etc;set sth down/on, etc.;sets;setting
_source.learnerexamples_text: She set the vase down on the table.

_source.base_text: set fire to sth; set sth on fire
_source.definition_text: to make something start burning, usually to cause damage
_source.searchterms_text: set;set fire to sth set sth on fire;set fire to sth; set sth on fire;sets;setting
_source.learnerexamples_text: Enemy troops set fire to the village.; At this point nothing made sense anymore, so I just watched while Jake set the car on fire.

_source.definition_text: to start a journey by boat or ship
_source.learnerexamples_text: We set sail for home the next day.; What made things turn from grey to black was that soon after my return I was invited to set sail to the Spanish islands.

_source.definition_text: to decide to achieve something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's set her sights on becoming a doctor.; This resemblance was the final silent argument that convinced Wormold to promise Milly the expensive and beautiful horse she had set her sights on.

_source.base_text: set back sb/sth or set sb/sth back
_source.definition_text: to make something happen more slowly or later than it should
_source.searchterms_text: set;set back sb/sth or set sb/sth back
_source.learnerexamples_text: These delays have set back the publication date by a month.; Another failed harvest would really set these farmers back.; She would put off school which set her back a couple of years but she was free to choose and do what she really enjoyed do[ing].

_source.base_text: set off sth or set sth off
_source.definition_text: to cause something to begin or happen, especially a loud noise or a lot of activity
_source.searchterms_text: set;set off sth or set sth off
_source.learnerexamples_text: The spark set off a massive explosion.; The announcement set off a wave of riots.; He would set off the smoke alarm by lighting some of his matches.

_source.definition_text: to start a journey
_source.learnerexamples_text: What time will we have to set off for the station tomorrow?; They've just set off on a round-the-world cruise.; We set off [for] home at 5 o'clock.

_source.definition_text: to start an activity with a particular aim
_source.learnerexamples_text: She set out with the aim of becoming the youngest ever winner of the championship.; They set out to discover a cure for cancer.; That is why the day her son was named emperor a smile of satisfaction played round her lips, because at least she had achieved what she had set out to do, which was make her son ascend the throne.

_source.definition_text: to start a journey
_source.learnerexamples_text: Martin set out on his cycle ride before dawn.; When do you want to set out?; Next morning I packed my luggage and set out on our trip to France.

_source.base_text: set out sth or set sth out
_source.definition_text: to give all the details of something, or to explain something clearly, especially in writing
_source.searchterms_text: set;set out sth or set sth out
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the project costs are set out in this document.; She gave a presentation setting out the company's future plans.; But first of all I will set out briefly the reasons that made me take the final decision.

_source.base_text: set up sth or set sth up
_source.definition_text: to formally establish a new company, organization, system, way of working, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: set;set up sth or set sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: A committee has been set up to organize social events in the college.; She plans to set up her own business.; They've set up a fund for victims of the earthquake.; It is such a beautiful country that I wanted to stay there and set up a business.

_source.base_text: set up sth or set sth up
_source.definition_text: to arrange for an event or activity to happen
_source.searchterms_text: set;set up sth or set sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to set up a meeting to discuss the proposals.; The government has agreed to set up a public enquiry.; I suggest we try to set up a meeting with people from city hall, and give them all the right arguments.

_source.definition_text: a group of things which belong together
_source.learnerexamples_text: a boxed set of DVDs; a chess/train/chemistry set; a set of instructions/rules; a set of keys; We bought Charles and Mandy a set of salad bowls as a wedding present.

_source.definition_text: to be ready
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were all set to go when the phone rang.; So, there you go. I'm all set!

_source.definition_text: a part of a game of tennis
_source.learnerexamples_text: They won in straight sets.; Finally we managed to win the [second] set so we were equal.

_source.definition_text: the place where a film or play is performed or recorded, and the pictures, furniture, etc. that are used
_source.learnerexamples_text: a film set; a stage set; a set designer; They first met on the set of 'Star Wars'.; Her father, John, was a stuntperson and he died in an unfortunate accident while he was perform[ing] [o]n a film set.

_source.definition_text: fixed and never changing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most people work for a set number of hours each week.; I have no set routine.; Even if there is a set number of standard models, there is always ample room for personal choice according to your taste.

_source.definition_text: a problem that makes something happen later or more slowly than it should
_source.learnerexamples_text: The project has suffered a series of setbacks this year.; A strong bond between you and your friends, with whom you can have discussions about personal setbacks, is another very vital point.

_source.definition_text: the position of a house or other building
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their cottage is in a beautiful rural setting.; [It is] a beautiful setting with old architecture, trees and glittering water.

_source.definition_text: the time and the place in which the action of a book, movie, play, etc. happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: The play has its setting in a wartime prison camp.; The setting of "The Third Man" is Vienna after the Second World War.

_source.definition_text: to start living somewhere that you are going to live for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: After they got married, they settled in Brighton.; He travelled around Europe before finally settling in Rome.; I can understand why you have decided to settle near the Loire Valley, which is one of the greatest part[s] of France.

_source.definition_text: to decide or arrange something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Right, that's settled. We're going to Spain.; They haven't yet settled when the wedding is going to be.; "The tickets are £40 each." "Well, that settles that then - I can't afford that much."; I'd like to get this matter settled once and for all.; The details of the contract have not yet been settled.

_source.definition_text: to move to a lower level and stay there
_source.learnerexamples_text: The house had been empty for years, and dust had settled on all the surfaces.; Do you think the snow will settle?; The contents of this packet may settle.; Whenever I have cleaned my shel[ve]s you can just watch the dust settle on [them].

_source.definition_text: If you settle an argument, you solve the problem and stop arguing.
_source.learnerexamples_text: My father and I have agreed finally to settle our differences.; It took months to settle the dispute/strike.; Caroline and her husband had had an argument last week, but as he was going to be away for a few days, they had finally settled their differences.

_source.definition_text: If you settle a bill or a debt, you pay the money that you owe.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got some bills to settle.; Many individuals are caught overspending when they check their credit card statements, later having to borrow from money lenders to settle their bills.

_source.definition_text: to become familiar with a place and to feel happy and confident in it
_source.learnerexamples_text: She quickly settled down in her new house/job/school.; He seemed to be such a nice guy and I was very happy to find you [have] settled down so well in your new life.

_source.definition_text: to begin to feel relaxed and happy in a new home or job
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you settling in OK?; After you settle in, you'll find there's a lot of way[s] to save money on food.

_source.definition_text: to start living in a place where you intend to stay for a long time, usually with your partner
_source.learnerexamples_text: Eventually I'd like to settle down and have a family, but not yet.; I guess the changes occur once the young couple decides to marry and settle down.

_source.definition_text: to become quiet and calm, or to make someone quiet and calm
_source.learnerexamples_text: They settled down on the sofa to watch the film.; Come on class, stop chatting and settle down, please!; You should welcome your relatives, make them settle down and ask them to wait a moment.

_source.definition_text: an official agreement that finishes an argument
_source.learnerexamples_text: a peace settlement; All employees working for the public transport went on strike a week ago, and there is no settlement in sight.

_source.definition_text: an arrangement to end a disagreement without taking it to a court of law
_source.learnerexamples_text: They reached an out-of-court settlement.; Hoping for a settlement without having to involve the courts, I remain.

_source.definition_text: a town or village which people built to live in after arriving from somewhere else
_source.learnerexamples_text: a Jewish settlement; The traditional style of small living communities in tribes cannot be sustained, since the farmlands around a settlement cannot provide the people with sufficient food and work.

_source.definition_text: the number 7
_source.learnerexamples_text: The restaurant opens for dinner at seven o'clock.; We're open seven days a week.; Tomorrow I'll finish my work at six o'clock, so I think that I'll can arrive your home at seven o'clock.

_source.definition_text: 7th written as a word
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's the seventh (of May) today.; Our team came in seventh.; The day of [the] art class is [the] seventh of May.

_source.definition_text: the number 17
_source.learnerexamples_text: sixteen, seventeen, eighteen; Is that a seventeen on the front of that bus?; He is seventeen years old.

_source.definition_text: the number 70
_source.learnerexamples_text: sixty, seventy, eighty; This house was built seventy years ago.; It cost seventy pounds.

_source.definition_text: the years from 1970-1979
_source.learnerexamples_text: I grew up in the seventies.; The nineties is, indeed, a reverse of the seventies.

_source.definition_text: to be aged between 70 and 79
_source.searchterms_text: (be) in your seventies;be in your seventies;seventy
_source.learnerexamples_text: Both my parents are in their seventies.; After some minutes, an old man in his late seventies opened the door and told us in his trembling voice that Daisy wasn't at home.

_source.definition_text: some, but not a lot
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've seen 'Gone with the Wind' several times.; Several people have complained about the scheme.; Several of my friends are learning English at language schools in Cambridge.; I also got several books, a beautiful bag, a T-shirt, etc.

_source.definition_text: extremely bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: a severe chest infection/leg injury/toothache; This is a school for children with severe learning difficulties.; In parts of Africa there is a severe food/water shortage.; There is expected to be a severe frost tonight.; Their life was a severe financial struggle, and Tom's dream was to run somewhere far away.

_source.definition_text: a severe person is unfriendly or very strict
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had her hair tied back in a severe style.; The teacher was a small, severe man.; Jane Eyre is sen[t] away to [a] school for orphans. [...] The atmosphere in school is no better, with little food and severe teachers.

_source.definition_text: very seriously
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their daughter was severely injured in a car accident.; severely disabled; Job opportunities are severely limited/restricted at the moment.; In spite of trying to repair it, it is still severely damaged.

_source.definition_text: how severe something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: Flights were cancelled owing to the severity of the weather.; In conclusion, we have to accept the severity of the environmental damage, but we should not give up our hopes for a better future.

_source.definition_text: to make or repair clothes by joining pieces of cloth using a needle and thread
_source.learnerexamples_text: My grandmother taught me to sew.; I made this skirt just by sewing two pieces of material together.; She sews all her children's clothes.; He sewed the badge neatly onto his uniform.; Well, I used to sew my clothes on my own.

_source.definition_text: the activity of joining pieces of cloth together or repairing them with a needle and thread
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm not very good at sewing.;  I especially cherish the idea of finding myself in Camelot being a lady in waiting [to] Queen Guinevere - to spend my days reading, sewing, embroidering, learning about far off places and discoveries, adventures and the latest gossip from the court.

_source.definition_text: sexual activity between people
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sex before/outside marriage is strongly disapproved of in some cultures.; She was complaining about all the sex and violence on television.; She'd been having sex with a colleague at work for years.; Most young people now receive sex education at school.;  unprotected sex

_source.definition_text: the state of being either male or female
_source.learnerexamples_text: What sex is your cat?; Some tests enable you to find out the sex of your baby before it's born.; The teacher gave me the application form about my name, age, sex, nationality and address.

_source.definition_text: people who are the other sex from you
_source.learnerexamples_text: He would never dare to speak to a member of the opposite sex.; This is not only about trying to impress (preferably) a person of the opposite sex, but fashion also gives you a great chance to express yourself.

_source.definition_text: relating to the activity of sex
_source.learnerexamples_text: a sexual relationship; Most people remember their first sexual experience.; Before continuing with the story I would like to remind [you] that having sexual relationships was common to everybody in Brave New World.

_source.definition_text: relating to being male or female
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sexual equality will not be achieved until there is more provision for childcare.; Some steps have been taken towards ending sexual discrimination.; But we must not forget that there is still sexual discrimination when women apply for jobs higher up in [a] hierarchy.

_source.definition_text: looking untidy and in bad condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: shabby clothes/furniture; With neither lift nor room service provided our guests had to stay in dirty and shabby rooms on the 4th floor.

_source.definition_text: attractive or exciting in a sexual way
_source.learnerexamples_text: sexy underwear; He's very sexy.; Richard was only wearing Levis Jean[s] and a white T shirt but looked so sexy and handsome.

_source.definition_text: not fair or not honest
_source.learnerexamples_text: She received very shabby treatment from her employers.; Due to such shabby arguments, my adversaries lost the favour of the population.

_source.definition_text: an area where there is no light from the sun and so it is darker and not as hot
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd prefer to sit in the shade.; The sun was hot, and there were no trees to offer us shade.; The children played in/under the shade of a large beach umbrella.; The shade from huge trees kept me cool and fresh.

_source.definition_text: a small amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's perhaps a shade taller.; Their salaries are, even when the same job is done, mostly a shade under a man's salary.

_source.definition_text: a colour, especially when referring to how dark or light it is
_source.learnerexamples_text: a pale/dark shade of grey; Not only was it a beautiful day but the sky was a magnificent shade of blue as well.

_source.definition_text: a cover that stops too much light coming from the sun or from an electric light
_source.learnerexamples_text: a lamp shade; You will like sitting there at dark wooden tables, under the light coming from red and white checked lamp shades hanging from the ceiling.

_source.base_text: beyond/without a/the shadow of a doubt
_source.definition_text: If something is true beyond a shadow of a doubt, it is certainly true.
_source.searchterms_text: beyond/without a/the shadow of a doubt;shadow;shadows
_source.learnerexamples_text: He stole the money, without a shadow of a doubt.; It is beyond the shadow of a doubt that Douglas does not offer her this kind of life.

_source.definition_text: a dark area made by something that is stopping the light
_source.learnerexamples_text: The tree had cast a long shadow.; The children were playing, jumping on each other's shadows.; Jamie followed his mother around all day like a shadow.; This corner of the room is always in shadow.; Suddenly I saw a shadow and as I turned over I noticed that something was moving in the trees.

_source.definition_text: to move backwards and forwards or up and down in quick, short movements, or to make something or someone do this
_source.learnerexamples_text: A young boy climbed into the apple tree and shook the branches so that the fruit fell down.; Babies like toys that make a noise when they're shaken.; The explosion shook buildings for miles around.; She shook her hair loose from its ribbon.; Every time one of these big trucks goes through the village, all the houses shake.

_source.definition_text: to hold someone's hand and move it up and down when you meet them for the first time, or when you make an agreement with them
_source.learnerexamples_text: The two leaders smiled and shook hands for the photographers.; I shook hands with him.; I felt embarras[s]ed when all my friends thought they were my friends, so [they] all sh[ook] hands with them ex[c]ept me.

_source.definition_text: If you are shaking, your body makes quick short movements, or you feel as if it is doing so, because you are frightened or nervous.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was shaking as she opened the letter.; Her voice shook as she spoke about the person who attacked her.; I was shaking in my shoes/boots about having to tell Dad what I'd done.; I was shaking like a leaf before my exam.; She understood that it was absolutely foolish of her to stand [t]here shaking with fear.

_source.definition_text: to move your head from side to side to mean 'no'
_source.learnerexamples_text: I asked him if he wanted to come and he just shook his head.; He just looked at me shaking his head and got into his car and drove off.

_source.definition_text: If your voice shakes, you sound very nervous or frightened.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He looked pale, and his voice shook as he spoke.;  "Excuse me, my name is Heathcliff Moore, I'm a musician", he approached the owner with shaking voice.

_source.base_text: shake off sth or shake sth off
_source.definition_text: to get rid of an illness, something unpleasant, or something that is causing you problems
_source.searchterms_text: shake;shake off sth or shake sth off
_source.learnerexamples_text: I hope I can shake off this cold before the weekend.; He was capable of shaking off the criticism due to the fact that he believed strongly enough in himself, which I find quite remarkable.

_source.base_text: shake up sth or shake sth up
_source.definition_text: to cause large changes in something
_source.searchterms_text: shake;shake up sth or shake sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: Technological changes have shaken up many industries.; I believe that their aim is to shake up public opinion in the most impressive way they can.

_source.base_text: shake up sb or shake sb up
_source.definition_text: If an unpleasant experience shakes someone up, it makes them feel shocked and upset.
_source.searchterms_text: shake;shake up sb or shake sb up
_source.learnerexamples_text: The accident really shook him up.

_source.definition_text: used to make an offer or suggestion
_source.learnerexamples_text: Shall I cook dinner tonight?; We'll ask him later, shall we?; After the film, shall we go to eat pizza next to the cinema?

_source.definition_text: shocked and upset
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were not injured in the accident, but they were badly shaken.; After that encounter with her old classmate she felt shaken and upset.

_source.definition_text: used to ask someone what to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: What restaurant shall we go to?; Who shall I ask?; What time will you be free? When shall we meet?

_source.definition_text: not deep
_source.learnerexamples_text: The stream was quite shallow so we were able to walk across it.; She told her children to stay in the shallow end (of the swimming pool).; Fry the onions in a shallow pan.; These beech trees have shallow roots.; A heavy body plunged into the shallow water of harbo[r] No 14.

_source.definition_text: used to say what you are going to do in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: I shall be talking to her tomorrow.; I shan't forget to tell them.; I shall look forward to meeting you next week.; So we'll see you at the weekend, shall we?; I shall make sure that the work I miss is completed by borrowing my friend's notes.

_source.definition_text: not showing any interest in serious ideas
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is a very shallow person.; She is shallow and superficial, and she finds it hard to relate to her husband.

_source.definition_text: If you describe something as a shame, you are disappointed that it has happened.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a real shame to waste all this food.; What a shame that they had to destroy such a beautiful building.; Dear Ally, It's a shame you couldn't come to my party.

_source.definition_text: Something shameful is bad and should make you feel embarrassed and guilty.
_source.learnerexamples_text: shameful scenes;  What a shameful way of wasting natural resources!

_source.definition_text: when you feel embarrassed and guilty about something bad that you have done
_source.learnerexamples_text: He said he felt no shame for what he had done.; The children hung their  heads in shame.; You can't go dressed like that - have you no shame ?; In some societies, if a woman leaves her husband, it brings shame on her and her family.; It destroys the individual, brings shame to his family, and [is] a liability instead of an asset to his society.

_source.definition_text: the physical form of something made by the line around its outer edge
_source.learnerexamples_text: a circular/rectangular shape; You can recognize trees by the shape of their leaves.; Very few people are really happy with their body shape.; These bricks are all different shapes.; Kim's birthday cake was in the shape of a train.

_source.definition_text: a liquid substance that you use to wash your hair
_source.learnerexamples_text: an anti-dandruff shampoo; Directions: wet hair, apply shampoo and massage into a rich lather.; I think the soap and the shampoo are in the bathroom.

_source.definition_text: in good/bad, etc. health or condition
_source.searchterms_text: in good/bad etc shape;in good/bad, etc. shape;shape;shapes
_source.learnerexamples_text: She runs every day so she's in great shape.; I am of the opinion that if you are in good shape and the distance is not too much, you should leave the car at home and use the bike.

_source.definition_text: many different types of people or things
_source.learnerexamples_text: We saw people there of all shapes and sizes.; Personal Challenges come in all shapes and sizes.

_source.definition_text: to stay healthy and physically strong
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's important to keep in shape.; We want to keep in shape, and we are interested in a gym - do you have one or is there one close to there?

_source.definition_text: to start to develop and become more clear or certain
_source.learnerexamples_text: The project is slowly beginning to take shape.; It is high time that their dreams took shape!

_source.definition_text: not healthy or physically strong
_source.learnerexamples_text: Since I stopped cycling, I'm very out of shape.; I no longer run and it has been more than a year since the last time I raced, [so] I am out of shape.

_source.definition_text: to influence the way that something develops
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many people are not able to shape their own destinies.; My relationship with my father played a major part in shaping my attitude towards men.; He was very influential in shaping the government's economic policy/strategy.; Therefore, in my opinion, we are shaped greatly by the people in our surroundings.

_source.definition_text: to have or use something at the same time as someone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: Bill and I shared an office for years.; I share a house with four other people.; She's very possessive about her toys and finds it hard to share.; There are two beds because I share my room with a friend.

_source.definition_text: If two or more people or things share a feeling, quality or experience, they both or all have the same feeling, quality or experience.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We share an interest in sailing.; All hospitals share some common characteristics.; I don't share your views/beliefs.; Management and the union both share in the responsibility for the crisis.; She knew that he was the person she wanted to share her life with.

_source.definition_text: to divide something between two or more people
_source.learnerexamples_text: Will you share your sandwich with me?; Let's share the sweets (out) among/between everyone.; We should share (in) the reward.; We shared one big cake.

_source.definition_text: If two or more people share an activity, they each do some of it
_source.learnerexamples_text: Shall we share the driving?; We shared the preparation for the party between us, so it wasn't too much work.; Ask your employer and other colle[a]gues to share the work.

_source.definition_text: to tell someone your problems/thoughts, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: share;share your problems/thoughts/ideas etc;share your problems/thoughts/ideas, etc.;shared;shares;sharing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Would you like to share your thoughts with the group, Donald?; I have received your letter asking for my opinion about the Conference and have decided to write and share some of my thoughts.

_source.definition_text: a part of something that has been divided
_source.learnerexamples_text: The total bill comes to £80, so our share is £20.; We must make sure that everyone gets equal shares of the food.; The party's share of the vote fell from 39% to 24%.; She's not doing her share of the work.; We must all accept some share of the responsibility.

_source.definition_text: a lot of something and enough of it, usually something bad
_source.searchterms_text: share;shares;your (fair) share of sth;your fair share of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: We've had our fair share of rain already this summer.; It wasn't as if Jean hadn't seen his fair share of dead bodies, but these ones were far more, well, disgusting, than anything before.

_source.definition_text: a large fish with very sharp teeth
_source.learnerexamples_text: a great white shark; The movie 'Jaws' is about a man-eating shark.; By the way, this ocean was full of sharks, our guide said.

_source.definition_text: one of the equal parts that the value of a company is divided into when it is owned by a group of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: to buy/sell shares; We own shares in a number of companies. ;  Share prices have fallen for the third day running.; It is no longer the consumer but the shareholder who must be kept happy, in order to keep the share price high, and the simple worker pays the price.

_source.definition_text: a sudden and very large increase or reduction in something
_source.searchterms_text: a sharp rise/increase/drop etc;a sharp rise/increase/drop, etc.;sharp;sharp rise/increase/drop, etc.;sharper;sharpest
_source.learnerexamples_text: a sharp drop in temperature; a sharp decline in the standard of living; There was a sharp rise/increase in the number of flu cases.; If you have in mind my recommendations you will see a sharp increase in the number of students.

_source.definition_text: a very big and noticeable difference between two things
_source.searchterms_text: a sharp contrast/difference etc;a sharp contrast/difference, etc.;sharp;sharp contrast/difference, etc.;sharper;sharpest
