_source.definition_text: a television or radio programme or a theatre performance
_source.learnerexamples_text: a radio/television/stage show; a quiz/game show; Why don't we go to London on Saturday and see a show?; We had a puppet show for Jamie's birthday party.; You can see lots of traditional shows there, it will be very interesting for you.

_source.definition_text: an event at which a group of similar things are brought together for the public to see
_source.learnerexamples_text: a fashion/flower show; There were some amazing new cars at the motor show.; They put on a show of his work at the National Museum of American Art.; I do not know if it is possible to make any change[s], but we saw an ad in "Time Out" magazine last week about a fashion show which we would like to see.

_source.definition_text: being shown to the public
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her designs are currently on show at the Museum of Modern Art.; One of the facilit[ies] that really make[s] a difference is the Art Gallery, with its great exhibition on show, as well as the Art Library.

_source.definition_text: If you have or take a shower, you wash your whole body while standing under a flow of water.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got up, had a shower and got dressed.; I have to wake up [at] 7.30 AM. I run to the bathroom [to] take a shower.

_source.definition_text: a piece of bathroom equipment that you stand under to wash your whole body
_source.learnerexamples_text: He likes to sing in the shower.; And there are showers and [a] sauna you [will] be able to use any time after the gym.

_source.definition_text: a short period of rain
_source.learnerexamples_text: You're soaked! Did you get caught in the shower?; There will be thundery/wintry showers over many parts of the country.; Well the weather was really good during the morning [but] [there were] some showers during the afternoon.

_source.definition_text: to wash standing under a shower
_source.learnerexamples_text: We all showered before breakfast.; Singing is a hobby of mine but unfortunately I can only do it when I'm showering or cleaning up my flat.

_source.definition_text: to give someone a lot of presents, praise, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He showered her with expensive gifts.; She was showered with compliments after her performance.; As time passes the children start to see a pattern developing, every time that they request time or attention they are showered with expensive clothes or toys to compensate [for] the lack of it.

_source.definition_text: good at judging situations and making decisions which give you an advantage
_source.learnerexamples_text: a shrewd politician; a shrewd business plan; It was only much later that I realised what a shrewd investment on my parent's part this had been.

_source.definition_text: to become smaller, or to make something smaller
_source.learnerexamples_text: Your sweater will shrink if you wash it at too high a temperature.; The company's profits have shrunk from £5.5 million to £1.25 million.; After 5 seconds I started shrinking until I was as small as the smallest toe on my foot.

_source.definition_text: to move your shoulders up and down to show that you do not care about something or that you do not know something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I told him we weren't happy with it but he just shrugged his shoulders. ; Martina flushed to the root[s] of her hair and shrugged her shoulders.

_source.definition_text: to shake, usually because you are thinking of something unpleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: The sight of so much blood made him shudder.; She shuddered at the thought of kissing him.; She shuddered at the memory.

_source.definition_text: to close something, or to become closed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please shut the gate.; I've got a surprise for you! Shut your eyes tightly and hold out your hand.; Mary shut her book and put it down on the table.; This window won't shut properly.; The doors shut by [them]selves.

_source.definition_text: When a shop, restaurant, etc. shuts, it stops serving customers and does not allow people to enter.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The shops shut at eight o'clock on Wednesday evenings.

_source.definition_text: If a computer or machine shuts down or someone shuts it down, it stops operating.
_source.searchterms_text: shut;shut (sth) down or shut down (sth);shut sth down or shut down sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Make sure you shut down your computer before you leave.; The crew shut down the right-hand engine of the aircraft.; I was as happy as a lark. I shut down the computer and I called my m[u]m to tell her about the good news.

_source.definition_text: closed
_source.learnerexamples_text: I suspected something was wrong when I noticed her curtains were still shut at lunchtime.

_source.definition_text: to stop talking or making a noise, or to make someone do this
_source.learnerexamples_text: I wish you'd shut up for a moment and listen to what the rest of us have to say.; Just shut up and get on with your work!; My dad never stops talking. It's impossible to shut him up!; You must still remember that time we walked along the street, singing blues and rock, it's incredible the way that people shouted at us to shut up.

_source.definition_text: If a business or organization shuts down or someone shuts it down, it closes.
_source.searchterms_text: shut;shut (sth) down or shut down (sth);shut sth down or shut down sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company plans to shut down four factories and cut 10 000 jobs.; A great [number] of zoos ought to be shut down.

_source.definition_text: When a shop, restaurant, etc. is shut, it has stopped serving customers and does not allow people to enter it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The post office will be shut now.; On the advertis[e]ment it also said you could visit [the] restaurant after the show, and that is what I did, but when I got there it was shut for no reason.

_source.definition_text: to not talk about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you don't keep your mouth shut, there'll be trouble.; She made every effort to keep her mouth shut but it disturbed her to be the only one to know the truth, apart from her brother.

_source.definition_text: a bus, train, plane, etc. which travels regularly between two places, usually a short distance
_source.learnerexamples_text: the London-Glasgow shuttle; There's a shuttle service between the airport and the city centre.; I am convinced that a centre with less traffic and more pedestrianised areas will attract more other people. Especially if there is a parking opportunity outside of the centre with well-o[r]ganised shuttle buses to the centre.

_source.definition_text: not confident, especially about meeting or talking to new people
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was too shy to ask her to dance with him.; She gave a shy smile.; Children are often shy of/with people they don't know.; The deer were shy and hid behind some trees.; I was a little shy at first, but I ended up talking too much!

_source.definition_text: the state of being shy
_source.learnerexamples_text: When I met the Queen, I was overcome with shyness. ; Some of them were encouraged by their work-fellows to overcome their initial shyness.

_source.definition_text: ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: a sick child; My father has been off sick for a long time.; The old woman fell/took/was taken sick while she was away and had to come home.; Sarah called in/reported sick.; Everybody went except Natalie because she was sick.

_source.definition_text: a sister or brother
_source.learnerexamples_text: I have three siblings.; I am also lucky to have a sibling, an older sister, who took great care of me when we were children.

_source.definition_text: to vomit
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was sick after she ate too much chocolate.; I feel a little sick and I don't want to be sick in your lesson.

_source.definition_text: feeling ill as if you are going to vomit
_source.learnerexamples_text: Lucy felt sick the morning after the party.; If you eat any more of that cake, you'll make yourself sick.; He said he fe[lt] sick and had [a] headache.

_source.definition_text: to be bored with or annoyed about something that has been happening for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm sick of people telling me how to run my life.; Michael was sick of seeing the same story happen all over again.

_source.definition_text: cruel and unpleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's got a sick mind.; a sick joke ; It seems to us as if God had got a sick sense of humour.

_source.definition_text: when you are ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's a lot of sickness around this winter.; She's had three weeks off for sickness this year.; The simpl[e] joy and happiness will help you to feel in good shape and keep away any sickness.

_source.definition_text: one of the two parts that something would divide into if you drew a line down the middle
_source.learnerexamples_text: He likes to sleep on the right side of the bed.; In Britain, cars drive on the left side of the road.; There is no money on my mother's side (of the family).; I could just see Joan on the far/other side of the room.; Children came running from all sides.

_source.definition_text: a flat outer surface of an object, especially one that is not the top or the bottom
_source.learnerexamples_text: The names of ships are usually painted on their sides.; My room is at the side of the house.; Please write on one side of the paper only.; Canadian coins have a picture of the Queen's head on one side.; Please use the side entrance.

_source.definition_text: an edge or border of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: A square has four sides.; There are trees on both sides of the road.; They were surrounded on every side by curious children.; We are going to paint one side of the room orange and the others w[h]ite.

_source.definition_text: the area next to something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I have a small table at/by the side of my bed.; He stood at/by her side as she welcomed the guests one by one.; Linda is by my side right now and she asks [me to] send you a warm hug.

_source.definition_text: part of a situation that can be considered or dealt with separately
_source.learnerexamples_text: She looks after the financial side of things.; Finally, I think for me the most important [thing] is to enjoy life - don't be worried [about] little things and always find the funny side of each situation.

_source.definition_text: If two things or people are side by side, they are next to each other.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We sat side by side on the sofa.; It is not rare to see two people walking side by side, both talking on the phone.

_source.definition_text: a part of someone's character
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has a very practical side.; In fact the film describes the actions of this politi[c]ian, also saying something not very "Politically Correct", but true: he reveals that no one is always good, everyone has a dark hidden side.

_source.definition_text: If something moves from side to side, it moves from left to right and back again repeatedly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: swinging from side to side; I began to understand it when I went [to] Kenya in 1986, because I had the wonderful chance to look at the animals in their natural [surroundings], without being in a cage, walking nervously from side to side.

_source.definition_text: one of the people or groups who are arguing, fighting, or competing
_source.learnerexamples_text: Whose side is he on?; Whenever we argue he always takes Alice's side .; This is a war which neither side can win.; Don't be angry with me - I'm on your side.; I hope you'll be on my side.

_source.definition_text: a way of considering something, especially when there is disagreement about it
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are at least two sides to every question.; I've listened to your side of the story, but I still think you were wrong to do what you did.; This shows the other side of technology.

_source.definition_text: the players in a sports team
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's been selected for the national side.; Our side lost again on Saturday.; He also plays football for a local side regularly.

_source.definition_text: to not use or deal with something now, but keep it for a later time
_source.learnerexamples_text: She put the papers to one side, intending to read them later.

_source.definition_text: to find good things in a bad situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Look on the bright side - no one was badly hurt.; I am quite self-confident and I usually look on the bright side, as I am not keen on pessimistic thoughts.

_source.definition_text: in addition to your main job
_source.learnerexamples_text: She does a bit of bar work on the side.; At work, they gave her the worst jobs to do. She knew she didn't have much choice but she still tried to find something else on the side.

_source.definition_text: the part of your family who are either your mother's relatives or your father's relatives
_source.learnerexamples_text: They tend to be tall on my mother's side of the family.; Both on my father's side as well as on my mother's side of the family we formed a close knit group.

_source.definition_text: If you have someone at/by your side, they support you and help you.
_source.learnerexamples_text: With Dan at my side, I felt I could do anything.; She really needed someone by her side, someone to lean on and share her worries.

_source.definition_text: the two areas of your body from under your arms to the tops of your legs
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stand with your arms by your sides.; She lay on her side.

_source.definition_text: another effect that a drug has on your body in addition to the main effect for which the doctor has given you the drug
_source.learnerexamples_text: Headaches are one side effect of this drug.; Now, we have come up with something called Phyto essence that is designed to overcome skin problems effectively without causing any harmful side effects.

_source.definition_text: an extra result of a situation, especially one that you did not plan or expect
_source.learnerexamples_text: One side effect of getting a new job is that I can cycle to work and I've lost a lot of weight.; They seem to neglect the growing rate of unemployment and its possible side effects.

_source.definition_text: in a direction to the left or right, not forwards or backwards
_source.learnerexamples_text: The fence is leaning sideways.; If you would move sideways to the left, I can get everyone in the picture.; Take two sideways steps.; Unaware of all the sideways glances and chatter that paused as she passed, she headed back towards the river.

_source.definition_text: to breathe out slowly and noisily, often because you are annoyed or unhappy
_source.learnerexamples_text: She sighed deeply and sat down.; "I wish he was here," she sighed.; Having solid ground beneath her feet again she sighed with relief for having survived this adventure.

_source.definition_text: the sound that is made when someone sighs
_source.learnerexamples_text: He read the letter and gave a deep sigh.; I entered the house with a deep sigh!

_source.definition_text: the ability to see
_source.learnerexamples_text: If your sight is poor, you should not drive a car.; The old woman has lost her sight.; She had lost her sight although doctors didn't know if it was forever.

_source.definition_text: places of interest, especially to visitors
_source.learnerexamples_text: We spent a fortnight in Rome looking at all the sights.; I have many plans, I want to show you all [the] remarkable sights in Georgia.

_source.definition_text: when you see someone or something
_source.searchterms_text: sight;sight of sb/sth;sights;the sight of sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: The sight of so much blood had shocked him.; The child laughed at the sight of the clockwork toy.; She hated/loathed the sight of her former husband.; Just think; drinking our cold beers against the sight of the pounding waves and feeling the wind on our faces.

_source.definition_text: to forget about an important idea or fact because you are thinking too much about other, less important things
_source.learnerexamples_text: We mustn't lose sight of the original aims of this project.; Little do we realize that in the process we lose sight of the fundamentals, which in this case is the protection of our environment.

_source.definition_text: the area that it is possible for you to see
_source.learnerexamples_text: You should always keep sight of your bags while you're at the airport.; I dare not let the children out of my sight in this park.; The police officer was hidden out of sight behind a tree.; The castle came into sight as we went round a bend in the road.; We're looking for a house which is within sight of the mountains.

_source.definition_text: when you first see or hear about something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: It may, at first sight, seem a surprising choice.; It was love at first sight!; Nowadays shopping is considered one of the most enjoyable activities, especially if you are a woman and you are out to buy clothes. At first sight it is, but shopping is not always enjoyable.

_source.definition_text: to see something suddenly, often only for a short time
_source.learnerexamples_text: He caught sight of himself in the mirror.; All we could see were people bursting into tears when they caught sight of his coffin.

_source.definition_text: to decide to achieve something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's set her sights on becoming a doctor.; This resemblance was the final silent argument that convinced Wormold to promise Milly the expensive and beautiful horse she had set her sights on.

_source.definition_text: the activity of visiting places which are interesting because they are historical, famous, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did you do much sightseeing while you were in Paris? ; I'd like to go sightseeing and eat Italian food.

_source.definition_text: a symbol or message in a public place which gives information or instructions
_source.learnerexamples_text: a road sign; a shop sign; And it [is] easy to get there, just follow the sign.

_source.definition_text: something which shows that something is happening or that it exists or is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Flowers are the first sign of Spring.; His inability to handle the situation is a sure sign of weakness.; The fact that he's eating more is a sign that he's feeling better.; There's no sign of progress with the building work.; Billy's work at school has shown signs of improvement this year.

_source.definition_text: a movement you make to give someone information or tell them what to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: She pointed to her watch as a sign that it was getting late and she wanted to leave.; She made/gave a sign to her husband to stop talking.; The priest made the sign of the cross when he entered the church.; She looked at Paul and made a strange sign with her fingers.

_source.definition_text: a written or printed mark which has a standard meaning
_source.learnerexamples_text: + and - are mathematical signs.; £ is the sign for the British pound.

_source.definition_text: to write your name on something to show that you wrote/painted, etc. it or to show that you agree to it
_source.learnerexamples_text: to sign a letter/form/cheque/contract/agreement; Sign here, please.; He signed his name at the end of the letter.; He signed himself 'Mark Taylor'.; She said the painting was by Picasso, but it wasn't signed.

_source.definition_text: If there is no sign of someone or something, you cannot see them.
_source.learnerexamples_text: By eight o'clock, there was still no sign of Janne.; She said she'd left the book on the table, but there's no sign of it.; He was supposed to come on Wednesday just like you told me but there was no sign of him.

_source.definition_text: to arrange to do an organized activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've signed up for evening classes at the local college.; If you are interested in other activities, just sign up for them [on] the notice board.

_source.definition_text: a movement, light, or sound which gives information, or tells people what to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: At a signal from their teacher, the children all held up their flags.; Don't move until I give the signal.; The firework was a signal that the festival had started.; The police officer gave us a signal to stop.; The signal for a race to start is often the firing of a gun.

_source.definition_text: a series of light waves or sound waves which are sent to a radio, television, mobile phone, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't get a phone signal here.; On the other hand you can face problems with signal transmission.

_source.definition_text: to make a movement which gives information or tells people what to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: He signalled left, and turned the lorry slowly.; He was signalling with a red flag.; She signalled for help.; She signalled to the cars behind that they were going the wrong way.; The children's mother signalled them to be quiet.

_source.definition_text: your name written by yourself, always in the same way, usually to show that something has been written or agreed by you
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please put your signature in this box.; I thought it was a joke but when I saw the signature I knew it was for real.

_source.definition_text: the importance or meaning of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I still don't understand the significance of his remark.; This is a development which has great economic significance for the region.; In spite of the progress achieved in promoting the social status of women, one should not overestimate the significance of these achievements to ordinary women's careers.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is easy to see or by a large amount
_source.learnerexamples_text: My piano playing has improved significantly since I've had a new teacher.; Also, with today's machines, factories have significantly increased their production.

_source.definition_text: important or noticeable
_source.learnerexamples_text: There has been a significant increase in the number of women students in recent years.; These measures will save a significant amount of money.; The talks between the USA and Russia were very significant for the relationship between the two countries.; One of the most significant invention[s] is [the] computer.

_source.definition_text: a sign by the side of the road that gives information about routes and distances
_source.learnerexamples_text: Look out for the signpost to the airport.; There were no signposts and there was no one to ask where he could find a place to stay.

_source.definition_text: when there is no sound
_source.learnerexamples_text: The three men ate in silence.; A loud crash of thunder broke the silence of the night.; I suppose that you want to relax [o]n your holiday and so I suggest you visit the Alps - [some] beautiful countryside where you can relax, walk and enjoy the silence and nature.

_source.definition_text: a period of time in which there is complete quiet or no speaking
_source.learnerexamples_text: There were long silences during the discussion.; The progress of the story is very slow, but the author is descri[b]ing hard conditions, hard characters [and] long silences, which is quite t[y]pical of his way [of writing].

_source.definition_text: a period of time when someone says nothing about a particular subject or when someone does not communicate with someone at all
_source.learnerexamples_text: She ended her silence yesterday and spoke to a TV reporter about the affair.; I took his long silence to mean that I had offended him.; How dared he call her after such a long silence and order her what to do?

_source.definition_text: without any sound
_source.learnerexamples_text: The empty house was completely silent.; The countryside, like Chianti, is peaceful and silent.

_source.definition_text: without talking
_source.learnerexamples_text: She whispered a silent prayer that her wounded brother would not die.; The police officer told the criminal that he had the right to remain silent.; The minister was silent on/about his plans for the future.; Arthur has always been the strong, silent type.; When they were there, Aunt Patience was obliged by her husband to go to her room and remain silent.

_source.definition_text: without making any noise
_source.learnerexamples_text: She wept silently as she read the letter.; He silently vowed to take revenge.; After waiting silently for two minutes, she dropped the phone.

_source.definition_text: showing little thought or judgment
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't do that, you silly boy!; a silly mistake; It was silly of you to go out in the sun without a hat.; I feel silly in this dress.; They had some very silly games.

_source.definition_text: a type of cloth which is light and smooth
_source.learnerexamples_text: a silk dress; a silk shirt; Normally, I would prefer my blouses to be made of cotton or silk, as these materials make me [feel] comfortable.

_source.definition_text: small and not important
_source.learnerexamples_text: She gets upset over such silly things.; Pe[o]ple are so worried about silly things, about how to make money or how to be popular and they forget about what really matters.

_source.definition_text: a valuable, shiny, grey-white metal used to make coins and jewellery
_source.learnerexamples_text: We gave Alison and Tom a dish made of solid silver as a wedding present.; It was a beautiful ring, it was made of silver with a diamond on it.

_source.definition_text: If something or someone is similar to another thing or person, they have many things the same, although they are not exactly the same.
_source.learnerexamples_text: My father and I have similar views on politics.; I bought some new shoes which are very similar to a pair I had before.; Paul is very similar in appearance to his brother.; I can understand how you are feeling because at our age, every teenager has similar problems.

_source.definition_text: made of silver, or of the colour of silver
_source.learnerexamples_text: a silver ring; My grandmother has silver hair.; I g[o]t bea[u]tiful presents, but my favo[u]rite is a silver ring.

_source.definition_text: when two things or people are similar, or a way in which they are similar
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can see the similarity between you and your mother.; The book bears several striking similarities to last year's bestseller.; Another similarity between the two was their appearance.

_source.definition_text: in a similar way
_source.learnerexamples_text: The children were similarly dressed.; Cars must stop at red traffic lights; similarly, bicycles should stop too.; Business people would like to have a car park in the city cent[re], whereas most residents are against it, mainly because of the horrible noise made by cars. Similarly, some students, who are concerned about pollution, prefer the car park to be [o]n the outskirts of the city.

_source.definition_text: easy to do or to understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: The instructions were written in simple English.;  It's simple to find our house.; I want an explanation, but keep/make it simple.; I've bought a Sony mobile phone. It's very simple and really easy to use.

_source.definition_text: plain or not complicated
_source.learnerexamples_text: a simple life; a simple black dress ; We had a simple meal of bread and cheese.; You can eat simple food and drink good local wine.

_source.definition_text: used to describe the one important fact, truth, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We didn't go swimming for the simple reason that the water was too cold.; I'm very fond of working with animals, and the simple reason is that I'm plan[n]ing to become a vet.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being simple
_source.learnerexamples_text: The advantage of the plan is its simplicity.; The examination was simplicity itself.; I admire the simplicity of her designs.; Video facilities are rated as quite good [by] the students, and computer programmes have gained almost everybody's compl[i]ments for their simplicity and efficacy.

_source.definition_text: the process of making something more simple
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think these rules need some simplification.; It might be a simplification and an exaggeration, but as the word says: "The road of excess leads to the tower of wisdom", and although the idea expresses itself in crude terms, I do think there is some truth to it.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize what you are saying
_source.learnerexamples_text: We simply don't have the time.; You look simply beautiful in that dress.; The hunger in parts of Africa is terrible - there's (quite) simply no other word for it.; It's said that most of the centre's sports facilities are very expensive, [but] that is simply not true.

_source.definition_text: to make something less complicated and therefore easier to do or understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: the new, simplified tax system; He tried to simplify the story for the younger audience.; The technology has probably simplified life [i]n a way that no one could beli[e]ve was possible about 20 years ago.

_source.definition_text: only
_source.learnerexamples_text: A lot of people miss out on this opportunity simply because they don't know about it.; I am very interested in fashion, simply because it is a style, an attitude, a way of life.

_source.definition_text: in a way which is not complicated or difficult to understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: He explained it as simply as he could, but the class still didn't understand.; Try to organize your work as simply as possible.

_source.definition_text: a model of something that can be used to teach someone how to do something, or the process of making such a model
_source.learnerexamples_text: Students can study a computer simulation of these atomic processes.; Civilisation is one of the best-selling simulation games of all time.

_source.definition_text: If two or more things are simultaneous, they happen or exist at the same time.
_source.learnerexamples_text: simultaneous translation ; The people I most admire are simultaneous interpreter[s].

_source.definition_text: at the same time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Two children answered the teacher's question simultaneously.; The floods of information pour towards you and go through your brain simultaneously.

_source.definition_text: something which is against the rules of a religion
_source.learnerexamples_text: the sin of greed/pride; to commit a sin; Nurses and doctors in white or green overalls, smells of drugs and sweating patients, moans of pain during the night, all that was like sending me to hell for a sin I knew nothing about.

_source.definition_text: something that you should not do because it is morally wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've only got one life and it's a sin to waste it. ; It would be a sin not to grasp the opportunities one is given.

_source.definition_text: from a time in the past until a later time or until now
_source.learnerexamples_text: England have not won the World Cup in football since 1966.; It was the hottest October since records began.

_source.definition_text: from a time in the past until a later time or until now
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's been much happier since he started his new job.; I've known Tim since he was seven.; I was really surprised when I read the e-mail because I haven't heard from you since I visited you last year.

_source.definition_text: from a time in the past until a later time or until now
_source.learnerexamples_text: Emma went to work in New York a year ago, and we haven't seen her since.; He started working for the company when he left school, and has been there ever since.; I've long since forgotten any Latin I ever learned.; It was my grandmother who introduced me to teddy bears and she wanted me to love them as she did. _source.definition_text: large and with a lot of space

_source.definition_text: emails that you do not want, usually advertisements

_source.definition_text: time when you are not working
_source.learnerexamples_text: I like to do a bit of gardening in my spare time.; I like to play baseball and read in my spare time.

_source.definition_text: If something is spare, it is available to use, because it is extra and not being used.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a spare key/tyre; Have you got a spare pen?; We've got a spare room if you want to stay overnight with us.; Could I have a word with you when you've got a spare moment/minute?; "Do you want this cake?" "Yes, if it's going spare."

_source.definition_text: If you have time, money, etc. to spare, you have more than you need.

_source.definition_text: to give time or money to someone

_source.definition_text: to use a lot of effort/expense, etc. to do something
_source.searchterms_text: spare;spare no effort/expense etc;spare no effort/expense, etc.;spared;spares;sparing

_source.definition_text: to think about someone who is in a bad situation

_source.definition_text: a very small, bright piece of burning material

_source.definition_text: a small idea or event which causes something bigger to start

_source.definition_text: to cause an argument, fight, etc. to start happening

_source.definition_text: shining brightly because of reflected light

_source.definition_text: water/wine with bubbles in it
_source.learnerexamples_text: Would you like still or sparkling water?

_source.definition_text: special or exciting
_source.learnerexamples_text: a sparkling performance ;  sparkling conversation ; After, [it's] time for lunch with a lot of Champagne (for a more sparkling atmosphere!).

_source.definition_text: to say something using your voice

_source.definition_text: with small amounts and scattered over a large area

_source.definition_text: to be able to talk in a language
_source.learnerexamples_text: He speaks fluent French.; How many foreign languages do you speak?; I couldn't speak a word of Spanish when I got there.; I couldn't figure out what language they were speaking.; I don't speak English prop[e]rly.

_source.definition_text: to talk about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He refused to speak about the matter in public.; In the interview she spoke of her sadness at her mother's death.; They filmed the headmistress of our school. She spoke about the school's activities.

_source.definition_text: to make a speech to a large group of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was invited to speak at a conference in Madrid.; [O]n behalf of all its members, I would like to invite you to speak at one of our meetings.

_source.definition_text: used to explain that you are talking about something in a general/personal, etc. way

_source.definition_text: to express the feelings, opinions, etc. of another person or a group of people

_source.definition_text: used to explain that the words you are using do not have their usual meaning
_source.learnerexamples_text: That was our accommodation, so to speak.; In those cases, travelling turns into a sort of alienation, so to speak.

_source.definition_text: If something speaks for itself, it is clear and needs no further explanation.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The school's excellent record speaks for itself.; On the one hand the economic success of sports events speaks for itself.

_source.definition_text: If something speaks volumes, it makes an opinion, characteristic or situation very clear without the use of words.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She said very little, but her face spoke volumes.; It remains to be seen whether the effect of stem cells when applied to humans would be the same, but the achievements speak volumes about the fact that stem cells may one day turn a new [page] in many people's lives and let them get rid of that humiliating label of a "disabled person."

_source.definition_text: to say exactly what you think without worrying if it will upset anyone

_source.definition_text: to speak in a louder voice so that people can hear you
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you speak up? We can't hear at the back.; First of all, I read it far too fast and in a voice that was hardly a[udi]ble, and people started to shout that they couldn't hear me and that I should speak up; it was terrible!

_source.definition_text: the part of a radio, CD player, etc. which the sound comes out of
_source.learnerexamples_text: I bought some new speakers for my CD player.; I had lots of lovely presents: a mobile phone, stereo speakers, clothes, CDs, books, etc.

_source.definition_text: someone who can speak English/French, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's a fluent Russian speaker.; I think I'm going to be an English speaker sooner than I expected.

_source.definition_text: someone who makes a speech to a group of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: a good public speaker; Please join with me in thanking our guest speaker tonight.; The speaker told me many things about feeding birds.

_source.definition_text: better or more important than usual things
_source.learnerexamples_text: a special friend; I'm cooking something special for her birthday.; Is there anything special that you'd like to do today?; I have a suit for special occasions.; I got many presents from my friends, and I got a special present from my dad [-] it was a new bike

_source.definition_text: a price which is lower than usual

_source.definition_text: different from normal things, or used for a particular purpose

It's a special kind of canoe.

_source.definition_text: treatment that is better than usual
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't expect special treatment - I just want to be treated fairly.; As you know, an Austin Healey needs special treatment.

_source.definition_text: someone who has a lot of experience, knowledge, or skill in a particular subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: a software specialist; She's a specialist in modern French literature.; She's a specialist in childhood illnesses.; a leading cancer/eye specialist; Now, fully equipped and powerful computers can be so small and mobile that some specialists predict that new devices will replace [the] book.

_source.definition_text: a product, skill, etc. that a person or place is especially known for
_source.learnerexamples_text: We tasted a local speciality made from goat's cheese.; But even McDonald's realised there is another trend on the rise - local food and specialities - and therefor[e] started putting them on the[ir] menu.

_source.definition_text: to spend most of your time studying one particular subject or doing one type of business
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's hired a lawyer who specializes in divorce cases.; a restaurant that specialises in seafood; I enjoy working in general medicine, but I hope to be able to specialize in the future.; Some specialise in acting and others [work] back stage like adjusting the sound or light and preparing the outfits.

_source.definition_text: for a particular purpose

_source.definition_text: exact or containing details
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you be more specific about the problem?; To be more specific, our students discovered that the majority of your exhibits did not function at all.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a particular thing and not something general
_source.learnerexamples_text: English for specific purposes; The disease seems to be specific to certain types of plant.; Is there anything specific you want from the shops?; We need to see animals, study them, and in some cases find out why specific types of animals can't live in the nature which we have spoiled.

_source.definition_text: a group of plants or animals which share similar characteristics
_source.learnerexamples_text: Mountain gorillas are an endangered species.; Over a hundred species of insect are found in this area.; Then I wrote an article about saving endangered species.

_source.definition_text: for a particular reason, purpose, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're designed specifically for children.; She bought it specifically to wear at the wedding.; I specifically chose to travel with you since your travel brochure promised a half-day trip to St. Andrews, where I was to meet my friend Ann.

_source.definition_text: exactly or in detail

_source.definition_text: a detailed description of how something should be done, made, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are made exactly to the customer's specifications.; Translating technical specifications prepared by no[n]-native speakers can often cause serious problems.

_source.definition_text: to state or describe something clearly and exactly
_source.learnerexamples_text: He said we should meet but didn't specify a time.; The peace treaty clearly specifies the terms for the withdrawal of troops.; The newspaper report did not specify how the men were killed.; My contract specifies (that) I must give a month's notice if I leave my job.; The loan must be repaid within a specified period/by a specified date.

_source.definition_text: an animal, plant, etc. used as an example of its type, especially for scientific study
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is one of the museum's finest specimens.; Plant life to is being given a hard time, as the would-be mountain explorers walk off the designated [paths] and wreak havoc in the wilderness, destroying many priceless specimens.

_source.definition_text: someone who watches an event, sport, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They won 4-0 in front of over 40 000 cheering spectators.; At midnight sharp, fireworks covered the concert hall and I, as well as the rest of [the] spectators, felt the excitement and delight I've never felt before.

_source.definition_text: extremely good, exciting, or surprising
_source.learnerexamples_text: a spectacular view; The show was a spectacular success.; He scored a spectacular goal in the second half.; There was a spectacular sunset last night.; It is located in a tall building and has a spectacular view.

_source.definition_text: the set of colours into which light can be separated
_source.learnerexamples_text: The colours of the spectrum can be seen in a rainbow.; Then, at dawn, the sun slowly rises, producing a spectacular spectrum of colours, ranging from deep purple to blinding yellow.

_source.definition_text: all the different ideas, opinions, possibilities, etc. that exist
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has support from across the whole political spectrum. ; At the other [end] of the spectrum of opinions you can find some people who need to park in the city for business matters, like a local shopkeeper I talked to, who is afraid of losing customers.

_source.definition_text: the right to say or write what you want

_source.searchterms_text: send shivers/a shiver down your spine;spine;spines

_source.definition_text: a place

_source.definition_text: an unpleasant, small, red mark on your skin

_source.definition_text: completely clean

_source.definition_text: a strong light which can be pointed in different directions

_source.definition_text: your husband or wife

_source.definition_text: liquid in a container which forces it out in small drops
_source.learnerexamples_text: hair spray; spray paint; Actually, there was an attempt to cut down on using and producing sprays which destroy the ozon[e] layer.

_source.definition_text: to force liquid out of a container in many small drops

_source.definition_text: If information spreads, or if someone spreads it, it is communicated to many people.

_source.definition_text: to gradually affect a larger area

_source.definition_text: to arrange something over a large area, especially something that was folded

_source.definition_text: to arrange for something to happen over a period of time and not at once

_source.definition_text: when something moves to cover a larger area or affect a larger number of people

_source.definition_text: a chart produced on a computer which helps you to do business calculations and planning
_source.learnerexamples_text: She prepared a spreadsheet with the new sales information.; I would be very interested in joining your club, in order to learn how to use basic software like word processing, spreadsheet or database software.

_source.definition_text: the season of the year between winter and summer, when the weather becomes warmer and plants start to grow again
_source.learnerexamples_text: spring flowers/weather; Many bulbs flower in (the) spring.; Janet's coming over for a couple of weeks next spring.; You can come in spring.

_source.definition_text: to jump or move somewhere suddenly

_source.definition_text: a place where water comes out of the ground

_source.definition_text: to appear suddenly

_source.definition_text: to come from or be the result of something

_source.definition_text: to gently drop small pieces of something over a surface

_source.definition_text: to encourage someone to do something or something to happen

_source.base_text: on the spur of the moment

_source.searchterms_text: on the spur of the moment;spur;spurs

_source.definition_text: someone who secretly tries to discover information about a person, country, etc.

_source.definition_text: a group of police officers who have special skills to deal with particular problems

_source.learnerexamples_text: They tried to make me accept a lower wage, but I stood my ground.; She said she would stand her ground. In fact, she hoped that after the first flush of infatuation was over, Francis would come [to] long for his former love.

_source.definition_text: to support or represent a particular idea or set of ideas
_source.learnerexamples_text: This party stands for low taxes and individual freedom.; The Brandenburger Tor stands for freedom and unity.

_source.definition_text: to continue to support or help someone who is in a difficult situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has vowed to stand by her husband during his trial.; And I promise I'll stand by you.

_source.definition_text: If you will not stand for something, you will not accept a situation or a particular type of behaviour
_source.learnerexamples_text: I wouldn't stand for that sort of behaviour from him, if I were you.; Much as I admire the performance of the new aircraft today, I understand your need to fly and test new technologies, but I will not stand for it any longer.

_source.definition_text: If one or more letters stand for a word or name, they are the first letter or letters of that word or name and they represent it
_source.learnerexamples_text: 'GMT' stands for Greenwich Mean Time.

_source.definition_text: to be very easy to see or notice
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bright blue letters really stand out on the page.; Why wasn't that money spent in trying to make them more bearable to [look at], [rather] than making them stand out even more?

_source.definition_text: to be much better than other similar things or people
_source.learnerexamples_text: One candidate stood out from the rest.; Those small fishing villages will always stand out in my memory.

_source.definition_text: to do something that someone else was going to do because they cannot be there
_source.learnerexamples_text: She stood in for me when I was sick.; As I will be away these two days, I have asked Mr. Ryman's secretary Sandy, to stand in for me.

_source.base_text: stand up sb or stand sb up
_source.definition_text: to fail to meet someone you have arranged a romantic meeting with
_source.searchterms_text: stand;stand up sb or stand sb up
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was starting to think I'd been stood up when he arrived.

_source.definition_text: to defend or support a particular idea or a person who is being criticized or attacked
_source.searchterms_text: stand;stand up for sth/sb;stand up for sth/sb
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's high time we all stood up for our rights around here.; Don't be bullied, learn to stand up for yourself and what you believe in.; He decides to stand up for black rights and becomes an important leader.

_source.definition_text: a table or small structure from which goods are sold or shown
_source.learnerexamples_text: a hot dog stand; Visit our stand at the trade fair.; It would be extremely beneficial to our company to have a stand there next year.

_source.definition_text: to defend yourself against a powerful person or organization when they treat you unfairly
_source.searchterms_text: stand;stand up to sb/sth;stand up to sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He wasn't afraid to stand up to bullies.; They say that the best things in life are for free, courage, hope, love for freedom and the power to stand up to others, defending one's own rights.

_source.definition_text: to publicly defend something or stop something from happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's about time someone made a stand.; He refuses to take a stand on this issue.; We cannot simply stand by while our greenery is being [destroy]ed, so I am making a stand.

_source.definition_text: a piece of furniture for holding things
_source.learnerexamples_text: a music/hat stand; We go backstage, the audience is still clapping and the people in the orchestra are beating with their bow on the music stand.

_source.definition_text: a level of quality, especially a level that is acceptable
_source.learnerexamples_text: a high standard of service; low safety standards; His work was below standard.; She sets very high standards for herself.; This essay is not of an acceptable standard - do it again.

_source.definition_text: a level of behaviour, especially a level that is acceptable
_source.learnerexamples_text: high moral standards; According to my moral standards, adults should not take advantage of children's lack of experience and they should certainly not incite them to tell lies and betray others.

_source.definition_text: how much money and comfort someone has
_source.learnerexamples_text: a low/high standard of living; I think we would have a better standard of living if we had this situation.

_source.definition_text: usual rather than special, especially when thought of as being correct or acceptable
_source.learnerexamples_text: White is the standard colour for this model of refrigerator.; These are standard procedures for handling radioactive waste.; The metre is the standard unit for measuring length in the SI system.; It should be a standard price.

_source.definition_text: a particular way of thinking about a situation or problem
_source.learnerexamples_text: to look at something from a political/religious standpoint ; From a moral standpoint it can be argued that the income distribution that comes from such incredible payments is unacceptable.

_source.definition_text: a famous singer, actor, sports person, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a rock/movie/football star; Kids wanting to be stars come to Hollywood from all over America.; My favourite tennis star is Juan-Carlos Ferrero.

_source.definition_text: a ball of burning gases that you see as a small point of light in the sky at night
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stars twinkled/shone above them as they lay on the hill.; Well, it's really big, with two windows to see the garden [in the] morning, and the stars at night.

_source.definition_text: a shape or symbol with four or more points
_source.learnerexamples_text: star-shaped; How many stars has this restaurant got?; It has pink flowers and blue stars.

_source.definition_text: used to show how good a restaurant or hotel is
_source.searchterms_text: star;stars;two star/three star, etc.;two-star/three-star etc;two-star/three-star, etc.;twostar/threestar, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a five-star hotel; Also the facilities were great and people started building houses, and the small village became an attractive town with museums, universities, wonderful beaches, five-star hotels and other beautiful facilities.

_source.definition_text: someone or something that is better than all the others in a group
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is one of our star players.; She was the star of the English class.; He led Brazil to win two more World Cups, and in both of them he was the star player, the black prince.

_source.definition_text: when someone is very famous for acting, singing, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is heading for stardom.; The phenomenon of stardom is a complex one.

_source.definition_text: If a film, play, etc. stars someone, or if someone stars in a film, play, etc., they are the main actor in it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ben Kingsley starred in the film 'Gandhi'.; Fowles's novel 'The French Lieutenant's Woman' was turned into a film starring Meryl Streep.; As we both love romantic comedy, we decided to see Notting Hill [together], which starred Julia Roberts and Hugh Grant.

_source.definition_text: to look at someone or something for a long time and not move your eyes
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't stare at people like that, it's rude.; Chuck sat quietly for hours staring into the distance, thinking of what might have been.; David had seen her once before in a park, staring at him.

_source.definition_text: to begin doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: When do you start your course/your new job?; We'll be starting (the class) at six o'clock.; Can you start on Monday?; They started building the house in January.; I'd just started to write a letter when the phone rang.

_source.definition_text: to begin to happen or to make something begin to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: A new series of wildlife programmes has started on Monday evenings.; Police believe the fire was started by arsonists.; The Council has started another programme as well which calls people to collect the rubbish in their own street one weekend in every month.

_source.definition_text: If a business or other organization starts, or if someone starts one, it is created and starts to operate.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She started her own software company.; A lot of new restaurants have started up in the region.; It was the first time in many years he had the opportunity or time to think over his situation and life. He had started his company fifteen years ago and had been successful.

_source.definition_text: If you start a machine or an engine, you switch it on, and if a machine or engine starts, it begins to work.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car wouldn't start.; Do you know how to start the lawn mower?; The car would not start and it was impossible to get a taxi because it was Saturday evening, so the only thing we could do was to run all the way to the school.

_source.definition_text: used before saying the first thing in a list of things
_source.learnerexamples_text: To start with, we need better computers. Then we need more training.; There is some information I should tell you about. To start with, the T.V repairman didn't come on Wednesday morning as expected.

_source.definition_text: to begin your life, or the part of your life when you work, in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: My dad started out as a sales assistant in a shop.; She is a beautiful, talented wom[a]n who started out as a small actress in her own country, climbing up to become the fully-recognized celebrity that she is now.

_source.definition_text: to begin by doing something, or to make something begin by doing something
_source.searchterms_text: start;start (sth) off or start off(sth);start sth off or start offsth
_source.learnerexamples_text: She started off the meeting with the monthly sales report.; I'd like to start off by thanking you all for coming today.; We started off the trip by driving to the foot of the mountain, where there was a village.

_source.definition_text: to begin doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to make a start on (preparing) the brochure next week.

_source.definition_text: from the beginning of something to its end
_source.learnerexamples_text: I enjoyed the film from start to finish.; I found out that the service itself should last at least one and half hour[s] from start to finish.

_source.definition_text: the beginning of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were doubtful about the product's usefulness from the start.; They announced the start of a new commercial venture.; The weather was good at the start of the week.; The event got off to a shaky/poor start with the stage lights failing in the first few minutes.; That was a bad start [to] my holidays!

_source.definition_text: an advantage that you have over someone else when you begin something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm grateful for the start I had in life.; With a better start in life these children will be less likely to end up on the street again.

_source.definition_text: used when you are giving the first in a list of reasons or things
_source.learnerexamples_text: I won't be going - I've got too much homework for a start.; So this creates an awareness of the obligation to look after oneself for a start.

_source.definition_text: the state of having no food for a long period
_source.learnerexamples_text: These people are dying of starvation.; While a few decades ago people used to die from starvation even in industrialised countries like France, nowadays the situation has changed and food can be found so easily that it has become an increasing source of health-related problems when exceeded.

_source.definition_text: ill or dying because there is not enough food
_source.l_topic_text_text: body and health, food and drink
_source.learnerexamples_text: starving people; What shocked me most was the misery and poverty: thousands of homeless people roaming the streets starving and cold.

_source.definition_text: to become ill or die because you do not have enough food, or to make someone ill or die because they do not have enough food
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many people have starved to death in parts of Africa.; People were starving to death and various crimes took place.

_source.definition_text: the condition that something or someone is in
_source.learnerexamples_text: The building is in a terrible state.; She was found wandering in a confused state (of mind).; Give me the keys - you're in no fit state to drive.; After the accident I was in a state of shock.; I came home to an unhappy state of affairs.

_source.definition_text: very hungry
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm absolutely starving.; I've always been greedy, but [at] that moment, while my Chemistry teacher was explaining a difficult lesson, I was really starving.

_source.definition_text: a country or its government
_source.learnerexamples_text: The drought is worst in the central African states.; Britain is one of the member states of the European Union.; The government was determined to reduce the number of state-owned industries.; Some theatres receive a small amount of funding from the state.; I opted, since I must talk about my country's history, to choose an event not from the [w]hole history of the Greek nation, but from that of the independent Greek state (kingdom or republic, it depends [on] the period), which ha[d] a life of about 270-280 years.

_source.definition_text: to officially say or write something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our warranty clearly states the limits of our liability.; Union members stated (that) they were unhappy with the proposal.; Please state why you wish to apply for this grant.; Children in the stated areas were at risk from a lack of food, the report said.; Dear Mr Thomas, I've read your advertis[e]ment in [the] last issue of "The Traveller", [where] you state that you are looking for people to work on your campsites with English-speaking tourists.

_source.definition_text: provided, created or done by the state
_source.learnerexamples_text: state education/industries; state control; state funding/pensions; In general, the rules at private schools are much [strict]er than the ones at state schools.

_source.definition_text: something that someone says or writes officially
_source.learnerexamples_text: The government is expected to issue a statement about the investigation to the press.; He produced a signed statement from the prisoner.; We were not surprised by their statement that the train services would be reduced.; Dear Editor Referring to your article of today, I want to correct some statements [made].

_source.definition_text: a piece of paper that shows how much money you have put into your bank account and how much you have taken out
_source.learnerexamples_text: I always check my statement.; My collection consists of original, pre-WW2 hand-written documents - anything from love letters to bank statements, chores lists handed out to servants to pre-nuptial agre[e]ments, as long as it is hand-written, finds its way to my archives.

_source.definition_text: using the newest ideas, designs, and materials
_source.learnerexamples_text: It is a computer system that uses state-of-the-art technology.; It is the impressive and simply state-of-the-art graphics that entice the player to spend hours in front of the screen.

_source.definition_text: a building where trains stop so that you can get on or off them
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dad met me at the station.; a railway station; Our office is near the station.; We looked on our map to find the nearest underground/tube station.; [It] is near Waterloo station.

_source.definition_text: a building where a bus starts or ends its journey
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bus station is in the centre of town.; I will meet you at the bus station.

_source.definition_text: a fact in the form of a number that shows information about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Statistics show that skin cancer is becoming more common.; Wom[e]n have always been as bright and educated as men - statistics show that in Germany there are more women entering for exams at the universities than there are men.

_source.definition_text: a company that broadcasts television or radio programmes
_source.learnerexamples_text: a radio/television station; The reception is not very good - try to tune in to another station.; Last week I was [listen]ing to my favorite radio station and they announced a new sports club.

_source.definition_text: relating to statistics
_source.learnerexamples_text: There is no statistical evidence to support his claims.; I just wondered why your newspaper didn't stick to the statistical figures and the pie chart we announced on the next day [after] the fund-raising activity.

_source.definition_text: a collection of facts in the form of numbers that shows information about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Statistics show/suggest that women live longer than men.; According to official statistics, the Japanese work longer hours than workers in most other industrialized countries.; According to statistics based on the questionnair[e], the majority of students feel the most enthusiasm for [their] English class.

_source.definition_text: a model that looks like a person or animal, usually made from stone or metal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a statue of a boy; They planned to put up/erect a statue to the President.; After, we passed in front of the statue of the president.

_source.definition_text: an accepted or official position, especially in a social group
_source.learnerexamples_text: The association works to promote the status of retired people as useful members of the community.; There has been an increase in applications for refugee status.; The success of her book has given her unexpected celebrity status.; Applicants should have a degree or a qualification of equal status.; Their status and income were shadowed by the state.

_source.definition_text: something that people want to have because they think it will make people admire them
_source.learnerexamples_text: For him, a big car is an important status symbol. ; Jobs now play a very important role as status symbols.

_source.definition_text: to continue to be in a place, job, etc. and not leave
_source.learnerexamples_text: The weather was bad so we stayed at home.; Do you want to stay in teaching?; They need an assistant who is willing to stay for six months.; Can you stay late tonight to finish the report?; Because of the snow, schools have been closed and children told to stay at home.

_source.definition_text: to live or be in a place for a short time as a visitor
_source.learnerexamples_text: I stayed in Montreal for two weeks then flew home.; They said they'd stay at/in a hotel.; The children usually stay with their grandparents for a week in the summer.; On this holiday I stayed in Bedford with my English friends.

_source.definition_text: to continue to be in a particular state
_source.learnerexamples_text: The supermarket stays open late.; I was tired and couldn't stay awake.; Put a lid on the pan so the food will stay hot.; They stayed friends after their divorce.; Some people prefer to stay dry [rather] than be caught by the rain.

_source.definition_text: to avoid becoming involved in something that will have a bad effect on you
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stay away from drugs of any sort.; He started a help-program[me] to help children to stay away from criminality and do something useful with their lives.

_source.definition_text: to continue to be in the same place
_source.learnerexamples_text: He told me to stay put while he fetched the car.; It was extremely stressful and she didn't like the working conditions and atmosphere at work, but as it was [difficult] to find another job, she stayed put.

_source.definition_text: to stay in your home
_source.learnerexamples_text: Let's stay in tonight and watch a video.; I went with my friend, Marina, because she was not having classes any more, and she was bored of staying in [and] doing nothing.

_source.definition_text: to not leave a place when other people leave it
_source.learnerexamples_text: He stayed behind after class to speak to the teacher.

_source.definition_text: to not come home at night, or to go home late
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our cat usually stays out at night.; My mum won't let me stay out late.; Firstly, I like it so much because we have no school and we can stay out for as long as we want.

_source.definition_text: to continue to be in a place, job or school after other people have left
_source.learnerexamples_text: I stayed on an extra year at school.

_source.definition_text: to not become involved in an argument or discussion
_source.searchterms_text: stay;stay out of sth;stay out of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's better to stay out of their arguments.; You don't know anything about this, so just stay out of it!

_source.definition_text: to go to bed later than usual
_source.learnerexamples_text: We stayed up (late) to watch a film.; In Vegas, we were staying up all night gambling.

_source.definition_text: to spend the night somewhere instead of returning to your home or continuing your journey
_source.learnerexamples_text: Why don't you stay over and drive back in the morning? ; We stay[ed] over in a hotel and the next morning Tom brought me home.

_source.definition_text: a period of time that you spend in a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did you enjoy your stay in Tokyo?; Dear Candie, I have just arrived here on my holiday. I'm in Cannes, in the south of France. [I]t's a lovely place, [and] I'm enjoying my stay so much.

_source.definition_text: at a gradual, regular rate
_source.learnerexamples_text: Prices have increased steadily since the war.;  In the past people didn't read books all the time. Neither did their kids at school. Today they read even less books but the number of copied and read articles or book extracts ha[s] increased steadily.

_source.definition_text: happening at a gradual, regular rate
_source.learnerexamples_text: The procession moved through the streets at a steady pace.; Orders for new ships are rising, after several years of steady decline.; Over the last 10 years, he has produced a steady flow/stream of articles and papers.; Progress has been slow but steady.; There is also a steady rise in underweight [young girls] today.

_source.definition_text: still and not shaking
_source.learnerexamples_text: You need steady hands to be a dentist.; Make sure you hold the ladder steady.; I know very well you have steady nerves but what is strong can turn weak as well.

_source.definition_text: not changing
_source.learnerexamples_text: She drove at a steady speed.; Once on the road, keep a steady speed (not too slow, not too fast) and try to look confident.

_source.definition_text: a job that is likely to continue for a long time and pay you regular money
_source.learnerexamples_text: I wish he'd get a steady job.; They now had steady jobs, she reasoned; their time at college had been turbulent and not quite happy and they had badly needed a mother figure to see [it] through, but that time was over now.

_source.definition_text: a thick, flat piece of meat or fish
_source.learnerexamples_text: steak and chips; It was at the club and we had a steak and games at the pool.

_source.definition_text: to secretly take something that does not belong to you, without intending to return it
_source.learnerexamples_text: She admitted stealing the money from her employers.; The number of cars which are stolen every year has risen.; All my friends gave me lots of presents, but I like the bike best. I like it because my bike was stolen.

_source.definition_text: to get rid of your anger, excitement, etc. by being noisy or using a lot of energy
_source.learnerexamples_text: The children need to run around and let off steam.; I believe that listening to it on a daily basis will be an ideal way for us to relieve the day's pressure and let off steam.

_source.definition_text: the hot gas that is produced when water boils
_source.learnerexamples_text: Steam rose from the simmering stew.; a steam engine; the age of steam; The pump is driven by steam.; I've been interested in trains, in particular steam trains, since my childhood.

_source.definition_text: A steep slope, hill, etc. rises quickly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a steep slope; It's a steep climb to the top of the mountain, but the view is worth it.; The castle is set on a steep hill/hillside.; But the slope was terribly steep and I didn't dare to ski down.

_source.definition_text: a very strong metal made from iron, used for making knives, machines, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: steel pipes; a stainless steel sink; The object that I would choose is without any doubt my Katana, my Japanese Sword. It is a weapon that reminds me of my childhood games. I also like the form, and the cool steel of the blade.

_source.definition_text: to control the direction of a vehicle
_source.learnerexamples_text: She carefully steered the car around the potholes.; This car is very easy to steer.; After an hour she could keep [her] balance but she still had problems steering, but that didn't matter.

_source.definition_text: A steep increase or fall in something is very big and quick.
_source.learnerexamples_text: There has been a steep increase/rise in prices.; However, there was a steep increase in 1978 to 1982 when the figure reached about 60 million tonnes.

_source.definition_text: to avoid someone or something because they are unpleasant or dangerous
_source.learnerexamples_text: Steer clear of Tony this morning - he's in a bad mood.; Her speech steered clear of controversial issues.; Eating health[il]y doesn't mean starving, eating plants or steering clear of meat.

_source.definition_text: a wheel that you turn to control the direction of a vehicle
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took both hands off the steering wheel.; After leaving your house on Monday morning, I gripped the steering wheel, fixed my eyes firmly on the road, and bravely drove my way up to Scotland.

_source.definition_text: to develop as the result of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her problems stem from childhood.; This educational approach stems from strong family values and religious beliefs.

_source.definition_text: one of the movements you make with your feet when you walk
_source.learnerexamples_text: Sophie took her first steps when she was eleven months old.; He rose to his feet and took a couple of steps towards her.;  With every step, her feet hurt her more and more.; I tried to run but with my first step, I kicked something that fell to the floor.

_source.definition_text: one of the surfaces that you walk on when you go up or down stairs
_source.learnerexamples_text: a flight of steps; We had to climb some steps to reach the front door.; I asked them to leave the parcel on the (front) step.; I go down four steps and I am [o]n the beach!

_source.definition_text: one of the things that you do to achieve something
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's the next step in the programme?; We must stay one step ahead of our competitors.; Most people believe that the decision to cut interest rates was a step in the right direction.; The President took the unusual step of altering his prepared speech in order to condemn the terrorist attack.; We'd like to know how it feels to be in the film business, how you started and the steps you've taken to be where you are now.

_source.definition_text: moving slowly from one stage of something to the next
_source.learnerexamples_text: I know there's a lot to prepare, but just take things step by step and don't worry.; The book actually guides you step by step on how you can cope with this fear and defeat it.

_source.definition_text: to go back somewhere the same way that you came
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was lost so I retraced my steps.; Mentally retracing his steps of the morning, he remembered rushing out of his place at the last minute.

_source.definition_text: to put your foot on or in something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I accidentally stepped on her foot.; Be careful not to step in the mud.; I ha[d] to dance with a boy [whose] name is Alex and every time he stepped on my feet.

_source.definition_text: to move somewhere by lifting your foot and putting it down in a different place
_source.learnerexamples_text: She stepped carefully over the dog.; She stepped backwards and fell over a chair.; They stepped out onto the balcony.; The moment he stepped out of the train he realized he had left his suitcase inside.

_source.definition_text: to leave an important job
_source.learnerexamples_text: He stepped down as manager of the Italian team.; Thus, he decided to retire, to step down from the tough and competitive environment and planned for the rest of his life.

_source.definition_text: the man who is married to your mother but is not your father
_source.learnerexamples_text: His stepfather gave him a job.; Once, Matthew told Pat that he was mistreated by his stepfather in his childhood.

_source.definition_text: the woman who has married your father but is not your mother
_source.learnerexamples_text: My stepmother is only a few years older than me.; He made up his mind to defeat them, and asked his stepmother for some kibidango, one of [the] traditional snacks in Japan.

_source.definition_text: a fixed idea that people have about what a particular type of person is like, especially an idea that is wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: racial stereotypes; It seems commonly accepted that the new ''high-tech'' society has turned us into lazy people, without aims, targets, even hobbies in our spare time, unless watching videos or playing computer games. I am a student, I am young and I know a lot of people like me who do not fit in this stereotype.

_source.definition_text: very serious and without any humour
_source.learnerexamples_text: a stern expression/face ; stern criticism; He shot his sister Sarah a stern look which did not deter her from grinning maliciously.

_source.definition_text: having the qualities that you would expect a particular kind of person to have
_source.learnerexamples_text: a stereotypical student ; Another person would rather perceive a stereotypical celebrity, a singer or a sports star as a greedy, self-absorbed and shallow pleasure seeker, concerned only with his or her own appearance and flaunting undeserved wealth.

_source.definition_text: to become joined to something else or to make something become joined to something else, usually with a substance like glue
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tried to stick the pieces together with some glue/tape.; He stuck up a notice on the board with pins.; This glue won't stick.; My car's stuck in the mud.; Stir the sauce so that it doesn't stick to the pan.

_source.definition_text: If something sharp sticks into something, it goes into it, and if you stick something sharp somewhere, you push it into something.
_source.searchterms_text: stick;stick (sth) in/into/through, etc.;stick sth in/into/through etc;stick sth in/into/through, etc.;sticking;sticks;stuck
_source.learnerexamples_text: The nurse stuck the needle into his arm.; The body of his boss's wife lay on the ground, a knife stuck in her heart.

_source.definition_text: to continue to support someone when they are having problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll stick by you whatever happens.; She was determined to stick by her husband.

_source.definition_text: to go past the surface or edge of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Paul's ears stick out a bit, don't they!; There was a handkerchief sticking out of his jacket pocket.; The seat was damaged and something was sticking out.

_source.definition_text: to limit yourself to doing or using one particular thing and not change to anything else

_source.definition_text: hard and difficult to bend

_source.definition_text: despite that

_source.definition_text: even better/worse

_source.definition_text: not moving

_source.definition_text: to encourage something to grow, develop or become active

_source.definition_text: to make someone excited and interested about something

_source.definition_text: something that makes something else happen, grow, or develop more

_source.definition_text: to mix food or liquid by moving a spoon round and round in it

_source.definition_text: to move slightly or make someone move slightly

_source.definition_text: to make someone feel a strong emotion

_source.definition_text: a short line of thread that is sewn through a piece of material
_source.learnerexamples_text: The stitches around the neck are coming undone.

_source.base_text: stir up sth or stir sth up

_source.definition_text: all the goods that are available in a shop

_source.definition_text: one of the small pieces of thread that is used to sew together a cut
_source.learnerexamples_text: She needed 50 stitches in her head.

_source.definition_text: available/not available in a shop

_source.definition_text: to think carefully about a situation before making a decision

_source.definition_text: to have something available for people to buy

_source.definition_text: a very thin piece of clothing that covers a woman's foot and leg
