_source.definition_text: the place where stocks and shares in companies are bought and sold
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stock markets around the world are reacting to news of the US president's announcement.; The second unlucky job was office workers whose business was related [to] the stock market in Korea.

_source.definition_text: pain in your stomach
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got terrible stomach ache. ; I'm sorry but I have to [see] my doctor because I've got stomach ache.

_source.definition_text: a hard, valuable substance that is often used in jewellery
_source.learnerexamples_text: precious stones; You know, that gold ring, with a little precious stone in the centre, meant a lot to me, because it belonged to my older sister, Giulia.

_source.definition_text: a hard, natural substance that is found in the ground
_source.learnerexamples_text: a stone wall/floor; a flight of stone steps; They cut enormous blocks of stone out of the hillside.; Some demonstrators were arrested for throwing stones at the police.; There are houses made of stone and wood.

_source.definition_text: the hard seed that is at the centre of some fruits
_source.learnerexamples_text: a cherry stone

_source.definition_text: a very short distance

_source.definition_text: to do everything that you can in order to achieve something or to find someone or something

_source.learnerexamples_text: a bar/kitchen/piano stool; a three-legged stool; Despite being provided with a machine which gives out hot and cold drinks, the cafeteria does not contain any table, stool or chair.

_source.definition_text: to not continue doing something that you were doing

_source.learnerexamples_text: Does this train stop at Cambridge?; The train stopped at the station.

_source.definition_text: to prevent someone from doing something or something from happening

_source.definition_text: a large shop where you can buy many different types of goods
_source.learnerexamples_text: a DIY/furniture store

_source.definition_text: a thin piece of hair, thread, rope, etc.

_source.definition_text: the ability to do things that need a lot of physical effort or power

_source.definition_text: a good quality or ability that makes someone or something effective

_source.definition_text: when you are brave or determined in difficult situations

_source.definition_text: to become stronger or make something become stronger

_source.definition_text: using or needing a lot of effort

_source.definition_text: when you say one part of a word more strongly than the rest

_source.definition_text: to say one part of a word more strongly than the rest

_source.definition_text: making you feel worried and not able to relax

_source.definition_text: worried and not able to relax

_source.definition_text: easily noticed

_source.definition_text: to understand something in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Whatever I say she'll take it the wrong way.

_source.definition_text: to deal with something as it happens, without planning for it
_source.learnerexamples_text: With an illness like this you just have to take every day as it comes.; We should, for once, put our [jea]lousy aside, start to appr[e]ciate what we have and take life as it comes.

_source.definition_text: to measure something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you taken her temperature?; The importance of absolute truth in keeping the laboratory records, in taking the temperature of the test animals, was "engraved" in our young minds.

_source.definition_text: If something takes a particular quality, you need that quality in order to be able to do it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It takes courage to challenge your manager.; It takes courage to give up a certain sense of security and face the unknown.

_source.definition_text: used when you think that what you say is probably true
_source.searchterms_text: i take it (that);i take it that;take;taken;takes;taking;took
_source.learnerexamples_text: I take it you're not coming with us.

_source.definition_text: to not like something that someone says or does
_source.learnerexamples_text: He doesn't take kindly to criticism.; His wife didn't take kindly to his lateness and immediately snarled at him as though [she was] a tigress snapping her claws in a cat-fight.

_source.base_text: take the law into your own hands
_source.definition_text: to do something illegal in order to punish someone because you know that the law will not punish that person
_source.searchterms_text: take;take the law into your own hands;taken;takes;taking;took
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police did nothing about the thefts, so they took the law into their own hands.; Therefore, locals are scared to death, leading to their taking the law into their own hands.

_source.definition_text: to be annoyed or insulted by something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took exception to being asked to sweep the floor.; I hope you will not take exception to my words, but I think that this course of action is rather foolish and illogical.

_source.definition_text: If you take criticism or advice to heart, you think about it seriously, often because it upsets you
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't take it to heart - he was only joking about your hair.; I hope you will take my advi[c]e to heart.

_source.definition_text: to do something important or difficult, especially after thinking about it for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're finally going to take the plunge and buy a house.; Being unable to stand this m[y]stery, I decided to take the plunge and follow him.

_source.definition_text: to start to develop and become more clear or certain
_source.learnerexamples_text: The project is slowly beginning to take shape.; It is high time that their dreams took shape!

_source.definition_text: to think carefully about a situation before making a decision
_source.searchterms_text: take;take stock (of sth);take stock of sth;taken;takes;taking;took
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to pause and take stock of what still needs doing.

_source.definition_text: to have a bad effect on someone or something, especially over a long period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: The stress was starting to take its toll on him. ; The famine has obviously taken its toll on him.

_source.base_text: take a turn for the better/worse
_source.definition_text: to become better or worse suddenly
_source.searchterms_text: take;take a turn for the better/worse;taken;takes;taking;took
_source.learnerexamples_text: The weather took a turn for the better.; Despite all the environmental problems it is up to us to prevent things from taking a turn for the worse.

_source.definition_text: to be similar to an older member of your family
_source.learnerexamples_text: Peter's very tall - he takes after his father.; They are nice kids and they take after my mother.

_source.definition_text: to walk through a building or visit a place with someone, showing them the most interesting or important parts
_source.searchterms_text: take;take sb around/round (sth/swh);take sb around/round (sth/swh) ;take sb around/round sth/swh;take sb around/round sth/swh
_source.learnerexamples_text: A guide took us around the museum.; Can you imagine how [pleased] we were with your kind offer to take us around Kyoto.

_source.base_text: take away sth or take sth away
_source.definition_text: to buy food in a shop or restaurant and eat it somewhere else
_source.searchterms_text: take;take away sth or take sth away
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is that to eat in or take away?

_source.base_text: take away sth or take sth away
_source.definition_text: to remove something
_source.searchterms_text: take;take away sth or take sth away
_source.learnerexamples_text: A waiter came to take our plates away.; Supermarkets are taking business away from small local shops.; The animals were taken away from their own habitat and will spend the rest of their lives in a complete[ly] different situation.

_source.base_text: take away sth or take sth away
_source.definition_text: to remove one number from another number
_source.searchterms_text: take;take away sth or take sth away
_source.learnerexamples_text: Four take away two is two.; If you take 4 away from 12 you get 8.

_source.base_text: take down sth or take sth down
_source.definition_text: to remove something that is on a wall or something that is temporary
_source.searchterms_text: take;take down sth or take sth down
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've taken the pictures down.; We were taking the tent down.; He was taking down a picture of Laura.

_source.base_text: take back sth or take sth back
_source.definition_text: to return something to the place you borrowed or bought it from
_source.searchterms_text: take;take back sth or take sth back
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is it too small? Take it back and get a refund.; I must take my library books back.; She took her scarf back and the phone was returned to [its]owner.

_source.base_text: take in sth or take sth in
_source.definition_text: to understand completely the meaning or importance of something
_source.searchterms_text: take;take in sth or take sth in
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had to read the letter twice before I could take it all in.; It was an interesting exhibition, but there was too much to take in at once.; Daddy was dead. They couldn't take it in.

_source.definition_text: to be deceived by someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: He told her a pack of lies and she was completely taken in by him.; He may be surprised, but he'll never be taken in.

_source.base_text: take off sth or take sth off
_source.definition_text: to remove something, especially clothes
_source.searchterms_text: take;take off sth or take sth off
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took off his clothes and got into the bath.; When I go shopping I like to buy pullovers, because when I buy trousers it waste[s] such a long time [trying them on and] tak[ing] them off.

_source.base_text: take off sth or take sth off
_source.definition_text: to spend time away from your work
_source.searchterms_text: take;take off sth or take sth off
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took off two weeks in September.; I will try to take some time off so I can come with you, but I don't know if that is possible.

_source.definition_text: If an aircraft takes off, it leaves the ground and begins to fly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The plane took off at 8.30 a.m.; The plane took off at 12.

_source.definition_text: to suddenly start to be successful or popular
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her singing career had just begun to take off.; The waitresses are quite rude. If you hire new ones, your sales will probably take off.

_source.base_text: take on sth or take sth on
_source.definition_text: to accept a particular job or responsibility
_source.searchterms_text: take;take on sth or take sth on
_source.learnerexamples_text: Make sure you don't take on too much work.; So I would take on the job if you changed the conditions.

_source.base_text: take on sb or take sb on
_source.definition_text: to employ someone
_source.searchterms_text: take;take on sb or take sb on
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was taken on as a laboratory assistant.; To find a job will be no problem, because I work in a coffee shop and I am sure that they will take you on.

_source.base_text: take out sb or take sb out
_source.definition_text: to go somewhere with someone and pay for them
_source.searchterms_text: take;take out sb or take sb out
_source.learnerexamples_text: My dad's taking the whole family out to the theatre.; Our boss took us out for a meal.; He was going to take me out to have lunch.

_source.base_text: take out sth or take sth out
_source.definition_text: to remove something from somewhere
_source.searchterms_text: take;take out sth or take sth out
_source.learnerexamples_text: He reached into his bag and took out a book.; I've had a tooth taken out.; He took out a knife and when he was about to kill me, I woke up.

_source.base_text: take out sth or take sth out
_source.definition_text: to get money from a bank
_source.searchterms_text: take;take out sth or take sth out
_source.learnerexamples_text: I took out £50 for the weekend.

_source.definition_text: to start doing a job or being responsible for something that another person did or had responsibility for before
_source.searchterms_text: take;take over (sth) or take (sth) over;take over sth or take sth over
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took over from the previous headmaster in February.; She took over as manager two weeks ago.; Colin Lamb has taken over responsibility for this project.; The pigs take over all the managerial work, supervise the other animals and finally [make] all the decisions.

_source.definition_text: to become more successful or powerful than something or someone else that is involved in the same type of activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: Italy has taken over from Spain as Europe's favourite holiday destination.; TV has taken over as the dominant activity for lesiure time, providing something for everyone.

_source.definition_text: to start to like someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: For some reason I just didn't take to her.; Most children take to her almost immediately.

_source.base_text: take up sth or take sth up
_source.definition_text: to fill an amount of space or time
_source.searchterms_text: take;take up sth or take sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: This desk takes up too much room.; The children take up most of my time.; It doesn't take up much space.

_source.definition_text: your opinion about a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's your take on the plan to close the library?

_source.base_text: take up sth or take sth up
_source.definition_text: to start doing a particular activity or job
_source.searchterms_text: take;take up sth or take sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's taken up cycling in his spare time; She's taken up the post of supervisor.; I played badminton a couple of years ago and I would very much like to take it up again.

_source.definition_text: when people reach agreement by letting each person have part of what they want
_source.learnerexamples_text: In every friendship there has to be some give and take.; This relationship must be a balance of give and take, and considered as the basis for that process of growth which should help a young person to reach a point of life in which he or she will be able to make his or her own choices, being aware of the consequences.

_source.definition_text: a meal that you buy in a restaurant or shop but eat at home, or a shop that sells this type of meal
_source.learnerexamples_text: a Chinese takeaway; After pubs or [a] night club, they go to the takeaway.

_source.definition_text: when a company gets control of another company
_source.learnerexamples_text: The company was involved in a takeover last year.; Everything has to be cheap and fast and there are mergers and takeovers all the time.

_source.definition_text: a story, especially one which is not true or is difficult to believe
_source.learnerexamples_text: He told the most amazing tales about his life in India.; She told me some tale about missing the bus to explain her lateness.; She knows everything about Prague's history and many local stories and tales.

_source.definition_text: a natural ability to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her talent for music showed at an early age.; his artistic talents; Some people have skills and talent and some do not.

_source.definition_text: with talent
_source.learnerexamples_text: a talented footballer/pianist; He is so talented, so smart and very polite to all.

_source.definition_text: to say things to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were just talking about Simon's new girlfriend. ;  The teacher's always telling him to stop talking. ;  It was nice talking to/with you. ; I like to talk with my friends and my teacher.

_source.definition_text: to discuss something with someone, often to try to find a solution to a disagreement
_source.learnerexamples_text: The two sides have agreed to talk. ; I decided to talk to him and try to solve the problem.

_source.definition_text: to discuss a particular subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't like to talk business over lunch.; [Do] not talk politics or sports with him (!)

_source.definition_text: to give a lecture on a subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: The next speaker will be talking about endangered insects.; We think that the best topic you could talk about is your latest book, you could try to develop the subject, explain to the members how to become a writer, from where and how do you get your ideas, and the subjects of your book.

_source.base_text: know what you are talking about
_source.definition_text: to understand a subject because of your experience
_source.searchterms_text: know what you are talking about;talk;talked;talking;talks
_source.learnerexamples_text: He doesn't know what he's talking about - he's never even been to Africa.; I beli[e]ve that you don't really know what you're talking about.

_source.definition_text: to think about or make plans to do something in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're talking about building a new fire station just up the road.; 7 years ago they were talking about building another block of flats in the park.

_source.definition_text: to persuade someone to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's managed to talk me into doing a ten-mile run at the weekend.; I'm just writing to talk you into taking part in an International Camp as a child-minder, together with me of course.

_source.base_text: talk sb out of sth/doing sth
_source.definition_text: to persuade someone not to do something
_source.searchterms_text: talk;talk sb out of sth/doing sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a ridiculous idea - I've tried to talk him out of it.; Hard as he tried, he seemed to be unable [to] talk his partner out of his silly conduct.

_source.base_text: talk over sth or talk sth over
_source.definition_text: to discuss something with someone, often to find out their opinion or to get advice before making a decision
_source.searchterms_text: talk;talk over sth or talk sth over
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm going to talk it over with Marty before I do anything about it.; She is important to me because I can go to her when I have a problem and we will talk it over until we find a solution.

_source.base_text: talk sth through or talk through sth
_source.definition_text: to discuss all the details of something, often before making a decision
_source.searchterms_text: talk;talk sth through or talk through sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm thinking of taking out a loan, but I need to talk it through with my accountant.; She is always there for me both as mother and as friend. Whenever I have got a problem, whatever it may be, we sit down and talk it through and she tells [me] her point of view.

_source.definition_text: a conversation between two people, often about a particular subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's going to have a talk with his parents and see what they think.; We had a talk and he told me about Bradley and what the band was like.

_source.definition_text: when someone speaks to a group of people about a particular subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: He gave a talk about/on his visit to Bolivia.; I went to a few interesting talks.; Dear Tom, It was very nice to hear from you again and it's really kind of you to give a talk to our Cinema Club.

_source.definition_text: when people talk about what might happen or be true
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's been some talk of possible job losses.; There's been a lot of talk about green issues lately.; It is also true that there has been a lot of talk about euthanasia.

_source.definition_text: A talkative person talks a lot.
_source.learnerexamples_text: My son is very talkative.; I would advise you to film the classrooms, maybe a conversation class, during which students will be more talkative and less shy.

_source.definition_text: formal meetings, especially between political leaders, to discuss a problem and to try to reach an agreement
_source.learnerexamples_text: peace talks; US officials are holding talks with EU leaders over trade.; It should be dealt with [through] peace talks and more active communications between the countries.

_source.definition_text: used for talking or asking about the height of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's six feet tall.; How tall are you?; She's much taller than me.; I [am] sell[ing] the dress because now I'm taller than two years ago and so it is small.

_source.definition_text: having a greater than average height
_source.learnerexamples_text: a tall girl; a tall building; He's tall with dark hair.; He is a tall man.

_source.definition_text: when your skin is brown from being in the sun
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had a lovely tan.; If you want to get a tan, this is the place to be.

_source.definition_text: Something which is tangible is real and can be seen, touched, or measured.
_source.learnerexamples_text: tangible benefits/evidence; This was a tangible physical pleasure that I have felt ever since, whether I sing along with accompaniment, or in a chorus.

_source.definition_text: a large container for storing liquid or gas
_source.learnerexamples_text: a water tank; a fuel/petrol tank; The heater is automatic and there is plenty of fuel oil in the tank.

_source.definition_text: a large, strong military vehicle with a gun on it which moves on wheels inside large metal belts
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tanks rolled into the city at dawn.; They were inside the university and they were transmit[t]ing [o]n a radio frequency when the tanks invaded from the main entrance.

_source.definition_text: the part at the end of a pipe which controls the flow of water
_source.learnerexamples_text: the hot/cold tap;  Turn the tap on/off. ; As soon as I got in, I turned the tap on and waited for hot water.

_source.definition_text: a gentle knock or touch, or the noise made by knocking something gently
_source.learnerexamples_text: I felt a tap on my shoulder.;  There was a tap at the door.; While she was teaching, I fel[l] asleep and two minute[s] later I felt a tap [o]n my back.

_source.definition_text: to knock or touch something gently
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tapped on the window to try to get her attention.; She lit up the whole stage when she danced, as she tapped her feet in r[h]ythm with the music.

_source.definition_text: something or someone that you attack, shoot at, try to hit, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a military target; I had four shots but I didn't even hit the target.; Any major airport or station is potentially a terrorist target.; Foreign businesses in the region have become a target for attacks.; Paul Rebere, a famous professional assassin, had been in that room for two hours now, waiting for his target to show up.

_source.definition_text: something that you intend to achieve
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you want to lose weight, you have to set yourself a target. ; My target is to be a professional tennis player but I need to work hard for it.

_source.definition_text: the person or thing that people are criticizing or blaming for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Recently she has been the target of a series of obscene phone calls.; People get nervous, the bus driver gets nervous and finally the interpreter becomes the target of passengers' complaints.

_source.definition_text: the group of people that a programme, product, etc. is aimed at
_source.learnerexamples_text: Children aren't really our target market.; The target audience will be students with intermediate- to upper-intermediate command of the language.

_source.definition_text: to aim advertising, criticism, or a product at someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: The products are targeted at people in their late twenties.; When considering that the programme is targeted at young people, we conclude that it should be funny and amusing.

_source.definition_text: a piece of work, especially something unpleasant or difficult
_source.learnerexamples_text: We usually ask interviewees to perform a few simple tasks on the computer just to test their aptitude.; The government now faces the difficult task of restructuring the entire health service.; To be honest, the task we were given was incredibly easy.

_source.definition_text: the flavour of a particular food in your mouth
_source.learnerexamples_text: I love the taste of garlic.; The soup had a slightly sour taste.; I don't know how old it is but I've gone there since I was a child and the taste of the food has never changed.

_source.definition_text: the particular things you like, such as styles of music, clothes, decoration, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: You have very good taste!;  I don't like his taste in music. ; She has very expensive tastes.; In my opinion, the variety of films you show cover all kinds of tastes.

_source.definition_text: a short experience of something different
_source.learnerexamples_text: This was my first taste of freedom.; Before you catch your plane, your group could visit our nice city and have a taste of our culture.

_source.definition_text: to be acceptable in a way that will not upset or anger people
_source.learnerexamples_text: His speech was in good taste.; I therefore t[h]ought that it would be in good taste to write about two of them.

_source.definition_text: the ability to experience different flavours in your mouth
_source.learnerexamples_text: When you've got a cold you often lose your sense of taste.

_source.definition_text: when you like or enjoy something
_source.searchterms_text: a taste for sth;taste;taste for sth;tastes
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've developed a bit of a taste for opera.; Over the years I've lost my taste for travel.; This diary was supposedly in the hands of Madame Isabella Costa, the widow of the late Christian Rudolph, a German actor with a taste for antiques.

_source.definition_text: to be unacceptable in a way that will upset or anger people
_source.learnerexamples_text: He told a joke about a plane crash which I thought was in rather poor taste.

_source.definition_text: to have a particular flavour
_source.learnerexamples_text: This sauce tastes strange.; The bread tastes of onions.; This coffee tastes like dishwater!; The food is very typical and tastes good.

_source.definition_text: to put food or drink in your mouth to find out what flavour it has
_source.learnerexamples_text: Taste this sauce and tell me if it needs any salt.; Whatever's this? I've never tasted anything like it.; Of course I tasted tequila, and I liked it very much.

_source.definition_text: ugly or without style
_source.learnerexamples_text: tasteless decorations; A quick look at a major contemporary sports competition: Athletes bulging with muscles that were clearly not earned naturally, massive on-site medical invasion, and a tasteless supply of cheap gadgets.

_source.definition_text: attractive and chosen for style and quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: a tasteful beige suit; They have refurbished the house in a very tasteful way, so you can still find some evidence of my grandmother once living there.

_source.definition_text: likely to upset or anger people
_source.learnerexamples_text: a tasteless joke

_source.definition_text: Food which is tasty has a good flavour and is nice to eat.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They do a very tasty breakfast.; The meal was really tasty.

_source.definition_text: having no flavour
_source.learnerexamples_text: The meat was dry and tasteless.; The canteen's food is tasteless and with almost the same menu every day.

_source.definition_text: to make someone pay a tax
_source.learnerexamples_text: Husbands and wives may be taxed independently/together.; For example, pol[l]uters should be taxed more heavily, [and] they should be fined.

_source.definition_text: money that you have to pay to the government from what you earn or when you buy things
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're putting up the tax on cigarettes.; Tax cuts are always popular.; What do you earn before/after tax?; I pay my taxes.; In Kish or Aeshm you can buy electric[al] device[s] cheaper than [in] your country, because you can buy all goods without tax.

_source.definition_text: a person who pays tax
_source.learnerexamples_text: Taxpayers deserve better services than this.; Unemployment is not only a problem [for] those without jobs but also one [for] those employed, at present, since taxpayers have to suffer the burden of providing [an] increasing number of people with unemployment with welfare [payments].

_source.definition_text: a car with a driver who you pay to take you somewhere
_source.learnerexamples_text: I took a taxi from the station to the hotel.; a taxi driver ; You can go there by bus, taxi or by light rail transit (LRT).

_source.definition_text: a hot drink that you make by pouring water onto dried leaves, or the leaves that you use to make this drink
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd love a cup of tea, please.; They have a selection of herbal teas.;  He likes strong/weak tea.; She likes tea and coffee.

_source.definition_text: a small afternoon meal of sandwiches, cakes, biscuits, etc. and tea to drink
_source.learnerexamples_text: They invited us for afternoon tea. ; Every afternoon they organized a tea for all the members.

_source.definition_text: to give lessons in a particular subject at a school, university, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She teaches chemistry.; He teaches English to foreign students.; Both her parents taught.; I'd like [to] learn English very w[e]ll, because I'd like [to] teach in the f[u]ture.

_source.definition_text: to show or explain to someone how to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: My dad taught me to drive. ;  Can you teach me how to knit? ; Dear students, Here is a book called "Cooking", it teaches you how to cook better.

_source.definition_text: to punish someone so that they will not behave badly again
_source.learnerexamples_text: The next time she's late, go without her. That should teach her a lesson.; He didn't want to hurt Diane just teach her a lesson.

_source.definition_text: If a situation teaches you something, it gives you new knowledge or helps you to understand something.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The whole experience taught him to be more careful with money. ; This situation taught me that I should keep my important things with m[e] all the time.

_source.definition_text: someone whose job is to teach in a school or college
_source.learnerexamples_text: a history/science teacher ; I love my teacher too.

_source.definition_text: the job of being a teacher
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's always wanted to go into teaching.; modern teaching methods; The teacher has a lot of experience behind him, I think nearly 20 years of teaching.

_source.definition_text: a group of people who play a sport or game together against another group of players
_source.learnerexamples_text: a basketball/hockey/netball team; I'll come to England to watch my favourite football team.

_source.definition_text: a group of people who work together to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: a management team ;  a team of advisers ; He told me he was part of the sound team of the band I went to see.

_source.definition_text: when a group of people work well together
_source.learnerexamples_text: We won't achieve anything without good teamwork.; Nowadays teamwork is a skill that is highly demanded by employers.

_source.definition_text: to pull something so that it comes apart or breaks, or to become damaged like this
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tore my skirt on the chair as I stood up.; You have to be very careful with books this old because the paper tends to tear very easily.; A couple of pages had been torn out of the book.; Although it's quite expensive, the clothes that I buy from there will not tear easily.

_source.definition_text: to remove something by pulling it quickly and violently
_source.searchterms_text: tear;tear sth out of/off/down etc;tear sth out of/off/down, etc.;tearing;tears;tore;torn
_source.learnerexamples_text: She tore his picture down from the wall.; If you can't bear seeing an ear being torn off from somebody's head, don't watch this video.

_source.definition_text: to be unable to decide between two choices
_source.searchterms_text: (be) torn between sth and sth;be torn between sth and sth;tear;tearing;tears;tore;torn
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm torn between the apple pie and the chocolate mousse.; As a conse[q]uence, we find ourselves torn between what we want to eat and what we feel we should be eating.

_source.base_text: tear apart sth or tear sth apart
_source.definition_text: to destroy something that was united, such as a country, family or political party
_source.searchterms_text: tear;tear apart sth or tear sth apart

_source.definition_text: used at the beginning of a sentence to show that you are pleased or grateful about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thankfully, nobody was hurt.; Thankfully, with the help of the government, a recycling centre was built nearby and so the rubbish littering the streets, as well as that being taken to the dump, was cut down by 60%.

_source.definition_text: thank you
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thanks for the advice.; Can you pass me that book? Thanks very much.; Hi, Thanks for your invite.

_source.definition_text: used to refuse an offer politely
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Would you like a drink?" "No thanks, I've just had one."

_source.definition_text: because of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I passed my driving test, thanks to the extra help my dad gave me.; Its thanks to Sandy that I heard about the job.

_source.definition_text: used to tell someone that you are grateful because they have given you something, done something for you or made a polite remark
_source.learnerexamples_text: That was a delicious lunch, thank you.; "Here's your coffee." "Thank you very much."; Thank you for my lovely birthday present.; "You look very nice in that dress." "Thank you."; I like pork meat very much. Thank you very much.

_source.definition_text: words or actions that show you are grateful or pleased about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They expressed their thanks to the organisers.; He wrote a letter of thanks to the hospital.; Give thanks also to your wife, we really ap[p]reciate[d] her marvellous cooking.

_source.definition_text: something that you say or do in order to show that you are grateful for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to say a big thank you to everyone for all their help.; The chocolates were a thank you for looking after the children.; I'm writing to say [a] very big thank you for our fantastic weekend.

_source.definition_text: said to politely accept or refuse something that has been offered to you
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Would you like some more cake?" "Yes, I will have a small piece, thank you."; "Do you need any help?" "No, thank you."

_source.definition_text: used to refer to something or someone that has already been talked about or seen
_source.learnerexamples_text: Where's that pen gone?; She lives in that house by the bus station.; I like that place be[cause] I like swim[m]ing in [the] sea.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to something or someone that can be seen or pointed to
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did you know that woman in the post office?; How much are those shoes?

_source.definition_text: because of or for this reason
_source.learnerexamples_text: The course is good in that it provides a very practical training.; Nowadays it is widely argued that professional sports are damaging to people's health in that they involve gruelling training sessions as an integral part of the occupation.

_source.definition_text: used to show that what you have just said is only an example from a larger group of things
_source.learnerexamples_text: They sell souvenirs, postcards, that sort of thing.; I also enjoy using new clothes for the first time, but I prefer buying other stuff like electronic devices or that sort of thing.

_source.definition_text: used after some verbs, nouns, and adjectives to introduce a new part of a sentence
_source.learnerexamples_text: She said (that) she'd collect it for me after work.; Is it true (that) she's gone back to teaching?; We'll be there at about 7.30, provided/providing (that) there's a suitable train.; It was so dark (that) I couldn't see anything.; It's true that I bought a mobile phone.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to something that can be seen or pointed to
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's that in the corner?; I'd like some of those.;  That looks heavy.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to something that has already been talked about or seen
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you do that, you'll be sorry.; I don't think you should put up with that.; You can't wear those to a wedding.; After that we have a break.

_source.definition_text: used to make a connection with an earlier statement
_source.learnerexamples_text: My usual train was cancelled. That's why I'm so late.; She tricked him, and that's what really upset him.; I decided [not to] play football any more! That is why I want to sell them.

_source.definition_text: used instead of 'who' or 'which' at the beginning of a relative clause
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you eaten all the cake that I made yesterday? ; I like my old-fashioned blue jeans, [and] the old shoes that I always use.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something is correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: You need to push the two pieces together. That's it.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something has ended
_source.learnerexamples_text: Well that's it then, we've finished.; I think that's it for now - I'll email you about the other project next week.; Well, that's it. Good luck and have a good time.

_source.definition_text: used for saying that other similar things are included or that the whole of a situation is considered
_source.learnerexamples_text: He told us about his school and all that.; We decided to stay in bed, with it being a holiday and all that.; I really enjoy shopping for clothes, but not only for clothes, also for things like earrings and all that!

_source.definition_text: used to express a reaction to something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I didn't know she'd been so ill. That's terrible.; Turn the engine on, then put the car in gear. That's right.; Smile for the camera. That's more like it.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to events or experiences in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: That was before we had a car.; That was when I went to live in Barcelona by myself in a student residence.

_source.definition_text: used to say that something has happened or a decision has been made and there is nothing more to say or do
_source.learnerexamples_text: I won't agree to it and that's that.; That's it and that's that!" as they say in the "Sorbits-advertis[e]ment" Bye!

_source.definition_text: used to correct something you have said or give more information about something
_source.searchterms_text: that;that is (to say);that is to say;thats;those
_source.learnerexamples_text: Everybody was at the meeting, well everyone except Jeanne, that is.; All in all, the students who participated in this programme were quite happy and had an enjoyable time there, except for some, that is.

_source.definition_text: different things which are not very important
_source.learnerexamples_text: "What are you doing today?" "Oh, just this and that."; He used to call his friends daily, chat about this and that, release the tension through silly jokes, even go out with them once in a while.

_source.definition_text: used when describing the size, amount, or state of something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's too young to walk that far.; It wasn't (all) that good.; My English isn't that bad, actually I have been taught English in school for six years.

_source.definition_text: used before nouns when only one of something exists
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you seen the Eiffel Tower?; What will happen in the future?; She's travelling round the world.; They live in the north of Spain.; Ed Koch was for many years the mayor of New York.

_source.definition_text: used before nouns to refer to particular things or people that have already been talked about or are already known
_source.learnerexamples_text: I bought a shirt and some shoes. The shirt was expensive, but the shoes weren't.; Could you pass the salt, please?; I'll pick you up at the station.; I really enjoyed the book I just read.; [On] Saturday she go[es] to the cinema.

_source.definition_text: used before superlatives and other words, such as 'first' or 'only' or numbers showing something's position in a list, which refer to only one thing or person
_source.learnerexamples_text: That was one of the best films I've ever seen.; What's the highest mountain in Europe?; I shall never forget the first time we met.; You're the fifth person to ask me that question.; The best present I have ever got was a car from my grandma.

_source.definition_text: used before numbers that refer to periods of ten years
_source.learnerexamples_text: the sixties; For example, people in the 1950s who didn't have computers are likely to have had difficulty in checking information, booking tickets, and communicating with each other.

_source.definition_text: used before some nouns that refer to place when you want to mention that type of place, without showing exactly which example of the place you mean
_source.learnerexamples_text: We spent all day at the beach.; Shall we go to the movies this evening?; I must go to the bank.; I like to go to swimming and go to the beach.

_source.definition_text: used instead of a possessive adjective such as 'your', 'her' or 'my'
_source.learnerexamples_text: He held her by the arm.; Where did I park the car?; There [are] a lot of people, and there are a lot of cars, so you would have problems find[ing] a place to park the car.

_source.definition_text: used before each of two adjectives or adverbs to show how one thing changes depending on another
_source.learnerexamples_text: The longer we live here, the more we like it. ; In many cases, the more things you learn, the less things you know.

_source.definition_text: a building with a stage where people go to watch plays
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Lyceum Theatre; You can visit the museum and the theatre because they are very ancient and beautiful.

_source.definition_text: the action or crime of stealing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: car theft; Unfortunately, we have had several thefts in the building recently.; So, who was [it] that made this [such a] perfectly-organised theft?

_source.definition_text: belonging to or relating to a group of people, animals, or things that have already been talked about
_source.learnerexamples_text: He gave them their coats.; Anyway, that's their problem.; In the afte[r]noon [he] goes with his wife [and] visits their friends.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to what belongs to or relates to a person when you want to avoid saying 'his' or 'her' or when you do not know if the person is male or female
_source.learnerexamples_text: One of the students has left their book behind.; So did this person give their name?

_source.definition_text: the things that belong or relate to a group of people, animals, or things that have already been talked about
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think she's a relation of theirs.; I think I left my cellphone in your house and it's very important for me [be]cause my mother and father can't give me theirs.

_source.definition_text: used after a verb or preposition to refer to a group of people, animals, or things that have already been talked about
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've lost my keys. I can't find them anywhere.; S[ay] hello [to] your wife and children. I will have presents for them.

_source.definition_text: used after a verb or preposition to refer to a person when you want to avoid saying 'him' or 'her' or when you do not know if the person is male or female
_source.learnerexamples_text: When each passenger arrives, we ask them to fill in a form.

_source.definition_text: the subject of a talk, book, film, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The theme of loss runs through most of his novels.; I think that the basic theme of the book is very original and the author has written lots of great novels.

_source.definition_text: the reflexive form of the pronoun 'they'
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did they enjoy themselves at the theatre?; They asked themselves where they had gone wrong.; They helped themselves [to] some fruit and sweets.

_source.definition_text: alone or without anyone else's help
_source.learnerexamples_text: The kids arranged the party all by themselves. ; They did the catering themselves.;  They've decided to run the club themselves. ; Most people in Hong Kong do not make brea[k]fast themselves. They like eat[ing] out.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize the pronoun 'they' or the particular group of people you are referring to
_source.learnerexamples_text: The staff themselves were unhappy with the decision. ; They themselves had no knowledge of what was happening.; Many times they think they themselves [have taken] part in a car race.

_source.definition_text: at that time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was working in the city then.; I'm having a day off on Friday - I could meet you then.; Give it to me next week - I won't have time to read it before/until then.; I'll phone you tomorrow - I should have the details by then.

_source.definition_text: so or because of that
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have a rest now, then you won't be so tired this evening.;  "My interview's at 9 o'clock." "You'll be catching an early train, then?" ; You can read the text from a song on [screen] and then you can sing the song.

_source.definition_text: next, or after something has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: She trained as a teacher and then became a lawyer. ; Let me finish this job, then we'll go.; I finish work at 7 o'clock, and then I want to have a bath. [A]fter that I will come.

_source.definition_text: used in order to add something to what you have just said
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got two essays to write and then my science project to finish. ; This is the standard model, then there's the luxury version which costs more.

_source.definition_text: If something happens now and then, it happens sometimes but not very often.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I love chocolate, but I only eat it now and then.; If you really love to have a snack now and then, try to eat fruit and vegetables, instead of sweets.

_source.definition_text: sometimes, but not often
_source.learnerexamples_text: We still meet up every now and then.; Each day choose 10 new words and learn them by heart. In a week you will have learned 70 new words, and in a year 3640, a lot of words. Please, do not forget to repeat them every now and then.

_source.definition_text: based on ideas rather than practical experience
_source.learnerexamples_text: This explanation is entirely theoretical.; And while we are lucky enough to be discussing this on a theoretical level, it is good to remember that for some people in the world, the lack of money leads to death on a daily basis.

_source.definition_text: based on the ideas that relate to a subject, not the practical uses of that subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: theoretical physics; Prof. Haken is the renowned head of one of the institutes of theoretical physics at the University of Stuttgart.

_source.definition_text: in a way that obeys some rules but is not likely
_source.learnerexamples_text: It is theoretically possible.; Already now the problem of hunger and starvation seems immense, though - theoretically - the earthly supplies of food are sufficient to feed the approximately 8,000,000,000 people who live on this planet.

_source.definition_text: an idea or set of ideas that is intended to explain something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Darwin's theory of evolution ; He has a theory that the hole was caused by a meteorite.; During his full time schedule, he worked [o]n his project about "relative theory".

_source.definition_text: If something is possible in theory, it should be possible, but often it does not happen in that way.
_source.learnerexamples_text: In theory, the journey ought to take three hours, but in practice it usually takes four because of roadworks.; To sum up, in theory you can find a lot of solutions [to] this problem, but in practi[c]e, actually some people who hunt without permission [aren't] punished.

_source.definition_text: the set of principles on which a subject is based
_source.learnerexamples_text: economic theory; Only after a few decades of further research did it become clear how many possible applications game theory actually has.

_source.definition_text: helping to cure a disease or improve your health
_source.learnerexamples_text: the therapeutic benefits of massage; The drink produced, tsikondia, is one of the ne[c]essary drinks for the cold nights of winter. It is also believed to have therapeutic effects on people's health.

_source.definition_text: helping you to feel happier and more relaxed
_source.learnerexamples_text: I find gardening very therapeutic.; Some people consider shopping therapeutic, much like a hobby.

_source.definition_text: someone whose job is to treat a particular type of mental or physical illness
_source.learnerexamples_text: a speech therapist; Teams [for athletes or swimmers] are built of: coach, physiologist, diet therapist, physiotherapist, doctor and massage therapist.

_source.definition_text: the work of treating mental or physical illness without using an operation
_source.learnerexamples_text: speech therapy; group therapy; In another way, I can say that books [are] the best stress management therapy; they are easy to carry wherever you go.

_source.definition_text: used when you are pointing or looking at something in order to make someone look in the same direction
_source.learnerexamples_text: Put them in that box there. ;  Your bag's over there by the door.

_source.definition_text: used to show that something exists or happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are three pubs in the village.; There's not much room in the back of the car.; There have been a lot of accidents on this road.; Is there any milk?; There are three swim[m]ing pools inside, for different people.

_source.definition_text: in or at a particular place
_source.learnerexamples_text: We live in York because my wife works there.;  I went to the party but I didn't know anyone there. ;  We'll never get there in time! ; The museum is closed today. We'll go there tomorrow.; There's that book you were looking for.

_source.definition_text: used when you are giving someone something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's some money for your cinema ticket. ;  "Could I have a pencil?" "Yes. There you are."

_source.definition_text: in several different places but without any pattern
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tall trees were growing here and there.; In the cinemas there were a few broken seats here and there.

_source.definition_text: at a particular point in a process or activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you want to play another game or do you want to stop there? ; I'll have to stop you there, we've run out of time.;  Keep on trying - you'll get there in the end. ; My misfortunes don't stop there.

_source.definition_text: after a particular amount, time, or event
_source.learnerexamples_text: Faxes cost £1.10p for the first page, and 70p for each page thereafter.; The unemployment rate thereafter started to rise yearly and reached its highest rate in March 1998 (approximately 5.5%).

_source.definition_text: as a result of a particular action or event
_source.learnerexamples_text: The new dam will improve the water supply and thereby reduce hunger and disease.; By interacting live with people from all over the world, you can use non-native languages on a daily basis and thereby help developing your foreign language skills.

_source.definition_text: for that reason
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were unable to get funding and therefore had to abandon the project.; [I] want to make it look more modern. Therefore, I've decided to get a CD player and some speakers.

_source.definition_text: a piece of equipment that measures the temperature of air or of your body
_source.learnerexamples_text: Keep the thermometer under your tongue.

_source.definition_text: plural of 'this'
_source.learnerexamples_text: These boxes are heavy.; Which apples would you like, the red ones or these?; I like walk[ing] around these lakes.

_source.definition_text: a long piece of writing that you do as part of an advanced university course
_source.learnerexamples_text: a doctoral thesis ; For me, this is an advantage because I need to have a lot of information for my doctoral thesis.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about the present time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Vegetarianism is very popular these days.; How are you these days?

_source.definition_text: a theory that is suggested and can then be argued with or agreed with
_source.learnerexamples_text: That is the central thesis of the book.; This thesis applies not only to music but, in my opinion, also to many other walks of life.

_source.definition_text: used as the subject of the verb when referring to a group of people, animals, or things that have already been talked about
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've known the Browns for years. They're very nice people.; Where are my glasses? They were on the table just now.; There are a lot of shops, restaurants and disco[s]. They are open all day and all night.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a person when you want to avoid saying 'he' or 'she' or when you do not know if the person is male or female
_source.learnerexamples_text: "There's someone on the phone for you." "What do they want?"

_source.definition_text: people in general
_source.learnerexamples_text: They say that breaking a mirror brings you seven years' bad luck. ; They say it is getting harder and harder to live without computers. But is it really true?

_source.definition_text: growing close together and in large amounts
_source.learnerexamples_text: thick forest; thick dark hair; I was looking [at] a land of moor, m[a]rsh, and thick forest.

_source.definition_text: Something that is thick is larger than usual between its opposite sides.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a thick rope; a thick layer of dust; She picked up a thick volume and began to read out loud.; a thick sweater/coat; The walls are two metres thick.

_source.definition_text: If you support or stay with someone through thick and thin, you always support or stay with them in easy and difficult situations.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She'd stuck by Neil through thick and thin.; Fortunately Carol was strong enough to stand by him through thick and thin and made her dearest husband give up drinking.

_source.definition_text: difficult to see through
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thick, black smoke was pouring out of the chimney.; We tried to walk [down] the stairs but the smoke was just getting thicker and thicker so we had to climb up on the roof.

_source.definition_text: quickly and in large numbers
_source.learnerexamples_text: Calls were coming in thick and fast by the end of the programme.

_source.definition_text: someone who steals things
_source.learnerexamples_text: a car thief; Thieves stole £120, 000 worth of computer equipment.; I watched three police officers trying to arrest the thieves but they fail[ed].

_source.definition_text: the top part of your leg above your knee
_source.learnerexamples_text: My thighs were aching after the climb.; Cycling is - among other things - very healthy, the heart starts pumping blood, your lungs get exercised and of course, you get smashing, sexy thighs.

_source.definition_text: Something that is thin is smaller than usual between its opposite sides.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a thin slice of meat; The walls are very thin.; a thin jacket ; Wear some thin clothes because it will be very hot.

_source.definition_text: If a feeling or explanation starts to wear thin, it becomes weaker or harder to accept.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've warned you several times about being late and my patience is wearing thin.; Hardly could they fight against others, when their own convictions had started to wear thin.

_source.definition_text: A thin person or animal has very little fat on their body.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's too thin.; Thin, hungry dogs roam the streets.; He's tall, thin and he has got black hair and black eyes.

_source.definition_text: If you support or stay with someone through thick and thin, you always support or stay with them in easy and difficult situations.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She'd stuck by Neil through thick and thin.; Fortunately Carol was strong enough to stand by him through thick and thin and made her dearest husband give up drinking.

_source.definition_text: to suddenly disappear in a mysterious way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was walking ahead of me on the path and then he just vanished into thin air.; The fact is that vacations are not problem-solving, and whatever one wants to leave behind does not vanish into thin air, it just lurks in the corner of your mind until the returning date.

_source.definition_text: your possessions or a set of objects
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll just get my things together and we can go.; All their things were destroyed in the fire.; Bring your swimming things if the weather's nice.; I like this place because the people are happy to work for example [on] a farm and they don't need a lot of things [to] be happy.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to something without saying its name
_source.learnerexamples_text: I need to get a few things in town.; How do I switch this thing off?; I don't eat sweet things.; I saw a few things I'd like to get.; Please tell me before [you come] what things you like to eat.

_source.definition_text: a fact or characteristic of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The thing I like about Carol is her sense of humour.; He told me a few things about the army.; Your information is correct but you left out one thing.; Yes, I bought a mobile phone. The thing that I like [about] it is that it is very useful and it has got lots of cool [new] things.

_source.definition_text: used instead of 'anything' in order to emphasize what you are saying
_source.learnerexamples_text: I haven't got a thing to wear.; Don't worry about a thing. I'll take care of it.; We tried to fish, but didn't catch a thing, not even a shoe!

_source.definition_text: used to refer to an activity or event
_source.learnerexamples_text: Meeting Nina was the best thing that's ever happened to me. ; I've got so many things to do I don't know where to start.; The thing I like best is the dancing.; My favo[u]rite thing is reading books!

_source.definition_text: the same
_source.learnerexamples_text: Training isn't the same thing as education.; I had lost my favourite watch. Now I have another watch but it isn't the same thing.

_source.definition_text: what is happening, especially in your life
_source.learnerexamples_text: How are things with you?; Things have been going very well recently.; How are things in your part of the world? Things are fine with me.

_source.definition_text: similar objects, activities or events
_source.learnerexamples_text: We eat a lot of Italian food - pizza, pasta, things like that.; I do a lot of football and running and things like that.

_source.definition_text: everything about a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: I just want to forget the whole thing.; The whole thing is ridiculous!; And, less than five minutes later, our mother knew the whole thing.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to an idea or comment
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't believe he would say such a thing!; I got mad and said "How dare you say such a thing."

_source.definition_text: used to say that there are other details or examples in addition to the ones you are mentioning
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's worth visiting the museum while you're here. There's an exhibition about Darwin and a good collection of paintings, among other things.; To go by tram or bus is a waste of time and travelling by car is - among other things - a waste of money.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that something does not exist
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's no such thing as ghosts!; But when I asked for these, I was told that no such thing existed and so the advertisement was once again proved wrong.

_source.definition_text: If it's a good thing that something happened, it is lucky or fortunate that it happened.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a good thing (that) we booked our tickets early.; I think it's a good thing that your parents [are going to] come, because [...] maybe it would make it easier for you to convince them to let you spend a week here during Xmas.

_source.definition_text: used to introduce an answer, comment or explanation
_source.searchterms_text: the thing is;the thing is...;thing;thing is...;things
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd love to go out tonight, but the thing is, I've got to finish my report.; The funny/strange thing is that we'd actually met before.; The thing is that on July 23rd I had not found any outfit that suited me yet, which made me feel desperate.

_source.definition_text: not anything
_source.learnerexamples_text: After the guests had gone, there wasn't a single thing left to eat.; I'm terribly sorry, but I hit it with my hand while trying to turn on the light: I wasn't able to see a single thing because it was pitch-dark all around.

_source.definition_text: the most important fact in a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: You're happy and that's the main thing. ; The main thing is to be happy and to love yourself.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to a person or animal when you are expressing your feelings towards them
_source.learnerexamples_text: You look tired, you poor thing. ;  He's spending three months in Barbados, lucky thing! ; When I go to the zoo I like to see them close by me, [and] look at them carefully; but at the same time I say: "Poor thing, I wouldn't like to be one of them."

_source.definition_text: used for saying that something is true in general if you think about all its aspects
_source.learnerexamples_text: The show was a great success, all things considered.; All things considered, it seems like "Kavanagh Catering Services" would be most suitable for the students.

_source.definition_text: the thing that is best, if you cannot have or do the thing you really want
_source.searchterms_text: next best thing;the next best thing;thing;things
_source.learnerexamples_text: Coaching football is the next best thing to playing.; For many working people, there is hardly time to cook and prepare your dinner, so the next best thing is to rush into a Macdonalds' or Burger King.

_source.definition_text: something that is certain to happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: Death is the one sure thing about life.; There is only one sure thing, we are not able to even imagine what we will be able to do in the future to get communicated.

_source.definition_text: to live, act or behave in the way you want to, without depending on other people
_source.learnerexamples_text: While he was away travelling, he pretty much did his own thing.; Their attitude only stimulated me to do "my own thing".
