_source.definition_text: as a result of something that is part of a series of events
_source.learnerexamples_text: This could result in the loss of certain species of fish and this in turn poses a serious threat to the fishing communities along the river banks.; This, in turn, enabled them to find jobs and become financially independent from their husbands.

_source.definition_text: to decide to stop having contact with someone or something, or to refuse to help someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: She turned her back on Hollywood and went to live in Florida.; She gets to learn that Olivia turned her back on her past and merged totally with India through her attraction to and sympathy for the Nawab.

_source.definition_text: to start to behave in a better way
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm not drinking any more - I've turned over a new leaf.; She promised to turn over a new leaf.

_source.base_text: turn your nose up at sth
_source.definition_text: to not accept something because you do not think it is good enough for you
_source.searchterms_text: tiurns;turn;turn your nose up at sth;turned;turning;turns
_source.learnerexamples_text: He turned his nose up at my offer of soup, saying he wanted a proper meal.; Moreover, she will not turn her nose up at anybody who might be considered less worthy than her.

_source.definition_text: to return in the direction you have come from, or to make someone do this
_source.learnerexamples_text: They had to turn back because of the bad weather.; As we were walking along we came across a river we couldn't pass, so we turned back.

_source.definition_text: be unable to sleep properly
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was tossing and turning for most of the night.; As she tossed and turned, unable to sleep, she started [going over] the events that had taken place before that evening.

_source.base_text: turn down sth or turn sth down
_source.definition_text: to reduce the level of sound or heat that something produces
_source.searchterms_text: turn;turn down sth or turn sth down;turn down sth or turn sth down
_source.learnerexamples_text: I asked him to turn down the heating.; Actually, as I know nothing about instruments, the only thing I could do was just turn the volume up and down.

_source.base_text: turn down sb/sth or turn sb/sth down
_source.definition_text: to refuse an offer or request
_source.searchterms_text: turn;turn down sb/sth or turn sb/sth down;turn down sb/sth or turn sb/sth down
_source.learnerexamples_text: He offered her a trip to Australia but she turned it/him down.; He turned down the job because it involved too much travelling.; I hope you don't turn down my invitation.

_source.definition_text: to change and become someone or something different, or to make someone or something do this
_source.searchterms_text: turn;turn (sb/sth) into sb/sth;turn (sb/sth) into sb/sth ;turn sb/sth into sb/sth;turn sb/sth into sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: The council was hoping to turn a children's home into a residence for adolescent girls.; The town turned from a small seaside resort into a major commercial centre when oil was discovered.; After midnight it turns into a club where you can dance [to] any kind of music.

_source.base_text: turn off sth or turn sth off
_source.definition_text: to move the switch on a machine, light, etc. so that it stops working, or to stop the supply of water, electricity, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: turn;turn off sth or turn sth off
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you turned the computer off?; He turned the TV off and started thinking about Tania.

_source.base_text: turn on sth or turn sth on
_source.definition_text: to move the switch on a machine, light, etc. so that it starts working, or to start the supply of water, electricity, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: turn;turn on sth or turn sth on
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ben turned the TV on.; I turned the computer on to check my e-mail box.

_source.definition_text: to happen in a particular way or to have a particular result, especially an unexpected one
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bomb warning turned out to be a false alarm.; How did the recipe turn out?; But unfortunately, my experience of seeing the musical show named "Over the Rainbow" in your Circle Theatre turned out to be rather disappointing.

_source.definition_text: to be known or discovered finally and surprisingly
_source.learnerexamples_text: It turned out that we'd been to the same school.; It turned out that Corey was organizing the concert and he asked me and three of my friends if we wanted to help.

_source.definition_text: If people turn out for an event, they go there.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thousands of people turned out to welcome the England team home.; Over 800 people turned out for the protest.; On top of that, there were more than 5,000 people who had turn[ed] out [for] the festival!

_source.definition_text: to ask a person or organization for help or support
_source.learnerexamples_text: Eventually she turned to her aunt for help.; Her family lived a long way away, and she had no one to turn to.; People were very friendly and there was always someone to turn to in case of trouble.

_source.definition_text: to arrive or appear somewhere
_source.searchterms_text: turn;turn up (somewhere);turn up (somewhere) ;turn up somewhere;turn up somewhere
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you think many people will turn up?; She turned up at my house late one night.; A few minutes later two security men turned up.

_source.base_text: turn up sth or turn sth up
_source.definition_text: to increase the level of sound or heat that a machine produces
_source.searchterms_text: turn;turn up sth or turn sth up
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you turn the heating up, please?; In addition to that, my neighbour is always organizing part[ie]s during the week. He stay[s up] with his friends till late and they turn the music up.

_source.definition_text: the time when you can or must do something, usually before or after someone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is it my turn yet?; It's your turn to do the washing up!; In this game if you give the wrong answer you have to miss a turn.; I really enjoy[ed] the holidays in England with you, so now it's my turn to invite you to come to my country, Peru.

_source.base_text: take turns or take it in turns
_source.definition_text: When a number of people take turns, they do the same thing one after the other.
_source.searchterms_text: take turns or take it in turns;turn;turns
_source.learnerexamples_text: We take turns to answer the phone.; They all took turns carrying the suitcase.; I suggest that each family takes turns to cut the grass once a week.

_source.definition_text: one after the other
_source.learnerexamples_text: Each of us collects the mail in turn.; He spoke to the three boys in turn.; We had two different teachers in the mornings and in the afternoons in turn.

_source.definition_text: as a result of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He took out more loans, which, in turn, led to more debt.; People will study for a range of degrees, which may imply that a lot of new jobs, mainly related to computers, will gain importance, which, in turn, could result in a better organization of the jobs and, as a consequence, a reduction in the unemployment rate.

_source.definition_text: a change in the direction in which you are moving or facing
_source.learnerexamples_text: a left/right turn; We got as far as the school, and there we had to make a right turn.

_source.base_text: take a turn for the better/worse
_source.definition_text: to become better or worse suddenly
_source.searchterms_text: take a turn for the better/worse;turn;turns
_source.learnerexamples_text: The weather took a turn for the better.; Despite all the environmental problems it is up to us to prevent things from taking a turn for the worse.

_source.definition_text: the start of a new century
_source.searchterms_text: the turn of the century;turn;turn of the century;turns
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was born at the turn of the century.

_source.definition_text: the way in which a situation develops, especially a sudden or unexpected change
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were all shocked by this tragic turn of events.; She was not prepared for such an unexpected turn of events!

_source.definition_text: a corner where one road meets another
_source.learnerexamples_text: Take the first turning on the left.; Then, take the second turning on the left and go along that road until you get to the roundabout.

_source.definition_text: the amount of business that a company does in a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Large supermarkets have a high turnover of inventory.; For instance, clothes shops in Barcelona expect a big turnover in August because of the amount of tourists that will visit the city.

_source.definition_text: the rate at which workers leave an organization and new workers join it
_source.learnerexamples_text: The high turnover among daycare workers is an ongoing problem.; What used to amaze me was the very low staff turnover and I wondered what the secret was.

_source.definition_text: someone who teaches one person or a very small group of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: a private tutor; We could afford t[rips] abroad, modern labour-saving devices and private tutors.

_source.definition_text: television
_source.learnerexamples_text: What's on TV tonight?; You watch too much TV!; We ate in front of the TV.; TV personalities; She watch[e]s TV every evening.

_source.definition_text: the number 20
_source.learnerexamples_text: nineteen, twenty, twenty-one; space for twenty people; I think we were twenty people.

_source.definition_text: the number 12
_source.learnerexamples_text: ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen; a twelve-seater minibus; We can start at twelve o'clock.

_source.definition_text: to be aged between 20 and 29
_source.searchterms_text: (be) in your twenties;be in your twenties;twenty
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most of the staff are in their twenties.; Teenagers and people in their twenties will enjoy themselves in the atmosphere of the rock-café.

_source.definition_text: the years from 1920-1929
_source.learnerexamples_text: I love the fashions of the twenties.; You can find the car [that] won the first car race in the world, [and] lost movies from the twenties.

_source.definition_text: two times
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've already asked him twice.; You need to take two tablets twice daily.; There are twice as many houses in this area as there used to be.; The state is at least twice as big as England.; He's twice her size.

_source.definition_text: to carefully consider whether what you are planning is a good idea
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd think twice about spending so much money on one thing, if I were you.; Now I will think twice before I buy your paper again.

_source.definition_text: to do something immediately, without considering whether it is a good idea
_source.learnerexamples_text: When he asked me out, I didn't think twice!; Your advertisement seemed very convincing and as I intended to travel to exotic locations I did not think twice.

_source.definition_text: one of two children who are born to the same mother at the same time
_source.learnerexamples_text: My sister has twin sons.; a twin sister; I have twin cousins there and I love them [very] much.

_source.definition_text: to turn something in a circle using your hand
_source.learnerexamples_text: She sat there nervously twisting the ring around on her finger.

_source.definition_text: to turn part of your body to face a different direction
_source.learnerexamples_text: She twisted her head so she could see what was happening.; Through the right wing of the car I could [see] his eyes glitter like two flawless diamonds as he twisted his neck slightly from time to time to beam at me.

_source.definition_text: If you twist a part of your body, such as your knee, you injure it by turning it suddenly.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tripped and twisted my ankle.; The worst part is, that we had an older lady within our group who had twisted her an[k]le so she was somewhat disabled at the time.

_source.definition_text: an unexpected change in a situation or in a story
_source.learnerexamples_text: His arrest was just the latest twist in the story of his life.; The plot takes several twists and turns till the conclusion which sums up the contents of the film.

_source.definition_text: to change the meaning of something so that it fits what you want it to mean
_source.learnerexamples_text: You keep twisting my words - that's not what I meant at all!; Some members of the board twisted her words.

_source.definition_text: bent so that the original shape is changed or destroyed
_source.learnerexamples_text: a twisted tree trunk; a twisted ankle; twisted metal; When I got there, a very nice nurse told me that I['ve] got a twisted ankle and I [can]not walk for one week!

_source.definition_text: strange and slightly unpleasant or cruel
_source.learnerexamples_text: He'd become bitter and twisted.; Sometimes her morality seems a little twisted.

_source.definition_text: the number 2
_source.learnerexamples_text: They've got two houses.; I spent two years in Ethiopia.; It's two o'clock.; He'll be two (years old) in February.; I go to college two days per week.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about a small number of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I may bring a friend or two.; I also refused to eat any meal a day or two before the test but my mother made me, she said I needed the energy to be happy and celebrate afterwards.

_source.definition_text: to have difficulty making a decision
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm in two minds about accepting his offer.; If you are in two minds about having to share your room with someone else, there you can easily rent a studio apartment close to the college, which is situated in the centre of the city.

_source.definition_text: a person or thing that is part of a group of people or things that have similar qualities, or a group of people or things that have similar qualities
_source.learnerexamples_text: What type of house do they live in?; They sell over 50 different types of cheese.; Illnesses of this type are very common in children.; They sell dried flowers and baskets and that type of thing.; My favourite type of music is RAP.

_source.definition_text: to not be the type of person that someone thinks is attractive
_source.learnerexamples_text: I like Bertrand but he's not really my type.; It's true that he wasn't handsome, not at all the type she had used to prefer, but when he smiled, that wonderful smile that made his eyes sparkle, she realised, quite dazzled, that he was beautiful.

_source.definition_text: someone who has particular qualities or interests
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's the outdoor type.; Usually these adults are the hardworking type and save money for the future.

_source.definition_text: having all the qualities you expect a particular person, object, place, etc to have
_source.learnerexamples_text: I must look like the typical tourist with my shorts and my camera.; This sort of hot and spicy food is very typical of the food in the south of the country.; Typical symptoms would include severe headaches, vomiting and dizziness.; This film is a typical horror film.

_source.definition_text: to write something using a keyboard
_source.learnerexamples_text: She asked me to type a couple of letters.; He can type very quickly.; I was typing away into the early hours of the morning just to get the thing finished.; I'm typing this email to ask your permission to borrow your bicycle.

_source.definition_text: used for saying what usually happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: Typically, a doctor will see about thirty patients a day.; Tickets for such events will typically cost around thirty dollars.; The climate of Brazil is typically tropical so the weather is gorgeous.

_source.definition_text: in a way that shows all the characteristics that you would expect from the stated person, thing or group
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has that reserve and slight coldness of manner which is typically English.; Paul, in typically rude fashion, told him he was talking rubbish.; Your wife really made an effort to cook me typically English dishes.

_source.definition_text: a thick, round piece of rubber filled with air, that fits around a wheel
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got a flat tyre.; I keep a spare tyre in the back of the car.; We went by car [and] the trip was lots of fun - the only thing that went wrong was we had two flat tyres.

_source.definition_text: better, greater or worse than all similar things
_source.learnerexamples_text: Climbing Mount Everest is the ultimate challenge.; the ultimate luxury cruise; For me, rats are the ultimate horror.; Being on the road is always better than the arrival, so this journey would be the ultimate journey for me as well.

_source.definition_text: final or most important
_source.learnerexamples_text: the ultimate aim/solution; The ultimate aim [when] I joined your tour was to meet one of my friends in St Andrews.

_source.definition_text: finally, after a series of things have happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: Everything will ultimately depend on what is said at the meeting with the directors next week.; Ultimately, of course, he'd like to have his own business but that won't be for some time.; Ultimately, it leads to a lot of d[i]seases and early death.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize the most important fact in a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ultimately, he'll have to decide.; Ultimately, that is why we are influenced by other people's personalities.

_source.definition_text: a thing that you hold above your head to keep yourself dry when it is raining
_source.learnerexamples_text: I felt a few spots of rain so I put my umbrella up.; I left my umbrella on the bus yesterday.; I got some books, a bottle of wine and an umbrella.

_source.definition_text: to not be able to do something
_source.searchterms_text: be unable to do sth;be unable to do sth ;unable
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were unable to contact him at the time.; I was just shocked, and unable to speak at all, or to breathe.

_source.definition_text: too bad to be allowed to continue
_source.learnerexamples_text: The water contains unacceptable levels of pollution.; I find that sort of behaviour completely unacceptable.; The unions have described the latest pay offer as unacceptable.; So I waited for 45 minutes until the show started. [T]hat is an unacceptable delay.

_source.definition_text: not changed by something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Smaller colleges will be unaffected by the new regulations.; Only a genius could stay unaffected by such idolatry.

_source.definition_text: agreed by everyone
_source.learnerexamples_text: The jury was unanimous in finding him guilty.; Having spoken to neighbours, we reached a unanimous decision that the route of the aircraft should be changed im[m]ediately so that they no longer disrupt our lives.

_source.definition_text: with agreement from everyone
_source.learnerexamples_text: We agreed unanimously that he was the best candidate.; While it is true that there are quite a few opposing theories about losing weight, doctors unanimously agree that a hedonistic approach to eating can lead to unpleasant health issues like obesity.

_source.definition_text: too expensive for people to be able to buy
_source.learnerexamples_text: Such clothes are unaffordable for most people.; £5 per session is obviously unaffordable for students.

_source.definition_text: not able to be achieved
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unattainable ideal; Some economists think that full employment in Europe is an unattainable goal.; The ability to permanently record thought opened new dimensions to fields like philosophy, poetry and literature, enabling them to reach a degree of complexity, creativity and longevity unattainable by previous technologies.

_source.definition_text: not interesting or useful
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unattractive proposition; In our opinion, despite the friendly atmosphere of our club's meetings we find them very unattractive and rather "dull".

_source.definition_text: not beautiful or nice to look at
_source.learnerexamples_text: I felt old and unattractive.; Their new building is very unattractive.; This information is useful for [a person] who thinks his/her body is unattractive.

_source.definition_text: impossible to buy or get
_source.learnerexamples_text: The book is unavailable in Britain.; The third point was that the discount[ed] tickets were unavailable.

_source.definition_text: impossible to avoid or prevent
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unavoidable delay; Being aware of the two proposals our local government is considering in order to solve the apparently unavoidable matter of traffic in our beloved city, I feel compelled to offer my views on such a delicate subject.

_source.definition_text: not able to talk to someone or meet them, especially because you are doing other things
_source.learnerexamples_text: The manager was unavailable for comment.; Furthermore, a role-model for the younger generation could be the famous tennis player Joe Hill, who unfortunately is unavailable to give an interview.

_source.definition_text: not knowing about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was unaware that the police were watching him.; I was quite unaware of the problem.; Although you may be an expert in one subject you can be unaware [of] some basics in others.

_source.definition_text: in a way that could not be avoided or prevented
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was unavoidably delayed.; Even if you go abroad on your own, you unavoidably meet people [from] your country or speaking your native language.

_source.definition_text: slightly mentally ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: After his death, she became slightly unbalanced.; Many homeless people are mentally unbalanced, some are addicted to chemical substances.

_source.definition_text: false and not fair
_source.learnerexamples_text: He gave an unbalanced view of the situation.; I think that if a school measures a child solely by his or her academic success, it will be an unbalanced and narrow-minded method to measure a child and his or her ability as a whole person.

_source.definition_text: too painful or unpleasant for you to continue to experience
_source.learnerexamples_text: The heat was almost unbearable.; Life can be very difficult, almost unbearable sometimes.

_source.definition_text: extremely bad or good and making you feel surprised
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's unbelievable how lucky she's been.; You've had such bad luck - it's unbelievable.; The food is unbelievable and I'm sure you'll love it.

_source.definition_text: not probable and difficult to believe
_source.learnerexamples_text: I found most of the characters in the play totally unbelievable.; They made up unbelievable stories which almost made them cry in the end.

_source.definition_text: able to judge fairly because you are not influenced by your own opinions
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was able to give me some unbiased advice.; If you take into consideration only certain subjects, you are likely to end up despising other fields of knowledge, whereas the main point of education is to give an unbiased view of our own and foreign cultures.

_source.definition_text: not sure or not able to decide about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's uncertain whether to go to New Zealand or not.; Bridie was uncertain about meeting him.; [There are] things that I am uncertain about, and [that I would] be grateful if you c[ould] explain.

_source.definition_text: not known or fixed, or not completely certain
_source.learnerexamples_text: New arrivals face an uncertain future.; The political outlook is still uncertain.; Please do not bother posting them since we do not have a zip code where I live, and they might get lost with our uncertain Post Service.

_source.definition_text: in a direct and often angry way
_source.learnerexamples_text: I told him to go away in no uncertain terms.; Intellectuals are used to saying in no uncertain terms that money represents the bad side of the sport.

_source.definition_text: staying the same
_source.learnerexamples_text: The area has remained virtually unchanged in fifty years.; All the big and small things which defin[e] people's personal environment will be left nearly unchanged - the furniture, the pictures on the wall.... I suppose our future homes will be a mix of new technologies and good old tradition.

_source.definition_text: the state of being uncertain
_source.learnerexamples_text: There was a lot of uncertainty about whether or not he would attend the event.; The shortages of almost everything we have to face and cope with have made our lives full of uncertainty and helplessness, but on the other hand they released in some Poles enormous energy, in the effort to support their families and provide them with food, clothing and fuel.

_source.definition_text: the brother of your mother or father, or the husband of your aunt
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've got an uncle who lives there.; Did you bring me a present, Uncle Jack?; My uncle gave me the best present.

_source.definition_text: not easy to understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: The situation at the moment is unclear.; It's unclear what actually happened that night.; It's unclear whether he arrived before or after the shot was fired.; If something is unclear please give me a call.

_source.definition_text: If you are unclear about something, you are not certain about it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm unclear about a couple of points in your proposal - could you go over them again?

_source.definition_text: not feeling comfortable and pleasant, or not making you feel comfortable and pleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've eaten so much, I'm really quite uncomfortable.; These shoes are really uncomfortable.; The thing[s] I most hate wearing are shirts, I think they're very uncomfortable.

_source.definition_text: slightly embarrassed, or making you feel slightly embarrassed
_source.learnerexamples_text: an uncomfortable silence; It is interesting how people get embar[r]assed and uncomfortable when they have to face an English speech.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is not comfortable or pleasant
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was warm but not uncomfortably so.; I saw faces I see every day, but in uncomfortably long dresses and with starched white collars, I saw their effort to look nice, attractive and not to disturb the rules set by the society of their time.

_source.definition_text: done or given without any limits and without asking for anything for yourself
_source.learnerexamples_text: unconditional love ; But I am of [the] firm conviction that you cannot love [a child] too much, and this unconditional love does not include any rod, in both [the] literal and figurative sense of the word.

_source.definition_text: unusual
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's not uncommon for people to become ill when they travel.; NEW TRENDS: Vegetarian food is not uncommon nowadays.

_source.definition_text: An unconscious thought or feeling is one that you do not know you have.
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unconscious fear; Maybe it was her strict upbringing that had left her with an unconscious need to rebel, and that in turn caused her to be drawn to this rowdy young man.

_source.definition_text: in a state as though you are sleeping, for example because you have been hit on the head
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was hit on the head by a stone and knocked unconscious.; In the morning, Mrs Crozier went to visit Miss Appleford in number 42 only to find her lying on the floor unconscious.

_source.definition_text: If you do something unconsciously, you do it without knowing that you are doing it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was nodding her head, unconsciously urging him on.; We do this, for instance, when we buy a larger - and more expensive - car than we need for commuting to work, because we unconsciously want to be like the actors that drive them in films.

_source.definition_text: doing things in a way that is different from most people
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unconventional lifestyle; CHILDREN'S STORIES This event was successful and satisfied the kids since the heroes were exhilarating, with amazingly unconventional behaviour.

_source.definition_text: a noun which does not have a plural form and cannot be used with 'a' or 'one'
_source.learnerexamples_text: 'Information' and 'furniture' are uncountable nouns.

_source.definition_text: to discover something that had been secret or hidden
_source.learnerexamples_text: The inspectors uncovered evidence of corruption. ; Sitting in a restaurant and discussing provisions of the contract you will find much easier and feel happier than [just sitting] and look[ing] at [an] enormous number of clauses, trying unsuccessfuly to uncover what your client really thought when he wrote this or that.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is almost certainly true
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is undeniably the best student we have ever had.; Sport has undeniably become part of contemporary popular culture.

_source.definition_text: certainly true
_source.learnerexamples_text: an undeniable fact; It is undeniable that he has made a positive contribution to [the] history of my country.

_source.definition_text: below something, or below the surface of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He hid under the bed.; They were standing under a tree.; She was holding a file under her arm.;  She pushed her bag under the table.;  He could only keep his head under the water for a few seconds.

_source.definition_text: less than a number, amount, or age
_source.learnerexamples_text: All items cost/are under a pound.; You can buy the whole set of DVDs for just under £30.; The discount applies only to children under (the age of) ten.; Under-5s get in free.; If you get under 50%, you've failed the exam.

_source.definition_text: to think or understand a particular stated thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was under the impression (that) you didn't get on too well.; He was under the mistaken impression (that) you were married.; I am under the impression that people generally exercise a little, but if they eat the wrong food every day, it won't help.

_source.definition_text: in a particular state or condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: The President is under pressure to resign. ; Under no circumstances should the festival become too specialized.; I am used to working under pressure.

_source.definition_text: being affected by something at the present time
_source.learnerexamples_text: The town is once again under attack.; The cause of the fire is still under investigation.;  A new 16-screen cinema is under construction.;  Several different plans are under discussion.; We are working hard to get the situation under control.

_source.definition_text: If you say something under your breath, you say it very quietly so that other people cannot hear it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was muttering curses under his breath.; "We must have taken a wrong turn somewhere..." he kept muttering under his breath.

_source.definition_text: Australia, or in Australia
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was born in Scotland, but she's been living down under for 22 years.; Last year a good friend of mine and I went to Australia. After a couple of days of doing some sightseeing and sunbathing on bea[u]tiful sandy beaches, we decided that we need[ed] to get something more out of our stay down under.

_source.definition_text: If something bad happens under your nose, it happens close to you but you do not notice it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were stealing money from under my nose.; You will be surprised that there was something right under your nose that you could not live without.

_source.definition_text: to be already happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: Building work is already under way.; Sociologists are well-aware of the fact and experiments are under way to counterbalance these disadvantages.

_source.definition_text: not developed enough
_source.learnerexamples_text: They are working in underdeveloped parts of the city.; A shift of focus in underdeveloped and developing states' economic and social policies is vital to overcoming the problems which cause homelessness.

_source.definition_text: to feel ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm feeling a bit under the weather this morning.; Ann was a bit under the weather, [and] she felt quite lonely in her big flat.

_source.definition_text: to not understand how powerful or clever someone is
_source.learnerexamples_text: I thought it would be an easy game but I had underestimated my opponent.; At the beginning she will ask you many questions about yourself. But don't underestimate Ms Bates (that's her name).

_source.definition_text: to fail to understand how large, strong, or important something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many people underestimate the cost of owning a car.; We shouldn't underestimate the part that exercise plays in good health.; The report also seemed to underestimate the number of people that had attended.

_source.definition_text: to experience something, especially a change or medical treatment
_source.learnerexamples_text: The country is currently undergoing major political change.; He is undergoing surgery for a heart problem.; Nowadays, my country is undergoing a very difficult financial and social situation.

_source.definition_text: the system of trains that is built under London
_source.learnerexamples_text: the London Underground; Take the underground to Green Park.; Take the underground [to] Camden Town station.

_source.definition_text: below the surface of the ground
_source.learnerexamples_text: an underground cave/passage; Some animals, such as moles, live underground.; As it was expected, Harry was seen, and then he went underground t[h]rough a tunnel which crossed from the inner city to the Russian zone.

_source.definition_text: below the surface of the ground
_source.learnerexamples_text: an underground cave/passage; Some animals, such as moles, live underground.; As it was expected, Harry was seen, and then he went underground t[h]rough a tunnel which crossed from the inner city to the Russian zone.

_source.definition_text: to draw a line under a word or sentence, especially in order to show its importance
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the technical words have been underlined in red.; And, another disadvantage in my opinion is that is more difficult to underline or to write some notes if you study from the computer.

_source.definition_text: to emphasize the truth or importance of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The report underlines the need for more teachers in schools.; It is true that museums do not show the past as well as they could, but we must underline that they are always good enough if we are really interested in knowing about our past.

_source.definition_text: An underlying reason or problem is the real reason or problem, although it is not obvious.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to look at the underlying reasons for ill health. ; The underlying reason is of course a lurking threat of death and decay, which keeps sc[ie]ntists investigating new methods to postpone the age of death.

_source.definition_text: to make someone less confident or make something weaker
_source.learnerexamples_text: A series of scandals have undermined people's confidence in the government.; All this doesn't undermine the importance of charity workers and entertainers in our work for the greater good.

_source.definition_text: under or below something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The tunnel goes right underneath the city.; They found a bomb underneath the car.; She was dressed like a princess, after spending the whole day looking for an appropriate dress, which she finally managed to find underneath her bed.

_source.definition_text: under or below
_source.learnerexamples_text: Florian was wearing a dark jacket with a red shirt underneath.; The rock was about 70m high and there was water underneath.

_source.definition_text: not earning enough for your work
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her staff felt they were underpaid.; They claim that they are overworked and underpaid (it's [the] usual reason for striking, isn't it?)

_source.definition_text: a piece of underwear that covers the area between your waist and the top of your legs
_source.learnerexamples_text: I need some new underpants.; Was that woman me, standing there in those ugly-looking underpants, but with a smart sports bra, with everybody laughing around her?

_source.definition_text: to know the meaning of something that someone says
_source.learnerexamples_text: She explained the whole idea again, but I still didn't understand.;  I don't understand half of what he says.; Is there anyone here who understands Arabic?; My teacher help[s] me when I don't understand.

_source.definition_text: to know why or how something happens or works, or how to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We still don't fully understand how the brain works.; I don't understand why my computer crashes so often.; The teacher expla[i]ned her plan for teaching and we understood how to plan our time.

_source.definition_text: to know how someone feels or why they behave in a particular way
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't understand James sometimes.; I understand why she's so angry.; Maybe now you can understand why I hate shopping. kisses,

_source.definition_text: used to say that you believe something is true because someone has told you it is
_source.learnerexamples_text: I understand that the school is due to close next year.; I understand that the job entails enterta[in]ing people.

_source.definition_text: to say something to someone in a way that they understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had a little difficulty making myself understood.; (Find enclosed a paper slip on which I have written a destination, number of tickets, etc., in the German language - use it just in case you can't make yourselves understood.)

_source.definition_text: An understandable feeling or action is one that you would expect in that particular situation.
_source.learnerexamples_text: "I still feel really angry about it." "That's understandable."; Their refusal to help is perfectly/completely understandable, considering the circumstances.; I guess they wouldn't give me permission [to stay] at a female friend's home, but that's understandable.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is expected in a particular situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's understandably upset.; Furthermore, the use of the computer system caused long waiting times because everyone wanted - understandably - to find out more about suitable working opportunities.

_source.definition_text: knowledge about a subject, situation, etc. or about how something works
_source.learnerexamples_text: She doesn't have any understanding of politics.; My understanding of the agreement is that they will pay £50, 000 over two years.; It was my understanding that she would come alone.; It was my understanding that discounts were available on the tickets, as the advertisement showed, but there were no discounts.

_source.definition_text: sympathy
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thank you for your understanding - I do appreciate it.; Thank you for your understanding.

_source.definition_text: an informal agreement between two people
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have an understanding that we don't discuss the subject in front of his mother.

_source.definition_text: showing sympathy for someone's problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: Fortunately, my boss is very understanding.; They are famous, but they need to be alone sometimes. I think [the] media must be more understanding.

_source.definition_text: to do or begin to do something, especially something that will take a long time or be difficult
_source.learnerexamples_text: Students are required to undertake simple experiments.; To achieve it the above mentioned steps should be undertaken.

_source.definition_text: to promise to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She undertook to organize the meeting.

_source.definition_text: a difficult or important piece of work, especially one that takes a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Building your own house is a major undertaking.; While such an undertaking is most advisable, I should like to point out that there may be drawbacks.

_source.definition_text: under the surface of water
_source.learnerexamples_text: an underwater camera; Seals can hear very well underwater.; If you have diving equipment, you will spend a very good time underwater.

_source.definition_text: If something is underway, it is happening.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Economic recovery is already underway.; The weather was beautif[u]l and the sun sh[one] but as soon as I was underway, the weather turned on us and grew worse with every step.

_source.definition_text: to begin
_source.learnerexamples_text: The film festival gets underway on 11th July.

_source.definition_text: the clothes that you wear next to your skin, under your other clothes
_source.learnerexamples_text: They sell a wide range of underwear.; If I see some nice underwear, I will buy it too.

_source.definition_text: Something that is undesirable is not wanted because it is bad or unpleasant.
_source.learnerexamples_text: an undesirable influence; In this day and age, man is inextricably interwoven with the undesirable environmental damage, and the problems as far as the environment is concerned have generated a great deal of heated debate.

_source.definition_text: Undeveloped land has no buildings on it and is not used for anything.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The site is still undeveloped.; The Town Council decided to take measures in order to benefit our area, which has remained undeveloped for the last five years.

_source.definition_text: to open something that is tied or fastened
_source.learnerexamples_text: I took off my hat and undid my coat.;  Can you undo this knot for me?; Can someone help me to undo my seat belt?

_source.definition_text: to make a computer get rid of the last change you made to a document and make it the way it was before
_source.learnerexamples_text: You need to undo that change.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that something is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: Stress has undoubtedly contributed to her illness.; This trip will undoubtedly be a wonderful experience.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize that something is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: The project was an undoubted success. ;  her undoubted ability/talent ; Yet, in spite of the undoubted improvements to life progress has brought about, there are still those who condemn it.

_source.definition_text: not wearing any clothes
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got undressed and went to bed.; We got undressed quicker than ever and ran into the waterfall.

_source.definition_text: to remove your clothes or someone else's clothes
_source.learnerexamples_text: She undressed the children and put them to bed.; The chair is for my clothes when I undress.

_source.definition_text: more than is necessary
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't want to cause undue alarm.; On the other hand a badly [organised] holiday can put undue stress on the traveller.

_source.definition_text: worried because you think something bad might happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: I feel a bit uneasy about her travelling alone.; Anyway I was getting uneasy because of all that silence, so I began to sing.

_source.definition_text: not having a job that provides money
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's been unemployed for over a year.; I have been unemployed for four months.

_source.definition_text: people who are unemployed
_source.learnerexamples_text: We want to get the unemployed back into work.; I am a lawyer and not so long ago I worked in Poznan Unemployment Office where I happened to use English - not talking to the unemployed of course.

_source.definition_text: the number of people who are unemployed
_source.learnerexamples_text: a rise/fall in unemployment; Unemployment has fallen/risen again for the third month in a row.; Later, after a discussion about unemployment, we did reading, writing and listening.

_source.definition_text: morally bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: unethical business methods; Then, if you would like to perform an experiment, you cannot, because that would be unethical.

_source.definition_text: not level, smooth, or in equal amounts
_source.learnerexamples_text: an uneven floor ; At the same time we must solve the financial problems incurred by the uneven age distribution.

_source.definition_text: without problems and without anything exciting happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: The journey itself was fairly uneventful.; This rather quiet and uneventful life changed when we moved to the city.

_source.definition_text: not expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: His death was completely unexpected.; Last week I had an unexpected visit from my best friend - Mark.

_source.definition_text: in a way or at a time that is not expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: Retail sales unexpectedly fell last month.; He called in quite unexpectedly last week.; He called me really unexpectedly at work, and told me to go [to] his office at once.

_source.definition_text: not treating people in a equal way
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unfair system; The test was unfair because some people had seen it before.; He [always] gave me horrible marks and was very unfair.

_source.definition_text: not true and morally wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's unfair to blame Roger for everything.; Furthermore, it's unfair [to] say that there is nothing to do in the evenings, because there is lots to do.

_source.definition_text: in an unfair way
_source.learnerexamples_text: His employers treated him very unfairly.; Your report not only gave wrong information to your readers but also criti[c]ized a music festival unfairly.

_source.definition_text: not known to you
_source.learnerexamples_text: I noticed several unfamiliar faces in the meeting room.; His name was unfamiliar to me.; On the other hand, you may not like some dishes, because they may be unfamiliar to you.

_source.definition_text: to not have any knowledge or experience of something
_source.searchterms_text: be unfamiliar with sth;be unfamiliar with sth ;unfamiliar
_source.learnerexamples_text: A lot of people are unfamiliar with the system.

_source.definition_text: not fashionable or popular at a particular time
_source.learnerexamples_text: This kind of cooking is very unfashionable now.; I think that museums became a little bit unfashionable [as a] way of knowing or showing something.

_source.definition_text: negative and showing that you do not like something
_source.learnerexamples_text: unfavourable publicity ; [The] majority of people react positively and are able to change their previous opinions, if these were very unfavourable.

_source.definition_text: not good and likely to cause problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: unfavourable weather conditions ; Despite these unfavourable conditions I managed to get through the concert without any major problems.

_source.definition_text: not healthy because you do too little exercise
_source.learnerexamples_text: I really must do some exercise - I'm so unfit.; I was interested in practicing some sport, because I was feeling quite unfit.

_source.definition_text: not suitable or good enough
_source.learnerexamples_text: The building was declared unfit for human habitation.; Cars also emit carbon monoxide and make the air unfit to breath[e].

_source.definition_text: If a situation or story unfolds, it develops or becomes known.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The nation watched on TV as the tragic events unfolded.; The plot unfolds in an exciting way and the film is fraught with lies, surprises and insinuations.

_source.definition_text: to become open and flat, or to make something become open and flat
_source.learnerexamples_text: I unfolded the map.; Well, you will be if you saw our slide show and talk - members can hardly forget that relaxing afternoon when we unfolded the sails on the lake and enjoyed the tranquility of the area.

_source.definition_text: not expected
_source.learnerexamples_text: The concert was cancelled due to unforeseen circumstances.; Finally, owing to unforeseen circumstances, the half-day visit to St Andrews was cancel[l]ed and I was told about it only in the late morning, which prevented me from doing what I had planned.

_source.definition_text: Something that is unforgettable is so good, interesting, etc. that you remember it for a long time.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Seeing Niagara Falls was an unforgettable experience.; I've just arrived home and I'd like to thank you for the unforgettable weekend.

_source.definition_text: used to show that you wish something was not true or had not happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unfortunate mistake; It was so unfortunate that she lost her job just as her husband became ill.; It is unfortunate that he couldn't inform you about the conference.

_source.definition_text: used to say that you wish something was not true or had not happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd love to come, but unfortunately, I have to work.; Unfortunately, I didn't have my credit card with me or I'd certainly have bought it.; Unfortunately I lost my keys.

_source.definition_text: unlucky
_source.learnerexamples_text: One unfortunate person failed to see the hole and fell straight into it.; He was always an unfortunate person, because bad things happen[ed] to him all the time.

_source.definition_text: not friendly
_source.learnerexamples_text: I found her rather unfriendly.; My last teacher was very unfriendly.

_source.definition_text: the state of being unhappy
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her unhappiness was obvious to everyone.; They feel very unhappy living in a zoo, since for them it is like a prison, and their unhappiness can bring about their death.

_source.definition_text: not satisfied
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm unhappy about the situation.; We were very unhappy with the service at the hotel.; I'm still unhappy about my present accommodation [for] the following reasons.

_source.definition_text: sad
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unhappy childhood/marriage; He made her quite unhappy.; I was unhappy you couldn't come to my birthday party.

_source.definition_text: likely to become ill or likely to damage your health
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has a very unhealthy lifestyle.; The city is unsafe and unhealthy because [of] the pollution and the violence.

_source.definition_text: not wanting to help someone, in a way that seems unfriendly
_source.learnerexamples_text: The taxi driver was rude and unhelpful.; However, The Taverna has no uniform and the waiters there are sometimes pushy and unhelpful.

_source.definition_text: not improving a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unhelpful remark; Because of the unhelpful and useless solution from [this] company, called Energy Plus, I am looking for advice.

_source.definition_text: a special set of clothes that are worn by people who do a particular job or go to a particular school
_source.learnerexamples_text: school uniform; a nurse's uniform; I think I have left the skirt of my school uniform in your house.

_source.definition_text: Something that is unimaginable is difficult to imagine because it is so bad, good, big, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: unimaginable pain/wealth; Later, at the age of 60, after he had suffered from a stroke that was a side effect of the open heart surgery he underwent, he was left speech-impaired, which can be considered an unimaginable handicap for an actor.

_source.definition_text: If a place is uninhabited, no one lives there.
_source.learnerexamples_text: an uninhabited island; Me and my best mate, Kelly, had read in an ancient history book we found in our school library about the legendary Golden Caves which are made of gold, found [o]n the tropical uninhabited island of Tropai.

_source.definition_text: not important
_source.learnerexamples_text: Staffing is still a relatively unimportant issue compared to the other problems that we're facing.; Pat told him some unimportant things such as she learnt to swim at the age of five or that she loved ants.

_source.definition_text: not interested
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's completely uninterested in politics.; He is uninterested in his father['s] money.

_source.definition_text: not interesting
_source.learnerexamples_text: His later work is uninteresting in comparison with his first novel.; My neighbours are particularly uninteresting, they bore me stiff!

_source.definition_text: when two or more countries, groups, etc. join together to make one country, group, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: the European Union; Meanwhile, the debate on European political and monetary union continues.

_source.definition_text: an organization that represents people who do a particular job
_source.learnerexamples_text: a teachers'/firefighters' union; Otherwise there will be some problems with trade unions.

_source.definition_text: unusual and special
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do not miss this unique opportunity to buy all six pans at half the recommended price.; First of all, I would like to tell you that I really enjoyed my stay and it was a unique experience for me.

_source.definition_text: different from everyone and everything else
_source.learnerexamples_text: Everyone's fingerprints are unique.; Every book is unique because every writer is unique, with his own style and his own character.

_source.definition_text: to exist in only one place, or be connected with only one person or thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a method of education that is unique to this school.; I strongly believe that every country needs its local shops with products that are unique to the particular country, not only because it is very good for local development but also because this way the world will stay colo[u]rful and interesting.

_source.definition_text: a single thing or a separate part of something larger
_source.learnerexamples_text: The first year of the course is divided into four units.; Each unit of the course book focuses on a different grammar point.; I'm sorry but I can't come [to] tomorrow's class because my father [had a] car crash and I have to take care [of] him but don't worry I can do the unit of my workbook and do the exercise.

_source.definition_text: a group of people living or working together, especially for a particular purpose
_source.learnerexamples_text: the traditional family unit; an anti-terrorist unit; Dr Nussbaum is director of the Civil Liberties Research Unit at King's College, London.; Both soldiers spent two weeks in training before being allowed to rejoin their unit.; This is very important because once they [have] grown up, they have to be together in the family unit with their [own] kids.

_source.definition_text: joined together as a group, organization, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The whole village was united in their grief.; It was the first film festival to take place in a united Germany.; Despite all these advantages, I deeply miss the times [when] I had almost no technological facilities, but a very happy and united family.

_source.definition_text: to join together as a group, or to make people join together as a group
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need a leader who can unite the party. ; A barbecue would unite all members in a rarely seen way, because we would all be together for a day or an afternoon which would be enough to make some new friends and get to know the other members better.

_source.definition_text: when everyone agrees with each other or wants to stay together
_source.learnerexamples_text: national/party unity ;  family unity ; I would conclude by saying that [some] healthy competition is good, but your main goal has to be to work together as a group and work towards the achievement of goal[s] - as the saying goes, "united we stand, divided we fall" and unity is strength.

_source.definition_text: If people are united, they all agree about something.
_source.learnerexamples_text: On the issue of education the party is united.; We have the authority to make changes, that is if we stand united.

_source.definition_text: everything that exists, including all the stars, space, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is there intelligent life elsewhere in the universe?; I'm the last survivor of a great civilization that is now extinguished. I've been looking for a planet like yours for ages, to transmit the secret of my people. Take this box: this source of energy means strength, it is the most powerful item in the universe!

_source.definition_text: relating to everyone in the world, or to everyone in a particular group
_source.learnerexamples_text: a universal truth; Food is a subject of almost universal interest.; The new reforms have not met with universal approval within the government.;  Kittens and puppies have an almost universal appeal. ; I think [the film] Yasujino Ozo has something universal in [relation to] our daily life, a kind of feeling or emotion.

_source.definition_text: in a way that involves everyone in the world, or everyone in a particular group
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is universally adored.; Water is one of the most common and universally known substances.; Furthermore fame can [give] people the feeling that they are universally loved.

_source.definition_text: a place where students study at a high level to get a degree
_source.learnerexamples_text: the University of Cambridge; Which university did you go to?; James is studying chemistry at Bristol University.; a university course/lecturer; My friend [is a] student at the university [in my town].

_source.definition_text: done without a reason and not deserved
_source.learnerexamples_text: unjustified criticism; The location turned out to be far too small and the costs unjustified.

_source.definition_text: slightly cruel
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unkind remark;  I didn't tell her the truth because I thought it would be unkind. ; His daughter-in-law was most unkind towards him.

_source.definition_text: not famous
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unknown actor; Two unknown actors were being filmed while they were acting.

_source.definition_text: not known
_source.learnerexamples_text: The exact number of people carrying the virus is unknown.; Unknown to me, she'd organized a party for my birthday.; There w[ere] few words and the address was unknown.

_source.definition_text: someone or something that you do not know and so you cannot be certain about
_source.learnerexamples_text: The road conditions in that area are a bit of an unknown quantity.; As mentioned above, [the] laser [beam] was an unknown quantity even to its inventor and those who contributed to its enhancement.

_source.definition_text: things that you have not experienced and know nothing about
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's normal to fear the unknown.; The most important factor when learning English is the hunger for knowledge, the hunger for the unknown.

_source.definition_text: except if
_source.learnerexamples_text: I won't call you unless there are any problems.; You can't get a job unless you've got experience.; Unless you call me to say you're not coming, I'll see you at the theatre.; I never go shopping unless it's necessary.

_source.definition_text: different from someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The furniture was unlike anything she had ever seen.; Dan's actually quite nice, unlike his father.; Unlike you, I'm not a great dancer.; In fact the Hotel Astrid is now closed so I had to stay at the Riverside Hotel, [whi]ch offers great savings for students, unlike the Hotel Royal [whi]ch is quite expensive.

_source.definition_text: not typical of someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's unlike her to be quiet - was there something wrong?; Over the weeks he was getting more and more exhausted and started reducing [his] hours of work. That was so unlike him.

_source.definition_text: not likely
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's unlikely that we'll see them again.;  We might see them there but it's fairly unlikely.; He's unlikely to arrive before midday.; Unfortunately, it is very unlikely that I would be able to go and collect the keys at that time, because I have arranged an appointment with my doctor to see him about my leg.

_source.definition_text: without any limits
_source.learnerexamples_text: a service that offers unlimited Internet access; Moreover, who has the freedom to buy [whatever they need] with an unlimited budget?

_source.definition_text: difficult to believe and probably not true
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unlikely explanation/story; Reflections on an unlikely tale - "It started with a kiss and ended with a twist", one would remark on Ann Patchett's 'Bel Canto'.

_source.definition_text: to remove things from a vehicle
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you help me unload the car?; We began to unload the car and showed the children around the house.

_source.definition_text: to open something which is locked using a key or an electronic device
_source.learnerexamples_text: They haven't unlocked the computer room yet.; She unlocked the door and went in.

_source.definition_text: If a ship, aircraft, etc. unloads, goods are taken off it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The ship unloaded in Marseilles.; Old fishing boats from everywhere unload their merchandise there.

_source.definition_text: not married
_source.learnerexamples_text: She lives with her unmarried son.; It has even been proved by research carried out by [a] sociologist that the woman of today prefers to stay unmarried to keep her own identity.

_source.definition_text: having or causing bad luck
_source.learnerexamples_text: They played well and were unlucky to lose.;  Some people think it's unlucky to walk under ladders. ; I'm going to tell you a story of an unlucky man.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is not necessary
_source.learnerexamples_text: Of course we don't want to alarm people unnecessarily, but they should be alerted to potential dangers.; [The] community should understand the reality of the effects [of] using private cars unnecessarily.

_source.definition_text: not normal or right
_source.learnerexamples_text: an unnatural silence; unnatural conditions; Animals live in unnatural conditions, and die early.

_source.definition_text: describes something that could be avoided or that is not needed
_source.learnerexamples_text: You don't want to make any unnecessary car journeys in this weather.; The aim is to kill the animal as quickly as possible without causing unnecessary suffering.; Don't waste too much time with unnecessary TV shows or computer games.

_source.definition_text: without being seen or noticed
_source.learnerexamples_text: We managed to slip away unnoticed.; But by the time we stop and look around us, it is usually too late to say goodbye to things that were with us, watched us grow and then disappeared, alone and unnoticed.

_source.definition_text: An unpaid debt, tax, etc. has not been paid.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They had nearly £20,000 in unpaid debts.; This amount was unpaid by [the] previous owner.

_source.definition_text: to remove things from a suitcase, bag or box
