_source.definition_text: to be useful
_source.searchterms_text: be (of) any/some use;be of any/some use;use;uses
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is this bag of any use to you?; I hope my remarks [will] be of some use.

_source.definition_text: one of the meanings of a word, or the way that a particular word is used
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can you list all the uses of the word 'point'?

_source.definition_text: to not be useful
_source.searchterms_text: be (of) no use;be of no use;use;uses
_source.learnerexamples_text: His advice turned out to be no use at all.; My mother came immediately, but it was no use because my brother isn't afraid of her, so she called my father.

_source.definition_text: used to say that trying to do something has no effect
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was no use talking to him - he just wouldn't listen.; It was no use [trying to] smoke cigarettes in this pub.

_source.definition_text: permission to use something, or the ability to use something
_source.searchterms_text: the use of sth;use;use of sth;uses
_source.learnerexamples_text: Martin has offered me the use of his car.; She lost the use of both legs in the accident.; One of my closest friend[s] who lost the use of her legs five years ago in a tragic car accident took part [in] this trip.

_source.definition_text: to use something that is available
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were encouraged to make use of all the facilities.; Finally, I think the designers will make use of the raw materials and create an innovative look for all of us.

_source.definition_text: to become familiar with something or someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: You'll get used to Ted eventually.; Climbers soon become used to the thinner air at 5000 metres.; In addition, I've got used to look[ing] after them.

_source.definition_text: to be familiar with something or someone
_source.searchterms_text: be used to sb/sth/doing sth ;be used to sb/sth/doing sth;used
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're used to tourists here - we get thousands every year.;  He's used to working long hours.; She was not used to speaking Cantonese.; When I'm working, I'm used to wearing something more conservative.

_source.definition_text: If something used to happen or a situation used to exist, it happened regularly or in the past but it does not happen or exist now.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She used to live in Detroit.; He used to be a pilot.; You don't come and see me like you used to.; When we were younger, we didn't used to drink coffee.; It's an American film about a girl that used to live in Africa.

_source.definition_text: helping you to do or achieve something
_source.learnerexamples_text: useful information/advice; A good knife is probably one of the most useful things you can have in a kitchen.; It has a camera and it is very useful.

_source.definition_text: to be useful and help someone do or achieve something, especially when there is nothing else to help them
_source.learnerexamples_text: You should keep that paint - it might come in useful.; However, I take great ex[c]eption to the view that much of our school education is a waste of time because everything we learn at school might come in useful later during our adulthood.

_source.definition_text: the quality of being useful
_source.learnerexamples_text: He explained the usefulness of having a wi-fi connection. ; They came back yesterday and I have interviewed them to find out what they think about the usefulness of the programme.

_source.definition_text: If something is useless, it does not work well or it has no effect.
_source.learnerexamples_text: This umbrella's useless - there's a big hole in it.;  It's useless arguing with her.; I started digging, but it was useless.

_source.definition_text: having no skill in an activity
_source.learnerexamples_text: Dave's useless at football.; Every time I see her, she seems to be busy sewing, knitting etc. In this I really envy her, I'm quite useless at making clothes, although I can certainly do adjustments on my clothes, make curtains an[d] such things.

_source.definition_text: in the way that happens most of the time
_source.learnerexamples_text: As usual, James was the last to arrive.; As usual, I'll travel by plane.

_source.definition_text: someone who uses a product, machine or service
_source.learnerexamples_text: drug users; Unemployed people are the main users of this advice centre.; When you log in, you will be asked for your user name and password.; I would like to meet other experienced computer users in order to share programs as well as tips and tricks about programming.

_source.definition_text: normal and happening most often
_source.learnerexamples_text: I went to bed at my usual time.; You'll find the box in its usual place.; There was more rain than usual this summer in the mountain areas.; We are going to meet at 5 pm at the station and then go for a pizza - you know where, the usual place "Pizza Express".

_source.definition_text: in the way that most often happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: He usually gets home about 6 o'clock.; I usually just have a sandwich for lunch.; Is he usually so rude?; "Does this shop open on Sundays?" "Usually."; Hungarian people usually eat breakfast at 6 or 7 o'clock.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize how important or serious something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: a matter of the utmost importance ; The situation needs to be handled with the utmost care.; In my opinion, there are features of utmost importance that should be [careful]ly checked.

_source.definition_text: to try as hard as you can to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: We did our utmost to finish the project on time.; In addition, we l[i]ve in a materialistic society where we all do our utmost in order to make ends meet, but we are never satisfied.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She dismissed the article as utter nonsense. ; To act otherwise would be, in my opinion, utter nonsense.

_source.definition_text: to say something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She left without uttering a word. ; After I had told him about it, he was in such despair that he was not able to utter a single word.

_source.definition_text: completely
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's utterly ridiculous.; The information provided in your report about the final goal was utterly wrong.

_source.definition_text: a room that is available in a hotel
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you have any vacancies?; The hotels have no vacancies, the tourists are everywhere.

_source.definition_text: a job that is available for someone to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tell me if you hear of any vacancies for secretaries.; We look forward to meeting you at your ea[r]liest convenience to discuss details, go over our salary and health package as well as any other questions you might have, before starting the procedure of finding suitable candidates for the job vacancies.

_source.definition_text: A vacant job is available for someone to do.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The assistant marketing post is vacant - why don't you apply?; Therefore, I believe I am suitable for your vacant position.

_source.definition_text: Somewhere that is vacant is available because it is not being used.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a vacant building; The room next to ours is vacant at the moment.; You see, we have plenty of vacant rooms so you would not cause any trouble.

_source.definition_text: to give someone a vaccine to stop them from getting a disease
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you been vaccinated against polio?; Today, in most civilized countries, small kids are vaccinated against most lethal viruses, like hepatitis, and old people are even vaccinated against the flu.

_source.definition_text: an injection that protects you against a disease
_source.learnerexamples_text: All the children are given a meningitis vaccination.; Local health-care cent[re]s are assisting with birth-control advice, vaccinations and general check-ups.

_source.definition_text: a substance that is given to people to stop them from getting a particular disease
_source.learnerexamples_text: Doctors have run out of the flu vaccine.; An experiment was recently conducted by the same scientist group to verify if the vaccine works.

_source.definition_text: not clear or certain
_source.learnerexamples_text: I have a vague idea of where the hotel is.;  He was a bit vague about directions. ; Do not misunderstand me: I greatly enjoyed the conference but it did not give me the satisfaction of having even a vague idea of what I would like to do...

_source.definition_text: showing that someone is not thinking clearly or does not understand
_source.learnerexamples_text: a vague expression; If someone had asked him why, this person would have [given] a vague look, a dismissive shrug of two shoulders and a "oh, just because".

_source.definition_text: A vain attempt/effort, etc. does not have the result you want.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I made a vain attempt to engage him in conversation.; Many flew to cities in the vain hope of earning money, thus increasing the number of the homeless .

_source.definition_text: without any success
_source.learnerexamples_text: I tried in vain to start a conversation.; We looked in vain for the guide through three London parks.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is not clear or certain
_source.learnerexamples_text: I vaguely remember meeting him at Lionel's house.; I can vaguely remember the decor, and if I tried harder maybe I could remember the taste of the ice-cream.

_source.definition_text: based on good reasons or facts that are true
_source.learnerexamples_text: a valid excuse/reason; a valid argument/criticism; My ideas might be different from yours, but they're equally valid.; You could hardly think of Dr Quimper as guilty, because every one of the Crackenthorpe family had a valid reason to kill.

_source.definition_text: too interested in your own appearance and thinking you are very attractive
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's terribly vain.; Men are vain creatures who worry, maybe exces[s]ively, about beauty and keeping up with standards of beauty set by society.

_source.definition_text: how true or reasonable something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: We should question the validity of these statements.; This statement is so obvious we almost never question its validity.

_source.definition_text: officially or legally acceptable
_source.learnerexamples_text: The ticket is valid for three months.; My passport is valid for another two years.; You need to enter a valid password.; Is this offer valid for the weekends, as well?

_source.definition_text: an area of low land between hills or mountains, often with a river running through it
_source.learnerexamples_text: the Nile Valley; the Thames valley; There was snow on the hill tops but not in the valley.; My home town is situated in a valley.

_source.definition_text: Valuable objects are worth a lot of money.
_source.learnerexamples_text: valuable paintings; These antiques are extremely valuable.; So as you can imagine, not only is the ring valuable but it also means a lot to me since it makes me remember Brazil!

_source.definition_text: Valuable information, advice, etc. is very helpful or important.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was able to provide the police with some valuable information.; This trip will allow me to gain valuable knowledge and experience.

_source.definition_text: If something is good value, it is of good quality or you think the amount of money you spent on it was right.
_source.searchterms_text: good value (for money);good value for money;value;values
_source.learnerexamples_text: The meal was very good value.; It's real[l]y good value for money, including all equipment, accom[m]odation and food.

_source.definition_text: how much money something could be sold for
_source.learnerexamples_text: The new road has affected the value of these houses. ; She had already sold everything of value that she possessed.; Cars quickly go down in value.; The value of the pound fell against other European currencies yesterday.; "Well, there was nothing of value in [the suitcase]," my mother remarked, but I was close to tears.

_source.definition_text: the beliefs people have about what is right and wrong and what is most important in life, which control their behaviour
_source.learnerexamples_text: family/moral/traditional values; A tragedy occurs which causes Andrew to rediscover his moral values.

_source.definition_text: how useful or important something is
_source.learnerexamples_text: The documents are of great historical value.; The necklace had great sentimental value.; I was really sad because th[ese] shoes had a lot of sentimental value for me, and they were made of genuine le[a]ther!

_source.definition_text: If you accept something at face value because of the way it first looks or seems, you do so without thinking carefully about it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can't just accept everything you read in the newspapers at face value.; These results should not be taken at face value - careful analysis is required to assess their full implications.; People are assessed at face value [by] the type of cars they drive.

_source.definition_text: to consider something important
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've always valued her advice.; I will learn how other people live and I will also learn to value the things I have.

_source.definition_text: to judge how much money something could be sold for
_source.learnerexamples_text: The ring was valued at $1000.; My house was valued at £200,000.

_source.definition_text: a vehicle that is used for carrying things but which is smaller than a truck
_source.learnerexamples_text: a delivery van; a van driver; I looked in my mirror and saw [a] white van.

_source.definition_text: the crime of intentionally damaging things in public places
_source.learnerexamples_text: There has been more vandalism in the town centre recently.; As the members of the local council will know, our area is facing many problems with youths hanging around on the weekends causing grievances such as vandalism, noise and stealing in the local shops.

_source.definition_text: to disappear suddenly
_source.learnerexamples_text: The sun vanished behind the clouds.; The child vanished while on her way home from school.; I [went after] the thief but he vanished into the crowd.

_source.definition_text: when someone thinks they are very attractive and is too interested in their own appearance
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her vanity is staggering.; The vanity of wearing the most fashionable clothes bores my other friend, Kate, to death.

_source.definition_text: a number, amount, or situation which can change
_source.learnerexamples_text: A patient's recovery time depends on so many variables, such as age, weight, and general health.; There are too many variables and happiness may also depend on the soci[al] background of a person.

_source.definition_text: changing often
_source.learnerexamples_text: The sound quality on the recording is variable.; By contrast the figure is more variable regarding the other topics.

_source.definition_text: a difference in amount or quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: variations in price/temperature; There was some variation in the quality of the prints.; Apart from this, there is very little variation in temperature between day and night.

_source.definition_text: something that is slightly different from the usual form
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a variation on the standard apple pie.; Big Brother's counterpart, "Lost Story", did really well the first time and a bit less the second time. Still, it is very popular and a variation on this theme, called "Nine people", still does very well today.

_source.definition_text: many different types of things or people
_source.searchterms_text: a variety of sth/sb;varieties;variety;variety of sth/sb
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ben has done a variety of jobs.; Hi Nick, I'd like a variety of music [at the party].

_source.definition_text: consisting of many different things or types
_source.learnerexamples_text: a varied diet; a long and varied career; Remember you should always eat a varied diet.

_source.definition_text: the quality of often changing or of being made of many different things
_source.learnerexamples_text: Factory work often lacks variety.; I think you need a bit more variety in your diet.; You know, I like variety a lot and don't like my friends to see me with [the same] clothes.

_source.definition_text: many different
_source.learnerexamples_text: I left London for various reasons. ; They have offices in various parts of the country.; We had various problems on our journey, including a puncture.; There are various ways of raising money.; We played various games and danced too.

_source.definition_text: If things of the same type vary, they are different from each other.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Car prices vary greatly/widely across Europe.; The samples varied in quality but were generally acceptable.; The price of the dishes varies.

_source.definition_text: a container that you put flowers in
_source.learnerexamples_text: a glass vase; a vase of flowers; Yesterday I went to a shopping centre with my mother, and bought a small desk, a radio, a vase, and a small s[ofa].

_source.definition_text: to change or to cause something to change
_source.learnerexamples_text: Temperatures vary depending on/according to the time of year.; I try to vary what I eat.; To vary the pictures of cultural events, I would recommend [visiting] the Wednesday market, which starts at 8 am.

_source.definition_text: extremely big
_source.learnerexamples_text: a vast amount/sum of money; vast areas of forest; The vast majority of pupils attend state schools.; Among the vast choice of interesting buildings to photograph I can name the "National Portrait Museum", a huge building in renaissance style, [and] the old "Castle of Sforza", built in the eleventh century.

_source.definition_text: someone who does not eat meat or fish
_source.learnerexamples_text: Of the four million people who have become vegetarians in Britain, nearly two-thirds are women.; I've heard that even the non-vegetarian food is good there, but I'm a vegetarian.

_source.definition_text: a plant that you eat, for example potatoes, onions, beans, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: fresh/frozen vegetables; vegetable soup/curry; fruit and vegetables; In the winter we eat more root vegetables, such as carrots and parsnips.;  Raw vegetables contain more vitamins than cooked vegetables.

_source.definition_text: not eating, containing or using meat or fish
_source.learnerexamples_text: All her children are vegetarian.; vegetarian cooking/food; a vegetarian dish/meal; She's recently gone/become vegetarian.; Do you like vegetarian food?

_source.definition_text: the plants and trees that grow in a particular area
_source.learnerexamples_text: They hacked a path through the dense vegetation.; I dream of being the first one to set foot on a white sandy beach, to admire a new kind of vegetation: cranberry bushes, sweet potatoes, wild turkeys, a different climate; how scary and exciting at the same time!

_source.definition_text: something such as a car or bus that takes people from one place to another, especially using roads
_source.learnerexamples_text: The driver of the vehicle was unhurt.; Sometimes I watch programmes about cars and other vehicles, because I'm keen on them.

_source.definition_text: something that you use as a way of telling people your ideas or opinions
_source.searchterms_text: a vehicle for sth/doing sth;vehicle;vehicle for sth/doing sth;vehicles
_source.learnerexamples_text: The paper was merely a vehicle for his political beliefs.; And you, as our local newspaper, will become a vehicle for our objections.

_source.definition_text: a thin piece of material that covers a woman's face
_source.learnerexamples_text: She wore a thin veil.; And most brides wear a long veil so grooms can't see their wife's face.

_source.definition_text: one of the tubes in your body that carries blood to the heart
_source.learnerexamples_text: the veins in the leg/neck; Do you love the sensation of your blood rushing in your veins, your knees trembling slightly and your hair standing [to] attention? Well, I do, and dangerous sports are the thing for me.

_source.definition_text: cloth that has a thick, soft surface on one side
_source.learnerexamples_text: a black velvet jacket; Then came the day of his funeral and we attended the ceremony (as good neighbours do when someone from next door dies), only to find that it was held by a group of 12 sombre men, clad in dark velvet robes, each one of them holding a black candle, chanting some kind of mourning song that haunted our memories for the rest of the day and, perhaps even the following night.

_source.definition_text: to express strong anger or another strong feeling
_source.learnerexamples_text: He gave vent to the frustration that had been building up inside him.; It's a great fallacy that giving vent to our emotion will be a solution to the problem itself and will lead to anything at all.

_source.definition_text: to do or say something to show your anger or another strong, bad feeling
_source.searchterms_text: vent;vent your anger/frustration etc;vent your anger/frustration, etc.;vented;venting;vents
_source.learnerexamples_text: He vented his anger by kicking the door.; The room at the attic was my only haven, the sole asylum where I could forget the wrinkled face ranting and raving at me, fuming with animosity towards me, venting her anger and frustration and all the other feelings bottled up in her.

_source.definition_text: a new activity or business
_source.learnerexamples_text: a business venture; They even give vast amounts of people a means of living, and can become very lucrative business ventures.

_source.definition_text: to leave a safe place and go somewhere that may involve risks
_source.learnerexamples_text: If the snow stops, I might venture out.; After having visited some of the more frequented island[s], we decided to venture out to the island of Fourni.

_source.definition_text: used to say that it is worth trying something, even if you may not succeed
_source.searchterms_text: nothing ventured nothing gained;nothing ventured, nothing gained;venture;ventured;ventures;venturing
_source.learnerexamples_text: It will be quite expensive ... still, nothing ventured nothing gained!; It was a demanding task to prepare it but nothing ventured nothing gained.

_source.definition_text: a place where a sports game, musical performance, or special event happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: The hotel is an ideal venue for conferences and business meetings.; The stadium has been specifically designed as a venue for European Cup matches.; This festival has already got [a] good reputation as [an] alternative venue for both artists and audience.

_source.definition_text: a word that is used to say that someone does something or that something happens. For example the words 'arrive', 'make', 'be', and 'feel' are verbs.
_source.learnerexamples_text: a regular/irregular verb; It is very good for grammar, irregular verbs, etc. The name of the book is "M[urphy's] grammar" and it's only four Pounds.

_source.definition_text: spoken and not written
_source.learnerexamples_text: a verbal promise/agreement

_source.definition_text: relating to words or the use of words
_source.learnerexamples_text: verbal ability/skills; Not only would this system help the keen students to improve their verbal fluency, it would also help them to prepare their lessons in time for the next class.

_source.base_text: be on the verge of sth/doing sth
_source.definition_text: to be going to happen or to do something very soon
_source.searchterms_text: be on the verge of sth/doing sth;verge;verges
_source.learnerexamples_text: a company on the verge of financial disaster; I was on the verge of leaving my job.; I was on the verge of depression, when I decided to take control of my own life.

_source.definition_text: a decision made in a court of law or by a person in authority
_source.learnerexamples_text: a guilty verdict; The jury took nine hours to reach a verdict.; As far as I can see it the redundancy verdict is based on the judgement about an employee's value.

_source.definition_text: having many different skills
_source.learnerexamples_text: a versatile player/performer; She is a very gregarious and versatile person whose scintillating and jocular personality makes everybody melt.

_source.definition_text: to prove that something is true, or do something to discover if it is true
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was impossible to verify her statement.; The Canadian Patent Office Branch will be responsible for verifying if new inventions are truly new or have already been invented somewhere in the world.

_source.definition_text: useful for doing a lot of different things
_source.learnerexamples_text: a versatile tool; The Internet today is the most versatile tool in so many ways.

_source.definition_text: one of the parts that a song or poem is divided into
_source.learnerexamples_text: I only know the first verse of the poem.; Each verse was sung as a solo and then everyone joined in on the chorus.; But I was so puzzled that when I tried to sing, I couldn't remember a word of the verse I had written.

_source.definition_text: one form of something that is slightly different to other forms of the same thing
_source.learnerexamples_text: An English-language version of the book is planned for the autumn.; The original version of the film is much better.; a new/updated version; Who has never said that the original book was better than the film version?

_source.definition_text: someone's description of what has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: Bates gave his version of events to the police.; For that reason, I have to ask you for a formal apology in print, where you could give the correct version of events and also change the bad image you gave to the readers of the people of my organisation.

_source.definition_text: used to compare two things or ideas, especially when you have to choose between them
_source.learnerexamples_text: private education versus state education ; Mobile phones - fashion versus utility Nowadays, [everywhere] you look, there is someone speaking [on] a mobile phone.

_source.definition_text: used to say that one team or person is competing against another
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tomorrow's game is Newcastle versus Arsenal.; Starting in chronological order you can see the first game - Argentina versus Germany - which was a revenge for the final competition in the previous World Cup, '88.

_source.definition_text: pointing straight up from a surface
_source.learnerexamples_text: a vertical line; The vertical axis shows the percentage of age groups attending the cinema at least once in a year, while the horizontal axis represents the years from 1990 to 2010.

_source.definition_text: used emphasize an adjective or adverb
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thank you very much.;  She was very pleased.; He's very kind.; The situation is very serious.; Think about it very carefully before deciding.

_source.definition_text: not good, tall, happy, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: not very good/tall/happy etc;not very good/tall/happy, etc.;very
_source.learnerexamples_text: The film wasn't very good.; He doesn't sing very well.; My college is not very big.

_source.definition_text: to a large amount or degree
_source.learnerexamples_text: Thank you very much for the flowers!; I like her very much.; I like Bradford very much.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize a noun
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is the very book I've been looking for all month.; You're the very person we need for the job.; The letter was sent on Monday from Manchester and arrived in London the very same/next day.; You cannot infringe individual liberties and ban the purchase of cars - it would go against the very fabric of modern society.

_source.definition_text: a piece of underwear that you wear under a shirt
_source.learnerexamples_text: You'll need a vest in this weather.; The contents include two [items of male] underwear, size medium, white colour. Also a pair of white sock[s] and one vest medium size.

_source.definition_text: someone whose job is to give medical care to animals that are ill or hurt
_source.learnerexamples_text: Helen is training to become a vet.; Sorry Mr Smith but I'[ll miss] tomorrow's class as I have to go to the vet with my dog.

_source.definition_text: someone who has been in an army or navy during a war
_source.learnerexamples_text: a veteran of World War Two ; But even now I can recollect my unwillingness to get involved in parades, to join the veterans, military men, soldiers who were really proud of having a rare opportunity to feel a cog in a big wheel.

_source.definition_text: going through or stopping at a place on the way to another place
_source.learnerexamples_text: The train to Utrecht goes via Amsterdam.; Two years ago I travel[l]ed to Canada via Italy.

_source.definition_text: someone who has done a job or activity for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: a 20-year veteran of BBC news ; Since I'm a passionate and veteran traveller, I do agree with some points.

_source.definition_text: using a particular machine, system or person to send or recieve something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Reports are coming in via satellite.; I only found out about it via my sister.; I hate shopping via [the] internet.

_source.definition_text: something bad that someone often does
_source.learnerexamples_text: Smoking is his only vice.; At present I'm a heavy smoker and I think I will do my best to keep them away from this unhealthy vice.

_source.definition_text: used for referring to the opposite of what you have just said
_source.learnerexamples_text: Never use indoor lights outside and vice versa.; The piles of cash are not far away from any celebrity and we all know that time equals money and vice versa.

_source.definition_text: effective and able to be successful
_source.learnerexamples_text: a viable alternative to nuclear power;  an economically viable plan; This is a question that demands reasonable answers and viable solutions.

_source.definition_text: violent and dangerous
_source.learnerexamples_text: a vicious attack on a child; a vicious dog; She was a real, vicious murderer.

_source.definition_text: in the area near a place
_source.searchterms_text: in the vicinity (of sth);in the vicinity of sth;vicinity
_source.learnerexamples_text: A number of buildings in the vicinity of the fire were damaged.; This centre would provide new sports and leisure premises for our town and would certainly attract young people from other towns in the vicinity as well.

_source.definition_text: intended to upset someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: a vicious rumour ; One advantage with this school that rose above the others, was the fact that there was virtually no cruel bullying or vicious teasing.

_source.definition_text: a continuing unpleasant situation, created when one problem causes another problem which then makes the first problem worse
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many people get trapped in a vicious circle of dieting and weight gain.; So we could say that it becomes a vicious circle.

_source.definition_text: someone who has suffered the effects of violence, illness or bad luck
_source.learnerexamples_text: victims of crime; The children are the innocent victims of the fighting.; The new drug might help save the lives of cancer victims.; His wife was his last victim.

_source.definition_text: a short film that can be watched on television, a computer, a camera, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: music videos; video sites; They showed me their wedding video.; I like it because it has a camera to make videos.

_source.definition_text: when you win a game, competition, election, fight, war, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Phoenix managed a 135-114 victory over Denver. ; Grant won/achieved/gained a comfortable/easy victory over Cooper in yesterday's match.; This result is a victory for democracy.; They were all celebrating their victory with a gorgeous dinner.

_source.definition_text: a short video recording that you can see on a website
_source.learnerexamples_text: The website has several video clips of Murray's recent matches.; It shows how a band or a singer do their video clips.

_source.definition_text: a film, television programme, etc. recorded on a long, narrow, magnetic strip, or the recorded strip itself that is inside a rectangular plastic container
_source.learnerexamples_text: He just used to stay in and watch videos.; We had the whole series on video.; [O]n that chan[n]el you have the chance to watch many videos of your favourite singer, and learn about their news.

_source.definition_text: a game in which you make pictures move on a screen
_source.learnerexamples_text: He plays a lot of video games.; We played cricket, and we also played video games.

_source.definition_text: your opinion
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have different views about/on education.;  In my view, her criticisms were justified.; I take the view that everyone should be free to decide for themselves.; It's my view that everyone should have the right to choose. ; We had a friendly exchange of views.

_source.definition_text: how well you can see something from a particular place
_source.learnerexamples_text: We had a great view of the procession.; Don't stand in front of me - you're blocking my view of the stage.; She turned a corner, and disappeared from view.; In a few seconds, he disappear[ed] out of my view.

_source.definition_text: the things that you can see from a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: On a clear day, the view from the top of the mountain is amazing.; The rooftop restaurant has a spectacular view across the bay.; The view from the window of my room is the best one.

_source.definition_text: because of
_source.learnerexamples_text: In view of recent events, we have decided to cancel the meeting.; In view of what happened, I would advise you not to try to mislead people like this [again].

_source.base_text: with a view to doing sth
_source.definition_text: so that you can do something
_source.searchterms_text: view;views;with a view to doing sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's doing some improvements on the house with a view to selling it.; The purpose of this report is to assess the success of the latest tour our sports club organised and make relevant suggestions with a view to enhancing future trips.

_source.definition_text: a position from which something can be seen
_source.learnerexamples_text: The house was hidden from view behind a wall.; He turned the corner and the harbour came into view.; The animal disappeared as unexpectedly as it came into view.

_source.definition_text: to have a particular opinion about someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: In all three countries he is viewed as a terrorist.; There is of course the argument of many young people: that they live in a society that op[p]resses them, where they cannot express themselves freely and where, whatever they do or say, they are viewed as 'punks' or 'idiots' by adults.

_source.definition_text: to watch something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They were able to view the city from a helicopter.; People sit in p[a]latial cafes and restaurants to view the beauty of that "lazy river".

_source.definition_text: someone who watches a television programme
_source.learnerexamples_text: Millions of viewers will be watching this match.; He's an extraordinary person and TV viewers will love him because of his good sense of humo[u]r and his honesty.

_source.definition_text: a way of thinking about a situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: From his viewpoint the action seemed entirely justified.; As a student, I feel concerned [about] the traffic issue and I asked some people about their viewpoints on the two proposals.

_source.definition_text: someone who lives in a village
_source.learnerexamples_text: Most of the villagers are opposed to the new road.; We, the villagers, are very worried about the effect the noise will have on our children and their sense of hearing.

_source.definition_text: a place where people live in the countryside that includes buildings such as shops but is smaller than a town
_source.learnerexamples_text: a small fishing village;  She lives in a small village outside Oxford.; Many people come from the surrounding villages to work in the town.;  a village shop; My grandmother lived in a village and I often went there.

_source.definition_text: a plant that grapes grow on
_source.learnerexamples_text: The wall was covered in a vine.; After follow[ing] the walking path through the vines at Canon-Fronsac you could climb the Canon Mountain to have a view all over the region.

_source.definition_text: a sour liquid that is used in cooking, often made from wine
_source.learnerexamples_text: red wine vinegar

_source.definition_text: to not obey a law, rule, or agreement
_source.learnerexamples_text: Countries that violate international law will be dealt with in court.; All three points strongly violate the regulations and immediate action is required.

_source.definition_text: when someone tries to hurt or kill someone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: an act of violence ;  A number of people were killed in the violence.; Violence against women has increased in recent years.; The recent outbreak of violence in the region is very disturbing.; Today, it is important that children and teenagers do something with their free time and do not get in contact with criminality and violence.

_source.definition_text: extreme force and energy, especially of something causing damage
_source.learnerexamples_text: Such was the violence of the explosion that three buildings collapsed.

_source.definition_text: involving violence
_source.learnerexamples_text: a violent crime;  a violent protest; His films tend to be very violent.; Some say that television can affect people in bad ways and sometimes causes violent incidents.

_source.definition_text: in a way that involves violence
_source.learnerexamples_text: He often behaved violently and they were terrified of him.; He claimed to have been violently assaulted while in prison.; Sometimes they behave violently because of their [imprison]ment.

_source.definition_text: using force to hurt or attack someone else
_source.learnerexamples_text: a violent criminal; He shouts a lot but I don't think he's ever been physically violent towards her.; Now Mary knew what happened at Jamaica Inn and it was very dangerous for her because her uncle was a violent man.

_source.definition_text: sudden and causing damage
_source.learnerexamples_text: a violent explosion/storm; The violent storm was rocking the ship back and forth.

_source.definition_text: a wooden musical instrument with four strings, which you hold against your neck and play by moving a bow across the strings
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've been learning the violin for the last four years.; My hobb[ies are] reading and playing the violin.

_source.definition_text: someone who has never had sex
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was a virgin at the time of her marriage.; Why was it that everybody assumed that after your 18th birthday you could not possibly be a virgin any more?

_source.definition_text: Virgin land, forest, etc. has not been used or damaged by people.
_source.learnerexamples_text: 50 acres of virgin woodland; The balance of nature is threatened by the construction of luxurious hotels in the middle of virgin forests.

_source.definition_text: almost a particular thing or quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ten years of bad government had brought about the virtual collapse of the country's economy.; War in the region now looks like a virtual certainty.; However the growth of our cities and townships co[up]led with an exponential increase in traffic and facilities have transformed these areas into virtual no-go zones

_source.definition_text: using computer images and sounds that make you think an imagined situation is real
_source.learnerexamples_text: a virtual art gallery online; However, I go far away from my family and other people and have virtual relationships.

_source.definition_text: almost
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've virtually finished.; Their twins are virtually identical.; That wine stain on my shirt has virtually disappeared.; Virtually everyone today can go out and buy their own personal computer.

_source.definition_text: when a computer produces images and sounds that make you think an imagined situation is real
_source.learnerexamples_text: virtual reality games; virtual reality software; Magnificent scientific pro[j]ects are done by computers, [as well as] daily shopping, com[m]unication with people in other parts of the world, games, getting any kind of information and, soon, virtual reality!

_source.definition_text: in a way that uses computer images and sounds that make you think an imagined situation is real
_source.learnerexamples_text: Nowadays all these things can be experienced virtually.; I also have the possibility of making new friends: I can connect to a special site which will enable me to [meet people] virtually.

_source.definition_text: a good quality that someone has
_source.learnerexamples_text: Patience is not among his virtues.; The saying 'patience is a virtue' has been very over-used but that does not make it any less true.

_source.definition_text: because of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She succeeded by virtue of hard work rather than talent.; However, you should take into consideration the expenses, which might be exorbitant by virtue of the fact that you inten[d] to create places with a beautiful ambience and a wide range of comforts offered that will facilitate residents' lives.

_source.definition_text: an advantage or useful quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: The great virtue of having a small car is that you can park it easily.; Finally it should be said that despite the negative attitudes towards the overcrowding [of] our good old Earth, longer life seems to have more virtues than drawbacks.

_source.definition_text: behaviour that is morally good
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was a woman of great virtue.; Mother Theresa, she was a model of virtue.

_source.definition_text: a program that is secretly put onto a computer in order to destroy the information that is stored on it
_source.learnerexamples_text: My computer has been behaving oddly and I suspect it's a virus.; That document was a "virus" and erased all my documents [o]n my computer.

_source.definition_text: an official mark in your passport which allows you to enter or leave a particular country
_source.learnerexamples_text: We travelled to Argentina on a tourist visa.; Tomorrow I am not going to attend [the] class because I have to apply for my visa at 9.00.

_source.definition_text: an infectious organism too small to be seen that causes disease, or an illness that it causes
_source.learnerexamples_text: a flu virus; I don't know exactly what's wrong with her - I think it's some sort of virus.; My "friend" Pat told everybody that my brother died and that he died because he got a virus - that's why I didn't have friends because all the people thought that I had the virus too.

_source.definition_text: obvious or noticeable
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is a higly visible environmental spokesperson.; There is a visible improvement in your essay writing.; After about three months I noticed a visible improvement.

_source.definition_text: able to be seen
_source.learnerexamples_text: You should wear something light-coloured when you're cycling at night so that you're more visible.; The fire was visible from five kilometres away.; There are few visible signs of the illness that kept her in hospital for so long.; The comet should be visible to the naked eye.; He waited curiously for her to become visible through the fog, which seemed to have [become] denser in the last few seconds.

_source.definition_text: an idea or image in your mind of what something could be like in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: a vision of a better society; We see in his novels his grim vision of the future.; All in all, I think you must write a new report to apologize for having been so pessimistic and having given such a bleak vision of this Festival.

_source.definition_text: in a way that can be seen
_source.learnerexamples_text: He was visibly upset.; However, it is my firm conviction that if the authority reconsiders some of its regulations and take urgent steps, [the number of] unemployed people will be visibly reduced.

_source.definition_text: the ability to see
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has poor vision in his left eye.; Her hands were sweating and her vision had become a blur because of the tension in the air.

_source.definition_text: the ability to make plans for the future that are imaginative and wise
_source.learnerexamples_text: As a leader, he lacked vision.; A man of vision, Eleftherios Venizelus played a significant role in the history of my country, as in his time it became, with [few] changes, what it is today.

_source.definition_text: to go to someone's home and spend time with them
_source.learnerexamples_text: Will you visit me when I'm in hospital?;  We have friends coming to visit this weekend.; She visits her parents once a week.

_source.definition_text: to go to a place and spend a short amount of time there
_source.learnerexamples_text: We visited a few galleries while we were in Prague.; It's a very nice place with a lot of shop[s] and museum[s] to visit, like the "Louvre" for example.

_source.definition_text: to look at a website
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's the usual invitation to visit their website.; If you want more information or you want [to] see photos about [the] art class, visit our website: www.artclass.com.

_source.definition_text: someone who visits a person or place
_source.learnerexamples_text: Ben, you've got some visitors to see you.;  The museum attracts large numbers of visitors.; I did [a] very good meal for all of my visitors.

_source.definition_text: when you visit a place or a person
_source.learnerexamples_text: the President's visit to Argentina; I think I'll pay a visit to the hairdresser's while I'm in town.; We had a visit from the school inspector last week.; The problem is that my mother arranged a visit [to] the doctor, and after that [to] the dentist.

_source.definition_text: relating to seeing
_source.learnerexamples_text: The film has some powerful visual effects.; It also provides a clear idea of how people's lives were in a particular period by showing us the visual images of that time.

_source.definition_text: energy and strength
_source.learnerexamples_text: At 48, he still projects an image of youth and vitality.; His bad behaviour was often excused, being blamed on his "boyish vitality", [while] I was expected to be a good girl most of the time.

_source.definition_text: necessary or extremely important
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tourism is vital to the country's economy.; The kidney plays a vital role/part in the removal of waste products from the blood.;  It's absolutely vital that you follow the instructions exactly.; If you don't mind I would like to ask you some vital questions.

_source.definition_text: in a very important way
_source.learnerexamples_text: Safety at work is vitally important.; Being able to use the computer and the Internet successfully is vitally important in today's society but it will be even more important in the future.

_source.definition_text: one of a group of natural substances that you need to be healthy
_source.l_topic_text_text: body and health, food and drink
_source.learnerexamples_text: a vitamin pill; Oranges are full of vitamin C.; On the one hand, we eat a lot of sweet [or] fat food, which lack[s] vitamins.

_source.definition_text: A vivacious person, especially a woman, is full of energy and enthusiasm.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She is extremely vivacious.; She was a vivacious and audacious girl keen on getting to know the world outside Israel.

_source.definition_text: A vivid colour is very bright.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was wearing a vivid pink shirt.; Students would like to have some vivid colours or pictures on the walls but the best solution would be to repaint the walls.

_source.definition_text: Vivid descriptions or memories produce strong, clear images in your mind.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He gave a very vivid account/description of life in Havana.; I still have a very vivid memory of the evening.; She has a very vivid imagination.; Each memory is still so vivid.

_source.definition_text: in a vivid way
_source.learnerexamples_text: I vividly remember my first day at school.; She could vividly remember the last time he hurt her, only then it was with a razor.

_source.definition_text: all the words you know in a particular language
_source.learnerexamples_text: a broad/wide/limited vocabulary; Reading helps to broaden your vocabulary.; I'm sure I will improve my vocabulary and English Grammar.

_source.definition_text: a strong feeling that you are right for a particular type of work, or a job that gives you this feeling
_source.learnerexamples_text: He knew that teaching was his true vocation.; He was a teacher, seeing teaching as his vocation, [and] nothing could boost his confidence as much as excellent students and successful [results].

_source.definition_text: all the words that exist in a language, or that are used when discussing a particular subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: Computing has its own specialist vocabulary.; The tuition is well adapted to our needs, I mean a specialized vocabulary and the ability to speak with our clients from the English-speaking areas in a fluent way even for technical matters.

_source.definition_text: Vocational education and skills prepare you for a particular type of work.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The college offers both vocational and academic courses.; Homeless people need coun[s]elling and education in order to ad[a]pt themselves [to] modern society, appropriate guidance on how to get a job, what vocational qualification is required, and to equip them with confidence to resist the temptation of being in [a] rut again.

_source.definition_text: the sounds that are made when people speak or sing
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has a very loud/quiet/soft voice.; a clear/deep voice; You could tell from her voice that she wasn't pleased.; She lowered her voice to a whisper.;  Could you please keep your voices down?

_source.definition_text: to speak loudly and angrily to someone
_source.learnerexamples_text: He never raised his voice at the children.; Not every au-pair family is pleasant. And believe me, mine was giving me hell on earth. [...] After I returned home I took some time to learn not to freak out when someone raised his voice and eventually I started to see my time in Germany as a great [lesson in] life.

_source.definition_text: to become unable to speak, often because of an illness
_source.learnerexamples_text: She had a bad cold and was losing her voice.; I immediately became agitated and at the precise moment of my speech I lost my voice completely.

_source.definition_text: to say what you think about a particular subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has voiced concern about the new proposals.; And in the end they voiced their wishes to re-unif[y] Germany.

_source.definition_text: a mountain with a large hole at the top which sometimes explodes and produces hot, melted rock and smoke
_source.learnerexamples_text: an extinct/active volcano;  Erupting volcanoes discharge massive quantities of dust into the atmosphere.; Finally, I think that a good place to go is Santorini, a beautiful island which has a volcano.

_source.definition_text: a game in which two teams use their hands to hit a ball over a net without allowing it to touch the ground
_source.learnerexamples_text: They played volleyball on the beach.; My hobbies are playing volleyball and watching TV.

_source.definition_text: the number or amount of something, especially when it is large
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was put off by the volume of work involved.; The volume of traffic in the city is causing problems.; Nowadays, marketing volume is rapidly increased in Internet business, according to one of [the] major newspaper[s].

_source.definition_text: the level of sound produced by a television, radio, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you turn the volume up/down, please.; After we went to the disco and we danced together, but the volume of the music was too high to talk!

_source.definition_text: a book, especially one of a set
_source.learnerexamples_text: a new dictionary in two volumes; This book which I adored as a child, and as a matter of fact, one which I often come back to, comprises seven volumes, each giving a vivid account of the adventures that the Pevensie siblings, Lucy, Edmund, Susan and Peter, encounter in the magical land of Narnia.

_source.definition_text: If something speaks volumes, it makes an opinion, characteristic or situation very clear without the use of words.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She said very little, but her face spoke volumes.; It remains to be seen whether the effect of stem cells when applied to humans would be the same, but the achievements speak volumes about the fact that stem cells may one day turn a new [page] in many people's lives and let them get rid of that humiliating label of a "disabled person."

_source.definition_text: a person who does something, especially helping other people, willingly and without being forced or paid to do it
_source.learnerexamples_text: a Red Cross volunteer ; The charity relies on volunteers to run the office and answer the telephones.; Well the concert was Friday night and I went there with the Red Cross volunteers, did you know I'm one of them?

_source.definition_text: Voluntary work is done without being paid and usually involves helping people.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She does voluntary work for Doctors Without Borders.;  voluntary organizations; I did voluntary work for a whole year in 1998 in Britain.

_source.definition_text: If you do something voluntarily, nobody has forced you to do it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She left voluntarily.; After he had himself discharged voluntarily from the hospital, he drove up to the cliff, [and] left his car there.

_source.definition_text: If someone vomits, the food or liquid that was in their stomach comes up and out of their mouth.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was vomiting blood. ; They assured me that they felt very sorry for me, but then they always changed the subject quickly and began joking and laughing, whereas I went into the toilet and vomited, because I could not live with all the disgust.

_source.definition_text: to offer to do something without being asked or told to do it
_source.learnerexamples_text: Rob volunteered to look after the kids.; One of my classmates, Maria, has volunteered to talk about the different courses and summer activities that the school offers.

_source.definition_text: when someone shows their choice or opinion in an election or meeting by writing a cross on an official piece of paper or putting their hand up
_source.learnerexamples_text: He lost the election by twenty votes.; The suggestion was approved, with 25 votes in favour, and 7 against.; She cast her vote for the Green Party.; [T]he one who get[s] the most votes will get 1000 Baht as first prize.

_source.definition_text: to show your choice or opinion in an election or meeting by writing a mark on an official piece of paper or by putting your hand up
_source.learnerexamples_text: Who did you vote for?;  The unions voted against strike action.;  Staff have voted to accept the pay offer. ; She was too young to vote in the national election.; The committee voted on the proposal, and accepted it.

_source.definition_text: when someone is officially allowed to vote
_source.learnerexamples_text: In some countries women still don't have the vote.; Women acquired the vote only 70 years ago.

_source.definition_text: a way of making a decision by asking a group of people to vote
_source.learnerexamples_text: We called a meeting in order to take a vote on the issue.

_source.definition_text: to vote
_source.learnerexamples_text: Many people cast their votes for the opposition.; When the day of the General Elections came, no woman cast her vote [for] James and he lost his seat to a man from a minority party, not even the man representing the Labour Party.

_source.definition_text: a person who votes or who has a legal right to vote, especially in an election
_source.learnerexamples_text: Of course, tax cuts are usually popular with (the) voters.; Are you a Labour voter?; Raising taxes to support low-cost housing or provide support for children and women who have been exposed to domestic violence may be unpopular with voters, but it should be emphasised that spending money to reduce homelessness certainly will pay off in the long run.

_source.definition_text: a serious promise or decision
_source.learnerexamples_text: marriage vows ;  I made a vow that I would write to him once a week. ; The vows (and the rings) are exchanged after a short speech given by the priest.

_source.definition_text: to make a serious promise or decision
_source.learnerexamples_text: She vowed that she would never leave the children again. ;  I've vowed never to go there again. ; Most definitely Yiannakis' plan had not worked out and after that episode he vowed that he would never set foot in a stadium again.

_source.definition_text: a speech sound that you make with your lips and teeth open, shown in English by the letters a, e, i, o, or u
_source.learnerexamples_text: A short vowel is a short sound as in the word 'cup'.; A long vowel is a long sound as in the word 'shoe'.; [In the game,] he let the student[s] cho[o]se [a] vowel or consonant.

_source.definition_text: a long journey, especially by ship, or in space
_source.learnerexamples_text: Cook's voyage to Australia; Besides, I have a good command of French and I speak English fluently, which might be also useful during the voyage around the world.

_source.definition_text: easy to hurt or attack physically or emotionally
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was a vulnerable sixteen-year-old.; The troops are in a vulnerable position.; He's more vulnerable to infection because of his injuries.; Therefore they are vulnerable to being twisted by their environment, by events, or by more manipulat[ive] minds.

_source.definition_text: the amount of money a person regularly receives for their job
_source.learnerexamples_text: weekly wages; He earns/gets good wages at the factory.; a very low/high wage; the minimum wage; an hourly/daily/weekly wage

_source.definition_text: the part of the body above and slightly narrower than the hips
_source.learnerexamples_text: a small/narrow/tiny/large waist; These trousers are a bit tight around my waist.; She has a 26-inch waist.; Chris was holding his arm tight[ly] around Claire's waist.

_source.definition_text: to be late so that someone has to wait for you
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry to have kept you waiting.; The dentist kept me waiting for ages.; I'm sorry for keep[ing] you waiting.

_source.definition_text: to stay in a place until someone or something arrives, or until someone or something is ready for you

_source.definition_text: said in order to interrupt someone, or to get their attention or when you have suddenly thought of something important
_source.learnerexamples_text: Now, wait a moment - I don't agree with that.; Wait a minute - I've just had an idea.; Oh! Wait a minute...

_source.definition_text: used to say how excited you are about something that you are going to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't wait to see him.; I can't wait to see you!

_source.definition_text: to wait to discover what will happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: We'll wait and see what she says.; We will just have to wait and see.....

_source.definition_text: to not do something until something else happens

_source.definition_text: a man who works in a restaurant, bringing food to customers
_source.learnerexamples_text: The waiter brought our drinks.; The waiter and waitress working there are kind and friendly.

_source.definition_text: when you stay in one place until someone or something arrives, or someone or something is ready for you
_source.learnerexamples_text: a long wait; well worth the wait; We had a three-hour wait before we could see the doctor.; The long wait for the doctor/to see the doctor really made me anxious.

_source.definition_text: a woman who works in a restaurant, bringing food to customers
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's working as a waitress at the moment.; She is a waitress [and] she likes this job.

_source.definition_text: to stop sleeping or to make someone else stop sleeping

_source.definition_text: to move forward by putting one foot in front of the other and then repeating the action

_source.definition_text: to stop sleeping or to make someone else stop sleeping
