_source.definition_text: a journey that takes a short time/ten minutes, etc. when you walk
_source.searchterms_text: a short/ten minute, etc. walk;a short/ten-minute etc walk;a short/ten-minute, etc. walk;a short/tenminute, etc. walk;short/ten-minute, etc. walk;walk;walks
_source.learnerexamples_text: The station is just a five-minute walk from the house.; A fi[f]teen-minute walk was necessary to reach it and there were no neighbours around.

_source.definition_text: a path or route where people can walk for enjoyment
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are some lovely walks in the forest.; The walk ends in Valli del Natisone, but from here there are 2 other different routes that can be chosen.

_source.definition_text: someone who walks for exercise or enjoyment
_source.learnerexamples_text: This pub is popular with walkers.; If you are a keen walker and you like unspoilt nature, the walk between Granna and Tranas in the South [of] Sweden will be the one.

_source.definition_text: the activity of going for a walk, especially for pleasure in the countryside
_source.learnerexamples_text: We're going walking in Wales for a week.; a pair of walking boots; My hobbies are swimming, walking, running and playing football.

_source.definition_text: a vertical structure, often made of stone or brick, that divides or surrounds something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The walls in this apartment are so thin you can hear just about every word the neighbours say.; The walls look a bit bare - can't we put some pictures up?; We had to climb over a ten-foot wall to get into the garden.; The Berlin Wall came down in 1989.; We will paint the wall orange.

_source.definition_text: a small folding case for carrying paper money and credit cards, used especially by men
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you seen my wallet anywhere?; He pulled out a big fat wallet stuffed with notes.; I think I have left my wallet in your house.

_source.definition_text: to walk around slowly in a relaxed way or without any clear purpose or direction
_source.learnerexamples_text: We spent the morning wandering around the old part of the city.; He was here a moment ago but he's wandered off somewhere.; If you can't afford it you can just wander around the city and enjoy meeting people.

_source.definition_text: If someone's attention/mind, etc. wanders, they start thinking about one subject when they should be thinking about a different subject.
_source.searchterms_text: sb's attention/mind/thoughts etc wander;sb's attention/mind/thoughts, etc. wander;wander;wandered;wandering;wanders
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was bored and my thoughts started to wander.; His mind kept wandering off and he always found himself dreaming of her beautiful blue eyes, her long, dark eye-lashes and her soft, curled hair.

_source.definition_text: to hope to have or do something, or to wish for something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I want some chocolate.; She wants a word with you.; What do you want to eat?; Do you want me to take you to the station?; I just wanted to write a letter [to] you.

_source.definition_text: armed fighting between two or more countries or groups, or a particular example of this
_source.learnerexamples_text: nuclear war; civil war; a war film/grave/hero; If this country goes to war we will have to face the fact that many people will die.; Britain and France declared war on Germany in 1939.

_source.definition_text: an attempt to stop something bad or illegal
_source.learnerexamples_text: the war against crime/drugs; Some years ago, she had given an interview [o]n a local channel, explaining why she chose to devote herself to the war against the destruction of the environment.

_source.definition_text: a room or area in a hospital, where people receiving treatment stay
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's in a ward on the fourth floor.; I spent two days alone in a ward [in] Biarritz's hospital.

_source.definition_text: a large cupboard for keeping clothes in
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was showing me her new built-in/fitted wardrobes.; I want to sell a wooden wardrobe, because I've bought a new one.

_source.definition_text: a large building for storing goods that are going to be sold
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have several thousand of the books in our warehouse.; Whether we sit hunched over our computers, telework in the dim light of a reading lamp at home or perform physical jobs in a warehouse, we are surrounded [by] numbers of colleagues.

_source.definition_text: all the clothes that you own
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has an extensive wardrobe.; Our wardrobe seemed to have changed from neutral colours which symbolised no freedom of expression to purple-green outfits that tell you: ".. that's me, if you don't like it, get...".

_source.definition_text: having a temperature between cool and hot
_source.learnerexamples_text: Are you warm enough or do you want the fire on?; I've got my hands in my pockets to keep them warm.; I like to [go] surfing there because [the] water is warm.

_source.definition_text: describes clothes and covers made of a material that keeps you warm
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't have a warm winter coat.; Those gloves look nice and warm.; Remember you should wear warm clothes.

_source.definition_text: friendly and loving
_source.learnerexamples_text: They're a very warm family.; He has a lovely warm smile.; I'd like to give a warm welcome to our guests this evening.; He is warm and friendly.

_source.definition_text: to become warm or make something become warm
_source.learnerexamples_text: You're so cold - come and warm your hands by the fire.; Your supper's just warming through in the oven.; We can warm (up) the room quite quickly with this electric fire.; After they save[d] me, I put those gloves on to warm my hands.

_source.definition_text: in a way that keeps you warm
_source.learnerexamples_text: You're not dressed warmly enough - put a sweater on.

_source.definition_text: in a friendly or loving way
_source.learnerexamples_text: He shook my hand warmly.; He embraced me warmly and whispered 'You wouldn't have believed me.'

_source.definition_text: a friendly and loving quality in someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I still remember the warmth of their welcome.; They gave us so much when we were children, their love and their warmth, and now it is up to us to stay with them and give back the love we [recei]ved.

_source.definition_text: the heat that is produced by something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've put a T-shirt on under my sweater for extra warmth.; We lay down on the sand enjoying the warmth of the sun and listening to the birds.

_source.definition_text: something that tells or shows you that something bad may happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's a warning on the cigarette packet that says 'Tobacco seriously damages health'.; The bombs fell completely without warning.; Just a word of warning - restaurants in this area can be very expensive.; The government have today issued a warning about the dangers of sunbathing.; Without any warning he pushed [me].

_source.definition_text: to make someone realise a possible danger or problem, especially one in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were warned not to eat the fish.; Have you warned them (that) there will be an extra person for dinner?; I was warned against/off going to the east coast because it was so full of tourists.; This particular curry is extremely hot - be warned!; Put that ball down and come over here, Laura - I'm warning you!

_source.definition_text: a person who has experience and skill in fighting in a war, especially in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: These warriors used spears made from iron.; It is true that the Vikings were warriors, some would say bloodthirsty as well, but that is something I will leave to you to judge.

_source.definition_text: If you are wary of someone or something, you do not trust them completely.
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's still wary of strangers. ; Therefore, I strongly believe that consumers should be wary of "pots of gold" and promises [made] in vain. They should trust solely in what their doctors recommend for each specific case.

_source.definition_text: to clean yourself, or a part of yourself, with water and usually soap
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to wash before dinner.; I suppose they are in your bathroom, I put them [t]here before I washed.

_source.definition_text: to clean something using water
_source.learnerexamples_text: wash your hair/hands; wash the car/clothes/floor; These sheets need washing.; I'll wash the bottle out and use it again.; We can wash cars to earn some money for the necessary materials.

_source.definition_text: to clean the plates, pans, and other things that you have used for cooking and eating
_source.searchterms_text: wash;wash (sth) up or wash up (sth);wash sth up or wash up sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: He washed up his mug and put it back on the shelf.; After the meal, I have to wash up the dishes.

_source.definition_text: when you wash something or a part of your body
_source.learnerexamples_text: Those curtains need a wash.; Erik needed a good wash after playing in the garden.

_source.definition_text: a machine for washing clothes, sheets and other things made of cloth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Could you empty/load the washing machine, please?; I've left my mobile phone on [your] washing machine.

_source.definition_text: when you wash the dishes, pans, and other things you have used for cooking and eating a meal
_source.learnerexamples_text: Mick was doing the washing-up.; I can do the washing-up and cooking.

_source.definition_text: an unnecessary or wrong use of money, substances, time, energy, abilities, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: That meeting achieved absolutely nothing - it was a complete waste of time.; She's been unemployed for two years and it's such a waste of her talents.; This food mixer's been a total waste of money - we never use it.; I don't [watch] m[uch] television because I think it's a waste of time.

_source.definition_text: a black and yellow flying insect that can sting you
_source.learnerexamples_text: There's a wasps' nest in that old tree.; a wasp sting ; We were sitting in the garden and suddenly a wasp entered my T-shirt.

_source.definition_text: unwanted matter or material of any type, often that which is left after useful substances or parts have been removed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Britain produces 20 million tonnes of household waste each year.; He opposes any kind of nuclear waste being dumped at sea.; Oil spills are common, as is the dumping of toxic waste.; What I did to get it was send them an article based on some possible solutions to the problem of nuclear waste in my local area.

_source.definition_text: Waste material is no longer needed and can be got rid of.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The Japanese recycle more than half of their waste paper.; In addition, some waste materials are carried to the incinerator where they are burnt completely at very high temperatures.

_source.definition_text: to use too much of something or use something badly when there is a limited amount of it
_source.learnerexamples_text: You waste a lot of water by having a bath instead of a shower.; Come on, let's get started - we've wasted enough time already.; Don't waste your money on me, love, keep it for yourself.; It's nice to hear that you want to go to Colombia and I'm really happy because I can tell you all the details so you won't waste time and money.

_source.definition_text: to be clever or of high quality in a way that someone will not understand or enjoy
_source.learnerexamples_text: Good coffee is wasted on Joe - he prefers instant.; Many older pe[ople] can be heard grumbling that youth is wasted on the young, and I can see their point, though obviously I don't agree.

_source.definition_text: to look at something for a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had dinner and watched TV for a couple of hours.; I watched him get into a taxi.; I got the feeling I was being watched.; I sit by the window and watch people walking past.; She works at the Glade and she watches television at night.

_source.definition_text: to be careful about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I have to watch my weight now I'm not doing so much sport.; Watch how you cross the road!; Watch (that) you don't get glue on your fingers, won't you?; Watch what you're doing with that knife, Jim, it's sharp.; The odd glass of wine is fine but watch what you [eat].

_source.definition_text: to be careful
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Watch out!" he shouted, but it was too late - she had knocked the whole tray of drinks on the floor.; I definitely know that having a cat brings inconvenience, you have to watch out for your curtains, it can scratch your sofa or your hand, but these are so few problems in comparison [with] all the affection [it] can give you.

_source.definition_text: a small clock which is worn on a strap around the wrist
_source.learnerexamples_text: My watch seems to have stopped - it says 10:15 but I'm sure it must be later.; He glanced nervously at his watch.; I got 2 watches, flowers and some dresses.

_source.definition_text: an area of water, such as the sea, a lake or a swimming pool
_source.learnerexamples_text: The water's much warmer today - are you coming for a swim?; Dad, I swam a whole length of the pool under water!; There are a lot of beautiful beaches with clean water.

_source.definition_text: the clear liquid which falls from the sky as rain and is necessary for animal and plant life
_source.learnerexamples_text: hot/cold water; a bottle/drink/glass of water;  bottled/mineral/tap water; Can I have a drop of water in my whisky, please?; You have to bring some food, and a lot of water.

_source.base_text: be (like) water off a duck's back
_source.definition_text: If criticisms, insults, etc. are like water off a duck's back to you, they do not affect you at all.
_source.searchterms_text: be (like) water off a duck's back;be like water off a duck's back;water
_source.learnerexamples_text: She calls him lazy and useless, but it's like water off a duck's back.; The main lesson I have learned is by looking at some people who have lived alone for most of their life and faced with neither contradiction nor argument, they stay in their ivory tower, so sure of their opinions that whatever you say is like water off a duck's back.

_source.definition_text: If a place has running water, it has a working water system.
_source.learnerexamples_text: They bought an old house with no electricity or running water.; It is hilarious to think that at the same time people in [the] north of Europe were still living a primitive and uncivilized life not even able to invent an axe, the Romans managed to install running water in their huge houses.

_source.definition_text: If you say that an argument doesn't hold water, you mean that it can't possibly be true.
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry, but what you are suggesting just doesn't hold water!;  It remains to us to prove that the opinions of some scientists are far-fetched and don't hold water.

_source.definition_text: water from lakes, rivers, etc. that has no salt in it
_source.learnerexamples_text: These fish live in fresh water.; You find stunning white beaches, clear, fresh water lakes, isolated tropic islands, reef, rainforests, buzzing cities, challenging mountain range, bush, outback - and the desert.

_source.definition_text: to have just enough money to live or to continue a business
_source.learnerexamples_text: With extra income from private sponsorship, the club is just about managing to keep its head above water.; I also started to realise how much she had on her plate, how very little help she had and how, at times, she had to struggle just like me to keep her head above water.

_source.definition_text: If food makes your mouth water, it makes you want to eat it, sometimes making your mouth produce liquid.
_source.learnerexamples_text: The smells from the kitchen are making my mouth water.

_source.definition_text: to pour water on to plants or the soil that they are growing in
_source.learnerexamples_text: I've asked my neighbour to water the plants while I'm away.; I cleaned [the flat] every day and watered your flowers.

_source.definition_text: water, especially from a river or stream, dropping from a higher to a lower point, sometimes from a great height
_source.learnerexamples_text: We walked for an hour and arrived at the waterfall.

_source.definition_text: not allowing water to go through
_source.learnerexamples_text: Canvas boots are all right but they're not as waterproof as leather.; Probably warm jumpers and a waterproof coat would do, don't you think so?

_source.definition_text: to raise your hand and move it from side to side in order to attract someone's attention or to say goodbye
_source.learnerexamples_text: I waved to/at him from the window but he didn't see me.; She was so annoyed she wouldn't even wave us goodbye/wave goodbye to us.; She waves her hands about/around a lot when she's talking.; She waved at me and I smiled.

_source.definition_text: a line of higher water which moves across the surface of an area of water, especially the sea
_source.learnerexamples_text: At night, I listened to the sound of the waves breaking/crashing against the shore.; I already know you surf and the waves at Reserva will be huge this weekend [so] we will surely surf together.

_source.definition_text: to move from side to side in the air or make something move this way
_source.learnerexamples_text: The long grass waved in the breeze.; He started waving his arms about wildly.; I can picture myself standing in front of the "Casa Prosada", waving my arms and cheering with all the other patriots.

_source.definition_text: a group of people or things that arrive or happen together or in a short period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: There has been a wave of kidnappings in the region.; Another wave of refugees is arriving at the border.; These people, who belong mostly to the middle class, and some other[s] like explorers [...] or youngsters seeking some adventure, produce the big wave of tourists to different countries.

_source.definition_text: the pattern in which some types of energy, such as sound, light and heat, are spread or carried
_source.learnerexamples_text: radio waves; Indeed, it is thought that using a mobile phone may cause brain damage owing to magnetic waves.

_source.definition_text: when you suddenly feel an emotion
_source.searchterms_text: a wave of hatred/enthusiasm/sadness etc;a wave of hatred/enthusiasm/sadness, etc.;wave;wave of hatred/enthusiasm/sadness, etc.;waves
_source.learnerexamples_text: She felt a sudden wave of sadness.; As he counted the money, a wave of shame and horror hit Berthold.

_source.definition_text: to cause problems by asking difficult questions or criticizing
_source.learnerexamples_text: He has earned a reputation for making waves during political campaigns.; If we don't want to regret anything, it is time we started to make waves by s[c]rutinizing our history.

_source.definition_text: when you raise your hand and move it from side to side in order to attract someone's attention or say goodbye
_source.learnerexamples_text: She gave a little wave as the train left.; And as with a wave of a magic hand, everything changed.

_source.definition_text: how you do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: There are many ways of solving the problem.; That's not the way to do it - let me show you.; That method hasn't worked, so let's try your way.; I think it's the best way to relax.

_source.definition_text: If two people are on the same wavelength, they have the same way of thinking and it is easy for them to understand each other.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We chatted occasionally, but I never really felt we were on the same wavelength.; We were on the same wavelength and we therefore started our own research.

_source.definition_text: the route you take to get from one place to another
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you know the way to the train station?; I've only been living in Madrid for a couple of weeks so I don't really know my way around it yet.; We'll have to stop for fuel on the way to the airport.; Can you find your own way out of the building?; The coach stopped for us to eat lunch but within half an hour we were on our way again.

_source.definition_text: used when you say something new or on a different subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: I think we've discussed everything we need to - by the way, what time is it?; Oh, by the way, my name's Julie.; By the way, I want to buy a raincoat for my brother.

_source.definition_text: the direction in which something is facing or travels
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Which way does the room face?" "North."; This bus is going the wrong way.; Which way up should this box be?; The numbers are the wrong way round - it should be 71, not 17.; Although he had told us he knew this address, he went [the] wrong way.

_source.definition_text: a distance or a period of time
_source.learnerexamples_text: We walked a long way yesterday.; The holidays seem like they're a long way away/off.; I like this best because [it] is not a long way from home.

_source.definition_text: the manner in which a person lives
_source.learnerexamples_text: She told us all about her way of life in Japan.; He told me about his hobbies, his way of life and especially about his love [of] learning languages.

_source.definition_text: used to tell someone that something is impossible
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry but there's no way we can help you.; No way will she agree to you leaving early.; Don't worry, there is no way I'm going to miss it!

_source.definition_text: in some way that is not stated
_source.learnerexamples_text: One way or another these bills have to be paid.; Everyone at the party was related in one way or another.; All of them made a big difference [to] our personal life and have affected it one way or another.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about two possibilities where the result will be the same
_source.learnerexamples_text: You can get there by train or bus - either way it'll take an hour.; He might have to resign or he might be given a desk job, but either way, his career is effectively over.; If that doesn't work, you can ask them to talk to your friends' parents so you could all go together. Either way, I know you will have lots of fun this summer.

_source.definition_text: in any way that is possible
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have to make a decision one way or the other about what needs to be done.; Our transportation system nowadays is also very well organised and there is a wide range of buses, subways, etc. with which you can reach your destination one way or the other.

_source.definition_text: happening in the opposite way
_source.searchterms_text: other way round/around;the other way round/around;way;ways
_source.learnerexamples_text: I thought the older people would be more offended than the young people, but it was the other way round.; As you know, I did that the other way round for the States.

_source.definition_text: to get to a place
_source.learnerexamples_text: We slowly made our way down the river.; It's getting late - we should make our way home soon.; She made her way slowly to the waiting room and patiently waited for the train to arrive.

_source.base_text: in a way; in some/many ways
_source.definition_text: used to say that you think something is partly true
_source.searchterms_text: in a way in some/many ways;in a way; in some/many ways;way;ways
_source.learnerexamples_text: In a way, I would prefer it if they didn't come because it would mean extra work.;  In some ways it would be better if we met on Monday rather than Wednesday.; He was a remarkable politician in many ways.; I think that many people would like shops to be open all the time, and it might be good in some ways.

_source.definition_text: the complete distance
_source.learnerexamples_text: They cycled all the way to London.; I drove all the way to Bergen in only one day.

_source.definition_text: the manner in which someone behaves or thinks, or in which something happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't be alarmed - it's just his way.; He looked at me in a sinister way.;  It's amazing the way she manages to stay so calm.; The way he was shouting, you'd have thought he was badly hurt.;  To my way of thinking, they shouldn't be building so many roads.

_source.definition_text: the space needed for a particular movement or action
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Sorry, am I in your way? I'll move."; If you don't move that vase out of the way, it might get broken.; Don't let your new friends get in the way of your studies.; I couldn't see the stage because there was a pillar in the way.; Please make way so the ambulance can get by.

_source.definition_text: to be successful and make progress in your work
_source.learnerexamples_text: He managed to make his way in the film industry.; For each one of the famous sportsmen we re[cog]nise on television or in the newspapers, there are thousands of hopeful youngsters trying to make their way to the top.

_source.base_text: go out of your way to do sth
_source.definition_text: to try very hard to do something pleasant for someone
_source.searchterms_text: go out of your way to do sth;way;ways
_source.learnerexamples_text: He went out of his way to make us feel welcome.

_source.base_text: get/have sth out of the way
_source.definition_text: to finish a task or to get rid of something unpleasant
_source.searchterms_text: get/have sth out of the way;way;ways
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'll go shopping when I've got this essay out of the way.; It was a joyful reunion and everybody was grateful to have all misunderstandings out of the way and to be one big family once more.

_source.base_text: in no way/not in any way
_source.definition_text: not at all
_source.searchterms_text: in no way/not in any way;way;ways
_source.learnerexamples_text: This is in no way your fault.; This magazine will be loved by students as it will help them learn English in the best way and in no way will students find it boring.

_source.definition_text: as a type of something
_source.learnerexamples_text: He sent me some flowers by way of apology.; The Academy however provided nothing whatsoever by way of entertainment, though with a group of interesting young people and a little imagination this should not be a pro[b]lem.

_source.definition_text: used to say that someone or something does something to a large degree
_source.learnerexamples_text: They celebrate birthdays in a big way.; Tourism helps Greece's national economy - which is not at its best - in a big way.

_source.definition_text: to change into something else
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her excitement quickly gave way to horror.; This friendship gave way to love, but it was a really difficult situation, after all she was the Managing Director's daughter.

_source.definition_text: to be already happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: Building work is already under way.; Sociologists are well-aware of the fact and experiments are under way to counterbalance these disadvantages.

_source.definition_text: to get what you want, although it might upset other people
_source.searchterms_text: get/have your (own) way;get/have your own way;way;ways
_source.learnerexamples_text: She always gets her own way in the end.; They are provided with what they desire, and [the] majority of them are used to getting their own way.

_source.definition_text: If something gives way, it falls because it is not strong enough to support the weight on top of it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Suddenly the ground gave way under me.; Fred's voice trailed off as he felt his legs give way beneath him.

_source.definition_text: to be replaced by someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: They knocked down the old houses to make way for a new hotel.; In the UK most high-streets already look very much the same and the local shops had to make way for big conglomerates.

_source.definition_text: to do what is easiest in a difficult situation
_source.searchterms_text: (take) the easy way out;take the easy way out;way;ways
_source.learnerexamples_text: I know you don't approve of his working methods, but why not take the easy way out this time and agree to his request?; On the other hand you cannot survive without your pay-check and to be able to both make a car[ee]r and have the time to be green, sometimes you just have to take the easy way out.

_source.definition_text: If something paves the way for something else, it makes the other thing possible.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Scientists hope that data from the probe will pave the way for a more detailed exploration of Mars.; Many celebrities engage actively in UN projects and pave the way for others to contribute.

_source.definition_text: used as the subject of the verb to refer to the speaker and at least one other person when considered together or as a group
_source.learnerexamples_text: Can we all go to the swimming pool this afternoon?; If you don't hurry up we'll be late.; After dinner we want to go shopping.

_source.definition_text: to move carefully through a crowded place, changing direction in order to avoid people or things
_source.searchterms_text: thread your way through/between etc;thread your way through/between, etc.;way;ways
_source.learnerexamples_text: She threaded her way through the crowd.; And if I thread my way through the crowd along the street, I can find almost all things I want to buy, from inexpensive souvenirs to internationally known brands of suits.

_source.definition_text: to do or learn something by experiencing a lot of problems or difficulty
_source.learnerexamples_text: I learned the hard way that training every single day is not the best way to get fit.; If you don't know the past, you're liable to live through it again as instead of deriving the lessons from someone else's experiences, you'll have to learn them the hard way, by trial and error.

_source.definition_text: not physically strong
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's not surprising you feel weak if you haven't eaten properly for days.; I felt so weak that I wasn't able to tidy and wash up.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to people generally
_source.learnerexamples_text: The world in which we live today is very different.; Why can't we live without computers?

_source.definition_text: not good at something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She reads well but her spelling is weak.; Listening is my weak point so I have to improve.

_source.definition_text: A weak reason, argument or excuse is one that can easily be proved to be false.
_source.learnerexamples_text: He gave the weakest of excuses when asked why he was late.

_source.definition_text: not powerful, or not having a strong character
_source.learnerexamples_text: a weak leader/government/king; At the beginning of the story, [Mary] seemed to be a weak person, but in the end she demonstrated that she could overcome her fears in order to protect someone.

_source.definition_text: containing little taste or alcohol
_source.learnerexamples_text: weak coffee/beer

_source.definition_text: likely to fail
_source.learnerexamples_text: a weak economy; a weak team; A very difficult aspect currently is our weak economy, we could nearly speak of a recession.

_source.definition_text: difficult to see or hear
_source.learnerexamples_text: He spoke in a weak voice.; I could hardly see with the weak light of the candle and I couldn't remember the last time I had used it.

_source.definition_text: to become less certain or determined about a decision, or to make someone less determined

_source.definition_text: to like a particular thing or person very much

_source.definition_text: a large amount of something good

_source.definition_text: rich

_source.definition_text: any object used in fighting or war, such as a gun, bomb, sword, etc.

_source.definition_text: to have clothing, jewellery, etc. on your body

_source.definition_text: to arrange or grow your hair in a particular way

_source.definition_text: to show a particular emotion on your face.

_source.base_text: wear sb out or wear out sb

_source.definition_text: to use something so much that it is damaged and cannot be used any more, or to become damaged in this way

_source.definition_text: very tired

_source.definition_text: bored with something or someone

_source.definition_text: to feel ill

_source.definition_text: a type of net made by a spider to catch insects
