_source.definition_text: to try hard to achieve something
_source.learnerexamples_text: You need to work at improving your writing.; In my opinion, this is the part our college has to improve and to work at.

_source.definition_text: to spend time repairing or improving something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Tim loves working on old cars.; I believe that it would be best to paint a picture of me in the garage working on my new car.

_source.base_text: work sth out or work out sth
_source.definition_text: to do a calculation to get an answer to a mathematical question
_source.searchterms_text: work;work sth out or work out sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: We need to work out the total cost of the project.; I had to work out all my figures two times to make sure that my accounts were accurate.

_source.base_text: work sth out or work out sth
_source.definition_text: to understand something or to find the answer to something by thinking about it
_source.searchterms_text: work;work sth out or work out sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: There will be a full investigation to work out what caused the accident.; Investigators needed several months to work out that a fraud had been committed.; They gathered to work out how the Union [could find] remedies to the problem of unemployment.

_source.definition_text: to exercise in order to improve the strength or appearance of your body
_source.learnerexamples_text: Heidi works out in the gym two or three times a week.; At the time I use[d] to work out and I [saw] that he was looking [at] me while I was doing my exercises.

_source.definition_text: If a problem or a complicated situation works out, it ends in a successful way.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We were worried that the event would be disorganized, but it all worked out in the end.; I hope you follow my instructions and you'll see how everything works out fine.

_source.definition_text: someone who works too much and does not have time to do anything else
_source.learnerexamples_text: My husband's a workaholic.; Unless you are a real "workaholic", and there are some of them out there, working like a slave to get more money doesn't pay off.

_source.definition_text: someone who works for a company or organization but does not have a powerful position
_source.learnerexamples_text: factory workers; Many companies still treat their management staff better than their workers.; There is a man with a suitcase and he says: "Hi, I'm a worker in the a[ir]port and I found this suitcase."

_source.definition_text: all the people who work for a company or organization
_source.learnerexamples_text: We have a highly skilled workforce.; Before giving them rewards, companies need to train their workforce and identify their potential.

_source.definition_text: someone who works quickly/slowly/well, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: a quick/slow/good etc worker;a quick/slow/good, etc. worker;quick/slow/good, etc. worker;worker;workers
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's rather a slow worker, but he is very thorough.; I'll recom[men]d you [as] a hard worker and a very nice person.

_source.definition_text: all the people in a country who are able to do a job
_source.learnerexamples_text: 10% of the workforce are unemployed.; There is hardly a nation without representatives in Germany's workforce.

_source.definition_text: relating to your job
_source.learnerexamples_text: a 37-hour working week ; working hours; Working conditions in the mill have hardly changed over the last twenty years.; She has a difficult working relationship with many of her staff.; As you know, I work in [a] bank, so I have to [dress] smartly during working hours.

_source.definition_text: knowledge about something which is good enough to be useful
_source.searchterms_text: a working knowledge of sth;working;working knowledge of sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: She has a working knowledge of German and Russian.; Furthermore, I have a working knowledge of English, Spanish, Catalan and Italian.

_source.definition_text: the social group consisting of people who do not get paid much money and who often do physical work
_source.learnerexamples_text: He sees the prime minister's comments as an attack on the working class.; A member of the working class, for example, was not expected to wear something smart, as he didn't represent the company.

_source.definition_text: belonging to or relating to the working class
_source.learnerexamples_text: Working-class families can't afford these prices.; And young people from working-class families in the suburbs of Paris will make a point of having the latest fashion shoes or trousers.

_source.definition_text: the place where you work
_source.learnerexamples_text: We are trying to get rid of bullying in the workplace.; Nowadays, our jobs consume more and more of our time so a good atmosphere at the workplace is important.

_source.definition_text: a period of physical exercise
_source.learnerexamples_text: a light workout; Are there many fitness-cent[res] where we can practise our daily workout?

_source.definition_text: when a group of people meet to learn more about something by discussing it and doing practical exercises
_source.learnerexamples_text: a workshop on crime prevention; All in all, I thoroughly enjoyed this event, but I think there ought to be more computers provided and the numbers of participants to a single workshop should be limited.

_source.definition_text: your life and experiences
_source.learnerexamples_text: His whole world fell apart when she left.; I like this room because it's "my world" and because it is very big.

_source.definition_text: the Earth and all the people, places and things on it
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's travelled all over the world.; News of the disaster shocked the whole world.; We live in a changing world.; I like travel[l]ing and discovering new place[s] [i]n the world.

_source.definition_text: the people and things that are involved in a particular activity or subject
_source.learnerexamples_text: the entertainment world; the world of politics; Well, as you know, I'm not very interested in the fashion world, so I rarely spend much time shopping for clothes.

_source.definition_text: to have the advantages of two different situations
_source.searchterms_text: (have) the best of both worlds;have the best of both worlds;world;worlds
_source.learnerexamples_text: Living in the country and working in the city you have the best of both worlds.; Only those that can afford to live in the suburban areas can combine the best of both worlds and they tend to be rather affluent.

_source.definition_text: to be of extremely good quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: Their chocolate cake is just out of this world!; The dessert trays are out of this world.

_source.base_text: do sb a/the world of good
_source.definition_text: to make someone feel much happier or healthier
_source.searchterms_text: do sb a/the world of good;world;worlds
_source.learnerexamples_text: That swim has done me a world of good.; I feel a year abroad would do her a world of good in letting her care for children, learn to speak English properly, and see life from different aspects.

_source.base_text: not be the end of the world
_source.definition_text: If something is not the end of the world, it will not cause very serious problems.
_source.searchterms_text: not be the end of the world;world;worlds
_source.learnerexamples_text: It won't be the end of the world if I don't get the job.

_source.definition_text: existing or happening in all parts of the world
_source.learnerexamples_text: a worldwide success; An increase in average temperature by only a few degrees could cause environmental problems worldwide.; You can visit the main monuments of Paris, known worldwide, like Notre-Dame Cathedral or the Eiffel Tower, built in 1903.

_source.base_text: be/feel on top of the world
_source.definition_text: to be very happy
_source.searchterms_text: be/feel on top of the world;world;worlds
_source.learnerexamples_text: I had just won a major tournament and I was feeling on top of the world.; I felt like I was on top of the world and nothing could take that happiness from me.

_source.definition_text: anxious because you are thinking about problems or unpleasant things that might happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's really worried about her son.; I'm worried that someone will find out.; She was sitting behind her desk with a worried expression/look on her face.; You had me worried for a moment back there - I thought you wouldn't be able to stop in time.; I'm worried about your health.

_source.definition_text: a small creature with a long, thin, soft body and no legs
_source.learnerexamples_text: Blackbirds eat worms, insects, and berries.; Fishing is my hobby and that's why I bought these plastic worms, that are not [very] good - it's better to use live worms!

_source.definition_text: to think about problems or unpleasant things that might happen in a way that makes you feel anxious
_source.learnerexamples_text: Try not to worry - there's nothing you can do to change the situation.; It's silly worrying about things which are outside your control.; I'm worried about your health.

_source.definition_text: used to tell someone that they do not need to think about something or do anything about something
_source.searchterms_text: don't worry (about sth);don't worry about sth;worried;worries;worry;worrying
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't worry - she'll be all right.; Don't worry about phoning Ian - I'll do it later.; Don't worry about dinner, because I eat everything.

_source.definition_text: to make someone feel anxious because of problems or unpleasant things that might happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: It worries me that he hasn't phoned yet.; The lack of rain is starting to worry people.; Unemployment is increasing too, and today, it worries every single citizen of the world, specially the ones who live in [a] third world country.

_source.definition_text: a problem that makes you feel anxious
_source.learnerexamples_text: health/financial worries; Keeping warm in the winter is a major worry for many old people.; My worries proved to be wrong.

_source.definition_text: making you feel unhappy and afraid
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's a very worrying situation.; But the most worrying thing about this matter is you.

_source.definition_text: when you are anxious about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's been sick with worry.; Unemployment, bad health - all sorts of things can be a cause of worry.; You really need to spend a whole month without any kind of worry.

_source.definition_text: (comparative of bad) more unpleasant or difficult than something else that is also bad
_source.learnerexamples_text: The exam was worse than I expected.; His behaviour is even worse than his sister's.; The heat is much worse in the daytime.; It takes me more than one hour to get to work every day. In the evening it is even worse.

_source.definition_text: to become more ill, unpleasant, difficult, severe, etc. than before
_source.learnerexamples_text: My cold seems to be getting worse.; If the rain gets any worse, we'll have to stop walking.; I thought, it couldn't get worse.

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize how unpleasant, difficult, severe, etc. something is becoming
_source.learnerexamples_text: The economic climate is getting worse and worse.; The traffic situation in all big towns is getting worse and worse, so that bicycles or public transport must become more attractive.

_source.definition_text: comparative of badly
_source.learnerexamples_text: He did worse than he was expecting in the exams.; He was treated much worse than I was.

_source.definition_text: something that is more unpleasant or difficult
_source.learnerexamples_text: By the third month of the expedition they had endured many hardships, but worse was to follow.; "What about the bride's dress - wasn't it appalling?" "I don't know, I've seen worse."; But worse was to come at 19:30 when we went to see one of London's musicals.

_source.definition_text: to make a situation more difficult, unpleasant, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: To make matters worse, our car broke down!; To make matters worse, the newspaper said they only played for thirty-five minutes.

_source.definition_text: to become worse or to make something become worse
_source.learnerexamples_text: His condition suddenly worsened last week.; I believe erecting a car park in the cent[re] could worsen the situation drastically.

_source.definition_text: to have or show a strong feeling of respect and admiration for God or a god
_source.learnerexamples_text: In the various regions of India, Hindus worship different gods and observe different religious festivals.; The Revolution was of such importance because Greece became a free country again and the people were free to talk, worship their God and have Greek schools.

_source.definition_text: to love and admire someone or something very much
_source.learnerexamples_text: She worshipped her mother. ; Firstly, many famous people are considered as idols who are worshipped and imitated, which might make them believe they are important, especially when they have a certain media presence.

_source.definition_text: when you worship God or a god, often through praying or singing
_source.learnerexamples_text: daily acts of worship; Christian/Sikh/Muslim worship; For Jews, the synagogue is the centre for community worship and study.; Local people have complained about improperly dressed tourists entering places of worship.; There were Holy Masses celebrated by him in several cities and places of worship.

_source.definition_text: the most unpleasant or difficult thing, person, or situation
_source.learnerexamples_text: That was the worst I've seen him play in several years.; This situation was the worst I have lived [through].

_source.definition_text: (superlative of bad) the most unpleasant, difficult or severe
_source.learnerexamples_text: That was the worst meal I've ever eaten.; "It was the worst moment of my life," she admitted.; And you, what is your worst gift?

_source.definition_text: used to emphasize the worst thing, situation, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: We had no food or light, but worst of all, we had no water.; And worst of all, her mother had been always against that relationship and had given her advice many times.

_source.definition_text: to worry that something very bad will happen or that something very bad has happened
_source.learnerexamples_text: When there was no sign of the children, the rescuers feared the worst.; Her parents had been quar[re]lling constantly now for almost half [a] year, and she feared the worst.

_source.definition_text: (superlative of badly) the most badly
_source.learnerexamples_text: Small businesses have been worst hit by the recession.; Roads in the Tayside region were worst affected by the snow.

_source.definition_text: to have a particular value in money
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our house is worth about £400 000.

_source.definition_text: to be important or interesting enough to receive a particular action or to cause you to do something
_source.learnerexamples_text: When you're in Reykjavik, the National Museum is worth a visit.; His latest book is definitely worth reading.; It's really worth visiting.

_source.definition_text: to be useful or enjoyable despite needing a lot of effort
_source.learnerexamples_text: It was a long climb to the top of the hill, but it was worth it for the view.; Don't tire yourself out, Geri, it's really not worth it.; Forget him, love - he's just not worth it.; There were a lot of hills in the park, [and] it was very tiring to go up riding a bike, but when you got to the top, and stared at the amazing view, it was worth it.

_source.definition_text: If it is worth your while doing something, it is useful or enjoyable to do it.
_source.learnerexamples_text: It's worth your while taking out travel insurance before you travel.; It isn't worth my while going all that way just for one day.; It would be worth your while to visit the country's capital Havana, and don't forget to go into the Folklore Museum and Library, the War Museum and the Archeological [Museum].

_source.definition_text: not important or useful
_source.learnerexamples_text: He made me feel stupid and worthless.; One important aspect is, of course, that they will feel worthless.

_source.definition_text: useful and enjoyable, despite needing a lot of effort
_source.learnerexamples_text: She considers teaching a worthwhile career.; The time and expense involved in keeping up to date with all the changes has been worthwhile.; If you need him on this project, you've got to make it financially worthwhile for him.; It's a worthwhile trip. You'll have the op[p]ortunity to visit beautiful places and learn lots of history.

_source.definition_text: having no value in money
_source.learnerexamples_text: The painting's a fake - it's completely worthless.; I think that many people have these kinds of "worthless" objects, which they actually hold more dear to them than the gramophone they bought in an auction, or the car they won in a quiz-show, or even the wedding dress they inherited from their great-grandmother.

_source.definition_text: deserving to be given attention, noticed, etc.
_source.searchterms_text: worthier;worthiest;worthy;worthy of attention/notice etc;worthy of attention/notice, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Two points in this report are especially worthy of notice.; Try as I might, getting good grades was always met more with a sense of mission accomplished - duly noted - than a feat worthy of congratulations.

_source.definition_text: deserving respect, admiration or support
_source.learnerexamples_text: He is unlikely to succeed in getting his bill through Congress, however worthy it is.; Every year she makes a large donation to a worthy cause.; The performers are all neatly dressed and on the whole, they have all made a worthy effort.

_source.definition_text: used to say politely that you want something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd like a cup of coffee, please.; I'd like to talk to her myself.; I'd like fish and chips (but not too fat[ty]!)

_source.definition_text: used to ask someone if they want something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Would you like a drink?; Would you like me to come with you?; Would you like to come?

_source.definition_text: used to say that you would very much like something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd love some chocolate right now!; I'd love to be an actor.; I'd love some chop[s] and beer.

_source.definition_text: used to say that you would very much like to do something that someone has suggested
_source.searchterms_text: would;would love to (do sth);would love to do sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Would you like to come to the concert with us?" "I'd love to." ; We'd love to go to the beach - thanks for inviting us.; Yes, I'd love to come with you.

_source.definition_text: used to say what might happen if something else happens
_source.learnerexamples_text: What would you do if you lost your job?; They knew there would be trouble unless the report was finished by the next day.; I was just wondering if you would ask me that, because if you didn't, I would - I just love shopping!

_source.definition_text: used as the past form of 'will' to talk about what someone was willing to do or what something was able to do
_source.learnerexamples_text: The car wouldn't start this morning.; I asked her to talk to him, but she wouldn't.; My parents wouldn't let me stay in a hotel alone.

_source.definition_text: used as the past form of 'will' to talk about what someone said or thought
_source.learnerexamples_text: Archie said he would see his brother tomorrow.; They thought that she would never recover.; He said to me he would like to come back soon.

_source.definition_text: used to talk about a situation that you can imagine happening
_source.learnerexamples_text: It would be lovely to go to New York.; It would be great to join you and your friends in the mountains.

_source.definition_text: used to request something politely
_source.learnerexamples_text: Would you mind sharing a room?; Would you mind if I called you, to know what I've missed?

_source.definition_text: used to show that you prefer to have or do one thing more than another
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd rather have a beer.; Which would you rather do - go swimming or play tennis?; Wouldn't you rather finish it tomorrow?

_source.definition_text: used to talk about things that happened often in the past
_source.learnerexamples_text: He would always turn and wave at the end of the street.; Since my childhood I have always been fond of swimming. I would usually spend my summer holidays on a campsite near a river with my family.

_source.definition_text: wanting or trying to be
_source.learnerexamples_text: a would-be artist/politician ; Her schoolmates were greatly surprised that a would-be lawyer with a promising career like her had made such a decision.

_source.definition_text: would prefer
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd sooner spend a bit more money than take chances with safety.; However, with many living examples of unemploye[d] [people] getting by on benefits, some young people have been influenced to think that they would sooner live on benefits than work all week and receive moderate wages.

_source.definition_text: an injury, especially one that is made with a knife or bullet
_source.learnerexamples_text: a gunshot wound; a chest/leg wound; a flesh wound; Rollo discovered that his best friend was implicated in the penicillin racket: the racketeer would put sand into penicillin without worrying about the great suffering that they caused to people who needed penicillin for their wounds.

_source.definition_text: to injure someone, especially with a knife or gun
_source.learnerexamples_text: The police chief was badly wounded in the explosion.; Harry was wounded on his leg.

_source.definition_text: used to show surprise, excitement, admiration, etc.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Wow! Did you make that cake? It looks delicious!; Wow, this is very cool!

_source.definition_text: to cover someone with material in order to protect them
_source.learnerexamples_text: She wrapped the baby in a blanket.; He wrapped a towel around his shoulders.; After a few seconds I gathered my wits and wrapped the towel around myself again.

_source.definition_text: to cover or surround something with paper, cloth or other material
_source.learnerexamples_text: She wrapped the present and tied it with ribbon.; Wrap the chicken in foil and cook it for two hours.

_source.definition_text: to destroy or badly damage something
_source.learnerexamples_text: The explosion wrecked several cars and damaged nearby buildings.; In addition, they [agree] that the solution to the traffic is of utmost importance in a big city, because noise and pollution from car exhaust pipes wreck the nerves of city dwellers.

_source.base_text: wrap sth up or wrap up sth
_source.definition_text: to fold paper, cloth, etc. around something to cover it
_source.searchterms_text: wrap;wrap sth up or wrap up sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you wrapped up Jenny's present?; It was wrapped up in paper with a red ribbon.

_source.definition_text: a vehicle or ship that has been destroyed or badly damaged
_source.learnerexamples_text: Divers exploring the wreck managed to salvage some coins and jewellery.; The burnt-out wrecks of two police cars littered the road.; We turned around and saw fumes rising in the air from the wreck of the plane.

_source.definition_text: someone who is in a bad physical or mental condition
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was a complete wreck by the end of my exams. ; So much of what I really appreciate in this life is connected to music and the events that surround it, so a loss of that would totally dev[a]state me and turn me into a wreck!

_source.definition_text: the parts that remain of a car, ship, or aircraft that has been destroyed
_source.learnerexamples_text: Two survivors were pulled from the wreckage. ; When resting next to the wreckage he had got bitten by a snake and had crept into the cockpit to die there.

_source.definition_text: very unhappy or ill
_source.learnerexamples_text: I'd been feeling wretched all day so I went to bed early.; As a result, some people will realise they were unable to achieve their ends when they were younger and will feel wretched.

_source.definition_text: very bad or of poor quality
_source.learnerexamples_text: The refugees were living in wretched conditions.; Because working leads to self-esteem, that is most vital for people, especially when they are in wretched conditions.

_source.definition_text: a small line on your face that you get when you grow old
_source.learnerexamples_text: This cream reduces the appearance of wrinkles.; And so time goes by and old age is closing [in]. One morning you notice the wrinkles around your eyes and the grey hair that doesn't keep any of the old colour.

_source.definition_text: the part of the body between the hand and the arm
_source.learnerexamples_text: I sprained my wrist playing squash.;  I fell [o]n [some] stair[s] and hurt my wrist.

_source.definition_text: with a lot of wrinkles
_source.learnerexamples_text: a wrinkled face; To this day, and for many years to come, this piece of music brings back the dirty wrinkled face of the loneliest person I've ever known.

_source.definition_text: to produce letters, words or numbers on a surface or computer
_source.learnerexamples_text: Write your name at the top of the page.; When you fill in the form, please write clearly in black ink.; Can I borrow your laptop tonight - I need to write my essay.; Ev[e]ry le[sson] I read and write loads o[f] sentences.

_source.definition_text: to create a book, story, article, etc. or a piece of music
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's writing a book on Colombia.; She writes for Time magazine.; Walton wrote the Cello Concerto in 1956.; Stephen King wrote this book.

_source.definition_text: to send a letter or email to someone, giving them information or expressing your thoughts or feelings
_source.learnerexamples_text: James hasn't written to me recently.; I wrote my sister a letter.; My mother wrote to give me details about the party.; The travel company has written giving information about the trip.; I can write [my penfriend] a letter twice a week.

_source.base_text: write sth down or write down sth
_source.definition_text: to write something on a piece of paper so that you do not forget it
_source.searchterms_text: write;write sth down or write down sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Did you write Jo's phone number down?; I wrote the address down and left the restaurant.

_source.base_text: write sb/sth off or write off sb/sth
_source.definition_text: to decide that someone or something is not useful or important
_source.searchterms_text: write;write sb/sth off or write off sb/sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: They had written him off before they even met him.; She had written that man off.

_source.base_text: write sth up or write up sth
_source.definition_text: to write something on paper or on a computer in a complete or final form, often using notes you have made
_source.searchterms_text: write;write sth up or write up sth
_source.learnerexamples_text: Have you written up that report yet?

_source.definition_text: a person who writes books or articles to be published
_source.learnerexamples_text: a travel/sports/fiction/crime writer; She is a well-known writer of children's books.; The last book I read was a true story written by a young South-American writer.

_source.definition_text: the skill or activity of producing words on a surface
_source.learnerexamples_text: Teachers focus on speaking and writing in the afternoon classes.; [I]n my lessons I learn reading, writing and English grammar.

_source.definition_text: something which has been written or printed
_source.learnerexamples_text: The writing on the label was too small to read.

_source.definition_text: the way that someone writes
_source.learnerexamples_text: Do you recognise the writing on the envelope?

_source.definition_text: the activity of creating pieces of written work, such as books, stories, poems, etc., or the written work of one person or a group of people
_source.learnerexamples_text: I did a course in creative writing.; She is studying women's writing of the 1930s.; Black humo[u]r is a distinguishable feature of his writing.

_source.definition_text: An agreement that is in writing is official and is proof of that agreement.
_source.learnerexamples_text: Please confirm your reservation in writing.; I [am] tell[ing] you in writing that I would like to help you.

_source.definition_text: not correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: Three of your answers were wrong.; That clock is wrong - it's 12.30, not 12.15.; I'm sorry, you've got the wrong number.; We're going the wrong way.; We [listen to a] tape somet[ime]s, and mark wrong letters.

_source.definition_text: expressed in writing, or involving writing
_source.learnerexamples_text: written instructions; a written exam; I would like you to tell me what subject you're teaching tomorrow and the pages of the homework, so I can do the written test [in the] next class.

_source.definition_text: to think or say something that is not correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was wrong about the time - the shop closed at 7, not 8.; You're wrong in thinking that Matt is from the States - he's Canadian.; If I'm not wrong, it is in the living room.

_source.definition_text: to produce an answer or result that is not correct, or to say or write something that is not correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: I got most of the answers wrong.; The newspapers got the story completely wrong.

_source.definition_text: If something is wrong, there is a problem.
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've been quiet all evening. Is there anything wrong?; What's wrong?; There's something wrong with my computer.; I didn't kn[o]w him, so I thought that there was something wrong.

_source.definition_text: not considered morally acceptable by most people
_source.learnerexamples_text: Children should be taught that violence is wrong.;  It is wrong to tell lies.; What's wrong with having a bit of fun?; To sum up, I think it is wrong to keep animals in zoos.

_source.base_text: get off/start on the wrong foot
_source.definition_text: to start a relationship or activity badly
_source.searchterms_text: get off/start on the wrong foot;wrong
_source.learnerexamples_text: He got off on the wrong foot with my parents by arriving late.; One of the greatest pleasure[s] of reading "The Remains of the Day" would be to see the gradual development of the relationship between Stevens and Miss Kenton. From the beginning, they get off on the wrong foot.

_source.definition_text: in a way that is not correct
_source.learnerexamples_text: You've spelt my name wrong.

_source.definition_text: not suitable or correct, or not as it should be
_source.learnerexamples_text: She's the wrong person for the job.; She got in with the wrong crowd at university.; Personally I prefer to think that you gave the job to the wrong person.

_source.definition_text: used when you do not want someone to think that you do not like someone or something
_source.learnerexamples_text: Don't get me wrong, I like her, but she can be very annoying.; Don't get me wrong, I love my aunts, I really do, but not as houseguests.

_source.definition_text: to develop problems
_source.learnerexamples_text: Something's gone wrong with my computer.; Despite all that went wrong, there was something I really enjoyed. It was visiting the Diamond Cave.

_source.definition_text: not correctly
_source.learnerexamples_text: It has been said - wrongly - that Americans hate government.; Equally, the point about 'staying' is erroneous: we stayed at Riverside Hotel instead of Hotel Astrid, [which] closed last year, [and] Hotel Royal [was] wrongly [described as having] 'special rates' for students.

_source.definition_text: accused or punished unfairly or illegally
_source.learnerexamples_text: She was wrongly convicted of drug smuggling.; You have also wrongly accused the organisers of spending too much money on organising the event.

_source.definition_text: extreme dislike or fear of people from other countries
_source.learnerexamples_text: They accused her of xenophobia.; This creates a climate of social tension. The number of poor people increase while the rich become richer and the middle-class tends to disappear; xenophobia and other cultural 'harassment' become popular, accompanied by more violence and increasing crime rates.

_source.definition_text: a photograph that shows the inside of your body
_source.learnerexamples_text: They took an X-ray of his leg.; I was with my last patient trying to operate [on] his damage[d] tooth when I realized the X-Ray was on the wrong side and that I wasn't working on the damage[d] tooth.

_source.definition_text: a boat with sails and sometimes an engine, used for either racing or travelling on for pleasure
_source.learnerexamples_text: a luxury yacht; a yacht club; The class of boat that best fits my physical condition is the one called [S]nipe, that seems to be available at your yacht club.

_source.definition_text: a unit of measurement equal to three feet or approximately 91.4 centimetres
_source.learnerexamples_text: The garden is about 100 yards long.; I'm not a fitness maniac and I don't go to a shop which is 50 yards away from my house just to buy a newspaper, but if you go to school, why not go by bike[?]

_source.definition_text: yes
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Do you like your job?" "Yeah, it's all right I suppose."; "Will you drive?" "Yeah, sure."; Yeah, try wearing black because we're gonna [get] dirty.

_source.definition_text: to take a deep breath with your mouth wide open, because you are tired or bored
_source.learnerexamples_text: I can't stop yawning - I must be tired.; I think that the maths lesson is the most suitable one to be recorded. Watching ourselves yawning and nearly asleep would really reflect how boring maths [is].

_source.definition_text: a period of twelve months, especially from January 1st to December 31st
_source.learnerexamples_text: Elaine worked in Italy for two years.; 2006 was one of the worst years of my life.; last/next year; He joined the company a year ago.; This tree keeps its leaves all (the) year (round).

_source.definition_text: to be a particular age
_source.learnerexamples_text: Her son is six years old.; He is 53 years old [and] he live[s] in Madeira.

_source.definition_text: the part of the year, in a school or university, during which courses are taught
_source.learnerexamples_text: the school/college year; Emma's now in her final/first/second year at Manchester University.; The class is ev[e]ry Friday until the end of the school year.

_source.definition_text: for a long time
_source.learnerexamples_text: Roz and I have been going there for years.; I had not seen him for years.

_source.definition_text: 10/20, etc. years younger than someone
_source.searchterms_text: 10/20 etc years sb's junior;10/20, etc. years sb's junior;year;years
_source.learnerexamples_text: My wife is 8 years my junior.; I have a sister four years my junior and in my opinion we have no reason to complain.

_source.base_text: yearn for sth; yearn to do sth
_source.definition_text: to want something very much with a feeling of sadness
_source.searchterms_text: yearn;yearn for sth yearn to do sth;yearn for sth; yearn to do sth;yearned;yearning;yearns
_source.learnerexamples_text: They yearned for peace.; She yearned to get away.; I yearn to go there because I have never been to Africa before.

_source.definition_text: to shout something very loudly
_source.learnerexamples_text: Our neighbours were yelling at each other this morning.; The child yelled out in pain.; "Just get out of here!" she yelled.; "Cut," yelled the director.

_source.definition_text: a loud shout
_source.learnerexamples_text: Suddenly there was a loud/great yell from the bathroom.; Suddenly a big yell came out of my throat.

_source.definition_text: being the same colour as a lemon or the sun
_source.learnerexamples_text: a bright yellow T-shirt; It was early autumn and the leaves were turning yellow.; The walls are yellow and the cupboard is orange.

_source.definition_text: a yellow colour
_source.learnerexamples_text: You should wear more yellow - it suits you.; I wanna paint the room in blue and yellow.

_source.definition_text: used to show that you are listening to someone, or that you are ready to listen and to give them an answer or information
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Dad." "Yes, what do you want, honey?"; "Yes, can I help you?"

_source.definition_text: used to agree with something, or to give a positive answer
_source.learnerexamples_text: "Would you like a glass of wine?" "Yes, please."; "Do you like Thai food?" "Yes, I love it."; "He's a really nice guy." "Yes, he is."; "Report to me at nine o'clock tomorrow morning." "Yes, sir."; "Have you had enough to eat?" "Yes, thank you."

_source.definition_text: used when you are disagreeing with a negative statement
_source.learnerexamples_text: "I'm not a very good cook, though." "Yes, you are - you make wonderful food!"

_source.definition_text: up until now
_source.learnerexamples_text: I haven't spoken to her yet.; He hasn't finished yet.; "Are you ready?" "Not yet - wait a moment."; I haven't seen the sea yet.

_source.definition_text: on the day before today
_source.learnerexamples_text: He rang yesterday while you were out.; I saw her yesterday morning/afternoon/evening.; I got your letter yesterday.

_source.definition_text: now or as early as this time
_source.learnerexamples_text: I don't want to go home yet.; I don't need it yet because my parents gave me a new computer for my birthday.

_source.definition_text: from now and for a particular period of time in the future
_source.learnerexamples_text: She won't be back for a long time yet.; Our holiday isn't for weeks yet.; It's a fact that everybody knows that living in Poland is not easy now and it won't be for a long time yet.

_source.definition_text: the best or worst, etc. until now
_source.searchterms_text: best/worst, etc. yet;the best/worst etc yet;the best/worst, etc. yet;yet
_source.learnerexamples_text: Of all the songs I've heard tonight, that's the best yet.; That was my worst exam yet.; And that was my worst experience yet.

_source.definition_text: again after something has happened or been done many times before
_source.learnerexamples_text: The bus was late yet again.; Tom, thank you so much yet again for your interest. This talk is very important to me and to count on you is an honour for our college.

_source.definition_text: used to show that you are surprised or annoyed that something is being repeated or increased
_source.learnerexamples_text: He's given us yet more work to do.; The awe-inspiring view of the park must not be destroyed for yet another building.

_source.definition_text: used to say there is still a possibility that something will happen
_source.learnerexamples_text: He may win yet.; Weakened, the tunnel could yet crumble and fall at any time.

_source.definition_text: used to connect two words, phrases, or clauses when the second part adds something surprising to the first part
_source.learnerexamples_text: simple yet effective; I agree it's unlikely, yet she knows what she's talking about.; It was huge and yet gracious.

_source.definition_text: until and including this time
_source.learnerexamples_text: We haven't needed extra staff as yet, but may do in the future.; No ambulances had as yet managed to get across the river.; I would like to do something about it, but as I can't imagine building anything near my beautiful house (because I'm afraid it would destroy its wonderful harmony), I have no idea as yet how to solve this problem.

_source.definition_text: to not have done something that was expected before this time
_source.learnerexamples_text: They have yet to make a decision.; But she had yet to inform her fiancé.

_source.definition_text: to produce or provide something
_source.learnerexamples_text: to yield a profit;  The investigation yielded results.; It is to be hoped that my suggestion will be implemented and will yield immediate results.

_source.definition_text: a slightly sour, thick liquid made from milk with bacteria added to it, sometimes sweetened and with a fruit flavour added and sometimes eaten plain
_source.learnerexamples_text: natural/plain yogurt; strawberry yogurt; low-fat yogurt; I only had a yogurt for lunch.; In the morning they eat yogurt with masala chappaties.

_source.definition_text: a set of exercises for the mind and body, based on the Hindu religion
_source.learnerexamples_text: She does yoga three times a week. ; We do yoga in a heated room so we sweat a lot.

_source.definition_text: used to refer to the person or people you are talking to
_source.learnerexamples_text: You look nice.; I love you.; You're coming tonight, aren't you?; Are you two ready?; You painted that yourself? You clever girl!

_source.definition_text: people in general
_source.learnerexamples_text: You learn to accept these things as you get older.; You can't get a driving licence till you're seventeen in this country.; Too much alcohol is bad for you.; How do you get this thing to start?; You can get there by plane.

_source.definition_text: used when you are giving an explanation about something
_source.learnerexamples_text: I didn't know she was Welsh, you see.; You see, it was already late by that time.; Family matters had to stay in the family, you see.

_source.definition_text: said as a polite answer when someone thanks you for doing something
_source.learnerexamples_text: "It was very kind of you to help." "You're welcome."

_source.definition_text: young people generally
_source.learnerexamples_text: it's the sort of music that appeals mainly to the young.; I have nothing against mini-skirts, but I think they're strictly for the young.; In my opinion the young should work rather than wait for their pocket money.

_source.definition_text: a young person, especially an older child
_source.learnerexamples_text: He talked to the youngsters about the dangers of drugs. ; Like many other nations worldwide, with mastering much more knowledge and skills of information technology than [the] elder group of people, it is not surprising that Chinese youngsters learn more than their previous generations did about what is happening around the world.

_source.definition_text: having lived or existed for only a short time and not old
_source.learnerexamples_text: young adults/children; His girlfriend is very young.; Philippa is the youngest person in the family.; Angela is two years younger than Clare.; I have got two young children.

_source.definition_text: belonging or relating to the person or group of people being spoken or written to
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is this your bag?; It's not your fault.; Your mother is driving me crazy.; What's your problem?; I like your food.

_source.definition_text: belonging or relating to people generally
_source.learnerexamples_text: Of course you want the best for your children.; Garlic is good for your blood.; Riding [a] bicycle is a good [way of maintaining] personal fitness and doesn't harm your health either.

_source.definition_text: used to show that something belongs to or is connected with the person or group of people being spoken or written to
_source.learnerexamples_text: Is this pen yours?; Unfortunately, my legs aren't as long as yours.; I've got something of yours.; My bicycle is bro[k]en. Can you lend me yours?

_source.definition_text: used at the end of formal letters when you know the name of the person you are writing to
_source.learnerexamples_text: Yours sincerely, Emma Clarke.; I'm going to ask Tom for the [work] I will miss. Yours sincerely,

_source.definition_text: used to end a formal letter to someone whose name you do not know
_source.learnerexamples_text: Yours faithfully, Katherine Smith; Yours faithfully, SAMSON LAM (READER)

_source.definition_text: alone or without anyone else's help
_source.learnerexamples_text: We didn't mean to leave you all by yourself.; Can you lift it by yourself?; Did you make the dress yourself?; You can do that yourself.; It is difficult to g[et] there by yourself.

_source.definition_text: the reflexive form of the pronoun 'you'
_source.learnerexamples_text: Be careful with that knife or you'll cut yourself!; I hope you enjoy yourself.; After that you could choose a partner to talk about what you usually do in your free time and the last thing was to describe yourself in front of the class.

_source.definition_text: used to give special emphasis to the subject of the sentence
_source.learnerexamples_text: If you yourself ever need help, would you know where to get it?; If you are thinking of taking it up yourself always do [a] warm-up exercise before you run, don't go too fast at the beginning, and don't overdo it.

_source.definition_text: young people generally
_source.learnerexamples_text: the youth of today; a youth club; Finally I decided to join a new youth club in my town.

_source.definition_text: used when both the subject and object of the verb are 'you', and 'you' is also being used to refer to people generally
_source.learnerexamples_text: You tell yourself everything's all right but you know it's not really.; You help yourself by doing some exercise.

_source.definition_text: the period of time when someone is young
_source.learnerexamples_text: I was a fairly good football player in my youth.; I played several kinds of sports during my youth, but now I am not a member of any club.

_source.definition_text: an African animal like a horse with black and white lines
_source.learnerexamples_text: We saw a zebra in the distance.; Otherwise there would be many children and grown-ups who [would have] never seen an elephant, a tiger, a zebra etc.

_source.definition_text: the temperature at which water freezes in degrees centigrade
_source.learnerexamples_text: The temperature is expected to drop to ten degrees below zero tonight.; We have to learn that [it] is not natural for a lion [to live] in a country where, in winter, [the] temperature can fall below zero.

_source.definition_text: the number 0
_source.learnerexamples_text: Five, four, three, two, one, zero.; Can you [bring] me my laptop, because I have to do [some] homework on it - if I don't do this I will [get] a zero.

_source.definition_text: an area where a particular thing happens, that is used for a particular purpose, or where there are particular rules
_source.learnerexamples_text: an earthquake zone; a nuclear-free zone; He was charged with driving 75 mph in a 55 mph zone.; The UN Security Council has established a no-fly zone.; It is a very clean city with a lot of car-free zones.

_source.definition_text: a thing for fastening clothes, bags, etc. consisting of two rows of very small parts that connect together
_source.learnerexamples_text: to do up/undo a zip; I can't open my bag - the zip has stuck.; Suddenly the zip of my new dress broke.

_source.definition_text: a place where wild animals are kept so that people can go and look at them
_source.learnerexamples_text: I still remember my first trip to the zoo.; I like London Zoo. [It] is a very nice and beautiful zoo.
